Authors: Ryu H.J.
Author full names: Ryu, Hyeon Ji (60877449800)
Title: Analysis of retail resilience in Seoul's neighborhood commercial districts Amidst the COVID-19 shock
Abstract: This study examines the economic resilience of neighborhood commercial districts in Seoul in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Moving beyond static before–after comparisons, we employ a Panel Interrupted Time Series (Panel ITS) design to separately identify (i) the immediate level shift at the onset of the shock, conceptualized as resistance, and (ii) the subsequent change in the growth trajectory as conditions transitioned toward the endemic phase, conceptualized as recoverability. The results show that structural diversity, operationalized via Shannon's entropy, functions as a key buffering mechanism: it attenuates initial revenue losses and is associated with a steeper post-shock recovery trend. Importantly, we also document pronounced spatial heterogeneity across Seoul's five major sub-markets. Central business districts exhibit heightened exposure and larger initial downturns, while recovery trajectories vary across sub-markets. Taken together, these findings imply that urban management should complement place-based physical upgrading with ecosystem-oriented strategies—specifically, “portfolio diversification” approaches that strengthen sectoral complexity and reduce systemic vulnerability within local commercial ecosystems. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhang Y.; Ye Z.; Cui Z.; Hou Y.
Title: When AI ads violate expectations: the interplay of AI character, product type, and advertising appeal of AI ads on consumer attitudes
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Generative AI is rapidly reshaping video advertising production. Using expectancy violations theory as an interpretive lens, this study develops a framework in which ad appeal (rational vs. emotional), product type (high-tech vs. low-tech), and AI character embodiment (no character vs. animal-like vs. human-like) jointly relate to ad attitude and to two appraisals: perceived novelty and perceived uncanniness. This study tests the framework in five between-subjects experiments with consumers recruited from an online panel. Results show that rational appeals outperform emotional appeals in AI-generated ads, especially for low-tech products. Novelty is positively and uncanniness negatively associated with ad attitude, and the indirect effects through both appraisals are consistent with the proposed process. Human-like AI characters amplify uncanniness in emotional low-tech executions. In one rational low-tech execution, an animal-like character lowered uncanniness relative to a no-character baseline, but ad attitude did not differ significantly. The findings extend expectancy-violation theorizing in AI advertising and offer configuration-level design guidance for brands deploying disclosed AI-generated advertising. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Layered Defect-Filling co-Assembled Carbazole-Based SAMs Deliver 20% Organic Solar Cells and 17% Mini-Modules
Abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used as hole-transport layers (HTLs) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet conventional single-component SAMs often form quasi-monolayers with incomplete coverage and interfacial defects that become increasingly detrimental upon device scaling. Here, we develop a co-assembled multilayered SAM (coSAMu) strategy that combines two SAM molecules, 2PACz and 2Cl-4PACz, with distinct dipoles and steric configurations through blend casting and sequential casting. Photoelectron spectroscopy, X-ray analysis, and molecular simulations support a layered structure in which a chemisorbed, 2PACz-rich bottom layer primarily sets the indium tin oxide (ITO) work function, while a 2Cl-4PACz-rich upper layer fills interfacial voids, improves molecular packing, and passivates defects. Consistent with this picture, coSAMu promotes a more favorable vertical composition near the ITO surface and suppresses trap-assisted recombination, enabling more efficient charge extraction and collection. Consequently, a representative D18:L8-BO OSC incorporating the sequential-cast coSAMu HTL achieves a power conversion efficiency of 20.1% (0.042 cm2), outperforming pristine 2PACz. Importantly, when scaled to a 17.14 cm2 mini-module (six serially connected subcells), coSAMu delivers 17.0% efficiency versus 12.2% for the 2PACz control. This work demonstrates controlled multilayer co-assembly as an effective strategy for scalable OSC interface engineering that is broadly applicable to multiple donor–acceptor systems. Authors: Berrada Rekhami A.; Chnigri Y.
Author full names: Berrada Rekhami, Amine (60990052900); Chnigri, Yousra (58041009400)
Title: Management control systems and organizational innovation: A bibliometric analysis of the literature (1977–2026)
Abstract: Management control and organizational innovation are widely recognized as major determinants of firm performance and long-term competitiveness in contemporary business environments. Nevertheless, these two dimensions are frequently perceived as conflicting, as management control is traditionally associated with formalization, standardization, and performance monitoring, whereas innovation requires flexibility, experimentation, and organizational adaptability. This apparent tension has led several scholars to question the compatibility between management control systems and innovation processes, encouraging innovative organizations to explore new governance and coordination mechanisms. Against this backdrop, the present study aims to examine the evolution, role, and effectiveness of management control within innovation-oriented organizational contexts. To address this objective, the research adopts a bibliometric approach combined with a structured literature review in order to analyze the scientific production related to management control and innovation. The study investigates the conceptual transformations and practical reconfigurations of management control in response to contemporary organizational changes and emerging managerial challenges. Using 433 scientific articles published in the fields of economics, management, and organizational studies, the analysis identifies the main publication trends, influential authors, dominant research themes, and evolving theoretical perspectives within the literature. The findings reveal a significant and continuous growth in academic interest concerning the relationship between management control and innovation, particularly in relation to organizational agility, strategic performance, digital transformation, and dynamic capabilities. The study also highlights the progressive shift from traditional control mechanisms toward more flexible and interactive forms of management control adapted to innovation-driven environments. Furthermore, this bibliometric review contributes to ongoing debates by identifying emerging research streams and proposing future theoretical and methodological directions for scholars interested in the interaction between management control systems and organizational innovation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Author full names: Vedpathak, Kunal (58296802900); Bhatt, Ankur (57982603300); Lawler, Benjamin (42661890400); Gainey, Brian (57204633257)
Title: Extending ethanol energy fractions in ethanol-diesel dual-fuel combustion through EGR, intake conditions, and injection strategies
Abstract: Misfire and excessive maximum pressure rise rates (MPRR) typically limit the ethanol energy fraction (EEF) in ethanol–diesel dual-fuel combustion. To extend the allowable EEF while maintaining combustion stability and acceptable MPRR, experiments were conducted on a medium-duty engine (1.1 L/cylinder) operating in intake-fumigation dual-fuel mode with ethanol and diesel. Tests at 6, 10, and 15 bar gross indicated mean effective pressure (IMEPg) evaluated the effects of EGR, intake conditions, diesel injection timing, rail pressure, and injection strategy on combustion, emissions, and efficiency. At 10 and 15 bar IMEPg, operation was primarily constrained by excessive MPRR. Under baseline conditions, maximum EEF was limited to 51 % at 10 bar IMEPg and 39 % at 15 bar IMEPg. Increasing EGR from 14 % to 48 % at 10 bar IMEPg reduced peak heat release rates, lowering MPRR below 5 bar/deg and extending achievable EEF to 82 %. Intake temperature influenced combustion phasing and burn rates; reducing intake temperature from 350 K to 330 K decreased MPRR and widened the allowable EEF range. At 6 bar IMEPg, operation was limited by misfire rather than MPRR. Stable combustion could not be sustained above 87 % EEF because high ethanol fractions suppressed diesel cool-flame reactivity. Increasing intake pressure improved combustion quality by advancing combustion phasing and increasing in-cylinder temperatures. Diesel injection timing and rail pressure were varied to assess diesel reactivity under high-EGR, high-EEF conditions. Lower rail pressures favored advanced injection timings because richer spray plumes promoted stronger early-stage reactivity, whereas higher rail pressures benefited from later injection timings to avoid excessive spray overmixing before ignition. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Chang R.; Xu Y.; Deng Y.; Zhang Y.
Title: Scope 3 emissions reporting as an instrument for accelerating sustainable aviation fuel deployment
Abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a key near-term option for aviation decarbonisation, but its large-scale deployment is constrained by high production costs. At the same time, governance mechanisms, such as ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and Scope 3 emissions reporting under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, are reshaping incentives across the aviation value chain. This study conducts a systematic literature review of Scope 3 reporting, aviation decarbonisation technologies, and sectoral governance. Based on these insights, it proposes a conceptual financing framework showing how Scope 3 reporting can enable cost-sharing business models for SAF. The framework identifies emerging practices where corporates pay the SAF premium in exchange for Scope 3 credits, airlines cover conventional fuel costs and retain Scope 1 credits, and producers gain demand certainty. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhao P.-Y.; Ji S.-F.; Ji Y.-Y.
Title: Ensuring eco-resilience in Physical Internet-enabled production routing problem under ripple effect: a scenario-based robust possibilistic flexible programming approach
Abstract: Abstract: Resilience and eco-friendliness have emerged as two pivotal objectives for modern supply chains facing increasing disruptions and sustainability demands. The Physical Internet (PI), characterized by interconnectivity, resource sharing, and adaptability, represents a transformative approach to enhancing supply chain flexibility while mitigating environmental impacts. This study develops a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer optimization model to design a PI-enabled resilient production-routing system under the ripple effect. Furthermore, the model evaluates the influence of four distinct carbon policies, capturing the trade-offs between resilience and eco-friendliness. To address hybrid uncertainties arising from parameters, objectives, and constraints, this study proposes a scenario-based robust possibilistic flexible programming approach. The applicability and effectiveness of the proposed model and solution approach are validated through a case study. The results demonstrate that the PI significantly enhances both resilience and environmental sustainability by optimizing vehicle utilization, a benefit that cannot be realized in traditional noncollaborative or collaborative supply chains. Moreover, the analysis reveals that as policymakers adopt more conservative approaches, both total costs and carbon emissions increase simultaneously. Furthermore, higher carbon prices and lower carbon emission caps do not always lead to lower carbon emissions. © 2025 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: Physiological and behavioral modeling of stress and cognitive load in web-based question answering
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Time pressure and question difficulty can trigger stress and cognitive overload in web-based surveys, compromising data quality and user experience. Most stress detection methods are based on low-resolution self-reports, which are poorly suited for capturing fast, moment-to-moment changes during short online tasks. Addressing this gap, we conducted a 2 × 2 within-subjects study (N = 29), manipulating question difficulty and time pressure in a web-based multiple-choice questionnaire. Participants completed general knowledge and cognitive questions while we collected multimodal data: mouse dynamics, eye tracking, electrocardiogram, and electrodermal activity. Using condition-based and self-reported labels, we used statistical and machine learning models to model stress and question difficulty. Our results show distinct physiological and behavioral patterns within very short timeframes. This work demonstrates the feasibility of rapidly detecting cognitive-affective states in digital environments, paving the way for more adaptive, ethical, and user-aware survey interfaces. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Do negative emotions mediate the association between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions to involuntary musical imagery? Testing an OCD-analogue cognitive model of distressing earworms
Source title: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
Abstract: Purpose: Distressing involuntary musical imagery (INMI) or “earworms” are often experienced but rarely studied. Due to their similarity with obsessions, research can draw on models of obsessive-compulsive disorder. The present study followed a cognitive model and tested the hypothesis of a positive relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions, mediated by negative emotions. Methods: Individuals with OCD (n = 79) and students without OCD (n = 298) completed the Characteristics of Earworms Questionnaire (CEAR). The central hypothesis was tested using a mediation analysis. Results: The analysis revealed a significant direct effect of negative appraisals on dysfunctional reactions to INMI, but no mediation by negative emotions. Conclusions: These findings support the applicability of the cognitive OCD model to INMI, particularly the relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions. However, the results question whether negative emotions mediate this relationship. If replicated, results may provide a foundation for developing targeted interventions for distressing INMI. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Li D.; Xu H.; Cao G.; Liu F.; Ban J.; Zhang S.; Fan L.-Z.; Hu J.
Title: High-Conductivity and Moisture-Tolerant Sulfide Electrolyte Enabled by Bifunctional Coating for Practical All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
Abstract: The pursuit of safer and higher-energy-density batteries has driven the advancement of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Among various material systems, sulfide solid-state electrolytes (SEs) stand out as highly promising candidates owing to their exceptional ionic conductivity. Nevertheless, their extreme sensitivity to moisture results in the release of toxic H2S and rapid structural degradation, which severely impedes their scalable manufacturing under ambient conditions. A bifunctional (3-mercaptopropyl)trimethoxysilane (MPTMS) coating strategy is herein presented to shield Li5.5PS4.5Cl0.8Br0.7 (LPSCBr) from moisture-induced degradation. The MPTMS layer forms a hydrophobic barrier of approximately 10 nm, which reduces H2S emission by 93.0% after 35 min of exposure to 30% relative humidity, while maintaining 83.1% of the initial ionic conductivity (10.8 mS cm−1). This approach tackles the core challenge associated with sulfide solid-state electrolytes: the realization of compatibility with controlled ambient air without sacrificing critical electrochemical properties. The modified electrolyte maintains a high ionic conductivity (> 5.7 mS cm−1) even after 10 h of air exposure. When applied in all-solid-state cells paired with LiNi0.83Co0.11Mn0.06O2 cathodes, it exhibits remarkable electrochemical performance, delivering a capacity retention of 84.6% after 1000 cycles. By enabling moisture-tolerant processing, MPTMS-modified LPSCBr SEs lay a solid foundation for the scalable, high-performance, and cost-effective production of ASSLBs. Title: Toward Supply Chain Viability in SME Industrial Clusters: A Multi-Dimensional Decision-Making Framework
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: This study develops a multi-dimensional decision-making framework to enhance supply chain viability in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) industrial clusters operating under recurring disruptions and increasing uncertainty. Grounded in the viable supply chain literature and Industry 5.0 principles, viability is conceptualized as an integrated capacity emerging from the interaction of adaptation, legality, resilience, sustainability, digitalization, human-centricity, energy-system robustness, and risk mitigation. These high-level capabilities are operationalized through 22 implementation components covering product/design, functional/process, organizational, technological/informational, financial, and energy dimensions. A sequential hybrid methodology is employed to identify, synthesize, structure, evaluate, and operationalize these components. First, a systematic literature review, thematic analysis, and qualitative synthesis are conducted to identify and validate the components contributing to supply chain viability. Second, interpretive structural modeling (ISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC) analysis are used to examine hierarchical relationships and influence patterns among the validated components. Third, fuzzy step-wise weight assessment ratio analysis (SWARA) and combined compromise for ideal solution (CoCoFiSo) are applied to assess component importance while incorporating stakeholder preferences, uncertainty, and expert judgment reliability. Finally, the results are integrated into a mixed-integer linear programming model solved using the CBC solver to identify feasible capability portfolios under practical structural and resource constraints. © 2027 The author(s). Author full names: Fouladi Semnan, Afshin (58629149200); Maqsood, Tariq (57221378564); Dale, Ken (57191957004); Edwards, Mark (55465037300)
Title: Empirical Stage-Damage Functions for SME Content Losses in Australian Flood Vulnerability Assessment
Abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) dominate Australian business activity, yet empirically calibrated functions for nonresidential flood-related contents losses remain limited. Postevent surveys of 185 SMEs across 12 business types and 14 towns affected by the February-April 2022 Northern Rivers floods were used to derive stage-damage functions for stock, equipment, and fit-out. Contents-specific damage indices combined peak internal flood depth (0-6 m, relative to finished-floor level) with self-reported losses and preevent replacement values. Pooled curves were fitted using LOESS and a beta-family generalized additive model (Beta-GAM); a hierarchical Beta-GAM (HBGAM) generated business-type functions under partial pooling, while random forest and XGBoost provided depth-only predictive benchmarks. Across the pooled models, performance on the corresponding within-event 25% holdout sets was moderate (R2=0.57-0.69; RMSE=0.23-0.27), and neither machine-learning benchmark consistently improved performance. The Beta-GAM was retained because it provided smooth, bounded, interpretable relationships, model-based and bootstrap uncertainty intervals, and extractable threshold depths. The fitted mean damage index reached 0.50 at 1.03 m for stock, 1.09 m for equipment, and 1.27 m for fit-out, with uncertainty generally increasing above 3 m as data density declined. HBGAM-derived D50 values ranged from 0.66 to 1.18 m for stock, 0.81 to 1.18 m for equipment, and 1.09 to 1.48 m for fit-out, indicating model-derived sector variation. These event-calibrated functions support screening-level relative SME contents-loss assessment and evaluation of loss-reduction options in comparable settings; application elsewhere requires external validation or local recalibration.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Massa-Sánchez P.
Author full names: Massa-Sánchez, Priscilla (57200323027)
Title: Financializing the subsoil: Technical disclosure, extractive governance, and asymmetrical accountability in an emerging copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon
Abstract: This article examines how technical disclosure frameworks contribute to the financialization of mineral resources and shape forms of information disclosure within contemporary extractive governance. Focusing on the Warintza copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon, the study analyzes how geological information, investor-oriented valuation, environmental considerations, and community relations are structured within corporate disclosure practices. The research is based on qualitative documentary analysis of 18 publicly available disclosure documents produced between 2015 and 2024, including a NI 43–101 technical report, investor presentations, corporate reports, and sustainability-related documents. NI 43–101, a Canadian securities regulation designed to inform investors, structures highly detailed technical disclosures while offering only limited treatment of social and environmental dimensions. The findings show that disclosure systems prioritize geological and investor-oriented information through highly structured quantitative frameworks. Resource classification, drilling results, and corporate narratives of project potential translate geological uncertainty into investor expectations and position the deposit within global investment networks. By contrast, environmental and social dynamics are primarily represented through narrative descriptions that remain only partially integrated into investor evaluation. Rather than framing this as a problem of asymmetrical accountability, the article conceptualizes these dynamics as a condition of asymmetrical information disclosure across distinct governance domains. Different regulatory systems produce differentiated informational outputs, structuring what is disclosed, to whom, and with what level of precision. The findings also indicate that the limited disclosure of social conflict and Indigenous opposition may constitute a material gap in the representation of project-related risks within investor-oriented disclosure systems. By examining disclosure practices in an emerging mining region, the study contributes to debates on extractive governance, transparency regimes, and the financialization of natural resources. Authors: Kang H.; Lee S.-G.
Title: Guilt by association: Interpretable multiplex graph learning of accounting-risk contagion
Abstract: Severe accounting failures—material internal-control weaknesses, fraudulent restatements, and enforcement actions—are rare, costly, and relational: they cluster along the networks binding firms to common auditors, directors, and owners. We recast next-year failure prediction as node classification on a temporal multiplex firm graph whose layers encode a nested auditor hierarchy, board interlocks, and common ownership, and ask when the graph adds to the node-attribute signal. Methodologically, the usual graph-versus-tabular comparison is unfair: graph models receive node features that the tabular baselines are denied; once equalised, every standard graph network falls behind gradient-boosted trees. Architecturally, we introduce ACE-GNN, a pure multiplex network whose strength comes not from a richer operator—ruled out by a deliberate negative result—but from quantile encoding of node attributes and zero-inflated neighbour-exposure signals. ACE-GNN matches the strongest tabular learner, and a tree handed the same exposures attains near-identical accuracy, so the graph's advantage lies in faithful relation-level explanation, not accuracy. For interpretability, silent failures—firms whose warnings arrive only through their ties—are traced by edge-removal counterfactuals to specific auditor peers. These results delineate when graph-based AI earns its place on relational-but-tabular problems—and when it does not. © 2026

Authors: Alouk I.; Wang X.; Tang M.; Xiao Z.; Miao Y.; Chen S.; Wang Y.; Xu D.
Title: Calcium-modulated double emulsion for co-delivery of Monascus pigment and calcium
Abstract: Monascus pigments are susceptible to environmental and processing conditions, leading to degradation and reduced functionality, while calcium bioaccessibility remains limited due to interactions within complex food matrices that can restrict its release and uptake during digestion. In this study, a gel-in-oil-in-water (G/O/W) double emulsion with a gelled internal phase was engineered for the co-delivery of Monascus pigments and calcium, enabling systematic investigation of the role of calcium in modulating emulsion structure, stability, and digestion behavior. Physicochemical characterization, including droplet size, ζ-potential, rheology, and SEM, indicated that a gel-like internal network strengthened droplet interfaces, minimized coalescence, and enabled high encapsulation efficiency (92.94 ± 0.35%). In vitro digestion studies showed that the emulsion underwent clear structural evolution from intact droplets in the oral phase, to controlled aggregation in the gastric phase, and partial breakdown in the intestinal phase. This progressive structural change directly influenced the release kinetics of both Monascus pigments and calcium ions, resulting in enhanced bioaccessibility (64.94 ± 1.7% for pigments; 60 ± 2.7% for calcium). The formulation containing 5 mM calcium showed the most favorable stability and structural integrity. These findings demonstrate that calcium-mediated ionic interactions, together with the internal gel network, can regulate emulsion structure, stability, and simultaneous delivery performance, providing mechanistic insight into the stabilization and release of functional ingredients during digestion. The study offers a versatile platform for designing functional food and nutraceutical delivery systems based on double emulsions. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu X.; Chen Z.; Zhou D.; Zhao Q.; Feng H.; Cui Y.; Ding C.; Gao Y.
Title: Breaking the Specific Capacity Limit: 409% Boost in Manganese-Based Redox Flow Batteries at High Current Densities with a MnO2Semi-Solid Slurry Electrolyte
Abstract: The common-ion effect of SO42− limits the solubility of MnSO4 to ≤ 1 M in conventional H2SO4 electrolytes, resulting in low specific capacity of manganese (Mn)-based redox flow batteries (RFBs). Although MnO2 semi-solid RFBs are expected to improve the specific capacity, the sluggish electrochemical reaction kinetics leads to low operating current densities (≤ 1 mA cm−2). Herein, we employ a reverse-design strategy by introducing additional high-concentration MnO2 into the conventional Mn-based electrolyte. Leveraging the MnO2/Mn2+ electrochemical reaction successfully circumvents the common-ion effect, raising the concentration of soluble Mn species in the electrolyte to 3.76 M and achieving a specific capacity of 156.2 Ah LCatholyte-1 —a 409% increment over reported MnSO4-based electrolytes. Subsequently, the reverse disproportionation of electrolytic MnO2 generated during the second charging cycle shifts the redox mechanism from the MnO2(s)/Mn2+ couple to the solution-phase Mn3+(aq)/Mn2+ pair. This transformation not only elevates the discharge voltage but also enables stable operation at 30 mA cm−2, representing a current density 30-fold higher than reported Mn-based semi-solid RFBs. This work demonstrates a rational design strategy for semi-solid slurry electrolytes to enhance the specific capacity of RFBs, thereby advancing their applicability in grid-scale renewable energy storage. Title: Cultural value configurations and guests’ evaluations of AI-enabled service technologies
Abstract: As Artificial Intelligence reshapes hospitality service delivery, understanding how culturally diverse guests evaluate AI-enabled encounters is critical. This study examines how cultural value configurations shape evaluations of service robots in hotels. Cultural value configurations are coherent combinations of orientations that jointly influence how individuals interpret and assess service encounters. Using more than 3000 robot-related hotel reviews from guests across 77 countries, we integrate Hofstede's dimensions with Schwartz's value theory to explain cross-cultural differences in sentiment. Masculinity and uncertainty avoidance predict more negative sentiment, individualism shows a positive association that is sensitive to model specification, and power distance shows no direct effect. One configuration is robust: masculinity combined with uncertainty avoidance amplifies dissatisfaction, and this interaction holds under multilevel and combined estimation and survives correction for multiple testing. Two further configurations remain suggestive: power distance combined with uncertainty avoidance attenuates risk aversion, and individualism combined with masculinity increases tolerance for imperfection. Both are marginal and do not persist under multilevel or joint estimation, so we report them as patterns for replication rather than as established effects. Hofstede's indices provide the measurement, while Schwartz's value theory serves as an interpretive lens rather than as a measured individual-level construct. Findings position culture as a configurational system and provide guidance for AI service design and communication. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Classification of motor imagery EEG signals using CNN–Transformer hybrid models
Abstract: Motor imagery-based brain–computer interfaces aim to translate electroencephalographic activity into control commands without requiring overt movement. However, strong inter-subject variability, exacerbated by the limited spatial resolution of compact electrode montages, makes subject-independent decoding particularly challenging. This work presents a compact hybrid convolutional neural network–Transformer architecture designed for stable binary left/right motor imagery decoding using a low-density eight-channel sensorimotor montage. The model integrates convolutional feature extraction with a parameter-efficient temporal self-attention mechanism to capture both localized spatiotemporal patterns and long-range temporal dependencies in the electroencephalographic signal. Under strict subject-wise five-fold cross-validation on the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery dataset, the proposed convolutional neural network–Transformer achieved a mean macro F1-score of 0.816. Moreover, the statistical analysis revealed no significant performance difference (p>0.05) relative to larger architectural variants, thus justifying the selection of the proposed compact model for its computational efficiency and scalability. With only 0.232 million parameters and approximately 0.034 giga-floating-point operations per forward pass, the proposed convolutional neural network–Transformer constitutes a compact and resource-efficient backbone that supports low-latency subject-independent motor imagery decoding under low-density EEG. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Livelihood and production stabilization following state land recovery in Vietnam: A qualitative legal study of Thanh Hoa Province
Abstract: This study examined the legal framework and documented implementation of support for livelihood and production stabilization following State land recovery in Thanh Hoa Province, Vietnam. It aimed to clarify national eligibility rules, forms and levels of support, provincial implementation arrangements, and the main legal and administrative gaps. A qualitative legal research design was used, combining doctrinal legal analysis, documentary analysis, and descriptive analysis of secondary administrative data. The materials included the Constitution of 2013, the Land Law 2024, relevant national decrees and resolutions, provincial legal instruments, published studies, and three unpublished internal administrative reports covering 2023-2025. The findings show that Vietnamese law distinguishes support from compensation and resettlement and provides measures for livelihood stabilization, production and business stabilization, vocational training, occupational transition, job-search assistance, and resettlement-related needs. Thanh Hoa has specified several support levels and procedures through provincial instruments. However, the framework is more explicit about eligibility, calculation rules, payment levels, and administrative procedures than about longer-term livelihood outcomes. The administrative reports document a substantial site-clearance workload, but they do not provide sufficient information on payment timeliness, employment after training, income restoration, production continuity, or support-related complaints. The study therefore cannot determine the substantive effectiveness of the support measures. Clearer criteria are needed for special cases, together with reasoned decision-making, meaningful participation, livelihood and vocational assistance that extends beyond cash-based support and is linked to local labor demand, and reporting indicators that distinguish administrative progress from sustainable livelihood restoration. Because the study relied on legal and documentary materials from one province and did not collect primary data from affected persons, its findings should be interpreted cautiously. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: A graph model for conflict resolution incorporating movement willingness intensity under linguistic uncertainty
Abstract: In the graph model for conflict resolution (GMCR), decision-makers (DMs) are required to express their preferences over feasible conflict states. Under uncertainty, however, such preferences are often difficult to quantify precisely and are more naturally represented by linguistic preference relations. To address this issue, this study develops a linguistic GMCR framework. Four linguistic stability concepts, namely linguistic Nash stability, linguistic sequential stability, linguistic symmetric metarationality, and linguistic general metarationality, are defined in logical form for general multi-DM conflicts. Corresponding matrix-based representations are then derived to facilitate stability computation. To capture heterogeneity in DMs’ willingness to transition between states, the framework is further extended by introducing a two-degree linguistic preference structure with two flexible formulations of the linguistic satisficing threshold. This extension distinguishes strong and mild transition willingness and yields three classes of linguistic stability, namely general linguistic stability, strong linguistic stability, and weak linguistic stability. The proposed framework is applied to the Elmira groundwater contamination conflict to demonstrate its practical applicability. Sensitivity and comparative analyses show that the two-degree linguistic framework identifies differentiated stability patterns that cannot be captured by single-threshold approaches, thereby providing a more refined basis for conflict diagnosis and resolution under linguistic uncertainty and heterogeneous transition willingness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Yang Q.; Lu K.; Fang X.
Title: MAGE: A structural-prior-guided graph-language multimodal framework for business process anomaly detection
Abstract: Business process event logs record activities, resources, timestamps, and other process attributes, and therefore provide the basis for trace-level anomaly detection. Existing methods often lack a unified reference for normal behavior and do not explicitly coordinate structural deviations with semantic information. We propose MAGE, a structural-prior-guided graph-enhanced language embedding framework for business process anomaly detection. MAGE first constructs structural priors solely from normal traces in the training set, including normal directly-follows relations, trace-length statistics, and adjacent-event resource-switching statistics. It then compares each trace with these priors to generate structural deviation signals and constructs both an activity-resource-time-slice heterogeneous graph and a structure-aware textual representation. A heterogeneous graph Transformer extracts structural representations, while a LoRA-adapted Qwen3 model extracts semantic representations. Gated cross-attention fuses the two modalities for trace-level anomaly classification. The structural prior and graph self-supervised pretraining use only normal training traces, whereas the final multimodal classifier is jointly optimized on labeled training samples. Experiments on synthetic logs and public real event logs with controlled anomaly injection show that MAGE achieves the highest mean F1-scores of 0.872 and 0.860, respectively, among the compared methods under the evaluated settings. Ablation results further indicate that the structural prior, heterogeneous graph encoding, structure-aware prompting, and cross-modal fusion each contribute positively to F1-score under the evaluated settings. Together, these findings provide evidence for combining normal-process structural constraints with language-based semantic information in trace-level business process anomaly detection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zhang Q.; Li Q.; Li Z.; Gan K.
Title: From generative AI usage to entrepreneurial intention: The sequential roles of task and social self-efficacy
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is rapidly evolving and creating new possibilities for supporting students' entrepreneurial development. However, limited research has examined how GAI usage is associated with entrepreneurial intention (EI) through specific psychological pathways. Drawing on self-efficacy theory, this study examines the relationship between GAI usage and EI, focusing on the mediating roles of task and social self-efficacy. Using survey data from 521 Chinese university students, this study empirically tests the proposed model. The results show that GAI usage is positively associated with students' task and social self-efficacy. However, task self-efficacy (TSE) is not directly associated with EI. In contrast, social self-efficacy (SSE) accounts for a significant indirect association between GAI usage and EI. Moreover, a significant sequential indirect association is observed, linking GAI usage with EI through TSE and SSE. By disentangling the distinct roles of TSE and SSE, this study shows that the association between GAI usage and EI is consistent with pathways that differ in their functions and proximity to entrepreneurial action. The findings also provide practical insights for entrepreneurship education and AI-supported learning environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Gao L.; Li S.-C.
Title: What Strategies Can Payers Use to Negotiate Medicine Prices Globally? Insights and Lessons for Low-Income Countries from a Scoping Review
Abstract: Objectives No comprehensive global review has synthesized mechanisms, strengths, limitations, and implementation challenges of pharmaceutical pricing policies. This scoping review aimed to examine global pharmaceutical pricing policies and generate policy-relevant insights, particularly for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Methods Electronic searches were conducted in Medline, CINAHL, EconLit, and Embase using predefined inclusion criteria. Gray literature was identified through government publications and World Health Organization reports, and reference lists of relevant studies were screened. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review framework and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews guidelines. Results Searches conducted up to May 2024 and updated in February 2026 identified 88 eligible studies. Reference pricing was the most commonly reported strategy, used in 85% of identified countries, offering simplicity and transparency through price benchmarking. Value-based pricing was widely adopted in high-income countries, aligning prices with health outcomes but requiring strong health technology assessment infrastructure. Managed entry agreements were reported in 56% of countries and were used to improve access to new medicines while mitigating financial risk. Indication-specific pricing was implemented in 9 countries but faced operational challenges. Compulsory licensing in several LMICs improved access to essential medicines at lower cost, although concerns regarding impacts on pharmaceutical innovation were noted. Most countries combined multiple pricing approaches to balance affordability, access, and innovation. Conclusions Although value-based pricing and managed entry agreements are common in high-income settings, simpler approaches such as reference pricing and compulsory licensing may be more feasible in LMICs. Context-specific strategies are needed to balance access, affordability, and sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: From waste to Watts: Causal evidence on AI-enabled waste-to-energy and financial performance in tourism and hospitality using an empirics-first investigation
Abstract: This study examines whether artificial intelligence enabled waste to energy adoption improves financial performance in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms and identifies the mechanisms and conditions shaping these effects. Using an empirics first mixed methods design, we combine interviews with 41 managers and a firm year panel of United Kingdom listed tourism, travel, and hospitality firms from 2015 to 2025. Difference in differences models with firm and year fixed effects show that adoption is associated with significantly higher financial performance, particularly at greater levels of adoption intensity. The findings indicate that energy cost savings and operational efficiency partially explain these gains. Performance benefits are also stronger in firms with higher baseline waste intensity and during periods of elevated energy prices. The study demonstrates that AI enabled waste to energy functions as an operational capability that can generate measurable economic value when integrated into organisational routines and governance systems. © 2026 The Author.

Title: Chefs, kitchens, and stars: A literature review of fine dining in hospitality and management studies
Abstract: Fine dining represents a niche within the restaurant industry, yet it has garnered significant attention from both scholars and practitioners. Fine dining, due to its distinctive characteristics - such as extreme creativity and innovation, adherence to strict institutional logics, a rigorous system of social evaluation from customers and critics, and the juxtaposition of artistic logics and commercial logics - is a compelling setting for hospitality and management scholars. However, fine dining literature is quite fragmented. Drawing on a thematic analysis of 101 articles, this literature review provides scholars with five thematic clusters that emerged: (1) Work environment and career path; (2) Creativity and innovation; (3) Social evaluation and institutional logics; (4) Customer experience and engagement; (5) Entrepreneurship and business model innovation. Moreover, by presenting tensions among the clusters and illustrating gaps and opportunities in the methodological approach, this literature review develops a prospective research agenda for hospitality and management scholars. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Understanding the mixed consequences of diversity practices: A typology of migrant employees
Abstract: Organizational diversity practices are widely implemented to support the workplace integration of international migrants (IMs), yet their outcomes remain inconsistent. Little is known about why IMs respond differently to the same initiatives offered by their organizations or why these practices sometimes fail or backfire. Drawing on signaling and attribution theory, we argue that IMs interpret diversity practices through the lens of two key disadvantages: unfamiliarity with the destination country and exposure to discrimination within this context. We develop a dual disadvantage typology of IMs and theorize how resource and nondiscrimination practices differentially affect organizational commitment depending on migrants’ disadvantage configurations. This typology refines existing diversity frameworks by introducing a configurational view of migrant diversity and explaining why identical practices may produce divergent outcomes. Using survey data from 394 IMs working in Germany, we find that while nondiscrimination practices are consistently positively associated with commitment, the effects of resource practices vary: some IMs view them as empowering, while others interpret them as stigmatizing or misaligned with their needs. In particular, training initiatives can backfire for IMs who are already familiar with the labor market and face discrimination. Our findings demonstrate the importance of tailoring initiatives to different migrant groups. We contribute a theory-driven framework that explains how diversity signals are differentially interpreted across migrant disadvantage configurations and when diversity practices produce intended versus unintended effects. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Jiang L.; Liu Y.; Zhao H.
Title: Spatial trajectories and land-use potential of China's utility-scale photovoltaic expansion toward 2035
Abstract: China aims to reach 3600 GW of combined wind and solar capacity by 2035, requiring substantial expansion of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) deployment. Quantifying the geospatial footprint of this expansion is essential for sustainable land-use planning and ecological protection. This study develops a nationwide assessment framework that integrates multi-source remote sensing observations, Random Forest (RF) suitability modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for model interpretation, and scenario-based spatial allocation. Historical PV data from 2000 to 2025 show that China's utility-scale PV farms expanded to 13,800 km2, with growth concentrated in northwestern mega-bases and emerging decentralized installations in central-eastern regions, indicating a dual-track spatial trajectory. Scenario projections suggest that Scenario B (NDC Update-Aligned Pathway) requires an additional 21,420 km2, whereas Scenario C (Wind-Slowdown Compensation) increases land demand moderately to 24,405 km2. Scenario A (Business as Usual) could require up to 63,990 km2 and would disproportionately affect croplands and forests. However, China retains more than 206,000 km2 of high-potential land, indicating that ecological conflicts are driven mainly by spatial mismatch rather than absolute land scarcity. These findings underscore the need for integrated spatial governance, optimized ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transmission, and distributed PV deployment. By linking observed spatial trajectories, interpretable suitability modeling, and capacity-to-land translation, this study provides a transferable framework for assessing the land-use potential of utility-scale PV expansion toward 2035. © 2026

Title: Efficient nonconvex low-rank tensor recovery with a new t-fraction function penalty
Abstract: In recent years, low-rank tensor recovery has become an essential technique in computer vision and machine learning with many important applications, such as color image denoising, video recovery, and subspace clustering. Existing approaches typically leverage convex or nonconvex surrogates to approximate the intractable tensor rank. However, many of these methods treat rank components uniformly, neglecting their differential structural importance and thus leading to suboptimal reconstruction. To alleviate this issue, in this paper we propose a novel nonconvex fractional function that serves as a tighter and more adaptive surrogate for the tensor multi-rank. Unlike existing weighted schemes, the proposed function facilitates adaptive penalization of singular values without the need for heuristic weight assignment. With it, a principled low-rank minimization model is formulated to more faithfully characterize the intrinsic low-rank structures of tensors. Meanwhile, we develop an efficient algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), where each subproblem admits an analytical closed-form solution. Moreover, the convergence of the proposed algorithm is rigorously established through theoretical analysis. Extensive experimental results on both synthetic and real-world data demonstrate that our method achieves significant advantages over several state-of-the-art low-rank tensor recovery methods. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Uncorrelated Inequalities: A Multiproxy Measure for Household Archaeology
Source title: Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory
Abstract: Inequality has received increased attention in the social sciences since the 1990s, in part because of the harm it causes and because massive inequality is avoidable. Bolstered by the Gini coefficient, a quantitative measure of unevenness in a distribution that enhances comparative studies across time and space, archaeologists have expanded the study of inequality in recent years. Many of these investigations use multiple variables to assess inequality. A challenge of such multi-proxy studies is that simply averaging Gini coefficients for multiple variables can over-represent inequality in societies where variables for inequality are not correlated. This paper provides an experimental measure—the Domain Sensitivity Gini (DSG)—and applies it to a sample of Maya archaeological case studies with extensive domestic excavations. The DSG helps disambiguate societies where wealth variables are aligned from societies where such variables are not aligned. In cases where variables do not align, different forms of wealth are not strongly correlated: a household that is poor in one domain might be wealthy in other domains. The DSG also suggests that inequality is lower than estimates based on averaged variables. This finding is valuable when set within a broader comparative context because it shows that high inequality seen today is not natural and that ancient case studies are relevant. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Critical minerals and the U.S. industrial strategy: resource security, environmental justice, and the contradictions of decarbonization
Abstract: The United States has rapidly implemented a critical minerals industrial policy to support the clean energy transition and to advance national and economic security, using the Inflation Reduction Act, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and Defense Production Act to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce reliance on China. This review examines whether this strategy represents decarbonization, a new phase of green industrial policy, green extractivism, a geopolitical resource-security approach, or a contradictory project that advances climate goals while perpetuating inequalities. Drawing on 65 peer-reviewed articles, books, and policy reports, the Critical Minerals Justice Dilemma framework clarifies persistent tensions among decarbonization, supply security, industrial competitiveness, environmental justice, and geopolitical resilience. Evidence from Indigenous sovereignty research, conflict mapping in the Americas, and political economy analysis shows that U.S. policy accelerates green extractivism, overrides Tribal consent through crisis-driven measures, uses techno-legal solutions that undermine democratic governance, and shifts environmental and social burdens to Global South sacrifice zones. The analysis identifies three main gaps: limited theorization of racial capitalism and settler colonialism in domestic contexts, insufficient attention to epistemic justice, and a lack of demand-side political economy. The findings suggest techno-optimistic views on green transitions do not address structural inequalities. Achieving a just strategy requires prioritizing Free, Prior, and Informed Consent, Indigenous co-governance, and demand reduction as central political imperatives rather than technical solutions. Title: MCA-SSL: A synergistic fusion-optimization-alignment loop for incomplete multi-view clustering
Abstract: The missing of views in multi-view data brings challenges to multi-view clustering, such as how to deal with missing views, how to fuse cross-view information, and how to learn clustering-oriented representation. To address these, we propose MCA-SSL, a free-imputation model for incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC). MCA-SSL integrates mutual cross-attention mechanism (MCA), self-supervised learning (SSL), and global representation and label learning (GRLL), where MCA aims to fuse view-specific representations in a two-way mode for extracting cross-view complementary information in more detail, SSL focuses on optimizing the fused representation by combing contrastive and predictive learning for improving the quality of the view-specific representations, and GRLL is responsible for unifying the feature learning with the clustering task in a framework though contrasting the global representation and pseudo-label with view-specific representations and pseudo-labels for promoting clustering-oriented representations and improving clustering performance. The missing values of samples are initialized by random values, and their representations are iteratively optimized by SSL, which alleviates the difficulty of directly filling the missing values in original data space and enhances the robustness to view incompleteness. The entire process forms a “fusion-optimization-alignment” synergistic loop, providing an integrated learning framework and end-to-end trainable paradigm for IMVC. Extensive experiments on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that MCA-SSL significantly outperforms baselines. More importantly, ablation studies confirm that the performance gain stems from the effective collaboration, not merely the juxtaposition of its key components. Title: International scaling of social innovations through digitalization: A 3D framework
Abstract: Social enterprises that embed social innovations (SIs) play a critical role in advancing the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), representing an estimated US$12 trillion market opportunity. Yet, how SIs internationalize in the presence of institutional voids remains underexplored in international business research. Using a history-to-theory and history-in-theory approach, this study examines how dynamic capabilities and digitalization enable the international scaling of SIs. We find that international diffusion depends on capabilities such as boundary spanning, international sensing, legitimacy building, business diplomacy, and market shaping. Digitalization accelerates scaling, contingent on factors including timing, resources, intellectual property ownership, purpose, and technology scope. Our findings also suggest that traditional internationalization metrics—such as exports, FDI, subsidiaries, and foreign sales—do not adequately capture SI internationalization. Instead, internationalization is reflected in the cross-border diffusion of innovations and social impact, alongside the ability to attract international funding, partnerships, talent, and legitimacy while balancing social impact with financial sustainability. Title: Exploring the key drivers of biogas adoption: a business model for livestock farmers in developing countries
Abstract: The increasing number of livestock farms, coupled with inadequate waste management infrastructure, has become a growing concern, contributing to environmental pollution and productivity loss. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the key factors influencing the adoption intention of biogas technology as a business Model among livestock farmers. Employing a purposive sampling approach, this study gathered data from 336 livestock farmers. To ensure a comprehensive analysis, a combined methodological framework integrating both symmetric and asymmetric techniques was utilized, providing a profound understanding of the determinants impacting the intention to adopt biogas technology. This study observes a notable consistency between the findings derived from PLS-SEM and ANN. The analysis indicates that awareness of consequences (AOC) significantly influences ascription of responsibility (AOR). Additionally, findings indicate that personal norms are significantly shaped by herd mentality, initial cost, AOC, AOR, and self-esteem. Furthermore, herd mentality, personal norms, and self-esteem are significantly associated with biogas adoption. However, no significant association was found between perceived ease of use and personal norms. Meanwhile, findings from the fsQCA revealed eight distinct pathways leading to a strong intention to adopt biogas, highlighting herd mentality and AOC as critical prerequisites. Title: The role of deontological morality in shaping demand within the sharing economy

Abstract: This study examines how deontological and consequentialist appeals in Airbnb host self-descriptions relate to trust-related attention and marketplace performance. Authors: Li Z.; Ma M.; Yavuz M.
Title: Reservation-based intersection scheduling using dynamic programming with dominance pruning
Abstract: Scheduling connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) at reservation-based intersections faces a fundamental trade-off: existing methods sacrifice either optimality for computational efficiency or real-time applicability for optimal solutions. We bridge this gap by proposing a dynamic programming (DP) algorithm with dominance pruning ((Formula presented.)) that simultaneously achieves optimal batch formation, polynomial-time complexity, and superior solution quality. (Formula presented.) introduces a novel dominance rule that eliminates suboptimal child nodes by comparing analytically derived lower bounds, enabling batch-based processing of CAVs while guaranteeing optimality. Unlike existing approaches that assume predetermined batches or sacrifice optimality, (Formula presented.) integrates optimal batching decisions directly into the scheduling algorithm. The proposed method achieves a substantial improvement over existing exact algorithms with (Formula presented.) worst-case and (Formula presented.) best-case time complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that (Formula presented.) reduces computation time by 91% and 99% compared to a state-of-the-art DP algorithm and Gurobi solver, respectively, while consistently delivering superior performance in makespan, average delay, and maximum delay metrics across diverse traffic scenarios. Furthermore, (Formula presented.) outperforms heuristic algorithms in achieving better solution quality and comparative computational efficiency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that (Formula presented.) ’s dominance rule remains effective across varying mean headways, CAV counts, and batch proportions, with performance benefits extending beyond simple batch processing to complex traffic patterns. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: Factors associated with perceived frugal-innovation capability in traditional craft villages: A respondent-level PLS-SEM study in Hanoi, Vietnam
Abstract: Frugal innovation is increasingly treated as a capability for developing affordable, resource-efficient, and context-appropriate solutions, yet its antecedents remain fragmented across the literature and are insufficiently examined in community-embedded craft production. This study evaluates two connected sets of respondent-level associations in traditional craft villages in Hanoi, Vietnam. The resource-recombination route links perceived empowering leadership, knowledge management, organic innovative culture, and network embeddedness with bricolage and, in turn, perceived frugal-innovation capability. The institution-market route links network embeddedness with perceived government support, perceived customer requirements, customer participation, and frugal-innovation capability. A cross-sectional survey produced 432 returned questionnaires; 416 retained cases were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). All constructs are interpreted as respondents’ perceptions of practices and conditions in their focal production or business units rather than as objective organization-level measures. Bricolage had the largest direct association with perceived frugal-innovation capability (β = 0.441), and empowering leadership had the largest association with bricolage (β = 0.492). Network embeddedness was associated with several specific indirect routes, while perceived government support was associated with frugal-innovation capability both directly and through customer-facing constructs. The model explained 52.5% of the adjusted variance in perceived frugal-innovation capability. The findings support a resource-conversion interpretation centered on bricolage, but the cross-sectional, single-source design does not establish temporal mediation or causal effects. Title: Navigating travel paradoxes: Gen Z coping responses and implications for destination management
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Paradoxes involve contradictory yet interdependent poles that persist rather than disappearing when one side is chosen. Tourism routinely exposes travelers to such tensions, but traveler-level paradoxes and the responses used to navigate them remain underexamined. Using the early tourism-recovery period of 2022 as the empirical context, this study examines paradoxical tensions perceived by young adult Gen Z student travelers and how they respond to them. A two-stage qualitative design was employed. Study A recruited 98 Norwegian Gen Z student travelers, of whom 95 provided useable responses; Study B recruited 48 Gen Z student travelers from the United Kingdom and the United States, of whom 46 provided useable responses. Online open-ended essays were analyzed using thematic analysis, with constant comparison used as an iterative coding technique. Four persistent traveler-perceived tensions emerged: personal travel fulfillment versus environmental responsibility, community economic benefit versus community livability, business recovery versus service-capacity strain, and travel maximization versus travel restraint. Responses clustered into four types: integrative or balancing, prioritization, avoidance or resignation, and externalization or delegation. These responses did not permanently resolve the paradoxes; instead, they temporarily stabilized the tension, privileged one pole, reproduced it, or displaced responsibility. The study therefore positions the 2022 recovery period as an external intensifying condition that made enduring tensions especially visible and connects traveler paradox management to destination governance and shared responsibility. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Enhancing wind energy forecasting under constrained data conditions: a CRISP-DM-based deep neural network approach
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of wind energy production plays a crucial role in the efficient operation of energy markets. However, many advanced models depend on extensive datasets and detailed meteorological information that are rarely available in industrial environments. This work investigates short-term wind power forecasting under constrained industrial conditions, including limited data availability, incomplete high-resolution meteorological information, and noisy operational measurements. A Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM)-based workflow is adopted to support data preprocessing, model training, and validation throughout the forecasting process. An openly available dataset containing hourly records from multiple European wind farms is used, focusing on a single wind farm subset to evaluate forecasting performance under realistic single-site deployment conditions. A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model combined with lag-based and nonlinear feature engineering techniques is implemented to capture operational relationships without relying on complete external meteorological fields. Experimental results show that feedforward architectures can provide competitive forecasting performance under constrained data scenarios. The findings highlight the importance of balancing model complexity, data availability, robust validation, and deployability in real-world wind energy forecasting applications. © 2026

Authors: Xu X.; Jiang G.; Huang X.; Chen Q.; Tian Y.; Wen N.
Title: GenAI support to the rescue: Mitigating employees’ psychological stress following tourism service recovery
Abstract: Growing evidence suggests that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has a notable impact on employees' attitudes and behaviors, yet its potential to mitigate psychological stress remains underexplored. Combining conservation of resources (COR) theory with the “computers are social actors” (CASA) paradigm, this study investigates whether and how GenAI support (emotional versus informational) reduces tourism employees' post-recovery psychological stress. The results show that: (1) GenAI support effectively alleviates such stress following tourism service recovery; (2) emotional (vs. informational) support exerts a stronger stress-alleviating effect, which is serially mediated by social presence and emotional energy; (3) framing GenAI as an assistant (vs. a friend) further amplifies the relative effectiveness of emotional over informational support. This study enriches the understanding of GenAI's benefits and extends the workplace support literature. It also offers actionable insights into leveraging digital support tools to manage employee stress in tourism workplaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Ultralow Noise Orthogonal Fluxgates Enabling Weak Magnetic Field and Biomolecular Detection
Abstract: Noninvasive detection of ultra-weak biomagnetic signals is crucial for modern biosensing, but conventional magnetic sensors are fundamentally limited by intrinsic noise. Orthogonal fluxgates (OFGs) enable high signal-to-noise-ratio detection of weak magnetic fields, yet their performance is still constrained by intrinsic 1/f noise and Barkhausen-related magnetic fluctuations. This study reports a low-noise orthogonal fluxgate in which a newly designed magnetic core and circuit mitigate existing noise limitations. The CoP/Ag composite core, featuring an amorphous-nanocrystalline dual phase, is associated with reduced low-frequency magnetic loss and improved noise performance. When integrated with a closed-loop feedback, the sensor achieves a noise floor of 8 pT/√Hz at 1 Hz. The sensor enables reliable detection of ultralow-concentration magnetic-bead signals. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) was used as a model biomarker in an immunomagnetic bead assay, yielding a linear response from 50 fg mL−1 to 100 ng mL−1 and a detection limit of 50 fg mL−1, which compares favorably with representative reported AFP magnetic biosensors. OFGs demonstrate strong prospects in biosensing, geomagnetic measurements, and weak field detection. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: This study compares direct and indirect technology diffusion in higher education, focusing on plagiarism detection software in Indian doctoral education. Title: A mixed-integer linear programming approach to container terminal layout optimization: application to the port of Piraeus
Abstract: This study addresses the issue of designing a container terminal layout by developing a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) mathematical model. The methodology is applied to Pier II of the Piraeus Container Terminal. The mathematical formulation of the problem systematically incorporates real-world spatial constraints and operational factors related to container storage areas, while evaluating alternative scenarios to identify optimal layouts. The methodology considers the geometric and functional characteristics of the terminal, including data related to container handling equipment and the movement of conventional trucks and Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs). The objective function aims to minimize the total operational distance from the berthing positions to the container stacking blocks, thereby enhancing terminal performance. The optimized truck-based configuration reduced the total internal transport distance by 23.1%, while the AGV-based configuration also reduced total internal transport distance by approximately 23% in relation to the existing layout, but it resulted in higher absolute travel distances compared to the truck-based optimal solution. Applying the proposed methodology to real data from the Port of Piraeus shows how alternative layouts can reduce internal transportation distances and enhance operational efficiency. A comparative analysis of alternative scenarios confirms the effectiveness of the proposed solutions, highlighting their potential to significantly improve operational efficiency, while also offering prospects for future research and practical applications. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Production Capacity Forecasting Model: A Data Approach in the Apparel Industry
Abstract: In the clothing industry, a sector facing increasingly stringent demands regarding productivity, costs, and delivery schedules, the application of machine learning to forecast production capacity has become an essential management requirement. This study focuses on developing a production capacity forecasting model by analyzing the interplay between clothing order characteristics and sewing line parameters. The Naive Bayes model provides a probabilistic framework for classifying expected production capacity into distinct levels; consequently, the model’s output offers a clear basis for planners to assess capacity-related risks and make informed decisions regarding resource allocation and line balancing. Title: Start with the end in mind: An interview-based survey and gap analysis of biochar production and selected industrial applications in Europe
Abstract: Biochar occupies a distinctive position among carbon dioxide removal approaches, offering potential carbon storage and functional materials for several industrial sectors. However, technical potential does not by itself establish market integration. We combined two semi-structured interview studies comprising 13 supply-side interviews across nine European countries and 22 application-side interview sessions involving 23 participants. The main analysis covers asphalt, insulation materials, animal feed, biogas and packaging; one additional biofuel-sector interview is retained as contextual evidence. We examined production economics, application requirements and the gaps between them. Supply-side accounts identified feedstock costs, product specifications, energy offtake and carbon-credit revenue as important but configuration-dependent economic factors. Application professionals described barriers involving price–performance relationships, qualification and regulatory requirements, process compatibility and quality variability. These barriers differed within as well as between sectors, and reported trials and finished-product sales qualified a uniformly negative assessment. The findings suggest that production, processing and delivery need to be adapted to the intended end application. Exploratory gap scores and market calculations are reported separately as assumption-dependent tools, not validated rankings or adoption forecasts. Functional benefits may support particular applications, but cannot be assumed to resolve other integration requirements. Carbon-removal demand is likely to remain important for scaling several business models, although the interviews do not establish universal dependence on credits. The study identifies application-specific development priorities and policy options requiring further quantitative evaluation. Authors: Huang T.; Wang W.
Title: Assessment innovation in management education: Authentic assessment evaluation to develop workplace-ready graduates
Abstract: Authentic assessment is increasingly seen as essential in management education for aligning assessment tasks with the complex, collaborative, and uncertain, multi-stakeholder demands of modern workplaces. This paper argues that, despite its popularity, the impact of authentic assessment on graduate preparedness remains poorly understood. To address this, the paper builds and evaluates an integrative model relating authentic assessment design, feedback and reflection, perceptions of assessment value, professional self-efficacy, and perceived workplace outcomes among management students. Drawing on literature about authentic assessment, experiential learning, situated cognition, assessment for learning, and employability, the paper frames authentic assessment as a holistic pedagogical system. A cross-sectional survey of 412 undergraduate and postgraduate students in business and management at four universities provides the empirical basis. The instrument was honed through expert review and a pilot test, and analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and validity checks, correlations, and hierarchical regression and mediation tests. The findings show that authentic assessment design strongly correlates with workplace readiness, especially when dialogic feedback, reflection, and professional self-efficacy are present. External audience group projects, live case analysis, simulations, and portfolio-based evaluation proved effective with clear criteria and guided post-task reflection. The paper contributes a process model and actionable design principles for educators to enhance employability through meaningful assessment, advancing the discourse on management education. © 2026

Title: Impact of substitution on product families’ competition in networked markets
Abstract: The competition among product families supplied by different firms in networked markets is constructed as a bipartite graph model. Based on matrix analysis, the Cournot equilibrium of the product families’ competition is derived. Then, the impact of substitution between product varieties on product families’ competition is analyzed. The results show that when the networked markets were symmetric, the firms’ profits and total consumer surplus all decreased in substitution. But when networked markets are asymmetric, the profits increased in substitution for the firms with a smaller total commonality index or few product varieties, or supplying a segmented market with a larger demand intercept. Even in the asymmetric networked markets, the consumer surplus also decreases in substitution. Title: Multinational dynamic capabilities: How multinational, how dynamic, how capable?
Abstract: The dynamic capabilities perspective is a central framework used to explain how firms adapt, sustain competitive advantages, and/or create new competitive advantages in changing environments. Despite more than three decades of research, important questions remain about the nature, development, deployment, modification, and effectiveness of dynamic capabilities, particularly in multinational contexts. These questions are increasingly salient as multinational enterprises confront technological disruption, geopolitical fragmentation, institutional volatility, and other manifestations of an expanding global polycrisis. Drawing on our review of the evolution of the dynamic capabilities perspective and its extension into international business research, we argue that future research can advance our understanding of the dynamic capabilities construct by addressing three fundamental questions: How multinational are multinational dynamic capabilities? How dynamic are dynamic capabilities? And how capable are dynamic capabilities? Answering these questions requires greater attention to capability configurations and hierarchies, managerial and organizational microfoundations, heterogeneous multinational contexts, capability evolution, and capability measurement. The articles in this special issue advance our understanding of capability development, deployment, orchestration, and reconfiguration across a variety of international settings. They also highlight the importance of context-dependent capability systems and multilevel adaptation. Integrating these insights, we develop a framework for understanding multinational dynamic capabilities and identify directions for future research. We conclude that future progress will depend on developing more precise theories of multinationality, richer explanations of capability evolution, and more rigorous approaches to measure and evaluate multinational dynamic capabilities across contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Time for challenge, money for relaxation: The resource-activity fit in tourism

Abstract: Although money and time are essential resources that influence consumer decision-making, research has mostly ignored how resource concept activation affects tourists' decisions in the context of tourism. Across three experiments, the results show that when the concept of time is activated, tourists report stronger preferences for challenging activities, whereas when the concept of money is activated, they report stronger preferences for relaxing activities. Title: Low-Temperature All-Solid-State Batteries
Abstract: Reliable battery operation in sub-zero environments is critical for polar exploration, military missions, and space applications. However, conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face inherent limitations at low temperatures by intrinsic hurdle of poor ionic mobility in liquid electrolytes. All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), which replace liquid electrolytes with non-flammable and non-freezing solid electrolytes, are considered promising alternatives because these solid electrolytes provide high ionic conductivity at low temperatures, superior temperature stability, and exceptional safety. ASSBs still face practical limitations at extremely low temperatures due to degradation caused by interfacial side reactions and mechanical instabilities that increase resistance and polarization. Addressing these challenges is critical to realize the advantages of ASSBs and enable their practical deployment in low-temperature applications. This review provides an overview of historical developments, critical challenges, and recent progress in advancing the low-temperature performance of ASSBs. The key components of ASSBs, including solid electrolytes, cathodes, and anodes, are systematically investigated to develop strategies for improving ASSBs at low temperatures. By highlighting future perspectives, we emphasize both the potential and necessity of ASSBs to overcome the intrinsic limitations of LIBs and ensure reliable energy storage in harsh environments.
