Title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Fecal Immunochemical Test-based Versus Total Colonoscopy-Based Colorectal Cancer Screening in Japan: A Microsimulation Study
Abstract: Objectives Colorectal cancer is a major public health concern with a high mortality rate. Fecal immunochemical tests (FIT) and total colonoscopy (TCS) are recommended screening methods; however, their cost-effectiveness varies by country. This study addressed the lack of comprehensive cost-effectiveness analyses comparing TCS with the current FIT-based screening in Japan. Methods We developed a microsimulation-based decision analytic model to compare FIT-based screening (current practice) with TCS-based screening (alternative) in a hypothetical cohort of 10 000 Japanese adults over a 60-year period. The analysis was conducted from the healthcare payer perspective, with both costs and health outcomes discounted annually by 2%. We adhered to the 2022 Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards reporting guidelines and incorporated Japan-specific data on costs, participation rates, and disease progression. Results In the base-case analysis, FIT-based screening was more cost-effective than TCS-based screening. TCS-based screening also yielded fewer quality-adjusted life-years, making it the less favorable approach. Sensitivity analyses showed that FIT remained the dominant screening across most parameter variations. Conclusions In Japan, the current FIT-based colorectal cancer screening is more cost-effective than TCS-based screening. Efforts should focus on improving FIT program participation to achieve greater public health benefits, rather than transitioning to a costlier and less effective alternative. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Trustworthy artificial intelligence in advanced manufacturing
Abstract: Additive manufacturing is relying more and more on artificial intelligence for prediction, control, and real-time decisions. Deployment, however, is still difficult. The main reason is that the underlying thermal, flow, and microstructural behavior can shift as the process changes, which makes reliable model performance hard to maintain. This review examines how trustworthy artificial intelligence (TAI) can be used to close that gap in digital twins for additive manufacturing across both metallic and ceramic systems. It frames trustworthiness as a technical condition for deployment and translates it into an AM-specific operational framework. From that point onward, it examines how current workflows handle reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, explainability, robustness, generalizability, fairness, and transparency. A structured evaluation of sixty studies in metallic and ceramic additive manufacturing systems reveals a distinct trend. Robustness and generalizability receive much more attention than transparency, explainability, and fairness. The coverage is also stronger in metallic systems than in ceramic ones. To move beyond binary classification, the review further applies a structured evidence-depth rubric that distinguishes absent coverage, limited or implicit evidence, method-level evidence, and operational evidence for each TAI attribute. We further show that trustworthy deployment depends on more than predictive accuracy. It also depends on physically consistent models as well as updates that account for uncertainty. Decision support has to remain interpretable as well. Model transfer across machines and materials should be treated as controlled adaptation, where reusable physics, sensing, and validation elements are separated from material-specific features that require recalibration. The validation path must also support qualification and industrial deployment, leading to a more cohesive digital twin framework. It brings together physics-based models, reduced-order models, learning-based surrogates, multimodal sensing, and trust-aware evaluation. The main finding is that trustworthiness is the missing technical link between digital twins that can be confidently used in advanced manufacturing and promising AI-enabled demonstrations. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Muthia A.; Utari D.; Soesilo T.E.B.
Title: Environmental health conditions associated with childhood stunting during the first 1000 days of life
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Child stunting is increasingly recognized not only as a nutritional disorder but also as a complex environmental health issue. Household environmental determinants, particularly safe potable water and advanced sanitation infrastructure, exert a fundamental influence on minimizing children's susceptibility to environmental health hazards that compromise linear growth trajectories. Using the transtheoretical model as a behavioral framework, the study objectives were to examine how household environmental conditions, including access to improved drinking water and sanitation, together with maternal environmental health-related behaviors, are associated with child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life in Indonesia. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the fifth wave of the Indonesian Family Life Survey. Maternal behaviors related to nutrition, healthcare utilization, and environmental conditions were operationalized as proxies for advanced stages of behavioral change. Child stunting was defined using height-for-age z-scores based on the World Health Organization Child Growth Standards. A binary logistic regression model was utilized to evaluate the multivariate associations linking maternal behavioral patterns, socio-environmental covariates, and socio-demographic indicators to the latent risk of linear growth retardation in children. FINDINGS: The prevalence of stunting among children aged 0 to 23 months was 30.32 percent. Low birth weight and higher birth order significantly increased the odds of stunting. Maternal behaviors reflecting progression to the action and maintenance stages were protective, including routine antenatal care attendance, with an odds ratio of 0.642, and delivery assisted by a skilled birth attendant, with an odds ratio of 0.707. Findings indicate that higher maternal educational attainment, improved sanitation facilities, and safe drinking water sources significantly decreased the likelihood of stunting. In contrast, maternal under nutrition elevated the associated risk by 26.5 percent. CONCLUSION: Household environmental conditions constitute fundamental determinants of child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. Maternal progression toward advanced stages of stunting prevention behavior, reinforced by adequate health services and enabling environments, plays a critical role in reducing stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. The findings underscore the efficacy of the transtheoretical model as a robust conceptual paradigm for mitigating childhood stunting. By integrating maternal behavioral stages of change with healthcare access and environmental determinants, the research delineates a nuanced, stage-sensitive and contextually grounded architecture for analyzing early childhood growth dynamics. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Framing hotel strategies for demand uncertainty: The asymmetric effects of cancellation policies and F&B incentives
Abstract: This study examines how hotels manage demand uncertainty through two contrasting strategies: cancellation policies as loss-framed uncertainty reduction tools and food and beverage incentives as gain-framed coping mechanisms. Drawing on prospect theory, we argue that these approaches generate asymmetric behavioral responses with distinct temporal and revenue implications. The findings show that loss-framed uncertainty reduction initially suppresses demand by discouraging price-sensitive and uncertain customers; however, this negative effect is largely confined to the rooms department and diminishes over time. In contrast, gain-framed coping strategies stimulate in-stay consumption, encouraging guests to engage with additional hotel services and generating positive spillover effects that enhance revenue and profitability across other departments, including in subsequent periods. Overall, uncertainty reduction filters out volatile demand, whereas uncertainty coping enhances perceived value and stimulates consumption. These results underscore the importance of considering both temporal dynamics and cross-departmental effects when designing strategies to manage demand uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From Screening to Site Control: Phytic-Acid Mediated P-Tuning of M–N Coordination to Balance Iodine Adsorption and Stability in Zn–I2 Batteries
Abstract: Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries (AZIBs) show promise for grid-scale energy storage, but they are hampered by polyiodide shuttling, sluggish iodine redox kinetics, and irreversible active-site poisoning caused by uncontrolled adsorption. We provide a comprehensive screening of M1 (M1 = P, S, B) heteroatom dopants, and P is identified as the best candidate for achieving coordination-tuned, moderate adsorption that balances adsorption and catalytic activity while mitigating site poisoning. Using phytic acid as both the P source and an etchant, we create a universal in situ approach to core–shell single-atom catalysts (M2-P-CSNC, M2 = Fe, Co, Ni). The unique core–shell structure achieves stable confinement of polyiodides, rapid ion transport, and protection of active sites, while in situ P doping precisely regulates the local electronic environment and d-band center of the Fe–Nx active centers. In situ characterization confirms that Fe–P-CSNC has a strong reversible anchoring ability for polyiodides, which can significantly accelerate redox kinetics. The optimized Fe–P-CSNC/I2 exhibits almost no capacity decay after 20,000 cycles at a current density of 2 A g−1. This work’s facile heteroatom doping strategy for electronic modulation offers a reference for high-performance catalyst design in conversion-type energy storage systems. (Figure presented.) Title: Thermo-reversible bigels stabilized by soluble dietary fiber extracted from microwave-treated okara: Molecular interactions, network rearrangement, and application in mayonnaise
Abstract: This study investigates the preparation and structural regulation of thermo-reversible bigels composed of soluble dietary fiber from microwave-treated okara (M-SDF) hydrogels and carnauba wax/sunflower seed oil oleogels, evaluating their application in low-fat mayonnaise. Carnauba wax was introduced as the oleogelator to structure the oil phase, with its crystalline matrix largely determining the mechanical properties and thermal reversibility of the bigels, while M-SDF served as a macromolecular stabilizer to structure the hydrogel phase and enhance interfacial stability. Microwave pre-treatment altered the molecular characteristics of okara SDF, leading to altered monosaccharide composition, enhanced thermal stability and increased crystallinity, driven by strengthened hydrogen bonding and a more ordered network arrangement. Using variable-temperature FTIR and rheological temperature sweeps, the microstructure and phase transition of the bigels were systematically characterized. The spectral and structural responses were highly dependent on the oleogel-to-hydrogel ratio, with the 7:3 bigel exhibiting pronounced thermal reversibility. Temperature elevation intensified bands at 3677 and 1041 cm−1, indicating the progressive weakening of intermolecular interactions and interfacial rearrangement. Rheological measurements confirmed that the optimized bigels possessed elevated storage modulus (G′ up to 4.65 × 103 Pa) and high phase transition temperature (Tgel of 85.87 °C), supporting a mechanically robust matrix. Incorporating these bigels into mayonnaise significantly improved textural properties and viscoelastic behaviors, demonstrating their effectiveness as a clean-label structuring and stabilizing agent. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Solar Photovoltaic Adoption in East Java Non-Profit Organizations
Abstract: Non-profit organizations in East Java need dependable electricity for service continuity, daily operations, and cost control, yet face capital, regulatory, behavioral, and tropical-climate barriers to rooftop solar photovoltaic adoption. This study combines a focused literature review, bibliometric mapping of 25 verified domain studies selected from 79 unique Scopus records, a random-effects synthesis of five Global Solar Atlas locations, and a 50,000-iteration Monte Carlo model for a common 12 kWp system. The 25 studies met predefined adoption, finance/policy, governance/behavior, and tropical-performance criteria and passed metadata verification. Modeled annual output ranges from 17.231 to 18.227 MWh; pooled yield is 4.03 kWh/kWp/day (95% CI: 3.92–4.14). Median NPV is IDR 40.7–54.9 million, with a conditional positive-NPV probability of 86.4–92.5%. Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate, tariff escalation, capital cost, avoided electricity value, and self-consumption as the dominant drivers of NPV. The five-city results are screening evidence, not a representation of all tropical climates or roofs. A 30% grant or blended-finance contribution raises positive-NPV probability above 99.8% and reduces median payback to 5.8–6.2 years. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. All rights reserved.

Authors: Liu C.; Tao R.; Guo J.
Title: Developing and validating a scenario-based evaluation framework for age-friendly IPTV services
Source title: Universal Access in the Information Society
Abstract: As population aging and digital transformation advance, IPTV has become an important media platform for older adults. However, mismatches between interface design and older users’ capabilities continue to limit effective use. This study develops and validates a contextualized evaluation framework for age-friendly IPTV services. Policy review, interviews with older users, and regional case analysis were conducted to identify eight typical IPTV usage scenarios and construct an initial indicator pool. A two-round Delphi consultation refined the framework, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) determined indicator weights. The final framework comprises five primary dimensions and 22 secondary indicators. Evaluation of three provincial IPTV projects showed that security management, functional operation, and service quality are the highest priorities for improving user experience, whereas content format and product characteristics support initial adoption. Interviews further revealed that limited stakeholder coordination and delays between user feedback and system updates constrain age-friendly implementation. The proposed framework quantifies the alignment between older users’ capabilities and large-screen interaction while tracing usability problems to specific usage contexts. It also informs optimization through hierarchical support, progressive capability support, and social support mechanisms. The scenario-based indicators can be adapted to local technical infrastructures, service processes, and user behaviors, supporting localized application across diverse large-screen media ecosystems. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: How have flight operations between China and Europe changed since the Russia–Ukraine war?
Abstract: This study examines how direct flight services between China and Europe changed during the COVID-19 pandemic and after the Russia–Ukraine war began in February 2022. We use monthly airport pair–airline data from January 2014 to September 2024. Our baseline model is a panel regression with route fixed effects. As a robustness check, we also estimate a two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) specification with route and period fixed effects. After February 2022, passenger traffic fell and yields rose on the sampled routes, and these changes differed between European and Chinese carriers. In the baseline route fixed-effects model, European carriers had approximately 32.7% lower revenue passenger miles and 14.4% lower yields than Chinese carriers during the war period, relative to pre-war differences. The TWFE specification gives interaction estimates of similar sign and magnitude. These differences arose at the same time as the closure of Russian airspace to European carriers and are consistent with the longer routings that other studies document, together with other concurrent factors. During the COVID-19 period, passenger traffic fell sharply. Yields rose in the pooled sample but not in either travel direction separately, which is consistent with unequal travel demand in the two directions. Taken together, these findings highlight persistent vulnerabilities in the China–Europe aviation market and point to potential airline strategies, including greater operational flexibility, service enhancements, code-sharing arrangements, and bilateral coordination, that may strengthen market resilience. Title: Inclusive education as organizational inclusion: Creating inclusive business schools through co-curricular learning
Abstract: Knowing how to create inclusive business schools is crucial for the development of leaders navigating the workforce. This research examines co-curricular First-Year Experience (FYE) programming as an approach to supporting student integration, learning, and experiences. Using a quasi-experimental design, two studies examined academic performance and perceived transition success, belonging, self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and time management behaviours across in-person and online learning contexts. In Study 1, in-person students demonstrated higher academic performance and perceived transition success than online students. At the end of the semester, online and in-person students were comparable in outcome expectations, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management. General belonging was lower among online students across the two measurement occasions however, this difference was already present at baseline and did not change significantly over time. General belonging, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management were positively associated with perceived transition success, whereas outcome expectations were not a significant unique correlate. Study 2 identified exploratory within-format patterns across co-curricular in-person, bespoke in-person, and bespoke online course formats, with university belonging emerging as a significant correlate of perceived transition success across all three. Together, these findings position co-curricular and bespoke FYE approaches as promising frameworks for supporting inclusive business education while highlighting the central role of belonging in students’ transition experiences. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Navigating the successful digital transformation of correctional services: Challenges, good governance, and a hybrid framework
Abstract: Digital transformation initiatives are essential for advancing correctional services toward digital maturity in Macao. However, the absence of a well-defined overarching strategy presents a significant impediment to the effective implementation of reforms. Due to the fact that the intelligent construction of the penal system has not yet been integrated with the extant eGovernment, the governance of the correctional system and its capabilities necessitate rigorous enhancement. Good governance encompasses legitimacy, accountability, transparency, capacity, fairness, responsiveness, participation, and consensus, which are widely considered core principles of public administration and are well-suited to linking the vision of digital transformation and smart correction initiatives. Based on the practice of eGovernment in Macao, which aspects can facilitate the digital transformation of correctional services to enhance the modernization of governance systems and capabilities, and achieve good governance? This study employs qualitative research methods, including a comprehensive literature review, secondary data collection, and analysis of legal documents, regulations, and sentencing policies within the Macao penal system. A SWOT-Plus analysis is conducted to assess potential internal and external trends and identify extant challenges. A hybrid framework is proposed that incorporates the incentives for eGovernment and the fundamental principles of good governance, including key governance beliefs and values such as organization, process, regulation, and culture. The findings also outline a series of expected impacts on correctional services that navigate the transformation ideology and foster successful implementation, thereby coordinating the vision of smart government. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Nie J.; Gao F.; Liu Y.; Umair M.; Abdalla Adam N.
Title: Reputation and value signals as moderators of advertising spend efficiency in E commerce search advertising
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: China hosts the world's largest e‑commerce search advertising market, yet merchants persistently misallocate advertising budgets by treating ad spend as a monotonic driver of sales efficiency. Drawing on the Resource‑Based View (RBV) and Information Overload Theory, this study investigates how advertising spend intensity (ASI) affects two core efficiency metrics—the Ad‑to‑Sales Ratio (ASR) and Return on Ad Spend (ROAS), as well as the moderating roles of two structural market factors. Keyword Specificity (KS) reflects the semantic breadth of keywords ranging from generic terms to long‑tail queries, whereas Category Competition Intensity (CCI) captures the density of competing products within each keyword market. Based on keyword‑level panel advertising data from a home appliances and household goods retailer operating on China's leading business‑to‑consumer platform, alongside supplementary observational data on competing products, this study identifies an inverted‑U‑shaped relationship between ASI and both ASR and ROAS: advertising efficiency improves with greater spending initially but declines after crossing a category‑specific threshold. KS shifts the efficiency peak toward higher spend levels, meaning long‑tail keywords can maintain efficiency under greater advertising investment. By contrast, CCI compresses this optimal spending range and triggers earlier efficiency deterioration in highly competitive categories. These findings extend the RBV and Information Overload Theory to sponsored‑search research and provide keyword‑type and competition‑dependent spending benchmarks for practitioners in Chinese e‑commerce. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Learn AI with AI: Designing conversational agents to support older adults in learning about AI
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Older adults are motivated to develop AI literacy and consider it important. Prior research suggests that conversational agents can support older adults’ AI literacy learning by simplifying AI concepts and providing interactive learning experiences. However, little is known about how such agents should be designed to address the learning challenges older adults face. To address this, we interviewed nine older adults to explore their challenges and identify design opportunities. Findings revealed affective barriers related to confidence and engagement, emphasizing the importance of peer-like characteristics in agents, such as reciprocal knowledge sharing. Guided by these insights, we designed a peer-like agent and compared it with a website and an assistant agent in a between-subjects study with 45 older adults learning about deepfakes. Results showed that the peer agent fostered higher engagement and supported confidence more than the others. We conclude with design recommendations for conversational agents to support older adults’ AI learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Analysis of environmental and social impacts of quarry mining for bridging stakeholder perception gaps–a case study from Padukka, Sri Lanka
Abstract: This study investigates stakeholder perceptions of the environmental and social impacts associated with the China Harbour Aggregate Quarry in the Padukka Division of the Colombo District, Sri Lanka. Despite growing concerns about the impacts of quarrying on host communities, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how different stakeholder groups perceive and experience these impacts in the Sri Lankan context. A mixed-methods case study design integrated qualitative and quantitative approaches to examine stakeholder perspectives. The study involved 31 community members near the quarry, 3 quarry site professionals, and 4 officers from a technical services company, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews with all stakeholder groups and structured questionnaires comprising open- and closed-ended questions administered to community members. Thematic analysis was used to analyze interview and open-ended questionnaire data, while descriptive analysis was applied to closed-ended questionnaire responses. Findings indicate that vibration was the dominant impact, reported by all community participants (100%), with concerns about noise, water dry out, dust, and occasional flyrock events. Community responses revealed high perceived annoyance (93.5%) and opposition to the mining site (87.1%), although all respondents were unwilling to relocate, highlighting sociopsychological constraints. Comparative analysis revealed convergence and divergence between community perceptions and quarry personnel perspectives, with mitigation measures implemented but challenges persisting due to spatial constraints, communication gaps, and disputed compensation claims. The study contributes context-specific evidence on stakeholder perceptions of quarrying impacts and provides practical insights for strengthening community engagement, impact mitigation, and socially responsible quarry management in Sri Lanka. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Production decisions of a leasing-selling closed-loop supply chain under different authorization strategies
Abstract: Leasing or selling, when to choose which? This paper investigates the production decisions of a closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) considering authorized remanufacturing (royalty/fixed-fee authorization) under different business mode combinations. Furthermore, win–win authorization strategies for the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the third-party remanufacturer (TPR) are analyzed. The conclusion shows that: (1) Regardless of the business mode chosen by the OEM, the sensitivity of unit product authorization fee to consumer perceived value of remanufactured products (RPs) is always higher when the TPR chooses the selling mode than when it chooses the leasing mode. (2) For selling new products (NPs) and RPs mode and selling NPs and leasing RPs mode, the fixed-fee authorization strategy is a win–win strategy when the manufacturing cost per unit of NP for selling is high and the fixed authorization fee is within a certain range, and the royalty authorization strategy is a win–win strategy when this cost is low and the fixed authorization fee is within a certain range. The win–win authorization strategies for the leasing NPs and selling RPs mode and leasing NPs and RPs mode are affected by the manufacturing cost per unit of NP for leasing and the fixed authorization fee. (3) Under the royalty authorization strategy, the TPR is more profitable when the OEM chooses the leasing mode, but the OEM is more profitable when the TPR chooses the selling mode. Under the fixed-fee authorization strategy, when one of the two players chooses the leasing mode, the other is always more profitable. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: pH-dependent foam stability of egg white protein-sodium alginate-eggshell powder systems: Roles of soluble calcium availability, bulk structuring, and interfacial behaviour
Abstract: Egg white protein (EWP)-based foams are widely used in aerated foods, and their stability depends on bulk-phase structure and air-water interfacial behaviour. This study investigated how initial pH conditions regulate soluble calcium availability, structural assembly, interfacial behaviour, and foam stability in EWP-sodium alginate (SA)-eggshell powder (EP) systems. EWP-SA dispersions were initially adjusted to pH 5.0, 7.0, or 9.0 before EP incorporation. Wet ball milling reduced EP to a submicron particle size of 0.41 μm while preserving the calcite CaCO3 crystalline structure. The pH 5.0 group showed the greatest pH increase after EP addition and the highest SWeibull plateau values for soluble calcium measured colorimetrically (21.52-24.22 mM), consistent with enhanced CaCO3 dissolution under the initially acidic condition. This group also exhibited enhanced EWP-SA association, possible Ca2+-mediated alginate crosslinking, broader particle-size distributions, higher β-Sheet contents, stronger bulk viscoelasticity, greater aggregation, and improved long-term foam retention during standing. Although the pH 7.0 and 9.0 groups generally exhibited higher dilatational moduli under the applied oscillatory conditions, the pH 5.0 group showed a faster initial adsorption response, with a maximum Kdiff of 2.359 mN m−1·s−1/2. Moreover, the 1.5% SA-1% EP and 1.5% SA-2% EP systems in the pH 5.0 group retained 100% and 95.63% of their foam volumes after 12 h, respectively. Foam stability was associated with changes in soluble calcium availability, bulk viscoelasticity, and interfacial behaviour. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for constructing stable EWP-SA-EP foams by regulating initial pH to coordinate bulk-interfacial coupling processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Industrial Digital Twin-driven generation of blockchain-based Digital Product Passports for trustworthy product lifecycle management
Abstract: The integration of Digital Twins (DTs), blockchain, and Digital Product Passports (DPPs) is emerging as a promising direction for trustworthy, auditable, and interoperable industrial lifecycle management. However, an open issue is how heterogeneous lifecycle evidence generated by DTs from physical and industrial-system observations can be transformed into DPP-consumable claims while preserving provenance, integrity, temporal validity, and manageable certification costs. This paper proposes a framework for DPP-oriented dynamic certification of industrial DTs in distributed industrial environments. The proposed architecture connects physical assets, DT instances, off-chain evidence repositories, permissioned blockchain anchoring, and DPP interfaces. DTs derive structured lifecycle evidence from physical and industrial-system observations concerning products, components, materials, processes, and facilities; blockchain mechanisms provide tamper-evident anchoring through hashes, timestamps, signatures, and Merkle roots; and DPPs expose selected certified claims to authorized stakeholders. A parameterized discrete-event simulation evaluates DPP update policies, certification granularity, blockchain anchoring strategies, hierarchical lifecycle aggregation, and networked certification under heterogeneous IIoT and edge–cloud conditions. The results show that technical blockchain commit success alone is not sufficient to assess DPP feasibility: freshness lag, lifecycle coverage, on-chain payload, and energy cost must also be considered. Overall, the evaluation confirms that hybrid certification strategies can support scalable DT–Blockchain–DPP infrastructures by combining direct compact anchoring for critical lifecycle evidence with periodic, hierarchical, or Merkle-based aggregation for routine updates. Title: From natural-extract variability to reproducible nanomaterials: AI-QbD strategies for green synthesis from agro-food waste
Abstract: Green synthesis of metal nanoparticles from agro-food waste extracts offers environmental and economic advantages over conventional chemical methods, using natural phytochemicals as reducing and stabilizing agents. However, inherent variability in botanical feedstocks, arising from seasonal fluctuation, geographic origin, and extraction protocols, poses significant challenges to reproducibility and standardization. Current literature documents fewer than 300 systematically characterized synthesis studies using non-harmonized protocols, and botanical extract composition inherently varies 15–30 % seasonally and geographically, limiting the generalization of process parameters across waste sources. This review critically examines the materials science foundations of phytochemical-mediated nanoparticle formation, including the mechanistic roles of phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and terpenoids in metal-ion reduction, nucleation kinetics, and surface capping. We analyze how feedstock composition and extraction conditions influence particle size distribution, morphology, crystallinity, and surface chemistry properties, which ultimately determine biological identity and functional performance. We then evaluate the potential of Quality-by-Design (QbD) frameworks and artificial intelligence (AI) approaches to address these reproducibility challenges. However, we emphasize that significant prerequisites remain before AI deployment is viable: AI model performance reported in the literature ranges from 65 to 85 % accuracy across heterogeneous botanical waste sources, substantially lower than idealized estimates, and current models suffer from dataset-size limitations and the risk of overfitting. We propose a phased implementation roadmap: Phase 1 (18–24 months) requires establishing harmonized botanical characterization protocols and controlled extraction procedures; Phase 2 requires 300–500 documented synthesis experiments across multiple waste sources; Phase 3 can then build predictive AI models on this standardized foundation. Throughout, we distinguish between demonstrated evidence, emerging proof-of-concept results, and areas requiring substantial further validation before clinical or industrial translation becomes feasible. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Spectrally Partitioned All-Optical Memristors for Highly Linear Neuromorphic Vision Systems
Abstract: All-optical control of synaptic weights offers a promising route toward low-power and massively parallel neuromorphic hardware. However, existing optoelectronic memristors often require electrical assistance or exhibit nonlinear and asymmetric conductance updates, limiting their energy efficiency and scalability. Herein, we report a spectrally partitioned all-optical memristor based on a PbS/PEDOT:PSS/VOx heterostructure, in which near-infrared and visible light are coupled to opposite defect-state filling and depletion pathways. Near-infrared illumination selectively excites PbS quantum dots and drives gradual electron transfer into oxygen-vacancy-related defect states in VOx through the PEDOT:PSS-regulated interface, producing continuous conductance potentiation. By contrast, visible illumination activates VOx and promotes interfacial hole-assisted recombination, leading to reversible depletion of defect-state electrons and conductance depression. This wavelength-selective carrier-transfer process enables highly linear and symmetric all-optical weight updates, achieving a linearity of 0.9994 and an effective 8-bit conductance resolution. The electrical energy consumption per optically induced synaptic event is calculated to be as low as 0.63 fJ under an ultralow probing bias. By integrating the devices into a 32 × 32 all-optically programmed array, we further demonstrate hardware-based BloodMNIST microscopic blood-cell image classification with an accuracy of 96.5% and strong noise robustness. These results provide a viable strategy for developing high-linearity, low-power, and spectrally programmable neuromorphic hardware. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Selective partitioning of plant proteins during emulsification impairs foam stability: conformational changes of aqueous-phase residues relative to animal proteins
Abstract: The foam instability restricts the industrial application of plant protein-based whipped cream. Most current studies focus on the intrinsic properties of proteins, while there remains a lack of in-depth understanding regarding whether the emulsification process alters the protein composition in the aqueous phase and subsequently affects foaming performance. This study shows that during emulsification, aqueous-phase proteins undergo selective partitioning or depletion, altering remaining protein components and thus determining subsequent foam performance. Using animal proteins (sodium caseinate, SC; goat milk protein, GMP) as benchmarks, emulsions were formulated with plant proteins (pea protein isolate, PPI; soy protein isolate, SPI). Analysis of the results indicated that during emulsification, specific components of plant protein (66–175 kDa and 16 kDa) were preferentially depleted from the aqueous phase. Compared to animal proteins, this selective partitioning led to significant changes in the structure and surface properties of the residual protein in the aqueous phase: an increase of approximately 10% in β-sheet content, formation of more compact aggregates, and a reduction in surface hydrophobicity by over 39%. Ultimately, during whipping, the remaining plant protein exhibited lower diffusion and rearrangement rate constants at the air-water interface, resulting in slower interfacial dynamics, insufficient foam coverage, reduced whipping capacity (287%–308%), and faster foam breakdown. These results suggest that protein molecular characteristics, processing history, and non-protein components may collectively drive the selective partitioning process, with preferential adsorption at the oil-water interface potentially playing a key role. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zhang T.; Peng Z.; Zhao S.; Jin X.; Du Y.; Li Z.; Wang K.; Gao J.
Title: A Manganese-Chlorella Hydrogel for an Integrated “Remove–Remodel–Repair” Strategy in Pancreatic Cancer Therapy
Abstract: Pancreatic cancer faces the challenges of tumor progression and postoperative pancreatic fistula during the perioperative period, which severely affect patient prognosis. In this study, an injectable self-healing multifunctional hydrogel (CMCGel) was developed based on dynamic cross‑linking between manganese ions (Mn2+) and carboxymethyl chitosan loaded with chlorella extract (CE). This platform implements an integrated “Remove–Remodel–Repair” (3R) strategy for comprehensive perioperative management. CMCGel exhibits distinctive pH/laser dual-responsive behavior: In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the accelerated release of CE and Mn2+ enhances photodynamic therapy and chemodynamic therapy (CDT). This combination, activated by laser and gated by endogenous pH, achieves remarkable tumor suppression rates of 85.81% in vitro and 96.01% in vivo. As pH normalizes, Mn2+ shifts from CDT to activate the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway, remodeling the immune microenvironment. Crucially, CMCGel’s adhesion strength in artificial pancreatic fluid at 48 h was 4703.80 ± 50.36 Pa, only 8.17% lower than that at 10 min. This enzyme-resistant property enables durable mechanical sealing at the fistula site, reducing amylase leakage by 55.71% and creating favorable conditions for tissue repair. By integrating pH/laser-triggered combination therapy, immunomodulation, and enzyme-resistant barrier functionality into a single platform, CMCGel presents a clinically promising strategy for perioperative management of pancreatic cancer. Authors: Khan H.; Knight G.; Khan Z.
Title: Mechanisms for digital business model innovation in international new ventures from developing economies
Abstract: Digital international new ventures (DINVs) increasingly leverage ecosystem partnerships to drive digital business model innovation (DBMI) and navigate global markets. However, research to examine how such partnerships contribute to DBMI is limited, particularly in resource-constrained firms from developing economies. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities view, organizational learning theory and an ecosystem-based digital learning perspective, we investigate the role of ecosystem partnerships in enabling DBMI through the development of digital learning capabilities. Based on survey data from 147 DINVs in a developing economy, findings suggest that ecosystem partnerships enhance digital learning, which in turn facilitates DBMI. Moreover, foreign market turbulence tends to positively moderate the relationship between ecosystem partnerships and digital learning capability. In addition to demonstrating how DINVs build innovation capacity under volatile conditions, findings help to extend perspectives on capabilities, learning, and ecosystems. Leveraging ecosystem partnerships, digital learning, and digital business model innovation appears to enhance the performance of DINVs. Ecosystem partnerships appear to be especially valuable to DINVs when market turbulence is high. The study offers theoretical and practical insights into the mechanism through which DINVs from developing economies can achieve digital innovation, and provides policy implications for supporting their international growth. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Current Status of Bowel Preparation for Colonoscopy in Japan: A Web-Based Survey of Endoscopists (PRESS Survey)
Abstract: Objectives: The increasing number of patients with colorectal cancer underscores the importance of colonoscopy. Adequate bowel preparation is essential to ensure the quality and safety of colonoscopic examinations; however, data on the current practices in Japan remain limited. This study aimed to clarify the current status of bowel preparation, use of bowel-cleansing agents, and associated challenges among physicians performing colonoscopies. Methods: In March 2026, we conducted a nationwide web-based cross-sectional survey of physicians performing colonoscopies in Japan. The survey assessed bowel preparation practices, use of bowel-cleansing agents, constipation, and renal function before colonoscopy. Responses were obtained from 300 physicians who performed at least 10 colonoscopies per month. Results: Low-volume polyethylene glycol (PEG) plus ascorbate preparations were the most commonly used bowel-cleansing agents, followed by high-volume PEG preparations and magnesium-based agents. Cleansing efficacy and safety were the most highly valued characteristics of bowel-cleansing agents. 64.7% of physicians reported that the perceived frequency of inadequate bowel preparation was >10% among their patients. Although 64.3% of the physicians reported always assessing constipation, only 32.7% reported always evaluating renal function before colonoscopy. Compared with hospital-based physicians, those working in clinics reported a significantly lower proportion of inadequate bowel preparation, but a significantly lower rate of renal function assessment. Conclusion: Although cleansing efficacy and safety are prioritized in bowel preparation for colonoscopy in Japan, physicians perceived inadequate bowel preparation to occur in a substantial proportion of patients. Thus, further optimization of bowel preparation strategies and more consistent assessment of renal function before colonoscopy are needed. Title: From sustainability awareness to practical agency: Translating institutional activity into meaningful student learning
Abstract: The Principles for Responsible Management Education initiative calls upon business schools to embed sustainability and responsible management within their curricula. Although higher education institutions have made progress, student perspectives remain underrepresented in Education for Sustainable Development research. Drawing on an integrated theoretical framework comprising Transformative Learning Theory, the sustainability competency framework, social learning and students-as-partners pedagogy, this exploratory study reports a mixed-methods survey of 130 Business and Management students across two UK higher education institutions. The findings indicate generally favourable sustainability attitudes among the participating students, consistent with previous responsible management education research. Exploratory comparisons found broadly similar patterns across two contrasting UK cohorts: full-time undergraduate students and employed degree apprentices. The more distinctive finding concerns an institutional-to-educational translation gap. Students acknowledged aspects of current provision but indicated that institutional sustainability activity did not always become visible, participatory or educationally meaningful within their programmes. Across both cohorts, students called for stronger collaboration, practice-oriented education and solutions-focused learning through which sustainability knowledge could be connected with authentic organisational and societal challenges. These findings underpin a student-informed conceptual framework, Towards Transdisciplinary and Transformative Sustainability Education, which identifies conditions through which institutional sustainability activity may become visible, participatory and educationally meaningful to students. The study does not directly assess institutional transformation, transformative learning or behavioural change, nor does it test whether favourable attitudes persist when sustainability entails difficult financial, professional or lifestyle trade-offs. The Framework should therefore be understood as a conceptual proposition for supporting meaningful engagement rather than as evidence that transformative or behavioural outcomes have occurred. © 2026 The Authors

Title: A data-informed scaling parameterization for non-Fickian retention in atmospheric boundary-layer dispersion
Abstract: Pollutant dispersion in the planetary boundary layer is usually simulated with the advection–diffusion equation closed by the gradient-diffusion hypothesis, in which the turbulent flux follows the local concentration gradient. In the convective boundary layer it cannot represent transport driven by thermals spanning the full depth of the layer. The Bevilacqua–Galeão bi-flux model separates the material into a fraction that diffuses classically and a retained fraction that does not follow the local gradient, introducing a fourth-order term governed by a retention coefficient Kz2. In previous applications Kz2 was treated as a constant, with no means of relating it to the state of the boundary layer. Here the equation is solved by a high-order implicit finite-difference scheme, and a constrained Bayesian optimization identifies the parameters best reproducing the Copenhagen and Prairie Grass tracer experiments. Dimensional analysis of these optima yields Kz2(x) in terms of the friction velocity, boundary-layer depth, source height and downwind distance, so that the coefficient is specified in advance from routine meteorological data and grows as the plume travels downwind. The same expression covers the 115 m elevated release at Copenhagen and the near-surface release at Prairie Grass with no constant adjusted to either. When it is prescribed, the absolute fractional bias falls by 57% and 27% respectively, and the normalized mean square error by 12.7% and 17.3%, while other performance measures are preserved. The scaling was determined based on the optimization results, and the validated range is limited to the source heights considered in the tests. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Constitutive metabolic signatures associated with partial resistance to fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) in tropical maize inbred lines
Abstract: Fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) poses a major threat to maize production in sub-Saharan Africa, underscoring the importance of identifying durable sources and biochemical markers of host-plant resistance. This study investigated the constitutive metabolic basis of partial FAW resistance in tropical maize by integrating insect bioassays with complementary GC–MS and LC–Q-TOF–MS profiling. Whole-leaf tissues collected before infestation from three resistant (Mp716, CML71, and CKSBL10008) and three susceptible (CML370, CKSBL10025, and CML444) inbred lines were analyzed, and the same tissues were incorporated into artificial diets to evaluate larval growth and feeding preference. Diets derived from resistant genotypes consistently reduced larval relative growth rates and were less preferred by neonates than diets derived from susceptible lines, providing evidence that pre-existing leaf chemistry contributes to both antibiosis- and antixenosis-associated resistance. GC–MS detected approximately 800 analytical features and highlighted resistance-associated trends in amino-acid, nitrogen, and central-carbon metabolism. LC–Q-TOF–MS detected approximately 1,700 features, with 384 differing significantly between resistance classes after false-discovery-rate correction, revealing extensive remodeling of specialized metabolism. Resistant lines were characterized by higher relative abundances of several putative amino acids, purine-related metabolites, phytosterols, and putative defense-associated compounds, including a DIMBOA-hexoside-related feature. In contrast, susceptible lines generally contained higher levels of putative soluble sugars, central-carbon metabolites, and several flavonoid- and phenylpropanoid-related features. Pathway analysis identified 28 differentially abundant consolidated metabolites and significant enrichment of phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, indicating selective metabolic reconfiguration rather than generalized accumulation of secondary metabolites. Together, these findings demonstrate that partial FAW resistance is associated with a coordinated constitutive metabolic signature integrating nutritional composition and specialized defense chemistry. Although targeted and spatially resolved validation is required to establish the functions of individual metabolites, the identified signatures provide promising biochemical candidates for resistance screening and metabolomics-assisted breeding of FAW-resistant maize. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature B.V. 2026.

Title: Reproducing and benchmarking behavioral similarity methods for business process models
Abstract: In our primary work, we presented a comparative evaluation of behavioral similarity methods for business process models, assessing Prime Event Structures (PES), Transition Adjacency Relations (TAR) and trace alignment computed with PM4Py on the Process Model Matching Contest 2015 benchmark, where PES achieved the highest effectiveness. In this companion paper, we describe how to reproduce the entire experimental study through a Docker-based pipeline, with step-by-step instructions that regenerate every reported result, including the statistical analyses. While making the experiments reproducible, we identified and removed a source of non-determinism in the trace simulation of PM4Py: repeated executions now yield identical values, and the ranking of the three methods reported in the primary work is preserved. We also assess the stability of the findings on systematically generated process model variants with controlled structural and behavioral perturbations, and we explain how the experiments can be extended to new process models, parameters and similarity methods. All materials, including source code, datasets and protocols, are publicly available, enabling exact replication and extension by other researchers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The value of lost load in electricity intensive industry – combining and comparing stated and production value approaches
Abstract: The value of lost load (VoLL) is a monetary metric quantifying the cost of unsupplied energy (€/kWh) during outages, providing valuable insights for policymakers, utility providers, and industrial stakeholders. Leveraging a mixed-method approach that integrates and compares survey data with publicly available microeconomic data insights, results show how value-added based measures significantly underestimate the financial impact of power outages. Shorter outages are found to be disproportionately costly, primarily due to high fixed costs associated with initial disruptions. Businesses report that the effects of a 1-h outage could linger for months, with some unable to fully recover even 12 months after the event. These extended disruptions underscore the enduring consequences of power outages, particularly for electricity-intensive industries. In a regression type of approach, the cost of power interruptions is not significantly influenced by the type of industry. Instead, the economic impact of an outage is more closely tied to the volume of electricity consumed, duration and production hours. Highlighting sectoral aspects and methodological sensitivities, the paper offers relevant insights for setting reliability standards, designing compensation schemes, and for guiding infrastructure investment. © 2026 The Authors. Title: How does responsible governance affect firms’ Innovation resilience? A matching perspective on responsible leadership and responsible AI
Abstract: Innovation resilience has become a critical capability for firms to withstand risks and achieve sustainable growth. However, how responsible governance shapes firms’ innovation resilience remains underexplored. Drawing on signaling theory and conservation of resources theory, this study examines the effects of responsible leadership, responsible AI, and their congruence on firms’ innovation resilience. Using survey data from 480 firms in China’s manufacturing and strategic emerging industries, we conduct empirical analyses with nonlinear regression and response surface analysis. The results show that: (1) responsible leadership has an inverted U-shaped relationship with firms’ innovation resilience; (2) responsible AI has a negative effect on firms’ innovation resilience; (3) congruence between responsible leadership and responsible AI is conducive to firms’ innovation resilience; (4) firms exhibit higher innovation resilience under the high responsible leadership-high responsible AI configuration than under the low responsible leadership-low responsible AI configuration; (5) compared with the low responsible leadership-high responsible AI configuration, firms achieve higher levels of innovation resilience under the high responsible leadership-low responsible AI configuration; and (6) organizational unlearning and organizational innovation climate positively moderate the effect of responsible leadership-responsible AI congruence on firms’ innovation resilience. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Optimizing equity and efficiency in the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem
Abstract: This study addresses the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem, formulated as the strategic prepositioning of a heterogeneous aerial firefighting fleet across capacity-constrained airbases. A novel bi-objective model is proposed that simultaneously optimizes efficiency (aggregate risk-weighted accessibility) and equity (minimized regional service disparities). The model employs an enhanced spatial accessibility method with a distance-decay function to evaluate coverage effectiveness and distribution fairness. A multi-objective genetic algorithm is implemented to generate Pareto-approximate solutions, revealing quantifiable trade-offs. Applied to a national-scale case study in Greece using 25 years of wildfire data, results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides significantly wider coverage than current practices, thereby extending protection to underserved regions while reducing redundant overlap. Sensitivity analyses confirm robustness across various real-world conditions, such as different budget levels and aircraft availability. This transferable tool enables policymakers to make data-driven decisions by quantifying the balance between response effectiveness and social fairness in wildfire-prone regions. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Sour grapes or strategic choice? Socially disadvantaged tourism entrepreneurs' pursuit of ‘break out’
Abstract: While structural conditions impacting immigrant entrepreneurs' ‘break out’ are well-documented in tourism research, the underlying psychological processes remain underexplored. Informed by self-determination theory and adaptive preferences, this ethnographic study conducted between December 2024 and May 2025 explores how socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs negotiate structural constraints and individual agency while pursuing ‘break out’. Drawing on 345 h of ethnographic observation, digital data from two focal Nepali tourism entrepreneurs in Hong Kong SAR, and longitudinal object-oriented interviews with nineteen stakeholders, it reveals a psychological mechanism where frustration of basic psychological needs triggers adaptive preferences, hindering ‘break out’ efforts. It also shows how tourism's experiential nature enables entrepreneurs to counter stigma and negotiate autonomy. Practically, the findings highlight the need for psychologically informed support that goes beyond traditional skill-based training. While focused on Hong Kong's Nepali diaspora, the study offers broader insights into entrepreneurial ‘break out’ among socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Probabilistic wind power forecasting with tree-based machine learning and weather ensembles
Abstract: Accurate production forecasts are essential for the integration of renewable energy sources into the power grid. This paper illustrates how to obtain probabilistic forecasts of wind power generation using gradient boosting trees and an ensemble of weather forecasts. To this end, we perform a comparative analysis across three state-of-the-art probabilistic prediction methods-conformalized quantile regression, natural gradient boosting and conditional diffusion models-all of which can be combined with tree-based machine learning. The methods are validated using four years of data for all Belgian offshore wind farms. We benchmark the models against the power curve and a calibrated wake model as well as a probabilistic method using stochastic variational Gaussian process regression. The tree-based models significantly reduce the mean absolute error in comparison to the deterministic baselines. Additionally, all three methods outperform the Gaussian process baseline in probabilistic skill, while two out of the three also improve point forecast accuracy. The conditional diffusion model attains the best performance, with improvements of 5% in mean absolute error and 12% in continuous rank probability score compared to the probabilistic baseline. Title: A game-theoretic approach for the retailer-third party multiple market-site capture competition in an end-of-life product collection system
Abstract: This paper introduces a bi-level game-theoretic model for competition between two players collecting End-Of-Life (EOL) products within a circular economy framework. The model focuses on strategic market targeting in a geographically segmented market dominated by an established retailer. A new entrant (third party) acts as the leader, selecting a subset of nodes to capture. The incumbent retailer responds as the follower, recapturing lost nodes under its own budget. Due to NP-hardness, a Benders cut-based solution approach is developed. The model is extended to a partial interdiction formulation with continuous capture decisions, allowing gradual market entry. A genetic algorithm has also been developed for large-scale instances. A case study on EOL mobile phone collection in Tehran illustrates the practical application. Entry points and defensive and offensive strategies are derived under various budget scenarios. Results show that entry is not always advantageous. As the retailer’s budget increases, the third party faces higher financial barriers to entry, requiring a disproportionately larger budget to remain competitive. Title: Tackling cold-start emissions: an integrated strategy of active thermal management and oxygenated fuel formulation
Abstract: This study investigates the integration of bio-oxygenated fuel formulation with an electrically heated catalytic system to mitigate low-temperature cold-start emissions in compression-ignition engines. Four 20 % v/v oxygenated blends, comprising linear alcohols (butanol, pentanol) and cyclic compounds (cyclopentanol, cyclopentanone), were evaluated in a single-cylinder research engine coupled to a diesel oxidation catalyst. Active thermal management at DOC inlet temperatures of 355 °C to 415 °C achieved approximately 99 % CO conversion and 72 % total hydrocarbon reduction and increased the downstream NO2/NOx ratio up to 0.34. Catalytic post-treatment further reduced total particle number concentration by 41.1 % to 57.2 % with a simultaneous increase in count median diameter. These results, constrained by the single-cylinder steady-state operating conditions and specific engine loads evaluated, indicate that coupling tailored fuel formulations with active electrical heating offers an integrated methodological framework with the potential to resolve cold-start emissions limitations in low-exhaust-temperature applications. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Hydrophobic Eutectogels Reinforced by Zn2+-Coordinated Lignin Nanoparticles for Underwater Wearable Electronics
Abstract: Wearable flexible sensors for underwater communication and biomotion monitoring are gaining attention. However, developing gel-based strain sensors with high toughness, anti-swelling performance, robust underwater adhesion, and long-term stability remains challenging. Herein, we present a hydrophobic eutectogel (DPF-Zn@LNP-HEG) fabricated via the assembly of a polymerizable hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent (PHDES), 2-phenoxyethyl acrylate (PEA), and Zn2+-coordinated lignin nanoparticles (Zn@LNP). The resulting structure, composed of hydrophobic polymer networks and metal-phenolic complexes, forms hydrophobic microdomains that disrupt the hydration layer and prevent water penetration. Meanwhile, Zn@LNP serve as dynamic sacrificial cross-linkers, enhancing the material’s mechanical strength, energy dissipation, and anti-swelling properties. The resulting eutectogel exhibits remarkable tensile strength (1.14 MPa), superior toughness (3.15 MJ m−3), excellent anti-swelling properties (< 1% after 30 days), and robust underwater adhesion (1.07 MPa on glass). Based on these properties, we demonstrate an underwater strain sensor with high sensitivity (gauge factor = 8.12) and long-term stability, enabling underwater Morse code transmission, biomotion monitoring, and Bluetooth-based tracking of swimming movements. This work not only provides a versatile design paradigm for multifunctional underwater sensing platforms but also advances the high-value utilization of bio-based materials in next-generation flexible electronics. Title: Online direct-to-consumer channel introducing and ordering strategies of fresh supply chain considering disruption risks and yield constraints
Abstract: The rise of online direct-to-consumer (DTC) channels expands fresh producers’ distribution networks while intensifying competition with traditional retail channels. This study develops a theoretical framework to examine strategic interactions within a fresh supply chain, comparing a traditional monopoly model with an integrated distribution system that incorporates both DTC and traditional retail channels. Disruption risks and yield constraints faced by producers are considered. The findings suggest producers should introduce DTC channels during yield contraction but exercise caution in surplus periods. Despite disruption risks, DTC channels pressure retailers to accept higher wholesale prices and increase orders, enhancing the sales revenue of fresh produce with limited yield. Title: Artificial intelligence disclosure and the value relevance of earnings
Abstract: This study investigates the effect of AI disclosure on the value relevance of earnings using Chinese listed companies from 2013 to 2022. Title: From conventional multi-vendor failover to adaptive API routing: An industrial experience report on resilient third-party service integration
Abstract: High-scale online services often rely on third-party APIs in user-facing flows such as authentication, messaging, payments, fraud detection, and identity verification. Integrating alternate providers and operating conventional failover controls is a common resilience baseline, but redundancy alone does not make provider selection adaptive, explainable, or policy-aware. This paper reports an anonymized industrial experience evolving a conventional multi-vendor SMS-provider failover arrangement in a large marketplace setting into configuration-driven adaptive API routing. The approach uses operation-specific pluggable factor lists to separate routing policy from application code, combines hard eligibility gates with normalized weighted provider scoring, and closes the loop with business-outcome telemetry, decision logs, traffic-shift controls, and recovery safeguards. The report includes de-identified operational evidence, including before/after windows, a representative incident timeline, shadow-mode validation records, policy-tuning history, score-normalization snapshots, provider-attribution examples, feedback-bias controls, and sensitivity analysis. The evidence suggests that adaptive provider routing can reduce dependence on incident-time interpretation when the operation is critical, telemetry volume is sufficient, and organizational controls exist for policy ownership, explainability, and safe traffic movement. The paper concludes with practitioner guidance and transferability conditions for teams considering similar architectures. © 2026

Title: Advances in TMDs-Based Electromagnetic Wave Absorbers: From Structural Engineering to Multicomponent Synergy
Abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have garnered considerable attention as advanced electromagnetic wave absorption (EMA) materials due to their unique layered structures, tunable electronic properties, and intrinsic defect-induced polarization mechanisms. This comprehensive review systematically summarizes recent advances in TMDs-based absorbers, with particular focus on two fundamental development strategies. The first involves multiscale structural design of pure phase TMDs spanning from atomic to submillimeter dimensions, achieved through precise defect regulation, phase engineering, and sophisticated morphological manipulation to optimize electromagnetic parameters and attenuation capabilities. The second strategy focuses on constructing multicomponent composite systems, incorporating dielectric matrices, magnetic elements, and multicomponent hybrids to achieve synergistic enhancement through interfacial polarization, conductive loss, and magnetic dissipation mechanisms. The review critically analyzes pioneering research achievements across various subfields while identifying specific challenges and opportunities within each domain. Future perspectives highlight emerging frontiers including atomic level interface engineering, inverse design of multicomponent and multiscale architectures, sustainable large-scale synthesis techniques, and development of multifunctional smart-response systems. This work aims to establish fundamental principles and provide forward-looking guidance for designing next-generation high-performance TMDs-based EMA materials with tailored functionalities. Title: Don't promise me, prove it: Leveraging blockchain affordances to reduce uncertainty and build consumer purchase confidence in sustainable fashion

Abstract: While the role of blockchain technology in shaping sustainable consumer behaviors is increasingly examined, empirical understanding of its capability to reduce uncertainty and enhance consumers' purchase confidence remains limited, particularly within the sustainable fashion context. Title: Polymer-specific mechanical recycling of pre-sorted post-consumer municipal plastics for enhanced environmental sustainability
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical recycling of municipal plastic waste can reduce landfill burden, energy demand, and environmental impacts while recovering reusable polymers. The study objectives were to assess the performance of polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene using polymer-specific pre-processing methods, shredding, thermal consolidation, and compression moulding. The assessment focused on waste minimization, material recovery, energy requirements, estimated carbon dioxide emission reductions, sustainability, and mechanical and thermal performance. METHODS: A total of 37 kilograms of pre-sorted post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene was separately processed using polymer-specific treatment and compression moulding. Environmental performance was evaluated within a cradle-to-gate framework using secondary emission factors, and the Sustainability Index was derived from predefined parameters. Recycled materials were evaluated for mechanical and thermal properties. Exploratory one-way analysis of variance assessed polymer differences, with probability values adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. FINDINGS: Waste reduction and material recovery rates exceeded 95 percent for all polymers, with low-density polyethylene achieving the highest recovery of 99 percent. Low-density polyethylene also showed the lowest energy consumption of 0.95 kilowatt-hours per kilogram and the observed sustainability index of 82.6 ± 2.1, although polymer-specific differences in the Sustainability Index were not statistically significant. Polyethylene terephthalate showed the highest tensile strength (55.2 megapascals), compressive strength (83.4 megapascals), density (1.36 grams per cubic centimetre), and carbon dioxide emission reduction (2.10 kilograms of carbon dioxide per kilogram). High-density polyethylene showed intermediate performance. Analysis of variance indicated polymer-specific differences, with F-statistic values of 1.72–412.3 and probability values of <0.001–0.27. After Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, most physical and mechanical properties, energy consumption, and carbon dioxide emission reduction showed significant differences, whereas landfill diversion and the Sustainability Index did not differ significantly. CONCLUSION: Polymer-specific mechanical recycling of pre-sorted post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene achieved high material recovery while maintaining mechanical and thermal properties. The polymers showed differences in material recovery, energy consumption, carbon dioxide emission reduction, and evaluated material properties. Title: Mixed methods research: Critical review and guidelines for stronger design, integration, and contribution
Abstract: Mixed methods research has a prominent place in tourism and hospitality scholarship, yet adoption has advanced faster than methodological selectivity, which leaves many studies combining qualitative and quantitative strands without explaining why both strands were necessary, how the strands were related, or what integrated inference their combination alone made possible. Drawing on a critical review of 222 mixed methods studies published in leading tourism and hospitality journals, this article identifies dominant patterns, strengths and weaknesses, and underused possibilities. In response, the article offers a stage-based guide that links problem formulation, purpose selection, design fit, sampling bridges, strand roles, integration, divergence handling, reporting architecture, and contribution development. Title: Fostering creativity through interdisciplinary teaching: A meta-analysis of effectiveness
Abstract: Interdisciplinary teaching is widely promoted to cultivate students’ creativity, yet empirical findings remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis synthesized 55 quantitative studies (70 effect sizes, 7490 students) from 2013 to 2024, applying random-effects models using Hedges’ g. Results indicated a large overall positive effect ( g + = 1.090, 95% CI [0.913, 1.266]), with very high heterogeneity ( I 2 = 96.017%). Title: No Species Is an Island, Entire of Itself: Genetic Speciation Algorithm with Interplay among Species

The ablation study and sensitivity analysis reveals the positive effect of the incorporated mechanisms in GSAIS in finding global optimization, especially in large scale problems. Title: Security testing of RESTful APIs: Approaches and research challenges
Abstract: RESTful APIs have become a fundamental component of modern cloud-native and microservice-based applications, enabling seamless integration between distributed services. Since these APIs often expose sensitive data and business logic through publicly accessible endpoints, they have become attractive targets for cyberattacks. Recent security incidents and the growing number of API-related vulnerabilities demonstrate that traditional web application security mechanisms are insufficient for protecting RESTful APIs. Although numerous testing approaches have been proposed, existing research remains fragmented and often focuses primarily on functional validation rather than systematically addressing security vulnerabilities and adversarial exploitation patterns. This survey provides a comprehensive review of RESTful API testing approaches with a particular focus on those identifying security vulnerabilities. Based on a systematic analysis of 69 primary studies, we examine common RESTful API vulnerabilities and present a structured taxonomy that distinguishes between application-level weaknesses and configuration or deployment-level issues. We further analyze the attack patterns that exploit these vulnerabilities and review state-of-the-art testing approaches, including specification-based, model-based, property-based, and AI/ML-driven techniques. In addition, we analyze existing tools, datasets, and evaluation metrics used to assess the effectiveness of RESTful API testing methods. Finally, the survey identifies several critical research gaps that limit the effectiveness of current approaches, particularly around authenticated, context-aware testing and the detection and validation of logic-based security violations. We discuss emerging trends and outline potential research directions, including dependency-aware testing frameworks and AI-driven techniques for automated vulnerability discovery. This work aims to guide researchers and practitioners toward developing more systematic and robust frameworks for RESTful API security testing. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Balancing economic and environmental goals in green supply chains through a multi-objective optimization on financing and coordination contract
Abstract: This study aims to develop a green supply chain management (GSCM) framework that integrates buyer-backed purchase order financing (BPOF), advance payment discounts (APD), and coordination agreements to enhance sustainability and financial stability. Title: Machine Learning Parameters Identification for a New Unit Power-Logistic Quadratic Lindley Model

Abstract: This paper introduces a new two-parameter distribution for modelling unit interval data. It is named the Unit Power-Logistic Quadratic Lindley (UPLQL) model. Mathematical properties including moments, Lorenz and Bonferroni curves, order statistics, stress-strength reliability, and stochastic order are derived. Eight frequentist estimation methods are compared through an extensive Monte Carlo simulation (MCS), and a Bayesian analysis using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is also carried out. An amortised tree-based estimator (ATE) that predicts the parameters directly from a set of features is developed. It can be turned into a fast Bayesian tool using a parametric bootstrap. The performance of the UPLQL model is evaluated on two data sets, the flood-level proportions and petroleum reservoir measurements. Title: Continuous Fabrication of Bioinspired All-Biomass Aerogel Fibers for Thermal Insulation
Abstract: Aerogel fibers have been considered as a promising solution for thermal protection textiles due to their high porosity and low thermal conductivity. Title: Wearable Electronics for Precision Diagnosis Through Advanced Manufacturing and Integration
Abstract: Wearable electronics are rapidly transforming healthcare by enabling continuous, real-time monitoring of physiological and molecular signals directly at the point of need. This shift supports a transition from episodic, generalized care toward precision diagnosis, where individualized, longitudinal data guide early detection, risk stratification, and treatment decisions. Central to this transformation is the convergence of advanced manufacturing and heterogeneous integration strategies, which enable the development of compact, multimodal, and highly conformable diagnostic platforms. In this review, we examine how advances in materials engineering, micro/nanofabrication, and system integration have transformed wearable devices from single-parameter sensors into fully integrated, multimodal diagnostic systems. We outline key architectures and transduction mechanisms and highlight manufacturing approaches such as printing, 3D fabrication, photolithography, and laser writing.
