Title: The impact of entrepreneurship education on sustainable entrepreneurial intentions: A quasi-experimental study
Abstract: In this paper, we examine how a semester-long sustainability-oriented entrepreneurship course shapes sustainable entrepreneurial intention (SEI) through individual sustainability orientation (ISO). Grounded in an adaptation of the Theory of Planned Behaviour, ISO is conceptualized as a multidimensional construct encompassing sustainability-oriented (SO) values, SO motivation, awareness of sustainability issues, and SO self-efficacy, dimensions expected to mediate educational effects on SEI with different temporal sensitivities. We implemented a quasi-experimental design across two graduate introductory entrepreneurship courses at two Canadian universities: one redesigned around sustainability mechanisms (treatment, N = 112) and one covering standard content (comparison, N = 47). Pre- and post-test surveys were conducted. Results show no direct effect of the treatment on SEI and no change in SO values, which were high at baseline. However, the treatment significantly increased students’ sustainability awareness, self-efficacy, and, unexpectedly, motivation. Among these, changes in awareness and self-efficacy were positively associated with changes in SEI. These findings indicate that semester-long interventions can reliably influence proximal cognitions (awareness and self-efficacy), while deeper dispositions such as values, and to a lesser extent motivation, likely require longer-term or more immersive exposure. Theoretically, this study conceptualizes ISO as a temporally layered construct that helps explain why prior findings on education–SEI links are mixed. Methodologically, it demonstrates the value of coupling quasi-experimental designs with pedagogical reporting. Practically, it highlights workable mechanisms, such as sustainability-anchored projects, sustainable business modeling, and impact-oriented pitches, that strengthen awareness and SO self-efficacy. Title: The effectiveness of industrial gamma and e-beam sources, to inactivate B. pumilus spores in the presence of liquid water and considerations for validation of sterilization dose in accordance with ISO 11137
Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of industrial electron beam (e-beam) and gamma irradiators in inactivating Bacillus pumilus spores at varying levels of water availability. Commercially available B. pumilus spore strips were exposed to three hydration conditions: dry, immersed in saturated NaCl solution, or immersed in purified water, and subsequently irradiated. Gamma operated at a dose rate of 1 kGy/h, while the dose rate of e-beam was 1800 kGy/h. The results showed that gamma and e-beam irradiation were equally effective ( p = 0.111) in inactivating dry B. pumilus spores. These findings suggest that, provided the validated minimum dose is delivered, the dose may be transferred between industrial radiation sources without compromising product sterility, assuming no liquid water is present. In contrast, e-beam was more efficient than gamma in inactivating spores in saturated NaCl solution ( p = 0.007) and spores in water ( p = 0.009). It was observed that spore resistance increased with increasing water availability. The protective effect of water may have important implications for dose qualification strategies in sterilization processes. In the industrial sterilization of medical devices, the dose is often qualified by using Method 1/VDmax25, defined in ISO 11137. Method 1/VDmaxdose setting relies on the assumption that the product bioburden exhibits resistance to ionizing radiation that is consistent with the Standard Distribution of Resistance (SDR). If due to the presence of water, the resistance of the bioburden exceeds that of the SDR, Method 2 of ISO 11137-2:2013 should be used instead. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Dual-Ion Co-Storage via Solvation Structure Tuning Toward Ultrafast and Durable Zinc-Organic Batteries
Abstract: Aqueous Zn-organic batteries are promising due to the sustainability and tunability of organic cathodes. However, the critical challenge in their practical application lies in dissolution, degradation, and sluggish kinetics, ultimately degrading the cycling stability and rate capability. Herein, we demonstrate a simple effective electrolyte engineering strategy by introducing potassium chloride (KCl) as a co-solute into the ZnCl2 electrolyte to achieve high-performance Zn batteries utilizing 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTCDA) as the cathode. Experimental and density functional theory mechanistic studies unveil a new reversible Zn2+/K+ co-storage mechanism in the PTCDA cathode, where K+ acts as a charge shield and structural pillar, synergistically decreasing the ion migration energy barrier, enhancing reaction kinetics, and stabilizing the cathode structure. Title: Exploring the linkage between entrepreneurial education and entrepreneurial intentions among university students in Morocco
Abstract: The Moroccan labor market continues to struggle with the incorporation of its university graduates and the interest in entrepreneurship as an employment option is growing. Higher education institutions are an essential part of developing students' entrepreneurial competencies and intentions. This research investigates the effects of entrepreneurship education on students' entrepreneurial intention as based on the Theory of Planned Behavior. The research also investigates how attitudes toward entrepreneurship, perceived behavioral control, subjective norms, creativity, proactive behavior, and family background influence entrepreneurial intention. A self-administered questionnaire was used to collect data from 226 students at the Faculty of Economics and Management at Beni Mellal, Morocco, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that entrepreneurship education is positively related to entrepreneurial intention both directly as well as indirectly through attitudes toward entrepreneurship and perceived behavioral control; also, creativity and family background were found to positively influence entrepreneurial intention. In contrast, subjective norms and proactive behavior do not show a significant effect in this context. These findings highlight the importance of entrepreneurial education in strengthening students' entrepreneurial orientation while suggesting that social influences and individual proactivity may operate differently within the Moroccan context. Title: Reframing destination stability: how scale reshapes tourism volatility in the Balearic Islands
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Tourism destinations are often described as spatially differentiated systems, with coastal areas portrayed as more stable and inland areas as more volatile. Yet, it remains unclear whether these differences arise from location per se or from underlying structural properties of destinations. This paper develops a structural perspective on destination stability by examining the association between tourism-system scale and supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility at the municipal level in the Balearic Islands. Using annual data on regulated accommodation capacity for 62 municipalities over 2004–2024, supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility is measured as the standard deviation of growth rates in accommodation places and proxy system scale by average capacity. A log–log model, estimated with robust and bootstrap procedures and complemented by spatial diagnostics, reveals a strong negative elasticity between scale and volatility: larger destinations exhibit systematically lower fluctuations, while smaller systems are more unstable. Once scale is controlled for, the widely assumed coastal-inland divide in volatility largely disappears, and the independent contribution of spatial location becomes negligible. These findings indicate that structural stability in regulated accommodation capacity is strongly associated with tourism-system scale rather than being solely attributable to geographical location. The paper contributes to destination marketing and management by: (i) using supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility as an indicator of structural destination stability, (ii) providing evidence of a negative association between municipal tourism-system size and supply-side accommodation-capacity volatility, and (iii) qualifying spatially grounded interpretations of coastal stability. Title: MambaFusion: Registration-assisted lumbar CT-MRI image fusion via Mamba and dynamic feature modeling
Abstract: Medical images play a pivotal role in clinical diagnosis, yet a single imaging modality often fails to provide complete anatomical and pathological information. Multimodal image fusion addresses this limitation by integrating complementary information from different modalities. In this study, a CT-MRI registration and preprocessing procedure was first introduced to reduce spatial mismatch between lumbar CT and MRI images. The MRI volume was registered and resampled into the CT coordinate space, ensuring spatial consistency before image fusion. Landmark-based registration evaluation across 30 patients showed that the mean target registration error (TRE) decreased from 26.725 ± 0.847 mm after geometry-based initialization to 2.808 ± 0.983 mm after final rigid registration, corresponding to an 89.49% reduction. Experiments on registered lumbar CT-MRI images demonstrate that MambaFusion achieves competitive visual quality and quantitative fusion performance compared with existing methods. The fused images preserve CT-derived vertebral bone structures while retaining MRI-derived soft-tissue information, providing a complementary multimodal representation for lumbar spine imaging. Title: Will this time be different? Just transition pathways in eastern and Southern Africa’s critical minerals sector
Abstract: The global energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for critical minerals required for renewable energy technologies like solar panels, wind turbines, and battery storage systems. However, the future translation of mineral reserves into equitable socio-economic development in the region depends on policy frameworks and governance systems that promote inclusive participation, recognition, and benefit-sharing. This paper examines pathways for inclusive economic transformation, analyzing the conditions required to ensure mining-affected communities benefit equitably from the critical minerals boom. We employ a justice-centered framework of distributional, procedural, recognition and restorative justice to analyze five countries (Democratic Republic of Congo, South Africa, Zambia, Malawi, and Burundi) through stakeholder interviews with 43 actors and document and policy analysis, including Malawi and Burundi, whose emerging sectors are largely absent from the peer-reviewed record. Across the five cases the four dimensions are not encountered as separate problems. Findings suggest that employment opportunities do not always reach local populations, revenue mechanisms face transparency challenges, consultation processes have limited influence over outcomes, customary tenure is inconsistently recognized, and environmental legacies often persist without adequate remediation. Title: Aggregation and clustering of the multi-agent dynamics with density-dependent influence

Title: Determining the robust drivers of CO2 emissions in Africa: Machine learning and panel econometric evidence on the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis
Abstract: One of the primary greenhouse gases linked to global warming is carbon dioxide. This study investigates the determinants of carbon dioxide emissions in 29 African countries over the period 1990–2023 using a two-stage machine learning and econometric framework. In the first stage, Classification and Regression Trees, Random Forests, and Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithms are employed to identify the most important drivers of carbon dioxide emissions. The results indicate that Random Forests provide the highest predictive performance among the machine learning models. In the second stage, the variables identified by the machine learning analysis are incorporated into second-generation panel estimators that account for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity. Specifically, long-run and short-run relationships are examined using the Common Correlated Effects Autoregressive Distributed Lag estimator, while Augmented Mean Group, Common Correlated Effects Mean Group estimators, and Fixed Effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors are employed as robustness checks. The findings reveal that oil consumption is positively associated with carbon dioxide emissions, whereas renewable energy consumption is negatively associated with carbon dioxide emissions. The results provide limited but supportive evidence for the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis, with income and income-squared terms exhibiting the expected signs and the estimated turning point falling within the observed income range. Robustness analyses based on oil-exporting and non-oil-exporting country groups, as well as an alternative carbon-intensity measure, confirm the central role of fossil fuel dependence and renewable energy adoption in shaping environmental outcomes across Africa. These findings highlight the importance of accelerating renewable energy deployment, reducing reliance on fossil fuels, improving energy efficiency, and promoting sustainable development strategies to achieve long-term environmental sustainability in African economies. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Political elites and access to economic opportunities in China's rural market transition
Abstract: Understanding whether political elites maintain advantages in accessing economic opportunities during market transitions is crucial for assessing the distributional consequences of market-oriented reforms. Title: Automating execution and verification of BPMN+DMN business processes
Abstract: The increasing and widespread use of Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) business processes, which also incorporate Decision Model and Notation (DMN) tables, necessitates tools and methodologies to verify their correctness. This forces business processes designers to manually run single executions of their BPMN + DMN processes using proprietary tools in order to detect failures. Title: Flexible computational loads as demand-side resources for surplus renewable energy: A review of siting criteria, thermal management, and operational strategies
Abstract: Renewable curtailment often occurs behind local transmission constraints, yet studies rarely examine whether flexible loads are located where surplus arises. Title: Interfacial charge redistribution regulates surface hydroxyl dynamics during photocatalytic nitric oxide oxidation

Abstract: Water can replenish reactive surface hydroxyls during photocatalytic nitric oxide (NO) oxidation, yet excessive hydration blocks adsorption sites. Title: Student perceptions of generative AI in accounting education: A thematic analysis
Abstract: Generative AI has outpaced pedagogical and ethical guidance in accounting classrooms, leaving students and educators uncertain whether it supports or undermines the discipline's dual emphasis on procedural accuracy and professional judgment. To address this problem, this study examines how 92 business undergraduates perceive generative AI tools, notably ChatGPT, in accounting education, drawing on in-class, handwritten survey responses. Findings show that students view AI as a useful yet uncertain resource: valuing its speed, accessibility, and support while raising concerns over cheating, fairness, unclear institutional policies, and overreliance. Four interconnected themes emerged: Practical Affordances and Engagement, Ethical Tensions and Integrity, Curricular and Institutional Context, and Reflective Learning and Active Engagement. These results suggest student perceptions are shaped less by technology alone than by the pedagogical and ethical conditions of its introduction. Theoretically, the study identifies an augmentation–formation paradox specific to disciplines that combine codifiable procedure with professional judgment, which is advanced tentatively as extending the boundary conditions of paradox theory in education, a proposition that requires further empirical testing. Thematic analysis using a hybrid inductive–deductive coding strategy served as the primary analytic approach, supported by supplementary lexical analyses. The study contributes to management and accounting education by demonstrating that responsible AI integration requires clear guidance, reflective learning, and explicit alignment among AI use, assessment design, and academic integrity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Wang T.; Liu Y.; Wu J.; Wei X.; Li Z.; Zhao F.; Sun Y.; Fan C.; Wang Y.; Jiang Z.
Title: Covalent Organic Framework Membranes through Sequential Imine Exchange for Precise Molecular Separation
Abstract: Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes with high crystallinity hold great promise in precise molecular separation, but often suffer from the intercrystalline defects and thus poor membrane-formation ability. This study reports a sequential imine exchange strategy to fabricate highly crystalline, defect-free COF membranes for precise molecular separation. Two functional amines (aromatic and aliphatic amines) are employed in highly reversible imine exchange reaction to separately conduct crystallization and defect remedy processes according to their different energy gaps. Aromatic amine, which serves as COF framework building unit, undergoes the first-step imine exchange for high crystallinity because of its lower energy gap. Afterward, the hyperbranched aliphatic amine with abundant amino groups undergoes the second-step imine exchange, affording the tight connections between adjacent crystals and the excellent membrane-formation ability. Accordingly, the COF membrane exhibits high permeance (344 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 for water, 462 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 for methanol) and rejection (> 99.9% for Congo red and Alcian blue). Meanwhile, the membrane is endowed with an ultrahigh separation factor (> 528) for mixed dye aqueous solutions and large-scale processability (> 290 cm2). This work offers a new strategy to fabricate highly crystalline and defect-free COF membranes, revealing their large potential in diverse practical applications. Title: Driving sustainable development goal alignment through green consumption marketing and public mind
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable development demands synchronized efforts across socioeconomic and environmental domains, specifically targeting poverty alleviation, food security, and environmental stewardship. Although sustainable consumption patterns and ecological marketing act as established catalysts for environmental transitions, the specific socio-civic pathways translating micro-level pro-environmental behaviors into macro-level policy alignment remain underexplored. To bridge this gap, the study objectives were to evaluate the direct and indirect pathways through which green consumption behavior and green marketing drive local alignment with the sustainable development goals through the mediating role of the public mind among residents in Nonthaburi Province, Thailand. METHODS: A quantitative survey design was executed to gather data from 400 residents across administrative districts in Nonthaburi Province using proportionate stratified random sampling. The researchers collected primary data through structured questionnaires employing a 5-point Likert scale. Analytical procedures encompassed descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling to validate construct relationships and assess overall structural model fit. FINDINGS: The results of structural equation modeling indicate that both green consumption behavior and green marketing significantly influence the realization of local sustainable development goals, operating through both direct pathways and indirect pathways mediated by public consciousness. The public mind demonstrated the strongest direct influence on sustainable development goals realization (β = 0.69, p < 0.01), followed by direct impacts from green consumption behavior (β = 0.35, p < 0.01) and green marketing (β = 0.28, p < 0.01). Additionally, green consumption behavior was the primary driver of public mind activation (β = 0.37, p < 0.01), surpassing green marketing (β = 0.27, p < 0.01). The validated structural model accounted for substantial variance in sustainable development goals alignment (R^2 = 0.97) and the public mind (R^2 = 0.77). CONCLUSION: Green consumption behavior and green marketing are critical precursors to cultivating a collective public mind, which bridges individual eco-conscious actions with macro-level alignment of Sustainable Development Goals. Municipal authorities ought to embed the mobilization of public ecological awareness into environmental governance policies. Furthermore, this structural framework offers a scalable model adaptable to other rapidly urbanizing provinces in Southeast Asia. Authors: He Z.; Deng N.; Guo S.; Xiong T.; Lu Z.Y.; Li X.R.; Chen R.
Title: TikTok as a stage: How short video creators’ identity performance drives engagement with tourism experiences
Abstract: Destinations are increasingly collaborating with short-form video creators to engage consumers. Through Goffman's dramaturgical lens, this study explores how creators' performed identities in travel videos relate to audience responses. Combining machine learning and AI-powered analyses of over 10k short-form videos and 176k viewer comments with a controlled experiment, we identified four identities that creators performed in these videos (the “showman,” “diarist,” “docent,” and “photographer”) and classified them at scale. Results showed that identity performance is associated with distinct configurations of audiences' behavioral engagement. The “docent” generated more audience engagement than other identities, including audiences' learning, endorsing, and intending to participate dimensions. Guided by the knowledge gap theory, a subsequent experiment showed that the “docent” identity increased engagement by sparking curiosity. These findings guide content creators in adopting effective identity performance strategies, destinations in partnering with well-aligned content creators, and platforms in using algorithmic curation to achieve desired marketing outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Recursive self-regulation in genAI-assisted experiential learning: A task-contingent model
Abstract: Existing literature on generative AI (genAI) in business education has examined students’ attitudes, motivation, and the ethics of genAI use, alongside ongoing debate about whether genAI over-reliance may diminish self-regulated learning (SRL). However, how students self-regulate their learning while working with genAI during authentic tasks remains under-explored. This study addresses this gap by examining (RQ1) how students' self-regulatory strategies manifest during genAI-assisted learning and (RQ2) how these strategies change through genAI interaction. A thematic analysis was conducted of 34 metacognitive reflections generated across two scaffolded, four-stage experiential learning activities in a Lean Startup unit. Findings inform a three-stage AI-mediated recursive loop model, comprising monitoring, strategic adoption, and limitation identification, that extends cyclical models of self-regulated learning by showing how regulation may be initiated within the task by genAI-generated suggestions. Within this structured, reflective learning context, students indicated evaluative judgement and metacognitive regulation, providing preliminary evidence that scaffolded genAI activities can elicit active rather than passive engagement. GenAI-supported cognitive deepening was task-contingent, emerging most strongly during applied refinement tasks. The model offers management educators a pedagogical process model for designing scaffolded genAI-assisted activities that elicit monitoring, selective adoption, and critical reflection. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Complex adaptive governance for sustainable tourism villages: Explanatory insights from combined polycentric and chaos theoretical perspectives
Abstract: Sustainable tourism villages face complex governance challenges because they must simultaneously support economic development, protect local culture, preserve ecological resources, and respond to changing social conditions. Existing studies have examined sustainable tourism governance mainly from administrative, community-based, or institutional perspectives, but less attention has been given to how distributed authority interacts with nonlinear adaptive dynamics in village-level governance systems. To address this gap, this study develops an integrated framework that combines polycentric governance theory and chaos theory. Using a quantitative explanatory design, survey data were collected from 590 stakeholders involved in tourism village governance across four regencies and one city in Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that institutional diversity has the strongest association with sustainable tourism village governance, followed by decentralization and local autonomy, bifurcation and cosmology, community participation, flexibility and adaptability, edge of chaos and the butterfly effect, and self-organization and strange attractors. The model yields a very high coefficient of determination, which suggests a close within sample fit between the proposed constructs and the observed perception data. This result is interpreted cautiously because the study is cross-sectional and several constructs are conceptually proximate. The study contributes to governance theory by showing that sustainable tourism village governance can be understood as both polycentric and complex-adaptive. Practically, the findings suggest that policymakers and tourism village managers should strengthen multi-actor coordination while maintaining flexibility to respond to uncertainty and local change. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Retreat in monastery stay tourism: the role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ connectedness and behavioural intention
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Monastery stay tourism is an emerging niche within spiritual and transformative tourism, offering immersive experiences that facilitate personal and emotional growth. Despite its rising popularity, limited research has explored how such experiences shape tourists' emotional bonds, identity formation, and revisit intention. Drawing on mindfulness theory, this study examines the role of mindfulness cultivated during Buddhist monastery retreats in influencing emotional solidarity, experience self-connection, place identity, and behavioural intention. Data were collected from 430 visitors and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (MGA). The PLS-SEM results underscore the critical role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ social interactions, emotional attachment to the destination, and self-connection, all of which significantly impact their intention to engage in spiritual retreats. Emotional solidarity and self-connection are found to significantly influence place identity and future behavioural intention. The MGA findings indicate that generational and experiential segmentation reveals that Generation Z is more responsive to mindfulness and experience self-connection, while older cohorts are more influenced by emotional solidarity. Repeat visitors report stronger mindfulness effects across all outcomes, whereas first-time visitors rely more on emotional bonding. These insights underscore the value of tailoring mindful retreat experiences to foster deeper engagement and sustained support for religious tourism destinations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Contextualized learning theory in practice: An assessment study of cultivating procedural vis-à-vis conceptual fluencies in operations management fundamentals through simulations
Abstract: Contextualized learning theory promotes effective learning by placing new information in meaningful contexts; however, despite its desirability among educators, identifying practical ways to apply this theory in specific classroom teaching remains an ongoing challenge. To that end, undergraduate business students often find operations management topics challenging to contextualize because of the inherently complex integration of theoretical concepts and methodical procedures that characterize the subject. Accordingly, instructors strive to identify viable instructional tools to help students overcome this challenge and achieve parallel mastery of the intertwined quantitative and qualitative aspects of operations management fundamentals. This paper presents the results of a comparative experimental study examining the effectiveness of simulation-assisted instruction in promoting contextualized learning in an introductory operations management course. The empirical results based on a quasi-experimental design showed that computer simulations enable students to experience contextualized learning, thereby enhancing their performance and fluency in understanding and applying OM concepts and techniques. On that note, performance-based assessment of learning outcomes revealed that students' conceptual fluency, as a reflection of their contextual efficacy, improved the most when simulations were used. Moreover, students' procedural fluency, as evidenced by their technical efficacy, was simultaneously improved, albeit to a lesser extent, when simulations were employed. Perception-based assessment of learning outcomes showed similar improvement patterns; however, unlike the performance-based results, these improvements did not reach statistical significance. The findings provide valuable insights into the utility of such instructional tools through a methodical inquiry into the objective and subjective assessments of polydimensional learning outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chen B.; Cheng X.; Li X.; Guan Q.; Li H.; Zhang Y.; Cheng S.; Li H.; Liu Y.; Zhang J.; Lin H.; Wang J.
Title: Decoupling Ion–Dipole Interactions via Competitive Coordination for Durable Dendrite-Free Zinc Metal Batteries
Abstract: Abstract: The aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are famous for high-safety and high-energy-density, but limited by severe challenges around the Helmholtz plane layer such as the strong ion–dipole interactions between Zn2+ and H2O, resulting in slow desolvation processes and limited transport kinetics as well as corresponding higher barriers. To reconstruct the ion–dipole surroundings, the interface chemistry of employing a high permanent dipole moment of L-Carnosine (L-CN) has been proposed, weakening the interactions between Zn2+ and H2O to realize a crowded Zn2+-conductive structure, accelerating the desolvation kinetics. As revealed, the strong affinity between L-CN and Zn2+ enables the L-CN molecules to repulse H2O, reconfiguring the inner Helmholtz plane layer, thereby inhibiting the active water molecular to form hydrogen evolution reactions. Consequently, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells with Helmholtz plane modulation achieve a long lifespan up to 7000 h, a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.72%, and a high stabilization at high depth of discharge (85.4%). The assembled Zn//V2O5−x full cell with optimal electrolyte delivers the capacity of 289 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g−1 under an N/P ratio of 3.98. Impressively, the large-scale pouch cell with optimal electrolyte stabilizes for 200 cycles, offering the bright future of reconstructing Helmholtz plane for achieving high-performance AZMBs. Title: Ballistic transport in nanoscale devices
Abstract: Ballistic transport refers to the condition where charge carriers traverse a conductor without scattering, where conduction is governed not by bulk properties but by how electrons are injected, transmitted, and collected at the boundaries. This review gives a unified and critical overview of ballistic transport in a wide range of nanoscale systems such as 1D/2D heterostructures, topological insulators, inorganic heterostructures, molecular junctions (MJs), perovskites, nanowire, nanosheet transistors etc. In these systems, charge carriers move over nanoscale length with near-zero momentum and phase-randomizing scattering. Starting with a historical and conceptual overview of ballistic transport, the conversation explains how the gradual reduction of device sizes below the elastic and inelastic mean free paths fundamentally invalidates diffusive transport models and requires a quantum-coherent description based on transmission eigenchannels, contact-limited resistance, and nonlocal electrostatics. We also discuss the key experimental signatures and theoretical ideas used to identify ballistic behavior, including conductance quantization, length-independent resistance, and nonlocal transport features. Finally, we critically evaluate the significant challenges that hinder the clear identification and technological utilization of ballistic transport and also outline future perspectives that are anticipated to convert ballistic transport from a mesoscopic phenomenon into a foundational principle for next-generation nanoelectronics and quantum devices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Employee cybersecurity awareness impact on cybersecurity posture of business organizations in Canada
Abstract: This study investigates the impact of employee cybersecurity awareness on the cybersecurity posture of business organizations in Canada, as the prevalence of cyber threats, such as ransomware, phishing, and data breaches, continues to rise. The study adopts Servant Leadership (SL) theory as the analytical framework, with particular emphasis on SL’s attributes of employee empowerment, training, and organizational culture as factors in building resilience against cyber threats. A systematic literature review (SLR) methodology was employed, drawing on peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 from databases including Google Scholar, Scopus, and Web of Science. The review process followed PRISMA guidelines, with rigorous application of inclusion and exclusion criteria, data extraction, and quality appraisal using the AMSTAR and CASP tools, resulting in 30 articles for the SLR. The findings reveal that organizations with strong servant leadership attributes, employee empowerment and training, combined with a cybersecurity-conscious culture, enhance employee cybersecurity awareness and training. The study further found that clear and consistently enforced policies are critical for guiding employee behaviour and fostering long-term adherence. The study recommends adopting targeted role-based and scenario-driven training approaches on cybersecurity for employees to improve their knowledge retention and threat response to cyberattacks for strengthening organizational cybersecurity posture in Canada. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

Authors: Arora L.; Jain S.
Title: Seeing through the mind: Explainable multimodal AI for depression detection—A review
Abstract: Depression detection using multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving, transitioning from traditional machine learning techniques to deep learning architectures built on pre-trained transformer encoders. These systems integrate textual, acoustic, visual, and physiological signal streams through early, intermediate, late, and hybrid fusion strategies to improve predictive performance. However, a significant gap persists in model interpretability: post-hoc attribution frameworks (such as SHAP and LIME) dominate recent work, accounting for over 70% of studies published in 2024–2025, while clinician-centered validation is reported in only about 18% of the full reviewed corpus. Consequently, existing explanations are rarely validated for explainability quality dimensions; for example, SHAP attributions are known to degrade under inter-modality collinearity, and reported systems frequently lack alignment with established diagnostic criteria (e.g., DSM-based or PHQ-9 symptom structures). To close the gap between predictive accuracy and clinical utility, this review jointly synthesizes multimodal datasets, feature extraction strategies, machine learning and deep learning taxonomies, fusion strategies, and explainability techniques across 72 included studies. Finally, we outline critical future directions, emphasizing standardized XAI benchmarks, clinician-in-the-loop validation studies, and knowledge-driven neuro-symbolic reasoning. © 2026

Title: Techno-economic analysis of hydrogen production utilizing offshore wind energy using the AHP method and the Weibull distribution approximation. A case of Sakhalin Island
Abstract: The study is devoted to assessing the suitability of the Sakhalin Island offshore zone for the development of a wind energy complex, with a focus on the potential production of green hydrogen. In the course of the research, the hierarchy analysis method was applied along with fuzzy logic. Criteria influencing the placement of wind farms were selected, experts in the field were interviewed to compile pairwise comparison matrices, after which the weights of these criteria were obtained. Using fuzzy logic functions, the absolute values of the parameters were unified. The territories where the construction of wind farms is undesirable were also taken into account. As a result, the final data set was obtained using the weighted linear combination method. As a result, it was possible to identify 4 zones with the best indicators of suitability for the construction of wind farms. The territories in the Gulf of Patience near the port of Poronaysk look the most promising. Based on the data collected, 8 promising locations within 4 zones have been identified. For each location, the potential amount of electricity and green hydrogen that can be produced has been calculated using the Weibull distribution model, with 6 different methods to parameter estimation. Six different turbine models have been used in the analysis. Additionally, LCOE (Levelized Cost of Energy) and LCOH (Levelized Cost of Hydrogen) calculations were conducted. As a result, the minimum LCOE calculated was 0.087 $/kWh and the lowest LCOH recorded was 7.4 $/kg. The Vestas V236-15.0 MW wind turbine demonstrated optimal performance for the study area. If actively invested in this area, this area could become an important hub for hydrogen trading in the Asia-Pacific region. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Tuning oxygen-proton coupling of oxygen electrodes to match electrolyte transport in reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells
Abstract: Understanding how oxygen-electrode functionality interacts with electrolyte transport is essential for advancing reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs), yet their coupling remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal an electrolyte-dependent performance reversal arising from the interplay between oxygen-proton coupled reaction pathways and electrolyte transport. Surface functionalization of BaCe0.5Pr0.3Y0.2O3−δ (BCPY) oxygen electrodes with Pr0.5Ba0.5CoO3−δ (PBC) and Ni-substituted Pr0.5Ba0.5Co0.5Ni0.5O3−δ (PBCN) perovskite coatings selectively tunes surface defect chemistry and reaction pathways. PBC promotes lattice-oxygen activation and oxygen-vacancy-mediated processes, whereas Ni substitution in PBCN suppresses vacancy formation while enhancing proton hydration through strengthened Co–O covalency and optimized adsorption of oxygen intermediates. Consequently, PBC-BCPY delivers superior performance on BaZr0.8Yb0.2O3−δ (BZYb) electrolytes with limited proton conductivity, whereas PBCN-BCPY outperforms on highly proton-conductive BaZr0.1Ce0.7Y0.1Yb0.1O3−δ (BZCYYb) electrolytes. Benefiting from the optimized coupling between electrode surface functionality and electrolyte transport, the PBCN-coated BCPY electrode achieves a peak power density of 1.88 W cm⁻2 and a current density of 2.57 A cm⁻2 at 700 °C and 1.3 V on BZCYYb, while maintaining stable operation for 300 h at 600 °C. This work establishes a mechanistic framework for tailoring electrode surface functionality to match electrolyte transport, offering new design principles for high-performance R-PCECs. © 2026

Title: Natural nano-fish bone as novel Pickering stabilizers: the emulsifying property
Abstract: Particles in the micrometer or nanometer range are widely used as stabilizers in Pickering emulsion systems. Nano-fish bone (NFB) could be an excellent stabilizer for Pickering emulsions, as it has the advantages of environmental friendliness and others. In this work, we prepared NFB particles through wet media milling treatment to investigate the mechanism behind the effect of adding NFB and peanut oil (PO) on Pickering emulsion formation and stability. The results suggested that increasing NFB resulted in increased particle coverage on the droplet surface, increased emulsion apparent viscosity, and improved stability. Similar changes in both apparent viscosity and emulsion stability were observed as the amount of PO increased. Therefore, the emulsifying properties and packing behavior of Pickering emulsions could be affected by NFB and PO content. This study provides a reference for the development of functional food-grade Pickering emulsions based on NFB stabilization. © 2026

Title: Rheologically Engineered 3D-Printed Highly Loaded Magneto-Dielectric Absorbers for Device-Level Electromagnetic Compatibility
Abstract: Highly loaded magneto-dielectric composite systems are promising for achieving strong electromagnetic loss and structural design flexibility, yet their processability and geometric controllability remain extremely challenging. Herein, a rheologically engineered direct ink writing (DIW) 3D printing strategy is developed. Graphene (Gr) is introduced to reconstruct the particle-loading network, which synergistically improves the ink’s yield behavior, shear-thinning property, structural recovery, and a magnetic–dielectric synergistic loss system is constructed with carbonyl iron powder (CIP). The critical CIP content (~ 84.06 wt%) is determined by the yield model, and a tunable Gr/CIP (GC) composite ink is obtained. The correlation among rheological response, geometric fidelity, and temporal stability is established, enabling high-fidelity 3D-printed gradient honeycomb structures. The rationally designed 3D-printed GC honeycomb (GCH) absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 18 GHz–4 THz, with an RLmin of − 84.30 dB at a thickness of 2.6 mm. When integrated into device-level terahertz reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), the GCH absorber contributes to a ~ 3.3 dBi main lobe gain enhancement, 1.9–3.3 dB sidelobe suppression, and a ~ 58% reduction in reflection beamwidth, showing excellent electromagnetic compatibility performance for communication, imaging, and radar. This work offers a practical strategy for the structural fabrication and device integration of high-load magneto-dielectric synergistic absorbers. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Beyond tool adoption: designing cognitive scaffolds in individual preparation to support critical thinking in generative AI integrated learning
Abstract: The integration of GenAI into higher education risks promoting passive information acceptance over critical thinking (CT), a challenge that is acutely felt in ill-structured problem-solving contexts such as engineering design. While cognitive scaffolds are recognized as a solution, limited research provides process-oriented evidence on how they mediate student engagement with GenAI. Currently, typical GenAI integration often leads to cognitive offloading where students bypass critical evaluation. To counter this automation bias, this study introduced a novel instructional framework that integrated the Preparation for Future Collaboration (PFC) paradigm with the Target-Criteria-Source-Analogy (TCSA) cognitive strategy to structure GenAI-supported learning. By analyzing the critical thinking patterns of 77 engineering undergraduates across high-, medium-, and low-performing groups, Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) identified distinct cognitive co-occurrence patterns across GenAI-supported preparation and subsequent AI-free collaboration. High-performing students showed stronger connections among Analysis, Evaluation, and Self-regulation, a pattern we interpretively describe as a “Triangulation Loop,” whereas low-performing students showed stronger connections between Interpretation and Analysis, described as a “Descriptive Loop.” The latter pattern was consistent with greater reliance on AI-generated information. Within the integrated PFC-TCSA instructional design, these observed patterns were characterized by stronger evaluative and self-regulatory co-occurrences, providing practical implications for designing human–AI collaboration. Title: Behavioral Economics as a Driver of Healthcare System Reform: Methodological Approach
Abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to develop and apply the Behavioral Economics in Health index as a methodological tool for assessing the role of behavioral strategies in healthcare reform, with particular attention to their impact on healthcare expenditure, life expectancy, and system-level adaptation in countries with varying levels of institutional maturity and economic capacity. Methods The research used system-dynamics-based simulation modeling using behavioral and economic parameters, followed by statistical analysis of the results. Results The AnyLogic simulation results showed that, under an intensive behavioral integration scenario for 2024 to 2034, per-capita health expenditure decreased by USD 200 in Ukraine and USD 190 in Poland. In these countries, the initial levels of behavioral integration were the lowest—0.51 and 0.59, respectively—and the 10-year increase was 0.30. This fact ensured a steady reduction in expenditure throughout the entire modeling period without significant fluctuations. In Denmark, where the initial behavioral integration level was higher (0.88), the decrease amounted to only USD 26 per person, indicating a limited effect of further behavioral interventions in an already prevention-oriented healthcare system. Conversely, in the United States, where the integration index was even higher (0.91), expenditure increased by USD 20.72 per capita. Conclusions These findings indicate that the maximum economic effect of behavioral strategies is achieved in countries with low initial levels of integration and limited resources. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhou Y.; Wang J.; Gao J.; Wang K.; Lu H.
Title: An integrated analytical framework for natural gas pricing: combining multi-source drivers, forecast enhancement, and model interpretability
Abstract: With the global pursuit of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), accurate forecasting and mechanistic interpretation of natural gas pricing have become increasingly important. As a transition fuel in the shift toward a low-carbon energy system, natural gas plays a vital role in balancing energy accessibility and environmental sustainability. However, rising economic uncertainty and geopolitical risks present significant challenges to effective price forecasting and policy formulation. In response, we develop a data-driven analytical framework for natural gas pricing that integrates feature engineering and forecast enhancement to achieve accurate point-interval forecasts and investment timing. Leveraging advanced explainability techniques, the framework systematically uncovers the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in global gas market drivers. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional models in predictive accuracy and reveals important lag effects and interaction mechanisms among influencing factors. These findings validate the framework's ability to support pricing decisions and risk hedging for energy enterprises, and to provide scientific evidence for regional energy policymaking through quantification of heterogeneity. Ultimately, it offers key support for improving resource allocation efficiency and advancing the achievement of SDG targets. © 2026

Title: Trend-risk vs trend-of-risk in portfolio optimization context
Abstract: This paper examines two highly relevant, distinct perspectives on trend-depending risk in portfolio decision-making, building on Neděla et al. (2024). In particular, trend-risk, which incorporates trend information extracted from asset cumulative returns, and the newly proposed trend-of-risk (ToR), which focuses on the temporal trend of the risk measure itself. We study and propose portfolio optimization frameworks that explicitly differentiate between these approaches. Additionally, we demonstrate how they lead to fundamentally different allocation outcomes despite identical instantaneous risk levels. By embedding the ToR as a dynamic penalization term, the framework captures the direction and persistence of risk evolution and enables a more forward-looking risk-aware allocation. The empirical findings highlight the conceptual and practical implications of treating risk trends as an intrinsic optimization input rather than a by-product of return dynamics on different markets. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Distributed gradient descent algorithm for robust kernel-based regression

Abstract: In this paper, we study the theoretical underpinning of a gradient descent algorithm with a robust loss function in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) framework. Authors: Zeng Y.; Liu Y.; Mei L.
Title: Curriculum greenwashing in business statistics education: Institutional decoupling in responsible management education
Abstract: Business schools increasingly state commitments to responsible management education (RME), yet institutional commitment may not be consistently reflected in pedagogical change. This study examines curriculum greenwashing as a possible divergence between RME language in curriculum artifacts and corresponding evidence in teaching practice and student learning, without assuming deliberate intent. Drawing on institutional theory and decoupling, we test whether signatory status in the Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME) is associated with declarative, procedural, and consequential integration in undergraduate business statistics courses. Longitudinal multilevel data were collected from 215 students and 45 faculty members across 30 institutions across three waves. PRME status was positively associated with RME content in syllabi, whereas associations with reported teaching and student learning gains were not detected. Faculty-reported practices were positively associated with student learning gains. The PRME status × faculty quantitative teaching self-efficacy interaction was positive but did not reach conventional statistical significance; exploratory probing indicated a positive PRME association only at high self-efficacy. The study contributes a three-level audit framework for evaluating how institutional RME commitment is reflected across curriculum representation, reported teaching practice, and student learning, while underscoring the value of evidence beyond syllabus language alone. © 2026

Title: Recurrent and eroding challenges in creative tourism: A longitudinal study of entrepreneurial resilience among urban handicraft artisans
Abstract: Despite the growing importance of creative tourism in emerging economies, the temporal nature of the challenges facing artisans—and the resilience strategies they employ—remains poorly understood. Grounded in the processual entrepreneurial concept, this study explores how handicraft artisans understand the challenges they face and how they enact resilience in response. Adopting a longitudinal interpretivist approach, the study examines the entrepreneurial resilience of urban handicraft artisans in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, across a period of compounding crises, including the pandemic, political instability, and socioeconomic volatility. The study identifies a novel “recurrent–eroding” dichotomy as a framework for understanding challenge temporality and three resilience enablers, namely personal resources, social support networks, and operational responses. Theoretically, the study introduces new typologies of entrepreneurial challenges and extends resilience theory in creative tourism. Practically, it provides critical insights for policymakers, advocating for institutional shifts from crisis-response measures to strengthening accountable support mechanisms, market linkages, and protections for cultural work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Embodied cognition and the luxury hospitality experience of in-flight wine in premium cabins
Abstract: This study explores how first- and business-class passengers experience in-flight wine as luxurious, even though flying reduces taste and smell. Drawing on embodied cognition theory, we argue that passengers do not simply judge wine by its quality. They build a sense of luxury by noticing how the airline tries to compensate for sensory limits, by feeling that the service fits their bodily experience, and by responding emotionally. We surveyed 500 premium-cabin passengers and used two analytical approaches: structural equation modeling and necessary condition analysis. The results show two related paths to luxury: a cognitive path, in which the service feels consistent with the passenger's bodily state, and an affective path, in which the service creates positive emotions. For first-class passengers, both paths had to reach a minimum level for luxury to emerge. For business-class passengers, the cognitive path was more important, and positive emotions were less essential. These findings help airlines design in-flight wine service that still feels luxurious despite the sensory challenges of air travel. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liang Y.; Chen R.; Zeng Y.; Yin S.
Title: Beyond participation: Creativity and entrepreneurial mindset across instructional modes and learner-level digital conditions in entrepreneurship education
Abstract: Entrepreneurship education is often examined as a uniform educational exposure, although its associations with student development may depend on instructional mode and learner-level digital conditions. This study compares six entrepreneurship education formats and examines their associations with two self-perceived outcomes—creativity and entrepreneurial mindset—while assessing whether these relationships vary by perceived digital literacy and functional social media use. Drawing on survey data from 1181 graduating students at a multidisciplinary university in Guangdong, China, we use propensity score matching to improve comparability between participants and non-participants on observed characteristics and estimate interaction models to assess conditional relationships. The results indicate that entrepreneurship education is more consistently associated with entrepreneurial mindset than with creativity. Business plan competitions, training programs, and practical workshops generally show comparatively strong associations, particularly relative to entrepreneurship courses, although public lectures are also notably associated with entrepreneurial mindset. Perceived digital literacy displays a selective and format-dependent moderating relationship with creativity but does not consistently moderate the relationship with entrepreneurial mindset. Functional social media use shows no stable moderation in the primary binary models, while supplementary continuous-measure models reveal some operationalization-sensitive patterns. These findings indicate that entrepreneurship education is best understood as a heterogeneous set of learning experiences whose associations with student development vary across instructional modes, developmental outcomes, and learner-level digital conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Optimal telepresence experience in heritage tourism: A multidimensional scale and its impact on tourist behavior
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly being integrated into on-site heritage tourism, yet little is known about how visitors evaluate hybrid experiences combining physical heritage environments with VR-mediated reconstructions. To address this gap, drawing on telepresence and flow theory, this study conceptualizes and validates Optimal Telepresence Experience (OTE) as a higher-order experiential construct reflecting visitors' overall technology-enhanced heritage experiences. Using a multi-stage scale development process with data collected at a heritage museum in Hue, Vietnam, the study develops and validates the OTE measurement instrument. The findings show that OTE, reflected through emotional, cognitive, and functional dimensions, strengthens visitors’ memory formation and revisit intention. Theoretically, the study advances immersive tourism research by conceptualizing and validating OTE as a higher-order experiential construct for hybrid technology-enhanced heritage experiences. Title: Designing sustainability communication across behavioral effort levels: How AI-generated micro-videos shape pro-environmental intentions
Abstract: The sustainability communication literature treats communication formats as functionally substitutable, overlooking how effectiveness may depend on the effort required to perform targeted behaviors. Drawing on processing fluency theory, this research uses perceived behavioral effort and procedural demands as an organizing lens for examining message effectiveness. Focusing on AI-generated micro-videos, the study examines how different formats influence hotel guests’ perceptions and pro-environmental intentions. Across three experiments, Study 1 demonstrated that dynamic AI-generated videos outperformed static signage, although the effect could not be attributed solely to AI generation. In Study 2, instructional clips enhanced perceived message fluency and task–technology fit for lower-effort behaviors, but not pro-environmental intentions. In Study 3, instructional clips significantly enhanced all three outcomes for higher-effort, rule-based behaviors. The study enriches sustainability communication theory by highlighting the value of explicit instructional guidance and offers actionable recommendations for designing hospitality sustainability initiatives in unfamiliar tourism service settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: How they collaborate matters: collaboration modes and task fit in human-AI recommendations
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Human-AI collaboration is increasingly used in online product recommendation, yet it remains unclear how consumers interpret different role configurations and when such configurations facilitate adoption. Drawing on mind perception theory, we argue that collaboration mode signals the collaborative system's task-relevant capability profile, and that its effectiveness depends on whether this profile fits the judgment-support requirements of search versus experience goods. Evidence from one field experiment and two scenario-based experiments indicates that AI-dominant collaboration is more effective for search-good recommendations, whereas human-dominant collaboration is more effective for experience-good recommendations, and that this fit effect is mediated by perceived diagnosticity. In addition, AI empathy functions as a compensatory interaction cue, improving consumers' evaluations of AI-dominant collaboration in experience-good contexts by enhancing perceived diagnosticity and recommendation adoption intention. Overall, this research moves product recommendation research beyond simple comparisons between human and AI sources toward a consumer-centered understanding of visible collaboration modes, while also offering implications for the design of more effective human-AI collaborative recommendation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Food hypersensitivity communication across physical and online foodservice menus in Brazil: fragmented regulation and consumer experiences in a mixed-methods study
Abstract: Inadequate communication of food hypersensitivity in foodservice settings is a recognised risk to consumer safety, yet in Brazil no national regulation governs disclosure in non-prepackaged foods. This study characterises how food hypersensitivity is communicated through physical and online foodservice menus across Brazilian cities, and whether communication differs by the presence of local legislation. A convergent mixed-methods study assessed food hypersensitivity communication in 1034 menus (323 physical; 711 online) from 18 Brazilian cities (seven with specific legislation, 11 comparators). Menus were classified by format: no information; ingredient-only; emphasised (typographic highlighting); or symbol/code-based (icons, codes or matrices). Four focus groups with 18 participants explored experiences of adults with food allergy, intolerance or coeliac disease, and parents of children with food allergy or coeliac disease. Most menus provided some information, predominantly ingredient-only (physical: 76.2%; online: 88.0%); few provided none (6.5%; 1.0%). Warning messages were uncommon (physical: 11.1%; online: 0.1%). Explicit food hypersensitivity information was more frequent in regulated than unregulated physical menus (regulated: 24.5%; unregulated: 12.7%; p < 0.001). Higher average customer expenditure predicted explicit information (OR = 3.46), and the effect of local regulation depended on establishment type (interaction p < 0.001). Regulation was associated with explicit information among independent establishments (OR = 8.29) but not among chains (OR = 0.55), which provided it at comparable levels regardless of regulatory context. No regulatory effect was observed online, where local laws rarely apply. Consumers valued clear, visually salient formats — icons and complete ingredient descriptions — and identified hidden hypersensitivity-relevant ingredients in composite dishes and inconsistent staff guidance as key barriers, particularly on delivery platforms. This is the first assessment of food hypersensitivity communication in Brazilian foodservice, showing that subnational regulation is associated with more explicit physical-menu communication among independent establishments. Establishments require structured communication and staff training; delivery platforms need mandatory disclosure fields and standardised warnings; policymakers should prioritise structured allergen fields on delivery platforms, with a national framework as a longer-term objective. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Chen N.; Huo L.
Title: A new three-layer metapopulation networks model coupling online-offline social interactions with epidemic spread
Abstract: The dissemination of epidemic-related information can effectively enhance public awareness of preventive measures and decrease infection risks. However, information dissemination through multiple channels, including both online and offline sources, and the dynamics of information dissemination across these channels are influenced by individual mobility. To address this gap, this study develops a three-layer metapopulation network coupled model that integrates online information dissemination, epidemic spreading, and offline information dissemination. The proposed model systematically investigates the patterns of information dissemination through both online and offline channels, as well as the epidemic reaction–diffusion process driven by individual migration. Furthermore, the social interactions dynamics of both information channels are influenced by migration, manifested as migrated individuals acquire offline information in destination patches and establish online connections with individuals residing there. Theoretical analysis using the Microscopic Markov Chain Approach (MMCA) derives epidemic thresholds, while Monte Carlo (MC) simulations validate the model and examine factors influencing propagation dynamics. Results indicate that migration enhances individuals’ offline information acquisition, and accelerates cross-patch online information dissemination. Both online and offline information interactions exert inhibitory effects on epidemic spread, effectively increasing the infection threshold and reducing the outbreak scale. Furthermore, increasing the connectivity and dissemination rate of online information, particularly the information dissemination via weak relationships between patches, can effectively inhibit epidemic outbreaks. Notably, when the suppression effect of information on the epidemic is weak, population migration facilitates epidemic spread. In contrast, when the suppression effect is strong, migration-driven information dissemination significantly reduces the probability of infection, thereby further suppressing the outbreak. Title: Wastewater heat recovery systems for sustainable building energy efficiency and decarbonization: A comprehensive review with practical insights
Abstract: Growing energy demand and carbon emissions pose a major challenge to the building environment, particularly in addressing heating and cooling needs sustainably. In this context, wastewater is recognized as an unconventional and largely untapped thermal energy resource due to its consistent supply and generally stable temperature. Wastewater heat recovery has the potential to significantly improve building energy efficiency and boost decarbonization efforts. This review provides a comprehensive and system-level assessment of wastewater heat recovery technologies for building- and district-scale applications, with particular emphasis on heat extraction locations, heat exchanger configurations, and wastewater source heat pump systems. Rather than treating individual components in isolation, the study integrates heat exchanger and heat pump technologies within a unified framework to support practical design and implementation decisions. State-of-the-art literature covering wastewater characteristics, recovery locations, heat exchanger technologies, and combined wastewater heat exchanger-heat pump systems is critically analyzed through comparative evaluation of performance indicators, benefits, and limitations. Key recovery locations, including building outlets, sewer networks, and wastewater treatment plants are examined in terms of thermal potential, operational constraints, and system compatibility. The review highlights that appropriately selected heat exchangers and wastewater source heat pump configurations can significantly improve energy recovery efficiency while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Finally, practical recommendations are provided to guide the selection, installation, and integration of wastewater heat recovery systems, identifying fouling control, system optimization, and data-driven design as critical factors for advancing wastewater as a viable unconventional thermal energy resource in modern building energy systems. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Individual entrepreneurial orientation in Spanish university students: The role of critical thinking disposition and intellectual styles in entrepreneurship education
Abstract: This study proposes a model that links students' disposition toward critical thinking (DTCT), Type I intellectual styles (oriented toward creativity, cognitive complexity, and autonomy) and Type II intellectual styles (oriented toward structure, conformity, and rule adherence), and individual entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) in higher education. A cross-sectional survey was administered to 208 students enrolled in entrepreneurship-related courses at a Spanish public university, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results show that DTCT is a strong positive predictor of IEO; Type I intellectual styles are positively related to both DTCT and IEO, whereas Type II styles display negative relations with entrepreneurial orientation. DTCT improves the effect of Type I styles on IEO, but not with Type II styles. These findings suggest that strengthening DTCT is a central pathway through which entrepreneurship education can enhance students' IEO. Title: Integrated system dynamics modeling for sustainable fisheries provisioning services
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Fisheries provisioning services deliver food production, livelihoods and ecosystem functions, but are increasingly under pressure from environmental degradation, declining fishery resources and socio-economic stressors. Traditional paradigms in fisheries governance often exhibit a deficiency in accounting for the multidirectional feedback loops linking ecological systems with socio-economic dynamics. The objectives of this study were to develop an integrated system dynamics model to assess interactions between these dimensions and identify management options to improve fisheries provisioning services through long-term scenario simulations. METHODS: A system dynamics model was integrated, consisting of social, environmental, and economic sub-models using primary and secondary data from 2018-2023. The model includes population, fishermen, floating net cages, alternative employment, willingness to be a fisher, water quality and aquatic conditions, fish restocking, capture fisheries production, fisheries productivity, fish processing innovations, income, costs, and fisher's income. The model was verified and validated using the mean absolute error and average variation error metrics. Subsequently, predictive simulations were projected to 2045 under current, moderate, and optimistic scenarios. FINDINGS: Actual capture fisheries production declined by 88.9 percent, from 588,100 kilograms in 2018 to 65,035 kilograms in 2023 and was projected to decline to 31,179 kilograms by 2045 under current conditions. Under the moderate and optimistic scenarios, the number of floating net cages was modeled with an annual reduction rate of 30% and 35%, respectively. Production recovery commenced in 2027 under the moderate scenario and in 2026 under the optimistic scenario. Furthermore, target water quality conditions were achieved by 2041 and 2037, respectively, while fisher's net income reached positive values by 2034. CONCLUSION: The integrated system dynamics model underscores the potential for the sustainability of fishery production services through coordinated actions across social, environmental, and economic dimensions. The faster realization of target outcomes under the optimistic scenario highlights that proactive, coordinated interventions effectively expedite ecological restoration, fisheries output, and socioeconomic progress. This model offers a decision-support framework for assessing long-term fisheries management strategies. © 2027 The author(s). Title: Teaching AI governance in management education: A serious game for accountable decision-making under uncertainty
Abstract: Management education increasingly needs ways to prepare students for AI governance, yet students have limited opportunities to practise the organisational judgement involved in deployment decisions. This paper presents “Leading in the Age of AI”, a card-based serious game in which student teams assume asymmetric C-suite roles, make AI deployment decisions under constraints, and document their reasoning in Model Cards adapted from AI documentation practice. Conceptually, the paper frames AI governance education as accountable decision-making under uncertainty: students negotiate competing priorities, allocate scarce safeguards, respond to disruption, and prepare written accounts for scrutiny. The paper contributes a reusable game design, a pedagogical adaptation of Model Cards as justification artefacts, and design patterns for management-education contexts involving accountable decisions under uncertainty. An exploratory evaluation across two undergraduate cohorts used matched pre-test/post-test data (N=67), post-session evaluations, and descriptive artefact analysis of team-produced Model Cards (n=15). Students evaluated the activity positively and reported immediate confidence gains across knowledge, ethics, and governance composites (dz=0.44 to 1.00), while quiz gains were modest and not statistically significant. Model Card analysis suggests the activity generated inspectable governance reasoning, while leaving causal learning, retention, and transfer for future research. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Lehto X.; Lee Y.J.; Chen J.
Title: Dance as destination infrastructure: Toward a progress agenda
Abstract: Tourism destinations increasingly seek embodied, multisensory, and culturally meaningful experiences whose significance extends beyond immediate consumption. Yet tourism management still has a limited vocabulary for explaining how embodied cultural practices generate value across destination systems. This Progress paper uses dance as a focused and theoretically revealing case to address this gap. Rather than treating dance merely as entertainment, heritage representation, or event programming, we conceptualize it as relational, embodied cultural infrastructure through which patterned movement can organize encounters, carry cultural meaning across generations, and contribute to the character and capabilities of destinations. Title: Effects of a design thinking education program for kindergarteners: A mixed-methods study
Abstract: Children as young as three can engage in oral and visual planning when creating tangible objects from materials, yet it remains unclear whether such design competencies can be systematically strengthened in early childhood to cultivate future design thinkers and innovative creators. To evaluate a research-informed design thinking (DT) education program, we conducted a mixed-methods study. The quantitative component involved a quasi-experiment with 133 children ( M age = 5.22, SD = 0.86) from a Chinese kindergarten (intervention group: n = 68; business-as-usual comparison group: n = 65), where the intervention group received an eight-week DT program. Each child’s DT competence was assessed immediately before and after the intervention, followed by play-based interviews with 12 children (six per group). Child-level analyses indicated a statistically significant improvement in overall DT competence favoring the intervention group (Cohen’s d=0.38). However, gains were uneven across specific DT dimensions. Children showed more apparent gains in Empathize, Define, and Prototype, whereas no significant gains were observed in Ideate and Test. Furthermore, the youngest children appeared to show larger gains, whereas gender did not significantly moderate the intervention effects. Qualitative interviews provided insight into the cognitive processes underlying these developmental variations. Together, these preliminary findings may inform DT education research and practice in early childhood settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Kang K.; He M.
Title: Financing assistance and concession strategies of the transnational supply chain under liquidity shock
Abstract: How to deal with financial distress caused by liquidity shocks has become an urgent problem for firms. We provide a framework on how to clarify the role of financing assistance and concession strategies in the context of transnational supply chains and aim to help managers understand how to choose strategies. With a small liquidity shock, the buyer provides financing assistance to the distressed supplier, resulting in a bailout effect. When the cross-effect of tax difference and vertical shareholding is large, buyer financing can hedge bankruptcy risk more effectively. With a large liquidity shock, the distressed supplier files for bankruptcy. When the reorganization cost is small or moderate, the distressed supplier reorganizes, and concession effect and bidirectional predation behavior occur in the reorganization process. When the reorganization cost is large, the distressed supplier goes into liquidation. The results provide suggestions for financing and bankruptcy decisions of firms under liquidity shock. © 2025 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Title: Integrating theory of planned behavior and value-belief-norm framework to explain voluntary carbon offsetting intentions in aviation: Evidence from Vietnamese air passengers
Abstract: The aviation industry faces growing environmental criticism for its high greenhouse gas emissions, necessitating both technological and behavioral solutions to mitigate climate change. This study examines passengers’ willingness to pay for voluntary carbon offsetting programs by developing and empirically testing an integrated model combining the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Values-Beliefs-Norms (VBN) framework. Using data from 342 Vietnamese airline passengers, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze both direct and indirect relationships among key constructs. Results confirm that biospheric values significantly shape awareness of environmental consequences, moral responsibility, and personal norms, which in turn directly influence behavioral intention. Within the TPB framework, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control are strong predictors of the intention to participate in voluntary carbon offsetting, with perceived behavioral control exerting the largest effect. Mediation analysis reveals that attitudinal and normative pathways bridge moral and cognitive antecedents with behavioral intention, underscoring the complementary roles of rational and moral motivations. The integrated TPB-VBN model demonstrates considerable explanatory power, providing a useful framework for understanding pro-environmental behavior in aviation. This research extends theoretical understanding by linking ethical and volitional determinants of sustainable consumption and offers managerial insights for airlines and policymakers to design effective carbon offset communication, education, and engagement strategies.
