Title: Dynamic regulation of β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrillation by hydroxytyrosol: Structural and functional insights
Abstract: β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils (LGF) are promising emulsion stabilizers, while their limited antioxidant activity restricts wide applications. In this study, hydroxytyrosol (HT) was introduced at different stages of β-lactoglobulin (LG) fibrillation to investigate its effects on fibril structure and emulsifying function. HT introduced at the initial stage inhibited nucleation and β-sheet accumulation, while HT at the end of the lag phase interfered with fibril elongation, producing shortened fibrils. HT added at the end of the growth phase remodeled complexes structure, preserving the typical fibrillar architecture. Moreover, the LGF-HT complex prepared with 100 μM HT at the end of the growth phase (LGF8-HT100) showed the best emulsifying performance (EAI: 14.28 m2/g; ESI: 71.36%), and enhanced the resistance of LGF-stabilized emulsions to lipid oxidation, decreasing TBARS value from 68.03 μM to 28.74 μM. LGF8-HT100 stabilized emulsions also exhibited the highest interfacial protein adsorption percentage, and reduced intestinal FFA release from 75.67% to 62.04%, indicating enhanced resistance to enzymatic hydrolysis. Accordingly, surface hydrophobicity analysis showed that HT intervention at this stage retained a higher H0, indicating that the hydrophobic driving force stabilizing the fibrillar structure was largely preserved. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that HT formed stable hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions within a buried LG pocket, and engaged a distinct surface groove on the LGF core. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms by which HT regulates protein fibrillation and lay a theoretical foundation for the design of LGF-based emulsion stabilizers with enhanced antioxidant capacity and stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Sun Y.; Li L.; Gao J.
Title: Designing stateful enterprise control for budget commitments: Identity continuity, context-bound transitions, and controlled execution
Abstract: Enterprise information systems manage business objects with persistent control states across transactions and changing organizations, posing a stateful enterprise control problem that requires consistent alignment of object identity, valid state transitions, execution authority, and audit evidence over time. This study establishes design knowledge for such scenarios, focusing on budget commitments. Using design science research, it proposes three technology-independent principles: Commitment Identity Binding, Context-Bound State Transition, and Controlled Execution Boundary and Evidence. These principles are implemented in a three-layer artifact combining a Knowledge Graph (KG), a state-transition module (SAI), and an audit evidence generation module (AIG) for context representation, state control, and structured evidence generation. Evaluated on 18 months of enterprise data, expert cases, ablation tests, historical replay, safety checks, and experiments with 30 practitioners, the artifact yields key findings: state consistency does not guarantee evidential completeness, and accurate rule identification cannot ensure valid transitions without temporal context. Historical Replay successfully replicated all 90 test cases under original contexts. When substantive information was held comparable, structured evidence improved final-state and rule-basis judgments and reduced review time. This work provides integrated design knowledge for stateful enterprise control over persistent business objects. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Yoganandan G.; Monisha S.R.
Title: From brand hate to behavioral response: A recourse-contingent exit-voice-loyalty-neglect framework for digital consumer markets
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Three decades of brand hate research have mapped what triggers consumer hate and catalogued how hateful consumers respond, avoiding, switching, complaining, retaliating, subverting, without connecting these two halves through one behavioral logic. This paper closes that gap by importing the Exit-Voice-Loyalty-Neglect (EVLN) framework into the brand hate domain and extending it with a boundary condition the literature has ignored: structural recourse availability. Brand hate's dimensional profile, whether anger, contempt, aversion, or fear dominates, depends on whether its trigger is relational (betrayal, transgression, ideological incompatibility) or structural (algorithmic, platform-based, institutional unfairness), and this profile sets a default EVLN response tendency. Whether that tendency is realized depends on structural recourse, the inverse of switching costs, platform dependence, and powerlessness. When recourse is blocked, Exit tendencies redirect toward Voice where a channel exists, and toward Neglect, termed informed helplessness, where none does. We develop eight propositions specifying this redirection process, including a measurement-validity proposition showing informed helplessness is indistinguishable from loyalty in standard satisfaction measures, and a release proposition explaining how dormant hate resurfaces when conditions change. The framework helps managers and policymakers identify trapped haters and sets an agenda for measuring them. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Determinants of visit intention to Lake Toba geopark: The roles of publicity, destination awareness, destination image, and word of mouth
Abstract: Tourism research has increasingly emphasized the importance of communication and perception factors in shaping tourists’ behavioral intentions, particularly in sustainable tourism destinations such as geoparks. However, limited studies have comprehensively examined the interplay between destination publicity, word of mouth (WOM), destination awareness, destination image, and visit intention within the context of UNESCO Global Geoparks. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the relationships among these variables in the context of Lake Toba Geopark, Indonesia, by applying the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework. A quantitative approach was employed using a structured online survey distributed to 425 respondents who had previously visited Lake Toba Geopark. The collected data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS. The findings reveal that destination publicity does not significantly influence destination awareness or destination image. Similarly, destination awareness does not directly affect tourists’ visit intention. In contrast, WOM significantly influences destination awareness, while destination awareness significantly enhances destination image. Furthermore, destination image emerges as the strongest determinant of visit intention. These findings indicate that tourists’ behavioral intentions are shaped more strongly by interpersonal communication and psychological perceptions than by conventional publicity exposure. This study contributes theoretically by extending the application of the SOR framework in geopark tourism through the integration of publicity, WOM, awareness, and image variables into a single model. Practically, the findings suggest that tourism stakeholders and destination managers should prioritize strategies that encourage positive WOM, strengthen destination awareness, and enhance destination image through authentic tourist experiences and digital engagement. Ultimately, destination image plays a central role in encouraging tourists’ intention to visit Lake Toba Geopark. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Predictors of Death Related to Drug Use Disorder and Interpersonal Violence in North Africa
Abstract: Fatal interpersonal violence and deadly drug use disorder are serious social issues resulting from criminal behavior, which require effective intervention policies. Prior research on African countries is limited, and the potential association between the two issues, as described in the literature, has not been investigated. In this study, a statistical analysis was performed with R packages to identify factors that predict the death patterns related to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence, and to show empirical evidence for the association between drugs and violence in North Africa. Data on annual counts of deaths attributed to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence between 1990 and 2023 were collected, and a bivariate copula modeling approach was adopted to account for the dependence of the two counts. The findings show that socioeconomic factors, including per-capita gross domestic product, youth unemployment rate, and urban population, are significant predictors of these death counts, and statistical tests show a positive relationship between deaths related to drug use disorder and deaths caused by interpersonal violence. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: How do sustainability capabilities create retail performance over time? dynamic evidence from U.S. and Chinese retailers
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines how sustainability-oriented technological innovation, sustainable supply chain management, and corporate social responsibility relate to environmental and manager-reported organisational performance in retail firms over time. A multi-group hierarchical Bayesian continuous-time dynamic structural equation model estimates within-firm relationships, effects over one-, three-, and six-month intervals, time-varying mediation, and country differences. Technological innovation predicts environmental performance in both countries, but it strengthens sustainable supply chain management only in China. Sustainable supply chain management predicts organisational performance in both countries. Corporate social responsibility predicts environmental performance in both countries, while its direct short-run organisational effect is positive in the United States and negative in China. Environmental performance converts into organisational performance, and all three proposed indirect effects emerge, only in China during the focal six-month window. Exploratory analysis identifies integration-driven accelerators, evidence-driven pragmatists, and weakly-coupled drifters. The findings characterise retail sustainability as a dynamic conversion system with country-specific pathways to environmental and organisational outcomes; implications for individual customer responses require separate empirical testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Association of observed ramp-electrification status with APU runtime and turnaround performance: A staggered difference-in-differences analysis at a tropical ASEAN hub
Abstract: Ramp electrification can reduce aircraft auxiliary power unit (APU) use during turnaround, but operational evidence from tropical airports remains limited and sensitive to treatment-timing and implementation definitions. This study presents a replacement reanalysis of 7122 de-identified turnarounds across 20 stands at a tropical ASEAN hub from 1 March to 28 June 2025. Fourteen stands exhibited an observed transition to active treatment status, six remained never observed treated, and five first-observed treatment-date groups were identified. Because official commissioning records were unavailable, treatment timing was defined by the first observed active-treatment timestamp rather than independently certified go-live dates. A cohort-by-event interaction regression incorporated stand and calendar-date fixed effects and adjusted for aircraft body class, carrier, time of day, wet-day status, temperature, relative humidity, and rainfall. Supported post-treatment cohort-event coefficients were aggregated using cell-count weights, yielding a turnaround-weighted post-treatment estimand across the realized distribution of observed post-treatment turnarounds. Inference used CR1 stand-clustered covariance and a 9999-replication restricted-residual wild-cluster bootstrap- t . Observed treatment status was associated with a 5.874 min/turn reduction in APU runtime (95% CI −6.586 to −5.162; p < 0.001; wild-bootstrap p = 0.0001), approximately 32.0% of the eventually treated pretreatment mean. At 6.5 kg CO2e/min, this corresponds to 38.18 kg/turn of gross avoided APU-related CO2e, a deterministic transformation rather than a net-emissions estimate. Average turnaround time was +0.657 min/turn (95% CI −0.539 to 1.853; p = 0.281; wild-bootstrap p = 0.353), with variation across group-specific estimates, including +6.15 min/turn for the single-stand second treatment group; these differences are interpreted cautiously because post-treatment support and follow-up varied across groups. Joint pretreatment tests were not statistically significant for APU runtime ( p = 0.157) or turnaround time ( p = 0.528), although the earliest pooled APU lead was individually positive. The findings support a consistent association between observed electrification status and lower APU runtime while requiring caution regarding counterfactual comparability, causal interpretation, operational variation, and net-carbon interpretation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Historical document restoration via an Adversarial Frequency-aware Guidance Network
Abstract: Historical document restoration aims to recover clean and readable document images from complex degradations such as stains, ink corrosion, background noise, and missing strokes. Existing methods mainly improve restoration backbones, but often overlook how to expose the model to challenging yet residual-bounded degradations during training. To address this issue, we propose AFG-Net, a frequency-domain hard-sample learning framework for robust historical document restoration. The key idea is to use input-restoration residuals as online degradation cues, enabling the model to focus on degradation components that remain difficult to recover. Specifically, an adaptive frequency mask generation module constructs hard samples by selectively recombining residual degradations in the Fourier domain, while a complementary-mask objective regularizes frequency selection and improves degradation diversity during training. In addition, we design the restoration branch with a text-structure-aware restoration backbone to better preserve character strokes, text lines, and layout structures. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that AFG-Net achieves superior restoration performance in terms of image fidelity, OCR-oriented readability, and computational efficiency. © 2026

Title: Design and simulation of a renewable energy-based microgrid for Accra Technical University
Abstract: Rising electricity costs, coupled with the unreliability of the supply, are big challenges facing higher learning institutions in developing nations, where the use of fossil fuels in centralized power generation systems limits the efficiency of the systems in providing sustainable power services. In the case of Ghana, the challenges are more pronounced in urban-based institutions where the availability of electricity is essential in the conduct of learning, research, and administrative activities. This study outlines the design and techno-economic optimization of the microgrid system, powered by renewable energy, for Accra Technical University (ATU) in Ghana, with the aim of providing reliable energy services while minimizing the cost of energy production and its impact on the environment. Using HOMER PRO, the study developed the microgrid model, where the optimized microgrid is composed of a solar–battery microgrid, comprising 3400 solar panels, Schneider Core inverters, and lithium iron phosphate battery systems, where the simulation results indicate the ability of the microgrid system to generate energy that meets 100% of the energy demand, with the expected energy generated per annum being 3.35 GWh, while the autonomy of the battery is expected to be 68.5 h. Economically, the optimized design realizes a Net Present Cost of GHS 17.1 million and a Levelized Cost of Electricity of GHS 0.350/kWh, which reflects a significant reduction in electricity cost compared to traditional grid-connected supply. The optimized configuration supplies the full campus electricity demand primarily from solar-based generation supported by battery storage, thereby reducing dependence on conventional grid electricity and improving the environmental performance of the institution. Apart from the cost savings, the suggested microgrid design enhances the reliability of electricity supply, reduces the risk of power outages, and realizes a significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, which aligns with the renewable energy goals of Ghana. The results prove that renewable energy-based microgrids for university campuses are technically viable and economically justifiable. Title: ThreatNet: A multi-class dataset and LLM-based framework with class-imbalanced fine-tuning for life threat detection

Title: Perceived authenticity of AI-generated tourism video and destination attractiveness: An entity-referent correspondence perspective

Abstract: Grounded in the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how three authenticity dimensions of AI-generated destination portrayals, true-to-ideal, true-to-fact, and true-to-self, relate to destination attractiveness via parallel and sequential pathways of place imagination and mental simulation. Title: Biomimetic Gradient Porous Core–Shell Fibers with Enhanced Gas Sensing for CO-Temperature Dual-Mode Early Fire Warning
Abstract: Early fire detection systems that are highly sensitive are essential for reducing the impact of fire disasters. However, their development still faces significant challenges due to the lack of capability for simultaneous monitoring of both temperature and gas. Herein, we propose a facile coaxial wet-spinning strategy to fabricate a dual-parameter fiber sensor capable of simultaneously detecting carbon monoxide (CO) and temperature for early combustion warning. Title: Cognitive appraisal of illegitimate tasks and research creativity: dual reflective processing pathways in graduate education
Abstract: Although graduate students frequently encounter illegitimate tasks—assignments perceived as inconsistent with their research roles—little is known about how such tasks influence research creativity and through what cognitive mechanisms. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), a dual-pathway model is proposed in which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity through problem-solving pondering and affective rumination, with supervisor–student relationship quality as a moderator. Illegitimate tasks were associated with increased affective rumination, which interfered with sustained creative engagement. However, under high-quality supervisor-student relationships, illegitimate tasks were more strongly related to problem-solving pondering, which facilitated creative thinking. Title: Applied economic reasoning in air transport management: A question- and concept-level analysis of an airport business course
Abstract: Economic reasoning underpins business decision-making. Yet how it is taught and assessed in air transport management education remains underexplored. Drawing on final-exam data from an Airport Business course for non-specialists at a Japanese university, this study identifies aspects of assessed economic reasoning that appeared relatively more demanding. At the question level, the higher-difficulty side concerned airport network financing, restructuring, and public support, whereas the lower-difficulty side addressed charge pass-through, the club-good characteristics of small-airport services, and concession-contract risks. This concept-level pattern did not follow a simple foundational–advanced distinction, with positions varying across institutional contexts and concept co-occurrence. Title: Inner-supportive destinations for psychologically vulnerable solo travelers: A framework of narrative reconstruction and reintegrative stabilization
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: This study examines how inner-supportive destination experiences support psychological reconstruction among solo visitors reporting self-identified emotional disruption. Drawing on constructivist grounded theory and 30 in-depth interviews with domestic solo visitors to Da Lat, Vietnam, the research identifies a process through which pre-travel emotional disruption is gradually reorganized through destination experience. Findings show that participants did not travel merely for leisure or stress relief, but because burnout, grief, relational rupture, life transition, or identity uncertainty had unsettled their self-understanding. Inner-supportive affordances, including temporal deceleration, sensory softness, perceived safety, and supported solitude, reduced defensive pressure and created conditions for regulated emotional exposure. This exposure enabled narrative re-authoring, through which distressing experiences were reinterpreted and integrated into a more coherent self-understanding. Based on these accounts, the study proposes the inner-supportive destination framework, explaining how destination affordances, regulated emotional exposure, narrative re-authoring, participant-attributed reintegrative stabilization, and boundary conditions relate within a contingent process. Theoretically, the study extends destination marketing and management by distinguishing narrative reconstruction from restoration, healing, or emotional elevation. Practically, it offers guidance for designing vulnerability-sensitive destinations that support autonomy, low-pressure engagement, and safe solitude without making therapeutic claims. The findings invite broader applications of inner-supportive design across wellness, cultural, nature-based, and urban retreat contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From airplanes to classrooms: A cross-domain literature review of seating assignment models and methods
Abstract: Seating assignments play an important role in customer-focused managerial decisions, yet existing studies are frequently limited in scope to isolated application domains. This paper addresses this fragmentation through the first systematic cross-domain seating assignment literature review, analyzing publications via bibliometric analysis and examining assignment methods (including optimization techniques) across transportation (airplanes and trains), dining establishments, entertainment venues, and classrooms. Co-citation analysis reveals that research communities operate in separate networks despite addressing similar challenges using mathematical programming, heuristic approaches, stochastic simulation, and other operational research methods. Our cross-domain synthesis identifies technique transfer opportunities previously invisible due to research silos, such as applying restaurant group-seating strategies to airline passengers traveling together or entertainment venue considerations to dining table assignments. Title: An EOQ model with green degree and population size sensitive demand under pentagonal intuitionistic cloudy fuzzy environment

As a consequence, a study is proposed, developed and solved in a crisp environment. Then, the model is transformed into a fuzzy model by using a pentagonal intuitionistic cloudy fuzzy number. Title: Advanced oxidation pretreatment of biomass for preparation of carbon-based adsorbents with high CO2 capture performance
Abstract: The advanced oxidation system composed of FeSO4·7H2O/K2S2O8 was adopted to pretreat pear tree branches, before carbonization and KOH activation, successfully producing porous carbon materials with excellent CO2 adsorption performance. Mechanistic analysis indicated that physical adsorption played a primary role in the uptake process, with pore filling playing a key role. The pretreatment strategy significantly reduced the amount of activator required, while achieving synergistic optimization of the microporous structure and surface chemical properties and also markedly enhanced the CO2 adsorption performance of the resulting adsorbent. Title: From fabrication to function: Electrochemical characterization of hyaluronic acid-based biomimetic hydrogels in aqueous ethanol
Abstract: Oral flavor perception currently relies predominantly on human sensory evaluation, and artificial sensory systems capable of mimicking oral interfaces remain limited. While hydrogels have been explored as soft substrates, most are designed as passive matrices or signal transducers. Here, we move beyond conventional hydrogel sensors by reconstructing a chemically relevant oral mimetic interface using two indispensable and physiological components of the oral cavity: hyaluronic acid (HA) and mucin. Inspired by biology, we investigate a biomimetic hydrogel that combines human tongue–like properties with electrochemical responsiveness and apply it to aqueous ethanol systems. We demonstrate that this hydrogel functions not merely as a structural mimic but as a dynamic electrochemical interface. Comprehensive characterization of its structure, rheology, and biosafety confirms its suitability as a biomimetic material. Electrochemical analyses further demonstrate its capability to operate as a responsive interfacial in aqueous ethanol environments. The hydrogel exhibits solid-like viscoelastic behavior and good biocompatibility, providing a stable and secure soft interface for studies related to artificial sensory systems. Overall, this work establishes a biomimetic hydrogel for oral-inspired sensing and advances artificial sensory systems toward mechanisms rooted in interfacial biophysics rather than solely pattern-based recognition. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: From duality to triadic structuration: Coupling Agile agency, generative technology, and regulatory structure
Abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) increasingly permeates software development, Agile organizations face growing pressure to achieve continuous lifecycle compliance amid rapidly evolving regulatory demands. Classical Structuration Theory and its derivatives account for technology as either an instantiation of social structure or a medium for human agency; neither pole adequately captures GenAI's quasi-autonomous capacity to reshape organizational practices and give rise to new regulatory obligations. This study addresses this gap by developing Triadic Structuration Theory. Following an incremental design science research (DSR) paradigm, we develop this abstract design artifact through cycle-level intermediate artifacts, with cross-cycle knowledge accumulation. Cycle 1 derives a problem backlog of GenAI-induced tensions in Agile practice. Cycle 2 conceptualizes RegOps, showing how Agile agency adapts under regulatory pressure. Cycle 3 designs an EU AI Act-aligned model card template, showing how regulatory structure becomes embedded in generative technology. Cycle 4 explores GenAI-enabled solutions to ISO-related compliance barriers in an Agile company. Together, the evidence and knowledge accumulated within and across the cycles position generative technology as a third construct rather than a medium between agency and structure. Regulatory structure is embedded directly into it; it reshapes Agile agency through quasi-autonomous action, and its use to meet existing obligations may recursively generate new ones. The study extends Structuration Theory as a middle-range theory to Agile and GenAI contexts, and demonstrates how nested DSR with intermediate artifacts can support theory development. For practitioners, it offers guidance on leveraging GenAI for compliance, cautioning that it is a structural intervention rather than a one-off fix. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Microwave effects on the flavor and storage quality of ‘Nongke Nuo 336’ sweet corn
Abstract: Microwave (MW) technology, characterized by its convenience and efficiency, has demonstrated significant effects on extending the shelf life of agricultural products. This study investigated the impact of MW on flavor compounds, gene expression, and metabolic processes in sweet corn. The results indicated that after 6 days of storage at room temperature, MW-treated corn maintained 12.22% soluble solids content, reduced weight loss by 9.71%, and slowed the rate of hardness increase by 41.55%. Simultaneously, it reduced the expression of genes such as α-amylase (ZmAMY1), thereby hindering the conversion of sugars into starch. MW treatment significantly downregulated the expression of key enzyme genes involved in abscisic acid biosynthesis (ZmZEP, ZmCHIL2, and ZmCFAT), delaying postharvest senescence in sweet corn. Furthermore, MW treatment upregulated the expression of antioxidant enzyme-related genes, including peroxidase (POD), among others, enhancing the stress resistance of sweet corn and thereby extending its shelf life. Metabolomics analysis further revealed that MW treatment activated the corn's defense system, leading to the accumulation of isoquercitrin, and hyperoside, which improved its stress resistance. Notably, esters, ketones, alcohols, aldehydes, and methylated compounds, which are the main flavor components, significantly enhanced the flavor characteristics of sweet corn. These findings provide valuable insights into the effects of MW on the storage quality and flavor of sweet corn. © 2026

Title: Designing Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells with Self-Assembled Monolayer Hole Transport Layers
Abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as highly versatile interfacial materials in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), offering tunable molecular structures, favorable energy-level alignment, high optical transparency, and minimized non-radiative recombination losses. Subsequently, the fundamental aspects of SAMs are systematically discussed. Further, common preparation methods of SAMs are reviewed, along with the key challenges encountered in achieving uniform SAM coating. Based on this, recent progress in SAM-based PSCs is comprehensively summarized, including their applications in high-efficiency single-junction devices, perovskite tandem solar cells, and large-area photovoltaic modules. The crucial roles of SAMs in energy-level modulation, interfacial modification, defect passivation, and charge transport are highlighted. Finally, the remaining challenges and future prospects of SAMs in inverted PSCs are discussed, with particular emphasis on interfacial stability and long-term operational reliability. Title: Architecting Anode Current Collectors for Practical Anode-Free Alkali Metal Batteries
Abstract: Anode-free alkali metal batteries (AFAMBs) are emerging as a compelling strategy to surpass the cell-level energy density limits of Li-ion batteries while simplifying battery configuration. In these systems, the working anode forms in situ on a bare current collector and is continuously reshaped during cycling with a limited alkali metal inventory. As a result, the anode current collector is not merely a passive electron conductor, but a multifunctional interfacial platform that governs alkali metal nucleation, growth, stripping, and interphase evolution. This review examines the fundamental differences among anode-free lithium, sodium, and potassium systems and highlights key performance metrics for practical AFAMBs. Recent current collector engineering strategies developed for these chemistries are then summarized. Essential parameters shaping current collector design are identified, including electronic conductivity, alkali metal affinity, collector morphology, and interphase stability. Finally, practical design principles are presented to balance electrochemical performance with manufacturability under realistic operating conditions. This review aims to clarify the alkali metal-dependent design logic of current collectors and to provide guidance for the practical development of next-generation anode-free batteries. Title: Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) in business and management education for developing AI and prompt literacy
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into organizational practice has created an urgent need for business and management education to move beyond tool exposure toward meaningful skill development. This study develops and implements a Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) approach that embeds GAI within active learning environments to support students' AI literacy and prompt literacy. A central feature of the approach is the use of structured scaffolds, particularly the RACE framework (Role–Action–Context–Explanation), which guides students in designing prompts, evaluating AI outputs, and linking responses to theoretical concepts. The approach was implemented in an undergraduate Organizational Behavior course (n = 93) using an explanatory mixed-methods design. Quantitative results indicate significant improvements in both AI literacy and prompt literacy, including gains in knowledge, application, and ethical awareness. Qualitative findings show that students engaged with AI iteratively and reflectively, using it as a “co-thinker” to refine prompts, assess output quality, and connect AI-generated insights with course theories. Cognitive and metacognitive engagement emerged as dominant, while collaborative and ethical dimensions, though less prominent, contributed to students’ developing awareness of responsible AI use. The findings demonstrate that structured, pedagogically guided AI integration transforms AI from a passive information source into an active learning scaffold. The SAIL approach, supported by RACE, offers a practical and transferable pathway for educators seeking to prepare students to navigate AI-augmented professional environments with critical, reflective, and responsible judgment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Inflow modeling strategies designed to enhance the ecological sustainability of hydroelectric reservoir operation planning
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid global expansion of water infrastructure alters major rivers, causes severe biodiversity declines, and destabilizes aquatic ecosystems. Amid intensifying eco-hydrological pressures, accurate prediction of reservoir inflow remains imperative to safeguard downstream aquatic ecosystems, yet data-sparse tropical environments chronically impair the generalizability of deep learning architectures due to pronounced overfitting. The study objectives were to evaluate three statistical inflow modeling frameworks, representative of design-era hydrological understanding, against the observed 1998–2023 flow regime to identify the most reliable forecasting approach for supporting environmental-flow-informed reservoir operation planning under monsoonal variability. METHODS: Using a multi-decadal hydro-meteorological dataset from 1998 to 2023 ( n = 312 monthly time steps) at Karian Reservoir in Banten Province, Indonesia, three primary modeling approaches were tested: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average, Markov Chain, and Multiple Linear Regression. To rigorously assess model diagnostics and predictive performance across historical drought and wet regimes, the Pearson correlation coefficient, Kling-Gupta efficiency, and operational trajectory metrics were integrated. FINDINGS: Deterministic multiple linear regression achieved the highest overall predictive accuracy with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.74, a Kling-Gupta efficiency of 0.64, and a superior operational trajectory guideline correlation of 0.85. The observed enhancement in model efficacy stems from the methodical integration of lagged streamflow predictors that effectively characterize catchment-scale moisture persistence. Conversely, the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model exhibited the weakest diagnostic capability (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.62; Kling-Gupta efficiency = 0.60) due to systematic overestimation of dry-season baseflows, risking artificial inflation of safe water availability. Meanwhile, the stochastic Markov yielded a commensurate aggregate Kling-Gupta efficiency score of 0.66 and exhibited a superior proficiency in replicating long-term probability distributions. CONCLUSION: While Multiple Linear Regression shows the strongest performance for monthly operational scheduling, the Markov Chain model offers a complementary probabilistic framework for screening extended seasonal drought risk. Independent out-of-sample validation against a held-out 2019-2023 period revealed substantial performance degradation for both models (Multiple Linear Regression Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency declining from 0.61 to 0.02; Markov Chain Nash-sutcliffe efficiency declining from 0.28 to -1.01), directly evidencing non-stationary rainfall-inflow relationships. Ultimately, these results establish that the evaluated models serve as an initial decision-support tool for raw water allocation planning, though their sustained operational reliability necessitates systematic recalibration. Title: Waiting for Uganda’s first commercial ‘Pearl Sweet’ oil: Discourses on social and environmental impacts and safeguards
Abstract: Uganda discovered approximately 3.5 billion barrels of commercially recoverable oil reserves in 2006 and is poised to become a major oil producer in Sub-Saharan Africa. In assessing progress towards full–scale oil production, expected by the end of 2026, Uganda’s President referred to the country’s commercial crude oil as “pearl sweet”, highlighting its medium-to-heavy, highly waxy characteristics, relatively low sulphur content, and ease of refining. Despite the anticipated economic benefits, considerable debate persists regarding the potential social and environmental impacts of oil development and the adequacy of safeguards ahead of full–scale production. Drawing on experiences from established oil–producing countries, this paper examines how environmental and social impacts are framed, how safeguards are prioritised, and what this implies for Uganda’s emerging oil sector. Anchored in environmental justice and political ecology, the study adopts a sequential integrative design combining a systematic literature review with empirical insights from twelve purposively selected stakeholders in Uganda’s oil-producing districts and national regulatory institutions. The literature review used Boolean search strings that connected terms within conceptual blocks using OR and combined blocks using AND, following a PRISMA-guided process across Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar and institutional data bases. Of 1800 records identified, 95 key sources were retained for analysis. The findings indicate that, although Uganda has initiated several safeguards measures including oil–spill preparedness training, buffer zone enforcement, afforestation, and resettlement programs – implementation remain fragmented, under–resourced, and heavily centralised. Comparative analysis further indicates limited integration of international climate frameworks, including the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement, into national oil governance. We argue that Uganda’s challenge is not simply the absence of safeguards, but the persistence of centralised, uneven, and under–resourced governance arrangements that constrain the translation of international safeguard commitments into effective national practice. This study contributes to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land), while also intersecting with SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: BD/ARAS-based financing risk management evaluation for fisheries enterprise: a framework for resilient risk management
Abstract: The financing environment for fisheries enterprises is fraught with volatility, shaped by financial market dynamics, policy shifts, and industry-specific trends. This study addresses the critical need for a systematic and resilient approach to financing risk management in fisheries, a sector particularly vulnerable to resource depletion, policy constraints, and market fluctuations. The research identifies gaps in current enterprise risk management practices, which often fail to mitigate the complex risks faced by these enterprises, particularly in the context of global disruptions such as the U.S.-China trade war, the COVID-19 pandemic, and geopolitical conflicts. To bridge this gap, the study proposes a hybrid evaluation method, integrating the belief distribution, the generalized combination rule, the decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory, and the additive ratio assessment, grounded in the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission framework’s eight components. The method incorporates expert opinions to assess and enhance the quality and effectiveness of risk management processes. The findings underscore the necessity of a comprehensive, resilient management framework that addresses the unique challenges of the fisheries sector. This study not only advances the theoretical understanding of enterprise risk management but also offers practical guidance for improving risk management practices, contributing to the sustainability and green transition of the marine economy. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: The sphere of risk influence of corporate security. A conditional model of mechanisms, barriers, and degree
Abstract: Corporate security is embedded within enterprise risk governance, yet its organisational influence remains uneven and often operationally confined. This article examines the nature and limits of corporate security’s risk influence through the concept of a sphere of risk influence. Drawing on a multi-phase qualitative study of literature, organisational failure events, and expert practitioner focus groups, it conceptualises influence as a conditional outcome shaped by enabling mechanisms, constraining barriers, and the degree to which influence is realised in practice. Situated within Enterprise Security Risk Management frameworks, the sphere of risk influence is understood as the organisational space within which ESRM principles are effectively enacted, particularly through cross-functional collaboration and the integration of security risks within enterprise risk management systems. Findings show that corporate security engages diverse stakeholders across governance and operational environments, but that influence beyond the technostructure depends on contextual salience, structural legitimacy, and cultural positioning. The study offers a unifying diagnostic framework and theoretical foundation for future research on governance, influence, and professionalisation in security practice. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Charging station planning strategy considering imbalanced distribution of response propensity
Abstract: With the advancement of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, Electric Vehicle (EV) participation in grid scheduling has become a growing trend. This paper addresses the heterogeneous response propensity of EVs under different operating states by proposing a charging station planning strategy that accounts for the imbalanced distribution of planning-relevant EV response characteristics. Firstly, an improved synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) based on driving routes is introduced to tackle the data imbalance among EVs with different states of charge (SOC). By generating synthetic samples, this method enhances the accuracy of charging station planning under imbalanced data conditions. Next, an improved Mean Shift algorithm is proposed for charging station siting, which considers differences in the planning-level response propensity of EVs under different SOC states, thereby reducing the distance required for EVs to respond to grid scheduling. Finally, a capacity configuration strategy is designed to optimize charging station capacity by comprehensively considering the charging and discharging demands of EVs in the area and their response characteristics. Validation using real data from Chicago demonstrates that the proposed strategy effectively reduces EV response distance in scheduling, achieving an 8.3% reduction in response distance compared to conventional methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Psychological safety as a driver of student learning outcomes in team-based learning environments: The mediating role of teamwork quality
Abstract: With the rise of constructivist approaches, team-based learning (TBL) has gained popularity as an instructional design in the field of management education. The extant research indicates that the positive effects of TBL on student learning outcomes, which many studies report, might depend on individual as well as social-contextual drivers. In this paper, we introduce psychological safety and the quality of teamwork processes as two important social-contextual drivers of student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Based on research on team processes and TBL, we argue that psychological safety fosters student learning outcomes because of its positive effect on intrinsic motivation and group interaction. We further hypothesize that the relationship between psychological safety and student learning outcomes is mediated by the quality of teamwork processes within the student teams. A field study based on a computerized business simulation involving 169 undergraduate management students, nested within 44 teams, at a German university supports our hypotheses. We contribute to research on constructivist learning and TBL by introducing psychological safety as an important driver and the quality of teamwork processes as a mediating mechanism for student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Our study also has practical implications for the design, support, and facilitation of psychologically safe team-based learning environments. © 2026

Title: The power of gastronomic cultural capital: How local food culture shapes residents' recommendation intention
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: While destinations increasingly leverage cultural capital for competitiveness, research predominantly focuses on top-down promotions of monument-centered heritage, neglecting the distinct social logic of gastronomic culture. Grounded in cultural capital theory, this study aims to examine how Hong Kong's tea restaurants food culture translates into residents' recommendation intentions toward culturally diverse individuals. It untangles the core inquiries: how everyday food culture fosters attachment; how this attachment subsequently shapes cultural identity and confidence; and how nostalgia and knowledge moderate these psychological pathways. Additionally, it identifies which specific tea restaurant's food culture dimensions serve as the primary drivers. Utilizing an empirical sample of 615 Hong Kong residents, this research adopts a PLS–SEM–ANN approach. The PLS–SEM analysis confirms that cultural identity and confidence act as pivotal mediators, while the complementary ANN analysis reveals that gastronomic identity, exceeding mere sensory flavour, is the predominant driving dimension. Empirically, nostalgia amplifies the culture–attachment link, and knowledge strengthens the attachment–confidence relationship. These findings advocate for a paradigm shift in destination marketing: beyond institutional campaigns, mobilizing residents as active cultural transmitters is crucial for gastronomic tourism, establishing a scalable mechanism for everyday cultural capital transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Rational Design of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Oxygen Electrocatalysis: Recent Advances and Mechanistic Insights
Abstract: Due to the excessive consumption of fossil fuels and the increasingly severe global environment, the world urgently needs to develop new clean and renewable energy sources. However, these energy sources have intermittency and instability, so it is necessary to vigorously develop efficient and large-scale energy conversion and storage technologies such as fuel cells, water electrolyzers, and metal–air batteries based on the core reactions of oxygen evolution reaction and oxygen reduction reaction. Because of their excellent molecular designability and structural tunability, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) show great potential for applications in this field. In this review, we first classify COF-based electrocatalysts based on the nature of active sites. Subsequently, strategies including structural design and functional synthesis for improving performance of COF-based electrocatalysts in the field of oxygen catalysis are systematically reviewed. Importantly, mechanism discussion of the performance improvement is highlighted. Finally, we put forward prospects for the future research directions, challenges, and development opportunities in this field. This review aims to provide guidance for the development of high-performance COF-based electrocatalysts through critical analysis of existing research, revealing the correlation between material design and mechanism for performance improvement. Title: Machine Learning-Assisted optimization of acetylene Dual-Fuel combustion using Copper oxide (CuO) Nano-Enhanced waste Plastic Oil in Compression Ignition (CI) Engine
Abstract: In this study, an experimental and machine learning-assisted investigation was conducted on a modified single-cylinder direct-injection Compression Ignition (CI) engine operating in acetylene dual-fuel mode using copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticle-enhanced waste plastic oil (WPO) blends. The proposed approach integrates waste-to-energy fuel utilization, catalytic nano-additives, high-reactivity gaseous combustion, and data-driven predictive modelling within a unified sustainable combustion framework. Experimental investigations were performed using WPO10 and WPO20 blends containing 50 and 100 ppm CuO nanoparticles under acetylene flow rates of 5 and 10 LPM. Among all tested fuel combinations, A5WPO10Cu100 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a maximum brake thermal efficiency of 33.12 %, corresponding to an 8.27 % improvement over diesel, together with a 21.03 % reduction in brake specific energy consumption. The optimum fuel also reduced HC, CO, and smoke opacity by 41.46 %, 47.62 %, and 43.58 %, respectively, while A10WPO10Cu100 produced the highest combustion intensity with a peak heat release rate of 68.9 J/°CA, maximum cylinder pressure of 90.5 bar, and minimum ignition delay of 8.75 °CA, indicating enhanced premixed combustion and catalytic oxidation. Although NOx emissions increased under higher acetylene induction due to elevated combustion temperatures, the overall combustion efficiency and emission trade-off were significantly improved. To further establish predictive capability, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models were developed using the experimental dataset. Among these, the Random Forest model demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy with R2 values ranging from 0.995 to 0.999 and prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, confirming its robustness in predicting nonlinear combustion, performance, and emission characteristics. The integrated experimental and machine learning framework demonstrates that CuO nano-enhanced WPO coupled with acetylene induction is a promising strategy for improving CI engine efficiency while simultaneously advancing intelligent combustion optimization for sustainable transportation applications. To further enhance predictive capability and intelligent engine diagnostics, advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) were developed using experimentally measured combustion, performance, and emission parameters. The Random Forest model demonstrated superior nonlinear prediction capability with prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, coefficient of determination (R2) approaching 0.995–0.999 for major engine responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Cai S.; Lai K.
Title: The power of morality: The effect of moral appeals on tourists’ attitudes in rural tourism destinations
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Rural tourism has become an important tool for rural-revitalization and poverty alleviation, which has been increasingly framed as a moral narrative in public discourse. However, destination marketing often prioritizes utilitarian attributes while overlooking the role of moral appeals. Drawing on affective events theory, this study employs two experiments to examine the effects of moral appeals on tourists' attitudes, the underlying mechanism, and boundary conditions. The findings reveal that moral appeals significantly enhance tourists' visit intention and perceived value of rural destinations, with anticipated guilt mediating this relationship. Notably, these effects are more pronounced in low-quality destinations than in high-quality ones. Specifically, in rural destinations with low quality, high-intensity moral appeals are more effective than low-intensity ones in enhancing tourists’ visit intention and perceived value. This study contributes to the literature on rural tourism marketing and highlights the strategic value of moral appeals, particularly for rural destinations with limited resources. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation for single-phase-to-ground fault type identification in distribution networks
Abstract: Single-phase-to-ground (SPG) faults are the most frequent fault type in medium-voltage small-current grounding distribution networks. Due to arc suppression coil compensation and nonlinear grounding behaviors, fault currents are weak and highly nonstationary, making accurate fault type identification challenging under complex operating conditions. This paper proposes a physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation framework based on the Hilbert–Huang Transform (HHT) for SPG fault type identification. A typical 10 kV distribution network model is established in PSCAD/EMTDC to generate multi-scenario fault samples. HHT is applied to construct complementary dual-modal features, including time–frequency energy maps and instantaneous temporal evolution sequences. A parallel Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN–LSTM) architecture is developed to model spectral–spatial patterns and temporal dependencies, while channel and temporal attention mechanisms are introduced for adaptive feature enhancement. Results show that the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 99.2% across five fault types. Under additive white Gaussian noise with signal-to-noise ratios down to 5 dB, the accuracy remains above 93.6%. These simulation-based results indicate that the proposed framework maintains robust performance within the modeled PSCAD/EMTDC scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge of the Arhuaco People on Water Management in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
Abstract: This article analyzes the role of Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) of the Arhuaco people in water management in the upper Ariguaní river basin, in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (Colombia), in a context of accelerated socio-environmental transformation. From an ethnohydrological approach, the study adopts a mixed-methods design that integrates community surveys, participatory techniques, spatial analysis of land use change (2000–2023), and dynamic socio-hydrological modeling. A TEK Index was constructed to evaluate three dimensions of water management: cultural management, indigenous norms, and government norms. The results show that traditional water knowledge is mainly based on ritual practices and indigenous norms guided by indigenous spiritual authorities, while coordination with state institutional frameworks is limited. Spatial analysis shows a loss of forest cover and expansion of agricultural uses around the sacred sites that sustain TEK. Modeling indicates that, although indigenous norms slow the deterioration of the system, only co-governance scenarios can cushion pressures and avoid trajectories of collapse. Taken together, the findings show that the effectiveness of TEK depends on its articulation with multiscale governance arrangements. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Bridging the implementation gap in MCABC inventory management: from a taxonomy to practical archetypes
Abstract: Despite increasing demands for resilient and sustainable supply chains, inventory management often relies on outdated single-criterion analyses. While multi-criteria ABC (MCABC) analyses provide a theoretically mature assessment of resilience-sustainability-benefit trade-offs in inventory, their adoption remains limited due to fragmented methodologies, lack of standardization, and unclear design guidance. This study addresses this gap by developing a taxonomy of eight dimensions and 25 characteristics to structure the MCABC analysis design space. Using a dataset of 108 configurations, cluster analysis identifies six recurring archetypes that serve as implementation-ready templates for inventory analysis. Archetype 2: artificial intelligence (AI)+-driven cluster minimalist enables rapid, cost-focused inventory structuring with minimal data and no expert input. In contrast, Archetype 1: AI+-driven complex ranker uses expert-weighted multi-criteria analysis to support holistic and sustainability oriented inventory strategies. The taxonomy and archetypes provide a unified framework for researchers to theorize inventory design trade-offs and for practitioners to apply scalable blueprints for mature inventory analyses. © 2025 The Author(s). Title: Decoding entrepreneurial intention: A systematic review, theoretical framework synthesis, and research trajectories
Abstract: Entrepreneurial intention (EI) is a critical psychological construct for understanding the precursors of entrepreneurial behavior. Despite a surge in empirical research over the past decade, the literature on EI remains fragmented across theoretical frameworks, methodological approaches, and contextual applications. This study systematically reviews 53 peer-reviewed articles on entrepreneurial intention published between 2018 and 2025 to synthesize theoretical frameworks, methodological patterns, key findings, and future research directions. Guided by the PRISMA approach, the review reveals the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) as the predominant model, frequently integrated with constructs from Social Cognitive Theory, Technology Acceptance Model, and moral or contextual frameworks. Quantitative cross-sectional designs dominate the methodological landscape, often involving university student samples and the use of structural equation modelling techniques for hypothesis testing. Findings consistently confirm the central role of attitude, perceived behavioral control, and self-efficacy in predicting EI, while more recent studies highlight the growing significance of emotional intelligence, cultural influences, institutional support, and entrepreneurship education. However, the review identifies key limitations, including the overreliance on student-based samples, a lack of longitudinal and experimental designs, and limited generalizability to actual entrepreneurial behavior in real-world settings. Additionally, contextual diversity across emerging and developed economies remains underexplored. In response, the study proposes five future research trajectories: theoretical expansion beyond dominant models, increased adoption of behavioral and longitudinal approaches, broader contextual and demographic inclusion, pedagogical innovation in entrepreneurship education, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration. By mapping evolving trends and gaps in EI research, this review provides a foundation for more dynamic, inclusive, and practically relevant scholarship in entrepreneurship studies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Greener Urban Environments, Greater Climate Anxiety? Pro-Environmental Behavior and Well-Being Across Levels of Green-Space Provision
Abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that urban green space may alleviate climate anxiety, reinforcing its conventional role as a psychologically restorative environment. Yet this relationship may be more complex than a uniformly protective effect. This study examines whether perceived green built environments are associated with climate risk perception and climate anxiety, and whether climate anxiety, pro-environmental behavior, and well-being are differently associated across levels of neighborhood green-space provision. We analyzed survey data from 434 residents across four Taipei districts using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (PLS-MGA). Contrary to a purely protective interpretation, perceived green built environments were positively associated with both climate risk perception and climate anxiety. Climate anxiety was positively associated with pro-environmental behavior but showed no significant direct association with well-being, whereas pro-environmental behavior was strongly associated with greater well-being. This latter association was significantly stronger in high-green than in low-green districts. These findings highlight the complexity of human–environment relationships under climate change, showing that urban greenness may coexist with greater climate-related awareness and anxiety and that the psychological relevance of pro-environmental behavior varies across green-space conditions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Zou L.; Yu C.; Klophaus R.
Author full names: Zou, Li (23011079200); Yu, Chunyan (7404976658); Klophaus, Richard (8538639500)
Title: Survival analysis of U.S. regional airline routes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
Abstract: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, U.S. regional airlines have faced substantial operational challenges, including reduced flight activity, fleet restructuring, rising labor costs, and persistent pilot shortage. Between 2019 and 2024, domestic departures by regional airlines declined by nearly 24% from 3.81 million to 2.92 million, while passenger enplanements fell by 19% from 165.2 million to 133.7 million. Mainline carriers temporarily increased their reliance on regional partners during the pandemic but subsequently reduced regional operations during the post-pandemic recovery. Against this backdrop, we examine the determinants of route survival in U.S. regional airline markets during and after the pandemic. Using airline-route panel data for 2017–2024, we estimate Cox proportional hazards models with time-varying route-performance covariates. The results show that routes operated by independent regional airlines face significantly higher discontinuation hazards than those operated by wholly-owned subsidiaries of mainline carriers. Routes serving large hub airports exhibit higher survival probabilities, underscoring the importance of network connectivity beyond local market size. Support through the U.S. Essential Air Service (EAS) program is also associated with greater route survival, while larger aircraft are linked to improved route persistence, consistent with post-pandemic upgauging and capacity consolidation. The analysis also accounts for market demand conditions and operational characteristics, including population, per capita income, unit cost, stage length, and aircraft size. This study extends the literature by examining how ownership structure, network position, route performance, and EAS support jointly relate to regional route survival following the COVID-19 pandemic. The findings also inform EAS program design by highlighting the importance of risk-based route monitoring and service-continuity assessments that consider carrier structure, hub connectivity, market conditions, and fleet availability. Title: HAD-TAM: Health insurance anomaly detection via truncated affinity maximization with degree-normalized scoring
Abstract: Substantial financial losses are incurred annually as a result of medical insurance fraud, driven by subtle behaviors such as false diagnoses and over-prescription. Although heterogeneous graph structures can be exploited by existing graph neural network-based methods, they often rely on manually selected meta-paths, and the identification of structural anomalies remains a persistent challenge. To address these challenges, Health insurance Anomaly Detection via Truncated Affinity Maximization (HAD-TAM) is proposed as a health insurance fraud detection method, wherein degree-normalized anomaly score-guided meta-path selection is first combined with dual-threshold edge pruning to capture structural anomalies. First, the meta-graph with the highest degree-normalized anomaly score is selected by the model to highlight structures potentially indicative of fraud. Second, non-homophily edges are iteratively pruned by the model using both global and local thresholds to suppress noise and preserve meaningful structure. Finally, the neighborhood affinity of normal nodes is maximized by the model to better separate them from anomalies and improve fraud detection accuracy. Experimental results show that HAD-TAM outperforms eleven advanced baseline methods on two real-world medical insurance datasets, achieving a 2.41% improvement in AUROC and a 1.06% improvement in AUPRC. Furthermore, it exhibits good generalization to public datasets such as Amazon and Reddit. © 2026

Title: Municipal utilities and SDG adoption: Evidence from Austria and Germany
Abstract: This paper explores how municipal utilities (MUs) in Austria and Germany adopt and integrate the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into their strategies, strategic projects and management controls (MCs). MUs have a long tradition of delivering public infrastructure services, such as energy, water, and public transport, in the two focus countries. As important municipal enterprises, MUs must position themselves on a continuum between their public mission and their business orientation, and therefore act in a financially sustainable manner. Taking SDG adoption seriously is in line with the public mission orientation. Drawing on legitimacy theory, the study investigates whether MUs engage with the SDGs symbolically or substantively. The research is based on nineteen semi-structured interviews conducted with representatives from sixteen MUs, allowing for an in-depth qualitative analysis of strategic alignment, project implementation, and related MCs. The findings reveal considerable variation in SDG integration, showing that most MUs are still in an early, emerging stage of adoption, which is still at a symbolic level. By providing empirical insights from two countries with long-standing traditions of municipal service provision by local government-owned public utilities, the study contributes to the limited literature on SDG adoption in municipal enterprises and enhances understanding of the legitimacy dynamics shaping SDG practices in local state-owned entities. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Enhancing repeat patronage in beauty clinics: An integrated model of trust and consumer perceptions
Abstract: This study aims to explain how trust drives repeat patronage in the beauty clinic industry by examining the roles of service quality, price fairness, and influencer credibility. A quantitative explanatory approach was applied using survey data from 360 beauty clinic consumers in the Jabodetabek area. The data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS to test direct and indirect relationships among variables. The results show that perceived service quality, perceived price fairness, and influencer credibility each have positive and significant direct effects on both repurchase intention and brand trust, and that brand trust itself significantly and positively drives repurchase intention. Brand trust also partially mediates the effects of all three antecedents on repurchase intention, indicating that consumers' evaluations of service, price, and influencers shape repeat patronage both directly and through the trust these evaluations help to build. These findings suggest that improving service quality, price fairness perception, and influencer credibility can enhance consumer trust in a brand, which ultimately increases repurchase intention in beauty clinic services. This study is limited to beauty clinic consumers in the Jabodetabek area. Beauty clinic managers should focus on trust-building strategies through consistent service quality, transparent pricing, and collaboration with credible social media influencers to foster long-term consumer relationships. This study provides an integrated model that empirically demonstrates the mediating role of brand trust in the beauty clinic industry. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Disulfide bond cleavage in lentil legumin enhances interfacial properties at liquid interfaces
Abstract: Plant proteins often have inferior functional properties compared to animal-based proteins with respect to emulsion and foam stabilization because their larger and more rigid complex structures affect their ability to form a cohesive and stiff interfacial layer. To enhance film formation at liquid interfaces, molecular properties can be changed by using reducing agents such as dithiothreitol (DTT) to cleave disulfide bonds. Here, we explore this strategy for lentil legumin, one of the main proteins in lentils for which its structure is held together by covalent and noncovalent bonds, particularly disulfide bonds, giving it a rigid structure. Legumin was modified with different DTT concentrations (5, 50, and 100 mM) to obtain different degrees of modification. Disulfide bond cleavage in legumin led to increased surface hydrophobicity, resulting in enhanced adsorption kinetics, while particle size and surface charge remained similar to those of native legumin. Native and modified legumin were studied for their interfacial rheology at both oil-water and air-water interfaces. The interface formed by the modified legumin was stiffer than that of native legumin at both interfaces. The increased stiffness of the oil-water interface was attributed to the formation of denser interfacial layers rather than to stronger in-plane protein-protein interactions. In contrast, the stiffer air-water interface was associated with both stronger in-plane protein interactions and formation of denser interfaces. This was also confirmed by visualization of the interfacial film at the air-water interface, where the modified legumin formed denser and more cohesive networks than native legumin. Lastly, emulsion formation and stability were studied to assess whether structural changes following legumin modification affect stability on the macroscopic scale. Both native and modified legumin displayed stable emulsions against droplet flocculation and coalescence for 14 days, owing to the droplets having sufficient surface charge. Title: Environmental sustainability in the Lancang–Mekong River Basin: Research progress, emerging themes, and future directions under climate change and hydropower development
Abstract: Climate change and hydropower development are reshaping environmental sustainability in the Lancang–Mekong River Basin (LMRB) through their interacting effects on hydrological processes, ecosystems, water resources, and socioeconomic systems. This study provides an integrated review of environmental sustainability research in the LMRB by combining scientometric analysis with systematic thematic synthesis. A total of 356 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2005 to 2024 were analyzed to characterize the evolution of research output, collaboration patterns, influential studies, and major thematic hotspots. The reviewed literature is concentrated around three broad themes: climate change and hydrological change, environmental degradation and ecosystem responses, and hydropower development and water-resource interactions. The synthesis further highlights important concerns related to river connectivity, sediment and fisheries, biodiversity, water quality, and the social consequences of environmental change. An indicator-based comparative risk characterization shows that connectivity loss and sediment–fishery interactions represent particularly important environmental pressures, while social dimensions such as equity, vulnerability, public health, and adaptive capacity remain comparatively underrepresented in basin-scale assessments. Future research should strengthen multi-source data integration, cumulative-impact assessment, environmental–socioeconomic analysis, and transboundary cooperation to support more adaptive and integrated sustainability management across the basin. Title: Banks and informality: Two perspectives of microenterprises’ balance sheets
Abstract: Our paper studies how the nationwide expansion of bank branches affects the performance of informal microenterprises. We exploit the Branch Authorization Policy (BAP) in India, which directed banks to open branches in “underbanked” districts. Using a regression discontinuity design, we find that microenterprises in underbanked districts report higher value-addition, revenues, and productive assets, but no increase in local registration. However, borrowings on the enterprise balance sheet do not increase. The household balance sheet offers a second perspective that reconciles these findings: households in underbanked districts increased their bank borrowings for non-farm business by an amount comparable to the increase in microenterprise productive assets. Micro-entrepreneurs thus accessed bank credit as households rather than as enterprises, weakening a key incentive to formalize and helping explain how expanded access to finance can coexist with persistent informality. © 2026

Title: Improving spectral reproducibility in SERS analysis of exosomes via surface charge-modulated and biofunctionalized gold nanoparticles
Abstract: This study introduces an improved SERS platform for analyzing exosome heterogeneity. We compared three gold nanoparticle substrates: negatively charged citrate-Au NPs (cit-Au NPs), positively charged cysteamine-Au NPs (cyst-Au NPs), and anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs. Conventional cit-/cyst-Au NPs yielded fluctuating SERS signals due to random exosome localization, limiting accurate heterogeneity assessment. In contrast, anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs specifically anchored exosomes via CD63 targeting, producing highly reproducible spectra. Principal component analysis (PCA) confirmed significantly reduced spectral variance with the antibody-based approach, with 95% confidence ellipses showing substantially tighter clustering compared to charge-based substrates. Theoretical simulations and sensitivity tests further showed the cyst-Au NPs strategy achieved a detection limit of approximately 1.3 × 103 particles/μL, while cit-Au NPs and anti-CD63-functionalized cyst-Au NPs exhibited LODs of 7.9 × 103 and 8.1 × 104 particles/μL, respectively. Notably, the PCA plot for the biofunctionalized strategy revealed two distinguishable circles, potentially indicating the presence of exosome subpopulations or distinct CD63 epitope distributions. By integrating surface charge control with biofunctionalization, this work enables reproducible, sensitive SERS detection, offering a reliable platform for exosome heterogeneity analysis. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Determination of discount rates in business valuation and public project evaluation: A systematic review from the perspective of international finance and financial theory
Abstract: The discount rate plays a central role in business valuation and public project appraisal because it links risk to the valuation of future cash flows and guides the efficient allocation of resources. However, the global literature lacks methodological consensus and shows significant divergences between private and social approaches, as well as between developed and emerging economies. The present study aims to synthesize the main theoretical and empirical approaches used to determine discount rates from the perspective of international finance. A systematic literature review was conducted following the prisma protocol. Searches were conducted in scopus, web of science, sciencedirect, ssrn, and jstor, using boolean search strings related to “discount rate”, “wacc”, “capm”, “social discount rate”, and “country risk premium”. Studies published from 2000 to 2025, in english and spanish, were included. Only studies with a clear methodological foundation in finance and economics were considered. The analysis was carried out through a qualitative thematic synthesis. The reviewed literature indicates the predominance of the wacc and asset pricing models as the primary references for estimating private discount rates, and reports the increasing use of multifactor models and country risk premiums in the international context. For public projects, the literature identifies two main approaches: the social rate of time preference and the social opportunity cost of capital. The studies also suggest substantial heterogeneity across countries, with generally higher discount rates in emerging economies. No single discount rate is universally applicable; instead, its estimation depends on the local institutional context, the objectives of the investment, and the nature of the risks being evaluated. These findings should be interpreted in light of the qualitative nature of the synthesis. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.
