Title: Targeted Modulation of Zn Deposition Behavior toward High-Performance Stable Zn Anodes
Abstract: Dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions at the Zn metal anode remain critical obstacles to the commercialization of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Zn anode design regulates Zn deposition behavior from its thermodynamic and kinetic roots and is therefore recognized as a pivotal strategy to address the above bottlenecks. However, Zn deposition evolves through a complex multistage nucleation-growth process, and the structure–property relationship between the anode designs and practical Zn deposition behavior remains to be elucidated. This review focuses on Zn deposition substrate and functional interphase engineering, systematically elucidates the microscopic mechanisms and key regulatory targets of Zn deposition at each stage, and establishes a multidimensional regulation framework covering atomic tuning, interfacial modification, and spatial confinement. Based on this framework, we summarize three core design strategies, namely zincophilic regulation, lattice-matched effects, and three-dimensional structural engineering, and provide in-depth elucidation of the working mechanism and structure-property relationship of each strategy. By correlating these fundamental principles with the latest research advances in the field, we highlight the paradigm shift from empirical trial and error to rational material design. Finally, we outline the prevailing challenges and future research directions for Zn anode design, aiming to provide actionable insights for the development of advanced dendrite-free Zn anodes toward high-performance AZIBs. Authors: Li M.; Yi D.; Wu T.; Li C.; Hu B.; Shao C.
Title: Optimal carbon quota allocation for power system decarbonization: a two-stage peer-to-peer market framework
Abstract: Amid the global pursuit of deep decarbonization, effectively harnessing demand-side resources has emerged as a crucial strategy, particularly as end-user consumption is a primary driver of carbon emissions. However, existing demand-side carbon policies often impose a significant financial burden on consumers and struggle to utilize carbon quota resources to achieve effective emission reductions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel two-stage framework for carbon quota allocation to advance the decarbonization of power systems. The first stage introduces an allocation strategy that accounts for the heterogeneous low-carbon potential among different consumers, thereby regulating the supply-demand dynamics of the secondary carbon market. The second stage establishes a peer-to-peer carbon market based on a double-auction mechanism to support efficient and transparent rule-based trading. Within this market, an optimal bidding model is formulated to capture the strategic interactions among participants. To solve this complex optimization problem, an enhanced multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is developed, which incorporates a centralized reward mechanism to improve computational tractability. Finally, case studies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework. © 2026

Title: AI guest personalization as driver of hotel performance and hotel guest behavior: A dual-model analysis
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)–driven personalization is reshaping hotel operations, yet evidence on its financial effects and guest acceptance mechanisms remains limited. This study adopts a dual-perspective design combining hotel-level performance modeling with guest-level behavioral analysis. Study 1 examines revenue dynamics using Interrupted Time Series (ITS), SARIMA forecasting, and TOPSIS, comparing AI-driven and non-AI-driven hotels based on publicly documented implementations of AI personalization. Findings indicate heterogeneous short-term responses but more consistent differences in long-term revenue stability and predictability. Study 2 develops a Diffusion of Innovation–based structural model extended with trust in AI as a mediator, using survey data from 1396 hotel guests. Relative advantage and compatibility increase trust and adoption intention, whereas complexity reduces them; trust partially mediates these effects. Multi-group analysis reveals model differences between business and leisure guests. Overall, the study provides complementary evidence on revenue dynamics and adoption mechanisms of AI personalization in hospitality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Time-accurate and highly-stable explicit two-step Runge-Kutta methods for stiff differential equations
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Time-accurate and highly-stable explicit two-step Runge-Kutta methods (TASE-TSRK) for solving stiff ordinary differential equations, inspired by the technique presented in Calvo et al. [1]. The objective of the methods is to improve the stability characteristics of explicit TSRK methods by pre-multiplying the vector field with a suitable TASE operator. In this work, the related order conditions are analyzed, and then a complete study of stability properties is carried out for TASE-TSRK methods with order k ≤ 4. By appropriately selecting the free parameters of the TASE operator family, we demonstrate that the 2nd-order method is strongly A-stable, the 3rd-order and 4th-order methods can be nearly strongly A-stable. Some numerical experiments are performed to show that the new TASE-TSRK schemes are competitive with TSRK methods and potentially more advantageous for stiff problems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Real-World Cost of a Bundle Payment Strategy for Thyroid Oncological 90 Days Treatment: A Time-Driven Activity-Based Cost Analysis
Abstract: Objectives Continuous increases in the incidence of thyroid cancer emphasize the requirement for effective management policies. This study estimated the cost of a bundle reimbursement strategy for thyroid oncological treatment and compared it with a real-world cohort of patients. Methods This retrospective single-center microcosting study was conducted in 2 steps: (i) thyroid oncological surgery bundle design and (ii) real-world cost variability between the estimated bundle and a cohort of patients. The bundle was designed based on clinical guidelines and the center’s thyroid oncological surgical experience, represented by clinical registry data on 8381 cases. Time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) was applied to estimate the bundle’s cost, using data from a real-world cohort of 29 patients. The estimated and measured cost data were compared descriptively, and cost variability was analyzed using linear multiple regression. Results The thyroid cancer bundle covered care from preparation for surgery through postsurgical monitoring, including standard medications, exams, and involvement of health professionals. The estimated cost for the thyroid bundle was R$20,288 (US$3757), with the surgery accounting for 90% of the costs. The mean bundle cost based on the real-world cohort of patients was R$19,448 (SD 6690), with 33% of costs justified on hospital facilities. Patient’ age and length of hospital stay were identified as cost drivers. Conclusion This study is unique in evaluating the economic impact of adopting a bundle reimbursement strategy for one thyroid cancer treatment. Applying TDABC demonstrated the value of accurate costing for evaluating pricing and increasing the chances of achieving sustainability through an innovative care and payment strategy. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: IMPORTANCE OF STAKEHOLDERS AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS IN CAMPUS MANAGEMENT
Source title: International Journal of Strategic Property Management
Abstract: Campus managers need to balance the competing claims of different stakeholders of higher education institutions (HEIs). Previous studies in general management have indicated that the decision-making processes are highly related to stakeholders’ attributes (power, legitimacy and urgency). However, such studies have not yet been conducted in the field of campus management. Therefore, this paper aims to identify the importance of key stakeholders in campus development and relevant key performance indicators (KPIs) that are essential for decisionmakers in determining and explaining how their efforts are progressing towards achieving various stakeholders’ goals. To explore the underlying importance of campus stakeholders, a theory on stakeholder salience and a questionnaire survey among Polish public HEIs were employed. In turn, to identify various KPIs, the content analysis of institutions’ strategies was conducted. Empirical research suggests that in Polish public HEIs, authorities and academic staff continue to be regarded as the most important stakeholders (at different stages of the building’s life cycle, respectively). This contrasts with the growing market-oriented approach seen in higher education globally. Moreover, the KPIs presented in HEIs’ strategies are predominantly result-focused and rarely user-centric (which have begun to be perceived as the most significant with respect to building performance). © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Research Competence of a Modern Teacher as a Factor in Improving the Quality of Education and Supporting Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This study examines teacher research competence as a factor in improving educational quality and supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Using theoretical analysis, survey data, and economic-mathematical modeling, the study clarifies the structure, conditions, and impact of research competence in modern teaching. Data from 10 secondary school teachers were collected through a questionnaire assessing professional competencies, temperament, motivation, stress resistance, and burnout. Communicative and methodological competencies were strongest, while research, managerial, digital, and inclusive competencies need further development. Research competence was positively related to intrinsic motivation and methodological competence. The study proposes a three-component model integrating research practice, professional communities, and motivational support to strengthen evidence-based teaching and sustainable educational improvement. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

Title: Government subsidy policy and farmer’s live-streaming strategy in the fresh agricultural products supply chain
Abstract: Live-streaming serves as an effective means to promote the sales of fresh agricultural products. Farmers cooperate with streamers for live-streaming through the direct or resale live-streaming strategy. The third-party logistics service provider offers cold-chain services to maintain the freshness of agricultural products. Meanwhile, the government provides subsidies to farmers, streamers, or consumers. Motivated by this background, this study investigates a farmer’s choice of live-streaming strategy and its impact on other supply chain members. We find that, first, when streamer traffic is high, the farmer should adopt the resale live-streaming strategy. When streamer traffic is low, the farmer should adopt the direct live-streaming strategy if the government subsidizes farmers or consumers; if the government subsidizes streamers, the farmer’s decision on live-streaming strategy is also affected by unit subsidy. Second, the high-traffic streamer always prefers the resale live-streaming strategy, whereas the low-traffic streamer’s preference for the live-streaming strategy depends on the government subsidy policy. Finally, if streamer traffic is low (high) and subsidy is low, the government can promote the sales of fresh agricultural products, increase the farmer’s profit, and improve social welfare by subsidizing farmers (streamers); otherwise, subsidizing consumers may improve social welfare, but it is not conducive to the sales of fresh agricultural products or farmer’s profit. Furthermore, we conduct an extension study with an endogenous subsidy to verify the robustness of the main results. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Why travelers prefer humans over artificial intelligence (AI): Developing and testing an AI aversion model in tourism
Abstract: As tourism businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance traveler decision-making, a persistent reluctance to rely on AI-generated recommendations has emerged as a critical barrier. This research addresses this gap by developing and validating an AI aversion model that identifies the factors driving traveler resistance to AI-generated recommendations. Using a mixed-methods approach, this research uncovered five core drivers rooted in the perceived absence of human nature attributes: lived experience, emotional engagement, contextual understanding, domain specific knowledge, and proactive engagement in communication. Twenty-three items were developed and validated in a multicultural context. Additionally, we revealed that individual differences (i.e., rational vs. emotional personalities) play a moderating role, which can offer a way to mitigate the negative impacts of AI. Title: Scenario-based robust optimization for the design of a resilient and sustainable power supply chain network using energy storage system
Abstract: The increasing demand for electricity, along with the growing reliance on intermittent renewable energy sources, presents significant challenges for building resilient and cost-efficient power supply chains. This study introduces a hybrid multi-objective mathematical modeling framework that integrates renewable and non-renewable power generation units, multi-level substations, and strategically located energy storage systems. A scenario-based robust optimization model is developed to jointly minimize total system costs and maximize the performance of selected energy storage system technologies. The latter is quantified through a hybrid hierarchical group decision-making method combining the best‒worst method and the technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution and is incorporated into the model as a secondary objective via the improved weighted augmented ε-constraint technique. To strengthen system resilience, the model includes strategies such as diversification of generation technologies, capacity expansion of substations and lines, deployment of redundant transmission paths, and optimal siting of energy storage systems. A real-world case study from an Iranian province is conducted to evaluate the model’s effectiveness under disruption scenarios. The results demonstrate the framework’s ability to provide robust infrastructure planning under uncertainty. Furthermore, Pareto-based analysis reveals the trade-offs between investment cost and system performance, supporting informed decision-making in resilience-oriented energy planning. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Pan B.; Bi X.; Liu Z.; Ma Y.
Title: Breaking the cycle of malice: Influence mechanism and intervention of social exclusion on malevolent creativity in adolescents
Abstract: Creativity is the core driving force for humans to break through existing boundaries and promote continuous social progress, and its positive impacts have been widely recognized. However, creativity also has a dark side, namely, malevolent creativity, which poses significant potential harm to society. Therefore, it is necessary and meaningful to conduct research on malevolent creativity to prevent its negative impacts. Based on the 4P model of creativity, this study explored the impact mechanism between social exclusion and malevolent creativity (Study 1) and the effectiveness of a group counseling intervention for self-concept clarity (Study 2). Study 1 conducted a field questionnaire survey (N = 1567). The results showed that social exclusion not only directly increased malevolent creativity, but also indirectly predicted it through the independent mediating effects of reduced self-concept clarity and heightened negative emotions, as well as through the serial mediating effect whereby reduced self-concept clarity led to increased negative emotions, which in turn predicted malevolent creativity. Trait mindfulness moderated the impact of social exclusion on self-concept clarity, with higher levels of trait mindfulness alleviating the negative effects of social exclusion on self-concept clarity. Study 2 utilized a group counseling intervention (N = 30) and demonstrated that the experimental group experienced a significant increase in self-concept clarity and a significant decrease in malevolent creativity after the intervention. The study's conclusions provide educators with references and insights for correctly understanding the impact of social exclusion and for offering interventions to enhance self-concept clarity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Enhanced Antibiotics Sieving by Exfoliated TiS2 Membranes via Surface Functionalization and Passivation
Abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) nanolaminate membranes hold great promise for molecular sieving due to their two-dimensional capillary structures, which facilitate size-restricted diffusion. However, many transition metal sulfides exhibit intrinsic instability and are highly susceptible to oxidation, which severely limits their durability under reverse osmosis operating conditions. In this work, we introduce a stable 1T phase titanium disulfide (TiS2) constructing nanolaminate membranes from Group IVB, enabling the formation of tunable capillary channels and achieving a permeance up to 46.8 L m−2 h−1 bar−1. Experiments confirm that water-initiated hydrolysis, rather than direct oxidation by molecular O2, dominates the degradation of TiS2, while alkyl-chain hydrophobic barriers effectively suppress this water-triggered degradation. The enhanced surface hydrophobic properties simultaneously improve antioxidation stability and ensure sustained performance over 30 filtration cycles and 15 days of continuous operation. Functionalized membranes further reached 96.9% rejection for diverse antibiotics, such as sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and rifampicin. This work opens new avenues for exploring emerging TMD materials in the efficient and reliable removal of trace antibiotics from water, contributing to safer water resources and promoting sustainable ecological practices. Authors: Xie L.; Bian Y.; Jin P.
Title: A novel hierarchical optimal control strategy for hybrid energy storage considering smoothing wind power fluctuations and compensating prediction errors
Abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind power, its inherent intermittency and prediction errors pose significant challenges to the stable operation of power systems. To fully leverage the rapid dynamic response of supercapacitors and the high energy density of lithium-ion batteries, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical optimal control strategy for a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) to smooth wind power fluctuations and compensate prediction errors. The upper layer model introduces the concept of virtual energy storage (VES) and proposes a novel power extraction strategy based on model predictive control to obtain the total VES power, which is considered as the HESS power. The middle layer model establishes a novel power optimal allocation strategy based on the improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise and the grey relational analysis. The strategy realizes the decomposition, reconstruction and correction of li-ion battery (LB) and supercapacitor (SC) power. It avoids the problem of LB and SC power in the opposite direction at the same moment. The lower layer model builds a multi-objective optimal configuration model considering the life loss of HESS, which is solved by the improved multi-objective slime mould algorithm based on generalized opposition-based learning. Finally, some indicators are proposed to assess the effects of smoothing and compensation, simulations are conducted using actual data from western China. Results indicate that, compared with Case 1 using the conventional HESS power allocation strategy, the proposed strategy increases the modeled HESS lifetime from 4.54 years to 14.39 years, corresponding to an improvement of 216.96%, while the configuration satisfaction degree reaches 0.6941. © 2026

Title: Bioinspired Molecular Magnetic Field-Responsive Catalyst for On-Demand Switching of 2e− and 4e− Oxygen Reduction
Abstract: Achieving precise and on-demand steering of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) pathway between the efficient 4e− route to H2O and the valuable 2e− route to H2O2 remains a pivotal challenge in electrocatalysis. Herein, we address this challenge by designing a bioinspired molecular magnetic field-responsive catalyst (MMFR-C) via magnetic single-atom-anchored Salen-based covalent organic frameworks (MSA-Salen COFs) onto magnetic nanoparticles (single/multi-domain Fe3O4). Mimicking cytochrome c oxidase, the MMFR-C employs MSA-Salen COFs as an ordered proton-transfer channel and well-defined N2-M-O2 moieties as enzymatic O2 activation sites, with Fe3O4 providing a built-in magnetic field for remote regulation of the active-site electronic structure. The bioinspired MMFR-C exhibits switchable ORR pathways. Relative to the pristine Co-Salen COF (26% H2O2 selectivity, n = 3.48), the MMFR-C integrated with a single-domain Fe3O4 exhibits a remarkably enhanced H2O2 selectivity of 63.9% (n = 2.72), while that with a multi-domain Fe3O4 diverts the ORR pathway toward the 4e− route (n = 3.67). (i) We elucidate that the uniform magnetic field from the single-domain Fe3O4 in MMFR-C favors orbital hybridization between its active N2-M-O2 moieties and the *OOH intermediate, with moderate *OOH adsorption suppressing O–O scission and thus steering ORR selectivity toward H2O2. (ii) In contrast, the enhanced specific magnetism from its multi-domain Fe3O4 core optimizes the d-band center of MMFR-C’s active sites, stabilizes triplet O2 adsorption, and reduces spin-forbidden transition barriers, thereby facilitating O–O cleavage and diverting its ORR pathway to the 4e− route. Title: Coupled supply and demand forecasting in platform accommodation markets
Abstract: Tourism demand forecasting is methodologically mature, but it usually treats accommodation supply as fixed, exogenous, or slow-moving. This Progress in Tourism Management article develops a narrated, conceptually focused review of forecasting in platform-mediated short-term rental markets, where supply is elastic, decision-driven, and jointly shaped with demand through pricing, information design, host participation, and policy intervention. The article reframes realized booked nights as a constrained outcome generated by latent demand, effective supply, and matching frictions. It synthesizes tourism forecasting, revenue management, two-sided market economics, causal inference, and compositional time-series methods; articulates a three-layer coupling framework spanning intervention, behavioral, and informational channels; and uses a stylized model experiment to illustrate one supply-shock failure mode. The contribution is a theoretical and methodological map: where platform accommodation forecasting has developed, what remains under-specified, and how future work can validate coupled supply–demand forecasting. It does not attempt a completed comparative empirical evaluation. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises: The roles of technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality in an ai-driven business environment
Abstract: The tourism industry is experiencing unprecedented transformation driven by digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, and the rapid evolution of smart tourism ecosystems. At the same time, tourism enterprises face growing pressure to enhance service quality while controlling operational costs and improving managerial responsiveness. In this context, management accounting effectiveness has become a critical capability for supporting strategic decision-making and maintaining sustainable competitiveness. Although previous studies have examined digital transformation and accounting systems separately, limited attention has been paid to how technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality jointly influence management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises operating in emerging economies. Addressing this research gap, the present study investigates the effects of these three determinants on management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism enterprises. Grounded in the resource-based view, contingency theory, dynamic capabilities theory, and sociotechnical systems theory, the study adopts a mixed-method research design consisting of expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. Data were collected from 315 tourism enterprises, with chief accountants, general accountants, and management accounting personnel serving as key respondents. The data were analyzed using SPSS through reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The empirical findings demonstrate that technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality all exert positive and statistically significant effects on management accounting effectiveness. Among these determinants, information technology infrastructure emerges as the strongest predictor, followed by technology readiness and data quality. These findings indicate that tourism enterprises equipped with integrated digital infrastructure, advanced technological capabilities, and high-quality accounting data are better positioned to generate timely, accurate, and strategically relevant management accounting information in AI-enabled business environments. This study extends the literature by providing empirical evidence from an emerging economy and contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital transformation and management accounting. The findings also offer practical implications for tourism managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen digital accounting capabilities, improve managerial decision-making, and enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of tourism enterprises in the era of AI-driven business transformation. Title: An advanced integrated cross-sectoral model for formulating government strategies on energy consumption management to reduce greenhouse gas emissions toward achieving net-zero emissions in the future
Abstract: This study aims to develop a model that identifies alternative scenarios for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by examining the interrelationships among the circular economy, socio-cultural, and environmental sectors, with the ultimate goal of supporting Thailand's net-zero emissions target. Using a mixed-methods research design, the study provides a foundation for developing integrated national management strategies that promote long-term sustainability. A novel model, referred to as the Path–Probit–Logit–ARx Model (Path Analysis–Probit–Logit Model based on Autoregressive with Exogenous Variables), was developed to address the study objectives. The findings reveal that, during the period 1992–2025, the circular economy sector experienced continuous growth, which directly contributed to the steady expansion of the socio-cultural sector. The growth of both sectors also exerted a positive influence on the environmental sector. Furthermore, the environmental sector was found to have a direct positive effect on the socio-cultural sector, indicating a bidirectional relationship between these two sectors. This finding suggests that environmentally responsible societies can promote long-term ecosystem development and that environmental and social development should progress concurrently. Based on the analysis, the study identified the adoption of electric vehicles as the most sensitive and effective scenario for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Under this scenario, the growth rate of final energy consumption is reduced to 33%, while greenhouse gas emission growth decreases to 53.73%, remaining below the critical threshold of 590.05 Mt CO2 equivalent and thereby meeting the government's target. To enhance the policy relevance and credibility of the findings, a focus group consisting of 15 experts was conducted to validate the results. The experts confirmed the appropriateness and accuracy of the proposed scenario and agreed that it is suitable for promoting sustainable development in Thailand. However, they emphasized the need for immediate action and strong governmental support to ensure effective implementation. Therefore, the findings of this study can support evidence-based decision-making and strategic planning, contributing to the development of Thailand's long-term national strategies through 2065. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Reducing the weighted tool replacement problem to min-cost flow on a linear-size graph
Abstract: We study the Weighted Tool Replacement Problem (WTRP), where a fixed sequence of n jobs must be processed using a tool magazine of capacity C, and each tool is associated with insertion and deletion costs. Our main contribution is a new exact reduction of WTRP to a min-cost flow problem that avoids the quadratic-size network of the classical Privault-Finke construction (with running time O(C3n2)). Starting from a packing formulation of WTRP, we build a flow network with O(n) nodes and O(Cn) arcs, yielding a polynomial-time algorithm with running time O(C2n+Cnlogn). Computational experiments show speedups of at least one order of magnitude over established exact approaches for WTRP, including the Privault-Finke method and the algorithm of Crama. Finally, we embed the proposed flow-based routine into a state-of-the-art heuristic for the Job Sequencing and Tool Switching Problem (SSP), thereby extending it to weighted replacement costs. Title: Human Factors and Safety Communication in Engineering Safety Performance: A Predictive PLS-SEM Model for Petrochemical Operations
Abstract: Petrochemical operations are complex engineering systems in which safety performance depends not only on technical safeguards and process controls but also on human and organisational factors that influence how workers perceive, interpret, and respond to safety requirements. Despite advances in engineering controls and occupational safety management systems, incidents continue to occur, highlighting the need to integrate human factors into engineering safety management. This study develops and evaluates a predictive model of engineering safety performance by examining the effects of two culturally embedded human factors, religiosity and fatalism, together with safety communication effectiveness in Malaysian petrochemical operations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 463 employees and contractors from major petrochemical facilities in Malaysia. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity. The structural model showed that religiosity significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.442, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.436, p < 0.001), while fatalism significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.451, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.378, p < 0.001). In contrast, safety communication effectiveness did not directly predict safety performance (β = −0.006, p = 0.954). The model explained 74.7% of the variance in safety communication effectiveness and 61.2% of the variance in safety performance. These findings demonstrate that engineering safety performance in high-risk petrochemical operations cannot be addressed solely through technical controls and communication systems. Title: A graph-based direct association strategy with fuzzy interpretability for linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality
Abstract: Existing coke quality prediction methods mainly rely on a two-stage prediction strategy, where blended coal properties are first estimated from individual coal properties and then used for coke quality prediction. This process inevitably introduces information loss and accumulated prediction errors, which limit the prediction accuracy and reliability of these models in practical coal blending applications. To address this challenge, this study proposes, for the first time, a graph-based direct association strategy linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality. Each coal blending scheme is transformed into a graph structure, where individual coal samples are regarded as graph nodes and their corresponding coal properties together with blending ratios are used as node features. Different graph neural network models are further investigated to directly learn the relationship between individual coal properties and coke quality indicators, namely Coke Reactivity Index (CRI) and Coke Strength after Reaction (CSR). A total of 306 coal blending schemes are used for model development and evaluation. Experimental results show that the proposed one-stage graph-based framework outperforms traditional two-stage prediction methods. Among different graph neural network models, the graph attention network achieves the best overall prediction performance, obtaining mean absolute errors of 2.06 and 2.60 for CRI and CSR prediction, respectively. The t-SNE visualization further demonstrates that the proposed one-stage framework can learn more discriminative feature representations than the traditional two-stage framework. In addition, the proposed framework demonstrates good robustness under blending conditions with different numbers of coal types and can provide interpretable analysis through feature importance and node importance visualization. Furthermore, fuzzy interpretability is introduced at the feature level to characterize the gradual contribution levels of different coal properties. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Diversification or concentration? Supply chain configuration responses to decoupling risk
Abstract: This study investigates corporate supply chain configuration strategies in the context of perceived decoupling risk. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2023, we employ textual analysis to construct a firm-level index of perceived decoupling risk. Building on this index, we empirically examine its effect on corporate supply chain configuration strategies. The findings reveal that a higher level of perceived decoupling risk prompts firms to pursue greater supply chain diversification, leading to a significant decrease in supply chain concentration; notably, the diversification response is concentrated among firms facing high-intensity risk perception, while low-intensity risk perception is associated with minimal supply chain adjustment. Further analysis reveals that this negative association is attenuated by both executive risk preference and the level of corporate investment irreversibility. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the reduction in supply chain concentration is more pronounced for firms with high overseas revenue exposure, those in strategic emerging industries, and small-scale enterprises. Additionally, this impact is amplified during periods of heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly following the U.S.-China trade frictions in 2018, and is more pronounced in the upstream ends of supply chains. Finally, we find that the proactive supply chain diversification triggered by decoupling risk significantly enhances firms' operational resilience after a three-year adjustment period, demonstrating a long-term benefit for corporate stability. By quantifying firms’ subjective perception of decoupling risk and confirming its significant impact on supply chain configuration, this study provides novel micro-level evidence on firms’ supply chain behaviors in response to external environmental uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: An Analysis of Interactive and Interactional Metadiscourse Markers in Applied Linguistics Webinars: The Case of Top-Tier Native vs. Non-Native Speaking Scholars
Abstract: Within the ecosystem of genres, audiences, and modalities, knowledge dissemination relies on metadiscourse markers that guide and engage academic audiences. Despite digital technologies reshaping communication after the pandemic, their use in academic webinars, especially regarding speakers’ linguistic backgrounds, remains an underresearched area of inquiry. Accordingly, this study aimed to comprehensively analyze interactive and interactional metadiscourse markers utilized by both top-tier native and non-native scholars in Applied Linguistics webinars. To this end, a corpus of 24 webinars (24 hours and 35 minutes) conducted by top-tier Applied Linguists over five years was purposively selected and analyzed using Hyland’s (2005) metadiscourse model, focusing on the frequency and distribution of interactive and interactional markers. The results showed that native scholars employed metadiscourse markers (both interactive and interactional) somewhat more frequently than non-natives, though both groups used them extensively to organize and engage audiences. While natives favored interactional markers over interactive ones, non-natives demonstrated the opposite trend, relying more on interactive than interactional markers. These findings highlight the need for EAP/ESP pedagogy to extend beyond accuracy, fostering non-native scholars’ interactional competence through training in hedges, boosters, attitude markers, and self-mentions, empowering them to communicate confidently, engage audiences, and sustain presence in global academia. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. Title: Subgroup testing for change-plane Cox models in heterogeneous credit risk data
Source title: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference
Abstract: Change-plane analysis has emerged as an effective tool to detect subgroups with distinct effects on the response of interest. Notably, the change-plane Cox model has gained significance in the subgroup analysis of survival data. Testing for the existence of a change plane can provide valuable insights into optimal decisions for the specific subgroups. However, classical supremum testing methods often suffer from limited efficiency in practical. To address this drawback, we propose a novel testing procedure designed to enhance statistical power. Our approach calculates the weighted average of the squared score test statistic (WAST) over the space of parameter that defines the subgroup, significantly improving power in practice. Moreover, we derive the asymptotic distributions of the test statistic under both the null and local alternative hypotheses. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated by extensive simulation studies, exhibiting better size control and higher power than existing testing approaches. Additionally, we illustrate the practical application of our approach using the Lending club loan dataset and the German credit dataset, showing its ability to identify subgroups with different default risks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Explicit reward mechanisms for local flexibility in renewable energy communities
Abstract: Incentivizing flexible consumption of end-users is key to maximizing the value of local exchanges within Renewable Energy Communities. If centralized coordination for flexible resources planning raises concerns regarding data privacy and fair benefits distribution, state-of-the-art approaches (e.g., bi-level, ADMM) often face computational complexity and convexity challenges, limiting the precision of embedded flexible models. This work proposes an iterative resolution procedure to solve the decentralized flexibility planning with a central operator as a coordinator within a community. The community operator asks for upward or downward flexibility depending on the global needs, while members can individually react with an offer for flexible capacity. This approach ensures individual optimality while converging towards a global optimum, as validated on a 20-member domestic case study for which the gap in terms of collective bill is not more than 3.5% between the decentralized and centralized coordination schemes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Economic design of residential solar resources under uncertainty: An adaptive robust optimization approach for EV households
Abstract: The integration of residential PV systems with electric vehicles (EVs) offers significant opportunities to enhance self-consumption, reduce reliance on the grid, and lower household energy costs. Effective PV system sizing, however, is challenged by uncertainties in PV generation, household electricity demand, and EV charging behavior. While traditional approaches often ignore uncertainties or assume predefined values for uncertainties, this paper develops an adaptive robust optimization framework for sizing residential PV systems in EV-integrated households, explicitly accounting for operational uncertainties and calibrating the uncertainty parameters using a Genetic Algorithm. The proposed model explicitly incorporates multi-source uncertainty using a budgeted adaptive robust optimization approach. Investment decisions, such as PV capacity, are modeled as here-and-now variables, while operational variability is captured as wait-and-see decisions responding to uncertainty realizations. To mitigate the inherent conservatism of robust optimization and identify optimal uncertainty settings, a Genetic Algorithm–based calibration is integrated. The GA iteratively searches for the best combination of uncertainty parameters through simulation-based evaluation, balancing robustness and economic efficiency. The results show that calibrated uncertainty parameters provide a cost-effective and resilient system design, avoiding oversized PV capacities while improving household energy performance by reducing the cost of energy up to 18%. © 2026

Title: Offshore infrastructure decommissioning, just transitions, and the struggle for the right to the sea: Small-scale fishers’ perspectives from coastal Ghana
Abstract: Offshore petroleum infrastructure decommissioning is usually framed as a technical and environmental process requiring technical expertise. Yet, offshore infrastructure decommissioning could have deleterious consequences on adjacent coastal communities and livelihoods. Drawing on qualitative data from 65 respondents from Ghanaian coastal communities of Saltpond and Kormantse, this paper investigates small-scale fishers’ experiences of offshore oil and gas infrastructure decommissioning. The paper frames decommissioning as a critical phase of energy transition and interrogates its outcomes through the dual lenses of just transitions and the “right to the sea.” The findings reveal that decommissioning produces socio-ecological and economic disruptions. These include the creation of offshore safety zones leading to spatial exclusion of fishing activities, the erosion of socio-ecological knowledge systems, material precarity through asset loss, and ecological uncertainty linked to perceptions of pollution. While these processes are officially justified on grounds of safety and environmental protection, they are experienced locally as forms of livelihood dispossession and governance exclusion. The study argues that decommissioning represents an unjust transition, in which the challenges associated with post-extractive restructuring are disproportionately shifted onto vulnerable coastal communities. At the same time, it is a struggle over the right to the sea, as regulatory and security mechanisms reconfigure access to marine space in ways that privilege state and industrial actors over fisherfolk. The paper concludes that achieving socially just and sustainable decommissioning outcomes requires moving beyond technical compliance toward inclusive governance frameworks that recognise local knowledge, ensure equitable access to marine resources, and address the livelihood impacts of transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Influencer beware: The buffering role of sponsor–influencer fit in the commercialization-authenticity trade-off
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As social media influencers (SMIs) increasingly commercialize their online presence through sponsored content, understanding how sponsorship intensity shapes consumer responses has become important. Drawing on attribution and congruence theories and the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how sponsorship levels influence audience engagement and purchase intentions through perceived personal authenticity (PPA) and whether these effects depend on sponsor–SMI fit. Three experimental studies were conducted to test the proposed relationships. The results show that higher sponsorship levels reduce consumers’ intention to follow influencers and share their content. Sponsor–SMI fit attenuates the negative effect of sponsorship intensity on PPA. Thereby mitigating its adverse effects on consumer engagement and purchase intentions. We further demonstrate that sponsorship level affects consumer responses indirectly through PPA and that this indirect effect is contingent on sponsor–SMI fit. These findings advance the influencer marketing literature by applying the ERC framework to distinguish the different authenticity types and their impact on consumer behavior. Title: Beyond the lecture: Creative and innovative pedagogies in management education – An integrative conceptual review
Abstract: Management education has been criticised for over-reliance on transmission-oriented pedagogies poorly suited to developing the competences contemporary business graduates require. The case for moving beyond the lecture is strengthened by generative artificial intelligence, which performs the analytical and reproductive tasks underpinning conventional assessment, shifting educational value toward judgement, situated decision-making, and reflection. This integrative conceptual review of creative and innovative pedagogies draws on literature published principally between 2013 and 2026, organising the field into six clusters: experiential and simulation-based learning; game-based and gamified approaches; arts-based methods; design-based pedagogies; problem-based learning; and student-generated multimodal artefacts. For each cluster it examines theoretical foundations, evidence strength, and implementation challenges, distinguishing outcomes with stronger evidence (engagement, motivation) from those with weaker evidence (durable transfer). Three cross-cutting themes are identified: the centrality of learner agency, the neglect of structured reflection, and institutional conservatism as a barrier to change. The review contributes a typology of creative pedagogy organised by locus of creation and mode of engagement, which is used to make explicit the trade-offs each configuration entails and where institutional conservatism constrains change, together with implications for programme design, assessment and facilitation, and a research agenda spanning longitudinal measurement, equity, programme-level integration, and generative AI. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Transforming value of sustainability in urban development: Reconfiguring logistics service in the construction industry
Abstract: Urban development depends on construction activity to improve sustainability, yet the logistics required to move materials, equipment, waste, and workers remains insufficiently integrated into urban planning. This paper examines how construction logistics can be integrated into municipal urban planning by analysing how actor groups perceive its impacts and coordinate value creation across fragmented urban systems. The study applies a qualitative interactive research design based on a Swedish construction logistics project. Data were collected between August 2022 and March 2024 through eight semi-structured group interviews, joint workshops, actor-specific validation workshops, and a final synthesis workshop with developers, main contractors, suppliers, and trade organizations. The analysis combines iterative thematic coding with value configuration theory. The findings show that suppliers emphasize efficiency and climate savings, main contractors focus on project efficiency and safety, developers stress sustainability, accessibility and accountability, while trade organizations highlight knowledge-building and sector coordination. These differences create misalignment because societal benefits are often separated from project-level costs. Four conditions are identified as central: clearer procurement requirements, stronger logistics knowledge, scalable logistics service designs, and systematic follow-up of time, cost, and emission effects. The paper concludes that municipalities should use procurement, planning requirements and follow-up mechanisms to enforce construction logistics values in urban planning. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A blockchain-enabled distributed service configuration approach for distributed smart manufacturing systems
Abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, distributed manufacturing (DM) paradigms, exemplified by cloud manufacturing (CMfg), have garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. These paradigms aim to achieve the precise matching of geographically dispersed manufacturing resources with personalized demands. However, existing research on service configuration predominantly relies on centralized information architectures, which pose critical challenges such as single point of failure (SPoF), data privacy leakage risks, and limited scalability. To address these issues, this paper investigates how blockchain technology can be leveraged to enable trustworthy collaboration and distributed decision-making in DM systems. Specifically, we propose a Blockchain-enabled Cyber-Physical Network (BCPN) architecture and design a complete and executable business process tailored to service configuration requirements. Furthermore, a systematic solution is developed that integrates several key components, including a reputation evaluation contract, a service pre-screening contract, a proof of reputation (PoR) consensus mechanism, a distributed service configuration contract, and a backward time propagation smart contract based on breadth-first search (BFS). Title: Hot war tourism: The touristification of unresolved conflict
Abstract: This article conceptualises hot war tourism as the touristification of unresolved conflict: configurations in which conflict continues materially to shape civilian vulnerability, security and visitor access while conflict-affected places and experiences acquire experiential, representational or market value. A critical integrative review clarifies its boundaries with dark, battlefield, military, risk, recovery and solidarity-oriented tourism and identifies five dimensions: temporal immediacy, spatial proximity, commodification, moral and motivational ambiguity, and governance and responsibility. Ukraine and Syria illustrate contrasting active-war witnessing and recovery–normalisation configurations. A relational framework locates war-related tourism according to the degree of unresolved conflict and the intensity of touristification, while a multi-actor governance framework specifies responsibilities for access, risk disclosure, representation, consent, platform accountability, humanitarian non-interference and escalation. Title: Determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java: The roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, innovation capability, and ESG
Abstract: This study examines the determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java by analyzing the roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) implementation, innovation capability, and organizational performance. Social enterprises in emerging economies increasingly face challenges in maintaining long-term sustainability due to resource limitations, institutional uncertainty, and dynamic social demands. Although previous studies have explored intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, ESG practices, and innovation capability separately, limited empirical research has integrated these variables into a comprehensive sustainability model within the context of social enterprises in emerging economies, particularly Indonesia. Therefore, this study seeks to address this gap by developing and testing an integrated model of social enterprise sustainability. This research adopts a quantitative approach using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Data were collected from 200 owners and managers of social enterprises operating across six provinces on Java Island. The findings reveal that entrepreneurial orientation has a strong and significant effect on innovation capability (β = 0.699, p < 0.001), while ESG implementation significantly influences social enterprise performance (β = 0.402, p < 0.001). Intellectual capital and entrepreneurial orientation significantly contribute to innovation capability, whereas ESG implementation directly improves organizational performance and sustainability. Furthermore, innovation capability acts as a crucial mediating variable that strengthens the relationship between strategic organizational resources and sustainability outcomes. Social enterprise performance also demonstrates a significant mediating role in achieving long-term sustainability. These findings highlight the importance of innovation-driven strategies, knowledge-based resources, and ESG-oriented governance in strengthening the resilience and sustainability of social enterprises. Title: Reflection quality and psychological safety as mechanisms of development in virtual management education
Abstract: This study examines the mechanisms linking behavioral participation in virtual management education to developmental learning outcomes. Drawing on experiential learning theory (ELT), this study investigates whether reflection quality mediates the relationship between behavioral participation and student development and whether team psychological safety moderates the participation–reflection relationship. Data were collected from an eight-week multicultural virtual leadership program involving 74 business students working in nine multicultural teams. To reduce common method concerns, this study integrated six independent sources of evidence: instructor activity logs, coded reflection reports, pre- and post-program competency surveys, psychological safety ratings, peer evaluations, and instructor-assessed team-performance scores. The findings indicate that higher behavioral participation is associated with deeper reflective responses. Reflection quality is more consistently associated with gains in cultural intelligence (CQ) and global leadership competency than participation alone. Furthermore, the relationship between participation and reflection is stronger in teams characterized by higher psychological safety, highlighting the importance of supportive learning environments in fostering reflective practices. Because reflection depth and post-program outcomes were assessed at the same measurement occasion, the mediation findings are interpreted as theory-consistent associative evidence rather than causal proof. Overall, the results are consistent with a sociocognitive extension of ELT, in which experiential learning is shaped not only by individual cognitive processing but also by the interpersonal safety of the team environment. For management educators, the findings emphasize three design priorities: systematic monitoring of behavioral participation, scaffolding and assessing reflection quality, and intentionally cultivating psychologically safe learning environments to enhance developmental outcomes in virtual management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The impact of digital marketing on consumer attitudes and behavioural responses: The role of perceived value and financial considerations in the decision-making process

Title: From eco-signals to green trust: How tourists evaluate sustainability credibility through online reviews
Source title: Journal of Destination Marketing and Management
Abstract: Growing sustainability claims in tourism have intensified concerns about credibility and greenwashing. This study examines how tourists interpret environmental practices by analyzing 138,683 online reviews from major Southeast and East Asian coastal and island destinations. Drawing on signaling theory and attribution theory, the study proposes that observable sustainability cues are associated with eco-authenticity inference, which is linked to green trust and, in turn, more positive review sentiment. Title: Can a transversal adaptation of teaching materials foster students’ entrepreneurial intentions? A quasi-experimental exploration in a statistics course setting
Abstract: We propose that a transversal integration of entrepreneurship content within other curricula may be an effective approach to foster students' entrepreneurial intentions. A qualitative follow-up exploration with seven participants suggested that the data collection itself may have prompted students to reassess their attitude toward entrepreneurship. Title: Human capital development through community digital centers for inequality reduction in Thailand
Abstract: Driving human capital development through community digital centers to reduce inequality requires multiple interrelated factors and components to ensure successful implementation. Title: Exploring digital culture: A bibliometric review using keyword co-occurrence and performance analysis
Abstract: Digital culture has become a central organizational phenomenon shaping how firms navigate digital transformation, emerging technologies, and sustainability pressures, yet prior research remains fragmented across disciplines and contexts. This study provides the first large-scale bibliometric mapping of digital culture research from an organizational perspective. Using the Scopus database, we analyzed 212 publications published between 2008 and 2025. Bibliometric techniques and VOSviewer were applied to examine (i) annual publication trends, (ii) thematic structures through keyword co-occurrence networks, (iii) influential knowledge producers across authors, affiliations, and countries, and (iv) document type distribution to infer field maturity. The results show a clear acceleration after 2020, culminating in more than 60 publications per year by 2025, indicating that digital culture has shifted from a niche conceptual topic to a consolidated research stream. Keyword co-occurrence reveals eight interconnected thematic clusters, with “digital culture” and “digital transformation” acting as the primary conceptual anchors and linking strongly to (1) digitalization and Industry 4.0 in SMEs, (2) performance and dynamic capabilities, (3) sustainability/ESG-oriented transformation, (4) digital strategy and structural alignment, (5) AI and IoT as emerging technological drivers, (6) the digital economy, (7) marketing and consumer interaction, and (8) leadership-driven innovation. Country production patterns highlight a recent geographic diversification, with rapid growth from emerging economies alongside established contributors. Document type analysis further indicates a field dominated by journal articles (68.0%), supported by book chapters (18.5%) and conference papers (11.0%), while reviews remain scarce, suggesting strong empirical expansion but limited synthesis. Title: Social and Spiritual Aspects Affecting Psychosocial Well-Being Among Early- and Late-Stage Oral Cancer Patients Presenting with Restricted Oral Functioning

Abstract: Objective: There is increasing awareness of the diverse negative effects of cancer stage on the psychosocial well-being of patients with oral cancer. Descriptive analyses, including correlation, were performed, followed by a hierarchical multiple regression using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) Version 25.0. Results: The multivariate analyses indicated moderate-strong relationships between the mean scores for oral functioning, social support, spiritual aspect, and psychosocial well-being among a cohort of both early (n=31) and late-stage (n=65) patients attending three visits: pre-treatment, 1 month, and 3 months post-treatment. However, only oral functioning and social support were found to be significant predictors of patients’ psychosocial well-being; with social support being the most significant predictor for both groups. In addition, social support was a mediator of oral functioning at pre-treatment among the late-stage group. Title: Fungal frontiers for sustainability: unlocking the hidden kingdom

We now have technologies that make previously inaccessible fungal questions tractable, which can help unlock the next generation of fungal breakthroughs. Informed by a workshop held in December 2025 that convened 20 leading experts across fungal disciplines, here we lay out key bottlenecks to fungal research and innovation through three lenses: functional mycology, human and institutional capacity, and governance. We identify selected sustainability-relevant fungal frontiers and use these to surface the recurrent gaps that cut across domains. Title: Dynamic hierarchical population-based differential evolution with parameter control and hypervolume diversity for numerical optimization
Abstract: A hierarchical differential evolution algorithm with individualized restart is proposed. In each generation, the population is split into an elite layer and an ordinary layer by an adaptive, progress-dependent threshold derived from normalized fitness deviations, and the two layers are evolved by different mutation operators and parameter-generation rules. Scaling factors and crossover rates are adapted from a success-history memory weighted by successful difference-vector magnitudes, supported by an archive whose members are aged out over time. A volume-based diversity indicator, combined with per-individual stagnation counters, triggers dimension-wise reinitialization of unproductive individuals, while a piecewise-decreasing population size concentrates the remaining budget on refinement. To validate the optimization performance of the proposed HPHD-DE algorithm, we selected six high-performing DE variants as competitors, including two champion algorithms L-SRTDE and RDEx, and conducted comparative experiments on 88 test functions from three well-known testbeds. The experimental results show that although the overall performance of HPHD-DE is inferior to L-SRTDE and RDEx, it significantly outperforms the other five competitors. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Mining transitions in the Mid West of Western Australia: A regional transition knowledge system
Abstract: Mining transitions are typically understood as the shift from active mining to post-mining futures requiring technical planning and stakeholder consultation. This framing overlooks how mining regions experience continuous transitions throughout project lifecycles and marginalises the knowledge communities accumulate through navigating these changes. Drawing on social constructionism and knowledge systems, this paper argues communities in the Mid West of Western Australia experience mining transitions within a broader regional context. Through community-engaged methodology, semi-structured interviews were conducted with twenty-two participants, including First Nations community members, across diverse sectors and sub-regions. Analysis revealed three interconnected knowledge forms: contextual knowledge situating mining within regional systems; observed knowledge from direct experiences of the mining industry; and practical knowledge of mining transitions and strategies to manage them. These forms constitute a regional transition knowledge system that already exists within communities in mining regions, distinct from industry expertise. Title: The impact of decision-making sequences on national and store brand competition: a game theoretic approach
Abstract: This paper examines how decision-making sequences influence pricing and advertising strategies in a dual-brand supply chain consisting of a national brand (NB) manufacturer and a retailer offering a competing store brand (SB). The manufacturer engages in national advertising, while the retailer conducts local advertising, creating asymmetric promotional effects. Title: Towards a digital skills framework for the energy sector: Evidence from the Australian LNG industry
Abstract: Digital innovations have become increasingly widespread in almost every industry, and Australia’s energy sector has not been immune to this. It therefore follows that the coordination of energy exports like liquified natural gas (LNG) across government, industry, and community stakeholders will be largely dependent on the ability of these constituents to share digital information between and among each other in useful timeframes. However, the success of these integrated data systems will hinge on the ability of the energy sector’s workforce to use these technologies effectively, but it is increasingly coming into focus that the industry’s workers have very uneven levels of proficiency with digital technologies. By synthesizing earlier digital skills frameworks from other industries and adding qualitative evidence distilled from 42 interviews with a broad range of employees throughout a midsize Australian LNG company, this paper puts forward a digital skills framework for the energy sector which identifies five skill areas that will be required in 2030: (1) data analytics, (2) digital communication and collaboration, (3) digital security, (4) digital ethical and social responsibility, and (5) digital innovation. The required level of proficiency that will be required in 2030 for each of these skill areas is then assessed for different discipline groups throughout the industry. Title: Surfactant-Derived Nitrogen-Bridged MoS2/C Heterostructures for Robust Lithium-Ion Storage

Title: Will the deepening of interdependence network coupling increase the robustness of the network?
Source title: International Journal of Modern Physics C
Abstract: Modern networks are increasingly interdependent, with a typical example being the coupling relationship between communication networks and power networks. As smart grids evolve and coupling intensifies, the overall security of the networks faces significant challenges. Some real-world cases have indicated that increasing the coupling strength between networks may increase the vulnerability of networks to failures. Many researchers have studied the coupling relationship in interdependent networks from various perspectives, including modeling the coupling relationship, considering load flow and developing strategies for failure mitigation and recovery. However, there is currently limited research on the specific effects of coupling strength on network robustness. This paper focuses on the interdependence between communication networks and modern power grids and investigates the influence of coupling strength on network robustness by constructing a cascading failure model. Title: E-retailer channel selection in live-streaming commerce: balancing traffic attraction and information disclosure
Abstract: Live-streaming commerce allows e-retailers to attract new consumers, but it also provides valuation-relevant information that can make consumers more selective. This paper studies an e-retailer’s channel-entry and pricing decisions when a live broadcast channel simultaneously generates additional traffic and discloses noisy information about consumers’ true valuations for a new product. In our model, consumers in the original channel are initially uncertain about their match values and purchase based on their prior expected valuation. If the retailer opens the live broadcast channel, newly attracted consumers and informed consumers from the original channel can watch the live stream and update their valuations, whereas uninformed consumers remain in the original channel. We show that live-channel entry is governed by a tradeoff between traffic attraction and information disclosure. Although the live broadcast channel expands market reach, more accurate information induces low-valuation consumers to exit and weakens the retailer’s pricing power. Title: Financial leverage in business sector profitability: A review

Title: High-Spatiotemporal and Multimodal Soft Tactile Interface with Layered Architecture for Simultaneous Structural and Thermal Perception
Abstract: Advanced robotic systems require tactile perception to interact reliably with objects in environments where visual information is limited by occlusion, illumination variations, and focusing issues. Each sensing layer operates through independent transduction mechanisms, enabling the simultaneous perception of structural and thermal profiles with minimal cross-interference. The fabricated multimodal array can spatially resolve both contact geometry and localized thermal distributions with high-spatiotemporal resolution. Furthermore, by applying a tactile scanning strategy in robotic perception, the platform successfully identifies geometric features and surface thermal profiles of target objects even under vision-limited conditions. Authors: Shen S.; Yang S.; Jiang Y.
Title: Enhancing communication competence and managerial skills through virtual reality based experiential learning in management education
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising pedagogical modality in higher management education, offering immersive, risk-free environments that simulate the complexity of real-world organizational interactions. This study investigates whether, and to what extent, VR-based experiential learning is associated with students' communication competence and managerial self-efficacy, drawing on Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory and Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory. Using a cross-sectional survey design complemented by platform-generated usage logs, we analyzed survey and behavioral data from 412 postgraduate and undergraduate management students across three program types at a research-intensive business school. Ordinary least squares regression served as the primary analysis, supplemented by instrumental-variable estimation (IV/2SLS), generalized method of moments (GMM), and propensity score matching to address potential endogeneity and selection bias. Bootstrap mediation analyses indicated that experiential learning depth and reflective practice partially mediate the associations between VR intensity parameters and both outcomes. Heterogeneity analyses revealed stronger associations among executive-education participants and where instructor facilitation quality was high. Findings were robust to alternative specifications and sample-trimming procedures. The study contributes a multi-method framework for integrating immersive technology into business-school curricula and offers actionable recommendations for curriculum designers, institutional administrators, and educational-technology policymakers. © 2026

Title: A physical model approach to order lot sizing
Abstract: Abstract: The increasing pressure to reduce operational costs and enhance supply chain efficiency has made inventory management a key area of optimization. In this context, the lot-sizing problem remains a fundamental challenge due to its direct impact on ordering and holding costs. We propose an analytical approach to the lot-sizing problem based on an analogy with a one-dimensional mechanical system of particles connected by elastic elements. This interpretation allows the cost minimization conditions to be derived naturally and leads to an exact solution without resorting to heuristic or computationally intensive methods. The model characterizes the optimal policy through a single dimensionless parameter,, which governs the system behavior: when, the optimal strategy is to place one order per period, whereas for, the optimal number of orders N is smaller than the planning horizon M (). By expressing the total cost in terms of the intensive variable N/M, the problem can be formulated as a single function of. This reduces the need for complex iterative optimization algorithms, requiring only simple adjustments (integer feasibility, rounding, and discrete order composition) to obtain a direct determination of optimal order frequencies and lot sizes. The relevance of this work lies in providing both a novel theoretical perspective and a practical tool for inventory control, allowing faster and more transparent decision-making, particularly in real-time and large-scale planning environments. The applicability of the framework is illustrated through a real-world case study involving a concentrated pulp processing plant, as well as a representative example drawn from the literature, allowing for comparison with classical EOQ-based policies. In addition, a sensitivity analysis with respect to the model parameters is conducted, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed approach. Managerial implications are also discussed, highlighting the interpretability and operational applicability of the model. Title: Alkaline-thermal and enzymatic pretreatment of PLA/PBAT plastics boosts methane production from anaerobic co-digestion with food waste
Abstract: The co-treatment of food waste (FW) and biodegradable plastics in anaerobic digestion (AD) is challenged by the slow degradation of polylactic acid and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PLA/PBAT) blends. This study systematically evaluated alkaline-thermal (AT) and enzymatic pretreatment of two PLA/PBAT plastics—starch-containing (PLA/PBAT/ST) and mineral dust-containing (PLA/PBAT/MD)—followed by anaerobic co-digestion with FW. AT pretreatment significantly enhanced methane production. The highest cumulative methane yield (223.40 ± 5.62 mL/g VS) was obtained with PLA/PBAT/MD pretreated at 140℃, a 25.2 % increase over the untreated control (CK-MD), while PLA/PBAT/ST showed an 8.6 % increase (197.60 ± 2.49 mL/g VS). Enzymatic pretreatment led to only marginal improvements. Scanning electron microscopy and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed that AT at 140℃ induced extensive surface erosion, pore formation, and ester bond cleavage, thereby increasing surface hydrophilicity and microbial accessibility. Microbial community analysis indicated that AT-pretreated plastics selectively enriched hydrogenotrophic methanogens ( Methanobacterium ) and syntrophic bacteria ( Syntrophomonas ), and showed higher relative abundance of genes putatively involved in electron bifurcation and methanogenesis (e.g., K14126). In contrast, enzyme-pretreated plastics promoted hydrolytic bacteria (Synergistota) and glycolysis-related genes, causing volatile fatty acids accumulation and metabolic imbalance. These findings demonstrate that AT pretreatment is a promising strategy to enhance methane recovery from FW and biodegradable plastic co-digestion, providing mechanistic insights for process optimization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Is green product trade a pathway to better air quality in China?
Abstract: This study evaluates whether green product trade can serve as an effective pathway to improving air quality in China. Using panel data for 28 provinces from 2010 to 2021, we are the first to jointly examine the impacts of green trade on six major air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, NOx, and CO2) while simultaneously identifying both its temporal dynamics and spatial spillover effects within a unified empirical framework. We construct an integrated green-product trade database combining the APEC, OECD, and World Bank classifications and employ System GMM and the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) to address spatial-temporal dependence. The results show that a 1% increase in green trade reduces PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations by approximately 1.1%. Moreover, green imports in neighboring provinces generate strong spatial spillovers, lowering local PM2.5, PM10, CO, and SO2 emissions by about 5%. We also find that green imports exert significantly stronger pollution-reduction effects than green exports, suggesting an import-driven technology-upgrade mechanism typical of developing economies. These findings provide robust evidence that green trade contributes to China's environmental improvements and offer important policy insights for emerging economies seeking to leverage green globalization for sustainable, lower-emission development. Title: When crowds converge: Link between events and crime
Abstract: This study draws on environmental criminology to conceptualize planned events as bounded opportunity contexts that temporarily reshape urban activity. Using high-dimensional fixed-effects Poisson models and a panel of 154,561 events in Houston, Texas, we estimate reduced-form associations across event attributes and offense types. The event-crime association is statistically detectable but economically modest. Formal comparisons reveal selective offense heterogeneity, with the Crimes Against Society coefficient exceeding the Violent Crime coefficient. Public opportunistic crime also shows stronger associations than private opportunistic and non-opportunistic crime, but not Other Crime. Event size exhibits significant heterogeneity, with the largest events showing stronger associations than those in all lower-attendance categories. Event type, day-type context, duration, and recurrence are not statistically distinguishable. Adjustment for contemporaneous foot traffic attenuates the event coefficient. The findings suggest proportionate, targeted situational prevention rather than generalized security escalation in urban destination safety planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
