Title: Petroleum fiscal regimes and contractor returns: empirical analysis of the North Sea and Gulf of Guinea
Abstract: Petroleum fiscal regimes are institutions through which resource rents, investment risks, public revenues, and domestic economic opportunities are allocated among states, firms, and producing societies. Yet they are often assessed primarily through tax burdens and contractor returns. This study develops a mechanism-based framework that distinguishes direct production-cost effects, cash-flow redistribution, timing-related liquidity effects, and their wider governance and development implications. A structured comparative analysis of legal, contractual, administrative, and regulatory documents from the United Kingdom, Norway, Ghana, and Nigeria is combined with a normalised cash-flow illustration. The findings show that royalties primarily secure early public revenue while reducing pre-payout contractor cash flow; cost-recovery ceilings mainly defer reimbursement and place particular demands on audit capacity; and profit-based taxes track profitability more closely but depend on transparent bases, loss rules, and predictable administration. State participation and local-content requirements can strengthen domestic capability and value retention, although poorly calibrated obligations may increase financing, procurement, compliance, and delivery pressures. Regulatory complexity and fiscal instability further shape administrative discretion, credibility, and investment risk. The comparison demonstrates that petroleum fiscal design is not only an economic allocation problem but also a resource-governance challenge. Effective regimes therefore require progressivity, credible cost verification, accountable state participation, capacity-sensitive local-content policy, transparent administration, and rules that align public revenue mobilisation with commercially viable investment and domestic development objectives. © 2026 .

Title: A Buried Sulfonate Molecular Bridge for Synchronous Charge Transport and Defect Passivation in High-Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
Abstract: The quality of the buried interface between the self-assembled molecules (SAM) and the perovskite layer directly governs the processes of charge carrier transport and non-radiative recombination, which ultimately dictates the efficiency and stability of the inverted perovskite solar cells. However, the simultaneous mitigation of poor SAM layer adhesion and perovskite substrate interface defects remains a significant challenge. Herein, low-cost and readily available 2‑formylbenzenesulfonic acid sodium salt (2‑FAS) is employed as a bifunctional interlayer to molecularly bridge the SAM and perovskite. The benzene ring of 2‑FAS interacts via π–π stacking with the SAM, strengthening adhesion and promoting hole transfer, while its sulfonate group (-SO3−) coordinates with Pb2+ to regulate crystallization and passivate surface defects. As a result, the 2-FAS-modified devices deliver a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.21%, with a significant fill factor of 86.15%. Furthermore, Na+ from 2‑FAS occupies A‑site vacancies in the perovskite lattice, which effectively suppresses ion migration and phase transition, thereby enhancing structural integrity. Benefiting from these combined effects, unencapsulated devices retain over 90% of their initial PCE after 4500 h of storage in a nitrogen atmosphere, demonstrating exceptional long-term stability. Title: Driving police engagement through talent management: Evidence from Abu Dhabi
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between talent management practices and employee engagement, as well as the moderating role of business analytics and the subsequent impact on employee performance within the Abu Dhabi Police. Specifically, the research explores how talent attraction, retention, learning and development, and career management influence employee engagement, which in turn affects job performance. Drawing on social exchange theory, dynamic capability theory, and Aon Hewitt's employee engagement model, a quantitative research design was employed using a structured questionnaire distributed to senior officers across various departments. A total of 383 valid responses were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 3.3.9. The findings reveal that all four dimensions of talent management (talent attraction, talent retention, learning and development, and career management) have significant positive effects on employee engagement. Furthermore, employee engagement strongly and significantly influences employee performance, underscoring its pivotal role in organizational effectiveness. The results of the moderation analysis indicate that business analytics significantly strengthens the relationships between talent attraction, learning and development, and career management and employee engagement, with learning and development and talent attraction showing the strongest moderating effects, whereas the moderating effect on talent retention is statistically insignificant. The model explains 53.8 of the variance in employee engagement, indicating satisfactory predictive power. These findings contribute to the literature by integrating business analytics into the talent management—engagement—performance nexus, particularly within a public sector policing context. Practically, the results highlight the strategic importance of leveraging data-driven and analytics-enabled HRM practices to personalize talent management interventions, enhance perceived fairness, and improve engagement outcomes. Overall, the findings demonstrate that while business analytics enhances most talent management dimensions, its influence is not uniform across all practices, particularly in the case of talent retention. Title: From AI use to AI capability: Developing responsible, reflective and employable learners in management education
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has entered management education faster than many business schools have redesigned pedagogy, assessment, and employability development. This study examines how management students’ AI use can be transformed into responsible, reflective, and employable AI capabilities. Using a pre- and post-intervention design with 412 management students across two comparable course sections, the study compared a conventional AI access condition with a guided AI capability condition. The guided condition included four pedagogical modules on task alignment, evidence verification, responsible reflection, and employability translation. Data was collected through survey measures, AI use logs, reflective journals, rubric-based project assessment, and structural equation modelling. The results show that the guided group achieved substantially higher gains in task-aligned AI use, responsible reflection, AI capability, and employability confidence. Project performance data confirmed this pattern, with the largest difference in ethical awareness between the two groups. The structural model shows that AI readiness does not directly influence employability confidence. Instead, readiness influences confidence through task-aligned use, responsible reflection, and AI capability. This study contributes by shifting attention from AI adoption to AI capability and by positioning responsible reflection as the key mechanism through which AI use becomes learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Enhancing DER hosting capacity of unbalanced low-voltage distribution networks with network exchangers: An Australian case study
Abstract: The rapid growth and subsequent utilization of distributed energy resources (DERs), particularly in low-voltage networks, is pushing distribution networks to the brink of their hosting capacity. Distribution network operators, especially in DER-rich countries such as Australia, are exploring novel technologies and effective strategies to enhance DER integration while maintaining network integrity, as an alternative to costly network upgrades. Simulation results indicate breaches in network integrity under business-as-usual conditions in both step-change and progressive-change scenarios. The performance of each technology is benchmarked across six low-voltage networks that exhibit higher levels of network violations and photovoltaic curtailment, with NEx resolving all voltage breaches and reducing transformer loading and photovoltaic curtailment by noticeable amounts, which can aid in delaying costly network augmentation. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis of Thalassemia Screening Cascade Efficiency: Single-Sample Versus Multivisit Protocols in Malaysia
Abstract: Objectives Malaysia's National Thalassemia Screening Program uses multivisit sequential testing (protocol 1), with a dropout rate of 20%, disproportionately affecting rural and underserved populations in Sabah and Sarawak. Monte Carlo simulations (10 000 iterations) assigned probability distributions to all parameters: gamma distributions for costs (15% coefficient of variation) and beta-binomial for dropout rates. Cost-effectiveness acceptability curves estimated probabilities across willingness-to-pay thresholds of MYR 10-50 per additional carrier detected. Scenario analyses tested protocol 2 dropout rates ranging from 0.5% (base case) to 5% (pessimistic). At MYR 25-50 thresholds, protocol 2 has a > 91% probability of cost-effectiveness in Sabah and ∼100% in Sarawak. Under pessimistic 5% dropout scenarios, probabilities remained ≥70%, indicating substantial implementation tolerance. Conclusion Probabilistic sensitivity analysis demonstrated that protocol 2 maintained favorable screening cascade efficiency across plausible operational scenarios. The lower incremental cost-effectiveness ratio in Sarawak suggests potential equity advantages in higher dropout settings. Illustrative willingness-to-pay thresholds of MYR 10-50 per additional carrier detected were explored for scenario interpretation rather than as normative policy thresholds. Title: From diagnosis to explanation: An integrated framework for examining spatially heterogeneous associations between temporary industrial-land use and neighborhood gentrification
Abstract: As Chinese megacities transition to post-industrialism, the socio-spatial consequences of temporary industrial land reuse—a pivotal urban renewal strategy—remain under-theorized. Title: Embedding ESG, sustainability and ethics in accounting assessment: Bridging global standards and educational practice
Abstract: The growing prominence of environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, sustainability, and ethical accountability is reshaping expectations of accounting and management graduates. While these competencies are increasingly embedded within global professional standards and competency frameworks, their translation into educational assessment remains underexplored. This study examines how ESG, sustainability, and ethics are embedded in documented assessment across global standards, professional competency frameworks, and Australian university accounting education. Using qualitative comparative document analysis, the study analyses the International Federation of Accountants’ International Education Standards, the competency frameworks of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, and assessment documentation from 104 undergraduate accounting units across 26 Australian universities. The findings reveal partial and uneven alignment. Although sustainability and ethics are explicitly articulated within global and professional frameworks, they are frequently embedded implicitly within technically oriented assessment tasks rather than explicitly assessed as judgement-focused competencies. To explain this pattern, the study introduces the concept of differential assessability, which explains why some professional competencies are more readily translated into assessment than others despite comparable prominence within professional standards. By reframing ESG integration as an assessment design challenge, the study extends assessment theory and offers practical implications for responsible management and accounting education. © 2026

Title: Designing ethical negotiation simulations for measurable metacognitive development: Boundary conditions in SCELM
Abstract: Ethical negotiation simulations generate strong engagement but often fail to produce measurable metacognitive development in students. This boundary condition design study argues that the problem is structural: many simulation formats are misaligned with the consolidation phase through which disruption becomes learning. We evaluated two implementations of Structured Cross-Cultural Ethical Leadership through Multilateral Negotiations (SCELM): a multicultural rotating format (N = 84 responses; matched n = 26) and a bilateral intercultural format (N = 39; Battle 1 n = 30) across four high-institutional-distance dyads in this study. Paired t-tests and thematic analyses of 124 reflections (κ = 0.81) were conducted in parallel. The rotating format produced no significant within-person changes across any metacognitive index (all d ≤ 0.17). In contrast, the bilateral format generated greater baseline assumption disruption, as indicated by a significant Welch's t-test (p = .028) and marginally higher role tension (p = .063). Qualitative findings showed that perspective revision occurred primarily during structured intra-team consolidation rather than during negotiations, indicating that immediate post-battle surveys underestimate learning. We propose four educator-facing design principles and a dual-timepoint Assurance of Learning protocol, recommending that perspective-shift outcomes be assessed after structured consolidation rather than immediately following negotiation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Multi-objective optimization for emergency primary logistics of refined products under pipeline disruption condition: a case study in China
Abstract: The primary logistics of refined products plays a critical role in ensuring regional oil supply security and supporting efficient oil allocation. As the dominant transportation mode in primary logistics systems, pipelines are critical for refined products transportation, and pipeline disruptions may significantly affect logistics performance and supply continuity. To address this issue, a multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model is proposed for emergency primary logistics planning of refined products under pipeline disruption condition. The model considers logistics cost and supply shortage as conflicting objectives while integrating multiple transportation modes, lateral transportation, temporary procurement, and temporary vehicle rental decisions within a unified optimization framework. The augmented ε-constraint method is employed to obtain Pareto optimal solutions and analyze the trade-off between economic efficiency and supply security. A real-world large-scale refined products primary logistics system in China is used as a case study. The results show that pipeline disruptions substantially alter transportation patterns, increasing the share of rail transportation from over 20% to more than 30%, while road transportation is generally between 3 and 5%. The analyses further illustrate the impact of pipeline disruption on logistics planning and show the effectiveness of the proposed multi-objective methodology in balancing logistics cost and supply shortage. The obtained Pareto optimal solutions provide flexible decision support for emergency primary logistics planning under different disruption scenarios. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Molecular insights into aldehyde-mediated assembly and bioactivity of peptide–polysaccharide composite hydrogels
Abstract: Inflammation and oxidative stress are central pathological drivers of numerous diseases and infections, necessitating the development of bioactive peptide-based hydrogels with integrated anti-inflammatory and antibacterial functionalities. This study reported the construction of novel composite hydrogels via synergistic integration of enzymatic yak bone collagen peptides with carrageenan-xanthan gum, functionalized with aromatic aldehydes including anethole aldehyde, vanillin and protocatechuic aldehyde. Rheological and microstructural analyses revealed that protocatechuic aldehyde-loaded hydrogel (COP-PC/CX) exhibited superior viscoelastic stability (crossover strain 22.1%), uniform porous architecture, and robust network connectivity compared with anethole aldehyde-loaded hydrogels and vanillin-loaded hydrogels. FTIR, 1H NMR and XRD confirmed that aldehyde-loaded hydrogel stabilization was governed by cooperative hydrogen bonding and dynamic Schiff base crosslinking, and different aromatic aldehydes altered the structure–function relationships of the peptide–polysaccharide hydrogels. The composite hydrogel of COP-PC/CX showed exceptional broad-spectrum antibacterial efficacy and antioxidant capacity, achieving inhibition rates of up to 97.18% against E. coli. Functionally, the treatment of COP-PC/CX hydrogel showed the most intense response to attenuate pro-inflammatory macrophage activation by downregulating TNF-α and IL-6 via cytokine signaling and leukocyte migration pathway modulation, while reducing intracellular ROS levels, which were corroborated by transcriptomic analysis of macrophages treated by these aldehyde-loaded hydrogels. This work advanced a sustainable design that valorized animal by-products through plant-derived bioactive integration, establishing a molecularly informed strategy for synergistic dual-functional biomaterials in food preservation and biomedical applications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Asymptotic analysis of tail moment in a dependent risk model
Source title: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: In this paper, we discuss a risk model with multiple business lines, where the log-discount process is a combination of a general adapted process with continuous paths and a compound stochastic jump process. We propose a dependence structure under the framework of multivariate regular variation, which not only captures the dependence among the insurance losses but also the one between the insurance losses and the financial jump sizes. We study a novel tail moment risk measure defined as the conditional moment of the present value of an individual business line's aggregate losses, given that the present value of aggregate losses of all business lines exceeds its Value-at-Risk. With the help of Extreme Value Theory, we derive asymptotic expansion of the tail moment. We illustrate the main results with some numerical studies which reveal that while the tail moment is notably impacted by the dependence structure, the heavy-tailedness plays a comparatively more significant role. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: From influence to empowerment: Unpacking capacity building and social learning in virtual communities
Abstract: This study explores how independent travel empowers women travel influencers and how meanings of empowerment are negotiated through interactions with their followers by examining the empowerment process at both individual and social levels. Drawing on capacity building theory and social cognitive theory, it investigates how travel experiences and digital content creation contribute to personal agency, skill development, and socially mediated expressions of empowerment. Using an interpretive paradigm and a netnographic approach, the study analyses the social media practices of 17 female travel influencers. Findings show that independent travel fosters self-efficacy, confidence, and the acquisition of skills and knowledge among influencers, while followers express inspiration, aspiration, identification, and negotiation of constraints in response to shared narratives of empowerment. The study underscores the dynamic interplay among digital influence, community engagement, and gendered empowerment, offering insights into virtual capacity building within contemporary travel cultures. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Multimarket contact, excess capacity, and low-cost carrier competition: A dual-channel model of mutual forbearance in international airline markets
Abstract: Research on the relationship between multimarket contact (MMC) and firm performance has produced mixed results. To help reconcile this discrepancy, we examine how firm-level excess capacity and low-cost carrier (LCC) competition condition the MMC–performance relationship in international airline markets. Drawing on mutual forbearance theory, we disaggregate total multimarket contact into contacts through strong resource-sharing markets (routes sharing endpoint cities) and weak resource-sharing markets (routes without shared endpoints), and we theorize a dual-channel model in which excess capacity determines which type of contact drives forbearance. Our analysis of 2979 firm–market–year observations spanning 82 airlines across 265 route markets serving Taiwan over the period 2009–2018 reveals three principal findings. First, total MMC exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with subsequent market share. Second, excess capacity channels the significant concave MMC profiles through different contact types: strong resource-sharing contact among high-excess-capacity firms (where idle capacity is visible at shared airports) and weak resource-sharing contact among low-excess-capacity firms (where network breadth sustains competitive awareness); in both cases the estimated downturn lies in a sparsely populated right tail and is interpreted cautiously. Third, LCC entry disrupts the forbearance equilibrium: the inverted U-shape is absent in markets with LCC competitors, and an exploratory positive linear pattern in those markets suggests that multimarket contact functions there as a competitive resource rather than as a forbearance signal. Accordingly, our study contributes to the multimarket competition literature by shedding light on how firm resources and competitive context jointly determine the mechanism and viability of mutual forbearance, helping to reconcile the inconsistent findings in prior research. Title: Generative AI communications and firm value: Evidence from digital innovation in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms using deep learning
Abstract: This study examines whether firm-initiated generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) communications are associated with firm value in UK-listed tourism, travel, and hospitality (TTH) firms. The final sample includes 177 firms from 2018 to 2024, comprising 68 firms with verified WeChat official accounts and 109 firms retained with zero-valued communication measures. From 105,429 archived posts, we develop a bilingual annotation scheme and supervised deep-learning classifiers to identify GenAI communication and distinguish implementation-salient disclosures from generic mentions. Our preferred measures are share-normalized, capturing both GenAI communication intensity and implementation emphasis relative to total posting activity. Firm- and year-fixed-effects results show that implementation-weighted GenAI communication is positively associated with Tobin's Q and operating performance. Digital innovation partially mediates this relationship, while industry dynamism and complexity strengthen it, but munificence does not. The study contributes a tourism-specific measure of GenAI capability signaling and clarifies the value relevance of implementation-oriented communication in service-intensive digital contexts. © 2026 The Author.

Authors: Zhang Y.; Pan J.; Cao Y.; Li R.; Wang W.
Title: Maximum-entropy minimal model for gas–liquid two-phase flow liquid holdup prediction across full pipe inclination angles
Abstract: Liquid holdup governs pressure drop, flow-pattern transitions, and separation efficiency in gas–liquid pipe flow, but accurate and interpretable prediction across operating conditions remains difficult. In this paper, a maximum-entropy minimal model is extended to continuous multiphase flow to seek a minimal set of dimensionless variables using a linear combination of transformed predictors and a residual-correlation stopping criterion with all excluded candidates. From 35 candidate features constructed from nine physical parameters, greedy forward selection yields a closed-form model containing six selected predictors: no-slip liquid fraction, gas superficial velocity, gas–liquid density ratio, momentum ratio, mixture Froude number, and cosine of inclination. Evaluated on 746 experimental points covering four fluid pairs, seven pipe diameters, and inclinations from − 90° to + 90°, the model attains R2 = 0.9822 and a root-mean-square error of 0.0377. Five-fold cross-validation (R2 = 0.9820 ± 0.0026), holdout data (R2 = 0.9837), and out-of-distribution tests withholding a data source, horizontal flow, or a pipe diameter (R2 = 0.924 ∼ 0.975) confirm robust generalization. However, uneven coverage of inclinations and fluid properties, together with dependence on the compiled experimental sources, constrains the demonstrated scope of generalization. Within the selected six-predictor representation, quadratic and three-way interaction extensions increased mean cross-validated R2 by less than 0.002 under the evaluated settings. Inclination-resolved analysis reveals a complexity hierarchy: downward, upward, and horizontal flows require 1, 3, and 12 features, respectively, describing differences in the selected model sizes across inclination subsets. The unified expression approaches the accuracy of a tuned neural-network benchmark with only seven fitted parameters, a 6034-fold reduction relative to the benchmark. These results provide a data-determined measure of the physical complexity required to describe gas–liquid phase distribution and yield a transparent relation for engineering deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Mental Health and Neurodivergence Disclosure Risk Mitigation in Private Higher Education Institutions: An Integrated Risk-Protection Framework to Support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
Source title: ASEAN Journal of Educational Research and Technology
Abstract: This study examines mental health and neurodivergence disclosure risk mitigation in private higher education institutions through an Integrated Risk-Protection Framework to support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 297 academic and non-academic staff from selected private higher education institutions in Selangor, Malaysia. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Structural power asymmetry, institutional trust deficit, stigma anticipation, and absence of safeguards reduce psychological safety in disclosure. Perceived enforceability of protection moderates these relationships and strengthens the explanatory power of the model. Title: Reliability modeling and evaluation for discrete competing failure processes
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: There are many engineering systems that can fail due to both the internal degradation of the system itself and the effects of external shocks. The external shocks also affect the degradation of the system. In this paper, discrete analogues of the competing failure processes previously studied in the literature for the continuous case are considered. Exact reliability equations are obtained for a system that is exposed to both internal degradation and external shocks over periods when the shock magnitudes have a discrete probability distribution. Title: Bismuth-engineered interfacial electronic modulation for enhanced selective conversion of NO-to-NO3− over UiO-66-NH2
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: It is still a key challenge to achieve the selective photocatalytic oxidation of NO-to-NO3− while inhibiting the release of NO2. Changing the reaction energetics of the photocatalytic process by adjusting the electronic structure of the active site provides an effective way to solve this problem. In this study, bismuth nanorods were introduced into UiO-66-NH2 to construct photocatalytic composites, in which the interface Bi-O-Zr interaction led to significant electron redistribution at the Zr center. This electronic modulation, while maintaining comparable generation capability of ·OH, 1O2, and ·O2−, substantially reshapes the thermodynamic and kinetic characteristics of photocatalytic NO oxidation. Specifically, the reaction energy barrier associated with the 1O2/·O2− mediated NO → NO3− pathway is markedly reduced. At the same time, the adsorption of NO2 derived from ·OH is enhanced, promoting its subsequent conversion to NO3−. The synergistic improvement of the two reaction pathways results in Bi@UiO-66-NH2 achieving nearly twice the effectiveness of the pristine UiO-66-NH2 in removing NO, while almost completely suppressing NO2 release. This study demonstrates that interface electronics engineering is an effective strategy for modulating reaction pathways and provides practical guidance for designing photocatalysts with enhanced selectivity. © 2026

Authors: Zhang J.; Li W.; Huang D.; Rajic V.
Title: An intelligent and adaptive algorithm for reliability enhancement of an energy harvester under fractional-order control and stochastic excitation
Abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent adaptive algorithm for enhancing the reliability of a tri-stable piezoelectric energy harvesting system under fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative control and Gaussian white-noise excitation. The controlled electromechanical system is reduced using an equivalent decoupling procedure and an improved stochastic averaging method. The conditional reliability function is obtained from the backward Kolmogorov equation, while the mean first-passage time is evaluated using the generalized Pontryagin equation. An adaptive particle swarm optimization method combined with a Logistic basis function neural network is then developed to solve the reliability equation and simultaneously optimize the two fractional orders. For the considered parameter set, the optimized controller increases the time-averaged reliability by 6.3% and extends the mean first-passage time by 29.2% relative to the uncontrolled case. The network solution achieves a mean error of 0.0044 compared with Monte Carlo simulations. Finally, a sensitivity analysis is discussed to assess the effects of the main algorithm parameters. The proposed algorithm provides an efficient reliability-oriented tool for the optimal fractional-order control of strongly nonlinear energy harvesting systems under random excitation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Awad A.
Title: Conformance checking on event streams: A comprehensive survey
Abstract: Event streams have become a core abstraction for building modern software systems, from cloud services and IoT deployments to cyber-physical and data-intensive applications. In such settings, developers and operators increasingly need runtime conformance monitoring: assessing whether ongoing executions comply with a prescriptive model or constraint set while decisions can still be taken. Classic offline conformance checking is ill-suited because streams are potentially unbounded, arrivals may be delayed or out of order, and monitoring must satisfy strict operational requirements, such as bounded state, low latency, and robustness to imperfect observations and evolving behaviour. This survey reviews the state of the art in online conformance checking. We derive a baseline of functional and non-functional requirements for online conformance checking and introduce a taxonomy that organises approaches across imperative, declarative, and emerging object-centric paradigms. Assessing the surveyed approaches against this baseline, we synthesise recurring design patterns and clarify the trade-offs that shape deployability on stateful stream-processing platforms. We find that existing techniques typically address only subsets of the requirements, and we identify underexplored challenges, including standardised benchmarking, principled state eviction, object-centric monitoring at scale, integrated handling of concept drift and model evolution, and unifying infrastructural robustness with expressive conformance feedback. Finally, we propose a reference architecture that maps these requirements to standard streaming operators and managed state, providing a blueprint for implementations and a concrete agenda for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Atomic High-Spin Cobalt Unlocks Reversible Multi-Electron Transfer Chemistry for Superb Aqueous Zn-Mn Batteries
Abstract: To settle inherent irreversible phase transition and motivate re-dissolution of deposited “dead” MnO2 without acid and redox mediator addition, we introduced atomic-dispersed Co atoms with high-spin state into layered MnO2, denoted as Co–MnO2, via an in situ topological phase transformation strategy, thereby unlocking reversible multi-electron transfer chemistry for superb Zn–Mn batteries. Specifically, atomic-distributed Co atoms within Co–MnO2 effectively modulate [MnO6] octahedral symmetry and reduce Co–O bond covalency along with enhanced lattice oxygen activity. Based on this, high-spin Co (t2g4eg2) greatly mitigates the Jahn–Teller distortion as well as promotes electrolytic MnO2 deposited onto the cathode surface completely converted from adsorbed Mn2+ for inhibited “Mn dendrites”, achieving reversible MnO2/Mn3+ and electrolytic MnO2/Mn2+ reactions with highly thermodynamical favorability. Benefiting from the “two-step, three-electron” mechanism triggered by high-spin Co, Zn//Co–MnO2 battery delivers an outstanding capacity of 658 mAh g–1 and ultra-long lifespan over 15,000 cycles. This work reveals the critical role of transition-metal spin state modulation for energy-dense and durable Zn-MnO2 batteries with reversible multi-electron storage mechanisms. Title: Benzylbiphenyl-regulated poly(aromatic ethylimidazole)s toward high-performance high temperature proton exchange membranes in fuel cells
Source title: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
Abstract: The development of high temperature proton exchange membranes (HT-PEMs) with simultaneously enhanced proton transport and mechanical robustness remains a major challenge for HT-PEM fuel cells. Herein, we report a molecular backbone engineering strategy based on the incorporation of 4-benzylbiphenyl (BBP) units into poly(p-terphenyl ethylimidazole) frameworks to regulate chain conformation and membrane properties. A series of BBP-containing P(TPx%-BBPy%-EIm) copolymers with systematically varied compositions are synthesized via a superacid-catalyzed Friedel-Crafts polymerization, enabling an in-depth investigation of the relationship between backbone architecture and membrane performance. Experimental characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that the sp3-hybridized methylene bridge in BBP disrupts continuous π-conjugation and induces a twisted, flexible polymer configuration, which enhances phosphoric acid (PA) affinity, promotes microphase separation, and facilitates proton conduction. Among the resulting membranes, P(TP70%-BBP30%-EIm)/214%PA achieves an optimized balance between conductivity and mechanical integrity, exhibiting a tensile strength of 15.7 MPa and a proton conductivity of 104 mS cm−1 at 180 °C under anhydrous conditions. When integrated into an H2/O2 membrane electrode assembly, this membrane delivers a peak power density of 783 mW cm−2 at 180 °C under non-humidified and zero-backpressure conditions, which also display a 144-h durability under 200 mA cm−2 at 160 °C. This work establishes flexible benzylbiphenyl-containing poly(aromatic ethylimidazole) polymers as a promising platform for HT-PEMs in fuel cells and also provides a molecular design strategy for developing advanced membrane materials for other new energy devices. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Workplace management of musculoskeletal and mental health risks: translating evidence into practice
Abstract: There is a large body of research evidence identifying the biomechanical and psychosocial hazards that can affect work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and stress-related mental health problems (MHPs). The APHIRM Toolkit was developed to facilitate more effective translation of this evidence into workplace risk management practices. Using APHIRM survey data from three occupations in the healthcare sector, this project compared hazard ‘riskiness’ profiles: (a) at occupational versus local workgroup levels, and (b) using hazard constructs versus individual hazard items. It was concluded that effective risk management is likely to require: risk assessment and prioritisation of control actions separately for each local workgroup; assessment of specific hazards rather than the generic constructs used by researchers. Results highlight the value of managing MSD and MHP risks together, because both were affected by both psychosocial and biomechanical hazards in combinations that varied widely between workgroups. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Photothermal Superhydrophobic Textiles: An Emerging Paradigm from Passive Water Repellency to Active Thermal Management
Abstract: Photothermal superhydrophobic textiles represent an emerging paradigm integrating active light-driven functionality with passive liquid repellency. While previous reviews treated superhydrophobicity and photothermal effects in isolation, this work pioneers a systematic analysis of their synergistic interplay—a critical, underexplored mechanism where superhydrophobicity preserves photothermal efficiency by minimizing water-induced heat loss, while photothermal activity prevents surface fouling that compromises non-wetting performance. Through detailed case studies of advanced material systems, this review highlights how this synergy supports significant advancements in adaptive wearable technology, energy-efficient infrastructure, and eco-friendly water treatment. This review presents an original “lab-to-life” roadmap that structurally links material design to durability assessment, environmental impact evaluation, and scalable manufacturing strategies—a holistic framework absent in existing literature. The review emphasizes urgent sustainability priorities including green material substitutions, non-toxic solvent processing methodologies, and circular design principles aligned with global environmental regulations. By connecting fundamental mechanisms to real-world deployment scenarios while outlining transformative future directions such as AI-accelerated material discovery, stimulus-responsive systems, and intelligent manufacturing protocols, this work provides a timely and actionable reference for advancing next-generation textiles toward technological sophistication and practical viability in sustainable development. Title: Urbanisation, gender vulnerability, and ecovocation among migrant women in prostitution
Abstract: This study examines how rapid metropolitan transformation in Jakarta produces structural vulnerability and social inequality among female migrants involved in covert sexual labour within the SPA industry. It investigates the relevance of the right to the city and an eco-vocational educational approach within Population and Environmental Education as critical frameworks for understanding exclusion, agency, and citizenship. Using a qualitative multi-sited case study design, the research draws on in-depth interviews, limited participant observation, and document analysis involving women workers, SPA managers, community actors, civil society representatives, and policymakers. The data were analysed thematically through critical urban studies and feminist perspectives. The findings show that women's involvement in covert sexual labour cannot be understood simply as an individual moral failure or fully voluntary decision. Rather, it reflects constrained agency shaped by unequal labour markets, limited educational capital, family economic responsibilities, debt relations, migration pressures, and regulatory ambiguity surrounding the SPA sector. Participants experienced layered forms of exploitation, symbolic violence, stigma, and disconnected citizenship: they contributed to the city's informal service economy but remained socially marginalised, politically unrecognised, and institutionally underprotected. Urban governance practices tended to intensify this vulnerability by emphasising surveillance, raids, and moral regulation rather than social protection, labour justice, and inclusive public policy. The study argues that the right to the city offers a useful analytical lens for revealing spatial injustice and the denial of substantive citizenship among marginalised women. It further proposes eco-vocational education as a transformative framework for restoring dignity, strengthening capabilities, expanding livelihood alternatives, and promoting more inclusive, just, and humane urban futures. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Energy transition materials, climate knowledge, and the imagined supply chain: Escaping the productive paradox of necessary mining
Abstract: Much scholarship, public discourse, and policymaking on ‘energy transition materials’ (ETMs) imagines a supply chain from material production to climate mitigation, despite the absence of any mechanism ensuring that mined materials will become an electrification technology, let alone replace fossil fuels or avoid warming impacts. Scholarship about energy transition material (ETM) discourse, including criticism, largely neglects this material-discursive contradiction and truncates final analyses to paradoxes productive toward extractive futures. Leveraging a review of 99 peer-reviewed articles published between 2013-2025, this article brings mining scholarship into conversation with climate knowledge politics. It charts the dematerialization of climate knowledge from warming impacts to values negotiated along three spectra (urgency, scale, and sacrifice) and rematerialization reflected in extractive rationales (developmental, Indigenous rights, nature, and futures). Most ETM discourse is enclosed in three narrative boundaries, which lean on the imagined supply chain and foreclose non-extractive possibilities: (1) The contingencies that link climate policy and mining, such as materials science, technological manufacturing and use, are taken for granted; (2) Scalar formulations separate and compare anthropogenic climate change and mining impacts; and (3) ETMs wield climate knowledge itself as a supply chain, dialectically illustrating a problem to its own solution. Pathways to overcome the boundaries can center the materiality of mining and climate change over the abstractions of supply chains and imagined climate benefits, critically reflect on the relationships between material production and technopolitical knowledge, and take seriously actually occurring alternative livelihoods. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Divalent cation-mediated regulation of the hierarchical structure and rheological properties of ovalbumin fibrils
Abstract: Metal ions can regulate the structural organization and macroscopic properties of protein fibrillar assemblies. Although previous studies have extensively examined ion-mediated regulation of protein fibrillation, the effects of divalent cations on the hierarchical organization of preformed egg-protein fibrils remain poorly understood. In this study, OVA fibrils were prepared by heating the protein at pH 2.0 and 90 °C for 8 h, after which Mg2+, Zn2+, Ca2+, or Fe2+ was added to evaluate the effect of each ion on the post-formation organization and properties of the preformed fibrils. Divalent-cation treatment caused ion-dependent changes in the secondary-structure distribution, colloidal properties, microscopic morphology, and rheological behavior of the preformed OVA fibrils. These changes were attributed to post-formation interfibrillar association, aggregation, and structural reorganization rather than enhanced fibril formation. All OVA fibril systems showed partial precipitation at 500 mM, indicating loss of colloidal stability rather than homogeneous hydrogel formation. ICP-MS revealed ion-dependent differences in apparent metal retention. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that divalent cations regulated the hierarchical organization and rheological properties of preformed OVA fibrils through ion-dependent post-formation structural reorganization, providing a basis for controlling the functionality of egg-protein fibrillar materials. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Numerical approximation in discrete portfolio optimization using DeFi as a new asset frontier: Risk contribution and correlation dynamics in a minimum-risk portfolio
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The introduction of decentralized finance (DeFi) as an innovative asset class necessitates a reevaluation of the conventional framework for portfolio optimization. Traditional continuous-time models are challenged by the complex and non-linear features of DeFi tokens, such as discontinuous trading, high volatility, heteroskedasticity, and regime-switching behavior. The use of numerical approximation is examined in this article, optimizing portfolios with discrete techniques, including DeFi assets in a framework with low risk. We use and compare several optimization techniques, such as mean variance, Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) and a number of Risk Parity (RP) strategies are at the core of our analysis. We used a dataset of ten well-known DeFi tokens for our empirical investigation. DeFi tokens from 2021 to 2024 show a fundamental trade-off. Concentration-based models (mean-variance and CVaR) generate highly concentrated weights portfolios, leading to extreme volatility, large drawdowns, and prohibitively high portfolio turnover, which would be severely affected by real DeFi transaction fees, such as gas fees. In contrast, Risk Parity models consistently demonstrate superior practical performance. They produce well-diversified portfolios that deliver smoother results and significantly lower compound return paths and more stable rolling volatility and drastically reduced turnover. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Impact of Livelihood Capital on Farmers’ Adoption of Sustainable Crop Residue Management Practices: Empirical Evidence from Punjab Province, Pakistan
Abstract: Sustainable crop residue management can increase agricultural productivity and reduce farming-related carbon emissions, yet adoption of sustainable crop residue management practices (SCRMPs) remains limited. This study investigates how farmers’ livelihood capital shapes SCRMP adoption in Punjab, Pakistan, using survey data from 500 farmers in three agro-ecological zones. A multivariate probit model, weighted with the entropy-TOPSIS method, estimates the effects of human, social, natural, physical, and financial capital on practices including on-farm use, livestock feed, residue retention, and biogas production. Human, social, financial, and physical capital positively influence on-farm residue use, while all five forms of capital significantly promote biogas production. Although livestock feed remains the most common use, many farmers are willing to adopt alternatives such as biofertilizer production and biogas. These findings indicate substantial potential to expand sustainable residue management in the region. Policymakers should prioritize farmer training, credit access, rural infrastructure, biogas technologies, extension services, and farmer cooperatives to encourage environmentally and economically sustainable practices. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Genesis and evolution of metaverses as socio-technological realities; [پیدایش و تکامل متاورس در جایگاه واقعیتی اجتماعی و فناورانه]
Abstract: This article focuses on exploring the evolution of metaverses as socio-technological virtual spaces, which, with further development, will lead to the growth of existing or potentially new forms of social interaction. Authors: Hamidi H.; Haji Seyed Javadi F.; Zahedi M.H.
Title: Beyond Digitalization: A Conceptual and Institutional Framework for Digital Transformation in Higher Education
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Digital transformation in higher education has emerged as a strategic priority for universities worldwide over the past decade. Despite the rapid growth of scholarly interest in this field, the existing literature remains conceptually fragmented, disproportionately focused on technological aspects, and limited in providing integrated frameworks to guide digital transformation processes. This study aims to systematically synthesize the digital transformation literature in higher education, identify dominant trends, key dimensions, challenges, and research gaps, and develop an integrated conceptual framework to address these limitations. Using a systematic literature review approach in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, 145 peer-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2026 were analyzed. Data were examined through systematic content analysis across multiple levels, including temporal and geographical trends, methodological characteristics, thematic classifications, and conceptual integration of findings. The results reveal a clear shift in the literature from technology-centered perspectives toward a multidimensional, institutional, and strategic understanding of digital transformation in higher education. Three interrelated dimensions, digital technologies and infrastructure, human resources and digital skills, and leadership, culture, and policy were identified as the core components of effective digital transformation. The findings further highlight persistent research gaps related to organizational readiness, institutional implications, change management, and the contextual localization of digital transformation frameworks, particularly in developing country contexts. In response to these gaps, this study proposes an integrated conceptual framework that conceptualizes digital transformation in higher education as a dynamic four-stage process encompassing readiness and assessment, pilot implementation, scaling and integration, and continuous optimization and innovation. The proposed framework offers both an analytical foundation for future research and a practical reference for university leaders and policymakers seeking to design and implement sustainable digital transformation initiatives. © 2027 The author(s). Title: A dynamic graph query-based data pricing method via multi-armed bandits
Abstract: Graph query-based data pricing is promising for pricing answer subgraphs in graph databases according to diverse buyer queries. However, existing methods provide limited support for adaptive price updates when the broker must balance transaction revenue with transaction success rate under incomplete buyer-valuation information. To bridge this gap, we propose GQPRM, which includes: (1) a vertex-edge pricing mechanism that prices a first-time queried answer graph through non-negative atomic prices; (2) a multi-armed bandit (MAB)-based strategy that discretizes repeated-query prices into candidate actions and uses historical acceptance/rejection records for exploration and exploitation; (3) an entropy-weighted feedback update that allocates the observed subgraph-level price variation to vertices and edges in a demand-sensitive manner, rather than assuming that binary feedback uniquely identifies a single overpriced element; and (4) a smart contract-based incentive allocation mechanism that records ownership and supports auditable reward allocation between the data broker and data owners. Experiments on three typical datasets demonstrate that GQPRM improves cumulative transaction value and transaction success rate over the static baseline under the evaluated settings. © 2026

Title: Higher-order random walks on complex networks

Abstract: We investigate higher order random walks on complex networks for which the walker jumps among higher-order substructures. Title: Barriers and Facilitators of Utilizing Real-World Evidence to Support Policy Decisions in Central and Eastern Europe
Abstract: Objectives We aimed to identify drivers and solutions to overcome the barriers of the effective use of real-world data (RWD) and real-world evidence (RWE) in Central and Eastern Europe. Methods First, a targeted literature review was followed by an experts’ workshop aiming to refine and complement the identification of current barriers and drivers. Next, we performed a gap analysis on the barriers based on their importance and actionability. The scores of importance and actionability for each barrier were determined through a questionnaire completed by the experts. Finally, a second experts’ workshop was held to develop recommendations to overcome the most important actionable barriers and to collect case studies of RWD/RWE utilization. Results A total of 22 publications were included in the data extraction phase of the targeted literature review. After the first experts’ workshop, 16 barriers and 9 drivers were identified. At the second workshop 9 solutions were proposed in 4 main intervention areas. In addition, 13 case studies were provided from the 4 countries, where RWD/RWE was used effectively. Conclusions The effective use of RWD/RWE in health-policy decision making still faces several barriers in Czechia, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia. This research highlighted the most important barriers and collected recommendations by key experts on how to improve the utilization of RWD/RWE. In addition, we have identified several drivers for the use of RWD/RWE, alongside with 13 case studies, in which RWD/RWE was used effectively. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Mechanochemical activation of recycled glass–biogenic CaO composites: Structural evolution, hydration behavior, and silicate-network modification
Abstract: Mechanochemistry has emerged as a sustainable strategy for producing advanced materials from industrial and biogenic wastes. In this study, mechanochemically activated composites were synthesized using post-consumer recycled soda–lime glass as an amorphous support and biogenic calcium oxide (BCO) derived from waste eggshells as the active phase. Composites containing 5–95 wt% BCO were prepared by high-energy ball milling and characterized by X-ray fluorescence (XRF), X-ray diffraction (XRD) coupled with Rietveld refinement, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results revealed that mechanochemical activation significantly reduced the CaO crystallite size from 148.5 to 25.4 nm, while preserving the amorphous nature of the recycled glass matrix. The degree of crystallinity increased progressively with increasing BCO content, reaching 66.2% for the composite containing 95 wt% BCO; however, a substantial amorphous fraction persisted in all compositions, suggesting the formation of highly disordered crystal–amorphous interfacial regions. FTIR and Raman analyses indicated progressive modifications of the silicate network, evidenced by the formation of non-bridging oxygens and Ca–O–Si interfacial species. The Raman intensity ratio (I356/I1084) exhibited segmented behavior, revealing a critical composition of approximately 75 wt% BCO, corresponding to the transition from a glass-dominated to a CaO-dominated structural regime. These findings demonstrate that mechanochemical activation not only promotes efficient dispersion and fragmentation of CaO but also engineers crystal–amorphous interfaces in waste-derived composites, providing new insights into the structural evolution of CaO–silicate systems and highlighting their potential for the development of sustainable functional materials. © 2026

Title: Food souvenir SMEs performance: Digital marketing, branding, innovation, and Hexa Helix moderation
Abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly in the food souvenir sector, play a vital role in supporting local economic development. However, increasing competition and rapid digital transformation require SMEs to strengthen their strategic capabilities in order to maintain their marketing performance. Previous research has largely examined digital marketing capabilities, branding, and product innovation separately, with limited attention to the combined effects of these three factors and the moderating role of collaborative ecosystems such as the Hexa Helix model. This study aims to analyze the influence of digital marketing capabilities, branding, and product innovation on marketing performance, while also examining the moderating role of Hexa Helix collaboration. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from 335 SMEs owners, and the data were analyzed using Warp Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (WarpPLS-SEM). The results indicate that branding has the strongest positive effect on marketing performance ( β = 0.318, p < 0.001 ), followed by digital marketing capabilities ( β = 0.289, p < 0.001 ) and product innovation ( β = 0.117, p = 0.015 ). Regarding the moderating role, the findings indicate that the Hexa Helix does not significantly moderate the relationship between digital marketing capabilities and marketing performance, nor between branding and marketing performance. However, the Hexa Helix significantly strengthens the relationship between product innovation and marketing performance ( β = 0.217, p < 0.001 ). These findings suggest that while internal strategic capabilities are the primary drivers of SMEs performance, external collaborative support through the Hexa Helix is highly effective in amplifying the impact of product innovation rather than uniformly strengthening all strategic relationships. Title: Evolving the DarTwin evolution language
Source title: Innovations in Systems and Software Engineering
Abstract: DarTwin is a notation for describing and planning evolution of digital twin systems. Originally conceived as a graphical notation, DarTwin has evolved into a domain-specific language formally defined in SysML v2. This evolution exposed challenges related to graphical notation support, tooling interoperability, and co-evolution between notation, language definition, and modelling environments. We experienced that SysML v2 tooling was not adequate to provide our DarTwin graphical notation even with some post-processing. The SysML v2 definition of DarTwin did, however, motivate improvements of the DarTwin DSL. To provide fruitful DarTwin graphical notation and still maintain the formal definition in SysML v2 we demonstrate how domain-specific tooling (MetaEdit+) helps improving the graphic editing and rendering support and thus achieve a more effective and intuitive use of DarTwin. By generating SysML v2 from MetaEdit+ we preserve the connection between the adequate graphical notation and the precision and formality of DarTwin. The combined DarTwin tooling made the methodology to apply general evolution transition patterns (DarTrans) more formal and precise while still intuitive through graphic notation using colour and dashes. This in turn motivated enhancing the DarTwin language by adding concepts related to the evolution transitions to facilitate discovering and documenting the transitions. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Atomic and Molecular Structure Regulated In Situ Cross-Linked Polyurethane Gel Electrolyte for High-Performance Lithium Metal Batteries
Abstract: The incompatibility of conventional electrolytes with high-voltage cathodes and lithium metal anodes limits the performance of lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Here, an in situ cross-linked polyurethane gel electrolyte (G-P3 AR) is designed through atomic and molecular structure regulation. The polyester segments widen the highest occupied molecular orbital–lowest unoccupied molecular orbital gap, extending the electrochemical stability window to 4.97 V for compatibility with NCM811 cathodes. Polyether segments exhibit a lower Li+ binding energy, reducing the desolvation barrier and enhancing anode stability. At the atomic level, sp2-hybridized boron in the chain extender immobilizes anions (TFSI− and DFOB−) through Lewis acid–base interactions, raising the Li+ transference number to 0.78 and enabling exceptional rate capability (157.7 mAh g−1 at 2 C in the Li||NCM811 cell). Hydrogen bonding between the polymer and solvent restructures the solvation sheath, promoting inorganic-rich interphases. The Li|G-P3 AR|NCM811 cell retains 81.7% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C charge/1 C discharge, demonstrating a rational electrolyte design strategy for high-performance LMBs. Title: Creative thinking ability: A hybrid systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: This study explores the development of creative thinking ability over the past few decades using a interdisciplinary approach in a global context. Various studies have investigated creative thinking ability over the past several decades, but the search is still fragmented in each field. Therefore, there is a significant gap in our understanding of how these concepts of creative thinking overlap and interact across disciplines. So that, in-depth research on this subject remains necessary. This study is a systematic literature review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis of creative thinking ability based on empirical studies that have been conducted. The methodology used in this study is a systematic literature review using term “creative thinking ability” in the article title, abstract, and keywords from the Scopus database, resulting in 4,487 publications from 1968 to 2025. The evaluation was conducted on January 5, 2026. The collected data were analyzed bibliometrically using the VOS (visualization of similarities) viewer. This study found that creative thinking intersects various disciplines, including psychology, education, and business, which holistically intersect with the cognitive dimension, the affective dimension, and the socio-cultural dimension. In psychology, an individual’s creative capacity can be optimized through cognitive stimulation aligned with their personality characteristics. In the business sector, a climate of innovation is encouraged through structured training programs adaptively designed based on employee perceptions and needs. Meanwhile, in the educational context, students’ creativity can be effectively cultivated through the implementation of transformative learning models supported by practical instructional strategies in the classroom. By integrating insights from these fields, it will be able to improve educational practices and foster a conducive environment for creativity that can lead to innovative teaching strategies. Title: The principles for Responsible Management Education and curriculum innovation in hospitality and tourism education: Children as a missing dimension
Abstract: The study provides compelling evidence of why a children dimension should be included in hospitality and tourism curriculum. The evidence are articulated around a reviewed and revisited approach of the Principle of Responsible Management Education, namely: Children: An Industry and Society Perspective (Principle 1: Value, Partnership and Dialogue); Children: Expertise and Research (Principle 2: Research and Method; and Children Tourist: A Conceptual Category (Principle 3: Purpose and Practice). Having said that, the suggested development of hospitality and tourism education curriculum is coming with challenges such as the emergence of hidden curriculum and opportunities such as augmented profile of students. Title: A probabilistic approach to reliability assessment of inventory management strategies in an MRP environment with random yield
Abstract: Although there are several strategies for planning production or replenishment in a material requirement planning (MRP) environment, they are all designed to calculate planned stock parameters. Other metrics, such as more precise probabilistic estimates of safety stocks, shortages and the reliability of the entire inventory management system, are rarely considered. Improving the accuracy of probabilistic estimates of these indicators is necessary to enhance the reliability of describing production processes under conditions of uncertainty. The article proposes calculated dependencies that allow determining the safety stock level based on analytical calculations rather than practical experience or arbitrary assumptions. A general algorithm was developed for selecting an inventory management strategy under random yield that takes safety stocks and random yield into account. This algorithm includes estimates of efficiency (order costs, on-hand stock holding costs and safety stock holding costs) and material planning reliability indicators in the form of failure-free probability during the planning period. Analysis of the results revealed that more precise probabilistic consideration of safety stocks in MRP under random yield leads to a change in the production planning or replenishment strategy. © 2025 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Authors: Gao S.; Li Y.
Title: Detection of spatial change boundaries in linear regression models
Source title: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference
Abstract: Detecting spatial change boundaries that separate regions with different regression relationships is important for the analysis of spatially heterogeneous data. We develop three residual-based procedures for detecting spatial change boundaries in linear regression models: a spatial path scanning procedure, a local block discrepancy procedure, and an integrated strip scanning procedure. The first and third procedures apply cumulative sum (CUSUM) statistics to one-dimensional sequences induced by spatial orderings, whereas the second procedure compares residual averages over neighboring local blocks. The asymptotic properties of the proposed procedures are established under a regular-lattice framework, while irregularly sampled designs are treated as computational extensions and evaluated through simulation. Simulation studies under different boundary configurations, sampling designs, and spatial dependence structures reveal complementary strengths and limitations of the proposed procedures in detecting and localizing spatial change boundaries. Comparisons with residual-based Point Wombling and the spatially clustered coefficient regression method based on a minimum spanning tree (SCC-MST) further illustrate the relative strengths and limitations of the proposed procedures. A Boston Housing application provides a real-data illustration of the spatial boundary patterns produced by the proposed methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Author full names: Galindo-Domínguez, Héctor (57209238017); Campo, Lucía (56026747800); Delgado, Nahia (60518415700); Urruzola, María-Victoria (57212091708)
Title: Brains on copy-paste mode? A mixed-methods study on the relationship between generative artificial intelligence use and students’ critical thinking skills
Abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence tools, such as ChatGPT, into higher education has raised important questions about their relationship with students' critical thinking (CT) skills. This study explored these associations among 398 undergraduate students using a mixed-methods design. Quantitatively, participants completed validated measures of critical thinking and a survey assessing frequency of AI use in academic contexts. Correlation analyses indicated a significant negative association between AI use and Analyzing/Organizing skills. Moderation analyses revealed that academic achievement moderated this relationship for Analyzing/Organizing and Evaluating, with higher achievers showing a stronger negative association. No significant effects emerged for gender and age on the remaining CT dimensions. Likewise, qualitative analyses of 200 open-ended responses identified three user profiles: (1) instrumental/uncritical, comprising younger low-achieving male students emphasizing AI speed and utility while reporting reduced verification effort; (2) stable/complementary, comprising older high-achieving students perceiving little change in their evaluative practices; and (3) ambivalent/skeptical-trusting, comprising women with medium achievement, divided between increased skepticism and greater reliance on AI outputs. Supplementary analyses linking Analyzing/Organizing and Evaluating scores to these profiles showed that lower development of both skills consistently aligned with the instrumental/uncritical profile. The interpretive consistency between both analytical strands suggests that the relationship between generative AI use and CT skills is nuanced and profile-dependent, limited in scope to specific dimensions and student groups rather than reflecting a broad negative impact, while highlighting the risks of uncritical reliance and the potential of AI as a complementary academic tool when used reflectively. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Nosakhare M.E.; Yusoff M.Y.; Halid H.
Author full names: Nosakhare, Monday Efosa (60013654700); Yusoff, Moh'd Yusmani (60913200300); Halid, Hafinas (57219115015)
Title: Rethinking institutional support for migrant businesses in Sweden: A strategic management– oriented scoping review
Abstract: Migrant entrepreneurship has become an increasingly important contributor to Sweden’s economic and social landscape; however, the institutional environment supporting migrant-owned businesses remains fragmented and difficult to navigate. This study conducts a scoping review to map existing knowledge on the opportunities, barriers, and systemic gaps affecting migrant entrepreneurs in Sweden. The review draws on peer-reviewed journal articles, policy reports, and grey literature published between 2020 and 2026, identified primarily through the Scopus database and complementary manual searches. A total of 18 studies met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using a thematic synthesis approach. The findings reveal that migrant entrepreneurs contribute significantly to job creation, innovation, and regional development, particularly in sectors such as retail, hospitality, and services. However, they face persistent barriers including limited access to finance, bureaucratic complexity, language constraints, and weak integration into institutional support networks. The analysis further shows that although Sweden possesses a wide range of support mechanisms, these are often poorly coordinated, resulting in duplication, inefficiencies, and limited accessibility for migrant entrepreneurs. Guided by the resource-based view (RBV) and contingency theory, this study develops a strategic pathways model consisting of three interrelated pillars: resource mobilization, adaptive strategy, and collaborative alignment. The model provides a conceptual framework for enhancing institutional effectiveness and improving the inclusiveness of entrepreneurial support systems. The study highlights the need for a more integrated, flexible, and strategically coordinated support ecosystem. It also identifies critical gaps in empirical research and calls for future studies to test the proposed model in real-world institutional settings. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Anchoring sustainability: A new paradigm for maritime clusters
Abstract: The environmental footprint of maritime transport, combined with growing social and regulatory pressure to tackle pollution, has brought the shipping industry to the forefront of the sustainability agenda. The role of industry clusters is becoming increasingly relevant to this discourse, given their influence across all dimensions of sustainability. Surprisingly, although this profound relationship is well documented, it has not received sufficient scholarly attention. This study analyses the highly fragmented literature on maritime clusters and sustainability using a novel combination of bibliometrics and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven thematic analysis. On this basis, a framework is developed that captures the interaction between clusters and the key components of sustainability. The findings suggest that sustainability should not be treated as an isolated strategic initiative or the outcome of regulatory pressure, but as a key dimension of cluster competitiveness. Additionally, it emerges that digital innovation acts as a cross-cutting enabler of sustainability in maritime clusters, linking the economic, social/governance, and environmental pillars of the proposed framework. Overall, this study provides actionable insights for maritime practitioners and policy makers alike. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Rotondo F.; Ison S.; Budd L.
Author full names: Rotondo, Federico (56644365800); Ison, Stephen (6701589918); Budd, Lucy (23396020100)
Title: The evolution of Italian airport ownership
Abstract: The ownership of commercial airports is increasingly essential for national competitiveness and regional economic development. Airport ownership directly influences the planning of airport infrastructure and air transport policies at both a local and national level. In Italy, historically, tight control by the state permitted the implementation of long-term development plans and ensured that the needs of local communities were addressed, but today, there are very few airports, and among the larger ones, almost none, without an equity share held by the private sector. In light of current debates surrounding the future viability of Italian airports following the COVID-19 pandemic, this paper aims to examine the evolution of Italian airport ownership compared to significant international experiences, such as the UK, in which airport privatisation followed the 1986 Airports Act. This paper critically examines the evolution of Italian airport ownership, focusing on the underlying drivers and consequences of these changes and comparing them with the UK case, by considering different ownership models, the nature of the private entities involved, the proportion of passengers flying through airports with different ownership structures, and the number of owners per airport. The analysis involves the main 33 Italian airports, controlled by 25 airport companies, and covers the period 1997-2024, which is analysed in three specific phases: 1997/2008-2009/2019, and 2020/2024. Among the primary outcomes of this research, there is a better understanding of how airport ownership has evolved in Italy compared with other international settings and whether airports can be considered public utilities or private assets to provide valuable recommendations for airport management and policymakers regarding the industry's future viability. Authors: Liu H.; Yan Q.; Sun F.; Fan L.; Wang Y.; Xu X.; Zhang S.; Cao G.
Title: Compact broadband low-frequency sound absorption using coupled folded side-slit Helmholtz resonators with dual-peak multimodal resonances
Abstract: In order to achieve efficient broadband low-frequency sound absorption within strict volume constraints, a compact absorber based on a two-cavity folded side-slit Helmholtz resonator (FSHR-2C) is proposed. The dual-cavity architecture, integrated with two independently tunable perforations, enables staggered resonances that anchor the low-frequency absorption edge and provides an additional tunable high-frequency response associated with the folded side-slit branch. Additionally, Helmholtz resonators with side slits (HRSS) are introduced as valley-filling elements to improve the continuity of the absorption spectrum through coupling with the FSHR-2C. A transfer matrix model incorporating thermoviscous losses in both slits and perforations is established, and its accuracy is validated by finite-element simulations. Furthermore, a coupled optimization framework based on sequential quadratic programming (SQP) is developed. By exploiting the high tunability of the unit cells and incorporating geometric feasibility constraints through piecewise penalty functions, the optimized theoretical absorber achieves an absorption coefficient above 0.8 in the frequency range from 250 Hz to 600 Hz and also exhibits a secondary high-frequency absorption region around 830 Hz to 970 Hz. Impedance-tube measurements further confirm the main two-region absorption behavior, showing good agreement with the theoretical prediction in the main absorption bands. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A reciprocal perspective on internationalization and ESG in EMNEs: The role of digitalization
Abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) has become a critical measure of multinational enterprises’ global competitiveness, yet emerging market multinational enterprises (EMNEs) face distinct legitimacy challenges due to weak home-country ESG regulations, known as the liability of home origin. Although prior studies have examined the relationship between internationalization and ESG, they have largely treated the two directions separately, leaving unclear whether they operate as competing explanations or as mutually reinforcing processes. Drawing on legitimacy theory, this study conceptualizes internationalization and ESG performance as exhibiting mutually reinforcing associations over time. Using longitudinal data from 2460 Chinese listed firms between 2009 and 2020, we examine the reciprocal relationship between internationalization and ESG performance, and the moderating role of digitalization. Findings indicate that internationalization is consistently associated with stronger ESG performance, suggesting EMNEs use ESG to mitigate liabilities of origin and build legitimacy abroad. The reverse association is weaker but most robust for foreign-country scope, indicating that ESG performance may support international expansion by signaling alignment with international sustainability expectations. The moderating associations of digitalization are uneven and are concentrated in visible foreign organizational and geographic presence, such as overseas subsidiaries and foreign-country scope, rather than overseas revenues. © 2026 The Authors.
