Authors: Setyowati M.S.; Hanum R.K.
Title: The effect of agricultural taxes and local agricultural policies on enhancing food security and environmental sustainability
Source title: Global Journal of Environmental Science and Management
Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Indonesia is currently working towards sustainability in line with Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger). Anticipated demographic growth to 10.8 billion by the year 2050 is expected to place unprecedented strain on global food security and production systems. The study objectives were to examine the biophysical factors, production inputs, economic conditions, socio-technological factors, agricultural business management, and agricultural tax policies regional agricultural policies and, ultimately, agricultural productivity. METHODS: This quantitative study employed structured questionnaires administered to a sample of 200 farmers in Surabaya. The instrument used a one-to-five Likert scale covering biophysical factors, economic factors, tax policy, tax morale, and agricultural productivity. Data was analyzed using partial least squares-structural equation modeling version 3. The analytical procedure comprised three distinct phases: first, evaluating the outer model for convergent and discriminant validity; second, conducting reliability assessments; and third, testing the inner model via bootstrapping to determine the coefficient of determination, the effect size, and hypothesis significance. Hypothesis significance was determined using t-statistic values of at least 1.96 and p-values of no more than 0.05. FINDINGS: Four hypotheses were rejected: economic factor on regional agricultural policy (p-value 0.557), agricultural taxation policy on tax morale (p-value 0.072), tax awareness on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.058), and tax morale on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.208). The findings reveal that regional agricultural policies are substantially driven by three key dimensions: biophysical factors (beta coefficient of 0.251, probability value of 0.000), production inputs (beta coefficient of 0.253, probability value of 0.002), and agricultural business management (beta coefficient of 0.228, probability value of 0.007). Agricultural tax policy significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.229, probability value of 0.000), while tax administration efficiency also significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.345, probability value of 0.000) and tax morale (beta coefficient of -0.634, probability value of 0.000), since clarity on procedures, benefits, and regulations fosters public responsibility and awareness of taxpayer obligations and rights. CONCLUSION: Elevating agricultural output demands comprehensive frameworks characterized by active farmer participation, supportive regulatory policies, targeted outreach regarding tax frameworks, and enhanced coordination between industry stakeholders and governmental bodies. Regional agricultural policies and tax awareness significantly influence agricultural productivity. These findings offer practical insights for policymakers aiming to strengthen agricultural governance and tax compliance frameworks in support of sustainable rural development. Title: Moral responsibilisation in destination management: The strategic framing of civic practices by DMOs
Abstract: This paper examines moral responsibilisation as an emerging destination governance mechanism through which destination management organisations (DMOs) and local stakeholders mobilise visitors to support sustainability goals. Drawing on an intrinsic qualitative case study of the Danish DMO, Wonderful Copenhagen , we develop a practice theory-based model showing that responsibilisation extends beyond narrative persuasion to include the organisational and material reframing of civic conduct. Analysis of interviews, participant observation, documents, and netnography identifies four interrelated stages: interpellation, involvement, intervention, and institutionalisation. Together, these stages connect inspirational messaging with participatory experiences, reward schemes, and decentralised service design. The findings also reveal tensions around the relevance, inclusivity, and feasibility of emerging civic practices. Resistance to responsible subject positions stems from stakeholders’ differing interpretations, negotiations, and disengagement from DMO-prescribed roles. The study advances the understanding of responsibilisation as a practice-based mode of governance and offers insights that may inform destination managers in varied tourism contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Zhang X.; Tinacci L.; Giusti A.; Kang H.; Deng W.; Li Y.; Sun Z.; Peng H.; Zou L.; Armani A.; Wen J.
Title: DNA authentication of shark meat products from a major Chinese e-commerce platform reveals trade-name opacity and traceability limitations
Abstract: Shark meat products are subject to a variety of regulatory and conservation frameworks, yet their characterization at the retail level is often constrained by the use of umbrella terms and limited species-specific information. In this context, the present study was designed as an exploratory case study examining shark meat products commercialized through a major Chinese e-commerce platform within a defined sampling period. Product descriptions, labeling information (including trade name, processing type, product presentation, declared production origin, and price), and molecular species identification obtained through DNA barcoding were jointly examined to characterize shark-derived products marketed through the platform. A total of 63 products were screened, and 165 tissue samples were analysed using COI and cytb markers. All products were marketed under generic umbrella terms, without scientific nomenclature, and prepackaged products showed variable labeling completeness. Molecular analyses detected at least one shark taxon in 61 of the 63 products examined, whereas the remaining two products contained billfish and batoid taxa. At the tissue level, 160 of 165 samples (97%) were assigned to shark taxa. Across all analysed samples, molecular identification revealed 12 species-level taxa, comprising 10 shark species (Alopias pelagicus, A. superciliosus, Carcharhinus brevipinna, C. limbatus, C. sorrah, Galeocerdo cuvier, Isurus oxyrinchus, Mustelus griseus, Prionace glauca, and Sphyrna lewini), one batoid species (Rhynchobatus australiae), and one billfish species (Istiophorus platypterus), together with three genus-level assignments including shark and billfish taxa (Scoliodon sp., Carcharhinus sp., and Kajikia sp.). The identified taxa include species listed as Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, and Critically Endangered according to the IUCN Red List. The two products containing non-shark taxa represented cases of non-conformity between molecular identity and the available product information and therefore warrant discussion in relation to labeling practices. Overall, the findings illustrate the utility of molecular approaches for documenting species composition in online retail settings and provide an exploratory baseline for future investigations into species-level transparency, product information practices, and shark product commercialization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Touchable cultural heritage: How alternative touch experience facilitates visitors’ cultural inheritance behavior
Abstract: Touch is a fundamental human need, yet in cultural heritage tourism, it is strictly restricted to protect fragile artifacts. While essential for preservation, touch restrictions limit multi-sensory experience and impede deeper cultural participation. This research addresses this touch dilemma by introducing alternative touch experiences, wherein tourists touch surrogate objects (e.g., artifact replicas) that simulate the haptic attributes of authentic artifacts. Across four studies with qualitative, experimental, and field evidence, we found that alternative touch experiences enhance tourists’ psychological closeness to heritage, which in turn fosters cultural inheritance intentions and actual behaviors (e.g., cultural learning, cultural knowledge sharing, and donation to protect heritage). However, this touch effect diminishes when artifacts carry negative (vs. positive) superstitious associations. These findings offer a new theoretical perspective on enabling embodied experience within the traditionally sensory-restricted context, and highlight the role of sensory engagement in facilitating heritage appreciation and cultural inheritance. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Sustainable urban planning in conflict-affected cities: Governance, displacement, and hierarchical sustainability in Marib, Yemen
Abstract: Sustainable urban planning frameworks presuppose institutional stability and regulated development, yet their applicability to conflict-affected cities remains theoretically underexamined. This qualitative case study examines how sustainability is interpreted and prioritised in Marib city, Yemen, an urban centre experiencing rapid growth amid armed conflict and mass internal displacement. Drawing on a framing analysis of global sustainability frameworks, semi-structured interviews with 16 city stakeholders, and structured observations in seven neighbourhoods, the study identifies a structural mismatch between global sustainability paradigms and local planning practice. Whereas international models assume balanced domain integration, the evidence from Marib reveals a context-conditioned hierarchy in which governance capacity and essential service provision operate as preconditions structuring environmental management, economic activity, and technological uptake. Locally, environmental sustainability is reduced to basic service continuity; social sustainability is dominated by displacement-driven absorptive pressures; economic sustainability narrows to livelihood survival; and technological adoption is fragmented and institutionally constrained. The paper advances a context-conditioned, hierarchical model of urban sustainability that challenges the implicit universality of parallel-domain planning approaches and calls for planning paradigms that recognise institutional capacity as foundational in fragile urban contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Group zero-norm regularized robust loss minimization: Proximal MM method and statistical error bound
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper concerns the group zero-norm regularized robust loss minimization problems. We propose a proximal majorization-minimization (PMM) algorithm to tackle a class of equivalent difference-of-convex (DC) surrogate optimization problems. Under the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz (KL) property, we establish the global convergence of the proposed algorithm and characterize its local (sub)linear convergence rate. Furthermore, for linear observation models with design matrices satisfying restricted eigenvalue conditions, we derive statistical estimation error bounds between the PMM-generated iterates (including their limit points) and the ground truth solution. To efficiently implement the PMM framework, we develop a proximal dual semismooth Newton method for solving the subproblems. Numerical experiments on both synthetic data and the UCI benchmark demonstrate the efficiency of our PMM method. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: The hub location and pricing problem under a tree topology: a bilevel formulation and a co-evolutionary algorithm
Abstract: This paper introduces the bilevel tree-of-hubs location and pricing problem, a multiple-allocation hub location problem in which both the design and pricing of a tree-shaped hub backbone network are determined. Two types of decision-makers are considered: a leader, who defines the network structure and sets usage prices, and a follower, who selects the optimal way to use the network for shipping commodities. The leader aims to maximize profit, while the follower seeks to minimize transportation costs. A bilevel optimization formulation is proposed and reformulated into a single-level equivalent model. To solve it efficiently, we develop a Co-Evolutionary Algorithm (Co-EA) and test it on three well-known datasets adapted to our problem. The novelty of the proposed Co-EA lies in the interaction between its co-evolving populations: rather than representing leader and follower solutions separately, each population is associated with a subset of the leader's decision variables. For each leader decision, the follower's optimal response is computed, ensuring bilevel feasibility. Extensive computational experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed Co-EA compared with general-purpose solvers applied to the reformulated model. The best Co-EA solutions are also used as warm-starts for the exact solver, confirming the quality of the heuristic results. Finally, managerial insights are derived regarding how the number of hubs affects the backbone network configuration. The paper concludes with directions for future research on bilevel hub location and pricing models. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Authors: Wang H.; Shan Q.; Zhang J.; Xiao P.; Liu A.
Title: An audio-visual fusion emotion generation model based on neuroanatomical alignment
Abstract: In the field of affective computing, traditional methods for generating emotions predominantly rely on deep learning techniques and large-scale emotion datasets. However, deep learning techniques are often complex and difficult to interpret, and standardizing large-scale emotional datasets are difficult and costly to establish. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a novel framework named Audio-Visual Fusion for Brain-like Emotion Learning(AVF-BEL). In contrast to conventional brain-inspired emotion learning methods, this approach improves the audio-visual emotion fusion and generation model through the integration of modular components, thereby enabling more lightweight and interpretable emotion learning and generation processes. The framework simulates the integration of the visual, auditory, and emotional pathways of the brain, optimizes the fusion of emotional features across visual and auditory modalities, and improves upon the traditional Brain Emotional Learning (BEL) model. The experimental results indicate a significant improvement in the similarity of the audio-visual fusion emotion learning generation model compared to single-modality visual and auditory emotion learning and generation model. Ultimately, this aligns with the fundamental phenomenon of heightened emotion generation facilitated by the integrated impact of visual and auditory stimuli. This contribution not only enhances the interpretability and efficiency of affective intelligence but also provides new insights and pathways for advancing affective computing technology. Title: Park-and-multi-loop with autonomous delivery robots in last-mile logistics
Abstract: This paper deals with the park-and-multi-loop routing problem, in the context of last-mile logistics, in which a fleet of traditional vehicles equipped with several autonomous delivery robots leaves from a depot to service a set of customer requests. Each delivery route involves a main tour of a traditional vehicle (subject to time-dependent travel times), which may stop at one or more parking locations, from which one or more walking sub-tours are carried out by the driver and the delivery robots on the pedestrian network. The goal is to minimize the overall cost of both van and walking routes. An alternative objective aims to minimize the (Formula presented.) emissions. A peculiarity of the problem is that the walking distance covered by drivers and delivery robots must not exceed given thresholds. For this problem, we propose a tailored destroy-and-repair mechanism embedded into a neighborhood search algorithm. The destroy-and-repair operators are parameterized, and the most appropriate parameter setting is chosen based on some performance measures of the solution. Computational results on a set of instances of varying size, derived from real data of two major Italian cities, certify the quality of the approach, compared to classic destroy-and-repair operators. Moreover, we also show the benefits of the proposed delivery scheme in terms of (Formula presented.) emissions when compared to a traditional delivery paradigm. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Li X.; Zhou Y.; Sun W.; Lei X.
Title: Uncertainty-aware nodal carbon intensity based on sliced Latin hypercube sampling
Abstract: The variability of climate conditions leads to significant renewable uncertainty. With the large-scale integration of renewable energy, it becomes necessary to consider uncertainties in the nodal carbon intensity (NCI) of power systems. However, the renewable uncertainty though the power flow propagates to the carbon emission flow, making an unclear relationship between the renewable uncertainty and the carbon emission flow. In this paper, an uncertainty-aware nodal Carbon intensity method is proposed to handle this issue. An explicit matrix-form relationship linking renewable forecast errors, AGC-based generation dispatch, branch power flow variations, and NCI is established. In addition, a Jacobian-based local sensitivity expression is derived to characterize the local response of NCI to renewable forecast errors. Then, sliced Latin hypercube sampling (SLHS) is employed to estimate the statistical characteristics and probability distribution of NCI. Case studies performed on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 300-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method is capable of accurately accounting for the uncertainty in the nodal carbon intensity. © 2026

Title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic

Abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. A software solution — a Python module for fuzzy inference and visualization has also been implemented, expanding the capabilities of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate that the developed system correctly ranks transport enterprises by risk level. Verification on five theoretical cases (TK1-TK5) confirmed the model's ability to generate an Integrated Safety Assessment (ISA) from 0 to 1, effectively distinguishing between exemplary compliance and systematic critical violations. Authors: Pan A.
Title: The AI-augmented collaborative learning model: A conceptual framework for integrating generative AI in business and management education
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) amplifies four tensions in business and management education: the threat to pedagogical coherence, the literacy-to-competency gap, pervasive ethical risks, and the assessment crisis. A first wave of practice-oriented frameworks – including the Human-Centric AI-First (HCAIF) framework and the Leeds Model – offers actionable roadmaps but lacks the theoretical architecture needed to explain the systemic classroom dynamics GenAI introduces. This conceptual paper addresses that gap by developing the AI-Augmented Collaborative Learning (ACL) Model, a second-wave framework organised around three research questions: (RQ1) which theoretical lenses explain the classroom dynamics that generative AI creates in business and management education; (RQ2) how can these be synthesised into an integrated pedagogical framework whose pillars address the four systemic challenges; and (RQ3) how can human-AI collaboration be operationalised as an assessable pedagogical meta-skill. Using Socio-Technical Systems Theory, Activity Theory, Actor-Network Theory, Constructivist and Experiential Learning Theories, and the AI-TPACK framework, the ACL Model specifies four interlocking pillars – Pedagogical Intentionality, Developmental Scaffolding, Ethical Guardrails, and Authentic Assessment. Title: Familiar faces, honest answers? The impacts of enumerator familiarity and modality on survey responses
Abstract: Survey data can be distorted through mistrust, discomfort, or demand effects on the part of respondents. We test whether familiar enumerators – those with whom a respondent has completed a prior survey – influence data quality in a panel survey with small business owners in Uganda. We randomly assign respondents to a familiar or a new enumerator and cross-cut a second randomization to an in-person or phone-based interview modality. Across a broad set of outcome types, we observe few impacts of either survey method on means, distributions, or attrition. However, respondents are significantly more likely to give norm-congruent answers to new surveyors compared to familiar ones. The effect of familiarity does not interact significantly with a prior experiment conducted with the same sample, suggesting that familiarity influences estimates of levels but not of treatment impacts. These findings suggest that surveys by familiar enumerators can improve the measurement of sensitive beliefs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Polyhydroxy Molecular Regulator Enabled Interfacial Microenvironment Programming for Alkaline Zinc–Iron Flow Batteries
Abstract: Alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries (ZIFBs) are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost, intrinsic safety, and scalable architecture, yet their practical deployment remains hindered by hydrogen evolution and uncontrolled Zn deposition in three-dimensional porous electrodes. Here, we report that isomalt acts as a polyhydroxy molecular regulator that reconfigures the interfacial microenvironment of porous carbon felt, thereby endowing the porous electrode with a more deposition-directing function for reversible Zn plating/stripping. In the bulk electrolyte, isomalt reconstructs the local hydrogen-bond network, lowers water activity, and suppresses hydrogen evolution. At the carbon/electrolyte interface, its preferential lateral adsorption establishes a hydroxyl-rich interphase that homogenizes zincate transport and directs Zn growth toward a preferred (002) orientation, thus promoting compact and reversible deposition. This interfacial microenvironment programming markedly reduces the charge-transfer resistance and activation barrier of the Zn anode, enabling stable cycling for over 500 cycles at 20 mA cm−2. In full-cell tests, the optimized ZIFB delivers a high energy efficiency of 87.5%, substantially outperforming the pristine electrolyte. Beyond identifying a low-cost green additive, this work establishes polyhydroxy molecules as interfacial programming units for three-dimensional porous electrodes, offering a new design concept for directional metal deposition in aqueous flow-battery systems. Title: Techno-economic optimisation and operational assessment of hydrogen-integrated renewable microgrids for remote communities
Abstract: Hydrogen-integrated renewable microgrids represent a promising pathway for sustainable decarbonisation of remote communities; however, conventional techno-economic optimisation often overlooks the operational behaviour of hydrogen subsystems, leading to optimistic performance estimates and less practically deployable designs. This study proposes an integrated framework combining Hybrid Optimisation of Multiple Energy Resources (HOMER) Pro-based techno-economic optimisation with Python-based post-optimisation operational assessment. The framework evaluates operational indicators, including minimum-load compliance, start-stop cycling, large-ramp events, and hydrogen storage utilisation, using hourly dispatch data and literature-informed criteria. A scenario-based design-space exploration is conducted for a remote off-grid community in Australia, followed by operational feasibility screening and Pareto-based multi-objective analysis balancing economic performance, renewable energy utilisation, and electrolyser operation. The optimised reference configuration achieves zero operational CO2 emissions with a levelised cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.258 AUD/kWh and a levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH) of 6.77 AUD/kg. Post-optimisation assessment reveals that 5,912 h of reported electrolyser operation reduces to 4,775 h of acceptable operation; the excluded 1,137 h (19.2%) correspond to low-load periods, indicating an overestimation of effective electrolyser utilisation of up to 23.8%. Threshold sensitivity analysis identifies hydrogen tank near-full hours as the most sensitive indicator, while core screening outcomes remain stable under low-load and ramp-event threshold variations. Operational feasibility screening reduces the 22 candidate designs to 15 feasible configurations, demonstrating that techno-economic attractiveness does not necessarily ensure operational viability. Title: The dialectic of the carrot and the stick in the expansion of the extractive frontier in Oaxaca, Mexico
Abstract: The expansion of large-scale mining in Mexico since the 1990s has been accompanied by intensifying socio-environmental conflicts, particularly in rural and Indigenous territories. While existing literature has shown that extractive governance frequently combines coercive practices with strategies aimed at securing local legitimacy, this article argues that these mechanisms are mutually constitutive rather than simply simultaneous or complementary. It develops the concept of the dialectic of the carrot and the stick to explain how corporate social responsibility (CSR) and coercion recursively reshape the conditions under which one another operate over the life of an extractive project. The article examines the San José silver and gold mine in Oaxaca, Mexico, operated by Fortuna Silver Mines (FSM). Drawing on qualitative fieldwork conducted between 2023 and 2024, including interviews, field observations, corporate publications, media reports, and civil society sources, it traces extractive governance over more than a decade of conflict. It shows that community programmes and relationships with local institutions produced differentiated and conditional forms of legitimacy, while repression, intimidation, and violence increased the costs of dissent and weakened resistance networks. Coercion thus transformed the terrain on which legitimacy was subsequently cultivated, while persistent limits to legitimacy generated renewed pressures to contain opposition. The dialectic therefore describes a recursive process through which coercion and consent reshape one another, enabling extraction to persist despite sustained opposition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Navigating CSRD compliance: Challenges in sustainability reporting for the real estate sector
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the challenges faced by the Norwegian real estate sector in complying with the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), addressing a critical gap in understanding how these regulations impact sustainability reporting practices. The research seeks new insights into the barriers to implementing CSRD-compliant reporting, contributing to a deeper understanding of the sector's readiness and areas requiring improvement. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, utilizing a scoping literature review to map existing knowledge and semi-structured interviews with industry stakeholders to supplement findings. Data were collected from peer-reviewed articles, master's theses, and interviews with key stakeholders, and analyzed using thematic coding and qualitative analysis. The results reveal that the main challenges include limited knowledge of sustainability matters, difficulties in conducting Double Materiality Assessments (DMA), high costs, poor data systems, and administrative burdens. These findings provide evidence that while some companies proactively prepare for CSRD compliance, many, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), struggle due to resource constraints and a reliance on manual processes. This highlights significant implications for improving digital solutions and stakeholder collaboration. This research offers a novel perspective on sustainability reporting in the Norwegian real estate sector, providing valuable insights into the sector's preparedness and key barriers. The study's findings contribute to advancing digital reporting practices and support for SMEs, highlighting areas for future research and potential policy development to ease the transition to CSRD compliance. Title: Capacity Degradation Mechanisms, Recovery Strategies, and Challenges of Flow Batteries
Abstract: Redox flow batteries, by virtue of their advantages in power/capacity decoupling, high safety, and long cycle life, have become a strategic support for long-duration energy storage systems; however, capacity degradation remains a bottleneck for their commercialization. This review systematically identifies the multi-dimensional mechanisms of capacity degradation: including volume imbalance caused by transmembrane migration, inactivation and decomposition of active species, electrode degradation, and valence imbalance induced by side reactions. Targeting these challenges, the review deeply explores recovery strategies from physical repair to intelligent scheduling: covering the research and development of high-selectivity membranes, precise regulation of valence states, functionalized repair of electrodes, and model-driven predictive pathways integrating digital twins. Finally, current challenges such as characterization limitations and incomplete recovery rates are summarized, and future development directions for capacity recovery are envisioned. This review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical guidance for extending the system cycle life of flow batteries and improving capacity recovery efficiency. Title: Beyond compliance: Community development committees and the transformation of resource governance in Tanzania
Abstract: Resource-rich countries worldwide often face persistent imbalances in the redistribution of resource wealth. Although mineral extraction generates substantial revenues, these funds are typically centrally managed and redistributed, leaving host communities, who bear the social and environmental burdens of extraction, impoverished and marginalized. In Tanzania, despite provisions allowing Local Government Authorities to levy a 0.3% service charge on mining revenues and receive Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) contributions intended to support local development, means of engaging host communities remain a challenge. Community Development Agreements (CDAs) have been identified as potential instruments to safeguard the interests of host communities. However, despite their widespread promotion, a critical gap remains in understanding how communities can effectively engage in, negotiate, and implement CDAs, particularly in contexts marked by power asymmetries. Communities are often poor, with limited knowledge of mining and the broader extractive industry, and with no access to decision-making power. This study addresses the gap by examining Community Development Committees (CDCs) as an inclusive, participatory institutional mechanism through which communities can effectively articulate their development priorities. Using semi‑structured interviews with 36 key informants across the mining value chain, including central government officials, mining representatives, and local communities, the study finds the CDC model as an effective approach for strengthening community voice, enhancing transparency, improving negotiations, and monitoring project implementations. Title: An applicable mechanism for regulating anti-etching performance through interface doping in periodic Y2O3-BaZrO3 films
Abstract: Plasma etching is widely used in the processing of semiconductor memory and the manufacturing of field-effect transistors, with precise transfer of nanometer level precision, high aspect ratio structures, and complex three-dimensional structures. Subsequent vacuum annealing of the films at 900℃ was performed to improve their atomic diffusion, crystallization, and density. 12-layer Y2O3-BaZrO3 film proved to be the hardest and most etch-resistant with the lowest relative etching rate (0.67 nm/min) under chemical plasma conditions (CF4/O2), compared with Y2O3 film (1.42 nm/min) and Y2O3-MgO composite film (0.91 nm/min). As chemical etching involves the formation of protective fluoride passivation layers such as Y-F, Ba-F and Zr-F, the surface stability is enhanced by the increased bonding energy of metal fluorides, indicating higher thermodynamic stability of the composite after adsorption of fluorine. Authors: Wen Y.; Tao X.
Title: Cost sharing in joint resource purchasing: balancing efficiency improvements and cost savings
Abstract: Joint resource purchasing by a subset of decision-making units (DMUs) may offer cost savings, such as bulk discounts, group buying deals, and lower shipping costs; however, determining an appropriate allocation of the resulting discounted total procurement cost becomes a key challenge. Existing studies largely focus on fixed cost allocation, where all DMUs participate in and allocated cost is treated as a new or complementary input of DMUs. However, these approaches fail to address a scenario where only a subset of DMUs jointly procures resources, and the cost to be allocated is the discounted total procurement cost that remains attributable to the input consumption of the participating DMUs. To address this limitation, we develop a novel data envelopment analysis (DEA)-based approach for the issue of cost sharing in joint resource purchasing. First, a traditional DEA model is used to evaluate DMUs’ efficiencies by treating the original procurement cost as an input. We then formulate a multi-objective programming model based on DEA to allocate the discounted total procurement cost among the participating DMUs to optimize their efficiencies. The proposed model ensures group, individual, and coalitional rationality, and incorporates a decision rule to select a unique allocation that balances efficiency improvements with cost savings. Title: Path-reliability analysis for perishable goods delivery in urban multigraph networks: Integrating non-instantaneous deterioration and failed-delivery risks
Abstract: With the rapid development of the instant retail business model, consumers have placed increasingly stringent demands on delivery speed and service quality in perishable goods distribution. In instant retail contexts, hot-chain delivery involves managing perishable goods characterized by non-instantaneous deterioration, where quality degradation progresses over delivery time in urban multigraph networks, thereby posing distinctive operational challenges. To address these issues, this paper defines path-reliability, denoting the reliability of a specific path between two customer nodes, to summarize path operating conditions, including congestion, reachability, and connectivity, and establishes a functional relationship between path-reliability and delivery delay time. On this basis, a perishable goods delivery (PGD) network model is developed under customer availability profiles, and a hybrid tabu search algorithm equipped with neighbourhood operators tailored to multigraph structures is proposed for its solution. The model is then validated on randomly generated benchmark instances as well as real-world operational data from a prefabricated-food distribution enterprise in Xi'an. The results indicate that in regions with dispersed customer distribution, multi-path planning combined with reliability assessment yields significant cost savings and risk reduction, whereas in highly clustered regions single-path planning is sufficient to achieve efficient resource allocation while simplifying computation and implementation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Adaptive auxiliary task generation and reinforcement learning-enhanced multi-task multi-population evolutionary offloading in IIoT
Abstract: Workflow-based computation offloading has become a fundamental technique for improving execution efficiency in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems. However, heterogeneous workflow structures, complex task dependencies, and dynamic resource conditions make multi-workflow offloading a challenging multi-objective optimization problem. Existing evolutionary offloading methods generally optimize workflows independently and lack effective knowledge sharing mechanisms, resulting in limited search efficiency and potential negative transfer across heterogeneous tasks. To address these issues, this paper formulates multi-workflow computation offloading as a multitask multi-objective optimization problem and proposes an adaptive auxiliary task generation and reinforcement learning-enhanced multi-population MOEA/D (ATRL-MT-MOEAD). The proposed framework assigns each workflow to an independent subpopulation for collaborative evolution, introduces adaptive auxiliary tasks to accelerate convergence, and employs a reinforcement learning-based knowledge transfer mechanism to dynamically regulate inter-task information sharing while suppressing negative transfer. Experimental results on representative IIoT workflow benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently achieves the best optimization performance. Compared with the strongest baseline for each metric, the proposed method reduces the average IGD by 72.0%, GD by 80.4%, ACT by 16.8%, and AEC by 14.5%, while consistently achieving superior Pareto-front quality. These results verify that the proposed framework provides superior convergence, solution diversity, and optimization effectiveness for complex multi-workflow computation offloading in dynamic IIoT environments. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: SHG wave propagation in functionally graded piezomagnetic sandwich plates with imperfect interfaces: Analytical modeling and machine learning prediction
Abstract: Shear horizontal guided (SHG) waves in functionally graded piezomagnetic structures are highly sensitive to material gradation, interfacial imperfections, and magnetic boundary conditions, making them attractive for smart sensing and structural monitoring applications. This study develops an integrated analytical and physics-informed learning framework for SHG-wave propagation in a composite sandwich structure comprising two dissimilar functionally graded piezomagnetic layers coupled through a spring-membrane imperfect interface and subjected to surface mass loading. Analytical dispersion relations are derived for two distinct velocity regimes under magnetically open-circuit (MOC) and magnetically short-circuit (MSC) conditions. The effects of magneto-mechanical coupling, material gradation, interface characteristics, membrane inertial density, and normalized density on the dispersion response are systematically examined. The results reveal pronounced dispersive behavior and demonstrate that magneto-mechanical coupling, functional gradation, interface stiffness, membrane inertia, and magnetic boundary conditions provide effective mechanisms for controlling SHG-wave propagation. The analytical formulation is further integrated with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and a physics-informed Deep Operator Network (PI-DeepONet) for rapid prediction of the dispersion response. PI-DeepONet achieves R2=0.99970, compared with 0.99811 for ANN, and reduces RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by approximately 69.6%, 73.1%, and 73.5%, respectively. The physics residual also falls below 10−3 over a substantial portion of the investigated wave-number range, while tests on unseen physical configurations demonstrate improved generalization. The proposed analytical–physics-informed framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient approach for SHG-wave analysis and offers potential for smart piezomagnetic sensors, acoustic-wave devices, and guided-wave-based structural monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS

Title: Hotspot to Homogeneous: Amorphous Interfacial Current Redistribution Enables Stable Solid-State Lithium-Metal Batteries
Abstract: Interfacial instability in oxide ceramic electrolyte (OCE)-based solid-state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs) is conventionally attributed to chemical incompatibility or mechanical failure, yet the underlying atomic-scale mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we reveal that grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline OCEs function as bipolar interfacial hotspots, accelerating three degradation pathways: lowering barriers for Li dendrite nucleation and enabling electron-leakage-driven reduction at anode side, while generating localized overpotentials for cathode phase transformation. The generality of this strategy is further validated on garnet-type and perovskite-type OCEs. Title: The punctuality stability of the Nash equilibrium: the advantage of a late player in potential and aggregative games
Abstract: In a Nash equilibrium, no player can gain by unilaterally deviating. We ask whether one can select a Nash equilibrium in which no player has an incentive to delay intentionally. To address this, we introduce punctually stable Nash-equilibrium, that is, a Nash equilibrium with the additional property that intentional tardiness is not advantageous. Title: Assessing the environmental–economic viability of expressway photovoltaics in China: A spatio–temporal life cycle perspective
Abstract: Expressway corridors are increasingly considered for distributed photovoltaic deployment, but their environmental–economic viability depends strongly on local solar resources, infrastructure availability, grid structure, and future decarbonization pathways. Inverter and monocrystalline silicon photovoltaic module production are the main contributors to environmental costs. Under the carbon-neutrality-by-2060 scenario, grid decarbonization reduces the avoided environmental burden of photovoltaic electricity and delays the transition to positive net environmental benefits from 2035 to 2037. Title: Information sharing in a dual channel with an agency-selling platform
Abstract: The dual-channel sales based on an agency-selling platform and a physical retailer have been one of the most common supply chain structures for a variety of consumer products. This paper studies the information sharing decisions of an agency-selling platform and a physical retailer in a dual-channel supply chain where a supplier sells a product through these two channels. We find that the commission rate and channel competition intensity play an important role in determining the equilibrium sharing decisions. In particular, a large commission rate prevents the platform from sharing information with the supplier because the platform is worried that the shared information will be used by the supplier to optimize retail sales and thus cause the demand transfer from the platform to the retailer. By contrast, a large competition intensity forces the retailer to share information to seek a strong responsiveness of the retail price to updated demand. Interestingly, both the platform and the retailer may encounter a prisoner's dilemma and the undesirable “lose-lose” outcome could potentially be mitigated if the platform reduces its information accuracy. Moreover, the supplier's decision to buy information will make all three players more profitable when it cannot obtain information for free. This research highlights how equilibrium information sharing decisions are affected by the interaction between the platform's agency-selling mode and the wholesale price contract used in the retail channel. The findings also provide useful insights for managers to make their information sharing decisions. © 2025 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

Authors: Cao Y.; Lin X.; Wu B.; Li Y.; Zhu W.; Liu B.; Zheng A.; Wu L.; Wang Y.; Liu X.; Wu M.
Title: Biomimetic PD-1-Functionalized Immunostimulatory Nanomedicine Enables STING Activation and Durable Antitumor Immunity in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) responds poorly to immune checkpoint blockade, largely because of an immunologically cold tumor microenvironment (TME) characterized by deficient antigen presentation and impaired cytotoxic T cell responses. Analysis of numerous HCC clinical cohorts, including our institutional datasets, reveals that stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway activity is positively correlated with patient survival, enhanced antigen presentation capacity, and an immune-activated TME. However, achieving effective and controllable STING activation in immune-cold HCC tumors remains challenging. Here, we develop a biomimetic nanomedicine that integrates photothermal therapy (PTT), STING pathway activation, and immune checkpoint blockade to treat refractory HCC. A coordination nanomedicine MCI-NP is engineered by co-encapsulating the STING agonist MSA-2 and indocyanine green (ICG) via Cu2+-mediated chelation, enabling stabilized PTT-induced immunogenic cell death together with robust STING-driven innate immune activation. Further cloaked with PD-1-overexpressing cell membranes, MCI-NP@mPD-1 achieves an approximately fivefold increase in tumor accumulation compared with uncoated MCI-NP and enables localized PD-1/PD-L1 axis blockade. Following a single treatment, MCI-NP@mPD-1-based photothermal immunotherapy effectively suppresses primary tumor growth and significantly prolongs survival by remodeling the TME toward an immune-active state, while inducing durable systemic immune memory that effectively limited postoperative lung metastasis. Without introducing additional nanocarriers or excipients, MCI-NP@mPD-1 offers a promising therapeutic paradigm for photothermal immunotherapy of immune-cold HCC. Title: Business simulation games and ethical decision making confidence and intentions: The role of self-efficacy, reflective practice, and teamwork
Abstract: This study examines the potential associations between experiential learning via participating in a business simulation game and business students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. While simulation games have been widely recognized for their effectiveness in developing business competencies, their associations with ethical decision making confidence and intentions in a non-ethics related environment remain underexplored. Drawing on Kolb's experiential learning theory, we carried out a quantitative survey with the use of a structured questionnaire. We collected data from 251 undergraduate students in a UK university and analyzed them using structural equation modeling. Our findings suggest that participation in simulation games is associated with higher levels of students' teamwork and reflective practice capabilities that, in turn, were found to be positively associated with their ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Moreover, students who participated in simulation games reported higher self-efficacy which, however, was not found to have a significant relationship with ethical decision-making confidence and intentions. Our findings highlight the potential value of integrating experiential learning tools, such as simulation games, into business education suggesting an association with improvements in students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Title: Healthcare Resources, In-Hospital Management Measures, and Outcomes for Acute Ischemic Stroke in China: A Cross-Sectional Study
Abstract: Objectives To assess how province-level healthcare resource configuration relates to in-hospital management and outcomes for acute ischemic stroke in China. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of 1 055 971 adults with acute ischemic stroke treated at 1456 secondary and tertiary hospitals in the Chinese Stroke Center Alliance, 2015 to 2019. Hospital-level management and outcome measures were linked to province-level resource indicators from the China Health Statistics Yearbook, including physician:nurse ratio, nurse:bed ratio, density of medical institutions, and total health expenditure. Associations were estimated using patient-number–weighted linear regression models adjusted for hospital level, provincial gross regional product per capita, admission timing, and year, with cluster-robust standard errors at the province level. Results Substantial interprovincial variation was observed. Most healthcare resource indicators were not significantly associated with composite adherence, although physician:nurse ratio showed a borderline positive association (β = 0.018 per 0.1 increase, 95% CI, −0.0004 to 0.036). Secondary prevention adherence was positively associated with health expenditure (β = 0.007; 95% CI, 0.0003-0.014). For thrombolysis within 4.5 hours, physician:nurse ratio was negatively associated (β = −0.062; 95% CI, −0.119 to −0.006), whereas nurse:bed ratio was positively associated (β = 1.232; 95% CI, 0.066-2.397). In contrast, healthcare resource indicators were not clearly associated with in-hospital outcomes. Conclusions Healthcare resource configuration showed modest associations with stroke management but limited associations with in-hospital outcomes, suggesting that resource availability alone may not fully explain variation in stroke outcomes. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Assessing and refining user stories using large language models: a replication study in a real-world organizational software-development setting
Abstract: Specifying and maintaining high-quality user stories is challenging because project contexts evolve, natural-language artifacts are ambiguous, and manual assessment requires substantial effort. The INVEST criteria provide a structured framework for evaluating whether user stories are Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, and Testable. This study examines run-to-run variability and model–expert alignment through a two-phase design. The first phase comprised a dependent replication in which 60 original Spanish-language user stories were evaluated by three experts, GPT-5.1 Thinking (ChatGPT interface), and GPT-5.1 (API-based). The second phase extended the design through structured refinement of the original stories followed by reevaluation of the refined versions under the same Likert (1–5) scale and INVEST rubric. Results were criterion- and execution-condition-specific. Evaluator-related differences in the initial evaluation were detected in a limited subset of comparisons. Across all criterion–condition combinations, paired analyses generally indicated smaller absolute expert–model discrepancies after refinement and reevaluation, although magnitudes were heterogeneous and zero changes were frequent. In the initial evaluation, model ratings more often fell below the expert median when ratings differed; this pattern persisted less uniformly after refinement. Agreement for the average of the three expert ratings was high under ICC(2,3), while ordinal agreement varied by criterion in one refined condition. Overall, the findings are consistent with a potential complementary role for large language models in INVEST-based evaluation and structured refinement, but they do not establish causal improvement, model superiority, or equivalence with expert judgment. However, human oversight remains essential for contextual validation, interpretation, and backlog prioritization. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Boosting baijiu fermentation efficiency through designed microbial community coalescence: Enhanced substrate conversion and flavor output
Abstract: In this study, we designed a synthetic community (SynCom) for directedly monitoring the yield of phenolic compounds and other flavor compounds of Baijiu, through inoculating the coalescence of synthetic community and autochthonous starter culture (Daqu). Compared with the fermentation endpoint, this SynCom, comprised of Wickerhamomyces anomalus, Pantoea agglomerans and Bacillus altitudinis, significantly enhanced the substrate utilization and metabolites formation.Specifically, the consumption of starch and protein was increased by 42.68% and 24.37%, respectively, calculated as the relative increase in consumption from the initial to the endpoint in the model group over that in the control group. Meanwhile, the yield of targeted aromatic compounds increased by 25.9%, with 4-methylguaiacol exhibiting a particularly marked increase from trace levels. Furthermore, we deduced W. anomalus exerted a strong priority effect to constitute over 90% niche of the fungal community and reduce 25% diversity of the community in the front fermentation stage. Therefore, the priority species provided a competitive starving and metabolism of the upcoming species (P. agglomerans and B. altitudinis), and their synergism contributed to the enhancement of targeted phenolic compounds and specific esters in the later stage of fermentation. Our study provided insight into monitoring and controlling the formation of desired compounds through the coalescence of a designed community and a common starter culture. This study also provided a validated framework for the rational designed consortia to control and improve the quality and function of complex fermented foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The potential for coordination between air and ocean transport in advancing Net Zero policies
Abstract: This study explores ways to achieve a modal shift in cargo transport markets for high-value commodities, with particular emphasis on shippers' awareness of climate change. Specifically, it aims to (i) provide insights for carriers in designing efficient cargo transport networks aligned with Net Zero policies; (ii) examine the robustness of the results by discussing the feasibility of sea-and-air services for high-value commodities while accounting for heterogeneity in shippers’ behavior; and (iii) inform policymakers in their efforts to support and facilitate such modal shifts. We apply a bi-level model to a simple four-node network and examine several scenarios by explicitly incorporating heterogeneity among shippers. The main findings are as follows. First, as shippers’ awareness of climate change increases, the share of all-air services declines in each market; notably, this decline is much larger in long-haul markets than in short-haul markets. Second, when the level of awareness among time-sensitive shippers is relatively low, the resulting reduction in GHG emissions in both markets remains quite limited. Third, if time-sensitive shippers with a high level of awareness of climate change occupy the major part of the market, ocean transport can become a feasible option for carrying high-value commodities. Under this condition, short-haul markets may become more competitive, whereas long-haul markets may exhibit greater cooperation between air and ocean transport. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Screening out ethics: How technology enables ethical fading in negotiations
Abstract: Negotiations are rife with opportunities and temptations to engage in unethical negotiating behavior. Such behavior is not always strategic or even intentional; rather, it can emerge from situational characteristics of the negotiation environment. One psychological process through which situational characteristics influence unethical behavior is ethical fading, a process that limits one's ability to recognize the ethical aspects of the situation and behave in line with one's ethical values. As technologies such as email, video conferencing, and artificial intelligence (AI) become increasingly common in negotiations, an important question is whether these technologies facilitate ethical fading. In this review, we explore the impact that technology and AI have on ethical fading and unethical negotiating behavior. We propose that technology and AI use in negotiations promotes three cognitive processes that facilitate ethical fading: psychological distance, cognitive offloading, and displaced accountability. We review how technology may serve as an antecedent to each of these processes and explain why these processes may facilitate ethical fading in negotiation contexts. Because research on the relationship between technology and unethical negotiating behavior remains limited, we conclude by identifying promising directions for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Local market framework considering flexible agents in energy communities: Theory and experimental validation
Abstract: In this paper, we experimentally test a local electricity market framework, considering both passive and active market participants as well as uncertainty from production, consumption and network flows. By solving a chance-constrained optimal power flow and expressing the uncertainty using generalized polynomial chaos, we can express nodal active and reactive power prices as polynomial chaos coefficients eliminating the need to perform computationally expensive Monte Carlo simulations. In the day-ahead stage, this produces probabilistic nodal prices, giving prosumers the ability to make optimal strategies ex ante. In the realtime stage a simple measurement of the stochastic drivers is sufficient to calculate realtime nodal prices, avoiding the need to run near-realtime optimization routines. Results are shown on two operating days as well as 30 days of operation with simulated flexible agents. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Interface Contact Optimization via Phosphomolybdic Acid Enables 24.9% Efficiency in MoOX-Based Silicon Solar Cells
Abstract: The development of cost-effective carrier-selective passivating contacts is critical for enhancing the commercial feasibility of silicon compound solar cells. Molybdenum oxide (MoOX) has garnered considerable interest as a promising hole transport layer (HTLs). A key advantage of MoOX is high work function, in addition to the low-cost processability. However, in silicon photovoltaics, MoOX-based p-type contacts face fundamental limitations at hydrogenated amorphous silicon (i-a-Si:H)/MoOX interface, where oxygen vacancy defects lower work function, as well as, weak van der Waals-dominated interactions impair charge carry transport. To address these challenges, we introduced an ultrathin phosphomolybdic acid (PMA) interlayer at the i-a-Si:H/MoOX interface. PMA passivated oxygen vacancy defects, resulting in a notable improvement in open-circuit voltage from 713 to 730 mV, and 0.11 eV work function elevation via dipole formation; meanwhile, PMA strengthened the interfacial bonding energy, reducing saturation current density and contact resistance by 63% and 24%, respectively, contributing to a fill factor enhancement from 83.7% to 84.9%. In the end, we demonstrated a record efficiency of 24.9% for MoOX-based silicon solar cells, which provides valuable insights for developing high-performance MoOX HTL devices for dopant-free p-type contact technologies. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Seven Sisters tourism under siege: Hybrid neural insights into stakeholder resilience
Abstract: Tourism stakeholders in insurgency-affected destinations navigate persistent insecurity that shapes their perceptions, adaptive behavior, and support for tourism in nonlinear ways. This study investigates how security-related perceptions influence tourism support in Northeast India's Seven Sisters region, a politically fragile zone characterized by prolonged insurgency. Using a mixed-method hybrid design, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), artificial neural network (ANN) modeling, sensitivity analysis, and content analysis were applied to 584 stakeholder surveys and 25 in-depth interviews. EFA identified four latent constructs: security forces concern, moral panic, social stability, and cognitive concern, which collectively explain 57% of tourism support variance. ANN modeling revealed a nonlinear inverted-U relationship between security visibility and stakeholder support, interpreted as a “ security-skepticism dilemma” grounded in Prospect Theory. Security forces concern (35%) and moral panic (24%) were the most influential predictors. These findings advance tourism resilience theory and provide actionable governance guidance for conflict-affected destinations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Reinventing the package holiday: Consumer preferences and optimal pricing for hotel room upgrades
Abstract: We examine a tour operator initiative enabling consumers to select their hotel room before departure for a supplementary fee. Using a stated-preference discrete choice experiment with 691 UK package holidaymakers, we estimate conditional and mixed logit models to identify drivers of upgrade acceptance, derive willingness-to-pay (WTP) estimates, and compute the uptake probability as a continuous function of the fee. Room facilities command the highest WTP (£8.04 per unit), and room location the second-highest (£3.67 per unit); hotel location is insignificant. The revenue-maximizing fee is £33.1 per person, yielding a predicted uptake of 54.1%. Latent class analysis identifies three consumer segments with distinct price sensitivities, and segment-specific revenue optima reveal meaningful variation across hotel categories, lengths of stay, and party types, supporting differentiated fee structures. These findings provide tour operators with a replicable framework for maximizing ancillary revenue from upgrade initiatives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: He Q.
Title: Using vertical integration to safeguard against unfavorable bargaining position
Abstract: This paper examines the effect of a change in bargaining power on the decision to engage in vertical integration. Market contracts are inherently incomplete; when contingencies arise, firms rely on conventions to facilitate non-contractable adaptations. The perceived flexibility of informal agreements increases as the firm’s bargaining power weakens. Using data on the U.S. airline market (2006-2011), I find that buyers (mainline carriers) are more likely to vertically integrate when they have low bargaining power vis-à-vis suppliers (regional partners). Furthermore, mergers are associated with increased outsourcing on routes and contexts where independent regional airlines were previously absent, but with reduced or unchanged outsourcing on routes where independent regional airlines are already present, especially among rival carriers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mapping the global landscape of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship: A bibliometric review (2000–2025)
Abstract: Mentorship is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of women’s entrepreneurial participation and success. However, existing scholarship remains fragmented, conceptually inconsistent, and unevenly distributed across global contexts. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship, examining peer-reviewed literature published between 2000 and 2025 globally. To enhance methodological robustness and address limitations associated with narrow keyword selection, a multi-stage search strategy was employed using the Scopus database. A total of 878 records were identified through the Scopus database. The final dataset includes 621 articles, allowing for a detailed analysis of publication trends, geographic distribution, authorship patterns, and thematic development within the field. The findings reveal a significant concentration of research output in the Global North, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom, with comparatively limited representation from developing regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa. Thematic analysis indicates strong clustering around mentorship, coaching, entrepreneurial ecosystems, and capacity building, highlighting both conceptual convergence and fragmentation. Furthermore, the results show that mentorship is frequently embedded within broader entrepreneurial support frameworks rather than examined as a standalone construct. In response, this study advances a Gendered Social Capital and Learning framework to provide a more integrated understanding of mentorship processes in women’s entrepreneurship. The study contributes to the literature by offering a robust, data-driven overview of the field, identifying key gaps in geographic and theoretical coverage, and highlighting the methodological implications of keyword selection in bibliometric research. The findings provide valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to design more inclusive and contextually relevant mentorship interventions for women entrepreneurs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Yao H.; Chen Z.
Title: How autonomy-supportive environments and growth mindset foster creativity efficacy in middle school students? Evidence from a large-scale survey in China
Abstract: This study examines the associations between multi-source autonomy-supportive environments, growth mindset, and creative self-efficacy among Chinese middle school students, with particular attention to the mediating role of growth mindset and individual heterogeneity in these associations. Using large-scale survey data from 6146 middle school students in Suzhou, China, and drawing on Bandura's (1997) social cognitive theory and Self-Determination Theory, we employed structural equation modeling and quantile regression to investigate these relationships. The SEM results indicate that teacher, parental, and peer autonomy support are all positively associated with creative self-efficacy, with teacher and peer support showing stronger total associations than parental support. Growth mindset mediated all three associations, with the indirect effect proportion being highest for teacher autonomy support, followed by parental autonomy support and peer autonomy support. Quantile regression analyses revealed meaningful heterogeneity across the creative self-efficacy distribution: teacher and parental autonomy support showed stronger associations at lower quantiles, peer autonomy support peaked at moderate quantiles, and all associations weakened at higher quantiles. These findings contribute to the cross-cultural understanding of how multi-source autonomy-supportive environments relate to creative self-efficacy in a collectivist educational context, and offer practical implications for differentiated educational interventions targeting students at different levels of creative self-efficacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wang P.; Xu S.; Wang S.; Cui X.; Bai J.; Sun Y.; Zhu X.; Zhao B.; Chou S.; Wu X.
Title: Anionic Bottom-Up Flux Orchestrated via Hard Carbon Surface Chemistry for Stable Sodium-Ion Batteries
Abstract: Hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries suffer from unstable solid-electrolyte interphase formation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and poor cycle stability. Herein, we demonstrate a molecular-level surface design that actively orchestrates an anionic bottom-up flux from the electrolyte bulk to the hard carbon interface. By engineering a synergistic pair of pyridinic-N and carbonyl groups on the carbon surface, we create a functional-differentiation microenvironment where pyridinic-N selectively anchors PF6− anions, while the cooperative carbonyl repels solvent molecules. This dual functionality establishes a sustained concentration gradient that drives a continuous reverse flux of anions toward the interface, fundamentally redirecting the electrolyte decomposition pathway from solvent-dominated to anion-preferential. The tailored surface lowers the PF6− decomposition barrier by over 70%, yielding a thin, inorganic-rich solid-electrolyte interphase dominated by NaF and Na2O. The optimized anode achieves 91.9% Coulombic efficiency with high reversible capacity of 368.2 mAh g−1, and 96.5% capacity retention after 5,000 cycles. A pouch cell assembled with NFPP cathode achieves an energy density of 239.1 Wh kg−1 and stable operation over 500 cycles, demonstrating strong practical potential. This work establishes active surface-guided anionic transport as a powerful strategy for interphase engineering in advanced sodium-ion batteries. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Elucidating the Respective Roles of Photochemical and Photothermal Effects in Photocatalytic Methanol Decomposition
Abstract: Photocatalytic reactions can be driven by both photochemical and photothermal processes. However, their individual contributions and synergistic effect remain to be clarified. Herein, we investigated the respective roles of these effects using a Cu–TiO2/Ti model catalyst that integrated photochemical and photothermal functionalities within a single photocatalytic system. Employing photocatalytic methanol decomposition as a model reaction, the Cu–TiO2/Ti catalyst achieved a high H2 yield rate of 0.511 mmol h−1 with selectivity of 96.6% toward HCHO among oxidation products, attributed to the cooperative action of photochemical and photothermal processes. In situ resonant Auger electron spectroscopy (RAS), together with in situ Cu K-edge X-ray absorption fine structure and excited-state density functional theory calculations, revealed the accumulation of photogenerated electrons at Cu sites from TiO2, suggests the possible formation of an electron transfer pathway from TiO2 to Cu, which promotes stepwise methanol dehydrogenation to HCHO and H2. Simultaneously, the photothermal contribution from Ti enhanced catalytic activity by accelerating reaction kinetics and promoting the desorption of HCHO, thereby suppressing its overoxidation to CO. Title: Entropy-guided circuit breakers for LLM-augmented intrusion detection: An empirical evaluation of uncertainty-routed cascades in LLMOps
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in security pipelines, but calling them on every input is costly and their reasoning can fail silently. We study an uncertainty-routed cascade for intrusion detection: a Random Forest (RF) classifies each network flow and forwards only low-confidence flows to an LLM, while an entropy-guided circuit breaker monitors token entropy during generation and falls back to the RF when entropy is high. We evaluate it on CIC-IDS2017, CICIoT2023 and NSL-KDD with four instruction-tuned models (Qwen2.5, 0.5B to 14B parameters), using 1200 test flows per model. The RF routes only 0.28%–9.48% of flows to the LLM. On routed flows, LLM accuracy rises with model size from 52.3% to 71.3%, against 56.5% for the RF, and the 14B cascade raises NSL-KDD accuracy from 78.7% to 81.1%. Token entropy, however, is a weak signal of wrong answers: its area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) is 0.51–0.56 early in generation. A threshold calibrated on training flows tripped on every routed flow, saving 88%–95% of the generated tokens, but only 5%–10% once prompt tokens are counted, and discarding the accuracy gains of the larger models. Title: Feelings of ease in generating ideas: My loyal companion that guides my mental action but does not help me generate more creative ideas
Abstract: The ability to generate creative ideas is an important skill for education. This study examined how feelings of ease in generating ideas act as a cue that allowed individuals to have information to monitor their mental action and make important metacognitive decisions while generating creative ideas. Participants were asked to generate four ideas to help deal with the problem of empty work offices during and after the pandemic of COVID-19. Feelings of ease in generating ideas were positively related to self-evaluations and the decisions to continue generating ideas and negatively related to choosing the first idea as the most creative. Title: Modified DEA-SBM efficiency-based diversion risk proxy assessment with peer similarity for decision support in aircraft diversion management
Abstract: Aircraft diversion is a critical component of aviation safety management, requiring close coordination among pilots, air traffic controllers, and airline operations teams. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model, three real diversion cases in the Philippines are used as baseline scenarios. Title: Energy management systems for hybrid AC/DC microgrids: a problem-oriented review of system challenges and control architectures
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources introduces several system-level challenges for hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs), including power coordination, voltage regulation, uncertainty management, load–demand balancing, and energy storage coordination. Energy management systems (EMS) play a key role in addressing these challenges and ensuring reliable and efficient MG operation. Existing review studies mainly focus on methods and optimization techniques, while system challenges are not always clearly identified or examined from a structured perspective. This paper reviews studies that support system design and the mitigation of operational challenges and presents a comprehensive classification of MGs and EMS. Review and research studies are compiled in separate tables and categorized according to system challenges and the applied EMS approaches. System challenges are identified and related to the control layers responsible for addressing them across primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. Title: Task value, effort regulation and critical thinking: Towards a unified learning configuration in financial management education
Abstract: Financial Management requires students to integrate motivational, behavioural, and cognitive competencies to solve financial problems. However, existing research has predominantly examined these learner characteristics independently, providing limited understanding of how they coexist to shape learning. This study adopted a person-centred approach to identify distinct learning configurations based on task value, effort regulation, and critical thinking among Business students studying Financial Management. A cross-sectional survey design was employed to collect data from 168 students using validated measures, and Latent Profile Analysis identified naturally occurring learning profiles. Four distinct learning configurations emerged: Low Learning Orientation (10.1%), Developing Learning Orientation (11.9%), Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation (31.0%), and Integrated Learning Configuration (47.0%). The Integrated Learning Configuration represented the largest group. Notably, the Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation profile reflected students with stronger task value and effort regulation relative to critical thinking. This finding suggests that valuing learning and regulating effort alone may be insufficient for developing higher-order financial reasoning. Profile membership differed by programme of study but not by sex or age. Title: Data-driven calibration sample selection and forecast combination in electricity price forecasting: An application of the ARHNN method
Abstract: Calibration sample selection and forecast combination are two simple yet powerful tools used in forecasting. They can be combined with a variety of models to significantly improve prediction accuracy, at the same time offering easy implementation and low computational complexity. While their effectiveness has been repeatedly confirmed in prior scientific literature, the topic is still underexplored in the field of electricity price forecasting. In this research article we apply the Autoregressive Hybrid Nearest Neighbors (ARHNN) method to three long-term time series describing the German, Spanish and New England electricity markets. We show that it outperforms popular literature benchmarks in terms of forecast accuracy by up to 10%. We also propose two simplified variants of the method, granting a vast decrease in computation time with only minor loss of prediction accuracy. Finally, we compare the forecasts’ performance in a battery storage system trading case study and propose a new automated trading strategy. We find that using a forecast-driven strategy can consistently achieve a substantial share of theoretical maximum profits while trading, demonstrating business value in practical applications. © 2026

Title: Gender Representation and Intercultural Competence in Iranian EFL Coursebooks from the 1960s to 2020s
Abstract: This study aims to investigate the representation of gender and intercultural competence in the images and texts of 15 Iranian secondary school English coursebooks, published over six decades. Gender representation was investigated using the framework proposed by Dahmardeh and Kim (2020), and the scale developed by Solhaug and Kristensen (2020) was used as the criteria for investigating intercultural competence. The data were coded and counted using manifest content analysis. The results showed that Iranian English coursebooks mentioned males and females unequally in their texts across different decades, with one gender being represented more in each decade. Regarding gender representation in the images, males were represented more than females in almost all decades. The representation of males and females in the books published in the 1970s was almost equal, followed by extreme and sudden changes in gender representation in the 1980s. However, the books published in and after the 2000s presented a balanced picture of males and females. The coursebooks dealt with intercultural competence in their texts and images very rarely, limiting this concept to religious issues and neglecting other aspects. In fact, the coursebooks addressed only one category out of the 11 categories.
