Title: Perceived social entrepreneurship education and entrepreneurial intention in times of crisis: Where moral obligation matters
Abstract: Social entrepreneurship education is widely promoted; however, the reflection of students' educational experience in social entrepreneurial intention remains insufficiently understood, particularly in institutionally fragile contexts. Drawing on survey data from 299 Lebanese university students, this study tests a moderated mediation model grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). Specifically, it examines whether personal attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control mediate the relationship between students' perceived social entrepreneurship education experience and entrepreneurial intention, and whether moral obligation conditions these pathways. More positive perceptions of the educational experience are associated with stronger intention indirectly through personal attitude and perceived behavioural control, while subjective norms show no significant effect, reflecting weakened normative reference points under prolonged crisis. Moral obligation operates selectively, strengthening the attitudinal pathway while leaving the control and the normative pathways unchanged. This study extends the mediated view of educational influence to social entrepreneurship education in a crisis setting, suggests that moral obligation may function as a conditional ethical amplifier, and shows how institutional fragility can affect the salient dimensions of TPB. In fragile settings, such education should cultivate reflective attitudes and moral engagement alongside structural reforms that enable normative support for socially oriented careers. © 2026

Title: Technological, economic and environmental aspects of the production of sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker based on the mineral resources of Karakalpakstan; [Қарақалпақстанның минералдық ресурстары негізінде сульфатқа төзімді портландцемент клинкерін өндірудің технологиялық, экономикалық және экологиялық аспектілері]; [Технологические, экономические и экологические аспекты производства сульфатостойкого портландцементного клинкера на основе минеральных ресурсов Каракалпакстана]

Title: Secondhand fashion subscription boxes: A necessary condition analysis of purchase intention determinants

This study examines the secondhand subscription box and eleven potential determinants from the secondhand fashion consumption literature. Using a sample of 215 German participants, we found that most determinants are necessity-based bottlenecks. They must be present and reach a certain threshold. Title: Screen-Printed Li Arrays with Reinforced Interphase as Ultrathin Anodes for High-Energy–Density Liquid- and Solid-State Batteries
Abstract: High-energy–density lithium metal batteries, either liquid or solid state, require ultrathin Li anodes, but their implementation is hindered by poor Li processability in fabrication and inhomogeneous Li plating behaviours upon cycling. This work addresses these challenges through a mask-patterned discrete array using a molten salt-derived Li nanocomposite. The screen-printing strategy circumvents the poor wettability of molten Li on copper that causes high Li|Cu contact angle and non-uniform Li spreading, thus fabricating ultrathin Li foils with equivalent thicknesses below 30 μm. Concurrently, the molten salt-derived inorganic nanoparticles in Li favour homogeneous Li deposition and induce inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase to jointly suppress active Li consumption. The resulting Li array (10–28 μm) anodes demonstrate remarkable performance in both liquid- and solid-state systems, achieving high energy densities up to 504 Wh kg−1/1071 Wh L−1 and stable cycling over 260 cycles with high-loading cathodes. This integrated approach resolves both fabrication and cycling challenges of ultrathin Li anodes and offers an alternative solution for high-performance liquid-/solid-state batteries. Title: A bibliometric and systematic analysis of artificial intelligence and the transition towards smart geotourism

Abstract: The rapid digital transformation of tourism has positioned artificial intelligence as a key enabler of destination intelligence, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable tourism management. Employing a retrospective approach, this study delineates the developmental trajectory of artificial intelligence applications in sustainable tourism while interrogating their integration into the paradigm of smart geotourism. Such findings delineate a burgeoning field of inquiry structured through the convergence of three intersecting axes: technological advancement, analytical intelligence, and visitor-focused experiential paradigms. The review study identified four principal domains through which artificial intelligence contributes to geotourism: predictive analytics, smart destination management, geoheritage interpretation, and environmental monitoring and geoconservation. The findings further highlight significant regional differences in technological adoption and reveal a limited integration between artificial intelligence, geoheritage conservation, and sustainable territorial governance. Based on these findings, the study proposes a smart geotourism framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning within a unified conceptual structure. By delivering an integrated appraisal of artificial intelligence within geotourism, this study contributes to extant scholarship by conceptualizing artificial intelligence beyond its technical dimensions—positioning it as a fundamental enabler of empirical territorial planning, destination analytics, and the sustainable preservation of geological resources. Title: Scenic spot crowd flow prediction: Combining large language model semantic understanding and spatio-temporal network
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of tourist flows is crucial for urban planning, transportation management, and overcrowding prevention. Title: Integrated optimization for fleet sequencing, deploying, and scheduling based on carbon intensity management
Abstract: The mandatory Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) regulations, enforced by the IMO since 2023, create significant operational challenges for shipping lines. To fill this gap, we propose a bi-objective mixed-integer nonlinear programming model that minimizes both total fleet operating cost and total fleet carbon intensity, thereby promoting active carbon intensity management. A customized hybrid solution algorithm, combining the ε-constraint method, rule-based heuristics, linearization techniques, and the CPLEX solver, is designed to solve the model efficiently. Furthermore, speed optimization serves as an effective short-term strategy to improve both cost and carbon performance. Title: Silent Valleys: Unraveling the Causes and Strategic Pathways for Reverse Migration in Hilly Regions of Uttarakhand
Abstract: This study examines out-migration and the prospects for sustainable reverse migration in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand, addressing three objectives: identifying the main drivers of migration, synthesizing reinforcement strategies to reduce distress migration and support return, and linking causes and responses within a human-environment systems perspective. Authors: Xu X.; Liu X.; Zhang L.; Wen J.
Title: Inside and out: Exploring how internal and external CSR perceptions influence hospitality employees’ service sabotage
Abstract: Although corporate social responsibility (CSR) has been shown to exert positive effects on hospitality organizations and their stakeholders, the interactive effect of internal CSR (ICSR) and external CSR (ECSR) perceptions on employees’ subsequent service behaviors remains unclear. Drawing on social cognitive theory and cue consistency theory, this study aims to explore how the interaction between ICSR and ECSR perceptions influences employees’ service sabotage. Title: Mapping the intellectual structure of digital transformation research in SMEs: A decade of performance-oriented studies
Abstract: Despite their vital contribution to worldwide economic progress, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are vulnerable to environmental fluctuations, resource limitations, and swift technological shifts. In this context, digital transformation has emerged as a critical strategic mechanism through which firms seek to enhance competitiveness, resilience, and organizational outcomes. Although this topic has attracted considerable scholarly attention in recent years, the available literature is dispersed across different academic fields, theoretical viewpoints, and methodologies, making it difficult to gain a holistic understanding of the area's intellectual organization and progression. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to examine digital transformation and firm-level outcomes in small business contexts from January 2016 to January 2026. Bibliographic data were retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix through its Biblioshiny interface and VOSviewer. A final dataset of 186 peer-reviewed journal articles was examined using descriptive statistics, keyword co-occurrence analysis, bibliographic coupling, citation analysis, thematic mapping, and research trend analysis. The results indicate a strong and accelerating publication trend, with an annual growth rate of 17.46, particularly since 2020, highlighting the increasing strategic importance of digital technologies in response to economic disruptions and uncertainty. The analysis identifies four major thematic clusters: (1) performance-oriented outcomes, (2) technology - and capability-driven transformation, (3) organizational and sustainability-related performance, and (4) strategic and Industry 4.0-oriented transformation. In addition, emerging themes include digital readiness, dynamic capabilities, and business model innovation. While the literature frequently associates digital transformation with improved organizational outcomes, the findings also reveal persistent heterogeneity in results and highlight substantial risks and failure rates, especially among resource-constrained firms. By mapping the intellectual foundations, thematic structure, and evolution of this research domain, the study provides an integrative overview that supports theory development and informs future empirical research. The results also offer valuable insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers who seek to understand and guide digital transformation initiatives in small business contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Development and validation of an ATP degradation model for predicting K-value progression in chilled greenling under variable temperature conditions
Abstract: Temperature fluctuations during refrigerated distribution can accelerate postmortem ATP degradation and complicate freshness management; therefore, a temperature-responsive model is needed to predict K-value progression under practical cold-chain conditions. In this study, a temperature-responsive kinetic model was developed to predict the K-value, a widely used indicator of fish freshness, using greenling (Hexagrammos otakii) as the model species. The pooled variable A = ATP + ADP + AMP was modeled as converting to IMP and then to H = HxR + Hx through two first-order processes governed by empirical effective rate coefficients k1 and k2. The coefficients were calibrated at 0 and 5 °C, while 2.5 °C and intermittent 0–5 °C data were reserved for validation. Across the 24 observations reserved for validation, K-value predictions yielded an RMSE of 7.976 percentage points, an MAE of 5.180 percentage points, and an R2 of 0.885. During commercial transport, the representative prediction at approximately 51 h was 12.48%, compared with a measured group median of 11.97%, without parameter re-optimization. Title: Renewable electricity penetration and retail price dynamics: Global evidence on transitional costs of the energy transition
Abstract: The global expansion of renewable energy represents a structural transformation with profound macroeconomic and financial implications. This study investigates the impact of renewable electricity penetration on retail electricity prices using a multi-country panel. The study employs a comprehensive multi-layered empirical framework to address endogeneity, dynamic adjustment, and cross-country structural heterogeneity. The results reveal that renewable penetration is associated with statistically significant short-to medium-term increases in residential electricity prices. However, this effect is nonlinear and conditional on fossil fuel dependence. Once fossil reliance falls below a critical threshold, the marginal price impact weakens substantially. Distributional evidence shows that renewable price effects are amplified in high-price electricity markets. Title: Recursive object-centric process discovery with fitness and rediscovery guarantees
Abstract: Digitized processes are an integral part of businesses to achieve their operational goals. Process mining aims to analyze such processes based on digital track records. These so-called event logs can be extracted from commonly used information systems. Traditionally, process mining remains limited as it requires individual business objects to define isolated process executions. However, in real-life processes, it is much more common to observe multiple business objects of various types that interact with each other. Object-centric process mining acknowledges this fact and fundamentally enhances traditional process mining techniques to analyze processes with interacting business objects. This analysis often requires a process model that describes the interacting control flows of all objects. Discovery algorithms are used to automatically construct such models from logs. For further steps, it is important that the discovery algorithm rediscovers a process model that is equivalent to the underlying business process. If it is impossible to rediscover the full behavior of a process, the discovered model should at least be fitting for the observed behavior. However, no existing object-centric discovery technique guarantees rediscovery or fitness. In this paper, we introduce a new algorithm that recursively constructs tree-structured object-centric models. We prove that our approach produces fitting models for all logs and rediscovers a subclass of processes within the used representational bias from logs that are sufficiently complete and free of incorrect recordings, unobserved or duplicated activities and loops. We evaluate our approach on a range of public logs and find it to produce fitting models in feasible runtime. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: OpenGATE-based gamma response mapping of a lead-collimated multi-range GM detector array for nuclear technical waste screening
Abstract: Rapid screening of mixed nuclear technical waste requires a radiation measurement layer that can provide both conservative risk estimation and region-level spatial information. This study proposes an OpenGATE/Geant4-based gamma response mapping framework for a 10 × 10 planar multi-range Geiger–Mueller detector array with a lead-grid coarse collimation structure. The simulated photon-transport response is converted into a simulation-normalized dose-rate score map through a statistical multi-range GM fusion model considering dead-time correction, valid-range weighting, and counting uncertainty. The framework was evaluated using particle-number convergence, lead-grid parameter analysis, measurement-time assessment, source-position and shielding response tests, known-level screening validation, independent randomized validation, and robotic sorting priority experiments. The lead grid reduced the neighbor-8/peak crosstalk ratio from 1.905 without lead to 1.075 for the 10 mm/40 mm configuration, with a 57.4% reduction in total counts. A 5 s acquisition achieved a repeated-postprocessing coefficient of variation of approximately 1.85%. The independent randomized validation achieved 96.0% accuracy with no dangerous underestimation. In 50 randomized waste-bag scenarios, the first selected item was an L3 or L4 source in 49/50 cases, with an average top-3 high-risk recall of 0.940. The reported values are simulation-normalized screening scores rather than calibrated ambient dose-equivalent rates; standard-source calibration and prototype validation are required before absolute dose-rate interpretation. Title: The impact of technological developments on the changing role of HR(M): A scoping review and research agenda
Abstract: Due to technological developments, jobs disappear, new jobs arise, and existing jobs change. This leads to opportunities and challenges regarding human resource management (HRM) and the role of the HR function in the future of work. In this article, we explore how technological developments such as the use of smart technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and robotics influence HRM and the role of the HR function. Through a scoping review, we highlight the influence of technological developments across macro (societal), meso (organization/HRM) and micro (individual workers) level work themes. We specifically focus on the dynamic interplay between technological developments and HRM. At the meso level, the analysis zooms in on how technological developments influence HRM at the strategic, tactical, and operational levels within organizational contexts. Our findings inform a future research agenda comprising avenues aimed at deepening our understanding of the challenges and opportunities associated with technological change in the context of HRM. More specifically, we propose future research to explore how the HR function can prepare the organization, itself, and other stakeholders, including line managers and workers, for the impact of technological developments to enhance HRM for the greater good. Title: Attribution of causality following service failure on online retail platforms: The roles of governance structure and recurring failures
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online retail platforms are increasingly mediating customer–vendor interactions, yet research offers limited insight into how platform governance shapes service failure attribution, especially after recurring failures. Drawing on attribution theory, this paper examines how centralized versus diffused governance structures influence consumers’ attribution of causality to the platform after service failure and their responses to recurring failures. Study 1 analyzes customer reviews using computational text analysis and shows that customers recognize governance structures and attribute causality to the platform more often under centralized than diffused governance. Employing scenario-based experiments, Study 2 demonstrates that centralized (vs. diffused) governance leads to higher failure attribution to the platform. Finally, we show that attribution following single and recurring failures serially mediates the relationship between governance structure and repurchase intention after a recurring failure. Importantly, platform attribution exerts opposite effects across failure episodes: following a single failure and successful recovery, greater platform attribution increases repurchase intention by signaling platform accountability and resolution capability. Title: Hemisphere-aware Graph Convolution and 3D Structural Fusion for multi-modal fMRI brain-disorder classification
Abstract: Multimodal functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data is a valuable source of information for precisely classifying neurological disorders, which is why it is widely used in the diagnosis of these diseases. However, traditional methods struggle to capture the spatiotemporal dynamics of the brain and single-modality approaches overlook voxel-level structural information. This limits the accuracy of imaging diagnoses of neurological diseases. This study therefore selected resting-state fMRI samples from the Autism Spectrum Disorder (ABIDE) and Parkinson's Disease (PPMI) datasets, proposing the multi-modal half-brain perception framework MSHAGL. This comprises a shared-weight half-brain–whole-brain graph convolutional network (CHW-GCN) and a three-dimensional structure encoder (GBConvNet3D). These are combined with multi-head gated fusion and redundancy suppression loss for joint optimization. Specifically, dynamic maps of the left and right hemispheres and the whole brain are constructed, cross-scale functional connectivity features are extracted, and 3D fMRI volumes are utilized to capture spatial structural patterns. Gating mechanisms achieve dynamic alignment and weighted fusion of temporal-structural features. In classification experiments on the ABIDE and PPMI datasets for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), the results demonstrate that hemispheric perception modelling and multimodal fusion effectively enhance diagnostic sensitivity and robustness while revealing abnormal connectivity and spatial activation patterns related to disease. Title: Digital and AI-enabled support for HACCP-based dairy food safety management: Functions, evidence, and implementation boundaries
Abstract: Dairy food-safety management spans primary production, purchasing, processing, packaging, storage, transport, and distribution. Biological, chemical, physical, and allergenic hazards vary with the product and process. Digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools can extend how data are collected, interpreted, and connected to Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) and food safety management system (FSMS) activities. Their value depends on the function supported and the evidence for the intended use. This narrative, function-oriented review examines sensors, Internet of Things systems, traceability platforms, machine learning, predictive microbiology, rapid detection, knowledge graphs, retrieval-augmented generation, and large language models. The comparison covers five functions: hazard analysis and risk prioritization; monitoring and deviation detection; verification and the screening–confirmatory interface; documentation, traceability, and plan review; and decision support at the corrective-action interface. The analytical framework records dairy relevance, deployment stage, and validation scope. It also distinguishes analytical outputs and alerts from verified deviations, confirmatory evidence, and site-specific actions. The reviewed tools are best established for data capture, monitoring, and verification inputs. Evidence is thinner for hazard prioritization, digital plan review, and AI-assisted decision support. Food-safety use requires dairy product and process context, fit-for-purpose evidence, approved procedures, auditable records, and review by responsible personnel. Title: Konjac glucomannan-modified ferrous fumarate emulsions with interpenetrating polymer networks: Physicochemical stability, microstructure, and bioaccessibility
Abstract: Ferrous fumarate (FF), a iron-rich organic fortificant, exhibits high oxidation stability; however, its poor solubility and severe sedimentation in neutral media limit bioaccessibility. This study developed an FF-loaded emulsion based on an interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) formed by whey protein concentrate (WPC), xanthan gum (XG), and konjac glucomannan (KGM). Increasing the KGM concentration reduced the emulsion particle size from 946.07 to 346.70 nm and raised the absolute zeta potential from 50.34 ± 1.17 mV to 53.34 ± 0.89 mV, thereby improving physical stability. The emulsions showed enhanced apparent viscosity with shear-thinning behavior and dominant elastic responses within the linear viscoelastic region. Microstructural analysis revealed that KGM incorporation converted a layered structure into a robust IPN architecture, confining FF near the oil–water interface and suppressing droplet aggregation. Spectroscopic results indicated strengthened intermolecular hydrogen bonding and increased β-sheet content. The incorporation of KGM effectively maintained the Fe2+ retention rate (∼95%) during thermal processing. The IPN emulsion achieved an iron bioaccessibility of 73.18%, representing an 11.86-fold increase over free FF. This study demonstrates the efficacy of IPN-structured emulsions in delivering poorly soluble active ingredients, providing a promising strategy for developing iron-fortified foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Data-Driven Risk Allocation and Incentive-Compatible Payment Schemes in Construction Contracts: Integrating Comparative Standard Forms, Public Works Disputes, and Principal-Agent Modeling
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Construction projects worldwide suffer from misaligned risk allocation, poorly chosen payment schemes, and opaque claims and dispute processes, leading to chronic cost overruns and litigation. Building on comparative analyses of widely used international and national standard forms of contract, empirical public works dispute case studies, and principal-agent theory of payment methods, this research develops a data-driven framework for designing incentive-compatible construction contracts. First, we code and compare more than 60 distinct risk events and 40 claims and dispute procedures across several representative standard contract regimes for large infrastructure projects. Second, we construct a dataset of approximately 80 real dispute or major change-order cases (including highway, bridge, and building projects) and classify them by triggering risk, procurement mode, and payment scheme. Third, we calibrate a structural principal-agent model of contractor effort, cost uncertainty, and risk aversion to this dataset, comparing fixed-price, unit-price, cost-plus, and target-price contracts. The calibrated model is then used to simulate how alternative combinations of risk allocation clauses and payment mechanisms affect expected owner cost, contractor risk exposure, and the probability of disputes. Simulation results are used to quantify potential performance gains from better-aligned contract design; illustrative scenarios target a 15%-25% reduction in expected total project cost, a 30%-40% reduction in formal disputes, and a 40% reduction in claims processing time when more balanced risk-sharing clauses and incentive-compatible payment schemes are adopted. Title: Developing a cyber-resilience framework for UAVs: insights from expert interviews on addressing cybersecurity challenges
Abstract: Rapid technological advances have greatly enhanced the development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their potential for beneficial uses. Such uses, however, have been limited by cybersecurity concerns. Despite considerable research attention, threat levels are increasing, and this is likely to further inhibit UAV use. This study proposes a holistic cyber-resilience framework for UAVs based on five resilience features, which are redundancy, flexibility, modularity, diversity, and tightness of feedback loops. Such a change, called for by several authors but yet to be achieved, can come through the components of a framework that are supported by expert perspectives. The study employs a mixed-methods design with in-person interviews of 32 expert professionals across eight sectors (aviation, military, security, insurance, aerospace, cybersecurity, logistics, and academia). A total of 261 vulnerabilities ranging across five threat categories are identified, with those related to communication facilitating a point of entry for cascading attacks. Drawing on expert evaluations of five resilience features, the novelty of this study is its proposed lifecycle-based framework that shifts UAV security from mitigation to embedded resilience. Title: Dynamic Diffusion of Legal Compliance and Ethical Conduct among Construction Project Owners: An Epidemiological Modeling Approach

Title: Plugging in feedback in the software development pipeline: Insights from DevOps practitioners
Abstract: In the rapidly evolving domain of software development, the integration and management of feedback within the development pipeline play a pivotal role in ensuring product quality and process efficiency. This paper explores the nuances of feedback mechanisms in contemporary software development practices, with a particular focus on DevOps and Continuous Integration (CI)/Continuous Deployment (CD) practices. Drawing insights from qualitative interviews with 19 experienced DevOps practitioners in various countries, the study delves into how teams incorporate feedback at different stages of the development pipeline. Title: Explainable spatiotemporal modeling in crime analytics: Robbery prediction via graph neural networks
Abstract: Urban crime prediction is a critical task for ensuring public safety, yet it faces challenges related to model accuracy and transparency. While crime is an inherently temporal phenomenon, its embedding within the city’s structure suggests that integrating spatiotemporal dependencies via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can improve model robustness, particularly in data-sparse environments. Traditional grid-based methods often fail to capture the complex network topology of cities, while the “black-box” nature of advanced models raises ethical concerns for predictive policing. This study proposes an explainable spatiotemporal framework to predict robbery risk by uniquely integrating three elements: (1) fine-grained, citizen-sensed data from a public safety application in Santiago, Chile; (2) a tailored graph neural network to learn how to represent the urban environment as a graph; and (3) an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) component using Integrated Gradients to ensure transparency. We evaluate the model’s performance against traditional classifiers across various prediction horizons (1, 3, and 7 days) and spatial granularities. The results show that the tailored architecture dramatically improves predictive accuracy (average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve -AUC-  ≈  0.85) compared to conventional methods. Furthermore, the XAI analysis provides novel empirical evidence that citizen reports of “suspicious activity” are highly significant predictors of future burglaries, often more so than prior robbery incidents themselves. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Quantifying Regulatory Bottlenecks in South Korea’s Clinical Trial Approval Process Through an Analytic Hierarchy Process Framework
Abstract: Purpose: Drug lag is a critical issue limiting South Korea’s pharmaceutical competitiveness and patient access, and it has been linked to delays in the Investigational New Drug (IND) review process. This study aimed to identify key barriers affecting IND review efficiency in South Korea by analyzing real-world industry experience and to propose concrete strategic actions to mitigate drug lag. Methods: We employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. First, we used grounded theory to identify problematic factors within the IND process through semi-structured interviews. We then applied the Analytic Hierarchy Process to evaluate these factors, followed by a quadrant analysis of importance and urgency to identify top-priority tasks. Results: Three core categories (rationality and patient-centricity, professional review, and operational efficiency), were identified as key domains for enhancing IND efficiency. Rationality and patient-centricity emerged as the most important and urgent criterion, followed closely by professional review. Within rationality and patient-centricity, four sub-criteria placed in the first quadrant (highly important and highly urgent): integration of patient needs into evaluation, global regulatory harmonization, acceptance of scientific evidence for new modalities, and adoption of overseas regulatory standards. Two sub-criteria within professional review (expert team review and standardized review guidelines) were also pinpointed in the first quadrant. Although operational efficiency ranked lowest, simplified Korean translation requirements stood out as the most critical factor within this category. Conclusion: Transitioning from focusing on procedural speed toward embracing regulatory flexibility to enhance scientific rationality and patient access is a viable pathway for mitigating drug lag in South Korea. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Collaborating with GenAI: A blessing or a curse for creativity?
Abstract: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) are increasingly shifting creative work from individual creation toward human–AI collaboration. Drawing on evidence from various creative domains, such as writing, design, and product ideation, this review highlights the gains and constraints of collaborating with GenAI, distinguishing between outcome-related and process-related effects. While GenAI can increase the number of ideas, enhance idea quality, accelerate idea generation, and reduce cognitive load, it may also lead to idea homogenization, diminished perceptions of authenticity and ownership, reduced independent creative engagement, and weakened team collaboration. To clarify when GenAI supports rather than hinders creativity, this review identifies four key moderating factors: 1) when GenAI is used (i.e., timing of GenAI involvement), 2) how it is used (i.e., interaction design), 3) what it is used for (i.e., task characteristics), and 4) by whom it is used (i.e., user expertise). The findings highlight the need for future research on how to better structure human–AI collaboration to support both creative performance and the development of human creative capabilities. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Structural Changes and Supply Elasticity of Potato Production: The Case of Slovenia
Abstract: This study investigates the long-term structural transformation and supply responsiveness of potato production in Slovenia, a sector that has experienced a substantial and sustained contraction (more than 90% of total potato area in comparison to 1961) over the past several decades. Drawing on official statistical datasets covering the period from 1961 to 2024, we analyze trends in cultivated area, yields, price dynamics, and regional production patterns. Descriptive statistics, ANOVA, and spatial analyses reveal a marked decline of more than 90% in potato-growing area, contrasted by significant yield improvements attributable to technological progress and farm consolidation. Kernel density analysis of GERK parcel data confirms a highly fragmented production structure, with the vast majority of holdings cultivating less than one hectare and only a small proportion engaging in commercially meaningful production. To evaluate supply elasticity, we estimate a log–log regression model and a Nerlovian partial-adjustment model. The empirical results indicate negligible short-run price elasticity and strong path dependence, with lagged area emerging as the dominant predictor of current production. Long-run elasticity estimates remain weak, underscoring the limited capacity of Slovenian potato producers to adjust to market signals due to structural constraints, including small farm size, perishability of the product, and limited integration into commercial supply chains. The findings highlight a sector characterized by persistent contraction and low supply responsiveness. This evidence contributes to the understanding of supply behavior in structurally constrained agricultural systems and provides an analytical basis for future research and policy interventions targeting farm structure, market development, and regional production potential. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Job shop scheduling problem with competing agents

Abstract: In this paper, we study the two-machine job shop scheduling problem with two competing agents. The goal is to minimize a given objective function for one agent, subject to a given upper bound of another objective function associated with the second agent. We prove the NP-hardness of this problem with respect to various criteria and settings. With respect to the makespan for both agents, we first exhibited polynomial time algorithms for several special cases. We then developed mathematical models, a branch and bound algorithm, and a genetic algorithm, followed by an intensive experimental simulation to study their performance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Negotiation impasses as meaningful outcomes: How AI is changing the cost structure of walking away
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is often expected to improve negotiation by strengthening information processing and analytical consistency. We argue that its effects on impasses are more selective. Extending the impasse cause, type, and resolution (ICTR) model, we distinguish two pathways. The first pathway is analytical augmentation: AI can reduce unwanted impasses caused by misunderstanding, poor option generation, and coordination failure. The second pathway runs through behavioral flexibility: Humans sometimes reach mutually acceptable agreements through aspiration adjustment, face-saving, and relational repair. Systems configured to apply stable decision thresholds and optimize focal-party outcomes without relational objectives reduce this flexibility and can thereby increase forced impasses. Which pathway dominates depends on AI's role as advisor or counterpart; its objective, training, and prompt; and whether agreement primarily requires analytical problem solving or interpersonal flexibility. These predictions concern system behavior, not whether AI experiences fatigue or social pressure: systems can be designed to respond to relational cues without experiencing them. Wanted impasses depend on both parties' underlying preferences, which AI does not change; AI instead helps negotiators recognize incompatibility sooner and justify walking away more openly. AI therefore changes the composition and meaning of impasses rather than uniformly increasing or decreasing agreement. Remaining impasses may reveal genuine incompatibility, but they may also reflect misspecified objectives or failures to encode principals' relational and economic costs. © 2026 The Authors

Title: When AI wears a face: How AI appearance shapes intentionality attributions in service success and failure
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Customer-facing AI agents are becoming frontline service interfaces, yet firms still face a consequential design question: should these agents look human-like or robot-like? This research examines how AI agent appearance shapes consumers' intentionality attributions in AI-mediated service encounters and how these inferences translate into satisfaction and future AI use intention. Drawing on attribution theory and anthropomorphism research, we propose that human-like and robot-like appearances do not have uniformly positive or negative effects; rather, their effects depend on consumers’ evaluations of service outcomes and their familiarity with AI. A 2 (AI agent appearance: human-like vs. robot-like) × 2 (service outcome: success vs. failure) between-subjects experiment was conducted with 350 U.S. participants in an airline customer-service chatbot context. Results reveal a reversal across outcome evaluations. When consumers experienced service success, robot-like AI elicited higher perceived intentionality than human-like AI, particularly among those with lower AI familiarity. When consumers experienced service failure, human-like AI elicited higher perceived intentionality than robot-like AI, although this effect weakened and reversed among consumers with higher AI familiarity. Perceived intentionality, in turn, increased satisfaction and future AI use intention, supporting a moderated mediation process. These findings reframe AI appearance as an attributional cue rather than a simple humanization strategy and demonstrate that consumers interpret the same AI appearance differently depending on how they evaluate the service encounter. Managerially, the results suggest that firms should not assume that increasing human likeness will universally improve customer responses. Instead, marketers should consider how different customer segments, particularly those varying in AI familiarity, are likely to interpret and respond to AI appearance cues across diverse service experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Prediction-correction dynamical systems for time-varying minimax problems with applications
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: This paper proposes three classes of prediction-correction dynamical systems (PCDSs) for solving a time-varying minimax problem (TV-MMP) under mild conditions. We propose an asymptotically convergent PCDS for TV-MMP and prove, via Lyapunov analysis, that its solutions converge asymptotically to the saddle point trajectory of TV-MMP with a vanishing tracking error. We also design a fixed time convergent PCDS for TV-MMP by replacing the linear correction term with the nonlinear one, and show its solutions converge to the saddle point trajectory of TV-MMP within fixed time. Moreover, we develop a predefined time convergent PCDS for TV-MMP by adding a scaling factor, and prove its solutions converge to the saddle point trajectory of TV-MMP within predefined time. In addition, we apply the above results to time-varying linear equality constrained optimization problems. Finally, we give several numerical examples to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Towards a datafication framework for higher education institutions student success: A systematic review
Abstract: Customer success is key to customer retention. Seemingly, this is equally true in the higher education space, as students are customers of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and, therefore, the primary reason for HEIs' existence. In view of this, it is important to understand and improve student success, which is dependent on different data indicators. Being guided by student success data indicators in HEI administration is necessary as it’s beneficial to both HEIs and their students, as through it, students can complete their qualification on time, and HEIs generate revenue. In the South African context, with its high unemployment rate and high dropout rates, understanding HEI student success is vital. However, HEIs are accustomed to collecting data rather than utilizing it for transformational activities, there has been an increase in research/publications on student success datafication frameworks in higher education in South Africa. However, these studies in isolation do not give the complete picture. This paper aims to systematically review the South African-based HEI student success data-related frameworks, including their underlying principles, trends, challenges, gaps, and future opportunities for improvement. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses method was used. Based on a clearly outlined search strategy, 508 publication abstracts were considered for review. Of these abstracts, 40 were selected for further review based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria, and thereafter, 16 publications were included in the final review. The systematic review findings indicated that mostly data point indicators exist as compared to datafication frameworks. Furthermore, limited studies have been conducted on private higher education institutions in South Africa. Additionally, public sector studies have focused on first-year students; therefore, no segmentation. The implication of this study is that it sets the tone for future work within datafication, student success, and higher education, potentially enabling HEIs to approach transformational data. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: When and why are negotiators overly pessimistic? The psychology of under-trust innegotiation
Abstract: Research on negotiation has devoted considerable attention to the risks of misplaced trust, particularly the possibility that negotiators may be exploited by deceptive counterparts. Less attention has been given to the opposite form of trust miscalibration: under-trust, and particularly, unwarranted pessimism regarding counterparts' honesty. This review focuses on such undue distrust and proposes a misperceived motivations account to explain its emergence. According to this account, negotiators' excessive distrust stems from an asymmetry between the motives that negotiators attribute to their counterparts and the motives that actually guide those counterparts’ behavior. When deciding whether to behave honestly, negotiators are driven not only by self-interest but also by concerns about moral self-image and anticipated moral emotions, which constrain dishonesty. However, when deciding whether counterparts are honest, negotiators assume that their counterparts are primarily motivated by self-interest and fail to foresee the constraining moral-identity concerns. We integrate evidence from the literature on negotiation, trust, and moral psychology to explain why pessimism is especially likely to emerge and persist in competitive bargaining contexts, highlight circumstances that may attenuate or amplify it, and identify implications for theory and research, alongside practical inferences for fostering truthful disclosure and credible honesty in negotiation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Do users trade performance for eco-visibility? Digital pollution awareness and stated preferences for social media platform configurations
Abstract: Digital platforms face growing pressure to demonstrate environmental responsibility, yet users’ preferences for eco-visible features remain underexplored relative to functional attributes. Using a full-factorial rating-based within-subject conjoint survey with a UK sample (N = 345) recruited to match national census distributions of age, sex, and ethnicity, combined with hierarchical linear modelling, this study decomposes willingness to use social media platforms across four attributes: media quality, loading speed, eco-visibility, and advertising frequency. Results show that technical attributes — media quality (relative importance = 34.9%) and loading speed (34.5%) — jointly dominate eco-visibility (8.1%), revealing a persistent performance-over-sustainability hierarchy in elicited trade-off preferences. A full 4 × 4 cross-level moderation analysis incorporating all 16 attribute-by-moderator interactions with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction identifies advertising receptivity — rather than green self-identity or environmental awareness — as the strongest individual-difference moderator, showing a dual pattern: it simultaneously attenuates the reduced-ads utility and amplifies the loading-speed premium. Green self-identity attenuates the media-quality premium but does not amplify eco-visibility utility; none of the eco-visibility moderations — by green self-identity, social comparison orientation, or digital environmental attitude — is confirmed. Exploratory benefit segmentation identifies three preference profiles — Technical Optimizers, Eco-Aware Pragmatists, and Ad-Averse Minimalists — revealing a sign reversal in eco-visibility utility across profiles. Theoretical and practical implications for sustainable platform design, multiple-comparison practices in conjoint moderation research, and green digital marketing are discussed. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Optimal Pricing Strategies and Channel Modes Selection for A Fresh Agricultural Product Supply Chain with Blockchain Traceability
Abstract: The traceability system supported by blockchain technology (BCT) provides consumers with authentic information, triggering the premium effect in the fresh agricultural product supply chain (FASC). This paper introduces BCT to the FASC, which consists of a powerful manufacturer and a retailer. We consider two channel modes: The dual-channel (DC) mode, in which the retailer sells products through an offline channel and the manufacturer sells through an online channel, and the buy-online-pickup-in-store (BOPS) mode, in which the manufacturer adds BOPS options to consumers. We analyse the optimal pricing strategies in scenarios with and without BCT and discuss the channel mode selection between DC and BOPS modes for the manufacturer and retailer with BCT. The results show that when the label cost is below the threshold, the manufacturer may adopt BCT, and the retailer is incentivised to join BCT when the premium effect is high. Furthermore, the channel mode selection of the manufacturer and retailer depends mainly on the demand for the BOPS channel. When the demand for the BOPS channel is low (high), both the manufacturer and retailer prefer the DC (BOPS) mode; when the demand for the BOPS channel is moderate, the manufacturer prefers the DC mode, and the retailer prefers the BOPS mode. To resolve the conflict of channel mode preference, we design a set of fixed transfer payment contracts to ensure the uniformity of channel mode preference between the manufacturer and retailer. The adoption of BCT may improve the consumer surplus when the premium effect is high, and the consumer surplus in BOPS mode is higher than that in DC mode when the demand of the BOPS channel exceeds the threshold. © The author(s) 2027.

Title: Why they come (back): Motive clusters of seasonal employees and their multiple workplace commitments
Abstract: This study develops seasonal employee typologies for the Alpine tourism and hospitality sector by connecting motives for seasonal work with varying levels of different workplace commitments and return intention. Conceptualizing the destination as an analytical lens rather than merely context, this study examines how employees’ social, economic, and leisure motives affect their commitment to the organization, coworkers, job, and destination. Drawing on survey data from 381 hospitality employees in an Alpine destination in Austria, cluster analysis, analysis of variance, and post hoc tests were applied. The analysis identified four employee clusters (lifestyle seekers, dedicated professionals, practical earners, and social contributors) that significantly differ in their motivational profiles, commitment patterns, and demographic characteristics. The findings demonstrate that commitment among seasonal employees extends beyond the organization and differs across motive-based segments. These differences may shape guest interactions and service delivery, ultimately impacting service quality, visitor satisfaction, and overall destination performance. By integrating a motive-based segmentation with a multi-target commitment perspective, this study advances research on seasonal tourism employment and underscores how destination-specific contexts impact employee attitudes and behaviors. Title: A multi-scale approach to hydrothermal liquefaction of two-phase olive mill waste: From laboratory test to regional biorefinery in Andalusia
Abstract: The olive oil industry produces over 3 Mt of two-phase olive mill waste (TPOMW) annually in Andalusia. Its management presents a significant environmental challenge due to its high moisture content and phytotoxicity. Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) is a promising valorization route utilizing the water content in the waste as a reaction medium, saving energy (no drying is needed). In this study a multi-scale approach has been used, integrating physicochemical characterization, laboratory scale experiments, kinetic modelling and a GIS-based location assessment for the location of HTL treatment plants. TPOMW shows high moisture (72 wt%) and a significant lipid content (16.4 wt% db), with a high heating value of approx. 23 MJ/kg. Kinetic results indicate that the solid fraction is the primary product for the first 22 min, after which the aqueous phase dominates due to rapid organic matter hydrolysis, obtaining a bio-oil yield around 20%. According to the resulting reaction network a model with three first order equation that can predict the behaviour of the process has been proposed. Finally, a GIS-based location-allocation analysis has been performed, proposing a decentralized network of 15 HTL plants across Andalusia. Results show a framework for the implementation of HTL-based biorefineries, supporting the transition toward a circular bioeconomy in the Mediterranean area. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Documentor mindsets: Considerations when contributing learning resources for software development technologies
Abstract: Many volunteers contribute learning resources for software development technologies online. Title: Not alone: How group photos enhance audience responses to virtual influencers
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Although marketers increasingly use virtual influencers to engage consumers, concerns about authenticity continue to limit their effectiveness. This research examines whether group photos can make virtual influencers appear more socially connected and authentic, thereby improving audience responses. We propose that, compared with no-person images or solo photos, group photos provide visual social cues that place virtual influencers in recognizable interpersonal contexts and make them appear more socially connected in shared experiences. Across one large-scale field study and two experiments, we test this proposition. Study 1 draws on a large-scale Instagram dataset of 17,878 posts from 109 virtual influencers collected between 2023 and 2026, with the main analyses based on 8558 non-video posts and finds that group photos receive higher post engagement than no-person images and solo photos. Study 2 provides controlled experimental evidence consistent with this effect and suggests that perceived social connectedness and perceived authenticity sequentially account for the relationship between group photos and favorable post evaluations. Study 3 identifies virtual influencer type as an important boundary condition: group photos are more effective for human-like virtual influencers, whereas this advantage weakens for cartoon-like virtual influencers. These findings contribute to research on virtual influencer humanization and authenticity by showing that visual social connectedness can make virtual influencers appear more socially embedded, more authentic, and more favorably evaluated. Title: Understanding grey sheep users in recommender systems: A systematic and critical review of detection, modeling, and evaluation
Abstract: Grey sheep users (GSUs), characterized by weak or unstable alignment with the broader user population, remain a challenge in collaborative filtering-based recommender systems. Despite extensive efforts devoted to their detection and treatment, a clear and consistent understanding of GSUs is still lacking. Existing studies typically adopt model-dependent definitions and often assume that GSUs necessarily reduce recommendation quality. This paper presents a systematic and critical review of GSUs, covering their definition, detection strategies, modeling paradigms, and evaluation practices. We revisit the classical similarity-based interpretation and show that the effect of GSUs depends on model design rather than being inherently harmful. Based on this observation, we introduce a refined conceptual perspective that describes GSUs as users with consistently misaligned preference patterns, and further propose a dynamic view that distinguishes between short-term irregular behavior and stable preference differences. We then provide a comprehensive taxonomy of existing approaches, including detection-dependent methods and detection-free strategies, and analyze their underlying assumptions and limitations. We further show that the form in which a detection result is expressed constrains which handling strategies are available, and that this correspondence is rarely exploited in practice. A key finding of this study is that current research is limited by weak evaluation practices. In particular, the absence of ground truth, inconsistent definitions, and dependence on aggregate performance metrics lead to circular reasoning and unreliable conclusions. Finally, we outline future research directions toward more robust modeling frameworks and user-centered evaluation protocols, with the aim of establishing a clearer conceptual foundation and guiding the development of more reliable and inclusive recommender systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Understanding event tourism competitiveness: From stakeholder-constructed attributes to visitor valuation
Abstract: This study examines event tourism competitiveness by integrating stakeholder-constructed competitiveness attributes with visitor valuation. Using Hong Kong as the primary empirical context and London as a validation context, the study combines thematic analysis, confirmatory composite analysis (CCA), and a discrete choice experiment (DCE). The thematic analysis identifies six competitiveness dimensions, including Resource Synergies, a novel dimension capturing cross-sector and cross-boundary integration. The DCE results show that Resource Synergies functions as a direct destination selection criterion for MICE participants, whereas its direct effect is not significant among leisure-event visitors. Professionalism and Facilities emerges as a universal competitiveness driver for both groups, while leisure-event visitors prioritise experiential distinctiveness and international content. These findings advance event tourism competitiveness research by explaining how competitiveness attributes are constructed by stakeholders and differentially valued in the event tourism context. Title: AI-driven cultural and creative packaging design and user purchase intention: AI-disclosure perspective based on SEM-ANN hybrid analysis

Abstract: Generative AI has introduced new possibilities for cultural and creative packaging design. Perceived factual disclosure does not significantly moderate the relationships involving functional value or social value. Title: When culture meets citizenship: The moderating role of instructional leadership
Abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of organizational culture and instructional leadership in shaping the organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) of high school teachers, as well as to explain the social mechanisms underlying this relationship. The qualitative stage was carried out through semi structured interviews to deepen and explain the quantitative findings. The results show that organizational culture has a significant effect on teachers' OCB, while instructional leadership has no significant direct or moderating effect. This indicates that cultural factors play a more dominant role than formal leadership practices in influencing teachers’ discretionary behaviors.Qualitative findings explain that teachers' OCB develops as a result of the internalization of collective values, trust, and peer relationships that are deeply rooted in school culture, while instructional leadership is perceived more as an administrative practice than an empowering pedagogical relationship. Title: What drives versus what is required: Sufficient and necessary conditions for consumer intention in an unfamiliar wellness service
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Despite the growing importance of wellness and health tourism, little is known about how individuals who have never experienced thermal spa treatments form intentions toward such services. This study addresses this gap by mobilizing an extended Theory of Planned Behavior framework enriched with subjective knowledge and expected health benefits. Based on a large-scale survey of French non-users, we combine Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling and Necessary Condition Analysis to examine both enabling and constraining mechanisms of intention formation. The results show that all predictors contribute positively to intention, with subjective norm emerging as the most influential factor. However, the necessity analysis reveals a markedly different causal structure: only subjective norm, expected health benefits, and perceived behavioral control establish threshold conditions that must be satisfied for higher levels of intention to occur. In contrast, subjective knowledge and attitude, although significant, do not operate as indispensable conditions. These findings reveal an asymmetry between the factors that raise intention and those that set the threshold for it. They suggest that, in this context, intention depends on socially mediated validation, not on individual evaluation alone. Title: How does empowering leadership shape employee service innovation behavior? The roles of employee adaptability and job crafting

Title: Self-awareness and negotiations
Abstract: How does directing attention toward oneself, or self-awareness, affect one's performance in a negotiation? This article reviews recent research on self-awareness and discusses the implications of these findings for a negotiator's actions before, during, and after a negotiation. Before a negotiation, self-awareness may affect one's choice to negotiate in the first place, one's planned strategy, and one's preparedness to manage difficulties. During a negotiation, self-awareness may affect one's ability to adapt one's tactics and make ethical choices, and outward expressions of self-awareness may affect one's counterpart's perceptions of oneself. After a negotiation, self-awareness may affect one's self-reflection and ability to improve. Title: When does inconsistency help? The nonlinear effect of AI summary-rating inconsistency on consumer purchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As generative AI becomes increasingly embedded in e-commerce platforms, AI-generated review summaries have emerged as an important information source for consumers. A growing concern is AI summary-rating inconsistency, defined as the degree to which the evaluative valence conveyed by an AI-generated review summary diverges from the aggregate product rating displayed on the same product page. However, prior research has paid limited attention to this specific form of cross-format evaluative cue conflict. This research investigates the nonlinear relationship between AI summary-rating inconsistency and consumer purchase intention and the psychological processes underlying this relationship. Using a mixed-method design, Study 1 analyzes 2654 product observations from Newegg and provides association-based marketplace evidence using nonlinear regression. Study 2 employs a 3 (AI summary-rating inconsistency: low vs. medium vs. high) × 2 (RIR feedback cue: high approval vs. high disapproval) between-subjects experiment to examine perceived trust in AI and cognitive load, as well as the moderating role of RIR. The findings show an inverted U-shaped pattern: moderate inconsistency is more persuasive than either low or high inconsistency. Perceived trust in AI and cognitive load operate as two parallel psychological processes, with trust transmitting a positive pathway and cognitive load transmitting a negative pathway. In addition, RIR serves as an important boundary condition by strengthening the trust pathway and weakening the cognitive-load pathway when summary-level user feedback is favorable. Title: Clouds and crowds: A meta-analysis of air pollution and tourism demand-experience dynamics
Abstract: Empirical evidence on how air quality shapes tourist responses remains inconsistent. Drawing on a meta-analytical framework and cognitive-relational theory, this study synthesizes the effects of air pollution on demand- and experience-related outcomes across the travel process. The analysis pools 974 estimates from 58 demand studies and 92 estimates from 8 experience studies on destination-side pollution, as well as 483 estimates from 17 demand studies on origin-side pollution. After correcting for publication bias, air pollution has a mild, partly remediable adverse effect on tourism demand, while evidence for tourist experience is less consistent. The demand effect remains robust across destination-only and origin-destination settings, whereas origin-side air pollution has a negligible, statistically insignificant positive effect. Meta-regression results indicate that between-study heterogeneity is mainly driven by international tourism contexts, online word-of-mouth measures, PM2.5 or air quality index measures, and long-run effects. Title: Home economics and sustainable futures: A systematic literature review
Abstract: This study aims to systematically examine the development, thematic structure, and research trends in Home Economics from 2015 to 2024, with an emphasis on its contribution to a sustainable future. Through the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach with Scopus indexed article data sources, a total of 22 articles were analyzed using a combination of thematic synthesis methods and bibliometric visualization through the VOSviewer tool to identify developing research patterns, relationships, and clusters. The results of the analysis show that Home Economics research has shifted its focus from traditional discussions of household skills to a multidisciplinary approach that emphasizes sustainable education, family economic literacy, health, and social responsibility. The keyword mapping process uncovered to have five major clusters—education, sustainability, health, students, and digital literacy—that intersect to have within the broader framework of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD). Quantitatively, publication trends show a significant increase over the past three years (2021–2024), reflecting to have the increasing global interest in issues concerning welfare and sustainability in the field of education. The main findings also suggest that Home Economics is increasingly being positioned as a transformative discipline that integrates economic literacy, environmental awareness and social responsibility. Theoretically, the results of this study expand the framework of Home Economics as a humanistic and ecological science, while practically, the implications confirm the need for contextual, collaborative, and project-based curriculum and pedagogy innovations to address the challenges of the 21st century. These implications are important for curriculum developers, educators, and policymakers in integrating sustainability values into the education system. Title: CO₂ emission modeling and synthetic fuel energy recovery for hydrogen-integrated sustainable fuel systems
Abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions pose a major challenge to sustainable fuel and energy transitions; however, when accurately predicted and reutilized, CO₂ can become a viable feedstock for synthetic and hydrogen-compatible fuels. This study presents an AI-driven framework for predictive CO₂ emission modeling, explainable decision support, and synthetic fuel energy recovery tailored to sustainable fuel infrastructures. A Random Forest Regressor, configured as reported in Section 3 and trained on an agri-food environmental dataset, achieved R2 = 0.9808, RMSE = 33,023.39, and MAPE = 0.1883 on the held-out test partition. LIME and SHAP provide local and global explanations of the model predictions. Beyond forecasting, the framework comprises three coordinated modules: (i) a CO₂ Utilization Energy Management Hub that translates predicted emissions into theoretical synthetic-fuel energy potentials (MWh); (ii) a DiCE-based counterfactual module that identifies model-consistent emission-reduction scenarios; and (iii) a rule-based decision module that maps sensor readings and predicted emissions to IoT-enabled mitigation actions. The case studies illustrate forecasting, counterfactual analysis, and standardized fuel-energy recovery estimates. Title: AI for guilt, human for encouragement? The interaction effects of creator type and emotional appeal on green purchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Green advertising inherently embeds emotional appeal to drive consumer responses. The proliferation of generative AI has shifted the creator from solely human-dominated to a hybrid landscape where AI-generated and human-generated coexist. Drawing on schema theory and attribution theory, this study investigates the interaction effects between creator type (AI-generated vs. human-generated) and emotional appeal (guilt vs. encouragement) in green advertising on consumers' green purchase intention. Three experiments, including two scenario-based lab experiments (one with a Chinese sample and one with an international English-speaking online sample) and a field experiment with actual purchase data from a live-streaming retailer, provide consistent support for our hypotheses. The results reveal that AI-generated guilt appeal elicits higher consumers’ green purchase intention than the human-generated one, mediated by reduced green moral pressure (a burden-alleviating pathway); conversely, human-generated encouragement appeal elicits higher purchase intention than the AI-generated one, mediated by green self-efficacy (a capacity-enhancing pathway). Furthermore, attribution focus moderates these interaction effects: behavioral attribution strengthens the advantage of AI-generated guilt appeal, whereas personal attribution strengthens the advantage of human-generated encouragement appeal. These findings move beyond the adversarial AI versus human comparison by demonstrating an interaction between disclosed creator type and emotional appeal in green advertising. The framework contributes to green advertising literature by integrating creator type and emotional appeal through an interaction logic, advancing schema theory and attribution theory in the green marketing context. The findings also provide actionable guidance for retailers on strategically collaborating AI and human in green advertising creation to maximize persuasive effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The impact of AI-based information system integration embedded with ESG considerations on perceived overall organizational performance
Abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI)-based information system integration, conceptualized as a perceived integration capability embedded in organizational workflows, is associated with perceived overall organizational performance. It focuses on the mediating roles of dynamic capability activities, employee AI action readiness, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices, defined as routinized monitoring, disclosure, and governance activities. Title: What you see is (not) what you got: The human factor in PDF signature verification
Abstract: Signed PDF documents have legally binding value under frameworks such as the EU's eIDAS regulation. Title: “Made in heaven, matched by parents”: Can arranged marriage restrict labour market autonomy and participation of women?
Abstract: This paper investigates whether parent-arranged marriage causally reduces women's post-marriage labour market autonomy and participation. We conceptualize and separately estimate two distinct dimensions of women's labour market engagement: autonomy (the power to decide whether to work) and participation (the actual decision to work), a distinction overlooked in the existing literature. Relative to parent-arranged marriages, self-matched marriages causally increase labour market autonomy by 30 percentage points and participation by 14–16 percentage points; jointly-arranged marriages yield gains of 22 and 10–11 percentage points, respectively. These effects are large, given that only 42% of women in our sample report autonomy over work decisions. Heterogeneity analysis suggests that the pronounced asymmetry between autonomy and participation arises from structural barriers rather than women's preferences. Title: MLOps for enterprise AI: A systematic literature review of frameworks, interpretability practices, and organisational readiness

Title: Pet-friendliness in hospitality and tourism: Definition, scope, and governance
Abstract: Pet-friendliness is a widely used hospitality label, yet it remains poorly defined and inconsistently specified. This paper clarifies what pet-friendly tourism means and how its scope is delimited within hospitality and tourism. Drawing on a systematic literature review and evidence from a global mixed-method survey, it shows that pet-friendliness extends beyond unrestricted pet access or isolated amenities and operates as a governance-mediated form of conditional inclusion supported by clear rules, appropriate infrastructure, staff practices, welfare, hygiene, safety, and coexistence management. Respondents converge on a stable core meaning, with variation arising primarily around tolerance for partial or restrictive arrangements. The findings provide an operational definition that can guide more comparable hospitality research, policy development, and managerial decision-making. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Liu X.; Geng Y.; Liu Y.; Ye Q.
Title: When more becomes less: Cumulative eWOM volume and automobile sales
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Consumers increasingly rely on electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) when purchasing high-involvement products, yet whether an expanding stock of accumulated reviews continues to benefit product performance remains unclear. This study investigates the relationship between cumulative eWOM volume and automobile sales using a panel dataset from the Chinese automobile market covering 2013 to 2025. Contrary to the conventional view that more reviews are always beneficial, we find that cumulative eWOM volume is negatively associated with subsequent automobile sales. A 1% increase in cumulative eWOM volume is associated with approximately a 0.206% decrease in automobile sales. This negative association is stronger when accumulated ratings exhibit greater heterogeneity, measured by both cumulative rating variance and entropy, providing evidence consistent with an information overload explanation. In addition, greater cumulative eWOM volume is associated with fewer newly generated reviews, which partially mediates its negative association with automobile sales. The negative association is weaker when cumulative eWOM ratings are higher, when a larger proportion of cumulative reviews is recent, and for higher-priced automobiles. Additional analyses show that the association persists when recent reviews are excluded from the cumulative measure, across automobile age groups and sample periods, and is stronger for domestic and conventional vehicles. These findings extend the eWOM research by showing that the value of accumulated reviews depends not only on their availability but also on their composition and processing demands. The findings also suggest that manufacturers and platforms should encourage recent reviews and emphasize recent evaluations and aggregate ratings in review presentation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Hart E.
Title: Post-negotiation behavior and attitudes: We have a deal, now what?
Abstract: Negotiators often equate “winning” with securing favorable agreement terms, yet the agreement is only one outcome of the negotiation process—and may not be the most important, particularly when interactions continue after the deal. This review broadens the lens to encompass post-negotiation outcomes, including emotions, satisfaction, relational perceptions, contract implementation, and subsequent behaviors. Considering a wider range of outcomes deepens understanding of the costs and benefits of negotiation, and can shed light on negotiation initiation and strategy. Integrating post-negotiation behavior also reveals when and why economic and relational motives collide. By treating agreements as the beginning, rather than the endpoint of negotiation, individuals can better align economic and relational objectives and ultimately maximize value beyond the bargaining table. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Ag-doped ZnTi-LDH-derived ZnO/TiO2 heterojunctions promote charge separation to achieve highly efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production
Source title: Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry
Abstract: To achieve high-efficiency photocatalytic H2O2 production, it is essential to modulate the charge-carrier lifetime of the photocatalyst. Herein, a series of xAg-ZnO/TiO2 (x = 0, 20, 30, 40 mg AgNO3) materials are synthesized by pyrolysing Ag-doped ZnTi-LDH. Among these, compared with pristine ZnTi-LDH, the 30Ag-ZnO/TiO2 sample shows a 113.7-fold higher photocatalytic H2O2 generation rate, reaching 4.6 mmol g−1 h−1. Meanwhile, Ag-ZnO/TiO2 retains the two-dimensional morphology of ZnTi-LDH, and a 9.8-fold increase in specific surface area is observed for 30Ag-ZnO/TiO2 relative to pristine ZnTi-LDH. The presence of Ag optimises charge distribution and introduces impurity levels near the Fermi level, narrowing the bandgap. Concurrently, the ZnO/TiO2 heterojunction further accelerates carrier separation and migration, enabling highly efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production. Furthermore, the photocatalytic mechanism of two-step single-electron ORR (O2 → •O2− → H2O2) is confirmed via XPS, EPR and DFT. This research can act as a reference for the fabrication of heterojunctions through metal doping and in-situ derivation, as well as practical guidance for the green synthesis of H2O2. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Whose story do we live? Experiential authorship threat in AI-mediated hospitality journeys and its consequences for meaning, memory, and engagement
Abstract: AI now functions as hospitality's concierge, curating itineraries, wellness plans, and trip narratives at scale. While such systems boost efficiency and personalisation, they raise a symbolic concern central to hospitality: when algorithms pre-write the journey, do guests still feel like the authors of their own experiences? This research introduces and validates Experiential Authorship Threat (EAT), defined as the perceived loss of agency, ownership, and self-authored meaning when AI curation displaces the guest's narrative role. Across six studies (scenario-based, embedded-field, and interface experiments; total n = 2073), AI (vs. human) curation elevates EAT, especially under rigid itineraries (Study 1), and EAT, rather than adjacent constructs, drives symbolic and behavioural disengagement through diminished psychological ownership, particularly among guests high in narrative identity (Study 2). Framing AI as a co-creator rather than a curator, and offering editable rather than pre-filled itineraries, restores autonomy and authorship and improves engagement and satisfaction (Studies 3 and 4). The cost of EAT is greatest for symbolic, identity-relevant trips and high-identity-salience guests (Study 5) and persists in impoverished post-trip memory (Study 6). Theoretically, the research integrates self-determination, narrative identity, and meaning-maintenance perspectives to position EAT as a distinct psychological mechanism in hospitality. For managers, preserving guest authorship through framing, interface design, and symbolic sensitivity emerges as a design priority alongside accuracy and speed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
