Title: The complex role of perspective taking in negotiations
Abstract: To reach an agreement, successful negotiators typically need to understand two things: what they themselves are willing to accept, and what the other side is willing to accept. Understanding the other party's threshold requires perspective taking. In negotiations over goods or services, these judgments shape perceptions of the bargaining zone: the range of outcomes both parties would prefer to walking away without an agreement. The present paper examines how negotiators form perceptions of the bargaining zone. These perceptions have important downstream consequences, influencing everything from the offers negotiators make to the agreements they reach. We review work on how negotiators form perceptions of what their counterpart is willing to accept. Perspective taking can help negotiators estimate the lowest price a seller would accept or the highest price a buyer would pay. However, it can also lead negotiators to erroneously internalize the other party's perspective as if it is relevant to their own valuation. As an example, we demonstrate that buyers are willing to pay more for the same good when the seller gives up an entire endowment rather than only part of it, although the seller's end state should not affect buyer's willingness to pay for the good. These findings show how taking the other party's perspective can shape valuations, fairness judgments and negotiations outcomes. We conclude by discussing implications for multi-issue bargaining and strategic framing, highlighting how psychological heuristics and social context interact to shape outcomes in complex real-world situations, such as salary negotiations and real estate transactions. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Selecting a project-delivery structure for Indonesia's first nuclear power plant: an expert AHP-weighted anchored-rating analysis of the bankability–strategic-control trade-off
Abstract: Indonesia's energy policy and supply plan include nuclear generation, shifting attention from adoption to delivery. This study evaluates five case-anchored delivery configurations against 14 criteria covering ownership, contractual risk allocation, strategic national value, and financing feasibility, using a hybrid AHP-weighted anchored-rating model: 19 purposively selected Indonesian experts derived criterion weights by pairwise comparison and rated each configuration on an anchored nine-point scale; each respondent's weights and ratings were combined before aggregation. All 95 pairwise matrices met CR ≤ 0.10 under software-enforced consistency requirements, whereas agreement on dimension priorities was weak (Kendall's W = 0.187). Within this panel and under the administered profiles, a host-majority public–vendor joint venture scored highest (0.710), ahead of a state-utility configuration (0.638); its margin arose from perceived bankability, construction-risk allocation, and funding access, not from strategic national value, the largest-weighted dimension (34.4%). Priority heterogeneity alone reversed the group choice for no respondent; assessment heterogeneity reversed it for five. A1 led in over 98% of resampling and weight-variation draws, but the lead reversed when its seven contracting and financing ratings were lowered together by more than about 1.2 points. Newcomer delivery choices should weigh the risk bearer's control rights, exposure, and loss-absorption capacity, not nominal allocation alone. Title: How Sociodemographic Factors Shape Community Well-Being in Sustainable Tourism Destinations
Abstract: Tourism significantly contributes to the livelihoods of host communities, influencing their social, environmental, and economic development. However, residents’ diverse demographics and attitudes often shape their perceptions of tourism, affecting the level of support or opposition within these communities. Such demographic factors may influence how individuals perceive tourism’s benefits and drawbacks, leading to regional variations in engagement. This study examined the relationship between sociodemographic factors, New Silk Road (NSR) infrastructure, community well-being, and tourism sustainability in destination areas. Specifically, it analysed correlations among NSR infrastructure, demographic variables, tourism impact (TI), quality of life (QOL), place image (PI), and support for tourism development (STD). The findings indicated that 24 of 28 relationships between variables were statistically significant, demonstrating strong associations. Title: Too much of a good thing? The curvilinear effects of job clarity on career satisfaction and creativity among hospitality employees
Abstract: This study challenges the assumption that greater job clarity always benefits service employees. Drawing on self-determination theory and the Too-Much-of-a-Good-Thing framework, we test a moderated curvilinear mediation model linking job clarity, career satisfaction, and creativity, with career calling as a boundary condition. Using three-wave, multi-source data from 164 supervisor–employee dyads in Chinese hotels, results reveal inverted U-shaped relationships between job clarity and both career satisfaction and supervisor-rated creativity. Career satisfaction mediates this curvilinear effect. Moreover, career calling amplifies the curvature—employees high in calling gain greater motivational and creative benefits as clarity increases but experience sharper losses at very high clarity levels. These findings position job clarity as a dynamic and context-dependent resource, offering theoretical and managerial insights for fostering creativity and well-being among hospitality employees. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Attention-boosted DistilBERT and Bi-GRU for cyber-attacks detection in electric vehicle charging networks
Abstract: The global transition to the Electric Vehicles (EVs) represents a major change of the transportation and energy industry, which is driven by a breakthrough in battery technology, positive government policies, and increased consumer demand. As the use of electric cars is becoming more accepted, it is necessary to implement Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) in the power grid to support the ecosystem. The interconnectivity, in its turn, makes the grid and EVSE infrastructure vulnerable to a variety of cybersecurity threats. The availability, dependability, and security of electric vehicle charging networks may be compromised by the vulnerabilities such as Denial of Service (DoS), Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, data manipulation, and malware threats. These attacks can disrupt power charging processes, cause financial damages, cause bodily injuries, or even destabilise the power systems. This paper introduces a hybrid architecture comprising of deep contextual proficiency of DistilBERT, the sequential modelling efficacy of Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Units (Bi-GRU) and an attention mechanism to detect cyber-attacks on Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) systems. The model is tested on CICEVSE2024 dataset, a high-rate collection of power consumption and network traffic data, which is based upon benign and harmful contexts. The results show that the classification accuracy is 94 percent, precision is 98 percent, recall stands at 95 percent, and F1-score is 96 percent, thus validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying the occurrence of cyber-attacks in complex and real-life contexts. The study highlights the potential of AI-assisted methods of real-time cybersecurity monitoring in the framework of electric vehicle grid integration, which is steadily advancing, and explains the need to implement resilient and scaleable solutions to mitigate the increasing cyber threats. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: FDI spillovers in history: Interwar Japanese “Zaikabo” investment in China's cotton spinning industry
Abstract: We estimate productivity spillovers from Japanese cotton-spinning firms in China (known as Zaikabo,"在華紡") to local Chinese cotton-spinning mills based on plant-level data for 1925 to 1938. In order to capture the important role of distance in facilitating such spillovers we geo-localised the plants. Our results provide clear evidence for positive spillovers from Zaikabo to local Chinese mills, which go hand-in-hand with an upgrade in production technology towards greater use of capital. Spillovers are very localised, being strongest within a radius of up to 10 km around the Zaikabo and particularly strong for mills in Shanghai. Exploiting information on the workforce composition of the Japanese affiliates, we find suggestive evidence of a skilled-labour channel: spillovers tend to be larger from Zaikabo employing higher shares of skilled labour. We also find some evidence in line with the idea that these gains are larger for Chinese mills with higher initial productivity, consistent with a role for absorptive capacity. Our paper is the first to document FDI productivity spillovers in a historical context and to characterise the channels through which they operate. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Hierarchical DEMATEL-based key risk identification for urban public safety within grid management
Abstract: With the acceleration of urbanization, urban public safety risks have exhibited characteristics of diversification, complexity, and linkage. Based on the grid-based governance concept of “comprehensive horizontal coverage and hierarchical vertical stratification” and combined with the hierarchical DEMATEL method, this paper constructs an urban public safety Grid Risk System for Urban Public Safety (GRSFUPS) and a risk analysis framework. GRSFUPS takes grids as the minimum governance units and progressively refines four types of A-level risks—natural disasters, public health, social security, and accident disasters—into B-level and C-level risks, forming a complex system with clear hierarchies and close linkages. Subsequently, using Kunming as a case study, a case application study was conducted on its critical public safety risks. Combined with centrality ranking and the Pareto principle, 55 critical risk factors were identified from 258 risk factors. Research results indicate that public health incidents and accident disaster risks occupy a dominant position in Kunming City, while natural disaster risks such as meteorological and flood hazards repeatedly appear across multiple districts and exhibit significant amplification effects. Theoretically, this paper enriches the urban public safety risk identification framework from a grid-based perspective. Practically, it provides a new analytical paradigm and methodological support for Kunming City and other similar cities to conduct risk governance under grid-based management models. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Large language models in software project management: A two-phase systematic literature review
Abstract: Background: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into Software Engineering (SE) processes and practices. However, their application within Software Project Management (SPM) remains fragmented and insufficiently synthesized. This absence of systematic evidence prevents both researchers and practitioners from understanding where LLMs can meaningfully contribute to project management processes in relation to established standards such as the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK). Objectives: This study aims to systematically synthesize existing evidence on the application and integration of LLMs in SPM by means of a two-phase method where Phase I systematically searches for existing secondary studies in the topic of interest, and Phase II (whenever applicable) carries out an SLR in the topic of interest. Method: We conducted a two-phase method: Phase I is a tertiary study that used 14 research questions to assess the existence, coverage, and quality of prior secondary studies in LLMs applied to SPM. As no suitable SLR was identified from Phase I, we also conducted Phase II, which employed the SEGRESS guidelines to analyze primary studies that empirically evaluated the use of LLMs in SPM via five research questions. Phase II also assessed coverage across PMBOK processes and synthesized reported mechanisms, outcomes, research designs and evaluation approaches. Results: The SLR (Phase II) shows that studies employ encoder-only and decoder-only LLM architectures in equal proportion (17 studies each). Their applications focus on a narrow set of SPM tasks, including effort estimation, project planning, and requirements-related activities. Coverage across PMBOK processes is uneven, with limited attention to areas such as procurement, stakeholder, quality, and cost management. Most studies rely on proof-of-concept evaluations, with scarce industrial validation and heterogeneous evaluation metrics. Conclusion: The results indicate that current research on LLMs in SPM provides limited guidance for systematic adoption. Title: RARSGAN: An End-to-End Intelligent Generative Framework for Regime-Faithful and Risk-Aware Electricity-Market Scenario Generation
Abstract: Electricity-market scenario generation is most difficult when synthetic paths must preserve not only marginal price behavior but also regime shifts, state-dependent risk, tail pressure, and heterogeneous hub conditions. This paper develops RARSGAN, an integrated end-to-end regime-faithful and risk-aware framework for forward hub-level electricity-market scenario generation. The framework transforms trading records into structured market states, dynamically validates latent regimes through a Student-t Markov layer, constructs a multi-component risk state, recursively simulates future regime-risk conditioning sequences using only information available at the simulation origin, and generates synthetic market-state paths through a conditional TimeGAN-based architecture. The method provides finite-sample structural-error bounds linking fitted risk, regime-occupancy, and transition discrepancies to the structures it is designed to preserve. Evaluation follows a locked chronological train-validation-test protocol with repeated runs and compares the generated paths with held-out observations through mechanism-aligned structural metrics, independent path-level diagnostics, synchronized cross-hub dependence tests, and downstream procurement-risk measures. The results show that joint regime-risk conditioning provides the most balanced mean preservation across the model’s primary structural objectives, while the supplementary tests identify important remaining limitations in real-synthetic distinguishability, simultaneous multi-hub stress, and tail-loss calibration. RARSGAN therefore offers a transparent framework for generating, stress-testing, and evaluating forward electricity-market scenarios without conflating improved structural balance with universal statistical or economic dominance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Forecast-guided multi-task scheduling for autonomous electric ride-hailing fleets under charging and maintenance constraints
Abstract: Autonomous electric ride-hailing fleets require real-time coordination among passenger dispatching, proactive repositioning, charging, and maintenance. A residual-based search mechanism reduces the computational burden introduced by graph expansion. Experiments using real-world ride-hailing data show that the proposed framework achieves a system matching rate of 79.76%, which is 5.52 percentage points higher than the classical Kuhn-Munkres matching baseline. It reduces average passenger waiting time to 6.68 min, corresponding to a 14.41% reduction compared with the non-predictive scheduling variant. It also improves spatial supply-demand balance, reducing the normalized demand-supply difference to 0.128, and completes each rolling scheduling decision within 1.42 s on average. The incremental ablation study further shows that virtual-node-based forecast conversion mainly improves service quality and spatial balance, while the residual-based search mechanism reduces computation time from 22.45 s to 1.42 s without observed degradation. Title: More alike than unalike: Contextually aligned authority arguments amplify sustainable choices across cultures
Abstract: Most research is conducted in Western societies, with few studies from Latin America. Title: When regulatory-focus language matches the product category: A within-person computational analysis of reviews from an online retail platform

Abstract: Online review platforms use helpfulness votes and related signals to rank and solicit reviews. Title: Exploring Technology Probe applications in software engineering practice
Abstract: Background: The development of software systems relies on user feedback, which can be captured with Validation Sessions (VS); however, VS are often conducted in an ad hoc manner. Technology Probe (TP) offers a participatory design method for capturing user perception; however, its application in software engineering lacks structure. Aim: This study consolidates evidence on TP applications in software engineering and identifies practices that support the systematic use of TP. Methods: A Literature Study, inspired by Rapid Reviews, was conducted in Scopus using backward and forward snowballing, screening 530 studies and selecting 53 primary works across the trials that support the results. Thematic analysis was employed to extract motivations, outcomes, and challenges associated with the use of TP in software engineering. Results: Through thematic analysis and open coding, 11 evidence-based characteristics were identified describing the use of TP in software engineering. These characteristics formed the foundation of an evidence-based checklist developed to assess and guide the development of TP techniques. Conclusion: It was found that TP has been applied across a variety of domains, with diverse techniques being crafted. Therefore, the checklist developed in this research aims to assist future researchers in crafting their techniques and supporting their decisions. © 2026 The Authors

Title: When AI meets DEI: Employee AI-beliefs and their implications for workplace diversity, equity, and inclusion
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes the workplace, its impact on diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) has been examined primarily through the lens of what AI actually does (i.e., system design, outputs). This review shifts the focus to humans' subjective beliefs about AI, identifying mechanisms through which three dimensions of AI-beliefs (competence, warmth, and morality) may affect DEI goals: improving representation of underrepresented groups, closing career gaps across groups, and fostering inclusion. Our synthesis shows that, independently of what AI does, AI-beliefs can disadvantage underrepresented groups in some contexts, while creating opportunities for bridging human subgroups in others. Authors: Mittal S.; Jha K.N.
Title: Emotional Factors in Quality Negligence: A Study of Residential Real Estate Construction Professionals
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Quality negligence in the construction industry, a significant originator of legal crises, is predominantly attributed to technical and procedural failures. However, the pivotal role of construction professionals' emotions as a precipitating factor remains a critically unexamined research area. This study addresses this gap by investigating the influence of specific emotions on quality negligence and its subsequent escalation into legal crises for construction firms. The research employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. Initially, a comprehensive literature review and unstructured interviews with industry experts identified seven prominent emotions (anxiety, guilt, pride, shame, elevation, injustice, and gratitude). Subsequently, a quantitative phase involved distributing a self-administered questionnaire to 162 Indian construction professionals within the Indian residential construction sector to assess their emotional states and quality negligence levels. Data analysis using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) indicated a statistically significant positive relationship between quality negligence and five emotions. The effects, in descending order of magnitude, were elevation (β=0.406, p<0.001), shame (β=0.405, p<0.001), gratitude (β=0.321, p<0.001), pride (β=0.261, p=0.009), and anxiety (β=0.179, p=0.047). In the final phase, consultations and brainstorming sessions with industry experts were used to identify the resulting legal crises and to establish a novel emotion-quality negligence-crises framework. This framework models the pathway from emotional antecedent to quality negligence and its culmination in a legal crisis. The study provides a critical diagnostic tool for practitioners in the real estate sector to mitigate risk and offers a new theoretical model for academics analyzing this psycho-legal connection.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Li Q.; Chen H.; Lin Y.
Title: Trust begins at home: The role of psychological distance in trust transfer for emerging technology
Abstract: The widespread adoption of emerging technologies holds substantial potential to benefit societal development. However, fostering public trust and acceptance of emerging technologies, which involve complex underlying principles and are in pre-commercialization stages, remains a critical multifaceted challenge. To address this issue, this study draws on trust transfer theory to identify an effective mechanism for enhancing people's trust in emerging technologies. Specifically, we propose and test that trust in emerging technologies can be transferred from that in familiar institutions of the public by reducing psychological distance to such technologies. Analyzing quota-sampling data, we find that greater consumption of news about local brain–computer interface (BCI) achievements was associated with greater trust in local technology institutions. Institutional process and purpose trust were, in turn, associated with lower psychological distance to BCI, which was associated with greater general trust in BCI and, subsequently, stronger BCI use intention. The corresponding pathway was not supported for performance trust. These findings extend trust transfer theory by introducing psychological distance as a vital mechanism. Practically, this study demonstrates a route through which practitioners can promote public acceptance of unfamiliar and emerging technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Risk propagation and vulnerability in the global industrial robot trade network: A cascading failure model with adaptive resilience
Abstract: Industrial robots underpin intelligent manufacturing and high-end equipment systems, and the stability of their global trade network is directly related to the continuity of international manufacturing specialization. Existing studies mainly focus on structural evolution and centrality features, while offering insufficient explanation of how risk shocks diffuse along trade relations, why core-node failure triggers cascading effects, and whether adaptive buffering mechanisms exist. This study examines the global industrial robot trade network from 2000 to 2023 and develops an adaptive cascading failure model integrating local buffering, global risk-control potential, technological-industrial support, trade-relationship stability, and supply reallocation. Because trade data cannot separate domestic production, processing trade, and re-exports, the propagation results describe network vulnerability and scenario-based trade vulnerability. The results show that network expansion and densification have generated more complex risk transmission paths; simulated risk diffusion is not determined solely by trade scale but by structural position, accumulated import gaps, and substitution absorption capacity; and adaptive supply reallocation can reduce simulated infection scale in some scenarios but cannot fully eliminate cascading risks caused by core-hub failures. Title: Evolution and lifecycle mapping of research methods based on the Boston Matrix in library and information science from 1995 to 2025
Abstract: Developing an evolution framework for research methods is essential for advancing Library and Information Science (LIS), but existing research method schemas remain fragmented and limited. This study proposes an automated framework combining AI-driven methods to mine, classify, and a temporal analysis based on the Boston Matrix to map the lifecycles of research methods. Using a comprehensive dataset of 31,913 articles from 21 LIS journals (1995–2025) as a validation corpus, the framework integrates semantic clustering for bottom-up entity extraction with generative top-down ontology mapping. This approach dynamically maps methods into a four-stage lifecycle schema: mainstream, emerging, marginalized, and mature, revealing distinct evolutionary trajectories and the broader computational turn within LIS. Validated through quantitative threshold testing and qualitative evaluation, the proposed framework significantly reduces manual coding subjectivity and enhances replicability. By empirically comparing the subfields of librarianship and information science, this study accounts for inherent thematic variations and uncovers their distinct paces of methodological adoption. Ultimately, this study offers a robust automated framework for longitudinal methodological tracking, theoretically demonstrating how diverse AI-driven and traditional methods synergistically coevolve and assume distinct scholarly roles within the emerging AI4Science paradigm. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Pan G.; Wang J.; Liu H.
Title: Crowding and green choice: Understanding a U-shaped relationship in China's organic food market
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Organic food represents a product category in which safety-and-health attributes and environmental attributes are both salient, making it an appropriate context for examining how retail situations shape sustainable consumption. This study investigates the nonlinear effect of shopping crowding on organic food purchase behavior and purchase intention, and further examines whether different crowding levels activate different organic food attribute cues. First, transaction records from a large supermarket chain in China provide associational evidence of a statistically supported U-shaped relationship between shopping crowding and organic food purchase behavior, with the turning point located in the upper portion of the observed crowding distribution and modest changes in predicted purchase probability. Second, a randomized scenario experiment provides causal evidence for the low–moderate–high nonmonotonic pattern in organic food purchase intention and identifies distinct indirect-effect structures involving positive emotion and perceived loss of control. Third, a 2×2 experiment compares the two crowding endpoints and shows that environmental-responsibility cues are relatively more effective under low crowding, whereas safety-and-health cues are relatively more effective under high crowding. Taken together, the findings extend crowding research and sustainable consumption research by identifying a nonlinear crowding effect, integrating compensatory control theory with consumer emotion theory, and showing how the match between retail situations and product attribute cues shapes organic food choice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: PSG-Net: Physical saliency guided adaptive fusion network for infrared and visible image fusion
Abstract: The core challenge in infrared and visible image fusion lies in achieving a seamless integration where thermal saliency does not overshadow critical texture details. Existing deep learning frameworks, however, often struggle with a fundamental disconnect, the inability to explicitly translate the inherent physical priors of thermal targets into learnable spatial guidance. This frequently leads to saliency-texture trade-offs, where fine visible textures are suppressed within high-thermal regions, compromising image fidelity. To address this challenge, we propose a novel Physical Saliency Guided Adaptive Fusion Network. Our approach begins by systematically analyzing the physical characteristics of high temperature IR targets and translating these properties into network design principles. By effectively coupling the physical saliency prior with learnable feature representations, PSG-Net achieves the synergistic enhancement of salient objects and background details, significantly improving the visual quality, detail fidelity, and application robustness of the fused images, demonstrating excellent performance on the MSRS, M3FD and LLVIP datasets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Emotion-aware retailing: Using biometrics to decode consumer experience in physical–digital environments
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The physical retail space, when blended with digital touchpoints, has created a multi-sensory consumer experience that cannot be fully measured in real time using legacy survey-based approaches. The work examines the opportunities offered by biometric technologies, such as electrodermal activity (EDA), facial action coding, eye-tracking, and heart-rate variability (HRV), to decode shoppers' affective experiences in a phygital retail space. The study is based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and affective computing theory, and has a mixed-methods experimental design that involved 312 study participants, who were offered four types of retail formats: department store, grocery hypermarket, experiential flagship store, and click-and-collect hub. All participants were given biometric sensors to wear and were monitored across three consecutive stages: browsing, assessment, and purchase decision. Behavioral and transactional data were used in real time and fused with multimodal biometric responses to create emotion maps for spatial retail areas. The findings show statistically significant positive relationships among high EDA arousal, positive facial affect, and conversion rates at digital interface points. Quantitatively, an optimal engagement window was identified at moderate stimulation levels (EDA = 2.10 μS), yielding a peak conversion rate of 41.2%. In contrast, HRV suppression was associated with decision paralysis at higher stimulation levels. Demographic cohorts and segmentation analysis showed that younger consumers reacted with much more emotion to augmented reality features and individualized digital signs. Eye-tracking and facial action coding confirmed that younger shoppers (<35) sustained an 8.42-s fixation duration with high positive affect (0.74) in flagship zones, whereas older cohorts (≥35) exhibited severe sensory avoidance. The article contributes to the theoretical understanding of emotion-behavior relationships in the store setting and offers practical guidance for store designers, digital experience architects, and consumer psychologists. Embargoes on biometric retail analytics that protect privacy are also discussed. Title: Algorithmic fairness as a human–technology interaction problem
Abstract: Algorithms shape high-stakes decisions across society. While promising efficiency, algorithms also raise fairness concerns. This article proposes that algorithmic fairness is best understood as a human–technology interaction problem rather than a purely technical challenge. Algorithms can reproduce human biases, amplify them through feedback loops, or create new forms of unfairness through objectives, proxies, and seemingly neutral variables. Yet they can make decision processes more explicit, disparities more visible, and actively mitigate discrimination. Fairness depends not only on statistical properties but also on how algorithms are designed, used and experienced by those affected by their decisions. Title: When do hedonic appeals backfire? Credibility, scepticism and the disconnect between emotional engagement and pro-environmental intention

Title: Incremental railway infrastructure detection via prototype-guided proposal refinement and frequency-based prompts from noisy-annotated UAV imagery
Abstract: Railway infrastructure incremental object detection (IOD) aims to generalize to new classes while retaining previously learned knowledge, requiring the model to balance stability and plasticity. Despite their effectiveness, the existing methods are limited in the following ways. On the one hand, they overlook the class ambiguity induced by fine-grained infrastructure structures. On the other hand, they underestimate the spatial ambiguity caused by noisy annotations. Furthermore, they ignore the knowledge corruption caused by spatial imitation in IOD tasks, which limits the discriminative knowledge transferred across tasks. To address the above issues, a robust IOD framework is proposed to enhance semantic discrimination and knowledge retention by integrating prototype-guided proposal refinement and frequency-based prompts. The prototype-guided proposal refinement consists of distribution-aware prototype and adaptive proposal refinement, which respectively model distinguishable infrastructure prototypes and perform iterative localization refinement. Specifically, the distribution-aware prototype constructs distinguishable infrastructure prototypes that serve as the stable class representations for proposal refinement. Moreover, frequency-based prompts are proposed to preserve discriminative representations between the current and previous IOD tasks, which are optimized only after each incremental task and kept frozen during task training so that they serve as stable knowledge carriers. Comprehensive experiments on real-world railway infrastructure datasets validate the superiority of the proposed framework over state-of-the-art baselines. Title: The role of psychological factors on the mathematics achievement among alternative learning students in the Philippine context
Abstract: This study examined the role of key psychological factors such as self-efficacy, self-regulation, and time management in explaining the mathematics achievement among students enrolled in an alternative learning system (ALS) at selected public high schools in the school districts of Cebu, Philippines. Title: Reframing artificial intelligence as an observable market signal: Extending Signaling Theory in luxury fashion retail
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming luxury fashion retail; however, existing research primarily views AI as an operational technology that enhances efficiency and personalization. Less attention has been given to how consumers interpret AI-enabled marketing applications as signals of luxury brand meaning. The exploratory segmentation identifies three consumer profiles with different signaling perceptions, while sentiment analysis reveals generally positive evaluations alongside concerns about excessive automation and diminished human interaction. Authors: Zhang A.; Li Z.
Title: Counterfactual Invariant Market Learning for Provincial Potato Price Forecasting in Agricultural Management
Abstract: Potato prices are influenced by recurrent production cycles, storage behaviour, regional circulation, and short-term market disturbances, making their future movements difficult to infer from isolated historical trajectories. This paper develops the Counterfactual Invariant Market Forecaster (CIMF), a forecasting framework that formulates provincial potato price prediction as a mechanism-aware forecasting and model-based counterfactual analysis problem rather than a purely supervised temporal extrapolation task. CIMF first decomposes historical price windows into seasonal anchors and residual shocks, allowing the model to distinguish recurrent potato price rhythms from local abnormal fluctuations. It then learns invariant mechanism representations across heterogeneous environments, including years, seasonal phases, volatility regimes, and regional partitions. Based on these representations, a learned response operator is constructed to describe model-implied cross-provincial associations between residual shocks and future prices. A differentiable counterfactual intervention layer further enables shock removal, amplification, and delay analysis, so that the model can simulate how its forecasts for the future potato price panel change under different local disturbance scenarios. Experiments on weekly potato prices from 25 Chinese provinces during 2012 to 2018 show that CIMF achieves lower MAE, RMSE, and MAPE than CNN, LSTM, N-BEATS, Autoformer, and Informer at both one-step and four-step horizons. Ablation results confirm the contribution of seasonal residualization, invariant mechanism learning, and structural response modelling. These findings suggest that combining invariant mechanism learning with qualified, model-based counterfactual analysis provides a robust and interpretable route for potato price forecasting under heterogeneous market conditions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to European Association for Potato Research 2026.

Title: Psychological vulnerability in conversational AI: How incentive and urgency manipulations alter trust formation and privacy behaviour across healthcare, financial, commercial, and security contexts

Authors: Chen Z.; Ma J.; Tan Z.; You D.
Title: Diffusion-augmented adversarial poisoning in QoS-aware cloud API recommender systems
Abstract: Data poisoning attacks pose a serious security threat to QoS-aware cloud API recommender systems by injecting carefully crafted fake user profiles into training data, thereby manipulating recommendation outcomes and compromising prediction reliability. Existing GAN-based poisoning methods often suffer from discriminator overfitting under limited interaction data, leading to pronounced distributional discrepancies between generated and real users, which significantly degrades both attack effectiveness and stealthiness. To address this limitation, we propose DA-GAN, a Diffusion-Augmented Generative Adversarial Network for poisoning attacks against QoS-aware cloud API recommendation systems. DA-GAN integrates diffusion probabilistic modeling into the adversarial training by constructing multi-step noise-augmented real users through a diffusion forward process, and generating fake users via noise-aligned posterior sampling in the reverse process. To further stabilize training, we design a multi-step noise-aligned discriminator that performs joint discrimination across multiple diffusion levels, providing reliable gradient supervision and effectively mitigating discriminator overfitting in small-sample settings. Extensive experiments on real-world cloud API QoS datasets demonstrate that DA-GAN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art poisoning baselines in both attack effectiveness and stealthiness across multiple mainstream QoS-aware recommender systems. Our findings reveal previously underestimated vulnerabilities in existing cloud API recommender systems and underscore the urgent need for diffusion-aware and attack-resilient defense mechanisms. Title: From smart cities to smart villages: Evolution, domains, and policy implications for smart rural development
Abstract: Smart villages have evolved from early parallels with urban smart city models into a comprehensive, multidimensional framework that integrates digital infrastructure, agriculture, local enterprises, tourism, and sustainability. This expanded framework recognizes the unique characteristics and potentials of rural areas, moving beyond the urban-centric logic of technology adoption. This review aims to examine the conceptual evolution of smart village research, track emerging methodological trends, and analyze global implementation trajectories. In the early stages, many studies concentrated on definitional debates and approaches that were primarily centered on technology. However, more recent perspectives have begun to emphasize the importance of integrating technological innovation with social innovation, community empowerment, participatory governance, and environmental stewardship. Methodological approaches have also advanced significantly, shifting from conceptual reflections and single-case studies toward more diverse methods including comparative studies, bibliometric mapping, and participatory action research. These evolving methods enable a deeper and more nuanced understanding of smart village dynamics. Regional approaches demonstrate distinct emphases: European initiatives focus on service revitalization and smart specialization; Asian and African strategies prioritize connectivity, renewable energy access, and digital inclusion; while Latin American programs increasingly integrate climate-smart agricultural practices. Despite regional differences, common challenges remain, including the persistent rural digital divide, fragmented coordination among multiple stakeholders, issues of financial sustainability, and the emergence of new forms of inequality. Policy directions increasingly stress the importance of place-based strategies, building local capacities, establishing supportive governance structures, and fostering inclusive participation. The review concludes by identifying critical areas for future research, such as the creation of unified evaluation metrics, conducting longitudinal impact assessments, and embedding smart village initiatives within broader rural development and climate resilience agendas. Overall, smart villages represent dynamic and promising pathways for driving innovation-led, inclusive, and sustainable rural transformation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Authors: Hu C.; Zheng J.; Lai N.; Wang Q.; He S.
Title: Can digital-real integration effectively curb urban sprawl? Evidence from China using double/debiased machine learning
Abstract: Urban sprawl (URS) has become a major challenge to China's sustainable development under the backdrop of rapid urbanization. Digital-real integration (DRI) provides a new pathway for urban spatial governance, yet its concrete impacts and mechanisms remain insufficiently tested. Based on panel data from 280 prefecture-level Chinese cities between 2013 and 2023, this study constructs a multidimensional DRI index and employs a partially linear double/debiased machine learning (DML) framework to estimate the effect of DRI on URS. Multiple robustness checks, including complementary instrumental-variable analyses, yield results consistent with the baseline finding. The findings show that a one-unit increase in DRI is associated with a 0.06-unit reduction in the URS index, and this conclusion holds under various robustness tests. The mechanism analysis provides evidence consistent with three potential transmission pathways: industrial structure upgrading, stronger aggregate city-level correspondence between employment opportunities and resident population, and reduced dependence on highway commuting. Further heterogeneity analysis reveals that the restraining effect of DRI is more pronounced in eastern regions, major national urban agglomerations, and cities at more advanced stages of urban development. This study not only provides empirical evidence on how digital technologies reshape urban spatial structures but also offers policy implications for implementing differentiated digital governance strategies and enhancing the effectiveness of spatial planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From design attributes to social life: Modelling conviviality in urban underground spaces
Abstract: From being infrastructure utilities, urban underground spaces (UUS) have developed into multipurpose public spaces that combine commercial, cultural, and transit functions. While their technical and spatial contributions to compact urbanism are evident, their capacity to foster conviviality, the experiential quality of inclusiveness, sociability, and shared belonging, is less understood. This study develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework that operationalizes conviviality in UUS by linking seven spatial-perceptual dimensions (safety and security, identity and meaning, accessibility, functionality, environmental comfort, aesthetics, and structure and form) to behavioral mediators of willingness to use and social interaction, culminating in perceived conviviality. Using the Theatre-Shahr underground complex in Tehran as a case study, data were collected through structured surveys and analyzed via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that although environmental factors generally have a positive indirect effect on perceived conviviality, social interaction emerges as the primary mechanism shaping conviviality in urban underground spaces, while willingness to use plays only a complementary and limited mediating role in this process. Among the environmental factors, accessibility, environmental comfort, and safety and security show the strongest effects. In contrast, some variables, particularly identity and meaning and structure and form, do not demonstrate statistically significant effects in certain pathways. These findings suggest that planning and design strategies for urban underground spaces should prioritize environmental qualities that support social interaction, to enhance perceived conviviality. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Can natural capital accounting bring accountability for nature?
Abstract: With increasing global ecosystem degradation, new ways of governing the relationship between people and nature are needed. As Western societies increasingly turn to the emerging practice of Natural Capital Accounting (NCA), this is a critical time to consider its institutional role. In this paper we consider the effectiveness of NCA in bringing accountability for nature. This study theorises the link between accountability and NCA practice and explores this link empirically through quantitative and qualitative analyses of four methods of practice - the Capitals Coalition, Integrated Reporting, the System of Environmental Economic Accounting – Ecosystem Accounting, and Accounting for Nature®. The study found that NCA methods employ a range of technical mechanisms for delivering accountability, including data processes, external audit, and participation of, and transparency with, stakeholders; however, there were substantial limitations for their effectiveness. Our results highlight five challenges for NCA in delivering accountability for nature, underpinned by the broader governance environment in which this institution operates. We discuss governance options for bringing accountability for nature both with, and without, NCA. The findings of this study will help academics and policy makers to design institutional arrangements which are fit-for-purpose for bringing accountability for nature. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Identification of subgroup causal effects in randomized trials under nonignorable missingness of covariates and outcome variables simultaneously
Abstract: Randomized experiments are widely regarded as the gold standard for causal inference. However, identifying subgroup causal effects becomes particularly challenging when pretreatment covariates and outcome are subject to simultaneous nonignorable missingness. The study investigates the identifiability of subgroup causal effects under five increasingly complex missing data mechanisms, ranging from an ignorable mechanism to nonignorable mechanisms in which missingness depends on different combinations of treatment, covariates, and outcome. Identification is established under several nonignorable mechanisms without imposing restrictive parametric assumptions. For the most challenging mechanism, identification is established under a parametric model with specific assumptions on the outcome distribution and the missingness mechanism. For estimation and inference, a fractional-imputation Expectation-Maximization algorithm is developed to maximize the observed-data likelihood. Simulation studies compare the proposed estimator with complete-case analysis, multiple imputation, and a full-data oracle estimator, demonstrating satisfactory finite-sample performance across the considered missingness mechanisms. The practical utility of the proposed method is further illustrated using data from the Oregon Health Insurance Experiment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Workplace responses to perpetration of family and domestic violence: a global scoping review
Abstract: Introduction Family and domestic violence (FDV), which includes intimate partner and family violence, affects workplace safety through spillover impacts on workers, organisations, and occupational health systems. To date, workplace interventions addressing the issue of FDV have predominantly concentrated on providing support to victim-survivors, while there is limited research regarding employer responses to employees who perpetrate such violence. Method A scoping review was conducted following Arksey and O’Malley’s framework and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines, which examined existing evidence from workplace policies, practices, and organisational mechanisms addressing FDV perpetration by workers. Peer-reviewed studies and high-quality grey literature on workplace responses to perpetration of FDV were systematically searched across multiple databases and online sources, and 28 documents on workplace responses to FDV perpetration were analysed. Results Findings from the scoping review reveal four dominant insights across the literature: 1. Perpetration of FDV is a major workplace problem, yet responses are under-researched; 2. Workplaces employ wide-ranging and varied responses, from zero tolerance dismissal of perpetrators to responsibility avoidance; 3. Responses lack a solid evidence-base and regulatory frameworks to address the problem remain weak; 4. Practical strategies are provided to better manage risk, strengthen safety, and reduce violence. Conclusion Our findings underscore the need for clearer organisational guidance, evidence-based strategies, and robust regulatory frameworks to strengthen workplace responses to FDV perpetration and improve occupational safety outcomes. Practical applications Effective workplace responses to perpetration of FDV should consider work design factors, referral pathways and confidentiality protections which are guided by graduated accountability models and regulatory frameworks. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: The relationship between intolerance of uncertainty and fear of missing out: Evidence from network analysis and a daily diary study
Abstract: Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) and fear of missing out (FoMO) are common psychological vulnerabilities during emerging adulthood, yet their item-level organization and daily temporal associations remain underexplored. Study 1 ( N = 875) used item-level network analysis in an undergraduate sample to examine the conditional association structure of IU and FoMO. Study 2 ( N = 235) used a 14-day diary design and dynamic structural equation modeling to examine their within-person temporal associations at the construct level. In Study 1, IU and FoMO formed two communities with stronger within-community than cross-community connections. In Study 2, both constructs showed autoregressive continuity and positive bidirectional cross-lagged associations. Higher daily IU was associated with higher next-day FoMO, while higher daily FoMO was associated with higher next-day IU. Together, the findings describe complementary aspects of the IU-FoMO relationship: Study 1 identifies candidate item-level interface domains, whereas Study 2 independently shows temporal coupling between daily IU and daily FoMO at the construct level. These findings may inform future research and the development of interventions for uncertainty-related distress and socially specific missing-out concerns among college students. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Audit fees under accounting and auditing standards: A communicative action perspective
Abstract: This study investigates audit fee determination under accounting and auditing standards by moving beyond dominant economic and agency-based explanations toward a critical, normative perspective. The study conceptualizes audit fees as a social construct shaped by the interaction between professional judgment, regulatory systems, and market forces by using Theory of Communicative Action developed by Jürgen Habermas. Using a semisystematic literature review (SsLR), this research synthesizes empirical audit fee studies published between 2010 and 2024 and analyzes them through a Habermasian lens to explore the tension between the auditors’ professional lifeworld and the systemic logic embedded in accounting and auditing standards. A comprehensive search of the Scopus database resulted in a final sample of 33 empirical studies. These studies were then used as the basis for an analysis examining how accounting and auditing regulations contribute to the colonisation of audit fee-setting practices. The findings indicate that standards such as IFRS, auditing standards, and regulatory oversight regimes function as steering mechanisms. These standards orient audit fee determination toward instrumental rationality, compliance, and risk mitigation. While these standards enhance transparency and comparability, they also increase audit complexity, documentation requirements, and litigation risk. The limitation of this study is that it depends on empirical literature with quantitative data. Nevertheless, this study contributes by expanding audit fee research into a normative-communicative framework, highlighting audit fees as a guiding medium in modern audit systems. This study offers a novel critical perspective by positioning audit fees as outcomes of communicative and power relations rather than purely economic transactions. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Zhang H.; Luo S.; Xie N.; Pan L.
Title: Precise integration of attack path and syntax logic analysis for vulnerability severity assessment
Abstract: Accurate assessment of vulnerability severity at the source code level is essential for anticipating potential risks and prioritizing remediation efforts. However, current approaches face two key challenges: (i) analyzing exploitability at the basic block level fragments syntactic and semantic logic, causing critical exploitation conditions to be overlooked and leading to severity misjudgments; and (ii) inferring attack paths from inter-block relationships often fails to distinguish benign control flows from exploit chains, polluting attack graphs with false paths and resulting in inaccurate exploitability assessment, especially for access-complexity-related evidence. To address these issues, we propose ASVA (Attack path and Syntax logic analysis for Vulnerability severity Assessment), a novel patch-aware source-code framework that integrates multi-scale syntactic logic extraction with attack path modeling. ASVA employs convolutional kernels with varying receptive fields to capture multi-scale syntactic patterns and leverages an attention mechanism to highlight exploitation logic, reducing misclassification. Furthermore, it utilizes CodeBERT to encode code lines and compute inter-line semantic relationships, enabling the construction of robust attack path representations that effectively distinguish genuine attack flows from normal control transitions. Experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that ASVA outperforms selected state-of-the-art baselines, improving accuracy and robustness over existing methods. This work underscores the importance of fine-grained logic modeling and attack path correlation in advancing automated vulnerability severity assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Early-life adversity and long-term outcomes: evidence from the cocoa swollen shoot virus outbreak in the Gold Coast
Abstract: How do early-life economic shocks that do not directly affect human biology shape long-term development outcomes? While a large body of work documents persistent effects of early-life exposure to health crises, famines, and natural disasters, much less is known about shocks that operate through economic disruption. This study addresses this gap by examining the long-term effects of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD), an agricultural epidemic that devastated cocoa production in the Gold Coast (now Ghana) during the 1940s. Combining historical data on climatically suitable cocoa-growing areas with georeferenced household survey data, I exploit variation in exposure across birth timing and space to estimate the epidemic's long-term effects. The results show that exposure during early childhood and school-going years led to substantial and persistent human capital deficits. Individuals exposed during early childhood lost about one year of schooling and were 8.5 percentage points (pp) less likely to obtain formal education, while those exposed during school-going years lost about 0.8 years of schooling and were 7.0 pp less likely to obtain formal education. Exposure is also associated with worse health outcomes, increasing morbidity by 6.2–8.5 pp and disability by 5–7.5 pp. In contrast, there is no systematic evidence of long-term effects on employment type or labor supply. Evidence on potential mechanisms points to both educational and occupational channels. Conditional on ever attending school, exposed individuals completed fewer years of schooling and were more likely to have incomplete primary education, indicating disruptions to both school progression and initial access to schooling. In addition, exposed individuals are more likely to work in the agricultural sector in adulthood, consistent with reduced educational attainment having narrowed their occupational options. These findings demonstrate that industry-specific economic shocks can generate long-term human capital deficits, even in the absence of direct biological exposure. © 2026 The Author

Title: Beyond landlockedness: transit structure, infrastructure, and the geography of trade costs
Abstract: This paper examines how geographic disadvantage and infrastructure shape bilateral trade flows, with a particular focus on landlocked countries. Using a global panel dataset covering 2007–2019, the paper moves beyond the conventional binary classification of landlockedness by decomposing the geographic disadvantage into coastal accessibility and transit structure. The empirical strategy combines an augmented gravity model with the Hausman–Taylor estimator to address endogeneity while retaining time-invariant geographic variables, and is complemented by Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (PPML) estimation and extensive-margin analysis to account for zero trade flows, heteroskedasticity, and trade participation. The results yield three main findings. First, infrastructure plays a central role in facilitating trade, with improvements in logistics performance significantly increasing bilateral trade flows. Second, the negative effect of landlockedness is largely driven by coastal accessibility: once distance to the nearest coast is accounted for, the estimated penalty of being landlocked declines substantially. Third, and most importantly, the structure of transit access matters. Landlocked countries that depend on a single coastal neighbor experience significantly lower trade, highlighting the importance of competition among transit routes. The findings are robust across alternative estimators, including fixed effects, Hausman–Taylor, PPML, and extensive-margin models. These findings suggest that the disadvantages faced by landlocked countries are multidimensional, reflecting not only geography and infrastructure but also regional political economy. Title: “The Right to Repair”: A systematic literature review and research agenda for an emerging interdisciplinary field
Abstract: The Right to Repair (R2R) is an important arena in which restrictive repair practices, including limits on access to spare parts, manuals, software, and specialised tools, as well as product designs that inhibit repair, are being contested. Although scholarly interest in R2R is growing rapidly, research remains fragmented across disciplinary and empirical domains, limiting the development of a coherent understanding of its implications for technology-society relations. In response, this paper presents a systematic literature review that maps and synthesises existing research on R2R. Specifically, it (1) consolidates empirical evidence on the implications of R2R; (2) examines how the concept has been theorised across disciplines; and (3) identifies key conceptual and methodological gaps that constrain theoretical and empirical advancement in the field. By organising this literature into coherent thematic domains and tracing the relationships between them, the review argues that the effective realisation of R2R depends on a socio-technical capacity: the practically exercisable ability to repair produced through the interaction between legal entitlements, technological architectures, economic arrangements, and social capabilities. It also reveals disciplinary and geographical imbalances and identifies four tensions structuring future research: formal ownership versus effective control, legal entitlement versus practical repair capacity, universal frameworks versus situated repair practices, and systemic transformation versus continuity. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Dependent development at the energy transition: placing lithium imaginaries in Neoliberal and Contentious Peru
Abstract: We examine lithium and development imaginaries in mining-dependent Peru, asking: What are these imaginaries? What narratives underpin them? Who articulates and shares them, and from where? What forms of state (in)action are envisioned in relation to them? The case study elucidates how alternative “imagined futures” coexist within a natural resource–dependent economy. The ruling national elites in Lima have a neoliberal imagination, treating lithium like any other mineral resource in the country. In contrast, professional elites in the mineral-rich but peripheral region of Puno adopt a resource nationalist view, advocating for direct state involvement in lithium industrialization and the transformation of the domestic energy system, shaped by beliefs on Bolivia's developmental pathway. Among rural community leaders as well as political and social leaders in the districts near lithium and uranium deposits, however, the prevailing idea is that of a social license. In this view, each community has the capacity to negotiate development terms with mining companies independently. In the broader imagination at the resource periphery of a peripheral national economy, the state is perceived primarily as a minimalist governmental actor, necessary only to oversee and ensure the enforcement of mine-community agreements and to provide basic infrastructure. Thus, elites at the political center and communities near expected resource developments converge in their immediate pursuit of rents promised by resource commodification. In the dominant discourses, environmental concerns are often subordinated to economic development goals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Fractional class-specific weighted random forest optimization

Title: What impacts can intertemporal trading have on carbon markets across different development stages? An economy-wide analysis

Title: A socio-technical maturity framework for design firms to enable the transition to design-out-waste in Indonesia's construction sector
Abstract: The construction sector remains a major driver of resource depletion and solid waste generation, with a substantial share traceable to early design-stage decisions. The results reveal an interdependent socio-technical structure, with Industry Structure emerging as the most influential dimension and an important upstream driver of other organisational capabilities. The resulting framework provides an empirically weighted basis for assessing organisational readiness, identifying capability priorities, and guiding DoW implementation towards circular construction. Title: GenAI-enabled human–AI collaboration: An integrative review of local augmentation, hidden work, and governable synergy
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is becoming part of everyday knowledge work, where it can accelerate drafting, coding, summarization, ideation, customer communication, and other language-intensive tasks. Yet the organizational problem is conversion: local GenAI gains create organizational value only when they survive the full work system, including verification, coordination, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability. Drawing on 251 academic and practice-facing sources across information systems (IS), management, human–computer interaction, human factors, organizational theory, and responsible AI, this article synthesizes why GenAI-enabled work often produces local augmentation but less often yields governable organizational synergy. The review develops three findings. First, GenAI shifts the relevant unit of collaboration from a one-step task interaction to a recurrent production-and-revision workflow in which human framing, prompting, verification, correction, and reuse become part of the value-producing system. Second, the augmentation-to-synergy boundary is net work-system value: visible task gains and reallocation benefits must exceed work displaced across roles and time into verification, rework, coordination, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability. Third, durable synergy requires behavioral embedding and multi-outcome governance: prompts, memory, feedback traces, review routines, and escalation rules must improve local fit while keeping reliance, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability observable. The article contributes a work-system conversion account that distinguishes substitution, augmentation, and synergy as different organizational states; a trace-centered behavioral-embedding view of how recurring GenAI use becomes a persistent, history-dependent workflow state within established sociotechnical IS theory; and a governance-instrumentation account that evaluates visible gains together with hidden labor, learning, ownership, risk, reviewability, and accountability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Artificial intelligence is not enough to enhance organizational performance
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), supply chain visibility, supplier integration, and organizational performance through the lens of Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT). Drawing on empirical data from UK-based organizations that have adopted AI technologies, we employ structural equation modeling along with mediation and moderation analyses to test our hypotheses. The findings indicate that AI does not have a significant direct effect on performance; instead, its impact is fully mediated through supply chain visibility and supplier integration. This supports the view that AI-driven supply chain visibility acts as an information-processing mechanism that enhances firms' ability to coordinate, collaborate, and integrate with supply chain partners, thereby improving organizational performance. Furthermore, supply uncertainty positively moderates the relationship between supplier integration and performance, amplifying the benefits under conditions of higher uncertainty. This study contributes to the literature by clarifying AI's indirect role in driving performance and highlighting the importance of embedding AI within broader organizational capabilities. It also offers practical insights for managers seeking to leverage AI to enhance supply chain integration and organizational effectiveness. © 2026

Title: Events under fire: Developing an urgent anthropology for events during armed conflicts
Abstract: This conceptual and methodological research note addresses event industry dynamics during armed conflicts, proposing an urgent anthropology approach to document transformations in real time. Using Ukraine as an example, we illustrate how event organizations have adapted to existential threats since the 2022 Russian invasion, demonstrating resilience through cultural initiatives, charitable events, and creative repurposing of resources. We argue that these practices have the potential to sustain cultural identity and to contribute to economic development, social cohesion and morale in conflict settings. To overcome the methodological and ethical challenges of traditional ethnography in war zones, we propose a novel citizen science framework within the urgent anthropology paradigm, leveraging digital technologies, social media, and participatory methods. This approach can decentralize knowledge production, mitigate researcher risk, and create longitudinal archives of industry adaptations. Authors: Liu Q.; Ma N.; Zhang X.
Title: Your recommendation and my choice: The impact of algorithmic recommendation convergence on consumers’ algorithmic recommendation aversion
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Personalized recommendation features launched by integrated online shopping platforms with multi-brand competition trap consumers in the dilemma of product choice constrained by algorithmic recommendation convergence, and induce consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion. Against this backdrop, this article systematically examines the existence, antecedents, and boundaries of consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion. The results show that algorithmic recommendation convergence significantly triggers consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion and suppresses their purchase intentions. Specifically, in addition to perceived lack of self-control affecting algorithmic recommendation aversion, consumers' state of choice overload caused by homogeneous recommendation convergence is the key reason for perceived lack of self-control and the emergence of algorithmic recommendation aversion. Meanwhile, the results further demonstrate that in multi-brand markets with multi-oligopolistic brand coexistence, brand agglomeration further narrows consumers' brand and product choice scope, making it more likely to induce consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion. In contrast, in a single-brand-dominated market structure, the core brand effect can leverage its dominant market position and market recognition to mitigate the impact of algorithmic recommendation convergence on consumers' algorithmic recommendation aversion. These findings expand the research perspective on consumer algorithmic bias, emphasize the importance of brand strategies, and provide timely and critical insights for understanding and alleviating consumers’ algorithmic recommendation aversion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Phygital pop-up stores: Measuring immersion, novelty, and post-visit purchase behavior using eye-tracking and biometrics
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Phygital pop-up stores hybrid retail environments fusing physical spaces with digital layers represent an accelerating frontier in contemporary retailing. Primary data were collected from 612 adult consumers across the United Kingdom and Australia via a stratified intercept sampling protocol. Objective measures of consumer immersion were captured using eye-tracking metrics and galvanic skin response indices embedded within a structured self-report survey. Title: The effects of adolescents' digital and environmental literacy on parents’ green consumption: A reverse intergenerational socialization perspective
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Drawing on reverse socialization theory, this study examines how adolescents' digital and environmental literacy influence parents' green consumption behavior (GCB). Using matched adolescent–parent survey data, we employ PLS-SEM to test net and mediating effects and fsQCA to identify configurational pathways leading to high levels of parents' GCB. Parents' decision-making confidence mediates the relationship between adolescents' digital literacy and parents' GCB, reflecting a capability empowerment pathway, whereas parents' personal norms mediate the relationship between adolescents' environmental literacy and parents' GCB, reflecting a norm activation pathway. The fsQCA results further identify nine configurational pathways, indicating that parents’ GCB is characterized by equifinality and conditional substitution. Title: Carbon trading in community-based forest management: A bibliometric mapping of scientific publications from 2000 to 2025
Abstract: Carbon trading in community-based forest management (CBFM) has emerged as a promising mechanism for simultaneously addressing climate change mitigation and improving the welfare of rural communities. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of 203 scientific publications obtained from Scopus, covering the period 2000 to 2025, with an analytical focus on the period 2010-2024. Using VOSviewer v.1.6.20 and Scopus's built-in analysis, this study analyzes publication trends, author participation patterns, geographic distribution, journal sources, and thematic structure through author collaboration, co-occurrence of keywords, and bibliographic linking networks. Results show a sharp acceleration in publication growth following key climate policy milestones, including the Warsaw Framework for REDD+ (2013), the Paris Agreement (2015), and COP26 (2021), with a record 21 articles published in 2024. Nepal and Indonesia emerged as dominant knowledge producers, collectively contributing 42.4% of total publications. Thematic mapping identified three main research clusters: carbon governance in CBFM, carbon measurement and quantification, and multifunctional forest landscape ecology. A critical knowledge gap was identified: while the supply side of carbon measurement of forest carbon stocks and biomass has been well documented, the demand side of how communities access, negotiate, and fairly obtain benefits from carbon markets remains largely unexplored. These findings underscore the urgent need for interdisciplinary research that links technical carbon measurement with institutional, economic, and social dimensions of equity to promote fair and scalable carbon trading within the framework of community forest governance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Lin S.; Liu Q.
Title: “Crossing the river by feeling the stones”: Sub-national agency in China's highway maintenance marketisation
Abstract: Marketisation reforms in China are often described as an extension of Western New Public Management (NPM), yet their meanings and effects vary substantially across regions and remain poorly understood from the perspective of policymakers themselves. Drawing on document review and interviews with sub-national officials and practitioners involved in highway maintenance in two underdeveloped provinces, this study examines how marketisation is interpreted, justified, and enacted through a "learning by doing" process shaped by administrative legacies, political incentives, and constrained market environments. The analysis shows that NPM-related principles, such as competition and performance management, are selectively adapted rather than directly transplanted, producing hybrid arrangements that combine bureaucratic control with quasi-market practices dominated by state-owned enterprises. The study identifies four narrative frames through which policymakers explain and evaluate reforms, as well as the recurring strategy of deliberate inaction, which emerges as a pragmatic response to tensions between central expectations and local socio-economic realities. It also considers the broader implications of marketisation for highway service performance, public satisfaction, fiscal sustainability, and technical capacity, pointing to uneven outcomes and persistent governance tensions. Title: Incomplete markets, crop portfolios, and agricultural productivity
Abstract: Using the Uganda National Panel Survey, I document that farmers face a trade-off between crop yields and risk, that most grow both high- and low-yield crops, and that poorer farmers concentrate on the low-yield, low-risk ones. I then develop an incomplete-markets model with a crop-portfolio choice, in which households trade off income returns against consumption smoothing. Wealth-poor households optimally under-invest in intermediates and shift toward safer crops. Crop portfolios, intermediate input use, and the wealth distribution are jointly determined in equilibrium. The model also reproduces the low pass-through of both income inequality and income volatility into consumption. Calibrated to rural Uganda, it implies that completing markets raises agricultural productivity by 12.8%, with 15.8% of the gain coming from eliminating the misallocation of inputs across farmers and crops. Consumption rises by 17.6% and welfare by 17.4%, with income inequality rising slightly and consumption inequality unchanged. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Hu J.
Title: Beyond sales: Seller explanation, product availability, and returns in livestream commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Livestream commerce combines seller explanation with continued product availability in a shopping cart. Our data separately record seller explanation duration and cart availability duration; these measures do not isolate informational content or establish actual consumer exposure. Sales alone may miss differences in the postpurchase outcomes associated with these durations. We therefore examine product returns as an indicator of postpurchase outcomes, estimating associations with streamer–product and broadcast fixed effects on a panel of nearly 190,000 livestream product listings. The two durations diverge sharply: longer explanation is associated with a lower return rate and longer cart availability with a higher one, even though both are associated with higher sales. The divergence widens with the scope for uncertainty about whether a product suits a particular buyer, while the price–discount pattern does not match the specific impulse-purchasing prediction examined here. The pattern is consistent with a buyer-screening interpretation, but the data do not observe purchasers’ exposure to explanation or distinguish screening from alternatives such as telepresence. Since only one of the two is scarce, the margin a seller controls is the allocation of the host's attention rather than the length of a product's stay in the cart. © 2026

Title: Negotiation and relationships: Insights from adjacent, psychologically-grounded literature
Abstract: Negotiations often unfold within ongoing relationships, making relationships integral to negotiation processes and outcomes. Yet, despite repeated calls for greater attention to relational dynamics, behavioral negotiation research has largely relied on paradigms that minimize the role of relationships. We review research from adjacent, psychologically-grounded literature (e.g., on close relationships, marketing, strategy, and operations) that conceptualize negotiation as embedded within ongoing relationships.
