Authors: Sun Y.; Shen X.
Title: FracBiNet: Fractional bilateral decomposition with heterogeneous dual-path modeling for cross-market stock index prediction
Abstract: Stock index levels are hard to predict one day ahead: daily series are noisy and near-integrated, with only a few thousand observations per market. We propose FracBiNet, a lightweight decomposition model with 4, 612 trainable parameters. Its core is a causal fractional bilateral kernel coupling a power-law temporal decay with an edge-preserving range gate. An innovation-whitening criterion on a dedicated learning-rate clock calibrates the kernel’s two parameters. Its latest level is the trend anchor, and a small additive-attention network models the residual. Every baseline is tuned per fold under identical grids, with five seeds and Diebold–Mariano tests against persistence. First, FracBiNet is Pareto-efficient among learned models. It is the only one never significantly worse than persistence on any market; all eleven baselines are significantly worse on at least two of three. It never fails catastrophically, and its seed-level variance is negligible relative to market-regime variation. Second, deep forecasters fail at level extrapolation on trending indices. The failure is only partly attributable to the target formulation: retrained to predict next-day changes, some architectures recover toward persistence while others collapse. Third, no model, including ours, demonstrates value beyond naive references (persistence, buy-and-hold) under two strict, complementary evaluations (moving-block bootstrap and Holm-corrected multiplicity). Title: Data-driven construction of asymmetric fuzzy numbers via entropy-based shape calibration
Abstract: In most fuzzy number families the membership-function shape is selected a priori by the decision maker, and the learned or adaptive approaches that infer it from data do so by optimising a task loss rather than through a closed-form link to the information content of the evidence. This arbitrariness distorts uncertainty representation and precludes principled comparison across families. This paper addresses this shape-selection problem by introducing the data-driven Entropy Calibrated Asymmetric Fuzzy Number (ECAFN), which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first fuzzy number whose left and right transition functions are calibrated in closed form from the Shannon entropies of the supporting evidence within a power-law L-R framework, and which can replace manual membership specification in Mamdani or Takagi Sugeno Kang (TSK) inference systems. Two theoretical results are established within the power-law family: an entropy-matching constraint uniquely determines the shape exponent for the admissible entropy range, and a uniqueness characterisation of the entropy-to-shape calibration map satisfying parabolic and triangular limit conditions and a constant proportional decay rate property. Generalization of standard families (triangular, trapezoidal, exponential, and parabolic) arise as special or limiting cases, the Gaussian is subsumed in a curvature-magnitude sense. A scalar Fuzzy Information Number (FIN) is proposed for cross-family comparison of informativeness, and an ablation study confirms robustness to the method’s hyperparameters. The framework is validated on three benchmarks structural health monitoring, multi-sensor altitude fusion and Basel-III credit-risk modelling. An extended comparative analysis positions ECAFN against recent (2020–2026) families including Fermatean, T-spherical, probabilistic linguistic fuzzy numbers, and Z-numbers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Lin X.; Yang M.; Liu C.; Agag G.
Title: How retailers build authenticity over time: A longitudinal study of transparency, frontline brand enactment, customer-company identification, and sales growth
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Retailer authenticity is treated as a commercial asset, yet its relevance may depend on identity conversion. This longitudinal study separates retailer-controlled evidence from customers' higher-order authenticity judgments and from the self-definitional response that follows. Retailer transparency supplies informational evidence concerning disclosure, clarity, accuracy, and candor, whereas frontline brand enactment supplies behavioral evidence that employees embody the retailer's professed identity. Three waves of matched survey data from 10,214 loyalty customers nested in 208 stores in China are linked to a 12-month archival comparable-sales-growth window beginning during the closing month of Time 3. Multilevel longitudinal structural equation modeling indicates temporally ordered positive associations from Time 1 transparency and frontline brand enactment to Time 2 authenticity, from Time 2 authenticity to Time 3 customer-company identification, and from store-level identification to follow-up sales growth. The direct authenticity-growth association is not reliable after identification is modeled. The authenticity-identification association is stronger at higher prestige, recorded frontline interaction frequency, and brand familiarity, consistent with proposed conditions of cue diagnosticity and identity relevance. The study's central contribution is an evidence-judgment-identity-performance account: the observed pattern links authenticity with commercial performance through identification, without establishing that this is its only pathway or that a direct premium is absent. The field design establishes temporal order and covariation, not random assignment or causal identification. © 2026

Title: A flow shop scheduling problem incorporating a reconfigurable material handling Robot: A constraint programming approach
Abstract: A reconfigurable manufacturing system (RMS) is a new paradigm for the manufacturing environment to respond to unpredictable market change and frequent new product introduction. One of the components of an RMS is a reconfigurable material handling system (RMHS). This paper investigates the permutation flow shop scheduling problem in a manufacturing system with RMHS. Hence, first, a novel Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is developed. Then, to tackle the inherent complexity of the problem, an efficient constraint programming (CP) approach is devised. Finally, comprehensive computational experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of both models, followed by a sensitivity analysis on three key performance indicators to further assess the CP model and extract the managerial insights. Results show that the CP model has better performance than the MILP model for solving large-scale problem instances and achieves a high-quality solution in a reasonable time. Title: Lifecycle costs of safety instrumented systems in process industries: a systematic literature review
Abstract: A safety instrumented system (SIS) is an automated system designed to detect and mitigate potential risk of hazardous conditions in industrial processes by taking actions to prevent or mitigate incidents. It is essential because it helps protect people, equipment, and the environment by reducing the risk of accidents in hazardous operations, such as in chemical plants, oil refineries, or power stations. While the primary objective of SIS design is safety, economic considerations, particularly lifecycle cost, play a pivotal role in decision-making during the design phase. Although research efforts exist to incorporate lifecycle cost with safety, the literature is fragmented and lacks a comprehensive lifecycle cost framework. Therefore, a systematic literature review is conducted to uncover safety instrumented systems’ lifecycle cost elements and the decision variables that impact them. The review results lead to a comprehensive and structured cost calculation framework to assess SIS designed to protect a process unit economically. Finally, this study provides perspectives on potential research directions relevant to SIS lifecycle cost, including the impact of systematic failures, cybersecurity integration, the relative weighting of different cost elements, inclusion of risk costs, and various SIS application types. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Nuclear ship Mutsu and the 1974 radiation leak Incident: Technical background and management lessons
Abstract: During its experimental voyage in September 1974, Japan’s first nuclear-powered ship, Mutsu, experienced abnormal radiation during a low-power reactor test conducted approximately 800 km east of Cape Shiriya in Aomori Prefecture. The immediate technical mechanism involved fast-neutron streaming and secondary gamma-ray generation caused by an inadequate shielding configuration. Although the event did not involve major fuel damage or a large release of radioactive material, it developed into a serious operational and political problem, leading to resistance to the ship’s return and to a government investigation. This paper reconstructs the incident and reviews the technical and organizational conditions that shaped its occurrence and subsequent handling. Drawing on official reports, technical records, and prior studies, it examines how inadequate project integration, limited design review, contractual separation, and communication failures complicated what began as a shielding-design problem. Using action system theory of management as a heuristic framework, we organize key task-level findings and relate them to recurrent patterns in major public technology projects. The case indicates that, in prototype nuclear systems, technical adequacy alone is insufficient: integrated review, clear responsibility, and effective communication are also essential to safe development and testing. Title: Using reusable ceramic vs. disposable cellulose-pulp plates in a wine tasting service in Italy: Findings from a life cycle assessment application experience
Abstract: Wine tourism, including winery visits, tastings, and cultural events, boosts sustainable development but generates environmental impacts ranging from food and wine production to tasting services. This study applies Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), focused on Carbon Footprint (CF), to compare the use of reusable ceramic vs. disposable cellulose-pulp plates in a tasting service in an Apulian winery. A cradle-to-grave analysis reveals that, in baseline scenario, reusable plates showed a slightly higher CF than single-use plates (0.0668 vs. 0.0635 kgCO₂eq/person served, respectively). Based on the results obtained, process optimisation solutions were identified: it was found that using photovoltaic-powered energy-efficient dishwasher may reduce the CF of reusable plates by 67%, reducing the impact to 0.0179 kgCO₂eq/person served in the best-performing scenario. Five service configurations were then tested over a total of 2500 customers served in six months, assuming a constant optimal dishwasher loading efficiency (i.e., operating exclusively at full capacity). Whilst the absolute reuse rate of the plate stock inherently scales with customer volume (averaging approximately 73 uses per plate in the baseline period), the results showed that, without technological improvements, the lowest-impact option was to serve 500 people with reusable plates and 2000 with disposable plates. Overall, this study extends the application of Life Cycle Assessment from conventional production systems to experiential tourism services. The findings demonstrate that the environmental performance of tableware is not solely dictated by intrinsic material properties, but is fundamentally driven by the systemic operational configuration, including dishwashing efficiency, service volumes, and the carbon intensity of the electricity mix. Consequently, this study provides a novel, scalable methodological framework to support wineries and tourism operators in designing scientifically grounded, lower-impact tasting services. © 2026

Title: Cross-Boundary Practices within the Construction Industry: The Case of the Quantity Surveyors
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The evolving dynamics of the construction industry have sharpened the need for quantity surveyors (QSs) to reinterpret their role, expanding beyond traditional commercial management practices to encompass broader strategic functions such as value optimization and interdisciplinary collaboration. At the same time, professional overlaps and cross-boundary practices have become an increasing challenge to the quantity surveying profession, leading to potential conflicts and quality compromises in construction projects. However, there is markedly less research on the negative effects of cross-boundary practices for the quantity surveying profession, particularly regarding professional identity and long-term industry implications. Therefore, this study aims to recognize the challenges posed to the quantity surveying profession by cross-boundary practices and to examine the underlying reasons for these challenges. A comprehensive literature review and 25 semistructured interviews were conducted with two samples: QS professionals and non-QS professionals, to collect data. The content analysis method was used to analyze the gathered data. The core quantity surveying functions, such as taking off quantities, preparing bills of quantities, and contract administration, are increasingly performed by non-QS professionals in the construction industry. Even if there are positive effects, including knowledge transfer and reducing the scarcity of QSs through cross-boundary practices, the negative consequences, such as lowering project quality and harming the professional image of QSs, were found to be more significant. By empirically investigating the causes and effects of cross-boundary practices in quantity surveying, this study addresses an overlooked vulnerability in the construction industry and fills a critical gap in the literature on professional role integrity and industry standards.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: River tourism based on community participation and regional linkages for sustainable livelihoods: The case of Can Tho City, Vietnam
Abstract: This study examines the role of community-based river tourism and regional linkages in supporting sustainable livelihoods in Can Tho City, Vietnam. A convergent mixed-methods approach was employed, combining surveys of 385 tourists, 47 local households, and 18 tourism officials and community representatives with 36 semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), cluster analysis, and multiple regression, while qualitative data were integrated through thematic coding, triangulation, and SWOT analysis. The findings indicate that community-based river tourism contributes to livelihood diversification, income generation, skill development, and social capital formation. Participating households reported relatively high livelihood stability (mean = 3.87) and moderate government support (mean = 3.59), whereas regional linkage participation remained low (mean = 1.79). EFA results revealed a common factor linking government support, regional cooperation, and livelihood outcomes, with factor loadings ranging from -0.64 to -0.51. For tourism officials and community representatives, EFA identified two governance dimensions—regional coordination and community-enterprise synergy—which explained 84.83 of the total variance. Tourists reported high overall satisfaction (mean = 4.35), strong community interaction (mean = 4.61), positive perceptions of cultural preservation (mean = 3.71), and willingness to pay for tourism services (mean = 3.98). Regression analysis showed that cultural preservation perception was the only statistically significant predictor of tourist satisfaction ( β = 0.146, p = 0.004 ). Open-ended responses highlighted key development priorities, including reducing crowding ( 29.6 ), increasing the availability of tour guides ( 26.8 ), enhancing cultural activities ( 23.9 ), and extending tour duration ( 19.7 ). Overall, sustainable livelihood outcomes depend not only on community participation but also on effective governance, cultural preservation, and stronger regional integration. The findings provide empirical evidence and practical implications for sustainable tourism planning in riverine destinations of the Mekong Delta. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Title: Stable recovery of k-sparse signal with non-convex (Formula presented) minimization

Title: Enhanced degradation of bamboo shoot shells via a two-step process: Sodium chlorite pretreatment and xylanase hydrolysis for xylooligosaccharides production
Abstract: To improve the high-value utilization of bamboo shoot shells (BSS), a two-step strategy combining sodium chlorite pretreatment and hydrolysis with a thermostable xylanase from Thermomyces lanuginosus Q231 was developed to produce xylooligosaccharides (XOS). The xylanase exhibited an optimum pH of 6.0 and an optimum temperature of 70°C, while maintaining good catalytic performance at 50–65°C. The effects of sodium chlorite concentration (1%–8%, w/v) on the chemical composition, structural characteristics, and enzymatic hydrolysis performance of BSS were investigated. The results showed that sodium chlorite selectively removed lignin in a concentration-dependent manner, thereby increasing hemicellulose exposure and xylanase accessibility while largely preserving the cellulose crystalline structure. The optimal pretreatment concentration was 6% (w/v), at which the XOS yield reached 22.30%. HPLC analysis showed that xylotetraose (X4) and xylopentaose (X5) were the major components, and the xylose/XOS ratio remained at a low level of 0.06 after 2 h of enzymatic hydrolysis, indicating high product selectivity. Under the optimized conditions, 50.50 g of XOS was obtained from 1 kg of pretreated BSS. These results suggest that the proposed process has strong potential for the valorization of BSS and offer valuable insights for further research on enzymatic XOS production from lignocellulosic residues. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Toward a relational typology: Mapping social entrepreneur-resident interactions in community-led tourism social entrepreneurship
Abstract: Research on tourism social entrepreneurship has focused on exogenous models while overlooking host communities' agency. The aim of this study was to examine interactions between social entrepreneurs and residents in the context of community-led tourism social entrepreneurship. The exploratory qualitative study design involved three fieldwork phases. We used two dimensions—the initiator's primary motivation and the embeddedness forms in the responder's actions—to identify four relationship types: traditional bonding ties, instrumental ties, patron–client ties, and value-congruent alliances. The social action and embeddedness theories guided our examination of relational formation. Findings further reveal a model of power shift and relationship dynamics. This model suggests that a power shift involves three principal stages centered around dependence. In summary, we provide here a typological framework for analyzing social entrepreneur–resident interactions and offer practical insights into sustainable community development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Resilience enhancement of multi-carrier microgrids under extreme weather: A distributionally robust operational strategy with actuarial risk
Abstract: Extreme weather can simultaneously perturb energy supply, demand, and infrastructure availability in multi-carrier microgrids (MCMGs), while physical service loss and its monetary consequence may differ across load classes. This paper develops a two-stage data-driven Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (WDRO) framework that separates physical service adequacy, actuarial valuation, tail-risk preference, and meteorological distributional ambiguity. Regional vulnerability is represented by an externally calibrated actuarial spatial vulnerability factor (ASVF), and a two-tail mean–GlueVaR functional characterizes multi-level upper-tail monetary exposure. The Wasserstein radius is calibrated exclusively from meteorological training data, with validation and holdout samples kept separate. For a fixed finite candidate support, the model admits an exact mixed-integer linear programming reformulation and a finite-candidate column-and-constraint generation (CCG) scheme with an explicit no-violation termination certificate. In the industrial-park case study, Glue-ASVF-WDRO yields zero held-out critical-service expected energy not supplied (EENS) and 21.339 kWh of general-service EENS, whereas risk-neutral WDRO gives nearly identical total EENS but 20.571 kWh of critical-service EENS. Matched-risk conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) and two-tail GlueVaR produce the same reported held-out outcomes, and the CCG and monolithic formulations attain the same objective value to numerical precision. Sensitivity analyses show stable held-out service outcomes across most tested perturbations, whereas stronger external distribution shifts cause marked deterioration. The results underscore the importance of separating physical service adequacy from actuarial valuation when evaluating resilient MCMG operation under extreme-weather uncertainty. Copyright © 2026. Title: Escaping the AI cage: construction workers’ perceived risk with AI gives rise to unsafe behaviors
Abstract: Reducing unsafe behavior among construction workers remains a central concern in construction management. While artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly adopted to replace or monitor workers, the negative perceptions workers hold toward the promotion of such technologies have largely been overlooked. This study introduces the concept of perceived risk with AI, defined as workers’ subjective perception of the potential negative consequences associated with AI adoption. Drawing on self-determination theory, which emphasizes individuals’ core psychological needs, we propose an inside-out theoretical model. This model explains how construction workers’ perceived risk with AI triggers unsafe behavior through two internal psychological pathways: emotional exhaustion and organizational identification. We further identify AI failure as a critical boundary condition that amplifies these effects. Data were collected from 343 frontline workers at 3 smart construction sites where AI actively interacts with human labor. Results indicate that perceived risk with AI increases unsafe behavior, and this relationship is mediated by both heightened emotional exhaustion and weakened organizational identification. Notably, these effects are significantly amplified when AI malfunctions occur. Our findings not only extend the application scope of self-determination theory but also contribute to the knowledge base on workers’ unsafe behavior in the context of human-AI coexistence. Practically, the study offers actionable insights for managers to mitigate the unintended side effects of AI implementation on worker safety. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The psychology of AI-mediated communication across languages
Abstract: Communication across languages is increasingly mediated by artificial intelligence (AI). This creates opportunities for people with different language backgrounds to communicate in their respective native languages. AI-mediated communication can therefore reduce cognitive effort, disfluency, and social stigma associated with speaking a non-native language. At the same time, non-native language use influences cognitive, emotional, and social processes that go beyond the accurate transmission of meaning. By affecting these processes and introducing new cues, AI-mediated communication could also have unintended effects on communication effectiveness and social evaluations between interlocutors. Title: Beyond Technology Readiness Levels: Developing and Evaluating an Industry 5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework for Regulated Life Sciences Manufacturing
Abstract: Purpose: Regulated life sciences manufacturing organisations face increasing pressure to adopt Industry 5.0 (I5.0) innovations while maintaining patient safety, product quality, data integrity, and regulatory compliance. Existing assessment models provide useful perspectives on technical maturity, expectation dynamics, and organisational innovation capability, but do not fully assess whether an innovation is ready to progress responsibly in a regulated, multi-stakeholder environment. This paper develops an I5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework and presents a preliminary practitioner-informed evaluation of its use in regulated life sciences manufacturing. Methods: This paper uses design science research structured through the Double Diamond process. The framework was developed through literature review, advisory feedback, subject matter expert input, practitioner workshops, case-based application, surveys, and thematic analysis. Evaluation was conducted with a small, purposively selected cohort of 16 practitioners from a single educational-industry programme. Results: The framework comprises three linked tools: the Innovation Maturity Assessment, Innovation Maturity Rubric, and Innovation Readiness Levels. Across two exploratory workshops involving 16 experienced practitioners, participants reported that the framework supported clearer discussion of readiness and improved visibility of adoption risks. In Workshop 2, descriptive feedback indicated that 91% of respondents viewed Innovation Readiness Levels as clearer than Technology Readiness Levels, 82% found the framework useful for comparing innovation timelines, and 75% would recommend it. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary practitioner feedback rather than sector-wide validation. Conclusion: The findings support the conceptual distinction between innovation readiness and technology readiness and indicate the need to assess technical, regulatory, organisational, stakeholder, and societal dimensions together when evaluating I5.0 innovation in regulated manufacturing. Title: Contextualizing negotiation research: The unique dynamics of buyer–supplier negotiations
Abstract: Effective buyer–supplier negotiations are important for organizations to attain their goals and for wider society to have a reliable supply of goods and services. These negotiations also have distinctive characteristics that differentiate them from other negotiation settings, such as personal buyer–seller negotiations, which have attracted much of the attention in the negotiation literature. Given the differences between professional buyer–supplier and personal buyer–seller negotiations, some findings from personal negotiations may have limited applicability in supply chain settings, while others hold across contexts. These findings have important implications for both negotiation research and education, calling for careful contextualization based on the type of negotiation. By reviewing recent studies in the supply chain management literature, this article highlights several common dynamics of buyer–supplier negotiations and how they affect negotiation outcomes. Title: LLMs’ reshaping of people, processes, products, and society in software development: a qualitative exploration with early adopters
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly reshaping software development, but their impact across the full software development lifecycle is underexplored. Existing work tends to focus on isolated activities such as code generation or testing, leaving open questions about how LLMs affect developers, processes, products, and the broader software ecosystem. We address this gap through semi-structured interviews with sixteen early-adopter software professionals who integrated LLM-based tools into their day-to-day work in early to mid-2023. We treat these interviews as early empirical evidence and compare participants’ accounts with recent work on LLMs in software engineering, noting which early patterns persist or shift. LLM use was highly phase-dependent, with strong uptake in implementation and debugging but limited influence on requirements gathering and collaborative work. Participants developed new competencies to use LLMs effectively, including prompt engineering strategies, multi-layered verification, and security-conscious integration to protect proprietary data. They also anticipated changes in hiring expectations, team practices, and computing education, while emphasizing that human judgment and foundational software engineering skills remain essential. Title: The Max–Min Kano framework: A context-sensitive method for evaluating office design features
Abstract: Product and building-related features are sometimes perceived differently across studies because they are experienced in different environmental contexts. The proposed Max–Min Kano methodology evaluates office design features under two contrasting contexts: a minimal environment with few positively appraised attributes and a maximal environment with many. Office-relevant attributes were identified through participatory elicitation and then evaluated using a Kano questionnaire (N = 32). Perceptual robustness was defined as retention of a Kano classification across the two contexts, while participant-level bootstrapping assessed sampling stability. View-related variables, window size, biophilic views, fewer façade obstructions, and proximity to windows were stable across contexts. They were Attractive, meaning they added satisfaction even when not strictly expected. In contrast, privacy provided by partitions emerged as a Must-be quality, while the presence of windows and ceiling height showed a One-dimensional relationship with satisfaction in both contexts. Other attributes, such as the seated-desk view, density, partition height, focal points, color, and materiality, were more sensitive to the baseline context. Adaptation-Level Theory, Stress Recovery theory, Attention Restoration theory, and Prospect–Refuge theory help explain these results. Overall, the Max-Min Kano approach helps identify features that remain perceptually robust across contexts, making it useful for prioritizing design features in real-world settings. The study shows that Kano categories are context-expressive rather than being intrinsic properties of features. For this reason, baseline context should be reported when evaluating user preferences across different spatial conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: When stigmatized workers become consumers
Abstract: Existing research on occupational stigma has focused primarily on workplace consequences, with less attention to how stigmatized service workers respond to service failures as consumers. Guided by cognitive appraisal theory, this sequential mixed-methods study integrates 20 interviews with a survey of 429 frontline workers in China. Qualitative findings show that perceived occupational stigma heightens sensitivity to disrespect and identity threat, whereas perceived work dirtiness shapes whether failures are attributed to situational constraints or preventable neglect. Quantitative results indicate that both constructs are positively associated with customer aggression and tolerance. Aggression may function as confrontational problem-focused coping, whereas tolerance reflects emotion-focused coping, and both are positively related to service recovery satisfaction. Title: Large language models in Scrum management: A practitioner survey of use, perceived benefits, risks, and human–AI collaboration
Abstract: Context: Scrum management includes knowledge-intensive activities such as backlog refinement, event preparation, and stakeholder alignment. Large language model (LLM) chat assistants may support these activities, but empirical evidence remains limited. Objective: This study investigates practitioners’ self-reported LLM use in Scrum management, perceived benefits and risks, and expectations for human–AI collaboration. Methods: We conducted a practitioner survey, and the results are based on a final analytic sample of 79 respondents who reported using LLM chat assistants in Scrum management. Closed-ended items were analyzed descriptively; open-ended responses underwent thematic coding. Results: In this sample, 48.1% reported daily or almost daily use, and 79.7% rated their LLM knowledge as at least qualified. Reported use centered on backlog refinement, event summarization, and Scrum-practice exploration. Perceived benefits included productivity (77.2%), reduced repetitive-task time (75.9%), and artifact quality (74.7%). Reported problems included almost-correct outputs (65.8%), hallucinations (54.4%), privacy concerns (50.6%), and content-validation difficulty (46.8%). Most respondents envisioned human-led or balanced human–AI collaboration (81.0%); 65.8% selected the no-role-replacement option. Title: BiCrossNet-DDI: Drug-drug interaction prediction based on bidirectional cross-view attention networks
Abstract: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction plays a crucial role in drug safety assessment and clinical polypharmacy management. Existing approaches predominantly rely on a single graph structure or adopt coarse-grained multi-view fusion strategies, making it difficult to simultaneously capture the multi-scale topological characteristics of drug relationships and fully exploit complementary information across different views, thereby limiting representation capacity and predictive performance. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a DDI prediction framework based on a bidirectional cross-view attention network, which achieves more comprehensive semantic modeling of drug interactions and robust prediction through multi-scale structural modeling and cross-view interaction alignment. Specifically, the proposed method performs consistent encoding over multi-scale diffusion views and similarity views, and further introduces a bidirectional cross-view attention module as the core component. Concretely, the original view is used as the query to selectively aggregate high-order structural information from the diffusion view, while the diffusion view is simultaneously employed as the query to reversely align interaction evidence from the original view, enabling bidirectional completion and collaborative enhancement between views. Residual connections are incorporated within network layers to preserve critical information and stabilize training, and unified drug embeddings are finally obtained for DDI prediction. Experiments on the ZhangDDI dataset demonstrate that our model achieves an absolute improvement of 3.17% in F1 compared with the strongest baseline method. Title: Examining perceptual spillover effects in social media influencer marketing effectiveness: A PLS-SEM and fsQCA approach

Abstract: Social media influencers (SMIs) play a pertinent role in shaping brand evaluations, yet how influencer-level perceptions translate into brand-level evaluations and SMI marketing effectiveness remains unclear. Title: When passion breeds silence: How coworkers’ work passion elicits envy and employee silence in hospitality workplaces
Abstract: While work passion is well-studied as an intrapersonal motivational construct, its interpersonal consequences for coworkers remain underexplored. Drawing primarily on the Social Functional Theory of Emotions, we examine how employees' observed work passion functions as a social signal that elicits coworker envy and, in turn, shapes silence behaviors. Across four studies (three experiments and a multi-source dyadic field study with hotel employees), we find a robust asymmetric pattern: harmonious passion primarily elicits benign envy, which is associated with prosocial silence, whereas obsessive passion primarily elicits malicious envy, which is associated with deviant silence. Cross-path effects were weaker and less consistent across studies. An exploratory field-study finding suggests that obsessive passion may occasionally relate to benign envy, although this association did not emerge in the experiments and warrants replication. Title: Environmental Mandated Delay: A Source-Based Classification Framework for Compliance-Driven Time Impacts in Construction Contracts
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: This article examines whether prevailing delay classifications in construction contracts adequately address time risk arising from mandatory environmental compliance obligations. It identifies a structural doctrinal gap in existing categories and proposes a distinct classification framework, environmental mandated delay (EMD), supported by a five-element cumulative test. A normative-comparative doctrinal methodology is employed, comprising (1) systematic analysis of delay provisions in major standard form construction contracts [the Fédération Internationale des Ingénieurs-Conseils (FIDIC) forms, the New Engineering Contract (NEC), and the Joint Contracts Tribunal (JCT) forms]; (2) comparative review of environmental regulatory frameworks in four jurisdictions (the UK, Australia, Indonesia, and the UAE); (3) a systematic review of published arbitral awards rendered under the auspices of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) and judicial decisions demonstrating recurring classification ambiguity; and (4) application of the proposed framework to documented infrastructure project contexts. None of the major standard form contracts articulates a delay category grounded in mandatory public law compliance. A structured content analysis of seven publicly available ICSID awards (2014-2022) confirms that compliance-based temporal disruption is recurrent across infrastructure disputes but no tribunal applied a structured delay classification framework in any case. Analysis of published arbitral decisions further identifies five recurring patterns that confirm the structural nature of the gap. EMD directly addresses each pattern by grounding entitlement in the public law source of the delaying obligation. The framework offers a structured analytical tool for extension-of-time (EOT) assessment, aligning delay classification with critical path-based scheduling analysis and improving consistency in contract administration and dispute resolution. The article makes three original contributions: (1) identification of a structural doctrinal gap supported by empirical arbitral evidence; (2) development of a source-based approach reorienting delay analysis from event- and actor-based models toward public law obligations; and (3) provision of an operational test applicable in engineering practice, enhancing predictability in the treatment of compliance-driven delay in climate-transition infrastructure projects.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Consumers and local short food supply chains: Critical purchasing factors

Title: Bidding and market dynamics in the Brazilian structural demand response program
Abstract: This paper studies the Structural demand response Program (SP) in Brazil from a consumer's perspective. In the first stage, consumers determine optimal bids that balance program revenues with production-related opportunity costs, while the second stage models the all-or-nothing market-clearing process as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming problem. To address computational challenges posed by the strategic bidding model, the nonconvexities are linearized via binary relations, and the bilevel model is reformulated as an equivalent single-level problem solved via a tailored Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm. Title: Upper credal Wasserstein envelopes for belief models: Choquet–Kantorovich duality and non-representability of universal rectangle lifts
Abstract: A basic probability assignment (BPA) on a finite ground space determines a credal set of compatible additive refinements. When only the BPA is observed, the classical optimal-transport value is therefore partially identified. We study its upper endpoint, the upper credal Wasserstein envelope Wc↑. Finite Kantorovich duality and credal support functions yield a Choquet–Kantorovich representation: the feasible geometry remains the ground-space Kantorovich dual polyhedron, while epistemic imprecision enters through upper Choquet expectations over focal supports. This representation separates Wc↑ from the maximum-lift Dempster–Shafer optimal-transport rectangle surrogate DSOT+. The former optimizes over the focal-max image of ground-feasible potentials; the latter optimizes over the full rectangle-dual region. On any class containing all categorical BPA pairs over the prescribed focal families, an exact BPA-independent linear rectangle representation must consequently use the maximum rectangle lift. On finite spaces, equality Wc↑=DSOT+ is equivalent to feasibility of at least one linear system indexed by a global focal-max pattern. Explicit examples show both equality and strict inequality. An unbounded line family has BPAs supported on non-singleton intervals and a unique maximizing pair of nondegenerate two-atom refinements. The minimum-lift rectangle program equals the lower credal endpoint for every finite cost; a cross-separable regime additionally gives upper exactness. These results identify the global realizability condition omitted by rectangle-wise surrogates and clarify when such surrogates are exact or only upper bounds. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Operational constraints in professional kitchens: A theory of constraints perspective on food waste reduction

Title: The dark side of AI customer service: How service failures damage consumer-brand relationships

Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) customer service is increasingly used as a frontline interface, yet its failures may create relational damage that extends beyond a single service encounter. Title: Consumer complaints as regulatory signals: Evidence from water services in Metropolitan Lima
Abstract: In regulated monopoly services, consumers lack effective exit options, making complaint systems a central mechanism for expressing dissatisfaction and generating regulatory information about service performance. However, complaint rates are not direct or unbiased indicators of service failures, as the decision to complain involves informational, procedural, and behavioral costs, reflecting both service problems and heterogeneous access barriers. Because administrative data record filed complaints rather than adjudicated outcomes, complaint rates are interpreted as noisy signals of perceived billing anomalies rather than direct measures of confirmed service failures, firm misconduct, or regulatory noncompliance. This paper reinterprets billing-related complaints as endogenous regulatory signals in essential public services. We develop a microeconomic framework in which households decide whether to complain when facing an atypical bill under uncertainty about its origin—whether it reflects a firm billing error or household-specific factors. The model’s predictions are tested using sector-month administrative data from Sedapal, the public water utility serving Metropolitan Lima (Peru), covering January 2022–June 2023. We estimate a dynamic panel model (System GMM) to identify persistence in complaint behavior and its response to unanticipated tariff shocks. We find strong persistence in complaint rates and a significant response to unexpected tariff increases. These patterns suggest structural frictions in service provision or communication and a critical role for tariff transparency. Overall, the results imply that regulators should strengthen tariff communication and incorporate complaint data into monitoring systems as screening and triage indicators, rather than as mechanical evidence of confirmed billing errors or firm misconduct. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Cao K.; Ma J.; Wang J.
Title: Paying for the future? Cross-season pre-sale product launch strategy in hotels
Abstract: Traditional hotels face persistent seasonal demand imbalance, with weak off-peak demand and constrained peak-season capacity. Drawing on Contingency Theory, this study examines cross-season pre-sale as a context-dependent hotel revenue management configuration and investigates how different configurations (i.e., no pre-sale, self-run pre-sale, and platform-based pre-sale) fit varying operating conditions. Results show that cross-season pre-sale does not universally outperform conventional practices; its value depends on the balance among incremental demand, impacts on existing demand, and implementation costs. Moreover, neither self-run nor platform-based pre-sale always dominates, as their relative effectiveness depends on the trade-off between platform-enabled market reach and channel costs. The study identifies boundary conditions for effective cross-season demand coordination and offers practical guidance for configuration choice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Driving impact? How imperfect displacement shapes heterogeneous rebound in carsharing
Abstract: Green technologies, products, and services, such as carsharing, are commonly promoted as pathways to lower environmental impacts by increasing efficiency. Yet rebound effects, behavioral and economic responses to improved efficiency, may erode these environmental impact reductions. Many rebound studies assume perfect displacement, where a new technology or mode of service provision fully replaces an existing service on a one-to-one basis. While analytically convenient, this assumption overlooks real-world complexity and consumer heterogeneity. Using survey data from nearly 4500 Belgian carsharing users, we compare rebound estimates under perfect displacement with those based on reported shifts in mobility. Under the perfect displacement assumption, we find a 53% rebound effect. When accounting for imperfect displacement, however, rebound effects vary widely across users. While median effects remain positive (20%–46%), at the individual level rebound effects range from substantial net benefits to strong rebound (5th–95th percentile: −331% to 147%). A cluster analysis further reveals distinct user groups with systematically different impacts, underscoring that displacement patterns vary not only in scale but also in direction. These findings suggest that carsharing's environmental impact is highly user-dependent, and that relying on a single aggregate estimate may mask critical behavioral variations. As this case study demonstrates, accounting for imperfect displacement in rebound analysis is critical for advancing theory and for tailoring more effective policy interventions. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Hoang Q.
Title: Factors influencing language choice of the Chơ Ro ethnic minority in Southern Vietnam: A socio-structural analysis
Abstract: This study examines the structural and socio-psychological factors shaping the language choice of the Chơ Ro— an indigenous community of fewer than 30,000 members in Southeast Vietnam—to identify the determinants of linguistic persistence amidst rapid industrial expansion. In the context of industrialization in Vietnam, ethnic minority communities navigate significant challenges related to language maintenance. This paper argues that Chơ Ro language choice reflects a phenomenon of language persistence, in which internal cultural motivations and communal networks function as determinants against the pressures of language shift. Utilizing a convergent mixed-methods design, the study analyzed quantitative data from 472 bilingual participants in Dong Nai, triangulated with qualitative data from 30 semi-structured interviews conducted with village elders and cultural custodians. The regression model yielded an adjusted R2 of.862, indicating that the independent variables account for 86.2% of the variance in language choice. Results indicate a predictive hierarchy: Cultural motivation (CM) emerged as a determinant predictor (β = 0.271, p < 0.001), followed by Endogamous social networks (ESN) (β = 0.225, p < 0.001) and Domain functional expansion (DFE) (β = 0.195, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that the Chơ Ro language remains a functional medium in domestic and communal domains, supported by Intergenerational Transmission Strength (ITS) (β = 0.171) and Institutional Support (IS) (β = 0.166). Qualitative themes reinforce these results, identifying a gendered buffering mechanism where domestic socialization counteracts external industrial pressures. This research provides an empirical framework for policy interventions aimed at addressing ethnolinguistic vitality through the reinforcement of community-based linguistic assets. By documenting the resilience of a small-scale minority, the study contributes to a comparative theory of bilingualism in urbanizing contexts, emphasizing that internal conviction and communal structures are necessary to mitigate linguistic attrition in high-density economic zones. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Authors: Luo Y.; Wei Y.; Cheng Y.
Title: Maintenance optimization in dynamic environment considering environment-induced maintenance delay
Abstract: Most maintenance optimization studies for production systems assume stationary environmental states. In practice, however, the operating environments vary over time, changing both degradation dynamics and production reward of the system. Moreover, under certain harsh environmental states, maintenance actions cannot be executed and must be postponed. These factors impact the production reward, degradation penalty, and maintenance cost in a coupled manner, posing challenges for making optimal maintenance decisions. In this paper, we develop a maintenance optimization framework for minimizing the operational cost of a production system operating in dynamic environments with environment-induced maintenance delay. The optimization problem is formulated as a Markov decision process (MDP) over an infinite horizon, including the quantification of the threefold impact of the environment on maintenance. We establish key structural properties and prove that the optimal maintenance policy has a control limit structure. Based on these properties, we develop an improved value iteration algorithm, exploiting the monotone threshold characterization of the optimal policy and avoiding redundant action comparisons, to obtain the optimal solution efficiently. A numerical study of offshore wind turbines illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework and algorithm. Managerial insights are provided through sensitivity analysis. Copyright © 2026. Title: Mechanistic interpretability of Mamba's selective gate in financial markets: A leakage-controlled study
Abstract: Selectively gated state-space models (SSMs), notably Mamba, are increasingly used for financial time series, yet how they internally represent market regimes (bull, bear, sideways) remains opaque. This paper applies Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) to a six-layer Mamba trained on approximately twenty-one years of daily data for a point-in-time set of S&P 500 constituents plus macroeconomic and Fama-French factors, decomposing per-layer hidden states with Top-K Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs). Our central contribution is methodological and cautionary. A prior, uncontrolled configuration recovered market regimes from SAE features at F1 = 1.00. Under a controlled protocol that (i) removes the three input features that overlap the HMM label definition, (ii) disables the auxiliary regime-classification head, (iii) uses a point-in-time constituent universe, and (iv) evaluates against labels disjoint from the inputs, the same regime label is recovered at only F1 = 0.398, indistinguishable from a logistic baseline on raw inputs (0.435) and from an SAE trained on a randomly initialized, untrained Mamba (0.364). A 2 × 2 attribution grid shows the near-perfect result is an interaction of auxiliary supervision and label-defining inputs: neither factor alone exceeds F1 ∼ 0.40. Effect sizes with block-bootstrap inference show the residual selective-gate (Delta t) regime effect is statistically detectable but economically negligible and uniform across layers rather than layer-specialized; the apparent polysemanticity gradient disappears under continuous, theory-grounded measures. We contribute a reproducible leakage-control protocol for interpretability evaluation of financial SSMs, a quantified demonstration that previously reported regime structure is a label-contamination artifact, and a modest economically grounded feature subset that genuinely survives the controls. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Chen J.; Wang S.; Ke W.; Zhang J.
Title: When culture speaks through E-commerce chatbots: How collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles shape impulsive buying
Abstract: E-commerce chatbots increasingly provide product advice during online shopping, yet it remains unclear how culturally framed recommendation language shapes impulsive buying. Drawing on cultural dimensions theory, cultural priming theory, and constructivist interpretation, this study conceptualizes collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles as message-level cultural language cues rather than as measures of consumers’ stable cultural orientation. Across four experiments with 880 participants, we show that a collectivistic persuasive style increases impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as socially supported and behaviorally acceptable choices, which strengthens social conformity. By contrast, an individualistic persuasive style reduces impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as choices requiring confirmation against personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit, which strengthens self-referencing. The findings further identify two boundary conditions. Human labeling strengthens the collectivistic pathway through social conformity by making group-oriented language more likely to be treated as socially relevant advice, whereas AI labeling shifts source perception toward algorithmic advice and strengthens the individualistic pathway through self-referencing by increasing attention to personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit. Low algorithm accessibility strengthens the collectivistic pathway, whereas high algorithm accessibility strengthens the individualistic pathway. These findings show that chatbot recommendations do more than transmit product information. They shape how consumers interpret the perceived source, social relevance, and personal applicability of recommendations, thereby influencing whether recommendations are quickly accepted as purchase decisions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhang S.; Sun W.; Wu T.; Guo X.
Title: Discount display in tiered pricing: Nudging subscriptions in online healthcare services
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Discounts are increasingly embedded within tiered pricing to encourage larger purchases or longer service commitments. However, such discounts are often implicit and embedded across the price options, heightening consumers’ cognitive burden of cross-tier comparisons. How platforms display these discounts and whether salient discount display in tiered pricing can drive consumer demand remain largely unclear. Drawing on nudge theory, we conceptualize discount display as a digital salience nudge and examine its effect on consumer subscription demand in online healthcare settings. We leverage a quasi-natural experiment on a leading Chinese online healthcare platform, which redesigned its subscription interface to render implicit savings across tiers salient to patients. Using an intensity-based difference-in-differences approach, we find that discount display significantly increases patient subscriptions. Further analyses suggest that this effect is unlikely to stem from physician-side price reductions or concurrent platform-side changes and is instead consistent with the informational effect of discount display. Moderation results further show that the promotional effect of discount display strengthens for physicians treating a higher share of chronic conditions and becomes statistically insignificant in predominantly episodic care. This study contributes to discount promotion literature by offering robust empirical evidence on the positive effect of salient discount display in tiered pricing contexts and provides managerial implications for interface design and promotion management in digital retailing markets. © 2026

Title: Rule-based BloodCell interpretable and actionable hematological classification using ConvNeXt-Tiny
Abstract: The automated identification and classification of peripheral blood cells is critical for diagnosing a range of hematological disorders, from systemic infections to leukemia. Such classification supports diagnosis by providing differential cell counts and by detecting abnormal cell morphology, rather than diagnosing a disease directly. Traditional manual microscopy is labor-intensive and prone to subjective error, while existing deep learning “black-box” models often lack the transparency required for clinical adoption. This study proposes an interpretable, research-oriented decision-support framework leveraging the ConvNeXt-Tiny architecture, optimized with tuned hyperparameters and an input resolution of 64 × 64 pixels to enable rapid, lightweight training. The model was trained on a dataset of 17,107 images, using 13,685 for training and 3,422 for testing across eight classes: Basophils, Eosinophils, Erythroblasts, Immature Granulocytes (IG), Lymphocytes, Monocytes, Neutrophils, and Platelets. On the held-out test set, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.98 and a weighted F1-score of 0.98. Reliability was assessed with a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.974 and a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.974, indicating strong agreement with the expert-labeled ground truth. A key contribution is the integration of Explainable AI (XAI) through LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations), which highlights influential superpixels to spatially validate cellular morphology. These visual explanations are complemented by a rule-based clinical decision-support (expert-system) module that maps the predicted cell class to predefined, non-diagnostic clinical guidance. By combining deep-learning feature extraction with rule-based recommendations drawn from standard hematology references, the framework provides a transparent and lightweight research prototype intended to assist, rather than replace, expert hematological assessment. Compared with existing approaches (Table 6), it addresses all eight clinically relevant classes with competitive accuracy and reliability while adding region-level LIME interpretability and a rule-based decision-support layer that most prior systems lack. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Uncovering heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on stock returns using causal forest double machine learning
Abstract: Global uncertainty has become an important source of financial market instability, yet its effects are inherently heterogeneous and difficult to identify using conventional econometric models. Existing empirical studies primarily rely on linear and average-effect estimators, which may conceal substantial heterogeneity across economic conditions. To address this limitation, this study proposes an explainable causal machine learning framework that integrates Causal Forest Double Machine Learning (CF-DML) with SHAP explanations to estimate and interpret heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on industry-level stock returns. Using a balanced panel of six major industries listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange from 2011 to 2022, global uncertainty is measured by the World Uncertainty Index (WUI), while macroeconomic and financial variables are incorporated as lagged covariates. The CF-DML framework enables robust causal inference under high-dimensional confounding and nonlinear relationships, whereas SHAP values identify the main drivers of treatment-effect heterogeneity. The results show that the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) of global uncertainty is statistically insignificant, yet substantial heterogeneity exists across observations. Differences across industries are relatively modest, indicating that global uncertainty is transmitted primarily through time-varying macro-financial conditions rather than fixed sectoral characteristics. SHAP analysis identifies exchange-rate volatility, inflation, and market valuation as the dominant factors explaining heterogeneous responses. The study contributes to the literature by combining causal inference, machine learning, and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified framework for financial analysis. The findings suggest that global uncertainty should be viewed as a state-dependent macro-financial phenomenon, providing practical insights for portfolio risk management, macro-financial surveillance, and the design of policies aimed at enhancing financial resilience in emerging economies characterized by persistent inflation and exchange-rate volatility. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Lee S.; Choi N.
Title: Club research: A review and research agenda
Abstract: Private clubs constitute a distinctive hospitality context defined by membership-based governance, shared authority, and long-term relational exchange, yet existing scholarship remains theoretically fragmented. This study systematically reviews 67 SSCI-indexed journal articles published through 2025 to examine the thematic evolution, theoretical foundations, and methodological patterns of club research. Using multi-layered bibliometric and content-based analyses, the review shows that research has expanded from managerial competency and member satisfaction toward innovation, governance, and digital engagement, but remains divided between consumer-experience and organization-centric management perspectives. This fragmentation under-theorizes clubs as hybrid governance-service institutions, especially at the member–management interface where authority, legitimacy, accountability, and value co-creation intersect. Methodological reliance on cross-sectional quantitative designs, U.S.-centric samples, and single-stakeholder perspectives further constrains cumulative theory building. Grounded in an institutional governance lens, the review advances a hybrid governance perspective and proposes future research on member–management dynamics, multi-role members, and access-sensitive, multi-stakeholder methods suited to private club settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: When animated avatars outperform: Leveraging avatar endorsers to enhance consumer adoption of AI-designed products
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) plays an increasingly important role in marketing, acting as both a product designer and an endorser, yet research predominantly examines these roles in isolation. This study addresses this gap by investigating how consumers’ adoption of AI-designed products is jointly shaped by textual designer disclosure (i.e., AI- vs. human-designed) and visual endorser cues (i.e., human-like vs. animated avatars). This research proposes that consumers integrate these two modalities into a single evaluation, and their adoption intention is shaped by the congruence between textual and visual cues. Drawing on schema-congruity and curiosity theories, this research tests a designer-endorser congruence effect across four studies. Study 1 (N = 240) demonstrates the congruence effect: for an AI-designed product, consumers show higher adoption intention when it is endorsed by an animated (vs. human-like) endorser, whereas the effect is reversed for human-designed products. Study 2 (N = 156) illustrates that perceptual curiosity serves as a mechanism: AI's involvement in design stimulates curiosity, which is then sustained by presenting the endorser in a congruent, animated form. Study 3 (N = 156) validates the mediating effect of perceptual curiosity alongside cognitive mechanisms, i.e., perceived trustworthiness and uncanniness. Study 4 (N = 340) examines how this congruence effect varies across consumers with different dispositional traits and shows that this effect is stronger among those with high anxiety about AI. These findings make a theoretical contribution by introducing designer-endorser congruence as a determinant of product adoption in AI-mediated marketing, and by identifying curiosity as an alternative affective mechanism that complements prior information-processing perspectives. In practice, this study provides insights for leveraging avatar endorsement to induce curiosity and to encourage the adoption of AI-designed products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Multi-task end-to-end portfolio optimization with self-supervised graph attention network
Abstract: End-to-end portfolio methods have attracted considerable attention owing to their capacity to simultaneously optimize the prediction and decision-making processes. Title: Incentivizing continuous personal health data sharing: A multidimensional contract model incorporating privacy concerns and health service needs
Abstract: Sustained health data sharing provides a critical foundation for digital health platforms to deliver proactive health management and personalized services. However, the multidimensional heterogeneity of users in terms of healthcare needs and privacy concerns, together with behavioral biases arising from platform bounded rationality, poses substantial challenges to the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. This study develops an incentive contract comprising a data-sharing duration and a task-based reward. Under the assumption that user types are unobservable, we derive the optimal contracts for two alternative objectives: platform profit maximization and social welfare maximization. We further incorporate reference dependence and loss aversion to characterize platform behavioral biases and compare the resulting contracts under expected utility theory and prospect theory. The results show that user heterogeneity, platform governance objectives, and boundedly rational behavior jointly shape the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. First, this study identifies how multidimensional user heterogeneity can be characterized and screened under information asymmetry. The marginal rate of substitution between users’ demand for health services and their privacy concerns enables the platform to map multidimensional user attributes onto a unified type ordering and induce self-selection through a differentiated menu of contracts. Second, the findings reveal the role of platform governance objectives in shaping incentive mechanisms. Profit maximization and social welfare maximization follow distinct resource-allocation logics, thereby generating different data-sharing durations, task-based rewards, and welfare-distribution structures. Third, this study uncovers the mechanism through which platform bounded rationality affects contract design. Loss aversion does not invariably strengthen or weaken incentives, rather, its effect varies with the platform’s governance objective. Under a profit-oriented objective, loss aversion may lead to an expansion of the incentive contract, whereas under a welfare-oriented objective, it tends to result in a more restrictive contract. Numerical analyses and robustness checks provide further support for these theoretical findings. By examining the information, governance, and behavioral mechanisms underlying incentive design, this study explains how incentives for sustained health data sharing are formed. It enriches the literature on incentive mechanism design for digital health platforms and provides theoretical guidance for platform governance and incentive decisions under information asymmetry and bounded rationality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Fracture mechanical properties and mechanism analysis of structural fiber recycled coarse aggregate concrete
Abstract: To investigate the influence of structural fibers (STF) on the fracture mechanical properties of recycled concrete, three-point bending tests were conducted to study the effects of STF type, STF content, and recycled aggregates (RA) substitution rate on the fracture failure mode, load displacement curve, load CMOD (crack mouth opening displacement) curve, residual bending strength, fracture energy, and fracture toughness of concrete. Finally, a bilinear softening constitutive curve for structural fiber-reinforced recycled concrete (STFRRC) was established based on the double-K fracture model. The results indicate that STF can change the failure mode of concrete and significantly improve its fracture performance; The fracture performance (residual bending strength, fracture energy, and fracture toughness) of STFRRC is positively correlated with STF content and negatively correlated with RA substitution rate. Among the STF types, ESF (End-hooked steel fiber) has the greatest effect on the fracture performance of STFRRC, followed by CSF (Corrugated steel fiber) and, finally, SCSF (Shear corrugated steel fiber). Compared with the non-fiber specimens, STFRRC exhibited improved fracture performance and post-cracking toughness. The bilinear σ−w relationship provides a model-derived representation of the post-cracking tensile softening behavior of STFRRC based on the measured ft, Gf, and CTODc, rather than an independently validated constitutive response. Title: The right endorser for the right stay: How human and AI endorsers shape accommodation booking
Abstract: This research examines how endorser presence and endorser type influence consumers’ accommodation booking intention. Drawing on Embodied Cognition Theory, it shows that endorsers shape booking intention by activating embodied mental simulation. It further examines two hospitality-specific factors, booking purpose and service mode, that influence when human and AI-generated endorsers are more effective. Title: Digital service nudges and consumer adoption of reusable packaging in online retailing: From convenience to circular responsibility
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online retailers increasingly offer reusable express packaging, but adoption remains difficult because sustainable options can conflict with the convenience expectations that define online retailing. This article examines reusable packaging adoption as a circular retail service conversion problem. Across three studies with adult online shoppers, we test how digital service nudges and responsibility framing influence adoption through perceived service friction, perceived environmental efficacy, and sustainable service trust, and how these effects depend on return convenience. Study 1 uses a quota-based, post-stratification-weighted survey to show that decision-relevant service nudges reduce perceived service friction and increase adoption intention, while responsibility framing increases perceived environmental efficacy and sustainable service trust. Study 2 uses a discrete choice experiment to estimate trade-offs among nudge timing, return convenience, deposit/refund rules, delivery delay, environmental benefit visibility, and responsibility framing. Study 3 uses an incentivized simulated checkout task to test behaviorally consequential reusable-packaging choice at the decision point. The results show that return convenience and deposit clarity are stronger adoption drivers than generic environmental claims, and that consumers penalize delivery delay more strongly than they reward verified environmental-benefit information. Decision-point nudges increase reusable-packaging checkout choice more than post-checkout reminders, especially when return convenience is high. Title: Technology and the psychology of experience: A temporal framework

Authors: Huang Z.; Guo Y.; Tong L.; Zhao M.
Title: Resilience asymmetry in city networks: State and private firm linkages across China's four mega-city regions
Abstract: In an increasingly uncertain global environment, the resilience of city networks has become a key indicator of regional stability and adaptability. This paper examines four mega-city regions in China by constructing two ownership-segmented city networks based on state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and privately owned enterprises (POEs). Comparative analysis of their structures and resilience performance reveals systematic “resilience asymmetry” associated with ownership logics. Both networks display a basic center–periphery pattern, but with distinct configurations and shock responses: SOE-based networks form highly centralized, radiating structures with strong resource integration, exhibiting a “weaker resistance—faster recovery” trajectory; POE-based networks exhibit multi-centered, proximity-based structures with greater initial resistance but slower recovery, showing a “stronger resistance—slower recovery” trajectory. Title: An empirical study on the capability of LLMs in decomposing bug reports
Abstract: Bug reports are essential to the software development life cycle. They help developers track and resolve issues, but are often difficult to process due to their complexity, which can delay resolution and affect software quality. This study investigates whether large language models (LLMs) can assist developers in automatically decomposing complex bug reports into smaller, self-contained units, making them easier to understand and address. We first conducted an empirical study using 127 resolved privacy-related bug reports collected from Apache Jira. We evaluated ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V1 using zero-shot and few-shot prompting. Under zero-shot prompting, the models correctly decomposed only 10 and 11 reports, respectively. Few-shot prompting increased their true decomposition rates by 140% (10 vs. 24) and 163.64% (11 vs. 29), respectively, although the overall accuracy remained limited. To examine whether the findings generalize beyond privacy-related reports and to expand the dataset size, we further analyzed 127 security-related bug reports using GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. We compared zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and persona prompting. Few-shot prompting achieved the best performance for both models, correctly decomposing 89 reports with GPT-5.5 and 51 reports with DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Across the experiments, we identify a concrete failure taxonomy for LLM-based bug report decomposition, including over-decomposition, over-analysis, incorrect interpretation of solutions, lacking key information, and empty output. Over-decomposition is the most common failure mode, suggesting that LLMs often struggle to distinguish independent bug units from supporting information such as logs, code snippets, background context, and proposed fixes. Title: Artificial intelligence in ports: A comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Ports, as a key component of transportation, have increasingly relied on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability. Despite the rapid growth of AI-related research in ports, a structured and integrated understanding of how major AI fields contribute to port operations remains lacking. Title: AI companions as hyper-attachment and caregiving targets
Abstract: How should we make sense of people's interactions with AI companions—conversational systems built for ongoing, emotionally meaningful relationships? First, I argue these interactions should be understood as attachment relationships, since users display all four established markers: proximity maintenance, separation distress, safe haven, and secure base, although evidence for secure base effects remains most tentative. Title: From image to action: How social proof turns brand image into repurchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study examines how social proof shapes the relationship between brand image and repurchase intention in an emerging digital marketplace, distinguishing three forms that operate through different mechanisms: user-generated content, brand ambassadors, and testimonials. Because online markets involve considerable information overload, consumers rely heavily on others' evaluations to reduce decision risk; however, forms of social proof vary in authenticity and persuasive effectiveness, and prior research has largely treated them as a single, uniformly positive construct. A two-study, mixed-methods design set in Vietnam addresses this gap. Study 1 applies a Vietnamese-optimized RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach) model to social media comments to surface authentic consumer sentiment, providing exploratory, triangulating context without constituting a direct hypothesis test. Study 2 tests the proposed relationships using moderated regression on survey responses from 394 active Vietnamese online shoppers. Results show that brand image exerts a strong positive direct effect on repurchase intention. User-generated content significantly strengthens this relationship, with the largest effect among consumers holding moderate brand-image perceptions. Brand ambassadors moderate the relationship but show a bounded pattern, with diminishing influence once brand image is already strong. Testimonials exert a dual effect: they amplify the brand image-repurchase link when perceived as credible, but, when seen as commercially motivated, they independently trigger skepticism and weaken repurchase intention. Title: Knowledge domains in particulate multiphase flow in porous media based on bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Particulate multiphase flow in porous media underpins research in energy exploitation, environmental protection, and geological engineering. Deep insights into such flow systems are critical for revealing subsurface fluid migration mechanisms, improving resource recovery efficiency, and assessing geological-engineering safety. However, a systematic bibliometric delineation of its knowledge structure and evolutionary trajectories remains lacking, particularly at the intersection of solid particulate phases, multiphase fluids, porous structures and particle-related transport. This study retrieved 936 records from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015–July 2026) using combined search terms covering particulate, multiphase, porous-media and transport concepts. After manual screening for eligibility, 912 publications were retained and analyzed via VOSviewer, CiteSpace, Bibliometrix and SCImago Graphica, mapping publication trends, collaboration networks, citation impacts and thematic evolution. Annual output increased from 35 publications in 2015 to 88 in 2025, with a compound annual growth rate of 9.7%. China ranked first with 239 publications (26.2%) and a total collaboration link strength of 83, followed by the United States with 150 publications and a comparable link strength of 82. Six core keyword clusters were identified: multiphase flow, mass transfer, porous media, particle hydrodynamics, lattice Boltzmann method, and discrete element method. Chemical Engineering Science was the most productive journal, Powder Technology had the highest average citations per article (33.6), and the top-cited lattice Boltzmann method review received 889 citations. These findings clarify the domain's intellectual boundaries and indicate that experimentally validated, cross-scale particle–fluid–pore interactions remain the central research priority. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
