Title: A knowledge-driven decision-support reference architecture for integrating cost estimation and optimization in open-cut pipeline construction
Abstract: Open-cut pipeline construction (OCPC) involves complex cost behavior driven by uncertain and interdependent factors, making it a challenging domain for decision-making. Although machine learning, simulation, and optimization methods have been widely studied individually, their integration into coherent knowledge-driven decision-support systems remains limited. Title: Traditional or New Media: Impact of Risk Perception and Government Trust on Media Trust in Various Risk Scenarios in China
Abstract: This study aims to explore the influence of public risk perception on media trust in different risk scenarios, examining the role of government trust therein. Risk scenarios include known and unknown risks. Media types are categorized as traditional and new. Based on data from 1,925 survey responses collected in China, the study employs multiple linear regression models and moderation analysis. The findings suggest a significant positive predictive relationship between risk perception and public media trust. However, this positive effect substantially diminishes under conditions of heightened risk uncertainty. Irrespective of risk uncertainty, the influence of risk perception on trust in traditional media consistently surpasses its impact on trust in new media. Furthermore, government trust emerges as a pivotal factor affecting public trust in media. Nevertheless, in contexts characterized by elevated risk ambiguity, the beneficial effects of government trust on media trust experience a marked reduction. Similarly, government trust exerts a more robust positive influence on trust in traditional media compared to its impact on trust in new media. Lastly, government trust serves as a moderator in the relationship between risk perception and media trust, with the nature of this moderation varying according to different media types and risk scenarios. These findings broaden the research scope on public trust in the media and provide valuable insights for entities involved in public risk management.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: One cart, many channels: How real-time inventory visibility shapes trust and purchase continuity in cross-border omnichannel retail

Abstract: This study isolates inventory data latency as an operational primitive of omnichannel retail, evaluating its impact on cross-channel purchase continuity and consumer trust. Title: The public funding of the New Space Economy. Confronting public procurement and public-private partnership
Abstract: This paper confronts public funding mechanisms in the New Space Economy (NSE). NSE refers to the rise of private actors’ activities in space; however, public funding remains crucial. Title: Perceptions of expertise and its development among critical care trainees and staff physicians: A qualitative interview study
Abstract: Background In highly specialized fields such as critical care medicine (CCM), understanding how expertise is defined and developed is essential for both clinical practice and education. Title: Dual replacement strategies for systems with dependent failures under lemon laws
Abstract: Lemon laws mandate vehicle replacement or refund when repair attempts or downtime exceed statutory thresholds. Abstract: This paper develops an on-board, knowledge-driven decision system for autonomous beam management in massive LEO constellations, in which a bounded local knowledge base and a provably objective-aligned inference rule replace the ground-side optimization loop that current constellations depend on. Title: Educational strategies grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour for sustainable food safety culture evolvement
Abstract: Food safety (FS) culture is a behavioural phenomenon that shapes the food safety and hygiene behaviour of people across all organisational levels, contributing to the prevention of foodborne diseases. Although interventions can strengthen FS-culture, evidence on how to systematically develop it remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) in improving food handlers’ behavioural intentions and strengthening the prevailing FS-culture within a Brazilian military food service. A quasi-experimental study was conducted between 2022 and 2025 with 137 food handlers and seven quality managers. Data collection occurred at three time points (t = 0 in 2023, t = 1 in 2024, t = 2 in 2025). FS-culture was evaluated using a mixed-methods approach, while TPB constructs (i.e., subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, attitude, and intention) were measured through a validated questionnaire. Educational interventions were designed to address the lowest-scoring FS-culture element and the TPB constructs most strongly associated with behavioural intentions. FS-culture changed from active (score 2) at t = 0 to active–proactive (score 2-3) at t = 1, with significant improvements in knowledge and communication elements. At t = 2, FS-culture remained at an active-proactive level. Perceived behavioural control was the strongest predictor of intention at baseline (β = 0.27, p = 0.004). Interventions were associated with an increase in attitude scores between t = 0 and t = 1 (p = 0.002) and t = 1 and t = 2 (p = 0.009). Authors: Fang C.; Guo F.; Yu M.; Belpaeme T.
Title: Show me your care: The impact of multimodal attentive behaviours for robots on user experience in a healthcare context
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: While robot attentive behaviours hold significant potential for improving user experience in healthcare contexts, how multimodal cues are jointly interpreted by users remains poorly understood. This study examines how multimodal attentive behaviours shape user experience in a simulated ward-round interaction with a Pepper robot acting as a healthcare assistant. A 2 × 2 × 2 within-subject experiment manipulated attentive behaviours across auditory, visual, and tactile modalities, including voice pitch (low vs high), lean forward (with vs without), and robot-initiated touch (with vs without). Subjective perceptions (questionnaires), visual attention (eye-tracking), and neural activity (functional near-infrared spectroscopy, fNIRS) were measured. Results showed that a high-pitched voice, a forward-leaning posture, and robot-initiated touch positively influence users’ perceptions. Robot-initiated touch attracted visual attention and was associated with increased neural activity in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Significant interactions revealed a cross-modal compensatory mechanism, whereby the absence of cues in one modality increased sensitivity to cues in another. Both visual and tactile cues independently improved user perceptions compared to the auditory-only condition, while combining visual and tactile modalities yielded diminishing incremental benefits. These findings provide converging subjective, behavioural, and neurophysiological evidence that multimodal attentive behaviours can shape users’ experience through cross-modal compensatory mechanisms rather than linearly additive effects. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Natural disasters and political beliefs
Abstract: This paper examines whether local exposure to extreme weather affects support for national climate and energy policies in Switzerland. We construct a municipality-referendum panel linking high-resolution MeteoSwiss data on extreme heat and intense precipitation to municipal voting outcomes in federal referenda. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design and Callaway–Sant’Anna event-study estimators, we compare municipalities first exposed to extreme weather shocks with not-yet-treated municipalities. The results provide little evidence that extreme weather increases support for environmental policy. If anything, the estimates point in the opposite direction: in selected rainfall specifications, environmental yes-shares decline by around 2.7–2.8 percentage points after extreme shocks. These estimates are based on small, geographically concentrated treated cohorts and should therefore be interpreted as cohort-specific. The findings are consistent with the view that salient local shocks may reduce willingness to support costly environmental policies, rather than producing experience-based updating in favor of climate action. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Stochastic inversion of multivariate uniform-distribution-preserving transformations

Title: Integrated scheduling of single-track channels, tugboats, continuous berths and quay cranes via learning-driven multi-objective artificial bee colony algorithms
Abstract: Container terminals, pivotal hubs for modern maritime logistics, underpin economic development and environmental protection. Furthermore, a learning-based local refinement strategy with adaptive neighborhood selection methods is designed. Title: The evolution of robo-advisors in FinTech: a global bibliometric and thematic analysis, review and future agenda
Abstract: This study presents a longitudinal bibliometric and thematic analysis of the global robo-advisory research landscape from 2017 to 2026, using a total of 384 peer-reviewed publications selected from an initial dataset of 865 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus databases. By employing co-citation, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis, the study attempts to highlight the structural and conceptual evolution of the field. Bibliographic coupling shows the central presence of a trust- and intention-focused core, supported by broad adoption and behavioural literature, and a newer wave of extending the field outward into more outcome-based peripheries. The keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis differentiates well-known themes from accelerating ones. AI, trust, LLMs, UTAUT, perceived risk and value, anthropomorphism, GenAI, and DeFi remain robust across temporal specifications. The study concludes by providing actionable implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers with a call for future research by converting the findings into four research programs: adaptive and personalized investment intelligence, human–AI collaborative advisory, responsible and autonomous financial AI, and programmable and expanded investment ecosystems to ensure responsible and inclusive development of robo-advisory systems across diverse financial ecosystems. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Zhu Y.; Han Y.; Li B.; Qi X.
Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of biomass energy carbon reduction in China
Abstract: This study assesses the spatiotemporal evolution, driving mechanisms, and future potential of biomass energy carbon reduction (BCR) in China using data for 31 mainland provincial-level units and a balanced 30-province analytical sample from 2012 to 2022, with projections to 2030. BCR is defined as the theoretical CO2 reduction from replacing coal-fired electricity with energy recovered from agricultural residues, forestry and orchard waste, livestock manure, sewage-derived organic matter, and municipal solid waste; it is not a project-level life-cycle estimate. Biomass-resource accounting was integrated with Moran's I, standard deviational ellipses, fixed-effects STIRPAT, spatial dynamic panel models, Random Forest with PDP/SHAP, and province-specific GA-LSTM forecasting. Results show significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.143–0.193, p < 0.05) and a northeast-to-southwest centroid shift. Population scale and energy consumption structure show significant positive linear associations (coefficients 0.66 and 1.05, p < 0.01), whereas environmental regulation and industrial structure show negative associations. Random Forest achieved R2 = 0.844, RMSE = 13.98 Mt CO2, and MAE = 6.43 Mt CO2; population scale (38.25%) and environmental regulation (30.59%) were the leading predictors, with nonlinear and threshold-like responses. Spatial dynamic estimates confirm path dependence (0.103) and cross-provincial spillovers. GA-LSTM projects aggregate BCR to increase from 1.854 Gt CO2 in 2023 to 2.092 Gt CO2 in 2030, led by Heilongjiang, Henan, and Shandong. These findings support differentiated infrastructure investment, cross-regional logistics, regulatory coordination, and technology transfer. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Data-driven decision-making in retail: Impacts on firm performance and consumer outcomes
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Concept: Big data and advanced analytics have radically transformed the retail industry's strategic landscape. In response, companies have adopted data-driven decision-making (DDDM) models as a competitive weapon to address these challenges. Objective: This study examines the multidimensional relationship between the intensity of DDDM adoption and two outcomes: firm performance and consumer welfare. It also investigates how firm size and retail subsector moderates these relationships. Tools: Using a mixed-methods design, we surveyed 386 retail firms across six subsectors and surveyed retail executives regarding application domain barriers in the United States. Quantitative methods included multiple regression, one-way ANOVA, and hierarchical moderated regression, supplemented by surveys from 1200 consumers measuring privacy percept (β = 0.61, p < 0.001, R2 = 0.492). Hierarchical modeling confirmed that firm size (ΔR2 = 0.026, p = 0.001) and specialized sectors like electronics and grocery retail act as significant positive moderators. Consumer satisfaction, product availability, and shopping experience quality improved significantly with increasing DDDM intensity. However, 61.3% of consumers express concern about excessive data collection, while 53.6% acknowledge that personalized offers enhance their shopping experience, revealing a 7.7 percentage point privacy paradox accompanied by a notable trust deficit (only 31.6% consumer trust). Application: These findings provide retail managers with ROI estimates (ranging from 2.4× to 3.2×) for analytics investments across application domains while identifying key infrastructure bottlenecks (52% legacy system friction). Title: Personality traits add incremental value beyond food choice motives in predicting food-group consumption
Abstract: Background: Big Five personality traits and food choice motives are well-established correlates of dietary behavior, but they are rarely examined together. If motives are the mechanism through which traits operate, trait effects should largely disappear once motives are controlled; if traits also act through channels people do not report as reasons, dispositional variance should survive. This study tested these competing accounts. Methods: In a Brazilian adult sample (N = 449), participants completed the NEO-FFI-R, the Food Choice Questionnaire (FCQ), and single-item weekly frequency measures for six food groups (meat, fish, dairy, eggs, vegetables, and fruits). We estimated Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control and hierarchical regressions entering sociodemographics, then food choice motives, then Big Five traits. Results: Openness to experience and conscientiousness were the most consistent trait correlates, in the direction reported meta-analytically. Food choice motives accounted for most of the explained variance, yet personality contributed small but reliable increments for five of the six groups: meat, fish, dairy, eggs, and vegetables (ΔR2 = 0.025–0.038). This incremental explained variance was driven mainly by openness, extraversion, and conscientiousness, with no reliable increment for fruit consumption. Conclusions: By controlling proximal motives, the findings indicate that broad dispositions are not fully reducible to the reasons people give for their food choices. The single exception, fruit, was also the group most tightly governed by explicit motives, suggesting that the division of explanatory work between traits and motives is food-specific. Title: Artificial intelligence-based employee selection in tourism and hospitality: Justice, inclusion, and gender differences in resume screening and interviews
Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in human resource management, its role in tourism and hospitality hiring remains underexplored. This study investigates job applicants’ perceptions of AI in employee selection, focusing on resume screening and interviews. Drawing on fairness heuristic theory and social role theory, we examine how AI affects perceived justice, inclusion, and organizational attractiveness. Four scenario-based experiments and one qualitative study were conducted with job applicants comparing AI-based and human-based selection methods. Results show that human recruiters are generally perceived as more just and inclusive, enhancing organizational attractiveness. However, gender moderates these effects: females favor AI-based resume screening, whereas males are more receptive to AI-based interviews. These findings provide insights for organizations seeking to integrate AI into employee selection while maintaining justice and inclusion. Title: Designing the waiting experience: How order tracking shapes consumer engagement and loyalty
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The post-purchase waiting period is an important yet underexamined stage of the digital customer journey. Consumers increasingly interact with order tracking systems during this phase, yet research has treated tracking primarily as a logistics tool rather than an experiential touchpoint. This study examines how tracking experience design shapes consumer engagement and loyalty through two psychological mechanisms: perceived control and anticipation. Drawing on perceived control theory and anticipatory utility theory, we develop a framework proposing that richer tracking interfaces enhance consumers' sense of predictability and forward-looking excitement, which in turn strengthen post-purchase engagement and loyalty. We test this framework using a three-study design combining scale validation (N = 240), a between-subjects experiment (N = 180), and structural equation modeling with a large field sample (N = 920) of online shoppers. Across all studies, richer tracking experiences consistently increase perceived control and anticipation, both of which stimulate engagement during the waiting period and contribute to customer loyalty. Engagement further mediates the effects of perceived control and anticipation on loyalty. Title: A domain-differentiated stress perspective on turnover intention
Abstract: This study examines the associations of job stress and work–family conflict with turnover intention among lecturers employed in private higher education institutions in Yunnan Province, China. Drawing on conservation of resources theory and a dual-stressor perspective, job stress and work–family conflict are conceptualized as distinct but potentially interrelated sources of resource depletion that may contribute to withdrawal cognition. Lecturers in Chinese private higher education institutions may face substantial teaching responsibilities, administrative demands, performance expectations, limited institutional resources, and employment uncertainty, making this an important context for examining turnover intention. Using a quantitative survey design, data were collected through the Wenjuanxing online platform. After data screening, 374 valid responses were retained. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to assess the measurement model, test the hypothesized relationships, and evaluate the model’s predictive relevance. The results showed that both job stress and work–family conflict were significantly and positively associated with turnover intention. Work–family conflict showed the stronger association, suggesting that difficulties reconciling professional and family responsibilities may play a particularly important role in lecturers’ intentions to leave. However, the interaction between job stress and work–family conflict was not statistically significant. Thus, the findings did not provide evidence that the association between work–family conflict and turnover intention varied across different levels of job stress. The model explained 62.1% of the variance in turnover intention, indicating substantial explanatory power. This study contributes to the literature by comparing the direct associations of work-domain and work–family-interface stressors with turnover intention in private higher education. Title: Identifying and prioritizing key factors influencing electric vehicle fast-charging infrastructure planning in China: A Delphi study
Abstract: The rapid expansion of China's new energy vehicle market has intensified demand for a coordinated, equitable fast-charging infrastructure system. Despite substantial growth, regional disparities, technical incompatibilities, and fragmented governance arrangements continue to constrain the efficiency and long-term sustainability of network deployment. Anchored in diffusion of innovation and institutional theory, the analysis integrates technological, economic, spatial, social, environmental, and governance dimensions into a coherent evaluative framework. Six principal factors emerged: governance and institutional coordination; economic and financial viability; technological integration and standardization; social equity and user-oriented considerations; spatial and urban planning; and environmental sustainability. Governance and institutional coordination ranked highest in importance, with strong consensus among participants (Kendall's W = 0.696, p < 0.001). Title: Multi-cue judgments of food healthfulness: Evidence for distinct consumer decision strategies

Abstract: Consumers frequently evaluate the healthfulness of packaged foods based on multiple on-pack cues presented simultaneously. While prior research has extensively examined individual signals such as nutrition labels or claims, less is known about how consumers integrate competing information and whether they rely on consistent or heterogeneous decision strategies. This study addresses this gap by investigating how different types of product-related cues jointly shape perceived healthfulness and by identifying distinct patterns of cue weighting across consumers. Using a mixed-methods design, we first conducted focus groups to explore how consumers conceptualize healthfulness in real-world evaluation contexts. At the aggregate level, ingredient-related information exerted the strongest influence, followed by claims and vitamin information, while calorie information played a more limited role. However, segmentation based on individual-level importance weights revealed three distinct health inference strategies: consumers primarily guided by ingredient simplicity, those anchored in energy-related information, and those relying on claim-based cues validated by nutrition tables. Accounting for these strategies substantially improved explanatory power, indicating that heterogeneity in healthfulness judgments is systematic rather than random. Title: Psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation influences safety behaviour: A moderated serial mediation of psychological safety climate, employee resilience, and ethical leadership

Title: Modular microgrids and their deployment: Aligning technological interoperability with integrators’ customization
Abstract: Modularity is recognized as a strategic instrument for advancing microgrid deployment and development. Title: Payroll taxes, firm dynamism, and aggregate productivity
Abstract: This study examines the impact of payroll-tax enforcement on firm dynamism and its implications for aggregate productivity. We exploit China's Social Security Collection Agency Reform, which transferred responsibility for collecting social-insurance contributions from local social-insurance agencies to tax authorities, thereby strengthening enforcement. We show that the reform increased firms’ social-insurance contributions, shifted workers toward informal employment without reducing overall nonagricultural employment, and reduced new firm entry while weakening incumbent firms’ profitability and investment. Title: “It's all just code”: How is responsibility embedded (or not) in the work of a team of software engineers?
Abstract: Recent research has documented how software can sometimes contribute to harm and inequality, affecting individuals, societies, and the environment. We argue that human values embedded in software, consciously or unconsciously during design and development, play a significant role in producing these outcomes. In other words, to understand responsibility in software engineering, it is crucial to understand how Software Engineers (SEs) incorporate responsibility into their practices, and if or how they reflect on the potential impact of their work. The research reported here probes this assertion by focusing on a team of research SEs involved in developing a commercial source code clone detection tool. Through reflexive thematic analysis of in-depth interviews, with meta-reflections from the SEs Principal Investigator, we offer a detailed account of the practices and artefacts referenced when these professionals reflect on responsibility in their work. Our analysis suggests that the team does not consider responsibility as a singular, unified concept. Instead, reflections on potential negative software impacts and mitigation strategies vary depending on whether they relate to the institutional/organisational context, the specific task, or the intended use. Overall, these SEs tend to perceive software as neutral or inherently beneficial, which, in turn, feeds into a lack of practice of engaging in speculation about the broader implications of the technologies they work with. To address these gaps, we propose a paradigm shift toward an infrastructural view of responsibility - interdisciplinary, sociotechnical, and situated – embedded within the diverse practices and organisational cultures of SE teams operating in different contexts. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Effect of AI authorship disclosure on purchase intention in cultural tourism souvenirs: The mediating roles of perceived effort and authenticity
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) expands in cultural tourism souvenir design and disclosure policies evolve, evidence remains limited on how AI authorship disclosure shapes responses across nationality groups and products. Drawing on signaling theory, two studies compared consumers from China and the U.S. across three disclosure conditions: unlabeled, human–AI co-created, and AI-generated. Study 1 used tourism postcard stimuli (N = 1110), and Study 2 used mug and tourism tote bag stimuli (N = 1255). Both studies found that disclosure affected purchase intention and interacted significantly with nationality. Differences across disclosure conditions were significant among participants from the U.S. but not among those from China. In Study 1, the unlabeled and human–AI co-created conditions did not differ, and both exceeded the AI-generated condition. In Study 2, the unlabeled condition exceeded both disclosed conditions for both products, whereas the latter two did not differ. AI-generated disclosure was consistently associated with lower purchase intention than no disclosure, whereas the relative position of human–AI co-created disclosure differed between studies. Parallel mediation analyses showed indirect effects through perceived effort and perceived authenticity. Perceived effort effects were significant for both comparisons with the unlabeled condition across three examined products, whereas the human–AI co-created versus unlabeled authenticity effect was nonsignificant in Study 1 but significant in Study 2. Nationality moderated some, but not all, indirect effects. Thus, firms should not assume that human–AI co-creation enhances responses and should consider clarifying human contribution and pretesting disclosure strategies across products and national markets. © 2026 The Authors

Author full names: Mislin, Alexandra (14063745600)
Title: Hidden dissatisfaction after agreement: Post-negotiation perceptual alignment
Abstract: Negotiations continue to have consequences after an agreement or impasse. When parties reach a deal, value is often created only later, as they implement commitments, adapt to uncertainty, or decide whether to negotiate again. This review introduces post-negotiation perceptual alignment, how accurately a negotiator understands the counterpart's post-negotiation experience. Integrating research on subjective value, interpersonal perception, and post-agreement outcomes, I distinguish four states: recognized satisfaction, recognized dissatisfaction, overestimated dissatisfaction, and hidden dissatisfaction. Hidden dissatisfaction is consequential because it creates a false sense of success where one party treats agreement as evidence that the negotiation went well while the counterpart carries forward negative appraisals that remain unrecognized and unaddressed. Recent research suggests tactics that appear successful at agreement can impose unrecognized social and relational costs. I review why misalignment arises, emphasizing how negotiators’ imperfect inferences about counterparts’ experiences can combine with social pressures that discourage dissatisfied parties from speaking up. I conclude by outlining directions for measuring alignment and testing how negotiators can recognize and respond to dissatisfaction after negotiations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Striking the right balance: How sanctions and consequences of customer misbehavior shape hotel guests’ fairness perceptions and rebooking intentions
Abstract: Customer misbehavior in hospitality has attracted attention, yet little is known about how observer guests interpret sanctions imposed on misbehaving guests as rule-enforcement signals. Because observers often outnumber offenders and judge a hotel's response, their reactions may shape fairness perceptions and rebooking intentions. We investigate this through a scenario-based online experiment with U.S. participants (Study 1) and a scenario-based framed field experiment with hotel guests in Senegal (Study 2), manipulating sanction severity and observer guest impact. Across studies, moderate sanctions were judged fairer on average than no or severe sanctions, suggesting that observers do not simply prefer stronger sanctions. Effects on rebooking intentions were more mixed: in Study 1, moderate sanctions produced higher rebooking intentions than no sanction but did not differ significantly from severe sanctions; in Study 2, moderate sanctions produced higher rebooking intentions than severe sanctions but did not differ significantly from no sanction. Title: Digital finance momentum and indonesian government bond yields: Evidence from an augmented affine term structure model
Abstract: This study examines the determinants of the Indonesian government bond yield curve by incorporating a digital finance momentum (DFM) factor into an augmented affine term structure model (ATSM). The study is motivated by the persistent inflation puzzle in Indonesia, where conventional inflation indicators frequently exhibit a weak empirical relationship with government bond yields despite their central role in macrofinance theory. To address this issue, the study introduces a novel DFM index constructed using principal component analysis (PCA) from high-frequency indicators of digital financial activity, including QRIS transaction values, fintech peer-to-peer lending, and e-money transactions. The first principal component explains 82.3% of the total variance across these indicators, supporting the validity of the DFM index as a unified single-factor measure of digital financial expansion. The empirical analysis uses monthly Indonesian data from January 2015 to December 2024 and estimates the model using Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques. The results show that the DFM factor significantly affects both the level and slope of the Indonesian yield curve and explains a substantial share of forecast error variance, particularly for medium- and long-term bond yields. In contrast, core inflation remains statistically weak in explaining yield dynamics. Impulse response analysis further indicates that shocks originating from digital financial activity generate persistent increases in government bond yields comparable to those produced by monetary policy shocks. These findings suggest that digital financial development has become an important transmission channel influencing macroeconomic expectations, liquidity conditions, and systemic risk in Indonesia. Under the rational expectations hypothesis, investors incorporate high-frequency digital financial signals into expectations of future inflation more rapidly than conventional macroeconomic indicators. Title: Corporate social responsibility and socio-economic impacts in the mining sector: A bibliometric review of local community empowerment and sustainable development
Abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of the scholarly literature on corporate social responsibility (CSR) and its socio-economic implications in the mining sector, with a focus on local community empowerment and sustainable development outcomes. Using the Scopus database, a systematic search yielded 217 documents published between 2015 and 2025, which were then refined into 182 articles and reviews through structured inclusion and exclusion criteria. The study covers three main dimensions: (1) the evolution of mining-related CSR publication trends over the period 2015–2025; (2) the identification of dominant countries, institutions, and authors along with evolving collaboration patterns; and (3) thematic clusters that shape the intellectual architecture of the field, specifically how these clusters reflect the tension between corporate interests and stakeholder rights as theorized by Stakeholder Theory. The analysis was conducted using VOSviewer and the Bibliometrix package in R to map publication trends, author productivity, international collaboration networks, and thematic keyword clusters. The findings show a progressive growth in publications, reaching a peak of 37 documents in 2023, reflecting increasing academic and regulatory attention to corporate accountability in the extractive industries. Five thematic clusters were identified: CSR and indigenous peoples, economic sustainability and the resource curse, artisanal mining and local livelihoods, coal mining and occupational health, and a methodological cluster related to data mining in computer science. The United States and Australia lead in publication volume, while Ghana records the highest citation-per-document ratio. Indonesia, while present in the corpus, exhibits limited citation visibility, indicating significant room for increased global research engagement. The study identified critical gaps, including a dearth of longitudinal CSR assessments, limited multinational accountability research, and underrepresentation of Southeast Asian perspectives as urgent research priorities for advancing equitable mining governance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Strategic decision-making in negotiation: Lessons from behavioral game theory
Abstract: Game theory provides a language and a set of tools for analyzing behavior in a wide range of strategic interactions, including negotiation. Here, we illustrate behavioral game theory's contributions to the study of negotiation, with a particular focus on the role that communication and emotion play in negotiation. We explain how researchers can use games to study various negotiation phenomena, including the effects of power, information asymmetry, and identity on negotiation processes and outcomes. Title: Enhancing customer decision-making through 3D body-scan-enabled personalization in brick-and-mortar stores: The moderating roles of human support and technology intrusiveness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Brick-and-mortar stores remain vital in today's retail landscape. To stay competitive, they must deliver experiences that go beyond what online retailers offer, increasingly relying on technology-driven personalization and convenience. Although retailers are investing in technology-enabled personalization (TEP), empirical evidence of its effectiveness remains limited. Across three scenario-based experiments and one field experiment in two product categories (lingerie and jeans), we demonstrate that TEP, specifically 3D body-scan technology, enhances decision convenience and subsequently fosters word-of-mouth (WOM) intentions, but only when human-enabled personalization (HEP) is absent. However, when HEP is present, TEP does not seem to offer additional customer benefits in this study's context. Although we hypothesized that perceived intrusiveness would further qualify the interaction between TEP and HEP, this three-way interaction was not supported. Instead, the findings indicate that perceived intrusiveness directly qualifies the effectiveness of TEP. Specifically, when technology intrusiveness is perceived as low, TEP enhances decision convenience, which in turn fosters WOM intentions. Conversely, high perceived intrusiveness of the technology used reverses this effect, diminishing convenience and indirectly reducing WOM intentions. These findings advance retail personalization research in brick-and-mortar stores by identifying when the examined form of TEP, a 3D body-scanning technology, is most effective in a fashion retail setting and offer managerial guidance for strategically implementing this technology alongside HEP to optimize in-store experiences while safeguarding retailers' cost efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: AI and negotiation: Facilitating learning or Fostering dependency?
Abstract: AI is being used in negotiation teaching and training both to promote learning and to facilitate planning for and executing a negotiation. This is a review of current empirical research on the relationships between AI negotiation interventions and learning and dependency. It categorizes AI negotiation interventions by practice, coaching, and feedback. It evaluates their effects on learning with respect to knowledge, satisfaction, behavior, and outcomes. Socratic coaching and post negotiation feedback and reflection appear to facilitate learning. However, interactive explicit AI coaching during planning or negotiation may risk dependency. Rather than dependency due to laziness, motivated students may defer to AI expertise. Alternatively, they may be overloaded by dynamic AI advice. The review concludes that there are many opportunities for future research on the question of if, why, and how AI can facilitate negotiators’ learning versus dependency. Research that looks broadly at learning, that compares separate versus packages of AI interventions, and that identifies mechanisms behind learning versus dependency is especially needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Reliability assessment modeling of multi-component series systems considering phase-type shocks and multiple degradation pathways
Source title: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics
Abstract: In order to solve the reliability evaluation problem of multi-component series systems affected by multiple impact sources, this paper proposes a unified modeling framework. Traditional approaches typically assume mutual independence among degradation paths and between degradation and shock processes, which may lead to errors. The proposed framework is capable of joint modeling (1) the dynamic impact of each shock source on multiple components, and (2) the strong statistical dependence among multiple degradation paths within each component. Specifically, vine copulas are employed to flexibly capture high-dimensional dependencies among degradation processes without restrictive parametric assumptions, while phase-type distributions are used to represent cumulative damage from mixed-type shocks in a tractable and general manner. Under this framework, an analytical reliability function for the system is derived and its effectiveness is validated through a case study on MEMS oscillators and sensitivity analyses. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Exploring livelihood assets among inland fishing communities: Evidence from the Sungai Pahang, Malaysia
Abstract: The Inland fishing community consisted of Inland fishermen and cage fish farmers. They are among the vulnerable rural groups that require economic assistance. Their dependence on natural resources results in unstable income and increased vulnerability. The vulnerability affects their well-being and livelihoods. Therefore, this study helps by addressing livelihood assets that help minimise vulnerability among the inland fishing community. This paper aims to identify and explore the livelihood assets of inland fishermen and cage fish farmers along the Sungai Pahang. The study employs the Sustainable Livelihood Framework (SLF) to identify five livelihood assets: human, natural, financial, physical, and social assets. A survey was conducted among 521 respondents, including 261 inland fishermen and 260 cage fish farmers, using a structured questionnaire. The study was conducted in five districts along the Sungai Pahang Jerantut, Temerloh, Bera, Maran, and Pekan. The data was then analysed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to identify the main dimensions of the five livelihood assets within the inland fishing community groups. The data were also checked with reliability coefficients (Cronbach’s alpha). The findings show that inland fishermen depend heavily on financial assets 79.53% variance and physical assets 76.48% variance, highlighting the importance of access to credit and fishing gear for their livelihoods. In contrast, cage fish farmers mainly rely on social assets, accounting for 77.96% of the variance, and human assets, accounting for 69.67 of % variance. This reflects the cage fish farmers' reliance on relevant government institutions for support, training & skills, health, and experience to sustain cage fish production. Although both community groups share the same river ecosystem, their needs is differ, highlighting the diverse in main livelihood assets within riverine communities. However, both communities identify natural assets as a weak livelihood dimension, reflecting their shared vulnerability. Policy interventions in Malaysia should therefore prioritise river conservation, stricter pollution control, sustainable fishing and aquaculture practices, and community-based environmental awareness programmes. Relevant agencies, including the Department of Environment Malaysia, should collaborate with inland fishing communities to implement integrated, participatory environmental management strategies that enhance livelihood resilience and ensure the long-term sustainability of the Sungai Pahang ecosystem. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Artificial intelligence and public sector transformation: A systematic literature review on applications, governance and acceptability factors
Abstract: The public sector is undergoing a profound digital transformation characterised by the increasing integration of artificial intelligence into its management control practices. Concurrently, the optimisation of public performance and accountability has emerged as a central concern among scholars, particularly within the broader context of digital transition. This period of structural change calls for renewed forms of governance and organisational steering grounded in innovative and adaptive approaches. Research on artificial intelligence in public administration has developed significantly since the early 2020s, although the effective adoption of these technologies continues to present substantial challenges. This article offers a systematic review of the literature published between 2020 and 2025, conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines to ensure methodological rigour and reliability. The content analysis is based on a corpus of twenty-five selected articles. The findings indicate that the adoption of artificial intelligence in public management control remains a critical issue. AI has contributed to innovation across five principal domains: financial auditing, budget forecasting, operational optimisation, public health, and legal support. These developments open promising avenues for enhancing the quality of public management, particularly through the effective implementation of technological innovations, the strengthening of institutional adaptability and resilience, the development of essential digital competencies, the cultivation of critical engagement with algorithmic systems, and the reinforcement of digital literacy among public officials. Nevertheless, significant ethical challenges persist, including algorithmic opacity, discriminatory bias, and tensions between efficiency and equity. Addressing these concerns requires the establishment of appropriate governance frameworks and the consolidation of broader societal acceptance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: When do sustainability-related fashion reviews become helpful? The credibility role of verified purchase in online retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online reviews are an important source of information in digital retailing, yet not all reviews are equally useful to consumers. This study examines whether sustainability-related content is associated with online review helpfulness and whether verified purchase status conditions this relationship. Using 1,680,956 Amazon Fashion reviews, sustainability-related content is identified through a two-stage procedure combining a keyword pre-filter with large language model–assisted semantic classification and is integrated with review-, product-, and reviewer-level information. The main analysis employs a full-sample Negative Binomial model with product-level clustered standard errors, review-age exposure and review-specificity controls, and an empirically estimated NB2 dispersion parameter. Sustainability-related content is negatively associated with expected helpfulness among unverified reviews (β=−0.763), whereas verified purchase status is positively associated with helpfulness (β=0.596). The interaction between sustainability-related content and verified purchase status is positive and statistically significant (β=0.958). A formal linear-combination test shows that the combined sustainability effect among verified reviews is positive (β,=0.195p=0.023), corresponding to approximately 21.5% more expected helpful votes. Binary Logit and OLS models, year and month fixed effects, and product-type proxy fixed effects support the same credibility-contingent pattern. Title: Trust in algorithmic governance: How algorithmic control and fairness shape justice perceptions and employee voice in luxury hotels
Abstract: Algorithmic management is increasingly embedded in hotel operations, raising questions about how employees interpret managerial authority and voice concerns. Drawing on organisational justice and trust perspectives, this study examines relationships among perceived algorithmic control, perceived algorithmic fairness, and employee voice intention. An explanatory sequential mixed methods design combined structural equation modelling with semi-structured interviews. Perceived algorithmic control was negatively associated with procedural justice, interactional justice, and voice intention, whereas perceived algorithmic fairness was positively associated with trust in the employer and voice intention. Procedural justice, interactional justice, and trust were positively related to voice intention. The indirect-association analysis showed that algorithmic control was negatively associated with voice through procedural and interactional justice, while algorithmic fairness was positively associated with voice through trust. Qualitative findings highlighted explainability, reviewability, and managerial discretion. The study positions algorithmic management as relational governance and distinguishes control and fairness as separate pathways associated with employee voice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From hostile feedback to withdrawal: Emotional exhaustion as a barrier to social media misinformation correction
Abstract: User-driven misinformation correction is essential for sustaining the integrity of democratic discourse on social media, yet the emotional costs that discourage engagement remain understudied. Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines how the emotional tone of other users' feedback affects correctors' emotional exhaustion and subsequent willingness to engage in future corrections in a social media environment. In a cross-national experiment (N = 2001) across Austria, Bulgaria, Denmark, and Poland, utilizing a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design, participants corrected misinformation and received feedback varying in valence and arousal. Results show that angry, high-arousal feedback uniquely depletes emotional resources, producing higher exhaustion than civil disapproval or positive feedback. This indicates that critical feedback does not inherently exhaust correctors, but it is the hostile tone, not the negativity itself, that drives depletion. Emotional exhaustion, in turn, predicts avoidance of future corrective engagement. This exhaustion-driven withdrawal is amplified rather than buffered by correction confidence, suggesting that individual motivation alone is insufficient in hostile environments. These findings highlight emotional exhaustion as a key psychological constraint on citizen-led fact-checking and suggest that platform-level moderation targeting hostile comments is critical to protect the emotional resources required for a resilient democratic debate in digital environments. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Generative AI as a social partner for young adults: Dual pathways to resilience and AI dependence
Abstract: This study examines LLM-based AI chatbots as social interaction partners. Title: Halo or horn? The role of prior attitudes in shaping consumer responses to high-protein food labels
Abstract: Front-of-pack nutrition claims can shape consumers' perceptions of food products by triggering inferences about their overall healthfulness. Among these claims, “high-protein” labels have rapidly expanded across food categories, yet their influence on consumers' nutritional judgments remains underexplored. The present study investigated whether a high-protein label induces a health halo effect and examined the role of product characteristics and individual differences in shaping these perceptions. In an online experiment (N = 218), participants evaluated five food products presented either with or without a high-protein label. For each product, participants rated perceived calories, healthiness, sugar content, additives, level of processing, and purchase intention. Individual differences in drive for muscularity and attitudes toward protein products were also measured. Linear mixed-effects models revealed that the high-protein label did not produce a generalized positive halo effect: it did not significantly affect perceived healthiness, caloric content, sugar content, or purchase intention. However, products labeled as high protein were perceived as containing more additives and as being more industrially processed, consistent with a horn effect. The influence of the label on calorie and sugar estimations was moderated by the caloric content of the product, with effects emerging primarily for high-calorie products. Attitudes toward protein products moderated the label's effect across nutritional judgments, whereas drive for muscularity did not moderate labeling effects. These findings highlight the central role of individual predispositions in shaping responses to nutrition claims and suggest that high-protein labels may generate complex and sometimes contradictory perceptual biases, with implications for dietary behavior and public health. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Do narcissistic personality traits and immature defense mechanisms hinder communication and cooperation in pilots?
Abstract: This study examines the safety operation behaviors of pilots within the framework of communication and cooperation, compares how these behaviors are affected by narcissistic personality traits, and compares the results for the correct evaluation and management of immature ego defense mechanisms, which are thought to be a factor triggering this relationship. It was observed that the participants frequently used the defense mechanisms of rationalization, isolation, and acting out. Title: Pathways to plant-based meal consumption: A two-wave test of the health action process approach (HAPA)

While past behavior remained most strongly associated with plant-based meal consumption, the parsimonious model reaffirmed action planning as the key intention-behavior mediator. Title: Digital transformation policy and production efficiency in state-owned electric power enterprises: Evidence from China
Abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly used to modernize public utilities, but its efficiency effects remain insufficiently understood. Title: Together or apart? Migration, education access, and intergenerational mobility in China
Abstract: This paper studies how hukou-based education wedges and child-arrangement costs jointly shape welfare and intergenerational educational mobility in China. I develop a quantitative spatial model with overlapping generations in which households sequentially choose education, migration, and child arrangement, and estimate it using census and household-survey data. Title: Exploring socioeconomic associations of crisis information processing via large language models and explainable AI
Abstract: Social media evolution has restructured corporate crisis communication, yet extracting regional intelligence from unstructured data remains a significant computational challenge. This study proposes an integrated AI-Spatial Information Framework to analyze provincial-level discourse patterns during a major corporate crisis. We then employed LASSO-based feature selection and FDR-corrected OLS regression to examine associations between provincial-level socioeconomic indicators and consumer discourse patterns across 31 Chinese provinces. Statistical results suggest that provincial socioeconomic factors account for a substantial portion of the observed variation in digital discourse. Life expectancy was positively associated with brand anthropomorphism, while tertiary education showed a tentative negative association with health risk perception. More importantly, these associations suggest that regional variation in brand-supportive discourse is closely related to socioeconomic conditions and is theoretically consistent with cognitive buffering processes. Title: Transformative leadership models and styles to improve the quality and development of Muhammadiyah school education in Blora Indonesia

Title: Strengthening strategic environmental assessment through ecosystem service valuation and public preferences: evidence from Ireland
Abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a key instrument for integrating environmental considerations into plans and programmes at an early stage of decision-making. However, effectiveness reviews highlight a significant gap in the systematic quantification of SEA benefits, particularly regarding non-market values and ecosystem services (ES). Results also indicate limited public familiarity with SEA instruments and relatively low trust in governmental environmental decision-making. Title: Fixed or flexible: How product formats affect consumer redemption behavior for live-streamed food and beverage (F&B) products

Abstract: With the rapid growth of live-streaming e-commerce in the food and beverage industry, low redemption rates despite high sales volumes have become a critical challenge for merchants. Title: Inertial bregman proximal iteratively reweighted algorithms for a class of nonconvex nonsmooth regularized problems

Abstract: In this paper, we study a class of nonconvex nonsmooth regularized optimization problems whose objective consists of a continuously differentiable loss function and a structured nonconvex regularizer. Title: Understanding work well-being: A systematic review and future research agenda on multilevel influences
Abstract: Work well-being has become an important topic in organizational research, as it is beneficial to employee performance and job satisfaction. Although studies on work well-being have increased recently, existing literature remains fragmented, with prior reviews predominantly focusing on general employee well-being or single-level analyses. This limitation constrains both theoretical clarity and the development of targeted organizational interventions. In particular, there is a need to systematically review how individual, group, and organizational factors shape employees’ well-being at work. To address this gap, the present study conducts a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing evidence from 53 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025, retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. This study has two key implications: It identifies knowledge gaps in the literature and supports evidence-based decision-making. By synthesizing findings across the individual, group, and organizational levels, this review develops a broad and integrated understanding of the drivers of work well-being. The findings suggest that work well-being is driven by the dynamic interaction between individual and social resources, and broader organizational conditions. These factors operate in combination rather than independently, shaping employees’ psychological experiences across work contexts. This study contributes to the literature by providing a structured and integrative multilevel framework, clarifying conceptual boundaries of work well-being, and identifying underexplored research areas. It also offers a more analytically grounded synthesis that advances theoretical development and informs evidence-based organizational practices. Title: Helpfulness and enjoyment in eWOM: A dual-value perspective for hedonic digital products
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As the digital economy increasingly pivots toward the experience sector, electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) serves not merely as a decision-support tool but as an intrinsic source of entertainment. Title: Cities under pressure: Tourism intensity and the erosion of social capital in Italy

Title: Political activism and indulgent preferences: Perceived moral contribution and deservingness

Title: A rapid on-site visual detection strategy for vanillic acid based on the specific diazo coupling principle
Abstract: The accurate determination of vanillic acid (VA) is essential for quality control and authenticity verification in food and pharmaceutical products. Title: What do feature branches tell us about feature implementation in open-source projects?
Abstract: Although “feature” is a common term across requirements engineering, product-line engineering, and agile methods, its operationalization in practice–especially through feature branches–has received little empirical attention. Feature branches are widely recommended on platforms like GitHub; yet, empirical evidence on how they are actually used is scarce. This study investigates feature-branch development practices in open-source software (OSS) projects. We conducted a large-scale empirical analysis of 27,103 feature branches from 3,388 popular GitHub repositories. Using branch-naming conventions, we identified feature branches and measured their lifespan, commit history, and commit-share distributions among contributors. In addition, we profiled contributors according to their opened issues, opened pull requests, number of followers, and total stars. Our analysis revealed that feature branches in open-source projects are long-lived, with a median lifespan exceeding two years, diverging from the short, agile iterations typically employed in software development. Commit intensity is low and irregular, averaging fewer than two commits per day. Contribution is highly unequal within feature branches: a small share of contributors accounts for most commits, revealing strong dependence on a small subset of developers. These findings have several practical implications. Title: EXPLORING THE HEALTH KNOWLEDGE CO-CONSTRUCTION ON SHORT VIDEO PLATFORMS
Abstract: Short video platforms have become an important channel for doctors to conduct health science popularization. This study aims to explore the factors influencing health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms. Based on arousal theory, we develop an empirical model to examine the effects of video vividness, video complexity, emotional attitudes, and doctor popularity on health knowledge co-construction. We collected data from the largest short video platform in China, comprising a total of 4,009 videos and 1,040,230 comments for empirical analysis. This study combined machine learning, large language models, and econometric models to test the theoretical model. The results show that: (1) video vividness has a significant positive effect on health knowledge co-construction; (2) video complexity has a negative effect on health knowledge co-construction; (3) there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between emotional attitude and health knowledge co-construction; (4) doctor popularity positively moderates this curvilinear relationship. This study contributes to the literature on knowledge co-construction, expands the understanding of health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms, and provides practical guidance for platform managers and doctors. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. Title: Bridging the Human-AI preference gap: A persuasion-oriented tripartite framework
Abstract: The remarkable performance of artificial intelligence (AI) systems on a wide variety of complex tasks has fueled its rapid adoption in recent years. Yet, many individuals still exhibit a human-AI preference gap, such that they prefer human-generated over AI-generated outputs and follow recommendations made by generative AI (GenAI) less than human advice. We conceptualize the rejection of a superior AI system in favor of an inferior human as a persuasion failure that necessitates psychological rather than technological resolution. Recent research has identified various interventions that compress the human-AI preference gap. We codify these interventions by introducing a persuasion-oriented tripartite framework that delineates three distinct paths by which the preference gap between humans and AI systems may be narrowed: (1) AI-centric interventions, which directly bolster perceptions and evaluations of AI systems; (2) human-centric interventions, which reduce the (often inflated) perceptions and evaluations of humans; and (3) hybrid interventions, which offer an integrated or reformulated alternative that combines human and AI elements. Ultimately, our tripartite framework illustrates how different persuasion tactics fundamentally reshape beliefs and attitudes about both AI and humans, thereby informing system design elements and communication strategies that can bridge the human-AI preference gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Mapping the research landscape of generative artificial intelligence in education with implications for teacher education: A bibliometric analysis
Abstract: The rapid emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models, has significantly transformed educational research and practice, resulting in a rapidly expanding yet fragmented body of literature. This study aims to systematically map the research landscape of GenAI in education and examine its implications for teacher education through a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. Using the Scopus database, 16,250 documents published from 2021 to 2025 were analyzed through performance analysis and science mapping techniques, including keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship network analysis, and citation analysis to capture the structural and intellectual development of the field. The findings reveal a sharp increase in publication output beginning in 2023, indicating a transition from an emergent to a high-growth phase of research development. Research productivity and scholarly influence are concentrated among a limited group of authors, institutions, and countries, particularly the United States and China, reflecting uneven global participation. Collaboration networks exhibit a multi-clustered structure, suggesting active yet fragmented research communities with limited cross-group integration. Citation patterns indicate that a small number of recent publications exert strong influence and serve as foundational references in the field. Thematic analysis further identifies three dominant and interconnected areas: core technological developments, educational applications, and domain-specific implementations, highlighting the interdisciplinary nature of GenAI in education. The field is expanding rapidly but remains structurally fragmented and is still undergoing intellectual consolidation. These findings emphasize the need for more cohesive research efforts, stronger international collaboration, and greater integration across thematic domains. Implications for teacher education include the integration of AI-related competencies into pre-service programs, the adoption of pedagogically grounded and context-sensitive approaches, and the provision of continuous professional development to support teachers in AI-enhanced learning environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Hallucinations in organization-backed AI advisors: Evidence about skepticism, verification, and reliance in goal-directed use
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems are increasingly used by organizations to deliver information to consumers, patients, students, employees, and citizens. These systems can hallucinate, producing plausible but inaccurate responses. A central question for AI-advised decisions is therefore not only whether users rely on inaccurate information, but whether they recognize that a response may require verification. To answer this question, we review emerging empirical evidence relevant to hallucination detection in goal-directed interactions, with a focus on organization-backed AI advisors. We distinguish three constructs that existing studies often conflate: whether users are skeptical of information presented, whether they verify it (distinguishing attempted from successful verification), and whether the result of verification affects reliance on the information. Across studies examining product search, medical decision-making, content generation, and chatbot-assisted tasks, several patterns emerge. Nearly all studies measure reliance, while variables such as user skepticism and verification of the information are more often targeted by an intervention than measured directly. The cues used to prompt scrutiny of the AI response are predominantly related to the AI output, such as source citations. Whereas general warnings about the risk of hallucinations are among the most deployable interventions for organizations, they show the weakest and most mixed effects in the studies reviewed. More targeted cues about where AI systems tend to fail appear promising, however evidence remains limited. Although the existing literature posits that users may be more likely to scrutinize responses related to particular areas of content, no studies varied the content category, leaving this question open for further research. In future research, measuring skepticism and verification separately from reliance may clarify what current evidence shows, what it only implies, and which questions require further exploration. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Techno-economic study and sensitivity analysis- benefits of complex petrochemical waste refining
Abstract: For the petrochemical industry to maintain resource sustainability, complex waste must be treated effectively. In the previous work, the Aspen Hysys V12.0 modeling tool was used to analyze the regeneration of water, aromatics (BTX), and glycols (MEG, DEG, and TEG) from petrochemical effluent and the operating parameters were validated with experimental study. This study presents a techno-economic and environmental assessment of an integrated petrochemical wastewater treatment system with resource recovery. The process enables recovery of water (7.8 MM kg/year), aromatics such as benzene and toluene (468,000 kg/year each), and glycols (over 16.5 MM kg/year). The total capital investment is estimated at $42.4 MM, with annual operating costs of $8.46 MM and revenue of $18 MM. The system achieves a net present value (NPV) of $31.8 MM, an internal rate of return (IRR) of 19.9%, and a payback period of 4.87 years. Sensitivity analysis identified product price and electricity cost as key economic drivers. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) showed a 95% probability of positive NPV, indicating robust performance under uncertainty. The carbon footprint is estimated at 11,970 tons CO2/year (0.12 kg CO2/kg treated), representing an 87% reduction compared to conventional systems. Carbon pricing further enhances economic viability. The novelty of this work lies in integrating techno-economic analysis, uncertainty quantification, carbon footprint evaluation, and circular economy principles into a unified framework. The results demonstrate that the proposed system is a sustainable and economically viable solution for petrochemical wastewater management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: QualiTact: A semantic model for quality-driven development of AI-based systems based on architectural tactics
Abstract: Systems operating in safety-critical industries increasingly adopt Artificial Intelligence (AI). Satisfaction of system quality attributes in these industries is mandatory and rigorously verified. To influence system quality, a crucial development practice is the use of architectural tactics. However, selecting and balancing these attributes is often based on experience rather than on conscious decisions. This can unexpectedly impact system quality and might be detected too late in the testing phase. For development projects, it is desirable to identify and plan the selection of architectural tactics in a quality-driven manner. This article presents an approach that calculates a tactic's relative influence between 24 linked quality attributes and 150 tactics as part of a semantic model that supports the quality-driven development of AI-based systems. Attribute selection and filtering create recommendations of relevant tactics for a specific design and development task. In an exploratory multi-case study, the suitability of the recommended tactics was analyzed using source code. Results show that the model can compensate missing quality attribute information input and can provide recommendations. Despite an average input of only 39.98% from 30 case-relevant quality attributes for the model, the average recommendation completeness reaches 49.26% for 20.67 known tactics in source code across cases, leading the model to suffer from gaps between the literature and cases. Yet, 28 new design tactics linked to 30 known quality attributes were identified. Our work thus lays the foundation to support quality-driven design and development by recommending architectural tactics based on quality requirements. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The role of citizen science in engaging older adults with age-friendly green spaces
Abstract: This project addresses the global challenges of an ageing population and rapid urbanisation by exploring how citizen science can support the engagement of older adults in shaping age-friendly green spaces. Conducted in the City of Unley, South Australia, the study engaged 30 older residents (aged 60+) as citizen scientists to trial a multi-format audit tool and co-reflect on its use in practice for creating age-friendly environments, generating practical insights for future research and design practice. Integrating audits into participants’ daily routines and everyday life spaces ensured that findings reflected lived experiences. Citizen science was not merely a data collection tool but a sustained dialogue, with regular workshops and informal café sessions supporting motivation, peer learning, and collaborative analysis. Participants reported challenges such as sustaining long-term motivation, but also highlighted opportunities for empowerment, confidence-building, and strengthened community ties. Importantly, many older adults described shifts in how they experienced their environments—becoming more observant, extending their walking habits, and growing more confident in voicing ideas. Several participants continued their civic engagement beyond the project, illustrating the lasting impact of participation. The study contributes methodological insights into designing inclusive citizen science initiatives, offering guidance on recruitment, tool development, and engagement strategies tailored to older populations. Overall, this study demonstrates the power of citizen science not only to generate grounded data but also to empower older adults and co-produce inclusive urban knowledge. Findings provide process-focused insights into age-friendly engagement and illustrate the broader potential of citizen science in shaping equitable, community led public spaces. Overall, this research demonstrates how citizen science can move beyond data collection to become a co-creative process that empowers older adults and informs age-friendly urban transformation. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Zou Y.; Cheng P.; Li T.; Sui H.; Liu Y.; Zhang L.; Lv X.; Jiang G.
Title: Layered lanthanum hydroxycarbonate turns phosphate pollution into slow-release fertilizer
Source title: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
Abstract: Mismanagement of Phosphorus (P) depletes phosphate finite rock reserves and exacerbates widespread aquatic eutrophication, driving an urgent demand for integrated strategies that simultaneously remove and recover phosphate (PO43−). Herein, we show that rough-surfaced oblate La(OH)CO3 particles capture PO43− with exceptional efficiency, and the spent one can serve as a slow-release P fertilizer, enabling full pollutant-to-resource conversion. The material achieves a maximum adsorption capacity of 211.59 mgP g−1, rapid chemisorption-dominated kinetics, a broad pH window (3–7), and strong selectivity against competing anions and natural organic matters. In fixed-bed column tests, effluent P concentrations stayed below 0.2 mg L−1 discharge threshold for a breakthrough time of 84 h and > 90% P recovery was achieved. When evaluated as a fertilizer in hydroponic cultivation of Pisum sativum, the spent adsorbent produced plant height and biomass that matched or exceeded those from a conventional soluble P source at the optimal dosage. Mechanistic and comparative studies with La(OH)3 and La2(CO3)3 reveal that the superior performance originates from the synergy of electrostatic attraction, surface OH− ligand exchange, interlayer CO32− anion exchange (facilitated by favorable size matching), and inner-sphere complexation, all enabled by the unique layered structure of La(OH)CO3 ([La(OH)]2+ framework layers and interlayer CO32−). This work reports a high-performance La-based adsorbent for efficient P control and establishes a broadly applicable pollutant-to-resource paradigm that bridges environmental remediation with circular nutrient economies. © 2026

Title: Enhanced dissipation and global well-posedness for a three-dimensional flame propagation model with couette flow

Abstract: We study a three-dimensional gravity-induced flame front model under a Couette flow. Title: From growth mindset to social-emotional skills in early and mid-adolescence: A educational-cultural examination of an integrated mind-body-behavior framework
Abstract: Background: Social-emotional learning (SEL) is a core educational goal, yet little is known about how adolescents’ cognitive beliefs, body-related self-perceptions, and everyday health behavior jointly relate to social-emotional skills across diverse cultural contexts and school stages. Objective: Based on mindset theory and self-regulation perspectives, we examined an integrated Mind-Body-Behavior framework in which growth mindset, positive body image, and health behavior show a theoretically specified pattern of associated with adolescents’ social-emotional skills. Methods: A two-stage quantitative design combined structural equation modeling and machine learning. Results: Growth mindset was associated with social-emotional skills both directly and indirectly associations via body image and health behavior. Conclusions: The study contributes an integrated view of how beliefs, body-related self-perception, and health behavior relate to social-emotional skills. Authors: Ding S.; Pan X.; Zhou Z.; Deng H.; Tan J.; Sun L.
Title: A probabilistic model for situation awareness reliability assessment in uncertain environments
Abstract: Human error remains a major contributor to accidents in safety-critical systems, partly because operators may fail to establish effective situation awareness (SA) within critical time windows. Existing approaches to situation awareness reliability (SAR) often use SAGAT scores directly as reliability measures, conflating observed single-trial performance with the probability of successful SA formation under repeated conditions. They also lack a unified probabilistic framework integrating individual cognitive ability, task uncertainty, and available time. To address these limitations, this study applies the stress-strength interference principle from reliability engineering and models SA formation as a stochastic competition between cognitive strength and cognitive demand. A closed-form SAR expression with interpretable parameters is derived, forming the SAR-SSI model. The model was evaluated in a controlled experiment involving 29 participants and 1740 trials. Trial-level AUCs were 0.8032 for the full-sample fit and 0.8011 under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, indicating similar discrimination for held-out participants within the same experimental paradigm. Higher values of the task-related indicator C and longer available time were associated with higher SAR, whereas greater task uncertainty was associated with lower SAR and attenuated these relationships. The SAR-SSI model provides an interpretable probability-based tool for comparing how alternative information-presentation and task configurations may affect the likelihood of successful SA formation in controlled dynamic tasks.
