Title: Going green to compete: Male-biased operational sex ratio, status motivation, and men's relative green product preference
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Motivating men to choose environmentally preferable products remains an important challenge. Across six studies, this research examines how operational sex ratio (OSR), defined as the ratio of reproductively available men to women, is associated with men's relative preference for green products over conventional alternatives. OSR can characterize a broader demographic environment or serve as a population cue in a local social setting. A cross-level analysis in China showed that men living in provinces with more male-biased OSRs assigned greater priority to environmental protection, whereas women showed no corresponding association. Randomized experiments showed that perceived male-biased OSR increased men's relative green product preference; perceiving a female-biased OSR did not produce a corresponding increase among women. Among men, the subsequent studies provided complementary evidence consistent with mediation by status motivation, linked male-biased OSR cues more closely to intrasexual competition motivation than to mate-attraction motivation, and showed that audience publicness moderated the indirect effect through status motivation. Title: A knowledge graph–enhanced retrieval-augmented framework for automated SysML model generation in MBSE
Abstract: Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) has become an important approach for modelling complex systems. However, transforming natural-language requirements into formal Systems Modeling Language (SysML) models remains difficult because of the complexity, multi-domain coupling, and knowledge-intensive nature of system design. To address this problem, this study proposes a knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation (KG-RAG) method for automatic SysML model generation. First, a domain-oriented SysML knowledge graph (KG) is constructed on the basis of the SysML metamodel and domain-specific knowledge. Second, a retrieval-augmented prompting strategy is developed to guide a large language model (LLM) in generating structured SysML artefacts under explicit syntactic and semantic constraints. Third, an automated transformation mechanism is established to convert the generated structured artefacts into tool-native editable SysML models. The proposed method is validated through a fixed-wing aircraft flight control system case study. The results show that the method can automatically generate eight types of SysML diagrams, including requirement, block definition, internal block, use case, activity, state machine, sequence, and parametric diagrams. Quantitatively, the automatically generated models achieve an average element-level model coverage rate of 90.42 ± 1.46%. These results indicate that the proposed method can reduce repetitive manual modelling effort and improve modelling efficiency, demonstrating its potential to support practical MBSE-based system design. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Digitalising waqf for sustainable development growth: Investigating user intentions through technology readiness and ethical commitment
Abstract: The digitalisation of cash waqf represents a promising avenue within Islamic social finance, offering substantial potential to enhance the welfare and socio-economic development of Muslim communities. Through digital platforms, cash waqf can be collected, managed and distributed more efficiently, transparently and widely compared to traditional methods. Despite these advantages, the level of public participation and contributions to digital cash waqf platforms remains significantly below expectations. Specifically, the study examines the roles of optimism, innovativeness, insecurity, discomfort, and moral obligation in shaping users’ behavioural intentions toward online waqf contributions. Data were collected through an online survey involving 211 Muslim respondents in Malaysia who have experience with digital financial services. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The findings reveal that optimism, insecurity, and moral obligation have a positive and significant influence on individuals’ intentions to donate cash waqf through digital platforms. In contrast, discomfort demonstrates a significant negative effect, indicating that feelings of technological anxiety and lack of confidence in using digital systems may discourage adoption. Given the limited empirical research on digital cash waqf, this study contributes valuable insights into the psychological and behavioural factors influencing online donation behaviour. Title: Growth Stage and Cultivar Influence the Interpretation of UAV-Derived NDVI for Potato Yield Assessment
Abstract: Single-date UAV vegetation indices are widely used to assess potato crop performance and estimate yield. However, whether their biological interpretation remains consistent across cultivars and growth stages is rarely examined. This study investigated how the relationships between UAV-derived multispectral and thermal canopy indicators and potato yield changed during crop development under contrasting irrigation in two cultivars with contrasting maturity classes (Anouk and Celandine). UAV surveys were conducted in July and August, and canopy metrics were related to final yield and tuber traits. The relationship between NDVI and yield differed markedly between cultivars and growth stages. In the early-maturing cultivar Anouk, July NDVI showed a strong positive correlation with yield (r = 0.87, p = 0.002), whereas August NDVI was not informative. In the late-maturing cultivar Celandine, the relationship reversed from a positive correlation in July (r = 0.56) to a strong negative correlation in August (r = −0.80, p = 0.009), indicating that greater late-season canopy greenness was associated with lower yield. Exploratory LOOCV Random Forest models achieved the highest yield prediction accuracy using July features for Anouk (R2 = 0.72) and August features for Celandine (R2 = 0.47), while multi-temporal features provided similar predictive performance. Title: Experiential and symbolic pathways to luxury fashion brand equity: The contingent role of brand attachment and subjective norm

Abstract: The study develops and tests an integrated moderated mediation model to explain how emotional attachment, shaped by experiential and symbolic brand stimuli, is associated with consumer-based brand equity (CBBE) in the luxury fashion context, and the role of consumers’ social environment, drawing on Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour. Title: FedVRU: Variational representation decomposition with uncertainty-aware refinement
Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative training. However, data heterogeneity across clients degrades the performance of a single global model. Existing Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) methods partially mitigate this issue via client-specific modeling. However, most rely on deterministic point estimation, ignoring the implicit uncertainty within personalized features and leaving the joint representation space vulnerable to local noise. We propose FedVRU, a unified framework for Federated Variational Representation Decomposition with Uncertainty-aware Refinement. Specifically, FedVRU models client-specific representations probabilistically through variational learning to characterize feature uncertainty. An Uncertainty-Aware Gating (UAG) mechanism then adaptively regulates personalized features according to the estimated uncertainty. Concurrently, a Multi-Contrastive Distillation (MCD) objective promotes temporal consistency of global representations and separation between global and personalized representations. Extensive experiments on multiple heterogeneous benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of FedVRU across diverse federated settings without additional communication overhead. Authors: Liu L.; Zhang K.; Zhang Y.; Zhao G.; Yuan Y.
Title: Descriptive or injunctive? The interactive effects of influencer type and social norms on alternative protein purchase intention
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As alternative protein products attract increasing attention, understanding how social norm messages and influencer type jointly shape consumers’ purchase intention has become increasingly relevant. Drawing on schema congruity theory, this study conducted three scenario-based experiments with Chinese panel participants. The studies manipulated influencer type (human vs. virtual) and social norm framing (descriptive vs. injunctive), with regulatory-mode message priming introduced in Study 3. The results showed significant interactions between influencer type and norm framing. In Study 1, human influencers elicited higher purchase intention than virtual influencers under injunctive framing, whereas virtual influencers elicited higher purchase intention under descriptive framing. However, descriptive framing generated higher purchase intention than injunctive framing within both influencer conditions. Study 2 provided evidence of moderated mediation through information processing fluency: the conditional indirect effect was significant for virtual influencers but not for human influencers. In Study 3, injunctive framing generated higher purchase intention than descriptive framing for human influencers under assessment-oriented priming, whereas this difference was not significant under locomotion-oriented priming. For virtual influencers, descriptive framing generated higher purchase intention under both priming conditions. These findings extend research on influencer marketing and social norms by identifying how influencer type and norm framing interact, highlighting information processing fluency as a potential explanatory mechanism and regulatory-mode priming as a boundary condition. They also provide practical guidance for selecting influencers and designing social norm messages in alternative protein marketing. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Feng Z.; Niu Y.; Zou H.
Title: Measurement scale for push and pull factors of Chinese pedestrian streets
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The concepts of push and pull theory have been proposed and extensively discussed in various studies, particularly in tourism research. However, push and pull theory in the field of pedestrian street is not addressed in the existing research. This study takes the perspective of pedestrian-street consumers, follows a systematic scale-development procedure, and uses samples from eight Chinese cities to develop and test a scale measuring perceived push and pull factors. The scale is composed of 11 dimensions for each of the push and pull domains. This study then examines the nomological validity by testing the associations between push and pull factors and revisit intention and recommendation intention. The results of the study support the nomological validity of the proposed relationships. This study does not propose push and pull as new constructs. Instead, it organizes and validates their context-specific manifestations within Chinese pedestrian streets and provides a culturally grounded measurement instrument for subsequent retail and consumer research. Title: Meaning in the age of AI: Experiencing less, needing more
Abstract: What does it mean to be human when artificial intelligence (AI) can simulate human thought and creative labor with increasing fidelity? Unlike AI, humans experience meaning in life. Yet AI may create a paradox for meaningfulness. AI may reduce people's ability to experience meaning by disrupting selfhood (loss of effort and self-efficacy), social relationships (reduced mattering and connection), and culture (erosion of value and stability). At the same time, it may heighten people's need for meaning by challenging human exceptionalism and increasing the need for coherence amidst upheaval. This paradox—experiencing less while needing more—is what we term the AI Meaning Gap. Yet meaninglessness is not inevitable. If developed and used intentionally, AI could become a tool for reflection, understanding, and self-growth, thereby enhancing meaning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Fu S.; Liu Z.; Niu Z.
Title: Product visual form and customer satisfaction: Multimodal evidence on affective value and functional diagnosis
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Product visual form conveys important aesthetic, quality, and use-related cues for functionally complex products. However, multimodal evidence from real-world retail settings remains limited regarding how product visual form relates to consumer evaluations in online reviews and satisfaction. Using data from 200 smart standing desks, 41951 valid reviews, and 200 product images, this study combined engineering-attribute encoding, CLIP image embeddings, and CLIP-text concept scores to construct a multilayer representation of product visual form. A large language model was used to extract affective and functional evaluations from the reviews, and the platform favorable rate served as a product-level proxy for satisfaction. Product-level path analysis showed that PC3 (Non-standard premium form) was positively associated with affective evaluation, and affective evaluation was positively associated with satisfaction. Together, these coefficients yielded a significant positive indirect association (indirect association = 0.075, 95% BCa CI [0.021, 0.156], FDR-Adj. p = 0.014). Functional evaluation, by contrast, was negatively associated with satisfaction (β = −0.254, p < 0.01). Further decomposition showed that this negative association was more closely related to functional-mention coverage than to overall polarity of functional evaluations. Noise control and Workspace size adequacy were the principal negative sources. These findings indicate that affective and functional evaluations relate to satisfaction in distinct ways. For online retailers and e-commerce platforms, combining analysis of product visual form with online-review monitoring can help identify design value, detect quality risks, and prioritize service recovery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Experimental and simulation studies on plasma gasification of medical waste for the co-production of ammonia and urea
Abstract: This study explores the novel integration of plasma gasification and urea synthesis using medical waste as a feedstock, a research area largely unexplored compared to conventional plasma gasification applications. This investigation is designed to evaluate the technical and economic viability of producing hydrogen-rich syngas followed by the synthesis of ammonia and urea via advanced process simulation and experimental validation. Medical waste gasification occurs under a CO2 environment to increase syngas quality when using medical waste such as syringes, gloves, surgical masks, and drip sets. Although, the maximum value of lower heating value (LHV) (12.4  MJ/m3) was achieved by utilizing plasma at 1.25  kW, the highest energy efficiency of 53.8 % was obtained at 1.00 kW due to lower energy input. Residue content decreased from 19 wt% (0.75  kW), 14 wt% (1.0  kW), and 11 wt% (1.25  kW). Ammonia and urea units show N2 and CO2 conversion efficiencies of 87.6 % and 81.56 %, respectively, with maximum urea production of 2853  kg/h. Techno-economic analysis shows that a CAPEX of $32.9 million and OPEX of $4.49 million/year result in a competitive urea cost of $0.49/kg and annual revenue of $6.7 million. Title: Auditing TikTok’s recommendations: Understanding the prevalence of misinformation on the platform
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: Short video platforms have rapidly increased in popularity, bringing forth a concerning trend: widespread dissemination of misinformation partially owing to the persuasive nature of the rich media these platforms support. However, little research has systematically investigated the role of algorithmic recommendations in this phenomenon. Our study addresses this gap by auditing the recommendation algorithm of TikTok, the leading short video platform, through four experiments. We explore the prevalence of misinformation in TikTok’s auto-complete suggestions, search results, and For You Page (FYP) recommendations. Our audits yielded a novel dataset comprising 8535 auto-complete suggestions, 1606 search queries, and 2893 videos labelled by stance (promoting misinformation, neutral in nature, or debunking misinformation). Our analysis reveals that TikTok’s algorithm exhibits sensitivity to user behaviours, often in unexpected ways. We find the algorithm recommends substantially more misinformation to newly created accounts lacking search histories, potentially shaping the tone of the content these accounts engage with. We also find that watching and engaging with videos (e.g., liking and favouriting) dynamically influence misinformation prevalent on the platform, potentially reinforcing existing beliefs and contributing to echo-chambers. Further, we emphasise how engaging with misinformation on one topic serves as a gateway, prompting the algorithm to recommend misinformation spanning both related and unrelated topics. Our work stands as the first large-scale, systematic, and empirical assessment of misinformation in TikTok’s recommendations, contributing valuable insights on the dynamics of misinformation dissemination on TikTok and also underscoring the pressing need for responsible auditing practices across digital platforms. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Fu Y.; Meißner M.
Title: Personalizing AI voice agents: How voice agents with similar voices shape trust, self-congruency, and behavior
Abstract: As voice agents become embedded in products as well as service interactions, firms increasingly seek personalization strategies that strengthen consumers' acceptance and engagement. This research examines whether voice agents that sound more similar to users' own voices elicit more favorable behavioral responses. Moreover, we investigate through which psychological mechanisms these effects occur. Across two experiments, we manipulate voice similarity using (1) pretested similar versus dissimilar AI voices and (2) individualized voice cloning that replicates users' voices. Results consistently show that higher voice similarity increases purchase intention, use intention, and willingness to disclose personal information. Mediation analyses indicate that voice similarity operates via two parallel mechanisms: self-congruency and trust. Title: When ads look worth keeping: Screenshotable design increases ad saving and Facebook ad liking
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: As social media advertising increasingly competes in fast-scrolling feed environments, an important but understudied question is whether some ads succeed by functioning less as transient persuasive messages and more as saveable information objects. The process was stronger when consumers anticipated a future rather than immediate need, such that perceived future utility translated more strongly into ad saving and liking under future-need conditions. Title: Threats to food security in rice farming: A scientific mapping of climate change impacts
Abstract: Climate change is severely disrupting many aspects of human life worldwide, particularly rice farming, as it feeds many people worldwide. In the absence of stable rice production, food security will is threatened for the global population. This paper examines how climate change is related to rice farming and what it means for overall food security. I used bibliometric analysis to examine the literature on this topic from 1998 to 2024, a 26-year period. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database using specific keywords, yielding 549 matching documents. Using VOSviewer helped visualize connections and identify trends in the research. Researchers have consistently focused on climate change, rice farming, and food security over time, but have not yet mapped the interrelationships between these variables. The findings suggest a reciprocal relationship. Agriculture produces greenhouse gases that exacerbate climate change, but climate change subsequently reverses itself and harms agricultural productivity. It is particularly difficult for rice to respond to changing temperatures, unusual rainfall patterns, and recurring extreme weather events. As a result, when crop yields decline, the availability of rice as a staple food decreases, directly impacting food security. These findings directly relate to Sustainable Development Goal 2, which aims to end hunger, making it urgent to find better ways to adapt agriculture to climate change and make it more sustainable. This necessary adaptation in rice farming aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 13, Climate Action. Therefore, this Action requires support from the government and the agricultural sector workforce to achieve food security and sustainable rice farming. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: When plateware shape matters: The congruence effects between food pungency and plateware shape on food preference

Abstract: Although considerable attention has been paid to enhancing the visual appeal of food, less is known about how plateware design should align with the sensory characteristics of food. Title: The duty to rescue at sea and Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS): Implementation under the IMO MASS code
Abstract: Under the international legal framework governing Search and Rescue (SAR) at sea, flag states are required to ensure that ships flying their flag render assistance to persons in distress, while coastal states must establish and coordinate adequate SAR services within their areas of responsibility. Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) pose challenges for ensuring compliance with rescue obligations due to difficulties in designating a master and limited embarkation and accommodation capabilities. This paper argues that autonomy does not justify an exemption from, or relief from, the duty to rescue. Against this background, the article examines how Chapter 21 (SAR) of the International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) translates the duty to rescue for MASS into a goal-based structure comprising goals, functional requirements, and expected performance, aligned with SOLAS. It further delineates the respective implementation responsibilities of flag states and coastal states, with a view to ensuring that MASS can render effective assistance to persons in distress at sea. On the one hand, flag states should implement Chapter 21 by survey, certification, and approval processes and oversee compliance through classification societies. On the other hand, coastal states must integrate MASS into SAR coordination arrangements and fulfil their obligation to coordinate the disembarkation of survivors to a “place of safety,” thereby completing the ship-side rescue duty upon delivery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Allocation of foreign aid in emerging economies: Investment in new vs maintenance of old infrastructure
Abstract: This paper analyzes the growth and welfare effects of allocating public resources — both domestic tax revenues and foreign aid — between investment in new public capital and the maintenance of existing public capital in emerging economies. Title: TKAM: A temporal-availability-aware encoder-decoder framework for multi-step forecasting of soybean futures prices
Abstract: Accurate multi-step forecasting of soybean futures prices is important for hedging, inventory management, and agricultural market risk management. Existing soybean futures price forecasting studies often organize heterogeneous predictors as a unified input sequence and overlook differences in their temporal availability at the forecasting origin. In addition, how complex forecasting models use information across forecast horizons remains insufficiently explained. This study proposes TKAM, an interpretable framework for multi-step soybean futures price forecasting. TKAM separates past-observed market variables from future-known time features, uses a Mamba-based encoder to represent historical market dynamics, and employs a Temporal Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (TKAN) decoder with a multi-output forecasting strategy to generate forecasts for multiple future trading days. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used to examine horizon-specific feature contributions. The empirical analysis uses 4165 daily observations from the No. 1 yellow soybean futures contract listed on the Dalian Commodity Exchange in China, covering the period from May 9, 2008, to June 27, 2025. The results show that TKAM achieves competitive and stable point-forecasting accuracy compared with twelve benchmark models, particularly for biweekly and monthly forecasts. The ablation results indicate that the branch-based input organization contributes substantially to forecasting performance and that the Mamba encoder is effective within this structure. The SHAP analysis shows that related agricultural futures prices, domestic spot prices, and time features contribute differently across forecast horizons. These findings provide methodological insights for multi-step agricultural futures price forecasting and empirical evidence for understanding the horizon-specific forecasting behavior of complex models in agricultural markets. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Corporate environmental credit rating and social stability: Evidence from capital-labor conflicts in China's polluting industries
Abstract: Mitigating capital-labor conflicts is essential for maintaining social stability. Title: A structure and splitting approximation based preconditioning method for solving space-time fractional advection-diffusion equations

Title: Clause-level structural alignment between ASME Section III and Czech NTD A.S.I. Section III: Domain- and component-resolved assessment

Authors: Pik E.
Title: Degradation of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast integrity: Temporal clustering and anomaly persistence
Abstract: As safety systems like the Airborne Collision Avoidance System X (ACAS X) increasingly depend on Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B), the structural reliability of these data streams is critical. Traditional monitors assume independent, stochastic failures. This study challenges that assumption by building a global baseline of longitudinal degradation from 229.0 billion state vectors. The framework integrates multiscale permutation testing with day-resolution, exposure-adjusted survival analysis. Significant temporal clustering appears in 98.9% of the high-utilization commercial cohort (≥20 flight-hours/month; N=30,716) and in 67.2% of the sparser remainder under the uniform null; 81.3% of sparse-cohort detections survive a stricter block-preserving null. Clustering peaks at a 3-second characteristic scale, and the mean sustained duration of 28.83 s exceeds the 5-second fault tolerance of decentralized fusion trackers. Across the fleet, 58.4% of aircraft record clustered anomalies on two or more distinct observation days, and 55.5% across two or more calendar months. With follow-up censored at the first >30-day observation gap, 56.0% of aircraft experience a first clustered anomaly, with a median of 9 observed days. A recurrent-event hazard model links recurrence to recent utilization (hazard ratio 1.19 per standard deviation) and, more strongly, to network observability coverage (hazard ratio 1.52). The negative time-to-first exposure coefficient is largely an artifact of onset timing. These results shift integrity monitoring from point-in-time anomaly detection to predictive system health management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Tailoring zeolite-based catalysts for mild, methane-selective VOC combustion in stack emission monitoring systems
Abstract: Accurate methane quantification in industrial emissions is frequently hindered by the presence of non-methane hydrocarbons and volatile organic compounds, which can interfere with conventional analytical methods. Commercial oxidation catalysts can remove these compounds, but their relatively high operating temperatures increase energy consumption and may also promote undesired methane oxidation. Here, we report a catalytic gas-conditioning strategy based on Cu- and Co-containing MFI, BEA, and FAU zeolites for the preferential oxidation of interfering hydrocarbons while preserving methane. The effects of zeolite topology, Si/Al ratio, metal loading, dispersion, and redox speciation on catalytic activity and selectivity were systematically investigated. Catalysts prepared from cobalt acetate showed superior performance, with activity increasing sharply above ~5 wt% Co. Structural characterization revealed that cobalt is initially present as highly dispersed Co2⁺ species that transform into mixed-valence cobalt oxides during reaction. Although cobalt migration and sintering occur under reaction conditions, the zeolite frameworks remain structurally stable and maintain high CO₂ selectivities (>90%). Compared with the commercial Carulite® catalyst, Co/MFI displayed superior atom efficiency and enhanced ethane-over-methane selectivity, attributed to the confinement of isolated cobalt species within the zeolite pore network. The combination of molecular confinement and highly dispersed metal sites was identified as the key factor governing low-temperature activity and methane selectivity. By integrating heterogeneous catalysis with energy-efficient, solvent-free gas-phase operation and real-time emission monitoring, this approach supports the green chemistry principles of pollution prevention, catalysis, energy efficiency, and real-time analysis. These results identify cobalt-loaded MFI zeolites as promising catalysts for selective VOC removal in methane-monitoring and air purification applications. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Integrated cognitive processing model of phishing detection: Mood state as moderating factor in the mindful cognition mediated detection process
Abstract: Previous studies have shown that security awareness alone is not consistently associated with phishing detection accuracy, yet the processes through which awareness is associated with detection remain underexplored. Existing phishing research has also predominantly adopted a cognitive perspective, despite the interdependent nature of affect and cognition in decision-making. To address these gaps, this study adopts an affect-integrated cognitive processing perspective and examines a proposed cognitive process involving security awareness, domain mindfulness, cognitive processing, and mood state, with particular attention to the conditional role of positive mood in performance-focused phishing judgments. Our findings show that security awareness is not directly associated with phishing detection accuracy; rather, a significant indirect association is observed through domain mindfulness and cognitive processing. Although temperament is not directly associated with detection accuracy, it is positively associated with mood state. Positive mood is negatively associated with detection accuracy, and the estimated beneficial indirect associations involving domain mindfulness and cognitive processing are weaker at higher levels of positive mood. Together, the results are consistent with a phishing-detection process involving both cognitive and affective factors. This study extends cognition-focused phishing-detection models by integrating affective boundary conditions into the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Store coolness in luxury fashion: Antecedents, outcomes, and the moderating role of price consciousness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: In the context of luxury fashion stores, this study investigates the mediating role of the dimensions of store coolness (extraordinary, subcultural, iconic, and high status) in linking service quality of employees, store display, and store creativity with customers' behavioral intention and positive word-of-mouth (WOM). Additionally, the study examines whether price consciousness moderates any of these relationships. To gain a deeper understanding of how coolness is perceived in luxury fashion stores, we collected customer insights through interviews with 16 frequent store visitors. We then tested our proposed model using a survey administered to shoppers immediately after they visited luxury stores (N = 213). Our results indicate that the extraordinary and subcultural dimensions of coolness positively mediate the effects of store display and creativity on behavioral intention and positive WOM. However, the iconic dimension did not play a mediating role, while the high status dimension negatively mediated these paths, including those involving service quality. Finally, we found that price consciousness weakens the path from store creativity to the studied outcomes via the extraordinary dimension. Building on these findings, we provide managerial insights for designing luxury fashion store experiences that foster store coolness and positive customer responses. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Cai B.; Bai Y.; Liu Y.; Wang F.; Zhang W.
Title: Quantifying the safe operating space of Chinese provinces through a dual-dimension water planetary boundary and trade framework
Abstract: Quantifying human water use relative to planetary boundaries is critical for limiting hydrological degradation. Here, we integrated a dual-dimension framework for blue- and grey-water planetary boundaries with virtual water trade analysis to assess water-related pressures across 30 Chinese provinces from 2002 to 2017. Grey water footprints dominated changes in boundary transgression, reaching a maximum in 2012 and declining by 49% by 2017 following the implementation of stringent national pollution control policies. This massive biophysical relief increased the number of provinces operating within the regional safe space from 10 in 2012 to 17 in 2017. Notably, no province transgressed the blue-water boundary alone, indicating that assessments excluding grey water may overlook the principal source of water-related boundary exceedance. Cumulative stress revealed hidden biophysical risks where aggregate pressure exceeds the regional boundary despite individual components remaining compliant. Highly stressed exporting regions such as Hebei support consumption in wealthier importing regions, including Beijing. The import dependence index and the export contribution index demonstrated that provinces with high export contribution remain in transgression, while provinces with high import dependence improved but rarely entered the absolute safe operating space. Structural decomposition analysis suggested that consumption structure shifts, rather than technological efficiency gains alone, drove the post-2012 restoration. These findings support the development of spatially differentiated regulatory strategies that align production, consumption and trade within regional hydrological limits. © 2026

Title: Unveiling research trends in artificial intelligence adoption based on the UTAUT: A bibliometric analysis supporting SDGs and future outlook
Abstract: The development of AI adoption across disciplines has become a major global concern, especially with the UTAUT model that runs concurrently. This study aims to map research trends on AI adoption within the UTAUT model in conceptual, intellectual, and social structures. The research utilises a bibliometric approach from the Scopus database for the period 2018-2025 on related topics. Data analysis was conducted descriptively using Biblioshiny (Rstudio). The study found a very positive and significant development in research on AI adoption within the UTAUT model across various disciplines, aligning with the SDGs, particularly points four, nine, and seventeen. The countries that contributed most were China and the USA. Interesting themes for studying the development of UTAUT model implications include social influence, performance expectancy, behaviour, perceived risk, digital literacy, and AI anxiety. In SDG 4, the adoption of AI in higher education is crucial by incorporating perceived risk and digital literacy to achieve effective personalised learning. In SDG 9, organisational and corporate levels within managerial structures are important for combining structural and psychological factors that influence AI adoption. AIMDSS in the healthcare sector is essential for supporting health innovation and infrastructure. Meanwhile, for SDG 17, discovering best practices for AI adoption across various fields needs to be accelerated, particularly in Africa, South America, and most of Eastern Europe. The implications of this research point to the development of institutional guidelines for AI adoption and the exploration of the UTAUT model. By highlighting the evolving role of contextual, ethical, and governance-related factors, this study provides a foundation for aligning AI adoption strategies with sustainable development objectives and informs future empirical and policy-oriented research. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Tell me the truth: Consumer responses to feedback solicitation with robots versus humans
Abstract: Advanced technologies enable service robots to handle a broader range of tasks than ever before. Among these, this research examines the potential of service robots to solicit and collect high-quality consumer feedback. This research, comprising four experimental studies, including a field study in a hotel, demonstrates that unsatisfied consumers are more likely to provide honest feedback to service robots than to human employees. Drawing on the theory of mind perception, the present research finds that such an effect is attributed to consumers’ concern for others' feelings (i.e., empathetic concern). Moreover, the proposed effects are diminished when the robot has a high (vs. low) level of emotional capability but are more pronounced among consumers with interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal. Authors: Yang Z.; Hu W.; Hu H.; Cui H.; Sun Q.
Title: ORBIT-FL: Scene-aware and budget-adaptive federated continual learning for multi-UAV environmental monitoring
Abstract: Multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) systems are increasingly critical for large-scale environmental monitoring, offering agile data acquisition through distributed sensing. However, applying state-of-the-art deep learning to these systems is hindered by the impracticability of centralized data transmission due to privacy concerns and communication limitations. While Federated Learning (FL) presents a promising decentralized alternative, standard FL approaches are inadequate for the unique challenges of real-world UAV deployments. These challenges include highly heterogeneous non-IID data distributions with few-shot labels, the need for continual adaptation to evolving sensing tasks without catastrophic forgetting, and strict, disparate onboard resource constraints. To address these issues in a unified manner, this paper proposes ORBIT-FL, an orbit/scene-aware, retrieval-augmented, and budget-adaptive FL framework. ORBIT-FL departs from single-model convergence, instead maintaining a composable model universe. It tackles non-IID and few-shot scenarios via a scene-conditioned hyper-adapter that generates lightweight, personalized parameters based on privacy-preserving context tokens. To support evolving missions, it introduces a retrieval-augmented federated continual learning mechanism using a time-indexed memory graph of semantic prototypes. Furthermore, ORBIT-FL incorporates budget-conditioned training and anytime inference routing to dynamically adapt to the heterogeneous compute and energy constraints of different UAV platforms. This framework enables robust, privacy-preserving environmental awareness across diverse and dynamic UAV fleets. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Tong R.; Li X.; Wang L.
Title: Factors associated with casualty injury severity in e-scooter crashes: A machine-learning approach with SHAP explainability
Abstract: The rapid adoption of electric scooters (e-scooters) as a micro-mobility mode has been accompanied by rising crash-related injuries, yet the factors associated with severe outcomes remain poorly understood. Because the released dataset is organised at the casualty level, the outcome analysed here is the injury severity of an individual casualty involved in an e-scooter crash, classified as slight versus serious/fatal ; the unit of analysis is the casualty record, not the collision. Using 5166 police-reported casualty records from Great Britain between January 2020 and November 2024, we examine 25 crash-scene, rider, casualty, and environmental features. Five supervised classifiers are compared via randomised hyperparameter search with stratified five-fold cross-validation, with all oversampling confined to the training folds; an integer-encoded SMOTE specification is held fixed as a common reference for comparison rather than as a preferred model. The three gradient-boosted tree models have similar aggregate performance: LightGBM attains a weighted F1 of 0.660 (AUC-ROC 0.624), while paired McNemar tests and bootstrap intervals show that LightGBM, XGBoost, and Gradient Boosting each outperform the fitted Logistic Regression baseline; the LightGBM–Random Forest comparison is not robust across the two inferential checks. Cost-sensitive learning raises serious-class recall to 0.536, and a native-categorical CatBoost pipeline raises it to 0.559. Although weighted F1 remains between 0.653 and 0.661 across the four encoding pipelines, minority-class detection and SHAP rankings are encoding-sensitive. SHAP identifies number of vehicles, latitude, casualty sex, time-of-day band, and rider age as the leading predictors in the common reference model, although encoding sensitivity shows that only NumVehicles and DayTime occur in every encoding-specific top five, and the cost-sensitive ranking agrees only moderately with the SMOTE model (ρ=0.6662). Casualties recorded in single-vehicle incident configurations had higher descriptive serious/fatal injury rates than those recorded in two-vehicle configurations (38.6% versus 26.6%), and a refit restricted to the driver/rider-casualty subset used as a proxy for e-scooter riders — in which NumVehicles remains the top predictor with a stronger single-vehicle effect — indicates the pattern persists within that subset rather than arising solely from mixing riders with pedestrians. A fall or head-impact mechanism is plausible but unmeasured: helmet use, fall occurrence, and head impact are absent from the data, and the subset used to test the pattern is defined by a driver/rider role code that proxies for, rather than verifies, e-scooter rider status. Records involving older riders had higher serious/fatal injury rates (28.8% below age 50 versus 42.7% at or above 50), without establishing age 50 as a policy threshold. DayTime band 0 had the highest observed serious/fatal rate, but the four-band rates are not strictly monotonic and their clock-time meanings are undocumented. Discrimination is moderate and the predicted probabilities are poorly calibrated (Brier 0.219 against a 0.208 prevalence baseline), so these results support cautious, locally evaluated hypotheses rather than causal, operational, or universally transferable prescriptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mobile internet connectivity and climate change literacy in Africa
Abstract: Addressing climate change requires individual behavioral shifts and a deep understanding of its impacts, yet the role of information and communication technologies (ICT), a powerful driver of social movements and cultural shifts, in shaping climate change literacy remains underexplored. This study addresses a critical gap by exploring how ICT, particularly mobile Internet connectivity, influences climate change literacy in Africa. I provide the first systematic evidence on the impact of mobile Internet connectivity on climate change literacy by exploiting variations in peer-based Internet connectivity in an instrumental variable strategy. Using newly georeferenced individual-level data on climate change literacy from over 42,000 respondents across 31 African countries, I show that mobile Internet connectivity has a modest yet robust effect on climate literacy, raising it by approximately 0.57 points for a typical adopter. Heterogeneity analysis shows that mobile Internet access primarily enhances the knowledge-based dimensions of climate literacy, particularly climate awareness and understanding, while also improving risk perceptions to a lesser extent. This suggests that mobile Internet contributes to climate literacy mainly by expanding access to factual information and knowledge about climate change. Suggestive evidence reveals that Internet connectivity can help close climate-related information gaps, among socio-economically disadvantaged groups, such as women, farmers, and those without formal education. Although Internet connectivity increases the frequency of using Internet and social media for news, there is no strong evidence that these platforms serve as channels linking Internet connectivity to climate literacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: A meta integral reinforcement learning-based cooperative guidance evasion scheme against noncooperative spacecraft
Abstract: The increasing congestion of space orbits has led to a growing number of close-proximity encounters between operational satellites and noncooperative spacecraft. To achieve online autonomous evasion from noncooperative spacecraft, this paper proposes a Meta Integral Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MI-MARL)-based cooperative guidance scheme. Firstly, the multi-agent orbital encounter is formulated as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP), where the interaction among spacecraft is modeled as an orbital pursuit-evasion process under incomplete information. Then, a meta multi-actor-critic architecture incorporating a convolutional recurrent inference network is developed to infer high-dimensional spatiotemporal features directly from stacked angle-only observations of noncooperative spacecraft. The proposed meta-network architecture enhances situational awareness and enables online policy retraining within a Dec-POMDP. Furthermore, by theoretical analysis in the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs framework, we formulate the rational decision-making and Nash equilibrium stability conditions of a perfect Bayes-Nash equilibrium, thereby guaranteeing the convergence and optimality of the MI-MARL. Finally, numerical simulations and computational efficiency evaluations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, superior performance, and real-time onboard feasibility of the proposed method in highly dynamic close-proximity encounter scenarios. © 2026 IAA. Abstract: As GenAI becomes increasingly embedded in AI-enabled service interactions, users' evaluations of AI are extending from functional performance to expectations regarding responsibility and obligation. Title: Factors affecting public transport adoption in Riyadh- case study
Abstract: Riyadh's greenhouse gas emissions and urban climate risks are likely heightened by accelerated urbanization and profound dependence on private cars. Despite the government's investment in public transportation, societal resistance to giving up private cars and using public transit persists due to cultural and traditional factors. Within the Gulf context, this study is the first to investigate the unique socio-cultural and urban context of Riyadh to understand university students' mobility behavior, identify four factors that significantly are associated with their travel choices, and quantitatively rank the relative influence of these factors. Surveys (n = 710) were used to assess four key factors, analyzed via multiple regression, chi-square, and t-tests. Results indicate that, in descending order of influence, psychological factors (explaining 23% of the variance) have the most significant association with students' willingness to switch to public transport in Riyadh, followed by trip characteristics (13%), urban factors (12%), and socioeconomic and demographic factors (12%). Title: Design, dynamic analysis, and optimization of a hybrid nuclear-storage power system for mobile applications
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of heat pipe-cooled reactor (HPR) technology, the integration of mobile nuclear power with energy storage offers a promising solution for energy supply in remote and off-grid scenarios. However, existing research predominantly focuses on stationary systems, lacking comprehensive investigation into the dynamic coupling of HPRs and hybrid storage in mobile environments. To address this gap, this paper proposes a novel hybrid nuclear-storage power system (HNSPS) integrating an HPR with a lithium-ion battery and supercapacitor for mobile applications. A high-fidelity system model is developed in MATLAB/Simulink, incorporating a nuclear power generation system, hybrid energy storage, and control models. A fully active parallel topology is employed for the storage subsystem, utilizing lithium-ion batteries for baseload and supercapacitors for transient power fluctuation mitigation. Simulation results demonstrate robust synergistic operation, characterized by excellent dynamic response and energy management performance. Parameter optimization indicates that the lithium battery rated voltage (determined by series configuration) should balance cycle life and manufacturing cost, while its response time should be extended for high-frequency operation and shortened for high-power-demand scenarios. For the supercapacitor, an initial voltage of 100–200 V and a series number of approximately 200 are recommended to balance transient power capability, safety, and cost. Title: Hungry for change: Inclusive dining for travelers with dietary restrictions
Abstract: Dining is central to tourism experiences, yet for travelers with dietary restrictions, it can become a source of exclusion rather than enjoyment. Guided by stigma theory, this study examines how dietary restrictions function as a form of concealable stigma in tourism dining contexts. Using a sequential exploratory mixed-methods design, the study combines Critical Incident Technique interviews with 32 individuals and text mining of 3,165 traveler Yelp reviews. Findings reveal that stigma manifests through internal (self-burden, anticipatory anxiety) and external (public, structural, associative) forms producing psychological and behavioral consequences that constrain participation in dining experiences. Individuals employ a range of voluntary and involuntary coping responses to navigate such challenges. Building on these findings, the study proposes a mutual reinforcement model in which internal and external stigma recursively sustain one another across repeated dining encounters, highlighting the anticipatory and cumulative nature of dietary stigma in tourism and offering theoretical and practical insights. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Liu R.; He X.; Lv L.
Title: Recommend or not? Investigating the effectiveness of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Online charitable platforms are important channels through which the public participates in micro-donations, and these platforms have increasingly leveraged algorithmic recommendation technologies to deliver personalized charitable advertisements to potential donors. Nonetheless, whether personalized algorithmic recommendations enhance or undermine consumers’ micro-donation intentions remains unclear. Drawing on moral identity theory, our research addresses this gap through five online scenario-based experiments. The results show that consumers exhibit lower micro-donation intentions when exposed to micro-donation advertisements with personalized algorithmic recommendations, and that this negative effect is driven primarily by perceived identity value threat. Furthermore, we find that the negative effect of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising is attenuated in the presence of legitimization cues or among consumers with low scores on the moral identity scale. Our findings not only extend the literature on the antecedents of micro-donations and the economic consequences of algorithmic personalization in the charitable advertising context, but also offer actionable guidance for charitable platforms seeking to optimize their algorithmic recommendation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Jia H.; Lin B.
Title: Appliance-level energy assessment and its implications for the environmental impact of household energy conservation: Evidence from urban China
Abstract: Accurate appliance-level energy judgments may help households identify and prioritize meaningful electricity-saving opportunities, with potential implications for the environmental benefits of household conservation. Using survey and experimental data from 2592 residents in Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, this paper assesses how accurately urban households estimate the electricity consumption of 11 common appliances, whether their judgments exhibit patterns consistent with availability-based reasoning, and whether a randomized heat-related information cue improves relative appliance-energy judgments. The results reveal substantial misalignment between perceived and benchmark electricity use: (1) respondents tend to overestimate the energy use of low-energy, frequently used appliances (e.g., televisions) while underestimating high-energy, infrequently interacted devices (e.g., water heaters); (2) appliance use frequency is positively associated with perceived energy consumption, a pattern consistent with greater cognitive accessibility of frequently used appliances; (3) random assignment to the heat-related cue increases perceived energy use for heat-producing appliances and improves respondents' measured relative correspondence with the benchmark; and (4) further analyses show that higher educational attainment is associated with closer benchmark alignment and that closer alignment is associated with lower reported household electricity expenditures. These findings document systematic deviations in appliance-level energy judgments and show that a targeted information cue can improve such judgments. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: What drives hybrid cultivated meat acceptance? Evidence from a controlled real-product tasting
Abstract: Despite growing interest in cultivated meat, most consumer-related evidence remains based on hypothetical assessments rather than real product exposure, limiting understanding of actual sensory-driven acceptance. To address this gap, the present study investigated consumer responses to a commercially available hybrid cultivated chicken product through a controlled affective sensory evaluation with young Singaporean consumers. Participants (n = 82) evaluated overall liking and sensory liking for appearance, smell, taste, texture, and aftertaste, completed Just-About-Right (JAR) diagnostics and were segmented according to Net Promoter Score (NPS) responses. JAR penalty analysis suggested that deviations from optimal sensory intensity systematically affected overall liking, with excessive intensity perceived in taste, smell, and aftertaste generating the largest penalties. Across sensory dimensions, oral attributes exerted a stronger influence on liking than appearance, with taste emerging as the primary driver of acceptance and texture showing a secondary contribution. Multiple regression analysis confirmed taste liking as the strongest predictor of overall liking, whereas the remaining sensory aspects showed weaker or non-significant effects. NPS segmentation further revealed clear differences in recommendation behaviour across detractors, passives, and promoters, closely mirroring hedonic liking patterns and supporting consistency between sensory evaluation and recommendation-oriented behavioural responses. Overall, this study provides an initial empirical benchmark of consumer responses to a commercially available hybrid cultivated meat product under controlled conditions, highlighting the central role of taste quality and sensory balance in shaping hedonic responses and consumer satisfaction. Authors: Kang I.; Wei S.
Title: Persuasive triggers and psychological pathways: Unplanned purchase behavior in live-streaming blind box commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Unplanned purchasing is increasingly embedded in digital experiences in which consumers encounter commercial opportunities without a prior intention to shop. This study examines how such opportunities become valued and actionable in live-streaming blind-box commerce. Using survey data from 231 Chinese consumers with experience purchasing blind boxes through livestreams, we test a process model linking scarcity messages, time pressure, economic benefits, and fear of missing out (FOMO) with perceived value, emotional and cognitive self-efficacy, and unplanned purchase behavior (UPB). All four conditions were positively associated with perceived value, which was positively associated with both forms of self-efficacy; emotional and cognitive self-efficacy were, in turn, positively associated with UPB. Streamer persuasiveness strengthened the relationships between all four antecedent conditions and perceived value. The findings show that an unplanned purchase need not arise simply from impulsive responding. Consumers may encounter an unexpected opportunity, judge it to be worthwhile, and feel capable of acting even when the purchase was not previously planned. The study extends research on livestream commerce by explaining how persuasive conditions relate to value appraisal and perceived capability, providing a process-based account of UPB in an uncertain and interactive retail setting. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of combining persuasive communication with clear and transparent presentation of purchase conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: When loyalty points become donations: The effects of redeemability, point expiration, and descriptive norm information
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Although loyalty programs and checkout charity are widely implemented across retail industries, the integration of reward point donations into online checkout charity remains rare, and consumer behavior in this context is not yet fully understood. While a few studies have explored reward point donations and generally reported positive consumer responses, to the best of our knowledge, little research has examined how reward point characteristics and situational factors influence consumers' willingness to donate. To address this gap, the present research examines, across three studies, the effect of point redeemability on consumers’ donation intention through online checkout charity, as well as the moderating roles of point expiration and descriptive norm information. Study 1 shows that consumers exhibit higher donation intention when their reward points are non-redeemable than when they are redeemable. Study 2 demonstrates that the interaction between point redeemability and point expiration significantly influences donation intention, while Study 3 shows that the interaction between point redeemability and descriptive norm information also significantly affects donation intention. Authors: Liu J.; An X.; Xu S.
Title: A framework integrating topological potential and semantic embeddings for identifying scientific research clusters in scholarly collaboration networks
Abstract: Multi-team collaboration is essential for addressing major scientific challenges. Previous methods focus predominantly on individuals or single teams, making it difficult to capture the structure of multi-team collaborative innovation systems. To address this, this study conceptualizes a research cluster as a multi-team system formed through inter-team relationships and related research goals within complex collaborative research environments. We further introduce a four-phase Topological Potential–Semantic Embedding Research Cluster Identification (TPSE-RCI) framework to identify scientific research clusters. First, research teams are detected and a team collaboration network is constructed. Second, team feature vectors are generated via topological potential–enhanced Node2Vec and initial clusters are identified with HDBSCAN. Third, team publications are analyzed using BERTopic with BGE-M3 semantic embeddings to derive hierarchical research goals. Fourth, validity criteria are applied to filter scientific research clusters. Using medical informatics publications as a case study, we detected 4262 research teams from 81,557 publications by 269,598 authors. At the structural level, 702 initial scientific research clusters were identified. At the thematic level, 319 topics were extracted from the team publications and consolidated into 21 secondary and 7 primary research goals. By integrating structural and thematic results, we ultimately identified 239 scientific research clusters. Comparative and ablation analyses indicate that incorporating topological potential improves team representation and structural-clustering quality within this empirical setting. The identified research clusters can provide decision support for practical tasks such as organized research management, major project coordination and optimization, domain expert identification, and research resource allocation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Kim P.H.; Ferragamo A.
Author full names: Kim, Peter H. (26643334700); Ferragamo, Alys (60240321200)
Title: Repairing trust in AI: Attribution, anthropomorphism, and the illusion of difference
Abstract: Trust repair between humans and AI systems is an emerging area of inquiry that builds on a well-established literature in human–human (HH) interactions. This review examines how key HH findings, particularly the differential effectiveness of repair strategies following competence versus integrity violations, generalize to human–robot interaction (HRI). While some patterns hold, important divergences exist. The paper argues that better operationalizations of integrity violations and increased anthropomorphism can align HRI findings more closely with HH research. However, enduring challenges remain regarding the ethics of anthropomorphic design, the moral values AI should adopt, and how AI should extend trust to humans. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Cheng Z.; Tu S.; Chen Y.; Deng X.; Zhu C.
Title: How do UAVs govern data sovereignty in decentralized federated sensing networks? Tokenized access control via policy-driven smart contracts
Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become pivotal in a wide range of applications due to their high mobility, broad coverage, and multi-sensor integration. Advances in wireless networks have further spurred interest in cross-domain collaboration among UAVs from diverse institutions, platforms, and control domains, giving rise to decentralized federated sensing as an emerging research direction. However, the absence of trusted intermediaries, dynamic network topologies, and heterogeneous data ownership make it challenging to achieve ownership-controllable and fine-grained data protection in such decentralized UAV networks. To tackle these challenges, we propose a blockchain-based decentralized access control framework integrating three novel mechanisms. First, a Hybrid Data Token Model (HDTM) unifies composable, fine-grained data permissions that distinguish fungible (replicable) from non-fungible (data-modifying) rights, and anchors them to data provenance via a cryptographic Data Ownership Signature. Second, an Unspent Fungible Token Outputs (UFTO) mechanism enforces attribute-level transfer constraints and discrepancy detection to govern permission lifecycle with full traceability. Third, a Smart contract-driven Attribute-Based Access Control (ScaBAC) algorithm distributes the ABAC decision pipeline across four modular, independently verifiable smart contracts, coupling access decisions to on-chain token state for auditable, verifiable authorization. An implementation implemented on Hyperledger Fabric achieves a throughput of 128–160 tx/s across the ScaBAC contract suite, a 32% reduction in average latency compared to the PpBAC baseline, and sub-10 ms read-query response. These results demonstrate that fine-grained, decentralized access control is feasible under the resource and topology constraints of UAV federated sensing networks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Yin Y.; Zhou J.; Peng K.
Title: Online dating paradox: Why lonely hearts choose to ghost
Abstract: This study examines the differential associations of state and trait loneliness with ghosting behavior in online dating, considering self-presentation strategies and dating fatigue as potential explanatory pathways. Survey data from 881 Chinese mobile dating app users were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that state loneliness was negatively associated with ghosting, whereas trait loneliness was positively associated with ghosting. Dating fatigue was positively associated with ghosting and statistically mediated the associations between both forms of loneliness and ghosting in opposite directions. Acquisitive self-presentation was positively associated with state loneliness and negatively associated with trait loneliness; unexpectedly, it was negatively associated with dating fatigue. Authentic self-presentation was not significantly associated with loneliness or dating fatigue. These findings suggest that temporary and chronic loneliness may correspond to different patterns of engagement and disengagement in online dating. The study contributes to mobile dating research by distinguishing state and trait loneliness and by identifying dating fatigue as an important correlate of ghosting behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Sustainable production and export performance of globe artichoke in Egypt: evidence from 2000 to 2023
Abstract: The globe artichoke is one of the major vegetable crops cultivated in the Mediterranean Basin, with global production reaching nearly 1.6 million tons in 2023. Egypt is among the world’s leading producers, contributing almost one-fifth of global production; however, its export performance remains relatively limited compared with its production potential. This study examines the production dynamics, geographical distribution, and export competitiveness of globe artichoke in Egypt during 2000–2023 within the framework of sustainable agricultural development. Both quantitative and qualitative approaches were used to analyze trends in cultivated areas, productivity, and exports, in addition to major competitiveness indicators in international markets. The results indicate that production growth was driven mainly by horizontal expansion rather than improvements in yield. The cultivated area increased to 50.4 thousand fed in 2023, with an average annual growth rate of about 8%, whereas yield increased only marginally during the study period. Expansion was more pronounced in new lands than in old lands, reflecting the crop’s adaptability to new production areas but also indicating limited progress in productivity efficiency. Despite the increase in production, globe artichoke exports declined by approximately 1.4%, largely due to rising competition from Mediterranean countries, export market concentration, and price fluctuations. Italy, France, and Spain remained the main importers of Egyptian artichokes while simultaneously representing major competitors in international markets. The findings suggest that improving productivity efficiency, promoting value-added products, and diversifying export markets may contribute to strengthening export competitiveness and enhancing the long-term sustainability of globe artichoke production in Egypt. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Yu H.; Yang S.; Wang H.
Title: Quantifying compressibility-induced hydrodynamic deviations from isothermal assumptions in immersed top-blowing reactors
Abstract: Current designs of high-temperature top-blowing reactors predominantly rely on isothermal water models or incompressible simulations. These approaches inherently neglect gas thermal expansion, leading to a systematic underestimation of actual mixing capacity and equipment wear. To explicitly quantify these compressibility-driven effects, a compressible volume of fluid (VOF) model was established for an industrial-scale reactor. By contrasting a high-temperature condition (1473.15 K) against a cold baseline (293.15 K) representing conventional isothermal assumptions, this study isolates the hydrodynamic contribution of thermal expansion. The results are as follows: i) Thermal expansion-driven mechanism: The primary driver of liquid agitation is the rapid thermal expansion and pressure release of the injected gas. The resulting volumetric expansion strengthens gas–liquid momentum transfer, increases the required upstream supply pressure, extends gas residence time, and slows the periodic oscillation of the impinging cavity. ii) Enhanced liquid mixing capacity: Thermal expansion expands the impinging cavity volume to twice that of the cold state. Consequently, the total liquid kinetic energy increases by a factor of 2.31, the net gas–liquid interfacial area expands by 81%, and the dead zone volume fraction sharply decreases from 58.41% to 22.40%. iii) Intensified splashing and scouring: The thermodynamically enhanced mixing inherently triggers more violent interfacial dynamics, yielding a 2.47-fold increase in splash volume. This intensification corresponds to a fourfold escalation in reactor wall shear forces and a 62.2% rise in lance shear force. This study explicitly quantifies the physical deviations embedded in traditional isothermal models. These findings provide a quantitative reference for correcting isothermal modeling assumptions in the design and wear-risk assessment of high-temperature gas–liquid reactors. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Zeng T.; Zhang R.; Ke Q.; Yu Y.
Title: Does low-carbon policy improve the environmental performance in China?
Abstract: This study examines the impacts and driving mechanisms of low-carbon policy on environmental performance, with a focus on both direct policy effects and the underlying structural drivers. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions and years, the analysis employs a combination of econometric modeling and configurational approaches to capture heterogeneous and non-linear relationships. The results indicate that low-carbon policy significantly improves environmental performance, particularly in terms of emissions reduction, energy efficiency, and pollution control. However, the magnitude and direction of these effects vary across regions depending on differences in economic development, industrial structure, and governance capacity. Further analysis reveals that technological innovation, green investment, regulatory intensity, and public participation are key driving factors that jointly shape policy effectiveness. The study also identifies multiple pathways through which these factors interact to enhance environmental outcomes, highlighting the importance of synergistic policy design. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how low-carbon goals translate into measurable environmental improvements and offer practical implications for policymakers seeking to optimize policy implementation in diverse socio-economic contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Epistemic justice and deep-sea mining: UNCLOS’s facilitation of epistemic diversity the International Seabed Authority’s decision-making process
Abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. The paper reflects on epistemic justice in energy- and ocean governance, and asks whether and how United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) facilitates that such justice is sought in the regulatory process of deep sea mining by focusing on procedural rules for the International Seabed Authority (ISA) and the representation of different knowers in the decision-making process, including its Council's structure, authority, and composition. It concludes that a very small number of individuals has the power to bring about a very large change in deep sea mining regulations, currently without legal requirements to include experiential, traditional or other forms of knowledges beyond the scientific method in the decision-making process. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Technostress in the age of digital transformation and AI: A bibliometric–systematic literature review for HRM research
Abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are reshaping human resource management through algorithmic recruitment, automated evaluation, predictive analytics, and generative tools. While these systems improve efficiency, they also intensify technostress through opacity, surveillance, reduced control, and digitally intensified work arrangements. Responding to a fragmented literature spanning both AI-enabled and broader digital work systems, this study provides a B-SLR that maps technostress in digital transformation while identifying AI-specific stressors as a key emerging stream for HRM research. Drawing on 194 Scopus-indexed articles, we combine performance analysis and science mapping to identify publication trends, dominant themes, and intellectual structures. The review shows how AI-specific stressors extend established technostress mechanisms and shift attention toward transparency, control, fairness, and responsible HRM design. We conclude with actionable implications for researchers and practitioners aiming to design more transparent, responsible, and sustainable digital and AI-enabled HRM systems. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Li X.; Meng H.
Title: The allure of imperfection: How ugly-cute aesthetics drive purchase intentions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The rise of social media has increased both aesthetic diversity and consumer attention to product appearance and emotional appeal. This research examines the commercially successful yet under-researched “ugly-cute” aesthetic, exemplified by products like Pop Mart's LABUBU. Moving beyond traditional approaches that treat beauty (or ugliness) and cuteness as separate dimensions, we investigate their interactive effects through four studies: one field experiment and three online experiments, involving participants from both China and the United States. Our findings show that the combination of ugly-cute configurations can attenuate the purchase-intention disadvantage associated with ugliness-related aesthetic deviation, with this effect explained by perceived social value and moderated by consumption setting (public vs. private). Specifically, this effect is more pronounced in public consumption settings, where consumers are more likely to seek social approval and positive evaluation from others, thereby amplifying perceived social value in purchase decisions. These results advance the literature on product design and consumer aesthetics by identifying a psychological explanation underlying consumer responses to atypical aesthetics, and provide practical insights for designing products that generate perceived social value (e.g., feeling accepted, gaining approval, or being positively regarded by others). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Xu J.; Xu H.; Ma G.
Title: Political career incentives and the environmental costs: Evidence from China's promotion tournaments
Abstract: This paper shows that promotion incentives for county-level cadres in China are an important driver of air pollution deterioration. Building on the multi-winner tournament model proposed by Clark and Riis (1998), we predict an inverted-U-shaped relationship between the number of counties within a prefecture and the promotion incentives for county-level cadres. Using the length of small rivers as an instrumental variable for the number of counties within a prefecture, our empirical analysis identifies a robust inverted-U-shaped relationship between the number of counties and air pollution levels, suggesting that promotion incentives significantly exacerbate air pollution. Further analysis reveals that, in pursuit of economic growth, local cadres tend to relax environmental regulations and attract more pollution-intensive firms. In regions where cadres’ performance evaluation places less emphasis on economic growth, the inverted-U-shaped relationship does not exist. These findings suggest that local cadres’ career incentives stimulate economic growth at the expense of the environment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
