Title: Evaluation of Prompt Engineering for LLM-Based Construction Contract Risk Analysis
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasing potential for complex analytical tasks; however, their reliability in high-stakes domains such as construction contract interpretation remains insufficiently understood. This study presents a controlled, human-in-the-loop evaluation of how prompt-engineering strategies influence the quality and perceived reliability of LLM-generated risk analyses for New Engineering Contract (NEC4)-style clauses. Generative pretrained transformer GPT-4.1 was applied in a deterministic configuration to identify contractor risks across six synthetic NEC4-style Z-clauses using five prompt strategies: baseline, direct, role based, chain of thought, and guided prompting. Thirty outputs were evaluated under a blinded protocol against expert-derived reference risk lists by a mixed-expertise cohort, supporting exploratory comparison. Assessment combined descriptive quantitative analysis of Likert-scale ratings of accuracy, completeness, clarity, legal salience, and hallucination risk with qualitative thematic analysis. Results indicate that guided, clause-anchored prompting produced more structured, legally grounded, and traceable outputs, whereas less constrained strategies exhibited narrative drift and weaker clause linkage. These findings suggest that structured prompting may support more consistent clause-level interpretation under controlled conditions, although conclusions remain bounded by the exploratory design, limited sample, and synthetic dataset. The study contributes to understanding how prompt design shapes interpretability and verifiability in contract analysis. The clause-guided human-in-the-loop (CG-HITL) framework is presented as a conceptual approach to support structured use of LLMs in preaward contract risk assessment.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Author full names: Mader, Anna (59707856600); Mußhoff, Oliver (23005505500)
Title: When heat hits: Short-run saving and withdrawal behavior among microfinance clients in Benin
Abstract: Increased access to finance is widely viewed as a key driver to increase adaptive capacity in response to climate change. However, apart from limited studies on borrowing behavior, little is known about how exposure to extreme heat is associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. This study addresses this gap by investigating the short-run associations of unusual heat with microfinance clients’ saving and withdrawal behavior. In a case study, it combines geo-located temperature data with a unique dataset of around 50,000 clients of a leading Microfinance Institution (MFI) in Benin. Applying two-way fixed effects, seemingly unrelated regression, and ordinary least squares models, the study finds that exposure to extreme heat is heterogeneously associated with microfinance clients’ financial behavior. Specifically, non-agricultural clients show suggestive evidence of the accumulation of precautionary savings after extreme heat days in the preceding quarter, while extreme heat days are negatively associated with agricultural clients’ savings. Microfinance clients increase their withdrawals when exposed to extreme heat within the preceding quarter, but the association is not robust for agricultural clients’ withdrawals in response to an increase in annual extreme heat days. Addressing the heterogeneous financial responses across different clients to extreme heat consequently requires explicit policy attention. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the associations between extreme heat and individual economic outcomes, how financial behavior relates to weather risk, and how microfinance clients respond to shocks. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: From tourism pressure to overtourism vulnerability regimes: A municipal impact assessment framework for sustainable destination governance
Abstract: Overtourism is increasingly understood as a multidimensional sustainability challenge, yet local decision-makers still lack replicable tools for assessing where tourism pressure may translate into territorial vulnerability. This paper develops a municipal impact-assessment framework for diagnosing overtourism vulnerability regimes. The analysis follows a two-step logic. First, a regional tourism-pressure screening index is constructed for Euro-Mediterranean NUTS-2 regions to identify broader high-pressure contexts. Second, an Overtourism Vulnerability Index (OVI) is implemented for the main tourism hotspots in Apulia, Italy, using eight normalized indicators capturing direct tourism pressure, air accessibility, accommodation platformisation, economic dependence and heritage attractiveness. Authors: Han X.; Li S.; Liu H.; Zhang M.
Title: When GAI backfires: Understanding the process mechanism of consumers’ avoidance of generative AI conversational recommendation agents from a misaligned affordance perspective
Abstract: Generative AI-enhanced conversational recommendation agents (GCRAs) are being widely deployed on e-commerce platforms; however, consumers increasingly avoid these advanced recommendation tools. Prior research has not systematically identified which specific features of GCRAs drive such avoidance, nor has it clearly articulated the underlying process mechanisms through which avoidance emerges. To address these gaps, this study draws on affordance actualization theory and misaligned affordance theory to systematically investigate consumers’ perceived GCRA misaligned affordances and to model the complete pathways from these misaligned affordances to consumer avoidance behaviors. We employed a sequential mixed-methods approach. First, a qualitative interview research (N = 19) combined with a simple experiment identified three key GCRA misaligned affordances: limited choices, iterative dialogue, and hallucinated information. Second, a quantitative research (N = 538) validated that these misaligned affordances trigger cost-based comparative appraisals (opportunity and transaction costs), which in turn lead to negative experiences (both outcome-related and process-related), ultimately driving consumer avoidance. Finally, by integrating the findings across studies, we developed a comprehensive framework explaining consumers’ avoidance of GCRAs. Theoretically, this research advances the misaligned affordance actualization theory by highlighting the novel comparative appraisal stage, moving the theory from qualitative conceptualization to process-level mechanisms. Title: Effects of AI-based chatbot coaching on goal attainment, self-efficacy, and stress: A longitudinal randomized experiment
Abstract: Students in higher education face a range of academic challenges, which leads to high levels of stress among many students. While coaching has been shown to help students address these challenges, it is resource-intensive and therefore not broadly accessible. AI-based chatbots may help broaden access by providing interactive and personalized guidance at scale, yet empirical evidence on their effectiveness remains limited, particularly from longitudinal experimental studies. Students in the chatbot coaching and literature study conditions engaged in repeated interactions with the intervention, averaging approximately 100 min of cumulative interaction time accumulated across four sessions of 23–28 min each. We examined how students’ goal attainment, university-related self-efficacy, and stress developed over the course of the study. Results showed that students in the AI-based chatbot condition achieved significantly stronger increases in goal attainment over time compared to students in both control conditions. Self-efficacy also increased in the AI-based chatbot condition over time; however, between-condition differences were not consistent across time points, suggesting that the intervention had a more limited impact on self-efficacy relative to goal attainment. Furthermore, no significant effects were found for university-related stress. Title: Reliability evaluation of multi-state logistics networks with weibull-based capacities under time-dependent spoilage
Abstract: This paper investigates the reliability evaluation for a multi-state logistics network with time-dependent spoilage (MLN-TDS). In the MLN-TDS, arc capacities represent the number of available logistics vehicles, whose time-dependent availability is characterized by a Weibull distribution. Unlike conventional models that assume a constant spoilage rate, this paper evaluates the time-dependent spoilage (TDS) rate of each minimal path according to its delivery time. To account for the resulting discrepancy between dispatched and delivered quantities, intact flow vectors are constructed to determine the required dispatched quantities before deriving the corresponding capacity vectors. The MLN-TDS reliability is defined as the probability that demand can be fulfilled while simultaneously satisfying both loss cost and time constraints. Based on minimal paths and minimal capacity vectors, an algorithm is proposed to evaluate the MLN-TDS reliability, and the recursive sum of disjoint products method is used to compute its value. An illustrative example and a real-world fruit delivery case study are provided to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed evaluation procedure. The results identify critical demand thresholds and show how changes in TDS rates affect MLN-TDS reliability under high-demand conditions. These findings provide quantitative support for reliability-oriented logistics planning and operational decision making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Simple repair policies and decompositions for semi-coherent systems with simultaneous failures
Abstract: We consider semi-coherent binary systems that are subject to simultaneous failures of its components. These are systems whose components can be either working or failed; the system can also be working or failed depending on the state of the components; and repairing a component cannot cause the system to fail. We consider that one or more components can fail simultaneously, allowing us to model external shocks and disasters. For this, we use the Lévy-frailty Marshall–Olkin (LFMO) multivariate distribution to model the failure times of the components. We aim to answer in which states of the system we should repair the components. This is a challenging question, as the number of repair policies grows super-exponentially in the number of components. To tackle this, we propose a simple family of repair policies, which we call r- out-of- n repair policies , where one repairs all failed components when the system fails or when there are r or more failed components. Our main contribution is that we derive exact and simple expressions for key performance-evaluation quantities of the system operating under our proposed repair policies. That is, we give explicit expressions for the mean time-to-failure of the system, mean time-to-repair, probability of system-failure before repair, and component- and system-repair rate. We also give expressions for the expected cost and long-term average cost, when there are components’ and system repair cost. The only relevant parameters involved in the derived expressions are the structural signature of the system, and the Laplace exponent associated to the LFMO distribution. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Guest-origin and temporal heterogeneity in online hotel reviews: A structural topic modeling analysis

Abstract: This study examines whether the relative salience of hotel-review themes varies across guest-origin groups and review years. Structural Topic Modeling was applied to 29,304 Booking.com reviews from 144 hotels in Vietnam collected between 2022 and 2025. Under hotel-clustered inference, 15 of 21 guest-origin contrasts met the within-family false-discovery-rate threshold, compared with 1 of 21 2022-referenced temporal contrasts; 11 guest-origin contrasts showed strong multi-specification evidence. The largest difference was a 27.6-percentage-point higher expected prevalence of the Room cleanliness and comfort topic in Domestic than Western reviews; Domestic reviews also showed an 18.4-percentage-point lower expected prevalence of Staff, location, and breakfast satisfaction. Asian reviews exhibited a distinct profile spanning amenities, walkability, personalized hospitality, travel logistics, and leisure-related content. Temporal evidence was less stable: the 2025–2022 increase in Personalized hospitality and attentive service attenuated after hotel fixed effects, although a separate 2023-referenced analysis identified six supported temporal contrasts. Title: Conflict expression: A decade of group conflict research
Abstract: The conflict expression framework was developed to generate new practical and theoretical insights into how conflict communication affects group processes and negotiated outcomes. The framework proposes that conflict expressions vary along two dimensions: directness and oppositional intensity. The framework suggested that the effects of different types of conflict on group processes and outcomes likely depend on how the conflict is expressed, that conflict within groups is likely perceived differently by different members of the same social unit, and that conflict affects negotiation processes dynamically through reciprocated statements and responses. Title: Performative narratives and destination image in cross-cultural tourism livestreaming
Abstract: Tourism livestreaming allows global audiences to encounter destinations in real time, yet how livestreamers’ expressive behaviors shape audiences’ destination evaluations across cultures remains unclear. Drawing on a performative perspective, this research conceptualizes expressed destination image formation as a temporally situated process generated through live narrative enactment. Using multimodal cross-cultural livestream data, the study shows that emotional expression is positively associated with expressed affective destination image, explicit self-disclosure is positively associated with expressed cognitive image, and interactive engagement shows partial evidence of an inverted U-shaped relationship with expressed cognitive destination image. Title: Can stablecoin instability threaten emerging tourism payment infrastructure?
Abstract: Stablecoins are increasingly discussed as an emerging form of digital tourism payment infrastructure. This study examines whether instability in stablecoins creates vulnerabilities in emerging tourism payment ecosystems by analysing the UST and USDC depeg events. Drawing on tourism systems theory, tourism resilience theory, and financial economics, the analysis combines high-frequency market data, on-chain transaction activity, and tourism payment indicators. The results show that depeg events degrade market quality by widening bid–ask spreads, reducing market depth, and increasing transaction costs. Large market participants also reduce risk-bearing and withdraw liquidity during periods of stress. In addition, depeg events strengthen dynamic correlations among closely linked stablecoins. Evidence from tourism payment activity suggests that severe depeg events may reduce the use of stablecoin-based payments within crypto-native tourism ecosystems. Title: Encountering the “familiar stranger”: Activating latent cultural identification among Vietnamese tourists in China
Abstract: Tourism studies have largely examined cultural identification through encounters with difference, while paying less attention to culturally proximate travel contexts. Drawing on schema theory, this study examines how latent cultural identification (LCI) emerges when sedimented cultural meanings become perceptible and interpretable during travel. Title: Modeling Japanese consumers' acceptance and rejection of tech-enhanced foods
Abstract: To maintain the well-being of the global population, strengthening the food supply system is necessary. Title: Activating competing goals: The dual effect of environmental fee

Title: Barriers and enablers to circular economy implementation in 3D concrete printing: A fuzzy decision-making approach
Abstract: The circular economy (CE) is increasingly emphasised in 3D concrete printing (3DCP), yet evidence remains limited on the key barriers to its implementation and the enablers needed to support practical uptake. Title: Emotional interaction and conversion value in live streaming E-commerce

Abstract: Multi-agent emotional interaction constitutes a core characteristic of live streaming e-commerce. Title: The temporal shift in consumer hue preferences in hotel booking
Abstract: Despite the hospitality industry's ongoing pursuit of optimal color marketing strategies, it remains unclear whether consumers respond more favorably to cool or warm hues. This research investigates how consumers' hue preferences in digital marketing imagery shift as a function of time of day. These preferences are mediated by the need for uniqueness and the need for belonging, respectively. Title: Respect your privacy: An identifiable and authorized privacy-preserving data retrieval protocol through decentralized identifier
Abstract: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires personal data processing to satisfy both the principles of lawfulness and data minimization. However, existing privacy-preserving data retrieval protocols rarely meet both principles, especially at the batch scale. To solve these problems, we present IAPDR, an Identifiable and Authorized Privacy-Preserving Data Retrieval protocol that builds on Decentralised Identifier (DID) that focuses on data-subject privacy under GDPR compliance. Under the same dataset sizes and network settings on public benchmarks, IAPDR achieves an average 1.36 × improvement in computational efficiency and an average 3.62 × reduction in total communication compared with state-of-the-art schemes. Title: A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
Abstract: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Additionally, organizational strategic flexibility and digital leadership positively moderate the relationships between these individual factors and resistance. Title: Is state fragility a hindrance to trade openness in Africa?
Abstract: This paper analyses the effects of state fragility on trade openness in Africa, using panel data for 50 African countries over the period 1995–2018. Title: Achieving emotionally and factually grounded interactive comments through a large language model-driven adaptive dialogue engine

Abstract: With the rapid development of e-commerce, online product comments have become a major reference point for consumers in making purchase decisions. Title: Do platform and seller cues improve price prediction? A study on online food delivery platforms using machine learning
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: This study investigates value-based pricing on online food delivery platforms by examining the role of beyond-core service attributes—platform brand and Observed Restaurant Activity Duration—as observable platform- and restaurant-level cues. Title: The generalization and diversity of global urban regularities
Abstract: The simple but appealing regularities have been observed in the complex urban systems, yet their applicability to contemporary global urbanization remains controversial. Here we conducted a global synthesis of urban regularities, including Zipf's law, Gibrat's law, and scaling law, through multiple urbanity dimensions across 9,014 consistently defined urban areas from 1985 to 2020. We found that general urban regularities governed global urban evolution, as evidenced by the enduring power distributions and common spatial scaling relationships, but with localized diversity reflecting urban development. Globally, Zipfian α moved toward 1, declining from 1.12 to 1.00 for urban area, increasing from 0.91 to 0.97 for population, and declining from 1.34 to 1.17 for GDP during the past decades. These changes were associated with the persistent deviations from Gibrat's law, linking size-dependent growth to the evolution of urban size distributions. Urban rank changes illustrated urban economic transformations and spatial realignments, particularly in Asia and Africa. Population scaled sublinearly with urban area, whereas GDP, nighttime light intensity, and CO2 emissions scaled superlinearly, revealing paradoxes in urban prosperity and environmental impact and prompting a reconsideration of sustainability paradigms, especially in less-developed regions. Title: When does AI design help or hurt? Brand positioning and the dual effects of homogeneity and trend relevance in fashion retailing
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in fashion design to generate product aesthetics and forecast trends. While prior research has separately examined algorithmic homogeneity risks or efficiency gains, how consumers simultaneously process these opposing signals, and whether this processing differs from human-generated design, remains unclear. A 2 (design source: AI vs. human) × 2 (brand positioning: avant-garde vs. mainstream) between-subjects experiment with 412 consumers reveals that AI-attributed designs simultaneously heighten both perceptions. Brand positioning moderates these effects asymmetrically: the negative homogeneity pathway is amplified for avant-garde brands, while the positive trend-relevance pathway is strengthened for mainstream brands. Title: Who eats matters: How eating-agent identity in short-form retail videos influences consumers’ purchase intentions
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Short-form retail videos frequently depict food consumption, yet little is known about whether the identity of the visible eater shapes how consumers evaluate the product. Consequently, consumers infer greater product naturalness and greater healthiness, increasing purchase intention. This inference depends on how the consumption episode is structured: visible human assistance attenuates the pet advantage by altering the product-use relationship, whereas sponsorship disclosure changes the surrounding commercial context without necessarily disrupting that relationship. Five preregistered online experiments with 2462 retained participants from Chinese consumer panels support this account. Study 1 establishes the effect and examines alternative explanations. Study 2 demonstrates the sequential pathway through perceived naturalness and perceived healthiness. Study 3 manipulates naturalness information to provide causal evidence for the perceived naturalness component of the proposed pathway, Study 4 identifies eating autonomy as a boundary condition, and Study 5 shows that the focal pathway remains evident in the sponsorship disclosure context. Title: WISE: An interpretable word intensity framework for emotion-aware conversational systems
Abstract: Emotion-aware conversational systems are increasingly adopted in healthcare, yet most emotion detection approaches rely on sentiment polarity, which fails to capture emotional nuance and intensity in short, informal chat messages. Title: Knowledge graph–based data governance for small and medium-sized enterprises: A systematic literature review and socio-technical framework
Abstract: Established data governance frameworks provide valuable guidance for large enterprises, yet their assumptions about stable funding, dedicated governance teams, and mature infrastructure often do not reflect the realities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Recent research has explored the use of semantic technologies and knowledge graphs to automate governance tasks, improve traceability, and support policy enforcement. Yet, whether these approaches effectively address SME-specific needs remains unclear. This paper presents a systematic literature review of knowledge-graph-based data governance approaches, focusing on their relevance to SMEs. Following the PRISMA method, we analyzed evidence from 43 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 through multiple lenses, including core data governance activities (Define, Implement, Monitor), components of the Data Governance Institute framework, and stages of the data lifecycle. Using thematic network analysis we synthesize recurring limitations and structural patterns across the literature. Our findings show that while semantic technologies demonstrate strong potential for automating policy enforcement, metadata integration, and interoperability, most approaches are designed for mature enterprises. They commonly assume formal governance hierarchies, specialized expertise, and sustained operational capacity, conditions that are often absent in SMEs. As a result, governance designs are skewed toward technical controls and early lifecycle stages, with limited attention to monitoring, organizational roles, decision rights, and end-to-end governance. Building on these findings, this study advances a socio-technical perspective on data governance in SME contexts by reframing governance as a lifecycle-embedded and practice-oriented capability rather than a purely technical implementation. It further conceptualizes knowledge graphs as boundary objects that mediate between governance intent, technical enforcement, and organizational practice. Our key contributions include a structured synthesis of knowledge-graph-based data governance research, identifies eight recurring gaps that hinder SME applicability, and derives nine design principles alongside a conceptual research framework to guide future research and the development of SME-suitable governance solutions. © 2026

Title: Fuel vs. food? Climate shocks, biofuel expansion, and the future of global food security
Abstract: The expansion of biofuel production has generated debate over its potential trade-off with food security, particularly regarding land diversion, rising food prices, and climate-related agricultural stress. This study utilizes panel data from 5 emerging (BRICS) and 7 advanced economies (G7) employing Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MM-QR) and Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) for robustness to examine the association between biofuel production and agricultural total-factor productivity, crop value, and global food security during the period 2012-2022. The differing associations of environmental policy stringency are broadly consistent with the conditional predictions of the Porter hypothesis, rather than indicating uniform regulatory benefits. Title: Convergence of Implicit Gradient Descent for Training Two-Layer Physics-Informed Neural Networks
Source title: East Asian Journal on Applied Mathematics
Abstract: The optimization algorithms are crucial in training physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), as unsuitable methods may lead to poor solutions. Title: Shared value vs plural values. Contesting renewable energy projects of the Enel Group

Title: From precarious work to occupational health outcomes in hotel housekeepers: a narrative review with meta-synthesis
Abstract: Introduction: Hotel housekeepers sustain the core functioning of the hospitality industry yet perform demanding, repetitive, and undervalued work associated with substantial physical and psychosocial risks. Results Findings revealed employment precarity, work intensification, musculoskeletal pain, chemical and biological hazards, and elevated stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Time pressure fostered coping strategies such as skipping meals and delaying bathroom use. Workers also expressed pride, intrinsic motivation, and collective action to make their contributions visible. Improving occupational health requires organizational and policy transformations: realistic workloads, safer equipment, secure contracts, participatory risk management, and leadership practices grounded in dignity and fairness; rather than reliance on individual coping. Title: Communication-efficient distributed quantile regression neural networks via convolution smoothing and poisson sampling

Title: Inter-class co-movement of retail electricity tariffs and the residential adjustment gradient: evidence from a new Latin American panel
Abstract: How do the published retail electricity tariffs of different consumer classes move together, and do the schedules of captive residential users adjust more slowly than those of large consumers? Title: Research on interruption risk propagation in aircraft supply chain network: A multi-layer network coupling model
Abstract: The aircraft supply chain (ASC) is a core component of national high-end equipment manufacturing systems, which have complex network characteristics of strong coupling. Subsequently, the microscopic Markov chain approach is employed to establish state transition Eqs., and the mathematical characteristics of interruption risk outbreak are derived through theoretical deduction. Title: Multi-output stability prediction of salt cavern energy storage using optimized machine learning model with interpretable features
Abstract: Salt cavern stability prediction is essential for the safe operation and risk prevention of underground energy-storage systems. In this study, a multi-output machine learning framework was developed to simultaneously predict maximum wall displacement (MD) and volume reduction rate (RV) of salt caverns. Fifteen machine learning algorithms were first compared using the Friedman test and Nemenyi post-hoc test, and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) was selected as the optimal base learner. Subsequently, four metaheuristic algorithms, including Jellyfish Search Optimizer (JSO), Tunicate Swarm Algorithm (TSA), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), were used to optimize the MLP hyperparameters. Title: D4RNet: A lightweight distracted driver detection network with knowledge distillation and gradient reversal layer
Abstract: Distracted Driver Detection (DDD) is critical for intelligent transportation systems, yet existing methods often incur high computational costs, leading to non-real-time detection on terminals and/or limited generalization across different camera views. In this work, we propose D4RNet, a lightweight Distracted Driver Detection network that integrates knowledge Distillation with a gradient Reversal layer (GRL) for the first time in this domain. We employ a Swin-B as a teacher guide a MobileNetV2 student for training, in addition to predicting the type of distraction, the forward path extracts multi-scale, low-semantic features to predict the auxiliary tags, while during backpropagation the GRL reverses the gradient to adversarially suppress the auxiliary label, thereby enforcing the model to learn domain-invariant representations of the distraction behaviors, rather than noise such as image modality, camera angle, or vehicle scenes. Experimental results show improvements of 3.4% on D-all and 4.3% on N-all over the baseline, attains 81.32% average accuracy over eight subsets, surpassing the previous SOTA by 3.36%, while achieving 52 FPS on a real edge device, Jetson Nano via ONNX Runtime. Qualitative tests on real driving videos also demonstrate strong performance and robustness. Moreover, we introduce five new temporal–spatial combined splits for the 100-Driver dataset along with corresponding baselines, to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of model performance. We also indicate, based on numerous experiments, that future work should prioritize annotation quality and image diversity rather than architectural over-engineering. In summary, D4RNet offers a fast, accurate, and open-source solution for real-time DDD at the edge. Code, data, and models are available at https://github.com/jerodzhao/D4RNet. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Exponential decay for a class of fourth order parabolic equations with logarithmic nonlinearity
Abstract: We consider the initial boundary value problem for a fourth order parabolic equation with p-Laplacian diffusion and logarithmic nonlinearity. For global weak solutions under subcritical initial energy, we establish that the H2 and W1,p norms decay exponentially, which improves the previous algebraic decay result of Liao and Li (2020). The key ingredient in our proof is an energy difference inequality. This refined estimate yields sharper long-time asymptotics and stronger quantitative control than the original algebraic estimate. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Renewable peak shaving via integrated biomass gasification, fuel cell, and storage systems: Biomass selection, life cycle assessment-driven exergoenvironmental analysis, and machine-learning optimization
Abstract: Integrated biomass-fed systems offer a viable alternative to conventional plants, aiming to meet the growing global demand for clean and reliable power. This research investigates a hybrid biomass-fed system designed for energy storage and peak shaving. The configuration includes biomass gasification combined with heat recovery, incorporating a CO2-based power cycle and an organic Rankine cycle. Here, the syngas derived from biomass gasification is used as the primary fuel for a molten carbonate fuel cell integrated with a heat generation component and a Kalina cycle. The system also incorporates compressed air energy storage to enhance load balancing. Utilizing Chlorophora excelsa (BW4), identified as the most suitable biomass fuel among several candidates, the system's performance is assessed from exergy, sustainability, environmental, and life cycle assessment-driven exergoenvironmental perspectives. Afterward, a hybrid machine learning optimization framework is developed, employing artificial neural networks (ANN) with a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II). The optimization targets three key metrics: total exergy destruction rate, overall sustainability index, and overall specific exergoenvironmental impact. The optimization shows these objectives at 56.69 MW, 1.297, 5.86 mPts/GJ, respectively, indicating a balanced trade-off between thermodynamics and ecological impact. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of machine learning in advancing environmentally responsible energy system design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Global research trends in nuclear forensic: A bibliometric review
Abstract: Nuclear forensic science is essential for global nuclear security, supporting the identification and attribution of nuclear materials outside regulatory control. Despite its strategic importance, a systematic understanding of the evolution, thematic structure, and key contributors shaping nuclear forensic research remains limited. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global nuclear forensic publication trends from 1973 to 2024 using peer-reviewed records from the Scopus database as of October 2025. Bibliometric indicators and network analyses were applied to examine temporal publication patterns, source journals, research themes, and authorship characteristics. Findings show that nuclear forensic research has transitioned from an emergent activity to a maturing and structured scientific discipline, mainly driven by international nuclear security priorities. The journal landscape is dominated by analytical chemistry, radiochemistry, and nuclear measurement science. Thematic analysis reveals a consolidated focus on uranium-based materials and attribution-oriented analytical techniques, whereas emerging approaches, such as microstructural analysis and computational methods, remain peripheral. Authorship and country-level analyses demonstrate a high concentration of research output within a limited number of nuclear-capable states and government-affiliated institutions. The results reveal methodological maturity yet highlight structural constraints, emphasizing the need for thematic diversification, interdisciplinary collaboration, and international capacity building to enhance nuclear forensic science globally. © 2026 Korean Nuclear Society, Published by Elsevier Korea LLC. Title: Foodborne microplastics: Occurrence in food matrices, health implications, analytical challenges and multi-tiered control strategies
Abstract: This review critically synthesizes current knowledge on foodborne microplastics (MPs) to establish a scientific foundation for risk assessment and control. Despite their widespread presence in food systems, research is hindered by a lack of standardized detection methods and unresolved uncertainties regarding their health implications. Our synthesis shows that the toxicity of MPs arises from a combination of physical abrasion, chemical leaching, and a “Trojan horse” mechanism that carries co-pollutants, collectively triggering oxidative stress and inflammation. A primary challenge remains the absence of harmonized analytical protocols, especially for nanoplastics. Key conclusions emphasize the need for a multi-tiered control strategy, spanning from source reduction to the development of safer alternatives. While vigilance is warranted, the likely existence of a dose-response relationship argues against undue alarm. Future work should focus on standardizing methods and using human-relevant models to inform evidence-based food safety policies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Trends in access to basic sanitation services across Brazilian municipalities under a new legal framework
Abstract: Federal Law No. 14,026/2020 updated Brazil's sanitation legal framework, reinforcing universalization targets for water supply and sewage services. It mandates that by the end of 2033, sanitation contracts must ensure 99% of the population has access to potable water and 90% to sewage collection and treatment. Given Brazil's vast territory and regional disparities, achieving these targets across all municipalities poses a significant challenge. This article examines whether water and sewage coverage rates converged between 2010 and 2022, analyzing municipalities segregated by state and region. The study provides an up-to-date assessment of these indicators and identifies challenges in meeting the established targets. Empirical estimation of convergence draws on economic methodologies for growth and income convergence, incorporating beta-convergence and sigma-convergence hypotheses. This robust methodological approach enables a comprehensive analysis of the evolution of sanitation services in Brazil, offering insights to guide effective public policies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Material use and its relationship with per capita income. A panel data analysis at the global level
Abstract: Global use of materials has significantly increased over recent decades, causing a wide range of environmental and social concerns. In this study, we use the latest available data from the UN database on global material flows to investigate the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis for two widely used material flow indicators, Domestic Material Consumption and Material Footprint, for a dataset of 147 countries. Using both semiparametric and parametric methods over a longer period than any previous study (1970–2019), we find no evidence in support of the EKC hypothesis. A concerning result is that material-income elasticities are higher after 1989, implying that the situation has not improved. We conclude that major changes have not yet occurred in the income-material use relationship and that strong policy measures remain necessary to reduce material consumption. Title: Management of Disputes in the Construction Industry during COVID-19: Contractors' Takeaways for Future Pandemics
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic intensified construction disputes. While dispute management has been widely studied, limited research has examined pandemic-induced disputes globally, especially within the Sri Lankan construction context. Hence, this study aims to investigate how to manage the disputes due to COVID-19 in the Sri Lankan construction industry, considering the contractors' perspective. The study adopts an interpretivist philosophy and employs a qualitative Delphi technique involving two iterative rounds of semistructured interviews, thereby making a methodological contribution. The data were analyzed through manual content analysis. The findings reveal six positive impacts and 12 negative impacts of COVID-19 on the construction industry, along with suitable preventive measures to manage the 12 important causes of disputes arising from the pandemic. This is positioned as one of the limited studies identifying both positive and negative impacts and suitable preventive measures in managing the identified causes. The findings can be applied for developing contexts of a similar nature, particularly in managing disputes during future pandemics.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Li X.; Zhou Y.; Li P.
Title: From sound to resonance: Club anthem attractiveness and fan–brand relationships
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Auditory branding plays an increasingly important role in sensory service experiences; however, limited research has examined how recurring auditory brand cues relate to consumer–brand relationship outcomes. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework as an organizing logic, this study examines associations among club anthem attractiveness (CAA), positive emotion (PE), post-exposure brand cognition (BC), and fan–brand resonance (FBR) in sports leisure services. Data were collected from a screened nonprobability online sample of 468 respondents in China. Participants listened to one of three standardized 90-s club anthem excerpts before evaluating CAA, PE, BC, and FBR. CAA was positively associated with both PE and BC, and these responses were positively associated with FBR. The two prespecified coefficient products were positive, whereas the residual direct CAA–FBR association was not significant. A separate balanced validation study (N = 450) supported CAA's empirical distinction from simple anthem liking, PE, BC, FBR, and prior brand attitude. CAA explained additional variance in PE and BC beyond simple liking and pre-exposure controls, while its incremental association with FBR was small. The findings indicate that evaluations of recurring auditory brand cues covary with consumer–brand relationship outcomes alongside affective and cognitive responses. This study extends auditory branding and sensory service literature by conceptualizing recurring branded sound as a service-embedded cue and examining theoretically ordered affective and cognitive associations. Because CAA was measured and the focal constructs were self-reported within one session, the findings support an association-based interpretation and do not establish temporal mediation or causality. © 2026

Title: Toward sustainable oceans: Redirecting fisheries subsidies through cleaner production in Chile
Abstract: Fisheries subsidies are often linked to overcapacity, overfishing, and environmental harm. As a result, global efforts have increasingly focused on eliminating harmful subsidies, while paying less attention to how public support can be designed to promote positive environmental outcomes. This study analyzes an alternative paradigm from Chile’s industrial shrimp (Heterocarpus reedi) and prawn (Cervimunida johni and Pleuroncodes monodon) fisheries, where a government-supported Clean Production Agreement (CPA) incentivized the adoption of cleaner production methods. Using a mixed-methods approach that combines qualitative documentary analysis with quantitative evaluation of environmental and economic indicators, we assessed the design, implementation, and outcomes of the CPA. Our findings reveal that the scheme enhanced environmental performance by reducing fuel consumption, bycatch, freshwater use, waste, and air emissions, while simultaneously delivering tangible economic benefits for participating companies. The initiative’s success was driven by four key design features: conditional funding tied to environmental goals, mandatory private co-financing, independent auditing and certification, and collaborative governance involving both public and private sectors. Importantly, subsidies did not cover fuel, fleet expansion, or other activities that could increase fishing capacity, thereby mitigating the risks of overcapacity and greenwashing. The Chilean case demonstrates that well-designed environmental subsidies can effectively support sustainability transitions in fisheries and offers valuable policy lessons for differentiating beneficial subsidies from those that threaten marine sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Data-driven virtual engine framework for predicting performance and emissions of biomass waste-derived biofuel engine
Abstract: This research study aims to develop virtual engine models with biofuel blends to forecast their characteristics in terms of combustion, performance and emission by employing multimodal data driven modelling through artificial neural networks. Title: Beyond technological determinism: A multidimensional framework and research agenda for consumer trust in blockchain applications
Abstract: Blockchain technology is increasingly integral to domains such as finance, supply chain, commerce and tourism, yet consumer trust remains a pivotal barrier to its widespread adoption. Studies on trust in blockchain contexts have significant conceptual and contextual limitations that inhibit a holistic understanding of trust formation. In this study, we draw on the antecedents, decisions, outcomes and theory, context, methods (ADO-TCM) framework to systematically review 53 high-quality multidisciplinary studies. We identify three critical issues: (1) technological determinism that conflates technical capability with consumer trust, marginalising psychological, social and institutional factors; (2) theoretical convergence around acceptance models that obscures blockchain-specific trust phenomena; and (3) a narrow geographic and domain scope that creates self-reinforcing knowledge hierarchies limiting generalisability across applications and cultures. To address these gaps, we propose a multidimensional trust framework integrating three dimensions: technological architecture trust, information source trust and social actor trust, reflecting blockchain's sociotechnical structure. Central to this framework is a four-paradigm typology that classifies trust into interpersonal, technology, institutional, and sociotechnical perspectives, revealing that the prevalence of technological determinism reflects theoretical inertia rather than genuine consensus. We complement this with three research themes: multi-level theoretical integration, innovative methodologies and contextual expansion. This study contributes to the information systems discourse by providing a theoretical foundation for understanding trust in complex sociotechnical systems beyond acceptance models. By conceptualising consumer trust as a dynamic, multidimensional construct shaped by interactions between users, technology, and institutions, we offer a research agenda with actionable directions for advancing blockchain trust theory and practice. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The dark side of disrespect: How workplace incivility breeds service sabotage and turnover
Abstract: This study examines how different sources of workplace incivility affect frontline hotel employees. Drawing on Conservation of Resources Theory and Social Identity Theory, Study 1 compares the effects of employee incivility (originating internally) and customer incivility (originating externally) on emotional exhaustion. Based on a scenario-based experiment with 263 participants, the results show that employee incivility causes greater emotional exhaustion than customer incivility. Study 2 further differentiates in-group sources by their hierarchical level—supervisor, same-level colleague, and subordinate—and examines their specific impacts on emotional exhaustion, which, in turn, affects sabotage and turnover intentions. Using survey data from 302 respondents, the findings reveal that same-level colleague incivility has the strongest negative impact, followed by supervisor, subordinate, and customer incivility. Title: Incompetence or deception: Unraveling the asymmetric mechanisms of AI hallucinations on trust and distrust
Abstract: Reliance on generative artificial intelligence (AI) for knowledge work is increasing, yet confidently presented hallucinations can elicit strong negative user reactions. Existing literature frames hallucinations as technical failures that reduce trust, conflating the decline of trust with the emergence of distrust. However, trust and distrust are theoretically distinct constructs rather than opposite ends of a single continuum. Drawing on information manipulation theory (IMT), this study reconceptualizes AI hallucinations as violations of conversational norms. It proposes a model linking hallucination cues to perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially related to trust and distrust. It further examines whether perceived AI autonomy moderates the relationship between hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The model was tested using a sequential mixed-methods design that combined qualitative semi-structured interviews with a two-wave survey of 506 GenAI users. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and necessary condition analysis (NCA). The findings revealed that hallucination cues were differentially associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, with the former more strongly associated with trust and the latter with distrust. Perceived AI autonomy moderated the associations between some hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The PLS-SEM–NCA analysis provided complementary evidence on net effects and necessary conditions that neither method could offer alone. Overall, this study extends research on AI hallucinations by conceptualizing them as distinct forms of conversational norm violations and explaining how different hallucination cues are associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially linked to trust and distrust. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Software-defined vehicle ecosystems in transformation
Abstract: Context: The automotive industry is transitioning from hardware-centric development toward software-defined vehicles (SDVs), where software drives functionality, value creation, and competitive differentiation. This shift challenges proprietary software development, firm-centric innovation, and traditional supply chain models, giving rise to ecosystem-based collaboration. However, SDV transformation is primarily framed as a technical change, leaving its broader ecosystem implications insufficiently understood. Objective: This study explores the transformation of SDV ecosystems, their stakeholders, collaborative structures, roles and authority, and highlights associated challenges and opportunities. Methods: This systematic literature review collected 351 studies from six databases and selected 25 for detailed analysis. Results: Four interrelated shifts (from hardware-centric to software platforms, from supply chains to collaborative ecosystems, from proprietary to open and standard solutions, and from firm-level control to distributed governance) characterise the transformation, with six levels of collaboration involving twelve stakeholder groups. These collaborations are influenced by five dimensions of authority. The literature also highlights six core software development challenges and various organisational, industry and market, and regulatory, legal, and ethical challenges. It identifies five software development opportunities and various organisational, industry and market, and public value and ethical opportunities. Conclusion: The first contribution integrates previously fragmented literature on the SDV ecosystem transformation, demonstrating how SDVs are transforming the automotive industry through the four interrelated shifts driven by software advancements. Second, it proposes an SDV ecosystems model that integrates SDV architecture, stakeholder groups, collaboration structures, and governance levels to facilitate sustainable SDV ecosystems. Additionally, agendas for research and practice are outlined. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Structural Determinants of Household Resilience in Earthquake-Affected Communities: A Case Study from Bawean Island
Abstract: This study examines the socioeconomic impacts of the March 2024 earthquake on household resilience in Bawean Island, East Java, Indonesia. Data for this study were collected through a survey with a snowball sampling technique, with a total of 221 valid respondents from affected regions. Using a household survey across 12 affected villages and partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), the study identifies critical factors contributing to household resilience, namely social, economic, human, and physical capital assets. Title: Participatory short film production and student well-being: A narrative review from media literacy and sociocultural perspectives
Abstract: In an AI-driven media ecology, short-form video platforms have intensified interest in participatory filmmaking (PFM) as a learner-centered practice in higher education. However, the relationship between student-led short-film production and holistic well-being remains conceptually scattered and methodologically uneven. This narrative review examines how PFM may support student well-being through media literacy and sociocultural learning processes, with particular attention given to the transferability of these mechanisms to Chinese higher education. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2014 and 2025 were searched in Scopus, Web of Science, and CNKI using combinations of “participatory video,” “filmmaking,” “higher education,” and “well-being.” A total of 238 records were screened. Studies were excluded if they focused on non-higher-education settings, addressed media consumption rather than student production, contained no interpretable well-being-related outcomes, or lacked peer-reviewed empirical content. Fifteen studies were retained for full analysis. Data were extracted on context, modality, participants, methods, well-being domains, and pedagogical mechanisms and then coded through a hybrid deductive-inductive thematic analysis informed by Braun and Clarke and sensitized by media literacy and sociocultural theory. Three recurring mechanisms emerged: reflective authorship, which supports meaning making, critical judgment, and psychological resilience; collaborative scaffolding, which strengthens belonging, shared regulation, and social confidence; and embodied practice, which connects tool-mediated action to attention, physical vitality, and situated learning. However, the evidence base remains small, course bound, and dominated by short-term qualitative designs, with limited work in non-Western settings. This review therefore proposes the participatory filmmaking well-being framework (PFWF) as an empirically anchored synthesis and outlines implications for curriculum design, student support, and future mechanism-testing research in Chinese universities. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: The fantasy of digital immateriality: AI, ecologically unequal exchange, and appropriation of lived human time
Abstract: The purported immateriality of AI technologies is as illusory as the general understanding of conventional technologies as simply the application of politically neutral knowledge to nature. The materiality of technologies and their foundation in global inequalities has been illuminated by studies of ecologically unequal exchange (EUE). The aim of this article is to extend the applicability of EUE theory to digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) by highlighting how even the data that they process have an inevitably biophysical history. AI technologies represent a novelty mainly in the sense that, in addition to exploiting extractive areas through EUE, they are based on the appropriation of data from the public. We argue for understanding the materiality of data as derived from lived human time. AI's dependence on data can thus be regarded as representing and embodying biophysical processes and asymmetric transfers implicating issues of justice. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. Title: The effect of rosé wine color: A conceptual replication and a generation-based extension
Abstract: Recent research on crossmodal correspondences from Jaud et al. (2025) highlighted the role of rosé wine color in shaping consumer responses. Building on their work, this study aims to assess the robustness and generalizability of these findings while extending the original model in two ways. Specifically, by using a within-subjects experimental design conducted in the United States (N = 448), we replicate the model in a different cultural context by shifting from a French to a US sample. Further, we extend the underlying process by introducing perceived lightness as an additional mediating mechanism. Finally, we broaden the model by incorporating generational belonging (Generation Z vs. Generation Y) as a moderating variable. This approach enables us to assess both the robustness and the boundary conditions of previously identified effects of rosé wine color. Our findings contribute to the literature on crossmodal correspondences by demonstrating the stability of color-driven effects while highlighting generational differences in the relationship between perceived fruitiness and willingness to buy. They also offer practical insights for wine producers and distributors seeking to better align product presentation with the expectations of different generation-based consumer segments. © 2026

Title: Exemption or backfire? The double-edged effect of AI attribution strategy on brand trust in digital content moral crises
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Human-AI collaboration has become central to brand content production, but AI's black-box nature obscures responsibility in digital content moral crises. When such content is perceived as violating widely shared social values, brands increasingly attribute such incidents to AI errors. Prior research has mainly emphasized the responsibility-exemption role of AI attribution strategy, offering limited insight into its moral risks, mixed consequences, and underlying mechanisms. Drawing on the fact-value model, this study conducts five scenario-based experiments to examine how AI attribution strategy affects brand trust in this crisis context. The findings reveal a double-edged effect. At the factual level, this strategy increases consumers' perceived responsibility reduction, thereby producing an exemption effect that supports trust repair. At the value level, it also triggers perceived moral indifference, thereby producing a backfire effect that damages trust. This double-edged effect is moderated by public opinion and consumer traits. High negative electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) dispersion strengthens the perceived responsibility reduction path, whereas low negative eWOM dispersion strengthens the perceived moral indifference path. AI literacy strengthens the exemption effect by helping consumers understand AI-related technical limitations, whereas hostile attribution bias strengthens the backfire effect by leading consumers to question the moral motives behind the brand's technical explanation. This study advances crisis attribution research by examining AI attribution as a proactive brand communication strategy under attribution ambiguity and shows how it can reduce factual blame while raising value-based moral concerns. The findings offer guidance for using AI attribution carefully and reducing ethical communication risks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The organic halo effect: A systematic review of the influence of organic labels and claims on healthiness perceptions
Abstract: Food labels and claims play an increasing role in shaping consumer perceptions in complex food environments. While claims about nutrients are known to influence judgements of food healthiness, less is known about whether organic cues can lead to similar halo effects. We performed a systematic review to examine how organic labels and claims influence perceived food healthiness. We searched Web of Science and PubMed for experimental studies examining the effect of organic cues on food healthiness perceptions. Studies were included if they compared products with and without organic cues and reported outcomes related to perceived healthiness or perceived nutritional content. Of the records screened, 18 studies met the inclusion criteria. We conducted a narrative synthesis following SWiM guidelines, examining differences by cue type and outcome. Most studies found that organic cues increased perceived food healthiness. This effect was observed across both general health evaluations and specific calorie or nutrient judgements. Effects were more consistent for certified organic labels, whereas unofficial claims showed somewhat greater variability across products. A smaller number of studies reported mixed or null results, often depending on consumer characteristics or informational context. This review provides a synthesis of evidence on how organic labels and claims influence perceived food healthiness. By clarifying how consumers translate this information into health- and nutrition-related judgements, it contributes to a coherent understanding of the mechanisms underlying health halo effects. These findings suggest that organic cues may simultaneously act as signals of production practices and triggers of broader inferences about healthiness. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: The impact of reverse wording on cross-cultural comparisons of food-related attitudes
Abstract: Reverse-worded items (RWIs) are commonly used in multi-item scales to reduce acquiescence bias, yet their implications for cross-cultural food attitude measurement remain underexamined. This study compared positively worded items (PWIs) and RWIs across four established food-related attitude scales using data from 6300 adult consumers across ten countries. RWIs generally showed lower internal consistency and weaker inter-item correlations than PWIs. Items showing the largest cross-country variation in standardized loadings from multi-group confirmatory factor analysis were predominantly reverse-worded. RWIs also produced lower mean scores and generally greater response dispersion than PWIs. These wording-related differences varied by construct and country, followed no uniform pattern across measurement indicators, and may reflect the combined influence of item content, linguistic structure, and culturally patterned response tendencies. Across these indicators, PWI and RWI subsets did not consistently function as psychometrically equivalent components of the same scale. The findings suggest that the use of RWIs in cross-cultural food attitude measurement may introduce wording-related measurement instability, and that wording-direction effects require explicit consideration in the design and evaluation of international consumer research instruments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The grass is not always greener: The effects of local labor market information on search and employment
Abstract: We examine how information about local labor market conditions shapes search and employment outcomes for Indian job seekers. Participants were randomly shown information about either job postings, job applicants, or both from a popular job portal for their preferred city and occupation. Treated respondents are more likely to be employed seven months later. This overall effect varies considerably by baseline employment status. Among the initially employed, treatments reduce search off the portal and increase employment, with suggestive evidence of higher persistence in baseline jobs. In contrast, among the initially unemployed, treatments increase search activity but do not raise employment. Employment gains are concentrated among job seekers with less optimistic beliefs about labor market conditions. These findings suggest that limited information about labor market fundamentals may contribute to job churn in lower-income countries. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Exploring Lean-Integrated Circular Economy in the Built Environment Setting: Implications for Project Governance and Compliance
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The current study establishes how lean tenets contribute to the circular economy (CE) with exploration of lean tools with circular economy core principles and framework development. While there seem to be synergies between the concepts of lean and CE, the construction management research fraternity has not fully tapped the huge research potential in this domain. To address this gap, a two-phased exploratory qualitative research design is proposed. The first phase involves mapping lean tools with 10 dimensions of CE in the context of the built environment sector through content analysis and expert validation (n=3). Continuous improvement and added value tools of lean attained maximum realization of CE dimensions. The second phase involves semistructured interviews of experts (n=9) on an understanding of the synergies between lean and CE through thematic analysis (TA). The current study identifies predominant lean tools that realize CE dimensions and develops a conceptual model of a lean-driven circular economy (LdCE) framework for construction projects. Also, the lean tenets and their allied tools enabled value optimization through effective mapping of non-value-added processes and minimizing wasteful aspects. These findings are intended to inform engineers, construction managers, and legal practitioners about actionable strategies for promoting sustainable, legally compliant project execution. This study proves to accelerate sustainable construction through a lean and CE integrated framework in developing nations. Analyzing the associativity of the lean tools in realizing the CE dimensions and the strategies of a lean-driven circular economy through models is a novel concept with this research.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Influence of environmental stimuli on sustainable food choices: the moderating role of AI-source disclosure
Abstract: Reducing meat consumption is necessary for public health and environmental sustainability. However, while the benefits of positively-valenced nature have been explored, the comparative behavioral effects and mediational patterns of positively-valenced and negatively-valenced environmental stimuli remain unclear. Across three studies, we examined how positively- and negatively-valenced environmental stimuli influence food choices. Study 1 showed that both types of environmental stimuli reduced meat-heavy meal choices compared to the control. Study 2 tested serial mediation models within a dual-system framework, and the results showed that positively-valenced stimuli were associated with stronger nature connectedness and greater consideration of future consequences (CFC), whereas negatively-valenced stimuli were associated with higher guilt and greater CFC. Study 3 manipulated AI-source disclosure for the environmental stimuli. Although AI-source disclosure did not significantly interact with environmental stimuli condition in predicting meat-heavy choices, it significantly attenuated the link between negatively-valenced stimuli and guilt, but did not attenuate the association between positively-valenced stimuli and nature connectedness. Collectively, these findings suggest that the environmental stimuli valence may be associated with food choices through two partially overlapping yet distinguishable psychological pathways, offering insights for nudging sustainable eating. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Text-driven causal mapping of PET/rPET circularity in Australia: A dynamic factor–network analysis
Abstract: PET circularity is often evaluated by recovery volumes, although performance ultimately depends on whether recovered material can be converted into quality-assured outputs and absorbed by viable end markets. Yet the mechanisms connecting policy, markets, technology, and stakeholder behavior remain dispersed across heterogeneous evidence. We developed a source-attributed, time-stamped causal-network approach using 750 Australian government, industry and NGO, corporate, and media documents published during 2010–2025. Causal extraction, semantic normalization, sentiment assignment, and graph construction yielded 2794 factor nodes and 1588 unique causal edges. The network was strongly externalized: policy, market, and social factors were more numerous and highly connected than internal technical and operational factors. Persistent barriers combined cost and price volatility, inconsistent recyclate quality, infrastructure gaps, and weak policy implementation. Positive mechanisms clustered around standards and measurement, design for recyclability, operational capacity, and end-market development; their circular value depended on retained material quality and the end use reached. Source attribution revealed systematic framing differences, with media coverage concentrating negative implementation narratives. Temporal and regional analyses indicated a shift from limited attention to rapid expansion and subsequent consolidation, alongside national structural hubs and differentiated state pathways. A full-text academic shadow corpus preserved the broad problem domains but changed their hierarchy: academic evidence foregrounded material and processing mechanisms, whereas the primary corpus foregrounded institutional coordination and market implementation. The contribution is therefore not a universal ranking of Australian interventions, but an auditable framework for identifying how technical feasibility becomes, or fails to become, operational circularity under different institutional conditions. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Hedging against asset-heavy network expansion delays through rapid deployments of FACTS and BESS
Abstract: Transmission expansion delays represents a critical barrier to the timely and cost-effective development of modern power systems, particularly for integrating renewable energy. Although network congestions arising from postponed major infrastructure projects (e.g., new transmission lines) can severely impact system efficiency, these effects can be mitigated through the rapid deployment of flexible technologies such as FACTS devices and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). In this paper, we propose a two-stage stochastic optimization framework that complements first-stage, asset-intensive network expansion decisions with second-stage, scenario-dependent investments in flexible transmission assets, including FACTS and BESS. The formulation explicitly captures the probabilistic nature of project delays, accounting for zonal variations in the likelihood of such delays and their implications for system planning. Through a set of case studies, we demonstrate that the strategic use of FACTS and BESS can serve as an effective hedge against the adverse impacts of transmission expansion delays. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Cu redistribution layers on permanent glass-core substrates for advanced packaging: Direct-on-glass and polymer build-up architectures
Abstract: Glass-core substrates are attracting increasing interest for advanced packaging because of their dimensional stability, high electrical resistivity, smooth surfaces, and compatibility with fine-pitch interconnect processing. This review compares Cu redistribution-layer (RDL) technologies implemented on permanent glass-core substrates through two principal architectures: direct-on-glass RDLs and polymer build-up RDLs. Direct-on-glass approaches reduce dielectric-stack complexity and can support low-loss lateral routing, but their scalability depends strongly on glass–Cu adhesion, seed-layer control, conductor dimensional fidelity, and stress transferred to brittle glass. Polymer build-up approaches enable multilayer routing and microvia-based redistribution while introducing additional constraints associated with dielectric properties, cure-induced dimensional change, moisture response, interfacial integrity, and multilayer registration. Reported studies demonstrate micrometer-scale wiring and vias, broadband signal transmission, multilayer integration, accelerated reliability testing, and large-area glass processing. However, the most aggressive dimensions, highest integration levels, and strongest electrical or reliability results have generally been demonstrated in different material stacks and test vehicles rather than concurrently within a single permanent glass-core platform. Accordingly, minimum feature size alone should not be interpreted as a manufacturing design rule. Future progress will require coordinated design of interfaces, dielectric materials, metallization, and routing architecture, together with statistically meaningful qualification of dimensional control, electrical performance, environmental reliability, and panel-scale manufacturability. © 2026

Title: From Classroom to Practice: Bridging BPM Education and Industry Expectations Through a Process Mining Tool Comparison Project
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: This paper presents an innovative assignment approach implemented in the Business Process Modelling, Mining, and Automation course for Master’s students at theUniversity of Ottawa. The course integrates Active Learning principles to train industry-ready business analysts, capable of supporting modern business process management, mining, optimization, and automation initiatives. The assignment approach involves a project-based process mining tool comparison project, where students evaluate industry-relevant tools using real event logs to address a concrete business problem. The assignment design integrates experiential learning, formative feedback, and peer review activities to support both technical and professional skill development. The assignment is structured around a set of guiding principles. First, it emphasizes the development of real-world skills aligned with the evolving demands of digital business processes. Second, it encourages students to critically challenge their assumptions, tool limitations, and existing practices through a data-driven, evidence-based mindset. Finally, it promotes continuous self-reflection and the active exchange of constructive feedback among peers to reinforce deeper learning and professional growth. These guiding principles offer a practical framework that can support other educators in the BPM community in designing effective and practical assignment strategies that help bridge the gap between academic learning and industry expectations. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Systematic and Automated Diagnosis of Process Models Using Reference Frameworks
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Reference frameworks in Business Process Management (BPM) are generic best-practice templates used to design, analyze, benchmark, and improve business processes (BPs). They promote consistency in BP structure and terminology and support BP model diagnosis by revealing gaps and weaknesses through comparison with a reference structure. Despite extensive research on the development and adaptation of reference frameworks, the BPM literature offers limited methodological support for their systematic application to existing BP models, leaving much of the analysis to manual work by domain experts. However, this analysis typically demands significant time, human, and financial resources and does not scale well to enterprise-wide BP sets, limiting its practical use for BP diagnosis. In this paper, following a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, we analyze existing approaches that leverage reference frameworks for BP diagnosis to identify their key characteristics, and propose a maturity model to systematically guide their application to existing BP models. Title: Bridging the privacy gap: Developers’ practices and the missing role of privacy engineers
Abstract: Context: Privacy has become a first order concern in software engineering, yet organizations still struggle to translate legal mandates into actionable engineering practices. Goal: This study investigates how Brazilian software practitioners perceive and operationalize privacy standards/practices. Methods: We conduct a conceptual replication of prior work via survey (N = 31). The instrument maps privacy-related perceptions/practices, use of standards/frameworks/techniques, organizational responsibility allocation, perceived challenges, and improvement opportunities. Results: Practitioners report distinguishing privacy from security, but formalization is limited. Although 60.7% report considering privacy across the software development, half do not use privacy-focused methods, and a substantial portion (46.4%) report being unaware of such approaches. Practices skew toward classic security controls (e.g., access control, 85.7%) rather than dedicated privacy engineering artifacts. The Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD) is the dominant compliance driver (82.1%), with low uptake of ISO 27701/NIST. Key barriers include unclear legal guidance (53.6%), insufficient training (42.9%), and late integration of privacy (39.3%). Automation remains incipient (14.3% fully automated; 42.9% manual). Organizational support is uneven (39.3% sufficient; 39.3% partial; 21.4% insufficient). Applying the Spearman correlation test revealed strong relationships (ρ up to 0.63) between experience, training, and integration practices, indicating that professional maturity and capacity building are strongly associated with privacy-by-design adoption. Conclusion: Results indicate a persistent gap between awareness and effective governance. We recommend (i) targeted training and curricular inclusion, (ii) clearer role/accountability assignments, and (iii) investment in tooling/automation to operationalize privacy-by-design. These actions can help shift privacy from reactive compliance to a sustained dimension in Brazilian organizations.
