Title: Access Rights Management and Digital Identity for Digital Product Passports
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: The Digital Product Passport (DPP), established by the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR, EU 2024/1781), is a regulated multi-actor digital infrastructure in which economic operators, market surveillance authorities, recyclers, repairers, and consumers each require access to different subsets of product data under different conditions. Managing these access rights correctly constitutes a legal compliance requirement, a governance challenge, and a systems engineering problem simultaneously. This paper makes four integrated contributions. First, a cross-regulation taxonomy is developed that classifies DPP data along three axes: data sensitivity tier, lifecycle mutability, and entitlement source. Second, the three generations of EU digital identity regulation eIDAS (2014), eIDAS 2.0 (2024), and the European Business Wallet (EBW) systematically analysed against the seven core DPP identity requirements, showing that eIDAS meets none, eIDAS 2.0 meets some, and the EBW is near-complete. Third, an updated hybrid authentication architecture is proposed that integrates three pathways: OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect for operator-delegated business actors, the EU Digital Identity Wallet (eIDAS 2.0) for individual authority and base-role actors, and the EBW for organisational and automated flows. Fourth, the taxonomy and architecture are evaluated against the battery passport the first mandatory DPP under EU law confirming full coverage and alignment with EN 18239 and the JTC 24 standard family. The EBW’s credential ecosystem gap and the unspecified presentation protocol layer (OID4VP, W3C VC 2.0) are identified as the critical near-term implementation risks for systems that must be operational before the February 2027 battery passport mandate. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: A Socio-Technical Lens on AI Adoption: Role Conflict and Ambiguity in Large Organizations
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Although AI adoption in private, daily use is accelerating, many initiatives in large organizations stall at the pilot stage and fail to reach production at scale, despite technical optimization. This study examines how heterogeneous organizational roles across business, technical, and functional domains experience role conflict and role ambiguity during AI adoption, and how these role tensions shape adoption outcomes. Based on semi-structured interviews with twelve professionals representing business, technical, and functional organizational roles involved in AI adoption, the Gioia methodology is applied to surface recurrent role conflicts (e.g., business expectations versus technical feasibility; novelty vs. business value) and role ambiguities (e.g., unclear stakeholder responsibilities, risk ownership, and decision-making authority). Substantial inter-coder reliability (κ = 0.74) supports the consistency of the analysis. By integrating Socio-Technical Systems Theory and Role Conflict Theory, a role-based socio-technical lens is proposed that explains why technically sound AI projects stall when role tensions remain unresolved during the simultaneous engagement of heterogeneous organizational roles. The study contributes a typology of role conflicts and role ambiguities, and discusses their implications for role clarity, decision rights, and cross-functional collaboration. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Ge C.; Lei Z.; Ji D.; Liu Y.; Chen Z.; Zhang Y.; Zhu H.; Hui G.; Chen Z.
Title: Closing the carbon loop: Recycled CO2 utilization in enhanced lacustrine shale oil recovery
Abstract: The application of CO2-enhanced oil recovery (EOR) in the highly heterogeneous lacustrine shales is challenged by severe gas channeling, poor sweep efficiency, and low carbon utilization performance by the conventional operation mode. To address the issues, this study proposes a Closed-Loop CO2 Recycling (CLCR) technology, in which the produced gas (including CO2 and light hydrocarbons) is captured, compressed, and reinjected to offset the total CO2 consumption amount. A compositional cross-scale numerical simulation model is developed that implicitly couples flow in the shale matrix, bedding fractures, and hydraulic fractures, including pressure-driven and diffusion-controlled mass transfer among the continua. The model is validated against field well history data from the Gulong shale, the most typical lacustrine shale in China, with a matching accuracy over 85 %. Based on a 20-year simulation, four metrics are evaluated including oil replacement ratio (ORR), CO2 sequestration efficiency (CSE), oil production multiplier (OPM), and net present value (NPV) for CLCR. The results show that an injection rate of 50 t/d in a 1650 m horizontal well gives the highest OPM of 2.39, and early CO2 injection without prior depletion is confirmed essential to formation pressure preservation and gas breakthrough delay. The reinjection start timing of the 5 % CO2 mole fraction in produced gas achieves the highest ORR of 0.152 t oil/t CO2 and a competitive OPM of 2.612. Early recycling preserves light hydrocarbons in the reinjected gas, which improves oil‑gas compatibility, strengthens the displacement efficiency, and enhances oil mobilization. By recycling, the CSE can be increased from 58 % to nearly 100 % which means most of the injected CO2 can be sequestrated in the shale formation. Single-well NPV by CLCR is 60.8 % higher than the conventional mode. CLCR enables substantially enhanced CO2 sequestration while increasing oil production performance, offering a viable pathway toward carbon–neutral shale oil development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mapping Rebound Mechanisms in Circular Manufacturing: A Causal Loop Diagram Approach
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: The manufacturing industry is undergoing a strategic transition toward a circular economy to mitigate its substantial environmental footprint. Although circular strategies such as remanufacturing, recycling, and servitization aim to decouple value creation from resource consumption, their implementation often triggers unintended rebound effects. These effects arise when efficiency gains stimulate systemic responses that partially or fully offset the expected environmental benefits. Although these offsets are well documented, research on rebound mechanisms (RMs) in business-to-business (B2B) contexts remains fragmented and largely exploratory. This paper addresses this gap by adopting a system dynamics perspective to map the RMs activated by circular strategies in B2B settings through a Causal Loop Diagram (CLD). The analysis identifies the key variables and feedback structures that shape these mechanisms, providing a qualitative framework for understanding how sustainability gains can be eroded across core business processes (i.e., business model, production, product design, and procurement). The resulting CLD provides a clear and comprehensive view of how circular strategies, despite being designed for environmental improvement, can inadvertently trigger systemic rebound effects. This work contributes to advancing a more nuanced and system-oriented understanding of circular economy implementation in manufacturing. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: AI-Enabled Knowledge Extraction and Transformation: Comparative Case Studies from Taiwanese Firms
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being adopted not only as a tool for automation and prediction but also as a mechanism for extracting, codifying, and transferring organizational knowledge. This study examines how AI contributes to knowledge transformation in Taiwanese business contexts through a qualitative multiple-case-study design. Based on semi-structured interviews conducted in Taiwan in March 2026, the study analyzes three firms operating in different domains: manufacturing automation, industrial AI platforms, and labor/legal advisory services. The findings show that AI-enabled knowledge transformation does not occur in a uniform manner. Instead, firms differ in how they extract knowledge from operational processes, expert judgment, and legal or advisory experience, and in how such knowledge is codified into digital systems and reused through organizational infrastructures. Across the three cases, a common pattern can be identified in the progression from AI-enabled knowledge extraction to codification, infrastructure formation, and knowledge transfer. At the same time, each case highlights a different organizational function of AI: process replication, analytical support, and expert knowledge formalization. The study contributes to the literature by showing that AI in business should be understood not only as a productivity-enhancing technology but also as an organizational mechanism for transforming tacit and experience-based knowledge into reusable forms. It also offers practical implications for firms seeking to preserve expertise, strengthen learning, and build scalable knowledge systems through AI. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: An ABI Architecture for Hospital Appointment Duration Prediction
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Hospitals face the ongoing challenge of managing limited resources in dynamic environments, where variability in appointment duration hinders scheduling efficiency, increases waiting times, and affects the utilization of healthcare professionals. Within the Hospital 4.0 paradigm, traditional Business Intelligence (BI) systems prove inadequate for supporting adaptive and data-driven decision-making. This paper presents an Adaptive Business Intelligence (ABI) architecture that integrates data ingestion, predictive modeling, appointment schedule optimization, and dashboard-based visualization, all orchestrated through containerized services. Each predictive model is encapsulated within Docker containers and exposed via FastAPI microservices, enabling scalability and modular deployment. The main contribution of this work is to demonstrate how real-time predictive insights can effectively support the optimization of hospital appointment scheduling and resource allocation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Evaluating the technical and economic viability of 3-hydroxypropionic acid production from biomass
Abstract: This study presents a techno-economic assessment of a conceptual 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP) biorefinery integrating ionic liquid (IL) pretreatment with lignocellulosic biomass conversion. This work provides a novel comparative techno-economic assessment of corn stover (CS) and brewer's spent grain (BSG) as feedstocks for IL-based 3-HP production. A literature-based process model was developed for the continuous production of 50,000 t/year of 3-HP and evaluated using both feedstocks. IL pretreatment was selected for its recyclability and potential to reduce chemical consumption compared with conventional pretreatment methods. Biomass-to-3-HP conversion efficiencies (on a dry basis) of 25.63% and 23.31% were obtained for CS and BSG, respectively, reflecting the lower fermentable sugar recovery achieved from BSG. Economic assessment yielded break-even selling prices (BESP) of $2472/tonne 3-HP for CS and $2643/tonne for BSG, indicating that both configurations are economically competitive with literature-reported bio-based 3-HP values. Sensitivity analysis identified yeast consumption as the dominant cost driver, followed by enzyme and IL requirements. The results highlight the potential of IL-assisted lignocellulosic biorefineries for competitive 3-HP production and identify the optimisation of yeast production and recycling, enhanced IL recovery and recycling, and co-product valorisation through bioethanol and lignin recovery as key opportunities to further reduce production costs. © 2026 The Authors. Title: The Influence of Social Capital on the Performance of Women Entrepreneurs Through the Mediating Role of Innovation and Knowledge Sharing in Special Region of Yogyakarta
Abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of social capital on the entrepreneurial performance of women in the Special Region of Yogyakarta Province, with innovation and knowledge sharing as mediators. A quantitative approach was applied using a cross-sectional survey of 422 women entrepreneurs through non-probability sampling. The results show that social capital has a positive and significant effect on entrepreneurial performance, both directly and indirectly through innovation and knowledge sharing. Regression analysis reveals that social networks, trust, and shared norms open up access to resources and opportunities, as well as encourage the exchange of knowledge and innovative practices that strengthen business competitiveness. The Sobel test confirms the significant role of innovation and knowledge sharing as mediators. These findings emphasize the importance of social capital in supporting the sustainability of women’s entrepreneurial performance and provide theoretical contributions by integrating the perspectives of social capital, innovation, and knowledge sharing, as well as practical implications for policymakers and the business community in strengthening an equitable entrepreneurial ecosystem. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Impulsive synchronization of chaotic neural networks involving unknown states and disturbances
Abstract: This article investigates the synchronization of master-slave neural networks (NNs) via observer-based impulsive control, where the slave system contains unmeasurable states and external disturbances. Two types of external disturbances are considered, i.e., vanishing disturbances and harmonic disturbances. Moreover, to deal with the unmeasurable states, a state observer is designed without imposing any restrictive prerequisites on the external disturbances. Then, an impulsive controller based on observer state is designed to achieve synchronization of master-slave NNs. Specifically, a disturbance observer utilizing state estimation is developed to estimate harmonic disturbances, and these estimates are used to compensate for the effects of harmonic disturbances on the synchronization goal. With the aid of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), the state observer gain, disturbance observer gain, and impulsive control gain are obtained. Finally, a simulation result is presented to verify the validity of the designed control strategies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Creative or uncreative partner: Comparing humans and AI in collaborative creative tasks
Abstract: Creativity is fundamentally a collaborative process. As generative AI becomes increasingly integrated into creative work, understanding how it reshapes collaboration becomes critical. This pre-registered study directly compares human-human and human-AI collaboration dynamics across two creative tasks: the Alternate Uses Task (AUT) and creative short story writing. Participants were randomly assigned to pairs in either human-human (N = 68 pairs) or human-AI (GPT-4o; N = 72 pairs) conditions, with partners alternating turns as first responders to examine how initiation order shapes the creative process. Our findings reveal that the apparent “AI advantage” in creative collaboration is illusory, driven primarily by increased AI verbosity rather than enhanced creativity. Critically, collaboration with AI partners negatively impacted humans' own creative responses compared to human-human partnerships, with human-AI collaboration failing to enhance idea originality or diversity relative to human-human collaboration. Human partners demonstrated higher collaborative creativity that strengthened over time, indicating that current generative AI systems, while producing more verbose outputs, do not replicate the collective creativity characteristic of human-human collaboration. These results challenge assumptions about AI's creative potential, with direct implications for AI system design and collaborative creative practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Electron-deficient boron-containing additive induced Lewis acid interface with O–S/B–S chemical adsorption of polysulfides for durable sodium–sulfur batteries
Source title: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
Abstract: Room-temperature sodium‑sulfur (RT Na-S) batteries hold great promise for large-scale energy storage, yet they face severe challenges from polysulfide shuttling and sodium dendrite growth. To address these challenges, this study proposes an innovative strategy by introducing a boron-based additive, 2,4,6-trimethoxyboroxine (TMBX), into the propylene carbonate (PC)/NaClO₄ electrolyte to in-situ construct a boron-rich interphase. On the cathode side, the cathode electrolyte interface (CEI) layer is enriched with electron-deficient Lewis acidic B₂O₃, which chemisorbs soluble sodium polysulfides via B-S and O-S bonds. Simultaneously, this interphase forms a physical barrier due to its high mechanical strength and favorable structural properties, and the two effects work synergistically to suppress the shuttle effect. On the anode side, the inner solid electrolyte interface (SEI) layer that rich in boron-containing inorganic components can effectively inhibits sodium dendrite nucleation. Benefiting from the synergistic regulation of the boron-containing interphase, the TMBX-modified electrolyte endows Na-S cells with excellent performance. This work establishes a rational electrolyte design principle of leveraging boron-centered Lewis acidity for targeted polysulfide anchoring, coupled with a high-modulus interphase, offers a scalable and efficient strategy toward durable RT Na-S batteries. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Transforming Business with Generative AI: Research, Innovation, Market Deployment and Future Shifts in Business Models
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This paper explores the transformative impact of Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on the business landscape, examining its role in reshaping traditional business models, intensifying market competition, and fostering innovation. By applying the principles of Neo-Schumpeterian economics, the research analyses how GenAI is driving a new wave of “creative destruction” leading to the emergence of novel business paradigms and value propositions. The findings reveal that GenAI enhances operational efficiency, facilitates product and service innovation, and creates new revenue streams, positioning it as a powerful catalyst for substantial shifts in business structures and strategies. However, the deployment of GenAI also presents significant challenges, including ethical concerns, regulatory demands, and the risk of job displacement. By addressing the multifarious nature of GenAI, this paper provides valuable insights for business leaders, policymakers, and researchers, guiding them towards a balanced and responsible integration of this transformative technology. Ultimately, GenAI is not merely a technological advancement but a driver of profound change, heralding a future where creativity, efficiency, and growth are redefined. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Ultrasensitive SERS detection of explosive molecules via iodide-enhanced concentrated silver nanoparticles
Source title: Spectrochimica Acta - Part A: Molecular and Biomolecular Spectroscopy
Abstract: Trace detection of nitroaromatic explosives such as 2,6-dinitrotoluene (2,6-DNT) and trinitrotoluene (TNT) is of great significance in the fields of homeland security, anti-terrorism monitoring and environmental governance. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) has become a research hotspot in the field of chemical sensing owing to its unique ‘fingerprint identification’ capacity and high detection sensitivity. Nitroaromatic molecule analytes exhibit weak binding affinity toward conventional citrate-stabilized Ag NPs, which limits the effective adsorption of target molecules to the Ag NPs surface. These conventional substrates only enable detection of 2,6-DNT and TNT at concentrations as high as 10−1 M and 10−2 M, respectively. In this study, a surface regulation strategy is proposed by pretreatment highly concentrated Ag NPs with KI to fabricate a high-performance SERS sensing platform on a low-cost aluminum foil substrate. Benefiting from iodide-mediated surface modulation, the detection performance is greatly improved, with distinct characteristic Raman peaks of 2,6-DNT observable at an ultralow concentration of 10−10 M. I− can be used as a cleaning agent to effectively remove citrate from Ag NPs surface and provide abundant active sites for the analytes adsorption. In addition, the AgI shell formed on Ag NPs surface by reaction of I− and Ag+ can provide additional chemical enhancement through charge transfer mechanism. This strategy enables highly sensitive detection of nitroaromatic explosives and provides a very competitive solution for the monitoring of trace explosives in the field of public safety. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Probabilistic ordered weighted averaging distances for tariff networks: an application to emerging countries
Abstract: This study develops a probabilistic ordered weighted averaging (OWA) tariff-distance framework to measure tariff cohesion among emerging economies. The proposed probabilistic OWA weighted average tariff distance (POWAWATD) extends the probabilistic OWA weighted average distance logic to tariff schedules by decomposing tariff dissimilarity into three interpretable layers: ordered tariff gaps, policy-importance weights and trade-salience probabilities. Generalized and quasi-arithmetic variants are also introduced to adjust the sensitivity of the measure to large tariff spikes, moderate discrepancies and flow-relevant deviations. The framework is illustrated using BRICS and BRICS+ economies. In the balanced specification, Brazil–India records a higher tariff distance than China–Russia, with POWAWATD values of 0.1070 and 0.0658, respectively. Under spike-vigilant and flow-salient specifications, the Brazil–India distance increases to 0.1186 and 0.1219, showing that its tariff misalignment is concentrated in upper-rank and economically salient product lines. The results indicate that POWAWATD provides a transparent and flexible tool for comparing tariff structures, identifying cohesion patterns and assessing how trade-policy distances respond to alternative aggregation attitudes. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Towards faster and deeper hoeffding trees: Fractional bounds and correlation-preserving multi-index statistics
Abstract: This paper presents two complementary enhancements to the Very Fast Decision Tree algorithm for data stream mining. The first contribution introduces the fractional Hoeffding bound, a relaxed splitting criterion where the original threshold is scaled by a factor f<1. Experimental evidence shows that with this modification, the resulting trees not only grow faster but also achieve higher accuracy compared to the original Very Fast Decision Tree. The second contribution proposes a novel data structure, called extended statistics, which extends the traditional sufficient statistics used in the Very Fast Decision Tree by maintaining additional information about attribute co-occurrences. This allows child nodes to inherit richer knowledge from their parent, leading to deeper trees with accelerated convergence to the target accuracy. Numerical experiments on synthetic data streams demonstrate that the combination of fractional bounds and multi-index statistics yields significant accuracy gains, particularly in the early phases of learning. The extended statistics improvement, however, comes at the cost of increased memory and computational requirements, emphasizing the trade-off between predictive performance and resource usage. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Modeling internalizing symptoms and substance use comorbidity using causal network methodology
Abstract: The cooccurrence of internalizing and substance use disorders can be explained from several perspectives, yet most are modeled in isolation and limited to correlational evidence. Advancements on two common etiological perspectives – i) internalizing symptoms predisposing toward substance use disorder symptoms, ii) transdiagnostic factors predisposing toward both symptom domains – are therefore hampered by scarce multivariate and causal evidence. The present study addressed this gap by modeling direct (causal) links from internalizing symptoms to substance use behaviors and (causal) links from the transdiagnostic factors cognitive control, locus of control (LOC), and meaning in life. We analyzed data from wave 7 (2019–2023; N = 1725), the 15-year follow-up of the ongoing longitudinal cohort study the Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety, using a correlational network and a causal network based on the fast causal inference algorithm. The correlational network showed that depression and social anxiety symptoms were positively related to alcohol-related problems and negatively related to alcohol consumption. Title: Metatranscriptomic analyses coupled with phenotypic and metabolic verification revealed competition mechanisms between grass carp spoilage bacteria in synthetic communities
Abstract: Bacterial competition is a major factor influencing microbiota succession in fish. However, the competition mechanisms among dominant spoilage bacteria in grass carp remain to be systematically investigated. Therefore, this study aimed to elucidate the mutual competition relationships and mechanisms among five representative spoilage bacteria isolated from grass carp. To this end, we constructed synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) with these five strains and employed metatranscriptomics coupled with phenotypic verification to demonstrate their interactions at both transcriptional and phenotypic levels. The results showed that bacterial competitiveness largely determined the microbiota composition in SynComs. Aeromonas rivipollensis ranked the most competitive bacterium by both inhibiting the virulence phenotypes (siderophore production, biofilm, and swimming motility) and disrupting the carbohydrate/amino acid metabolisms of Shewanella putrefaciens and Pseudomonas putida . Concurrently, A. rivipollensis enhanced its own siderophore production and motility when interacting with these competitors, which further promoted its advantage. In contrast, S. putrefaciens was the second most competitive, as it potently utilized amino acids and enhanced its siderophore production and motility in response to P. putida . Collectively, this study reveals that bacterial competition in fish is mediated by both phenotype interference and metabolism disruption, suggests siderophore as a new target for controlling microbiota succession and quality deterioration in fish, and therefore provides theoretical guidance for developing new fish preservation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Towards better long-range time series forecasting using generative forecasting
Abstract: Long-range time series forecasting is usually based on one of two existing forecasting strategies: Direct Forecasting and Iterative Forecasting, where the former provides low bias, high variance forecasts and the latter leads to low variance, high bias forecasts. In this paper, we propose a new forecasting strategy called Generative Forecasting (GenF), which generates synthetic data for the next few time steps and then makes long-range forecasts based on generated and observed data. We theoretically prove that under certain conditions, GenF can better balance the forecasting variance and bias, leading to a much smaller forecasting error. We implement GenF via three components: (i) a novel conditional Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) based generator for synthetic time series data generation, called CWGAN-TS. (ii) a transformer based predictor, which makes long-range predictions using both generated and observed data. (iii) an information theoretic clustering algorithm to improve the training of both CWGAN-TS and the transformer based predictor. The experimental results on five public datasets demonstrate that GenF significantly outperforms a diverse range of popular benchmarks and classical approaches. Specifically, we find a 5%–11% improvement in predictive performance (i.e., mean absolute error) while having a 15%–50% reduction in parameters compared to the benchmarks. Lastly, we conduct an ablation study to further explore and demonstrate the effectiveness of components comprising GenF. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhong W.; Luo J.; Yu S.; Lyu Y.; Guo J.
Title: Navigating AI affective support: The cognitive-affective pathway from appraisal to emotional well-being in learners
Abstract: As affective artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in educational contexts, understanding how learners emotionally engage with such systems is both timely and critical. Grounded in cognitive appraisal theory and the theory of affective bonding, this research examines how students interpret AI-delivered affective support during academic stress. Across two preregistered experiments (N = 202; N = 394), we find that AI affective support enhances emotional well-being via affective resonance, the perceived emotional alignment between learner and agent. Study 1 shows that affective resonance mediates the effect of AI affective support on positive and negative affect. Study 2 advances a process model in which learners' appraisals of task value and perceived AI emotional affordance are associated with emotional valence, which in turn is associated with affective resonance. Preliminary evidence suggests this indirect effect is stronger when tasks are perceived as personally meaningful. Our findings indicate that emotional responses to AI are not passive reactions to expressive cues but are actively constructed through motivational and cognitive appraisal. By clarifying how learners perceive and internalize AI affective support, this study extends theoretical understanding of human–AI interaction in education and offers actionable guidance for designing emotionally attuned learning technologies that support engagement, resilience, and well-being. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Beyond RSRP: UE-Side Detection of Multi-stage Fake Base Station Attacks Through NAS/RRC Layer in 5G Networks for Secure Mobile E-Business Services

Abstract: Fake base station attacks enable threats such as denial of service, user tracking, and security downgrades in modern mobile networks. Since many devices remain vulnerable, on-device detection has become an important defense mechanism. However, existing approaches relying on signal-strength metrics such as RSRP become unreliable when attackers manipulate radio conditions or perform protocol-level attacks. This study proposes an on-device detection framework that incorporates protocol-layer information by analyzing RRC and NAS signaling sequences alongside conventional signal features. Using a self-generated dataset capturing realistic FBS scenarios, we evaluate both classical machine-learning and deep-learning models across multiple feature configurations. Experimental results show that protocol-layer features significantly improve detection accuracy and reduce false positives compared to RSRP-only approaches. Title: Predictive Process Monitoring Through the Lens of Deep Online Learning
Abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) leverages historical event data recorded during historical business process executions, to forecast future scenarios of new ongoing process executions. Title: Entropy as a diagnostic for time-related constraints on circular transition: Evidence from plastic waste management in the OECD–EU countries
Abstract: This study examines time-related constraints on circularity by applying Shannon entropy to measure distributional dispersion across end-of-life fates in plastic waste management. Using OECD data for 1990–2018, end-of-life shares for recycling, incineration, landfill, mismanaged, and littered waste are combined with entropy to assess structural change over time. Entropy makes that structural shift visible and comparable across time. During the early 1990s, plastic waste management was highly predictable due to landfill dominance. From the mid-2010s onward, entropy stabilized at a high level despite continued growth in recycling. That plateau is consistent with persistent dispersion across competing end-of-life routes rather than convergence toward recycling dominance. © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier B.V. Title: Identifying a dynamic information trading zone framework via insights from full-scale emergency exercises
Abstract: The article examines how the co-creation of a Common Operational Picture (COP) in multi-actor crisis response operations can be understood through the concept of Information Trading Zones (ITZ). The analysis is grounded in the theory of Situation Awareness (SA), including Endsley’s conceptualisation of individual, Team SA and Shared SA, and draws on Galison’s notion of trading zones as intercalation, the insertion of an intermediate concept or mechanism to bridge existing explanatory levels. In this study, ITZ is introduced as an intercalating construct linking information exchange, sensemaking, and coordinated action. Drawing on extensive qualitative analyses of five full-scale crisis exercises, the study traces the evolution of an operational framework that conceptualises ITZ as both a precondition for and an integral component of the co-creation of a COP. Within this framework, ITZ are positioned as socio-technical spaces where information is negotiated, interpreted, and stabilised across organisational boundaries, enabling the development of Shared and Team SA in the face of uncertainty. The article offers concrete recommendations for both researchers and practice, outlining how the interplay among ITZ, COP, and SA can inform the design of information systems that more effectively support coordination, sense-making, and decision-making in Emergency Management contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Meng J.; Lyu Y.; Jiang L.; Wang J.; Zhang S.; Lyu C.; Wang L.
Title: The influence of mineral composition on coal wettability and pore structure evolution: experimental study and molecular simulation
Abstract: The wettability of coal dust is crucial for promoting green mining and clean utilization of coal. However, the mechanism of mineral components in this process remains unclear, hindering the development of the mineral-organic matter synergistic regulation theory. This study combines macro-characterization, Monte Carlo simulations, and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate the influence patterns of single and composite minerals on the wettability of coal organic matter. A model for the doping of coal organic molecules with minerals was constructed. Parameters such as water adsorption capacity, isothermal adsorption heat, and hydrogen-bond network were analyzed, and the pore-structure evolution induced by composite minerals and water molecules was investigated. The results indicate that the effectiveness of different minerals in enhancing wettability follows this order: quartz > muscovite > calcite > kaolinite > gypsum > pyrite. Water molecules are primarily physically adsorbed, with adsorption capacity positively correlated with isothermal adsorption heat. Mineral surfaces feature both primary and secondary adsorption sites. Composite mineral doping increased the maximum adsorption capacity from 80 mg/g to 120 mg/g, primarily due to enhanced electrostatic forces, hydrogen bond network restructuring, and the transfer of the strongest adsorption sites. Additionally, water molecules preferentially clog pores larger than 4 Å in diameter, resulting in reduced specific surface area, pore volume, and connectivity. These findings provide theoretical insights into the systematic regulation of coal wettability by mineral components and support the advancement of efficient coal dust prevention technologies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Upcycling traditional Chinese medicine residue into Fe/Zr bimetallic biochar for synergistic PMS activation: A superoxide-driven route for levofloxacin degradation and toxicity mitigation
Abstract: The practical application of biochar (BC) for peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation is hindered by its limited surface area, paucity of active sites, and poor electron transfer. To address these challenges, we synthesized an iron-zirconium bimetallic-modified BC (Fe/Zr0.8-BC) from traditional Chinese medicine residue via impregnation-pyrolysis. Comprehensive characterization confirmed the successful loading of Fe (Fe3O4/metallic Fe) and Zr (ZrO2), which dramatically increased the specific surface area from 4.10 to 269.59 m2/g and created a mesoporous architecture conducive to both PMS activation and pollutant adsorption. The Fe/Zr0.8-BC/PMS system achieved 89.54% levofloxacin (LVF) removal and 42.31% total organic carbon mineralization within 90 min under optimized conditions (catalyst 0.6 g/L, PMS 1 mM, LVF 10 mg/L, pH 7). The catalyst exhibited robust reusability, with only ∼19% activity loss after four cycles and leached Fe/Zr concentrations (0.10 and 0.02 mg/L) below regulatory limits. Mechanistic investigations, combining radical quenching and electron paramagnetic resonance, revealed synergistic contributions from O2•-, SO4•-, •OH, and 1O2, with O2•- playing the dominant role, suggesting a hybrid radical/non-radical pathway. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy further elucidated the interfacial catalytic mechanism driven by reversible Fe2+/Fe3+ and Zr4+/Zr3+ redox cycles. Ten degradation intermediates were identified via high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, enabling the proposal of three primary pathways: decarboxylation, defluorination, and piperazine ring opening. Toxicity assessment using the T.E.S.T software indicated that most intermediates possessed lower acute toxicity, bioaccumulation potential, developmental toxicity, and mutagenicity than the parent compound. This work not only provides a sustainable strategy for upcycling traditional Chinese medicine residue into high-performance catalytic materials but also offers mechanistic insights into bimetallic synergistic PMS activation, presenting a promising and environmentally benign solution for antibiotic-contaminated water remediation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Huang C.; Du S.; Tang W.
Title: Rethinking green technology interventions: Strategic motivations under uncertain regulations
Abstract: Governments increasingly rely on industry capability to assess the feasibility of implementing stricter environmental regulations. Rather than passively awaiting their imposition, this trend incentivizes firms to shape future regulations through green activities. To investigate how firms with different cost structures and market power strategically adopt and invest in green technology under uncertain regulations, this paper proposes a three-period game model. The equilibrium outcomes reveal the strategic motivations behind green technology adoption. Specifically, when unit green cost is high, technology-leading firms voluntarily adopt green technology to lobby for stricter regulations, thereby raising rivals’ costs and strengthening their competitive advantage. Conversely, when unit green cost is low, these firms adopt green technology to preempt potential threats from technology-following firms, who could dominate the green market through early adoption. Interestingly, our findings show that green technologies most likely to face industry resistance are not the most expensive, but those with moderate production costs. In such cases, regulatory uncertainty fosters tacit collusion, where competing firms collectively resist green technology adoption to reduce regulation probability and improve profits, even though adoption is economically feasible. To counter this strategic resistance, this paper identifies the most effective intervention mechanisms, such as subsidies or penalties. The results suggest that the optimal intervention strategy differs from the traditional approach of subsidizing high-cost green technologies and penalizing low-cost ones. Instead, it should focus on leveraging firms’ strategic motivations for voluntary green adoption. These insights are vital for governments to design more effective and feasible environmental regulations. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.

Title: AI Adoption Phases in Business Intelligence: From Outsourcing to Human-Centered Systems
Abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Business Intelligence (BI) is vital as it enables businesses to process vast amounts of information quickly and uncover patterns and trends that might otherwise go unnoticed. In this short paper, we propose a five-phase AI adoption in the context of BI drawing from our experience with numerous SMEs in Singapore and internationally. This progression begins with AI for BI 1.0, where businesses rely on outsourced AI services, offering accessible but limited AI capabilities. As organizations seek greater control, AI for BI 2.0 emerges, emphasizing in-house AI development with a focus on interpretability, making AI models more understandable to users. AI for BI 3.0 advances this by adding explainability, clarifying the decision-making processes of AI systems. The transition to AI for BI 4.0 introduces trust as a crucial factor, ensuring that AI models are not only useful and robust but also faithful to the data they analyze. Finally, AI for BI 5.0, integrates human-centered design, enhancing decision-making through continuous feedback and adaptation. This phased evolution reflects the growing demands for transparency, trust, and collaboration in AI-driven BI, ultimately transforming AI from a tool into a trusted partner in business strategy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Abstract: Business process models may generate large sets of execution traces whose size and structure depend on control-flow constructs such as choice, parallelism, and iteration. Title: Generating functions of dual K-theoretic P- and Q-functions and boson-fermion correspondence
Abstract: In this paper, we present a new algebraic description of Ikeda-Naruse's K-theoretic Schur P- and Q-functions and their dual functions in terms of neutral fermion operators. We introduce four families of “β-deformed neutral-fermion operators” depending on a parameter β, which reduce to the usual neutral-fermion operators when β is zero. Using these operators, we introduce two families of β-deformed vertex operators, power sums, and boson-fermion correspondences. From commutation relations among these operators, we naturally derive the K-theoretic Cauchy kernel of Nakagawa-Naruse. Exploiting this fact, we show that the four K-theoretic functions can be realized as vacuum expectation values of certain β-deformed fermionic operators. Title: Securing Small Businesses in the Late 2020’s Against Cyberattack

Abstract: The cyber-resilience of small businesses is important to the economy of every nation. This is because small businesses form the majority of all businesses and because they can function as subcontractors to larger businesses and governments. The security scene of small businesses in Finland was studied by looking at what instructions and guides national security agencies have published for small businesses and what security products are available from the biggest internet service providers. The assumption being that a small business will most probably procure their cybersecurity solutions from the same instance that they get their internet subscription from. A list of the most relevant threats was then compared to the information publicly available on the web pages of these organisations to find the level of security that a small business will obtain. The results show that most technical threats are controlled against but the importance of a good security policy and training is also highlighted. Title: Research on the mechanism of linking time pressure to career growth among hotel employees
Abstract: Research overlooks how and why identical cognitive appraisals of time pressure translate into divergent coping behaviors. Drawing upon the cognitive appraisal theory of stress, this study investigates the mechanisms linking time pressure to the career growth of frontline hotel employees. Utilizing a three-wave time-lagged design, we collected survey data from 323 frontline hotel employees in China and analyzed it using PLS-SEM via SmartPLS 4.0. The results reveal that challenge appraisal and hindrance appraisal play differentiated mediating roles between time pressure and career growth, with job crafting serving as a crucial behavioral bridge in the transformation from stress appraisal to career growth. Title: Linking need for cognitive closure to cyberchondria among health information seekers: Disentangling the roles of uncertainty discrepancy, health worry and information processing evaluations
Abstract: Despite growing research on online health information seeking behaviors, the psychological factors through which dispositional characteristics are linked to maladaptive information outcomes such as cyberchondria remain underexplored. Drawing on the Theory of Motivated Information Management (TMIM), this study establishes a conceptual framework to examine how the need for cognitive closure is associated with cyberchondria through interpretive constructs (i.e., uncertainty discrepancy and health worry) and evaluative assessments (i.e., perceived health information overload and self-efficacy). The study examines the pattern of associations among these information management constructs as theorized by TMIM. Analysis of data from 581 adults using structural equation modeling demonstrates that the need for cognitive closure was directly associated with cyberchondria and was also positively associated with uncertainty discrepancy and health worry. Uncertainty discrepancy and health worry were associated with perceived information overload and self-efficacy, and perceived information overload and self-efficacy were associated with cyberchondria. This research offers insights into the information management constructs associated with cyberchondria by illustrating how dispositional factors are linked to maladaptive information management outcomes in a pattern consistent with the structure theorized by TMIM. Title: A real-time concurrent packing and safety framework for consolidated electronics manufacturing services
Abstract: Warehousing and logistics play a crucial role in supply chain efficiency. Achieving Just-in-Time (JIT) delivery without waste remains a key goal for reducing manufacturing costs. Excess transportation of materials increases operational expenses and causes inventory buildup at production sites, leading to holding costs and complicating quality traceability. In today’s highly competitive environment with short product life cycles, upstream logistics planning and execution must ensure synchronized arrivals and safe transit. Under Industry 4.0, improving material flow efficiency is the main challenge beyond automation. This study examines emerging warehousing and logistics needs in the EMS (Electronics Manufacturing Services) industry by consolidating planning tasks for small and medium-sized businesses within large-scale distribution centers. Materials are dispatched based on customer-specific requirements and delivered just before production line demand, requiring near real-time efficiency in packing space utilization and transportation safety. This research moves away from traditional algorithms that focus solely on packing arrangements or load stability, opting instead for a balanced hierarchical method. It efficiently identifies load patterns in the Bin Packing Problem (BPP) and evaluates packing safety using fuzzy logic. Unlike previous work that applied constraints in a strict hierarchy, this approach allows natural-language descriptions and considers multiple constraints simultaneously. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed concurrent tier framework surpasses some earlier methods and reduces computational resources needed to find near-optimal load patterns while accommodating a broader range of loading constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Comprehensive advances of microneedle technology in addressing diabetes mellitus and its multisystem complications
Abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM), a prevalent chronic metabolic disorder with a global prevalence over 10.5%, features persistent hyperglycemia-induced micro-/macro-vascular lesions and severe complications. Conventional DM management suffers from high risks of cross-infection or hypoglycemia, poor compliance, and failure to address the multi-faceted needs of integrated diagnosis and nonspecific treatment for complications. Microneedles (MNs), a minimally invasive platform that painlessly penetrates the stratum corneum to access interstitial fluid (ISF) or deliver therapeutics, has emerged as a transformative solution for DM care. Despite significant progress in developing MN-based systems for glucose monitoring, insulin delivery, and treatment of complications, challenges remain in achieving precise drug release, high loading capacity, long-term stability, and clinical translation. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest advances in MN-based platforms for DM management, covering three major glucose detection modalities with improved sensitivity and portability, gastrointestinal and glucose-responsive transdermal MNs for insulin delivery, fully integrated close-loop MN platforms, and MN applications in diabetic wound healing and other complications (ketoacidosis diagnosis, vascular disorders, neuropathy, depression). By addressing the critical gaps in scattered research, this work holds great significance for advancing minimally invasive, integrated, and patient-centered treatment models, ultimately improving the prognosis and quality of life for DM patients worldwide. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Foreign Entrepreneurship in the District of Municipalities of Catania and Messina: Preliminary Findings
Abstract: This chapter examines immigrant entrepreneurship in the metropolitan areas of Catania and Messina in Sicily, focusing on foreign-born business owners holding an Italian VAT number. Based on a quantitative survey of 83 cases, the study analyses entrepreneurial trajectories, business characteristics, startup resources, support networks, and relations with the institutional system. The findings show that migrant businesses are concentrated in retail trade, food services, and personal care and are mainly organized as microenterprises and sole proprietorships. Startup capital derives mostly from personal and family savings, while access to formal credit remains limited. Family and community networks play a crucial role in both business creation and daily management, whereas relations with formal support systems remain weak. Overall, immigrant entrepreneurship emerges as both a strategy of socio-economic stabilization and a resource for local development and social cohesion. © The Author(s) 2027.

Title: Artificial general intelligence architectures and evaluation methodologies: A comprehensive review and future research roadmap
Abstract: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) seeks to create machines with broad, human-like cognition. However, rapid advances in narrow AI make it clear that general intelligence remains unresolved. This systematic review synthesises AGI research in five dimensions: definitions, enabling technologies, envisioned applications, evaluation methodologies, and open challenges. We performed a systematic search of major academic databases and search engines up to January 2026. After deduplication, two reviewers independently screened 927 records and included 393 studies that met the predefined criteria. We extracted data to address five research questions for each dimension and conducted a qualitative synthesis, as the evidence base did not support a meta-analysis. Across the literature, AGI is primarily characterised by broad adaptability and cross-domain generalisation. The main approaches include symbolic knowledge-based methods, machine learning, cognitively inspired architectures, hybrid neuro-symbolic systems, and brain-inspired or theoretical models Raman et al. (2025) [302]; each contributes partial capabilities, but exhibits limitations in isolation. The proposed application areas include healthcare, education, finance, transportation, smart cities, defence, scientific research, and more. Evaluation practices span multidimensional scales, cognitive test batteries, and safety-oriented benchmarks for alignment and autonomy. However, many benchmarks are saturated rapidly and do not fully capture real-world generality. Persistent challenges include the absence of a unified empirical theory of intelligence; the integration and scalability of heterogeneous methods; symbol grounding and embodiment; value alignment and control of highly capable agents; and the development of rigorous yet comprehensive evaluation protocols. In general, AGI research remains fragmented, with no approach that demonstrates the full spectrum of general cognitive competence. We operationalise “integration” as a system-level property in which learning, reasoning, memory, and social-ethical constraints are coupled through shared representations and closed-loop control so that each component can shape the others during task execution. We also describe two integrative candidate architectures proposed in the literature: (i) a Self-Evolving Binary-Symbolic AGI framework and (ii) the Cohomological Active Inference Architecture (CAIA). Whether a proposed architecture achieves this integration can be measured empirically using multidimensional AGI benchmarks and safety or alignment evaluations discussed in AGI assessment methodologies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Fostering institutional trust and organ donation: Evidence from a randomized informational intervention in Tunisia
Abstract: Organ transplantation saves lives and improves the quality of life of patients who would otherwise depend on costly and invasive treatments. The technology is becoming available in low- and middle-income countries, but the gap between the demand for and the supply of organ transplants remains large. In a randomized controlled trial at a Tunisian university, we evaluate an expert-led intervention designed to inform about organ donation and strengthen trust in medical institutions. The intervention consists of a short video testimonial from a heart transplant survivor, a presentation led by a medical doctor and a short Q&A session. We find that the intervention significantly increases deceased donor registration, with suggestive evidence of positive spillover effects on the control group. The survey data provides little support for changes in attitudes and social expectations as potential mechanisms. Instead, it reveals large and statistically significant increases in medical and legal knowledge, religious beliefs supportive of donation, and institutional trust among treated students. Finally, we show that treatment effects on organ donor registration are driven by male students and those whose families likely support organ donation. Targeting older segments of the population may further increase the impact and cost-effectiveness of this intervention. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Research trends and conceptual foundations of religious moderation: A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
Abstract: Although the concept of religious moderation has received increasing scholarly attention in recent years, comprehensive and globally integrative syntheses remain limited. In many Western scholarly traditions, similar ideas are often articulated through related concepts such as religious tolerance, pluralism, liberal pluralism, or collaborative secularism, resulting in fragmented conceptual discussions across disciplines and regions. This study therefore aims to map the development, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of research on religious moderation within global academic discourse. This study employs a hybrid approach combining Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database, where the keyword “religious moderation” was searched in article titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search identified 901 publications (2009–2026). After applying the PRISMA screening procedure, 235 articles met the inclusion criteria and were selected for analysis. Bibliometric mapping was conducted using VOSviewer to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, institutional affiliations, and thematic patterns within the field. The findings indicate that research on religious moderation has experienced gradual growth and increasing global visibility. However, the distribution of scholarly contributions remains highly concentrated in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia and Malaysia, suggesting that the concept has not yet diffused widely across Western, Middle Eastern, and African academic traditions. This geographical concentration reveals significant opportunities for comparative, cross-cultural, and interdisciplinary research. This study also, through an analysis of 235 articles indexed in Scopus, found several studies on the indicators and principles of religious moderation, which play an important role in fostering harmony amid social differences and diversity. In addition, the study proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework linking religious moderation to broader domains including social cohesion, conflict resolution, interfaith relations, family dynamics, and education, highlighting its relevance for sustaining inclusive and resilient communities. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Enhancing flood impact assessment accuracy: A comparison of IRIO-Flood predictions using HAZUS- and insurance claims-based business interruption estimates
Abstract: While input–output models are widely used to assess the economic impacts of natural disasters, their results strongly depend on how disaster shocks are specified. This paper examines two alternative characterizations of flood-induced business interruptions, and their effect on total economic losses. We compare restoration time estimates derived from the Hazus-Flood framework with a novel approach based on micro-level insurance claims data, which allows for partial reductions in plants’ productive capacity during the restoration phase, rather than assuming full inoperability.Using georeferenced plant-level data and high-resolution flood maps, we calibrate flood shocks for four major Italian flood events and simulate their propagation through the economy using the IRIO-Flood model. We find that Hazus-based specifications generally produce larger and more dispersed estimates of productive capacity contractions, leading to greater GDP and sectoral output losses – particularly in the short term – and to stronger spillovers to regions not directly affected by the flood. Despite these substantial differences in magnitude, both approaches identify broadly similar patterns in terms of the most affected sectors and regions, with discrepancies emerging more frequently when considering the medium-term propagation of losses.These results highlight the importance of accurate shock specification and suggest that the two proposed methods can be viewed as complementary tools for flood impact and risk assessment. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Validity Criteria for Explaining Variation in Process Complexity
Abstract: Business process complexity is frequently used to assess behavioral change. It is measured repeatedly over consecutive trace windows, resulting in a time series of complexity scores. When analyzing this data, it is a problem that complexity measures can fluctuate even when the underlying process remains stable. So far, business process management research lacks a formal observation model to distinguish process change from measurement-induced variation. In this paper, we build upon signal processing theory to develop an observation model for process complexity. The model decomposes observed complexity scores into a process complexity signal and measurement noise component. The measurement noise component consists of systematic measurement bias and stochastic measurement error. We derive three validity criteria to analyze signal-and-noise characteristics of complexity measures: (1) reliability, reflecting sensitivity to stochastic measurement error when process and observation setting do not change, (2) robustness, reflecting sensitivity to observation setting change, and (3) responsiveness, reflecting sensitivity to process change. We operationalize these criteria and apply them in a large-scale simulation study. The results reveal systematic differences in the signal-and-noise behavior of complexity measures. Our work contributes a measurement-theoretic foundation for interpreting changes in process complexity and for validating complexity measures. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Exploring the Impact of Soft Preventive Judicial Measures on Business Resilience and Performance Under Organised Crime Infiltration: Evidence from a Multi-Case Analysis
Abstract: Organised crime infiltration in legitimate businesses threatens market functioning, firm governance and local economic development. In Italy, alongside seizure and confiscation, the Anti-Mafia Code introduced continuity-preserving “soft” preventive measures—judicial administration (Art. 34) and judicial control (Art. 34-bis)—aimed at interrupting criminal influence while keeping firms operating. Yet, firm-level evidence on their economic and organisational consequences remains limited. This study adopts an organisational resilience perspective and investigates how firms’ operating and financial conditions evolve around these interventions. We conduct a comparative multi-case analysis of 11 firms subjected to Arts. 34/34-bis, identified through judicial records and matched with peer groups by sector, size and geography using AIDA data. We reconstruct trajectories across pre-intervention, intervention, and post-intervention phases using four indicators: value of production, current ratio, net income and debt-to-equity. Findings suggest that soft preventive measures mainly operate as contingent stabilisers: they support operational continuity, but liquidity, profitability and capital structure remain fragile, especially after the judicial phase. The study contributes by opening the firm-level process between preventive judicial intervention and economic outcomes, offering mechanism-oriented evidence that complements existing research on anti-mafia policies. © The Author(s) 2027.

Title: Simulation-Based Assessment of Business Process Robustness
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Business process robustness describes a process’s ability to meet performance targets despite variations in parameters such as arrival rates or resource availability. Assessing business process robustness quantitatively is challenging because dependencies between process parameters and performance are complex and stochastic. Business process simulation avoids the need to specify those dependencies by simulating the process and observing the resulting behavior. However, the space of possible parameter combinations grows quickly, which makes it challenging to identify parameters that still meet the required performance targets. In this paper, we address this challenge by proposing a simulation-based approach that systematically explores parameter configurations to efficiently identify those that maintain acceptable performance. Our evaluation demonstrates that the proposed approach substantially reduces assessment complexity compared to our baselines while accurately identifying parameter combinations under which a process remains robust. The approach provides users with insights into how parameter variations influence performance, enabling a step toward a quantitative foundation for assessing and improving business process robustness. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Mother tongue as a tool for africanization of the curriculum
Abstract: This paper explores the prospects of mother tongue education as a tool for the Africanization of the curriculum by addressing the research gap on the decline in the use of the mother tongue in educational institutions. The deliberation is targeted at promoting a more inclusive and culturally responsive education system in which the linguistic identity of learners is respected. Africanization in education aims at recentering African perspectives, values, and knowledge systems, challenging Western-dominated views that have long sidelined African cultures and languages in learning spaces. While many African countries continue to prioritize colonial languages such as English and French in education, the mother tongue remains a vital tool in assisting learners, as colonial languages often hinder learners’ academic success and reduce their engagement in the learning process. However, the African mother tongue remains at risk of becoming extinct as people continue to migrate in hopes of better economic opportunities. This paper reviewed the language policies of selected African countries, emphasizing the urgent need to prioritize mother tongue teaching and to develop African languages as effective instructional media across all subjects, going beyond just language classes to utilize it as a tool to Africanize the curriculum. The implications for the basic school curriculum are discussed, stressing that mother tongue integration not only supports language preservation but also enhances academic achievement and identity formation. The paper calls for curriculum designers, policymakers, and educators to collaboratively embed African languages and knowledge systems into the curriculum. This approach builds an education system that genuinely embodies and supports the values, cultures, and needs of African communities. The insights emerging from this discourse promise to nurture culturally grounded learners who are capable of addressing African challenges through an Afrocentric lens. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: An intelligent spectrum-aware trajectory data reduction approach for maritime decision support systems
Abstract: High-quality Automatic Identification System (AIS) data is the cornerstone of modern Maritime Expert Systems and Intelligent Decision Support Systems (IDSS). However, the exponential growth of AIS data challenges the real-time situational awareness and storage capabilities of these systems. Conventional compression strategies face a dichotomy: offline algorithms ensure fidelity but suffer latency, while online methods support streaming but often exhibit “geometric blindness,” neglecting kinematic variations like speed changes along linear paths. This study proposes a novel online method, Frequency-Aware Improved Open Window (FA-IOPW). FA-IOPW uses localized spectral information within an evolving Opening Window to adapt the PED–TED weighting during online compression. To support the evaluation, we developed a visualization platform for trajectory query, compression, comparison, and adaptive-weight display. The platform was tested with historical AIS records and controlled application-level replay; live satellite AIS feeds, production Vessel Traffic Service environments, and shipborne hardware were not included in the present validation. Results demonstrate that FA-IOPW achieves a Pareto-optimal trade-off between compression ratio and reconstruction accuracy. Under high-compression regimes, it significantly reduces position and speed errors compared to mainstream methods. Furthermore, we integrated an AI agent module into the platform, lowering the usage threshold for regular users. As a robust online method, FA-IOPW offers a high-fidelity solution for real-time maritime monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Ethics, economics, and environmental stewardship: Religious moral frameworks as constraints for rational policy choice
Abstract: Environmental policy often embeds ethical judgments implicitly in discount rates, welfare weights, prices, or informal constraints. This paper develops a constraint-based framework that makes major ethical commitments explicit before economic optimization begins. Drawing on convergent principles in Jewish, Islamic, Christian, Indigenous, Buddhist, and secular traditions, it identifies stewardship, restraint of waste, intergenerational responsibility, ecological limits, and institutional responsibility as candidate non-compensatory constraints. Economic analysis then compares costs, trade-offs, and institutional feasibility only among policies that satisfy the adopted constraints. Applied water-policy illustrations show how this approach can clarify minimum access, pricing, desalination, and wastewater-reuse choices without claiming that these policies were historically caused by the ethical framework. The contribution to ecological economics is methodological: moral commitments define the admissible policy space, while economics identifies efficient pathways within it. This division of labor improves transparency under moral pluralism and environmental scarcity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Revisiting code readability improvement with LLMs: A critical assessment of fine-tuned models
Abstract: Code comprehension is vital for software development. Still, unreadable code remains a significant issue, costing substantial time and money losses. While tools to identify code exhibiting a low readability exist, take actions to improve such a quality aspect is far from trivial. To support developers in such a task, Vitale et al. introduced at ASE’23 an approach using a transformer model (T5) fine-tuned on code commits in which developers explicitly stated their goal to improve code readability. The authors reported that their model is able to generate readability-improving changes being identical to those implemented by developers (exact matches) in 21% of cases and that, even when they differ, they still improve readability in the vast majority of cases (80%). Given the major advances in AI made in the last few years, we questioned whether a fine-tuning for such a task was still needed in the era of Large Language Models (LLMs), thus revisiting the work by Vitale et al. with state-of-the-art models. In doing so, we found out one major issue with the original study design: The training-test splitting was performed randomly (i.e., readability-improving commits mined from open source projects were randomly split between training and test) rather than by project, significantly inflating the reported performance due to repeating readability-improving commits done within the same project. Indeed, as we will show, even newer and more powerful LLMs fine-tuned for this task can only achieve a 1% of exact matches. Once fixed this issue, we shifted our attention on assessing whether fine-tuning on available developer readability improvements is actually needed given the recent advances in general-purpose LLMs. We compare the performance of fine-tuned state-of-the-art LLMs with what they achieve in zero-shot setting, also including in our study commercial LLMs (GPT-4.1). As we will show, quantitative metrics (e.g., exact matches, CrystalBLEU) tell very little about the readability-improving capabilities of LLMs and, thus, our study is mainly qualitative in nature, with a total of 9,500 inspected LLMs’ change recommendations. While all models do improve code readability, our results clearly show that fine-tuning using mined readability-improving commits does not help and, instead, results in sensibly poorer readability recommendations as compared to LLMs used in a zero-shot setting, with GPT-4.1 being the one achieving the best results. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Thermo-mechanical analysis of energy piles with different pipe configurations using numerical simulations and machine learning models
Abstract: Energy piles, which combine structural support and ground heat exchange, are a promising technology for shallow geothermal utilization. However, systematic frameworks for rapidly evaluating the coupled thermo-mechanical responses of energy piles with different pipe configurations remain limited. In this study, five pile configurations, namely U-type, W-type, 2U-type, 3U-type, and double-helix-type, were investigated using a validated three-dimensional thermo-mechanical numerical model. A dataset of 8000 cases was generated through Latin hypercube sampling and a Python-COMSOL automated workflow. Based on this dataset, four machine learning models, including linear regression, random forest, back-propagation neural network, and XGBoost, were developed to rapidly predict outlet water temperature, pile head displacement, and axial forces under different design and operating conditions. Among them, the XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance, with an R2 value of 0.9938 for the training set and 0.9697 for the test set. Then, a systematic comparative framework was established to evaluate the thermo-mechanical performance and parameter sensitivities of different pipe configurations. The results showed that the 2U-type pile achieved the highest heat exchange efficiency owing to its more uniform pipe arrangement. In addition, the sensitivity analysis indicated that the outlet water temperature was mainly governed by inlet water temperature, pile length, mass flow rate, and soil thermal conductivity, whereas pile head load, inlet water temperature, and pile length had significant effects on pile displacement and axial forces. The proposed framework provides an effective tool for rapid prediction, systematic comparison, and preliminary design evaluation of energy piles with different pipe configurations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Artificial intelligence systems distort upstream selection in human social learning
Abstract: Humans are social learners who depend on observing others to acquire knowledge, norms, and behaviors, a capacity that underlies cumulative cultural evolution. Social learning unfolds in two stages: upstream selection determines what information becomes visible, and downstream selection determines what learners copy from that visible sample. Downstream selection occurs through biases such as conformity bias (copying what appears common) and prestige bias (copying those who appear highly respected). These downstream biases can be adaptive when upstream selection yields a sample that reflects the population's true distribution, so that what appears common is actually common and those who appear respected are actually competent. We argue that digital technologies disrupt this condition, creating an upstream selection problem. Engagement-based algorithms amplify the tails of the distribution, surfacing rare and extreme content, whereas generative AI collapses it toward the mode (of the population or the user), erasing the surrounding diversity. Crucially, in each system the optimization signal shapes both visibility and prestige. For engagement-based algorithms, the signal is engagement: creators who post extreme content become more visible and, through the likes, shares, and followers, appear more prestigious. For generative AI, the signal is statistical typicality: it makes a modal answer dominant and, with no alternatives shown, makes the model that produced it appear more prestigious. These distortions can give rise to emergent group-level phenomena, including pluralistic ignorance and illusory consensus. Synthesizing evidence across psychology, cultural evolution, and computational social science, we provide a framework for how digital technologies disrupt social learning and outline interventions for restoring functional cultural transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Optimal service and charging scheduling of electric vehicle demand-responsive connectors considering multiple trips
Abstract: Demand-responsive connectors have emerged as a promising solution to the first- and last-mile transit connectivity challenge, particularly for linking metro stations with surrounding communities. This paper investigates the optimal service and charging scheduling problem of electric vehicle demand-responsive connector (EV-DRC) system, in which each vehicle serving multiple consecutive trips to minimize total cost (i.e., sum of the vehicle deployment and daily operational costs). This multi-trip electric vehicle routing problem (MTEVRP) is first formulated as an arc flow model, and then reformulated via Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition into a set-covering problem that can be solved by column generation. Subsequently, we propose an exact branch-and-price algorithm incorporating tailored acceleration strategies, including route classification, column selection, and interior point stabilization. Extensive computational experiments demonstrate the algorithm’s exceptional effectiveness − it achieves global optimality in 29 out of 30 test instances with up to 60 customer nodes, while reducing the runtime by a maximum of 71% compared to a standard branch-and-price. Sensitivity analyses reveal key insights regarding the impacts of vehicle capacity, battery specifications, and customer time windows on operational performance. These findings provide valuable guidance for operators to design economically viable EV-DRC services that meet high standards of customer satisfaction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
