Title: Accounting for the risk of restoration failure in ecosystem service valuation
Abstract: While ecosystem recovery is widely recognized to vary, valuations of ecosystem services often assume guaranteed outcomes. We examine whether omitting information on restoration failure risk causes bias in the utility estimates of ecosystem services. Further, we examine how two personal attitudes (connectedness to nature and place attachment) influence risk perception. In comparison to previous studies, we integrate both risk (known outcomes and their probabilities of ecosystem service provision following grassland restoration) and uncertainty (unknown outcomes and probabilities) within a single framework. We find that omitting information on risk leads to overestimation of the utility derived from ecosystem services. Controlling for subjective uncertainty and risk aversion using a hybrid choice model, we find no influence of connectedness to nature on risk perception, whereas the negative effect of high restoration failure risk on utility becomes weaker when place attachment is high. Both latent attitudes decrease the utility of uncertainty, i.e., of the opt-out alternative no restoration. Given the substantial utility implications of restoration failure risk, the EU should complement Member State-level monitoring under the Nature Restoration Regulation with project-level monitoring, open data sharing, and transparent reporting of restoration outcomes to the public. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Ohmic-assisted in-package processing combined with vacuum packaging as a multi-hurdle strategy to improve safety and temperature-dependent stability of frozen cooked shrimp
Abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of integrating in-package ohmic-assisted thermal processing with vacuum packaging as a multi-hurdle strategy to enhance microbial safety and storage stability of frozen white shrimp. Shrimp were packaged under vacuum (V) or atmospheric (A) conditions and processed by ohmic heating (OH) or conventional retort (RE) treatment to an equivalent pasteurization condition (72 °C for 15 s). Samples were stored for 10 months at −18, −15, −10 °C, or under fluctuating temperature (FT) conditions simulating cold-chain variability. OH reduced come-up time by approximately 60% (12.75 vs. 32.00 min), thereby limiting thermal exposure. During storage at −18 °C, sensory acceptability of OH-V samples remained relatively stable (8.00–7.60), whereas RE-A samples under FT declined markedly (7.10–4.40). Oxidative deterioration showed a similar trend: TBARS values reached 1.27 mg MDA/kg in OH-V under FT compared with 2.43 mg MDA/kg in RE-A, while carotenoid losses remained below 3% in OH-V at −18 °C but exceeded 9% in RE-A under FT. Kinetic analysis confirmed quality deterioration within the frozen storage range (R2 = 0.908–0.999; Q10 = 2.10–3.82). Notably, OH-V samples exhibited lower activation energy and Q10 values, indicating reduced temperature sensitivity and improved tolerance to cold-chain fluctuations. Principal component analysis revealed coordinated oxidative, microbial, and sensory quality changes during storage. No target pathogens were detected, supporting microbiological safety. These findings demonstrate that ohmic-assisted in-package processing combined with oxygen-restricted packaging can reduce deterioration kinetics and improve cold-chain stability, supporting its potential as a preventive food control strategy for frozen shrimp. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Zhang T.; Huo Z.; Wang T.
Title: Fed-AFD-GAN: A federated generative adversarial network framework based on adaptive feature distillation
Abstract: Federated Generative Adversarial Networks (FedGANs) enable distributed generative modeling without sharing raw data, thereby preserving data locality while jointly learning and generating multi-class data distributions across clients. However, under non-IID settings (e.g., label-partitioned data), global generators based solely on parameter aggregation suffer from distribution shift and mode collapse, leading to degraded generation quality. To address this, we propose Fed-AFD-GAN, a federated GAN framework with adaptive feature distillation. Beyond conventional parameter aggregation, Fed-AFD-GAN incorporates a multi-teacher feature distillation mechanism to transfer and fuse distribution knowledge from client generators in feature space, improving the global generator's ability to model heterogeneous data. Furthermore, an adaptive distillation strategy based on feature discrepancy dynamically controls distillation triggering and teacher selection, reducing training overhead in the early stages while improving generation quality in the later stages. Experiments on label-partitioned CIFAR-10 and MNIST demonstrate that Fed-AFD-GAN consistently outperforms the FedGAN baseline in generation quality, achieving FID improvements of 13.17% and 16.69% on CIFAR-10 and MNIST, respectively, while reducing the number of distillation updates by 55.1% and 59.46%, respectively, compared with static distillation, thereby yielding a more favorable trade-off between generation quality and computational efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Abstract: Big Data is transforming the way businesses make decisions and operate. Title: Footwear waste recycling: material complexity, technological barriers, and pathways to circularity
Abstract: The global footwear industry produces >20 billion pairs annually, yet post-consumer recovery rates remain below 5%, with the vast majority landfilled or incinerated. This review focuses on non-leather footwear, the dominant category in mass-market production. Unlike packaging plastics or single-polymer waste streams, non-leather footwear is an engineered multi-material composite that incorporates crosslinked polyurethane foams, ethylene-vinyl acetate, vulcanised rubber, thermoplastic polyurethane, polyester textiles, and permanent adhesive systems, whose structural complexity places it beyond the reach of conventional recycling strategies. This review critically examines footwear as a polymer waste stream from a materials, processing, and resource-systems perspective. Pre-consumer and post-consumer waste generation pathways are analysed, and the technical feasibility and economic viability of mechanical, chemical, and hybrid recycling routes are evaluated against the key barriers of multi-material integration, crosslinking, adhesive bonding, and additive contamination. Footwear recycling initiatives such as large-scale mechanical programs, automated sorting, and chemical pretreatment-led delamination are critically assessed. The review finds that no single recycling route adequately addresses the structural complexity of footwear, and that the most promising pathway lies in integrated frameworks that combine selective chemical pretreatment with polymer-specific downstream valorisation. Pre-consumer manufacturing waste is identified as the most immediately actionable entry point for circularity, offering compositionally defined, minimally contaminated feedstocks with substantially lower technical and economic barriers than post-consumer streams. Policy enablers, including Extended Producer Responsibility and design-for-disassembly, are discussed as necessary complements to technological advancement. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Endogenous directed technical change for energy transition
Abstract: The finite nature of certain fossil fuels, which are essential inputs in production, imposes a substantial constraint on the economy's long-term growth potential. This paper develops an endogenous directed technical change model under uncertainty regarding the timing of a potential backstop technology discovery. The model directs R&D towards increasing the probability of a technological breakthrough, triggering thereby a transition from a fossil fuel-dependent economy to one powered by cleaner, renewable energy sources. We derive analytical solutions using a general optimal control framework allowing to establish the Pontryagin (maximum principle) first-order optimality conditions, complemented with an adequate numerical assessment to a model of the optimal allocation of national economic resources between consumption, investment, and R&D. We identify the optimal time paths for consumption in both the pre- and post-backstop adoption economies, the depletion rate of fossil fuels, investment in R&D, and the utilization rate of the substitute, under two scenarios: when energy input and physical capital are substitutes in production, and when they are complements. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Yang Z.; Ren C.; Li M.; Huang G.Q.
Title: MetaTwin: A reconfigurable digital twin framework
Abstract: Digitalization initiatives have led to the widespread adoption of digital twins (DTs), particularly in manufacturing. The explosive growth of DTs makes us think about what the most abstract parts in building the DT systems are and how to promote the reconfigurability of DTs so that they can be agile to adopt the flexibility needs from Industry 4.0 manufacturing systems. However, the heterogeneous granularity and dynamic evolution of manufacturing systems present significant challenges to the reconfigurability of their corresponding DTs. To address these challenges, this paper presents MetaTwin, a reconfigurable DT framework as an integrated solution to abstract DTs into general domains. To be more specific, a novel Domain-Meta structure is first proposed, which addresses the granularity misalignment problem by decoupling the system into stable Domains and reconfigurable Meta units. Then, a dual-dimensional reconfiguration mechanism decomposes complex reconfigurations into macro and micro dimensions, achieved by composing Meta units and reconfiguring their internal pattern-driven Meta Models. A prototype-based case study involving the progressive reconfiguration from an assembly-only DT to a printing-and-assembly DT illustrates how MetaTwin supports reconfiguration scope identification, macro-level structural changes, micro-level behavioral adaptations, and runtime coordination. Furthermore, implementation-level indicators further suggest that the MetaTwin-based implementation localizes changes more effectively than a conventional implementation in the case setting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: MANET cybersecurity: A systematic review of OSI attacks, AI-based detection, and adaptive security gaps (2020–2025)
Abstract: – Mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) rely on the direct participation of network nodes, infrastructure-independent operation, and dynamically changing topologies, making their routing protocols particularly vulnerable to cyberattacks. Routing attacks, including black hole, gray hole, wormhole, Sybil, and routing table poisoning, remain significant threats because they can disrupt packet forwarding, reduce network reliability, and compromise service continuity. Recent research has investigated artificial intelligence, machine learning, trust management, blockchain, and edge/fog computing to improve MANET security. However, limitations concerning scalability, energy efficiency, realistic datasets, and validation under representative operating conditions continue to constrain the practical applicability of many proposed approaches. This paper presents a systematic literature review of 116 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025, conducted according to the PRISMA methodology. The review examines routing attack models, protocol vulnerabilities, defense mechanisms, and emerging research trends, while also identifying unresolved research challenges. Unlike previous surveys that address these aspects separately, this study proposes an integrated methodological framework that combines an OSI-based attack taxonomy with a four-stage security lifecycle encompassing prevention, detection, mitigation, and adaptive response. The reviewed literature is predominantly focused on intrusion detection, while limited evidence was identified of integrated security architectures capable of supporting the complete security lifecycle across multiple network layers. These findings highlight persistent methodological gaps and provide a structured analytical basis for future research on adaptive, distributed, and resource-efficient security architectures for MANETs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Ecosystem services of perennial grain crops
Abstract: Agriculture faces mounting pressure to produce food, feed, and renewable biomass from a finite land base while safeguarding soil and environmental quality for future generations. Perennial grain crops have emerged as a promising strategy to address these challenges by producing edible grain alongside substantial vegetative biomass, maintaining continuous soil cover, and developing deep, persistent root systems. A key strength of perennial grains is the provision of multiple ecosystem services. Evidence to date indicates that perennial grain systems can reduce nitrate leaching, lower nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions, increase carbon sequestration, improve soil structure and nutrient retention, enhance on-farm forage value, and promote biodiversity. Reduced reliance on tillage and external inputs may further decrease fossil fuel use and environmental externalities. In addition to these, perennial grains may provide cultural and aesthetic benefits, such as improving landscape aesthetics, and supporting local traditions and practices related to agriculture. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the ecosystem services provided by perennial grain crops and identifies critical research gaps related to their quantification, trade-offs, and scalability. Robust quantification can support economic valuation, providing a foundation for policy and market incentives that favor the adoption of perennial grain systems and add valuable biomass material to support the green transition. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Zhou L.; Wang S.; Zhou Y.; Wan S.
Title: Flying low for greener farms: Configurational pathways linking the low-altitude economy to agricultural green total factor productivity in China
Abstract: The low-altitude economy is increasingly viewed as a new technological frontier for agricultural transformation, yet its relationship with agricultural green total factor productivity remains poorly understood. This study examines how low-altitude economy-related conditions are associated with high agricultural green total factor productivity in China. We develop an institutional-technological-scenario framework and apply a sequential mixed-method design that combines qualitative coding, necessary condition analysis and dynamic fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis. The empirical analysis uses a balanced panel of 30 Chinese provinces from 2014 to 2022, covering 270 province-year observations. The period is treated as a formative and pre-consolidation stage of the low-altitude economy rather than as a fully mature integrated system. The results show that no single condition constitutes a statistically supported necessary condition for high agricultural green total factor productivity. Exploratory bottleneck analysis nevertheless reveals descriptive threshold patterns at higher outcome levels. The dynamic configurational analysis identifies three pathways associated with high agricultural green total factor productivity, namely technology-application coupling, institution-innovation coupling and scale-application diffusion. The non-high productivity configuration further shows that enterprise development, policy support and market support may fail to translate into green productivity improvement when industrial application is absent. Regional and temporal analyses reveal substantial spatial and temporal heterogeneity. The findings suggest that the low-altitude economy is better understood as an emerging socio-technical enabling system rather than as a single UAV-based technology, and that agricultural green transformation depends on the configuration of institutional support, technological capacity and application scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: A physics-cognitive proactive opportunistic maintenance and routing collaborative framework for offshore wind farms under extreme met-ocean conditions
Abstract: Reliable offshore wind operation requires maintenance decisions that account for multi-source uncertainty including stochastic degradation, environmental shocks, and incomplete condition information. Extreme met-ocean conditions also restrict maintenance access, coupling uncertainty in asset health with fragmented vessel operating windows and high operation and maintenance costs. To address these uncertain issues, this study proposes a proactive opportunistic maintenance and routing strategy. A physics-based competing failure model is developed to capture both cumulative degradation and shock-induced damage. To reduce the physics-cognitive divergence, defined as the inevitable divergence of state estimations from physical wear, an air–sea collaborative fleet using unmanned aerial vehicles enables active monitoring and dynamic replanning. A marginal-benefit-driven opportunistic maintenance strategy is introduced to exploit short and variable weather windows. A continuous weather filtering module proactively schedules critical tasks before adverse conditions, integrated with a bi-level mixed-integer non-linear programming model, which is solved by a bi-stage collaborative solution algorithm to co-optimize multi-vessel routing and maintenance bundling. Simulations on a 78-turbine offshore wind farm over a 90-day period show that the proposed strategy reduces total O&M costs by 96.4%, 46.4%, 19.4% and 46.2% compared to corrective, condition-based, non-opportunistic baselines and sequential scheduling and routing strategy, respectively. The framework offers a scalable and computationally efficient solution for multi-vessel routing and opportunistic maintenance, contributing to the development of cost-effective offshore asset management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The security unlock: How rural social pension makes people more entrepreneurial?
Abstract: Previous literature on the determinants of entrepreneurship has not explored the role of social pension. Leveraging variation in the roll-out timing of a universal rural pension program across Chinese counties, our analysis, at both the individual and aggregate levels, reveals that pension provision led to an increase in entrepreneurship among the younger generation. We show that this effect operates through two primary channels: an intergenerational transfer channel and a local demand channel. Specifically, the pension program mitigates upward transfers from adult children to elderly parents, while boosting local consumer demand, which exerts a demand-side “pull” effect on enterprise establishment. Our findings may shed new light on the interplay between pension, intergenerational resource allocation, and entrepreneurial activity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Governance and renewable energy adoption: Assessing the state's role in solar energy uptake in Iran
Abstract: This study investigates how government managers in Golestan Province, Iran, interpret and respond to national directives aimed at promoting solar energy adoption. Despite Iran's substantial solar potential and supportive national policies, the uptake of solar technologies within public institutions remains limited. Drawing on 28 semi-structured in-depth interviews with senior and mid-level government officials and employing thematic analysis, the study identifies two overarching themes: Managers' Actions and Managers' Orientations. The findings demonstrate that socio-political acceptance within the state is severely constrained by institutional decoupling. Provincial managers face conflicting mandates—such as national renewable targets that conflict with provincial security directives requiring diesel generators—leading to symbolic compliance (e.g., installation of decorative solar panels) while continuing reliance on fossil fuels. By integrating socio-political acceptance with institutional decoupling, the Technology Acceptance Model, and Diffusion of Innovations, this study extends renewable-energy acceptance research from public and market actors to acceptance and resistance within the state apparatus. The findings suggest that aligning national and provincial directives, strengthening inter-agency coordination, and improving managerial capacity are essential for renewable-energy implementation in centralized governance systems and other Global South contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Alternative Dispute Resolution in Construction Projects in the Middle East: A Systematic and Bibliometric Review

Abstract: The construction industry in the Middle East is undergoing unprecedented growth driven by megaprojects, strategic national visions, and large-scale infrastructure development. This expansion has intensified the complexity of contractual relationships, leading to frequent disputes that challenge project performance, cost control, and timely delivery. While litigation has traditionally dominated dispute resolution, alternative dispute resolution (ADR) methods such as arbitration, mediation, negotiation, and dispute review boards (DRBs) have gained prominence as more efficient and relationship-preserving mechanisms. This study provides an integrated systematic and bibliometric review of ADR in Middle Eastern construction projects, synthesizing findings from 77 peer-reviewed studies retrieved from Scopus and screened through a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-based process. Employing PRISMA guidelines and VOSviewer mapping, the research analyzes publication trends, thematic clusters, authorship networks, and country-specific practices. The results reveal the dominance of arbitration and litigation, the underutilization of mediation and DRBs, and significant legal variations across jurisdictions. The study highlights cultural factors such as hierarchy, honor, and relational norms as critical mediators of ADR effectiveness. Emerging innovations [including digital platforms, building information modeling (BIM), and expert systems] illustrate a shift toward technology-enabled dispute management. By bridging bibliometric evidence with thematic synthesis, this review contributes a comprehensive overview of ADR practices in the region, identifies gaps in enforcement and institutionalization, and proposes a holistic improvement agenda that balances legal reform, dispute avoidance, and sustainability. Findings provide actionable insights for policymakers, industry professionals, and international investors seeking to strengthen dispute resolution frameworks and enhance project outcomes across the Middle East.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Food authentication technologies in Sub-Saharan Africa: Regulatory integration, analytical capacity, and governance challenges in preventive food safety systems
Abstract: Food fraud and mislabeling represent persistent threats to food safety and public health, particularly in Sub Saharan Africa where fragmented supply chains, dominant informal markets, and limited regulatory capacity increase vulnerability to adulteration and misrepresentation. The growing complexity of global food systems has intensified the need for reliable authentication and traceability tools as integral components of preventive food safety frameworks. This review critically examines the current landscape of food authentication technologies in Sub Saharan Africa, with emphasis on their analytical performance, practical applicability, and integration into regulatory control systems. A systematic narrative review approach was adopted, guided by structured evidence synthesis principles. Peer reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2026 was analyzed across major scientific databases, focusing on spectroscopic, chromatographic, molecular, and isotopic analytical methods, alongside digital traceability systems and artificial intelligence-driven data analytics. The review employed thematic and comparative synthesis to evaluate technological effectiveness, adoption patterns, and regulatory relevance. The evidence indicates that spectroscopic techniques enable rapid screening, while chromatographic and molecular methods provide high precision confirmatory analysis. Isotope ratio analysis supports origin verification, while digital traceability systems, including blockchain-based ledgers, improve supply chain transparency, while artificial intelligence and machine learning tools function as analytical decision-support systems that enhance pattern recognition and predictive analytics for fraud detection. However, significant limitations persist, including inadequate context specific validation, high costs, limited infrastructure, and weak integration into preventive food safety systems. Technology adoption remains uneven, with concentration in urban laboratories and limited coverage in informal markets. Strengthening food authentication in Sub Saharan Africa requires coordinated investment in low cost technologies, context specific validation frameworks, and regulatory harmonization. Integrating authentication into risk-based food safety systems is essential for improving surveillance, enhancing consumer protection, and aligning regional practices with international standards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From Prediction to Actionable Insight: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework with Explainable AI for Proactive Customer Churn Management
Abstract: In the competitive telecommunications industry, customer churn is an area that requires proactive daily management as it has the highest impact on profitability. While predictive machine learning has dominantly achieved high predictive capability, the “black box” nature of such models has historically hampered the generation of actionable insights, thus resulting in a disconnect between predictions and resultant business activities. This research attempts to bridge this gap by developing and operationalizing a unique integrative paradigm that combines high-performance predictive models with cutting-edge explanatory AI (XAI) methods. We conduct an extensive model evaluation and comparison of four machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost) on the publicly available Telco Customer Churn dataset. Our proposed methodology relies on extensive hyperparameter tuning and class imbalance handling, as well as post-hoc model interpretation methods such as SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) which helps in globally and locally attributing features to model outputs. Our findings suggest that the CatBoost model post hyperparameter tuning exhibited the greatest predictive power (AUC = 0.839). Most importantly, SHAP analysis provides actionable insights by uncovering intricate and nonlinear drivers of customer churn that can assist in designing targeted customer retention strategies. Finally, we introduce a cost-benefit simulation model that monetizes the economic impact of using the framework, with up to 5 times ROI versus untargeted campaigns. This paper contributes a novel, end-to-end method for translating predictive models into interpretable, actionable, and financially viable business assets. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: From what to how and when: Implementing an enhanced MLOps framework for a structured AI development lifecycle
Abstract: Currently, AI-enabled solutions in the public sector are often developed in a fragmented manner, limiting their transferability across organizations and highlighting the need for methodologies that streamline the AI development process. In response, regulatory bodies have introduced standards defining the required characteristics of AI systems, while recent research has called for comprehensive methods to guide the integration of these requirements throughout the AI lifecycle. However, existing approaches tend to remain at a high level, overlooking the challenges of translating principles into low-level implementations and bridging procedural and technical perspectives. Moreover, the level of granularity of AI lifecycle stages does not facilitate the modularity of AI systems, which would enable the easy integration of new implementation to meet system requirements. To address these challenges, this paper enhances the AI lifecycle by introducing explicit operations that support the modular development and reuse of AI products. We propose a structured framework that operationalizes system-level objectives across the different phases of the AI lifecycle while systematically leveraging existing toolkits. In particular, the framework operationalizes cross-cutting requirements by bridging the gap between regulatory objectives and technical implementation, making explicit what requirements an AI product satisfies, how they are implemented, and when they should be addressed throughout the lifecycle. By promoting modularity and reusability, the framework facilitates the systematic development and adaptation of AI products, thereby supporting their scalability and cost-effective adoption across public sector organizations. An exploratory study conducted with ten AI researchers and engineers provides initial feedback on the framework. Finally, two proofs-of-concept use cases demonstrate its practical applicability. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. Title: Secure and adaptive user gait authentication framework for metaverse
Abstract: The Metaverse requires persistent and non-intrusive authentication for avatars across heterogeneous virtual environments. An individual’s walking pattern, or gait, provides a continuous and comparatively spoof-resistant verification mechanism compared with face, voice, or iris biometrics. However, gait-based authentication in avatar-mediated Metaverse environments remains vulnerable to algorithmic and statistical attacks, including synthetic gait generation, exploitation of feature dependencies, behavioral imitation, replay, and model drift. Conventional machine-learning, deep-learning, and transformer-based models also exhibit limited robustness to environmental variation, sensor noise, session variability, and adaptive adversaries. To address these challenges, we propose a secure and adaptive ensemble gait-authentication framework for continuous avatar verification that integrates Bagging, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Extra Trees classifiers through a Secure Majority-Voting Scheme (SMVS). The framework employs a dynamic per-session acceptance threshold that adjusts the required voting condition according to session-level gait dispersion, noise, pose variability, and feature stability, thereby reducing false accepts while preserving authentication usability. We also introduce MetaGait, a large Unity-simulated avatar-gait dataset grounded in biomechanical principles and designed to support realistic multi-session evaluation. Experimental validation is conducted on MetaGait, CASIA-B, and OU-ISIR-C using leakage-safe subject-disjoint grouped cross-validation, together with explicit cross-dataset transfer experiments in which models trained on MetaGait are tested on CASIA-B and OU-ISIR-C. The proposed framework achieves up to 97.2% accuracy, 94.1% precision, 99.7% recall, and 97.0% F1-score, while attaining a low Equal Error Rate (EER) of 3.3% and outperforming traditional machine-learning, deep-learning, and transformer-based authentication models. Furthermore, formal game-based security analysis with probabilistic bounds, supported by comprehensive empirical attack simulations, shows SMVS’s resilience against Adaptive Brute-Force Attacks (ABFA), Constrained Behavioral Attacks (CBA), and Model Drift Invasion Attacks (MDIA). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Qu Q.-X.; Tang Y.; Guo F.; Duffy V.G.; Man S.S.
Title: Mitigating cognitive workload in automated driving takeovers: Effects of non-driving-related tasks, takeover request modalities, and lead times
Abstract: In Level 3 conditional automated driving, non-driving-related tasks (NDRTs) may reduce drivers’ readiness to resume control, while behavioral indicators alone may not fully capture concurrent changes in workload and psychophysiological stress. This study examined the effects of NDRT packages, takeover request (TOR) modalities, and TOR lead time (TORlt) on cognitive workload, cardiac responses, gaze behavior, and vehicle-control performance. A within-subject experiment used EEG, eye movements, cardiac interval measures, NASA-TLX, and post-TOR driving indicators. News reading and video watching produced larger post-TOR changes in selected physiological indicators and greater vehicle-control effort than the phone call task, while video watching also resulted in higher subjective workload. Visual TORs were associated with higher subjective workload, altered cardiac interval responses in the primary analysis, and greater control fluctuation than auditory and auditory-visual TORs. Shorter TORlt was associated with greater changes in cardiac interval measures, whereas its relationship with steering corrections was less robust across sensitivity analyses. Physiological and behavioral responses were not always aligned, as drivers sometimes maintained relatively stable vehicle control despite elevated workload or psychophysiological stress. These findings support the value of multimodal driver-state monitoring during takeover transitions. Under the present simulator conditions, auditory and auditory-visual TORs may warrant further evaluation when drivers are engaged in screen-based NDRTs or when lead time is limited. Overall, the results provide preliminary evidence for condition-specific adaptive warning design and suggest that combining physiological, visual-attention, subjective, and vehicle-control indicators may improve the characterization of driver state during automated driving takeovers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Progress in extraction, purification, chemical structure, bioactivities, and food preservation applications of polysaccharides from Portulaca oleracea L
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: Portulaca oleracea L. is a classic medicinal–edible herb with longstanding traditional use in treating inflammatory disorders, dysentery, skin infections, and metabolic conditions such as diabetes and hyperlipidemia. Polysaccharides (POPs) are among its major bioactive macromolecules and are considered key contributors to these therapeutic effects, supporting high translational value in foods and medicines. Aim of the study: To systematically review advances in extraction–purification, structure, bioactivities, mechanisms and food preservation applications of POPs (2015–2025), and provide a theoretical basis for structure–activity research and industrial development. Materials and methods: Literature and patents were searched from CNKI, PubMed, Web of Science and patent databases using core keywords related to Portulaca oleracea, polysaccharides, extraction, purification, structure and bioactivities. Results: Among the extraction methods reviewed, ultrasonic–enzymatic extraction was associated with the highest reported yield (21.2%), while hot water extraction was noted for its low cost. Purification methods include ethanol precipitation, column chromatography and macroporous resins. POPs are classified into neutral, acidic and heteropolysaccharides; their bioactivities have been linked to medium molecular weight (104–105 Da), high galacturonic acid content, and specific glycosidic linkages. Reported signaling pathways include NF-κB and PI3K/Akt, through which POPs exert antioxidant, cardiovascular-protective, anti-inflammatory, hypoglycemic, antitumor and immunomodulatory effects in preclinical studies. They also show potential applications in edible films and natural preservatives. Conclusions: POPs have diverse structures, potent preclinical bioactivities and favorable safety profiles, making them promising functional ingredients and preservatives, though clinical evidence remains limited. Key challenges are unclear structure – activity relationships, high costs and unstable quality. Future work should clarify structure – activity links, optimize green production and expand applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Fuel blending impact on decarbonizing cold energy for district cooling and data centers
Abstract: Fuel blends are seen as a transitional strategy for decarbonising combustion-based energy conversion processes while retaining dispatchable service for electricity-critical cooling loads. This paper presents a 0-dimensional model for fuel-mixing integrated into a mixed-integer linear optimisation framework for both designing and operating a district cooling plant to meet a data center load. The model considers the Lower Heating Value, delivered cost and comprehensively the upstream carbon intensity of methane-hydrogen blends. It covers the on-site cogeneration, electrically and thermally driven types of chillers, photovoltaic generation and thermal storage. The hypothesis is that the system-level decarbonization performance is affected more by hydrogen production cost and carbon intensity than by the volumetric blend share. A 20 % hydrogen volumetric part is equal to only 7 % chemical-energy substitution. Therefore, it limits the direct point-of-use carbon-dioxide reduction to the same magnitude. As a matter of fact, a full substitution by green hydrogen reduces specific emissions by 46.4 % while it increases the levelised cold energy cost by 37.1 % due its high production cost shifts operation towards grid electricity. Yet, biomass-derived hydrogen reduces specific emissions by 96.5 % under the assumption of biomass carbon neutrality and lowers the levelised cold energy cost by 8.5 %. Moreover, in the case of brown hydrogen specific emissions increase by 124.4 %. The results show demonstrate that volumetric blending targets alone do not guarantee decarbonisation within the considered deterministic prices and emission factors. Certification of upstream hydrogen is crucial for a comprehensive carbon avoidance cost assessment for fuel-specific economic screening. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Fairness in Prescriptive Process Analytics: Integrating Fairness Constraints into the Learning Phase
Abstract: Prescriptive Process Analytics is a core field in business process management that provides automated activity recommendations to improve Key Performance Indicators in business processes. Because such recommendations can directly affect individuals involved in the process, ensuring fairness is essential. Recent work has begun to address fairness in process monitoring by enforcing group-level parity across demographic groups at the predictive stage. However, these approaches leave the prescriptive phase entirely unexamined and rely solely on group fairness notions, failing to account for individual-level counterfactual fairness (i.e., the requirement that a recommendation should not change when sensitive attributes are altered). To address this gap, we propose to enforce counterfactual fairness directly in prescriptive process monitoring. We develop a novel neuro-symbolic framework based on Logic Tensor Networks that encodes counterfactual fairness as a logical axiom over predictions, seamlessly integrated into the learning process. We evaluate our approach on real-world event logs and find that it enforces counterfactual fairness at the prediction level and improves recommendation-level counterfactual consistency under the considered policy, while maintaining competitive predictive and prescriptive performance, establishing the first fairness-aware framework for Prescriptive Process Analytics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Sustainable aviation fuels: a review of production technologies, life-cycle emissions, and key challenges
Abstract: The aviation sector is essential for global connectivity and economic growth but remains one of the most difficult industries to decarbonize due to its reliance on energy-dense liquid fuels and the anticipated increase in both carbon dioxide (CO2) and non-CO2 climate impacts. As the industry pursues net-zero emissions by 2050, Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAFs) have emerged as the most practical near- and medium-term decarbonization pathway because they are compatible with existing aircraft and fuel infrastructure. However, uncertainties persist regarding the sustainability, scalability, economic viability, and long-term climate benefits of different SAF production routes. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of SAFs by integrating feedstock availability, conversion technologies, fuel properties, life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, techno-economic performance, and future deployment prospects within a unified sustainability framework. Major SAF pathways, including Oil-to-Jet (OTJ), Gas-to-Jet (GTJ), Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ), and Sugar-to-Jet (STJ), are critically evaluated, with particular focus on ASTM D7566-certified fuels such as Fischer–Tropsch Synthetic Paraffinic Kerosene (FT-SPK), Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids (HEFA-SPK), and Hydroprocessed Algae-Based Fuels (HC-HEFA). Comparative analysis reveals significant differences in feedstock requirements, process efficiencies, production costs, fuel composition, and scalability. Life-cycle assessment (LCA) studies indicate GHG emission reductions ranging from 60% to over 100% relative to conventional jet fuel, with FT-SPK and FT-SPK/A offering the highest mitigation potential. Feedstock cultivation, resource extraction, and fuel conversion are identified as the most emission-intensive stages, underscoring the need for upstream process optimization. The review further examines critical barriers to large-scale SAF deployment, including feedstock scarcity, supply variability, high energy and hydrogen requirements, infrastructure constraints, and high production costs. While HEFA dominates current commercialization, scalable aviation decarbonization will require accelerated deployment of FT, ATJ, and Power-to-Liquid (PtL) pathways, supported by technological innovation, sustainable feedstock expansion, and enabling policies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Ferric iron availability and species identity jointly shape the metabolic profiles and spoilage potentials of grass carp spoilage bacteria: A combined metabolomic and physicochemical evaluation
Abstract: Ferric iron is essential for bacterial growth and spoilage-associated phenotypes, yet its specific influences on the metabolism and spoilage potential of fish spoilage bacteria remain unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the metabolic and spoilage potential changes of grass carp spoilage bacteria under varying ferric iron accessibilities, using combined metabolomic and physicochemical detection. The results showed that high ferric iron accessibility stimulated bacterial carbohydrate metabolism (glycolysis and tricarboxylic acid cycle) and fatty acid β-oxidation. Conversely, the low-ferric-mimicking condition partly hindered carbohydrate degradation and enhanced amino acid catabolism, evidenced by the increase in ammonia and a significant 29% decrease in glutamate level. As for spoilage potential, bacteria increased the accumulation of trichloroacetic acid (TCA)-soluble peptides (up to 2.17 μmol tyrosine/g) and biogenic amines (with histamine contents up to 19.32–30.04 mg/kg) under the low-ferric-mimicking condition, owing to possibly increased protease secretion, elevated siderophore synthesis, and decreased amine oxidase activity. Besides, the tested bacteria exhibited different characteristics, such as the potent activity of Pseudomonas putida in utilizing amino acids and carbohydrates, the high capacity of Shewanella putrefaciens in producing putrescine, cadaverine, and histamine, and the strong potential of Shewanella putrefaciens in degrading purine-related compounds. Taken together, this study revealed ferric-dependent metabolic and spoilage potential changes of grass carp bacteria, indicated the potential risk of ferric iron depletion on fish quality preservation, and thereby inspired the development of iron-based preservation strategies for aquatic products. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A dynamic, physics-driven life cycle model for citrus supply chain: Evidence from a South Africa–Netherlands maritime trade route
Abstract: Agri-food chains, especially fruit, produce about 10% of global GHG emissions, with more than half arising after harvest. Yet current methods, such as life cycle assessment (LCA), lack the spatial, temporal and physiological detail needed to resolve stage-specific drivers of environmental impact. We aim to overcome these limitations by developing a spatio-temporal, physics-based life cycle model that quantifies climate change (CC) and fossil resource use (RU,f) impacts for individual fruits and shipments across a transcontinental maritime supply chain. The proposed framework is demonstrated using a case study of the citrus supply chain connecting production in South Africa to consumption in the Netherlands. We show that variability among fruits and between shipments substantially alters CC and RU,f impact outcomes, demonstrating the need for dynamic rather than static supply-chain assessment. Energy use, maritime transport and food loss dominate impacts, with the farm-to-packhouse and overseas shipping stages contributing up to 0.5 kg CO₂-eq kg⁻¹ and 2 MJ kg⁻¹ of fruit consumed, depending on local conditions and cold-chain management. Stage-specific interventions, such as reducing field heat prior to forced-air cooling or increasing shipping temperatures from −1 °C to 1–3 °C under validated phytosanitary conditions, can meaningfully lower impacts. This dynamic framework offers a more realistic basis for identifying and achieving feasible decarbonization in global fruit supply systems. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. Title: Measuring success: A refined methodology for estimating long-term continuous improvement
Abstract: Successful resource management systems require current and detailed feedback on operational and corporate-level performance. Traditional savings estimation methods can be difficult to understand, particularly linear regression, and can provide varying results. Title: A signaling-cognitive architecture for product rating as quality inference
Abstract: Current product rating prediction methods generally rely on algorithmic construction and data-driven approaches, often overlooking the nature of rating generation as a result of quality inference from observable signals. To bridge this gap, we propose ScoRE (Signaling theory-guided and COgnitive-driven Rating prEdiction), an architecture that reframes rating prediction as a quality inference task. This framework integrates signaling theory with a four-stage cognitive process, incorporating a product quality signal strength index to weigh the importance of product-side signals based on their credibility. Specifically, compared with the strongest baseline on each dataset, ScoRE reduces RMSE by 14.85%, 7.17%, and 16.71% on the Clothing, Electronics, and Home datasets, respectively. Moreover, it surpasses the strongest LLM-based models by 34.25% on Clothing and 7.31% on Music. These results underscore the discrepancy between the generative objectives of LLMs and the requirements of numerical prediction, highlighting the necessity of task-specific and theory-informed designs. Authors: Yang Y.; Li J.; Li Y.; Zhang S.; Guo K.
Title: Facilitator or hallucination trap? A social-cognitive account of AI-generated misinformation handling in GenAI-assisted L2 writing
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has demonstrated remarkable potential in second language (L2) learning, yet it is prone to hallucinations. Empirical research on how GenAI-generated misinformation is handled in educational contexts remains scarce. Accordingly, little is known about how these practices shape learning processes and outcomes. Guided by social cognitive theory, the current study frames students' GenAI-assisted L2 writing (using a tailored GenAI writing agent) in a hallucination-prone context in which misinformation was implanted. We examine AI literacy, higher-order thinking resources (i.e., critical thinking and creativity), L2 writing resources (i.e., L2 writing grit and self-regulatory writing strategies), English writing self-efficacy (EWSE), AI-generated misinformation detection (AI-MD), and L2 writing performance within this framework. Using a multi-method approach, combining a qualitative interview study (N = 35), two lab experiments (N = 140), and a large-scale questionnaire survey (N = 406), we find that critical thinking positively predicts GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance via AI-MD, and that negative priming on AI hallucinations significantly improves students’ AI-MD and their GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance, relative to neutral or positive priming. Furthermore, the cross-sectional survey focuses on personal factors and shows that AI literacy significantly predicts EWSE both directly and indirectly through a cognitive–generative pathway involving higher-order thinking resources and a motivational–regulatory pathway involving L2 writing resources. These findings extend social-cognitive accounts of GenAI-assisted L2 writing and inform instruction that helps learners evaluate AI outputs, manage misinformation risks, and sustain their own writing processes. © 2026

Title: How Organizations Use Process Mining to Enable Automations: Evidence from Qualitative Interviews in Canada
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and Agentic AI (AAI) are increasingly positioned as central enablers of digital transformation, supporting organizations in automating repetitive, rule-based tasks as well as more dynamic and decision-intensive processes. However, organizations often face challenges in systematically identifying, prioritizing, and planning automation initiatives that align with strategic goals and deliver measurable value. This study investigates how industry practitioners plan and prioritize automation initiatives and how Process Mining (PM) can be leveraged to identify suitable candidates for RPA or AAI deployment. The research examines practitioners’ approaches to selecting automation opportunities, identifying technical feasibility with business impact, and measuring the automation impact on the improved business processes. The study’s qualitative research design involves semi-structured interviews with fifteen industry experts in Canada, including process analysts, automation leads, consultants, and technology specialists. Using Nvivo and concept coding, the analysis identified recurring patterns for each of the interview themes (6) and subthemes (19). The findings indicate that organizations strongly recognize the value of PM in accelerating the identification of RPA/AAI automation opportunities. However, maximizing its adoption and impact requires addressing several challenges, including data availability, budget constraints, limited technology awareness, and insufficient collaboration among teams. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Impact of intellectual capital on the competitiveness and business performance of microenterprises
Abstract: This study examines the influence of intellectual capital, understood in its human, structural and relational dimensions, on the competitive advantages and business results of microenterprises located in the canton of La Maná, province of Cotopaxi, Ecuador. With a quantitative approach, a structured survey was applied to owners of microenterprises; the data were analyzed through exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling with partial least squares. The sample comprised 867 valid responses from microenterprise owners in the canton of La Maná, covering different economic activities in the local microenterprise structure. The structural model included five blocks, defined as human capital, structural, relational, competitive advantages and business results. The reliability indices (Cronbach's alpha and Dillon-Goldstein's rho) and convergent validity (AVE) were satisfactory in most of the blocks, especially structural capital and relational capital. The overall goodness of fit of the model (GoF = 0.4396) was adequate. Among the key findings, structural capital significantly influences competitive advantages, which, in turn, influence business results. Human capital has a moderate direct effect on competitiveness and a smaller indirect effect on business results. Furthermore, the study identifies specific managerial practices for enhancing intangible assets and outlines avenues for future research on sector-specific variations in the dynamics of intellectual capital accumulation. Relational capital showed a weak influence on competitive advantages and business results, suggesting that external networks in this local microenterprise context may be informal, weakly institutionalized or insufficiently consolidated. The results highlight the relevance of structural capital and competitiveness as key elements for improving business performance in microenterprises and offer practical implications for their strategic strengthening. These insights contribute broadly to the discourse on intangible asset management and sustainable competitiveness in developing regions. Authors: Wang Y.; Wang Z.; Zou Y.; Song Y.; Xia G.; Chen S.; Guo H.; Cao C.; Yang X.; Deng Z.; Li J.; Gong D.; Wang W.; Lyu X.; Tao Z.; Huang X.
Title: Self-disclosure to intelligent virtual agents: A scoping review and the disclosure affordance–actualization–governance framework
Abstract: Intelligent virtual agents (IVAs) have become digital social objects to which people disclose personal, emotional, health-related, and other sensitive information. Yet similar cues—including anthropomorphism, social presence, empathy, gaze, anonymity, and structured questioning—are associated across studies with greater disclosure, refusal, impression management, socially desirable responding, or discomfort. Searches covered four bibliographic databases without publication-year restrictions through March 17, 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar searching on May 20, 2026. This review, reported with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), maps 88 empirical studies and introduces the Disclosure Affordance–Actualization–Governance (DAAG) framework as a middle-range account linking specific empirical findings with broader explanations of IVA-mediated disclosure. DAAG distinguishes sociotechnical interaction ecology; perceived safety from judgment, relational receptivity, expressive latitude, and boundary agency; disclosure actualization; affective, relational, and functional consequences; governance; and evidential reach—the extent to which studies observe perception, behavior, consequences, time, and governance. The literature is most developed for disclosure onset, sensitive reporting, emotional expression, and immediate system acceptance, but remains thin on persistence, reciprocity, subjective–behavioral divergence, correction, revocation, and downstream data use. Recurrent patterns are consistent with IVA cues being interpreted through evaluation risk, partner responsiveness, observability, topic sensitivity, competence, privacy, and control. DAAG is not presented as a validated causal model, but as a framework for explaining when digital social interaction supports, redirects, or appropriately constrains self-disclosure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Journey to the bargaining table: Signaling, seeking, and screening
Abstract: Negotiation scholarship has focused extensively on what happens at the bargaining table—how parties make offers, manage conflict, and reach agreements. Far less attention has been paid to how parties get to the table in the first place. In this article, we argue that the journey to the table deserves greater scrutiny. We organize pre-table dynamics around three behaviors: signaling (communicating whether and how negotiation might proceed), seeking (approaching a counterpart to propose bargaining), and screening (deciding whether to engage with or withdraw from a seeker). We review recent and foundational work bearing on each, identifying where the field has made progress and where significant gaps remain. These pre-table processes have important implications for negotiated outcomes, for negotiations that never occur, and for understanding how opportunity and bias operate before parties ever sit down together. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Guan Y.; Guo H.; Wang X.; Zhou X.; Fu W.; Ding X.; Xia D.; Zhao S.
Title: Enhancing anaerobic digestion of lignite with nano-Fe2O3 modified biochar: roles of liquid phase reconfiguration and microbial metabolic promotion
Abstract: Anaerobic digestion of lignite represents a promising approach for low-rank coal resource utilization and energy structure optimization, offering broad application prospects. To this end, nano-Fe2O3 modified biochar (NIBC) was synthesized and evaluated against biochar. Synthesis and characterization confirmed the successful loading of nano-Fe2O3 onto biochar, which led to significantly improved material properties (e.g., surface area, porosity, and surface functional groups). Consequently, NIBC substantially enhanced methane production (81.88 ± 6.78%, 4.89 ± 0.41 mL/g), system stability, and substrate degradation. Mechanistic analyses revealed a synergistic reconfiguration of dissolved organic matter, characterized by a shift toward more bioavailable intermediates (tryptophan-like and protein-like components), alongside a marked enrichment of key microbial taxa (e.g., Pseudomonadota, Methanobacteriota, Methanosarcina) and their associated metabolic pathways (e.g., glycolysis, reductive acetyl-CoA pathway). This work elucidates the integrated physicochemical-biological mechanisms by which NIBC enhances lignite anaerobic digestion, revealing previously overlooked cross-scale linkages between material properties, liquid-phase chemistry, and microbial ecology. The findings suggest potential opportunities for the development of biowaste-derived additives and the utilization of low-rank coal resources. Future research could focus on process scale-up, continuous operation, and techno-economic assessment to evaluate the feasibility of such strategies under practical conditions. Overall, this study provides a mechanistic foundation for advancing the clean conversion of lignite and supports the development of more sustainable bioenergy technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Wang L.; Dong H.; Luo Z.
Title: How do consumers react to unfair reviews? Examining the matching effects of review type and response strategy on purchase intentions
Abstract: Unfair negative reviews can harm businesses by damaging brand image and reducing customer trust. This research examines how tourism and hospitality businesses should respond to different types of unfair reviews through three scenario-based experiments. The findings reveal a congruity effect: rational responses are more effective in improving third-party consumers’ purchase intentions for low-arousal unfair reviews, while emotional responses are more effective for high-arousal ones. The results further show that social distance mediates this effect. In addition, in high-arousal cases, weak victimization responses are more suitable than strong reprimands. These findings enrich theories related to Communication Accommodation Theory and contribute to the literature on unfair negative reviews. They also provide practical guidance for tourism and hospitality businesses on how to effectively handle online consumer unfair reviews. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Disaster Management: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses
Abstract: This study presents an examination of artificial intelligence (AI) in the disaster management (DM) cycle to support human decision-making systems. There is an urgent need for holistic application strategies that support disaster risk reduction given the increasing frequency and severity of disaster events. This stems from the growing adoption of AI technologies, including machine learning (ML), deep learning, and natural language processing in transforming disaster management. This is to enable the development of high-performance tools for assessing disaster impacts and addressing un-met human needs. This study reviewed journals and conference proceedings articles from three different academic databases: Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Article selection and query refinement were conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines to support methodological approach. The review explored scholarly perspectives on AI application in DM phases to support human-centered decision-making processes in reducing disaster impacts on human lives. Findings from the review indicate that most existing studies focus primarily on the AI application in the response phase. Despite its potential, integrating AI into disaster management remains challenging, particularly due to widespread misconceptions about adoption of AI, as well as ongoing ethical, trust, and security concerns. This study emphasizes the comprehensive application of AI to enhance planning, encourage proactive measures, and improve response and recovery efforts during disaster events. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Pu Y.; Chen H.; Guo Y.
Title: Autonomy-supportive mediation and scam susceptibility: The role of literacy among middle-aged and older adults
Abstract: Although online scams increasingly threaten middle-aged and older adults, existing research has largely focused on individual literacy and short-term interventions, leaving the development and application of scam literacy in everyday contexts less understood. Drawing on parental mediation theory and self-determination theory, this study conceptualizes autonomy-supportive mediation (ASM) as a family-based socialization context for developing aging parents' scam-related literacy. It also considers face concern, a personal orientation reflecting individuals’ motivation to protect their social image from potential social judgment. This study tested two complementary models that distinguish between the foundation of scam literacy (scam knowledge) and its activation (cyber-risk beliefs). Data were collected through a cross-sectional vignette-based survey of 404 middle-aged and older adults in China between February 13 and February 27, 2025, using a volunteer-assisted convenience sampling strategy. The results indicated that higher levels of ASM were linked to lower scam loss, with this association mediated by scam knowledge and moderated by face concern. Moreover, ASM was positively related to cyber-risk beliefs, which were subsequently linked to greater systematic information processing and suspicion toward potential scams. These findings suggest that effective scam prevention depends not only on what individuals know, but also on whether they recognize and respond to risks in real-world situations. This study highlights the importance of autonomy-supportive family communication in combating online scams. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Efficiency-inducing lump sum taxation in non-renewable resource industries
Abstract: This paper studies the design of efficiency-inducing lump-sum taxes in common-pool non-renewable resource industries. Although fixed payments such as royalties, rents, and lease fees play a central role in real-world resource taxation, their theoretical properties remain largely unexplored. We develop a dynamic Cournot model in which firms exploit a shared exhaustible stock and pay a lump-sum tax that depends solely on the current resource level. We characterize the tax that decentralizes the social planner's extraction path under both open-loop and closed-loop information structures. When marginal extraction costs are independent of the resource stock, the optimal tax under open-loop strategies is positive and exceeds the corresponding tax under closed-loop strategies. In contrast, when extraction costs decline with the stock, the optimal tax in both information structures may be positive or negative, with its sign determined by a threshold of industry concentration, which varies across the two settings. Closed-form solutions for linear and iso-elastic demands reveal that the optimal tax can be strictly negative (resp. positive) even in the interval of resource stocks where the laissez-faire equilibrium output is higher (resp. lower) than the social planner's solution. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Gas flaring, agricultural productivity and labor reallocation: Evidence from Nigeria
Abstract: This paper investigates the impact of natural gas flaring—a byproduct of oil production—on agricultural productivity in Nigeria. Using a panel dataset of Nigerian households from the Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS) spanning 2012–2018, combined with geocoded data on monthly gas flaring volumes from oil fields, the study employs variation in the timing of interview surveys to assess effects of gas flaring during harvest and planting seasons. The analysis focuses on southern Nigeria, where oil production is concentrated, and leverages a 2010 policy reform (Local Content Act) that increased local onshore oil activities and thus gas flaring. The empirical strategy includes fixed effects (household, and region-by-month-by-year) to control for unobserved heterogeneity, weather variables (precipitation and temperature), and an instrumental variable approach using global oil price changes interacted with pre-sample flaring intensity to address endogeneity. Key outcomes measured are real crop yield per hectare and labor productivity (real agricultural output divided by worker-days). The findings reveal significant negative effects during the harvest season, particularly in rainy periods, but minimal impacts during planting. Mechanisms are explored through satellite data on air pollutants, showing elevated levels of black carbon, sulfur dioxide, and nitrogen dioxide in flaring areas. Robustness checks confirm the results against various confounders like conflicts, oil spills, and placebo tests. The paper contributes to literature on the impact of air pollution on worker productivity and crop yields and climate change impacts on agriculture, highlighting policy needs to mitigate environmental costs from extractive industries in developing countries. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Kuo C.-C.; Wu C.-H.; Ni Y.-L.
Title: Why and when does leisure-time physical activity enhance hospitality employees’ job satisfaction
Abstract: Employee engagement in leisure-time physical activity has been associated with greater job satisfaction. However, the conditions under which and the reasons why leisure-time physical activity enhances job satisfaction need to be better understood. Drawing on the integrated perspective of proactivity and the work–home resources model, we propose that employees with lower levels of proactive personality particularly benefit from leisure-time physical activity because it helps them proactively manage their vitality, thereby increasing job satisfaction. Consistent with our expectations, the results from a sample of 197 hotel employees indicate that leisure-time physical activity positively predicted job satisfaction through proactive vitality management. Moreover, the mediating effect of proactive vitality management was more substantial among individuals with lower proactive personality. Title: The transformation and release of phosphorus during conversion of chars produced from NH4H2PO4-doped biomass
Abstract: Phosphorus (P) additives, such as NH4H2PO4, improve bio-oil quality during biomass pyrolysis, but the fate of the retained phosphorus during char conversion remains unclear. This study investigates the P transformation and release during secondary pyrolysis (800–1100 °C) and combustion (5% O2, 550–1100 °C) of chars prepared from pine wood and wheat straw doped with NH4H2PO4 and pyrolyzed at 550 °C. Analytical characterization (XPS, XRD, ICP-OES, and SEM-EDS) revealed that P release increased significantly with temperature, reaching up to 53% during secondary pyrolysis and 79% during combustion. XPS identified C-O-P and C-P bonds in all secondary-pyrolyzed chars. XRD revealed that P remained amorphous in the secondary-pyrolyzed pine wood-NH4H2PO4 chars, whereas KPO3 formed in the wheat straw-NH4H2PO4 chars. Ca3(PO4)2, Ca(PO3)2, and KCaPO4 were more abundant in the wheat straw-NH4H2PO4 ashes than in the pine wood-NH4H2PO4 ashes. We identified four primary mechanisms for P release: (1) P2O5 vaporization from phosphoric acid dehydration; (2) C-O-P and C-P bond cleavage during char oxidation; (3) elemental phosphorus release through carbothermic reduction (800–1100 °C); (4) KPO3 vaporization (950–1100 °C). These findings provide new insights into P transformation mechanisms and shed light on the feasibility of process improvement towards better P recovery. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Lin Z.; Shen C.; Li S.
Title: Turning rivals into partners? emission reduction technology licensing strategies under market encroachment and Cap-and-Trade regulation
Abstract: This study examines the optimal licensing strategy for an emission reduction technology (ERT) innovator under Cap-and-Trade (C&T) regulation and the threat of market encroachment by a new entrant. We develop a game-theoretic model involving an innovator, an ordinary incumbent, and a potential entrant, and extend the framework to analyze entrant cost heterogeneity, Two-Part Tariff (TPT) contracts, and endogenous green marketing. Our analysis yields three main insights: (i) the threat of encroachment fundamentally reshapes the strategic landscape by catalyzing cooperation between incumbents through relaxed conditions for fixed-fee licensing, and can paradoxically benefit the innovator when ERL is high; (ii) the optimal contract exhibits a structural reversal contingent on emission reduction efficiency, where royalty-based contracts soften competition for incremental innovations, whereas fixed-fee contracts maximize surplus extraction for high-efficiency technologies—a transition accelerated by endogenous green marketing; and (iii) the innovator exhibits a robust preference for licensing to the incumbent rather than the entrant, which remains structurally robust across all model extensions. Furthermore, under entrant cost heterogeneity, licensing to the incumbent establishes an effective entry barrier to lock out the entrant, whereas royalty-licensing to the entrant serves as a flexible co-optation tool when entry is inevitable. These findings offer strategic guidance for firms managing coopetition and entry threats in carbon-constrained markets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Evolution of recommender systems: Approaches, advances, paradigm shifts, and future directions
Abstract: Recommender systems are essential tools across numerous digital platforms, helping users discover relevant products, content, and services. Research has traditionally focused on prediction accuracy and relevance, relying primarily on collaborative filtering and matrix factorization techniques. With the increasing complexity of user behavior and data modalities, modern systems have moved beyond simple rating prediction to address additional objectives, including fairness, transparency, privacy, long-term engagement, and trustworthiness. This article systematically reviews the evolution of recommender systems, covering key stages from early predictive models to modern human-centered and trust-aware systems. Each stage is discussed in terms of methodological advances and practical applications. Emerging paradigms, including causal reasoning for bias mitigation, reinforcement learning for long-term optimization, federated and privacy-preserving learning, explainable recommendation techniques, and blockchain-based trust mechanisms, are analyzed. These developments illustrate a broader shift from static, correlation-driven predictions toward adaptive, context-aware, and human-centered intelligence. By organizing research into coherent clusters, this review provides a unified perspective on the field, highlights the connections between past and current approaches, and identifies promising directions for next-generation recommender systems that balance accuracy, user satisfaction, ethical considerations, and long-term system effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: A multi-similarity matching framework for remaining useful life prediction based on spatiotemporal health indicators
Abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is a critical task in prognostics and health management (PHM) of industrial equipment. Health indicator (HI) based RUL prediction methods have attracted increasing attention because they represent equipment degradation using low-dimensional and interpretable trajectories. However, most existing similarity-based methods assess degradation similarity primarily through health indicators, without adequately exploiting temporal degradation characteristics and spatial dependencies among sensor data. Moreover, most methods provide only point estimates, limiting the characterization of prediction uncertainty and prediction reliability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel RUL prediction framework that performs multi-similarity matching based on spatiotemporal feature representations and HIs. The proposed framework consists of three modules: a degradation trajectory module, a health indicator construction module, and a multi-similarity prediction module. Specifically, the degradation trajectory module utilizes sensor data to construct degradation trajectories and extract temporal and spatial features. Based on the learned degradation trajectories, the health indicator construction module employs a change-point detection method to identify the onset of degradation and generate health indicators, while an offline HI library is established by constructing health indicators from multiple equipments. A multi-similarity matching strategy is developed to estimate the RUL of target equipment, and prediction intervals are constructed to quantify prediction uncertainty. Experimental results on publicly available datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved prediction accuracy and robustness compared with existing approaches. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Teachers’ skills as a moderator in the relationship between entrepreneurial self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention among form six students in Malaysia: A cross-sectional PLS-SEM study
Abstract: Entrepreneurship is increasingly promoted as a key career pathway for future graduates; however, many students remain reluctant to pursue it. They prefer to work with someone rather than being a boss for their own business. This study explores the relationship between self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention among Form Six students in Malaysia, emphasizing the moderating role of teachers’ skills. Using a quantitative research design, data were collected from 269 Business Studies students across Perak through structured questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). This cross-sectional survey investigates the relationship between entrepreneurial self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention among 269 Form Six students in Perak, Malaysia. Using PLS-SEM, the study tests the moderating role of teachers’ skills. Entrepreneurial self-efficacy significantly predicts entrepreneurial intention (β = 0.651, p < 0.001). Teachers’ skills do not directly predict intention; however, the interaction term is significant (β = 0.240, p = 0.028), indicating that teachers’ skills strengthen the self-efficacy–intention relationship. The results indicate a strong and statistically significant positive relationship between self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention. Although teachers’ skills do not have a direct effect on entrepreneurial intention, they significantly moderate the relationship between self-efficacy and entrepreneurial intention. Specifically, students with high self-efficacy are more likely to develop entrepreneurial aspirations when guided by teachers with strong pedagogical and business-related skills. These findings underscore the importance of equipping educators with the necessary competencies to strengthen entrepreneurship education. Title: Edupreneurship management in vocational education: Case study in vocational high school in East Java
Abstract: Vocational education is required to produce graduates who are not only ready to work but also able to create jobs. Edupreneurship is a strategic approach to meet these demands by integrating an entrepreneurial spirit into educational management and practices. This study aims to explore and analyze the model and implementation of edupreneurship management in vocational education in East Java Province. The study uses a qualitative approach with a case study method in several vocational education programs that are considered to have good edupreneurship practices. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with institutional leaders, teachers/lecturers, and students; participant observation; and document analysis. The results of the study indicate that effective edupreneurship management is built through five main pillars: (1) visionary leadership oriented toward innovation and the market; (2) an integrated curriculum that combines technical competencies, entrepreneurship, and real-life project-based learning; (3) strong strategic partnerships with the industrial and business world for cocreation and quality assurance; (4) the development of an internal entrepreneurial ecosystem (such as teaching factories, business centers, and production units) that directly involves students; and (5) an organizational culture that encourages creativity, measured risk, and learning from failure. The main challenges faced include the gap between the educational and entrepreneurial mindset among educators, limited supporting infrastructure, and the rapidly changing dynamics of market demand. This study concludes that the successful implementation of edupreneurship in vocational education in East Java is highly dependent on holistic managerial commitment, an agile curriculum design, and symbiotic collaboration with the business ecosystem. The findings of this study are expected to serve as a reference for policy makers and vocational education practitioners in designing and managing sustainable and economically impactful edupreneurship strategies.
