Title: Highly inclusive teachers’ practices in responding to all students’ learning characteristics
Abstract: Background: Although inclusive education places strong emphasis on addressing all students’ strengths and needs, the understanding of student diversity in its broadest sense remains limited. Studies exploring how inclusion is implemented tend to focus on specific groups of learners (e.g., students with SEN or those from socio-culturally disadvantaged backgrounds). However, this methodological shortcut has been repeatedly highlighted in review studies as a limitation that distorts the findings of research on inclusive education for all. To successfully address the learning characteristics of all students in heterogeneous classrooms, teachers must use inclusive practices. Aims: The aim of this research was to explore how the practices of highly inclusive teachers address all students’ learning characteristics, enabling them to learn successfully in a heterogeneous classroom. Sample: The study involved six teachers, forty-two students, and two teaching assistants. Methods: Triangulation of hundreds of hours of ethnographic observation, contextualised through various types of interviews and complemented by products written by students, allowed us to identify diverse types of student learning characteristics and teachers’ inclusive practices. Results: Our findings indicate that teachers' inclusive practices aimed at supporting student engagement, as well as determining and facilitating students' learning progress, were among the most extensively employed and addressed a wide spectrum of students’ learning characteristics. Title: From Event Logs to Process Performance Indicators via Declarative Process Mining
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Organizations increasingly rely on event logs to monitor and improve business process performance, yet identifying meaningful and measurable Process Performance Indicators (PPIs) remains a challenging and largely manual task. Recent work has shown that Large Language Models (LLMs) can support this process by suggesting, operationalizing and computing PPIs against an event log based on process descriptions and business goals. However, such approaches depend heavily on user input quality and are not explicitly grounded in observed process behavior. In this paper, we present Declare2PPI, a fully automated pipeline for generating PPIs directly from event logs. Our approach follows a bottom-up strategy in which declarative process mining extracts behavioral constraints that guide LLM-based generation. The resulting PPIs reflect process-wide execution patterns and are automatically translated into executable definitions and computed to ensure measurability. The approach also supports the exploration of multiple PPI sets and prioritizes indicators based on their relevance and variability. We evaluate the approach through a qualitative comparison with a state-of-the-art top-down method and a quantitative analysis of correctness and robustness. The results show that grounding PPI generation in observed behavior leads to more relevant, non-redundant, and consistently computable PPIs, supporting data-driven performance analysis with minimal effort. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Dynamic shelf-life prediction for foods in intelligent packaging: AI-driven multimodal sensing and closed-loop decision-making
Abstract: As conventional static shelf-life labels fail to account for environmental fluctuations across the supply chain, food waste and safety risks have become pressing challenges. Current intelligent packaging systems integrate multimodal sensing technologies, creating new opportunities for real-time monitoring of the food microenvironment. However, effectively predicting remaining shelf life (RSL) from multisource, heterogeneous sensor data—and translating these predictions into reliable decisions—remains a major research challenge. This review examines artificial intelligence (AI)-driven dynamic shelf-life prediction (DSLP) models for intelligent packaging, discusses the roles and applicability of different signal types in DSLP, and analyzes the distinct requirements of different food systems for prediction accuracy and decision-making. Compared with conventional approaches, intelligent-packaging-based DSLP models can handle diverse signal inputs more effectively and characterize food deterioration more accurately under complex environmental conditions. This review further organizes sensing evidence into environmental, state, and risk information, and clarifies three major DSLP outputs, including RSL, quality-state trajectory, and probability of spoilage. By linking these outputs with warning, inventory, distribution, and cold-chain management actions, the review highlights the transition from passive monitoring to closed-loop decision support. By integrating convolutional temporal models, multimodal fusion strategies, and interpretability analysis, intelligent packaging systems may enable multimodal-sensing-driven dynamic shelf-life updating, thereby supporting quality monitoring and evidence-based decision-making across food supply chains. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Business model, pricing, and transparency in neurosurgery and neurology journals
Abstract: The business model of scientific journals — gold open access (OA), hybrid, or subscription — creates different financial incentives for publishers, since in the author-pays OA model publication fees (Article Processing Charges, APCs) are collected upon acceptance. This descriptive audit surveys 109 neurosurgery and neurology journals from six major publishing groups (Elsevier, Springer Nature/Wolters Kluwer, Wiley, SAGE, Taylor & Francis, Thieme) and verifies, journal by journal, business model, notoriety indicator (Journal Impact Factor or Scimago SJR), publication fee, and, where publicly available, acceptance rate. Every data point was individually re-verified against official publisher pages and Scimago Journal Rank, correcting a JIF/SJR confusion, several unrecorded transitions to full OA, and one misclassified business model present in the initial collection. After verification, 83 journals (76.1%) are hybrid and 26 (23.9%) are full OA, including 5 diamond (no-APC) journals; no journal is subscription-only. Mean notoriety was similar between hybrid and full-OA journals on both indicators tested separately (JIF: 3.51 vs 3.61; SJR: 0.87 vs 0.89), but full-OA journals excluding the five diamond titles showed higher and more dispersed SJR values (mean 1.24, SD 0.93) than the diamond subset (mean 0.20, SD 0.09). Publication fees were, on average, higher for the OA option of hybrid journals ($4,279, SD $755) than for full-OA journals ($3,415, SD $845). Acceptance rate was the least transparent variable: only 6 of 109 journals (5.5%) publish an identifiable rate, all hybrid; no full-OA or diamond journal discloses this figure. This sample is too small, and too skewed toward hybrid disclosure, to support any inference about whether business model influences acceptance decisions; it instead documents a broad lack of acceptance-rate transparency across neurosurgery and neurology journals and identifies pricing, not acceptance behavior, as the dimension on which a verified between-model difference could be established. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Does artificial intelligence improve social stability risk performance in China?
Abstract: This paper examines whether and how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to improving the social stability risk level in China. Against the backdrop of rapid digital transformation and increasingly complex governance challenges, AI has been widely adopted in areas such as public security, social management, and risk monitoring. However, its actual effectiveness in mitigating social stability risks remains underexplored. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions in China, this study constructs an empirical framework to evaluate the impact of AI policy on social stability risk levels. The analysis integrates indicators of technological capacity, governance performance, and socio-economic conditions, and applies quantitative methods to identify both direct and indirect effects. The findings suggest that AI policy significantly reduces social stability risks by promoting digital economy development, increasing wage levels and investment in education. At the same time, the results reveal notable regional heterogeneity. The AI policy significantly reduces social stability risk in the central and western regions, and areas with moderate digital economy development, but has no statistically significant effect in economically developed and digitally advanced areas. The study also highlights potential challenges, including data governance concerns and uneven technological access, which may offset some of AI's benefits. This research contributes to the literature by linking technological innovation with social governance outcomes and provides policy implications for leveraging AI to promote social stability. It suggests that policymakers should not only invest in AI infrastructure but also address institutional and regional disparities to ensure inclusive and effective risk management. © 2026 The Authors

Title: HyITS: Interpretable tree-stacking framework via feature selection and hybrid resampling for imbalanced fraud detection
Abstract: Fraud detection in medical reimbursement claims and credit card transactions is challenged by high-dimensional feature spaces, extreme class imbalance, and limited interpretability of ensemble decisions. This paper presents HyITS, an interpretable tree-stacking framework for imbalanced fraud detection. HyITS comprises three stages: (1) importance-guided feature selection with sample rebalancing to compress the feature space and alleviate class imbalance; (2) a two-layer tree-stacking ensemble to enhance minority-class recognition; and (3) a hierarchical SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) post-hoc analysis to attribute predictions at both the base-learner and meta-learner levels. Extensive experiments on two highly imbalanced fraud datasets—a public benchmark and a real-world business case—demonstrate that HyITS consistently outperforms a range of state-of-the-art and representative baseline methods. Specifically, it achieves a remarkable reduction in feature dimensionality (approximately 43.3% and 59.4%, respectively) while setting new benchmarks in imbalance-sensitive metrics: on the public benchmark, AUPRC reaches 0.9375 and the F1-score attains 0.9178; on the real-world dataset, AUPRC is 0.9988 and the F1-score is 0.9689, indicating robust performance across scenarios. The SHAP analysis further identifies key risk-related features and their influence patterns, thereby significantly enhancing model auditability and providing actionable insights for decision-makers in high-stakes financial and healthcare applications. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Differential Utility of Explainable AI in Churn Mitigation
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Competitive markets are fundamentally concerned with mitigating customer churn. Although highly accurate predictive AI models are extensively utilised for this objective, they tend to act as “black boxes,” preventing businesses from translating predictive insights into clear and actionable retention strategies. There is a significant discrepancy between the predictive performance of sophisticated machine learning models (such as CatBoost or XGBoost) and their practical efficacy for managers in real-world business. While Explainable AI (XAI) methods such as SHAP and LIME have been proposed as potential solutions, the differences in their value across strategic and operational decision-making tiers are not quantified. This study provides a systematic comparison of interpretations produced by SHAP and LIME using a high-performance churn model. Within the context of the Actionability Score—a novel, business-focused metric—we measure the managerial utility of local explanations for front-line agents. We compared global feature importance ranks for strategic planning and local interpretations for operational interventions, using the Actionability Score to quantify the ratio of controllable features identified. The analysis delivers a dual utility: (1) for strategic alignment, the global explanations of SHAP and LIME are closely related and equally satisfactory for supporting higher-level strategic budgeting; (2) operationally, SHAP achieves a higher Actionability Score than LIME, demonstrating its superiority in bridging the gap between predictive modelling and front-line business intelligence. The study presents a prescriptive Dual-Level XAI Decision Framework, applying SHAP to generate trustworthy, real-time retention intervention scripts for operational success. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Multi-Task learning for predictive process monitoring with temporal graph neural networks on Object-Centric event logs
Abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) forecasts the future trajectory of ongoing process instances, including next activities and remaining execution times. While deep learning has advanced the field, modeling irregular temporal dynamics and long-range dependencies remains a significant challenge, especially within complex object-centric environments.We propose a multi-task predictive framework based on the Temporal Graph Attention Network (TGAT). By transforming object-centric event logs into temporal graphs with time-aware edges, our approach explicitly encodes continuous time intervals directly into the attention mechanism. This allows the model to capture subtle temporal irregularities often missed by sequence-based methods. A shared temporal graph encoder is jointly optimized for three critical tasks: next activity prediction, next timestamp estimation, and remaining time prediction.We evaluate our framework using four real-world BPI Challenge datasets (2014, 2016, 2017, and 2019). The results demonstrate that our model consistently outperforms or matches state-of-the-art sequence-based, graph-based, and Transformer architectures. Furthermore, attention visualizations and ablation studies confirm that integrating temporal graph modeling with multi-task learning significantly enhances predictive accuracy in complex process environments. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Generative AI use and sustainable pedagogical practices as predictors of 4Cs skill development: The mediating role of digital literacy among international postgraduate students in China
Abstract: This study examines how Generative AI Use (GAU) and Sustainable Pedagogical Practices (SPP) are associated with international postgraduate students’ critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, and communication (4Cs), with Digital Literacy (DL) examined as a mediator. Using survey data from 369 international Master’s and PhD students at China’s C9 League universities, this study applies Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) analysis. The 4Cs were modeled as a higher-order construct comprising four lower-order dimensions. The results show that both GAU and SPP are positively associated with students’ 4Cs, with SPP showing the largest standardized direct association. GAU and SPP are also positively associated with DL, which in turn is positively associated with the 4Cs. Significant indirect associations of both GAU and SPP with the higher-order 4Cs construct were observed through DL. The ANN results provide complementary predictive evidence, with SPP showing the highest normalized predictive importance, followed by GAU and DL. Together, the findings support a technology–pedagogy–capability perspective in which pedagogical design shows the largest standardized direct association with 4Cs development, while DL functions as a learner-side information-processing capability linking AI-supported and sustainability-oriented learning experiences with competence development. For practice, the findings suggest that universities may benefit from embedding generative AI within structured, sustainability-oriented learning activities that emphasize information verification, responsible use, and collaborative problem solving. Title: Mode of construction of oncoids containing early diversified calcimicrobes from the lower Cambrian Bayan Gol Formation, western Mongolia
Abstract: Oncoids, which are a type of microbialite, are widely known from the Precambrian to the present. However, the types of earliest Palaeozoic calcimicrobes within oncoids and their roles in oncoid construction are poorly understood. This study focuses on the construction of Cambrian oncoids from western Mongolia, based on microstructural types (i.e., types A–D), the variety of calcimicrobes and the abundance of fenestral fabrics. Type A microstructure is characterized by well-developed laminae and is dominated by Girvanella. Type B is similar to type A, but with an increased abundance of Kordephyton and Botomaella and with some fenestral fabrics. Type C is dominated by fenestral fabrics. Type D is markedly different from the other types, being characterized by irregular growth forms. Microstructures of types A–C exhibit gradational transitions in their laminae, calcimicrobes and fenestral fabrics, representing a continuous series that formed under changing hydrodynamic conditions. Type A was periodically overturned, forming laminated microstructures. Type C experienced episodic overturning that facilitated the development of Kordephyton and Botomaella, which contributed to the formation of fenestral fabrics and hindered the development of concentric laminae. Type B reflects conditions intermediate between those of types A and C. In contrast, type D was formed during long periods of quiescence with episodic overturning, resulting in highly irregular forms. These early Cambrian oncoids of western Mongolia are recording various microstructures with diverse calcimicrobial communities. The studied oncoids thus provide new information on how the early diversified calcimicrobes contributed to the construction of oncoids in the unique marine environment of the early Cambrian. © Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Based on window function optimization and DFT verification to establish terahertz fingerprint of triphenyl phosphate for non-destructive analysis

Abstract: Triphenyl phosphate (TPHP), an emerging pollutant with neurotoxic and reproductive toxicity, severely threatens global food safety and human health through environmental exposure risks and bioaccumulation. Title: The impact of critique on LLM-based model generation from natural language: the case of activity diagrams
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong potential for automating model generation from natural-language descriptions. A common approach begins with an initial model generation, followed by an iterative critique-refine loop in which the model is evaluated for issues and refined based on those issues. This process needs to address: (1) structural correctness – compliance with well-formedness rules – and (2) semantic alignment – accurate reflection of the intended meaning in the source text. Structural checks in LADEX can be performed either algorithmically or by an LLM, while alignment checks are performed by an LLM. We design five ablated variants of LADEX to study: (i) the impact of the critique-refine loop itself, (ii) the role of LLM-based semantic checks, and (iii) the comparative effectiveness of algorithmic versus LLM-based structural checks. To evaluate LADEX, we compare the generated activity diagrams with expert-created ground truths using both trace-based behavioural matcher and an LLM-based activity-diagram matcher. This enables automated measurement of correctness (whether the generated activity diagram includes the ground-truth nodes) and completeness (how many of the ground-truth nodes the generated activity diagram covers). Experiments on two datasets – a public-domain dataset and an industry dataset from our collaborator, Ciena – indicate that: (1) Both the behavioural and LLM matchers yield similar completeness and correctness comparisons across the LADEX variants. (2) The critique–refine loop improves structural validity, correctness, and completeness compared to single-pass generation. (3) Activity diagrams refined based on algorithmic structural checks achieve structural consistency, whereas those refined based on LLM-based checks often still show structural inconsistencies. (4) Combining algorithmic structural checks with LLM-based semantic checks (using O4 Mini) delivers the strongest results – up to 86% correctness and 92% completeness – while requiring fewer than five LLM calls on average. Title: Application of Process Mapping to Identify Nonvalue-Added Activities Associated with Formwork Labor in Reinforced Concrete Foundation Construction: A Lean Construction Study from India

Abstract: Formwork handling and assembly significantly contribute to the time and cost of reinforced cement concrete. Title: Assessing Perceived Construction Risk Allocation and Agreement under Design-Bid-Build Contracts: Evidence from a Developing Country
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: This paper examines perceived construction risk allocation under design-bid-build contracts and evaluates the degree of agreement between clients and contractors regarding which party should bear specific risks in the Indonesian construction context. Data were collected through a questionnaire survey of 53 respondents, who evaluated the allocation of 73 construction risks. Descriptive analysis based on median values was used to identify general patterns of risk allocation, while inferential analysis examined differences in perception and associations between allocation and agreement. Agreement was assessed at both the aggregate and individual risk item levels. The results indicate that contractors are perceived as bearing the majority of construction risks, and no statistically significant differences are observed between client and contractor respondents in risk allocation. Overall, allocation patterns are broadly consistent with expectations. However, several deviations are observed in which risks are partially shifted to other parties, even though they are largely within a single party's control. At the aggregate level, agreement is found to be unacceptable, with nearly half of the risks exhibiting a lack of or weak agreement, particularly for client-related and shared risks. Contractor respondents display higher levels of agreement, and risks allocated more heavily to contractors are associated with stronger agreement. These findings highlight the potential for conflict arising from disagreement in risk allocation and offer theoretical and practical implications.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Competitive anion precipitation governs corrosion product film evolution on corrosion-resistant magnesium alloys in physiological solutions
Abstract: In solutions containing Cl− as the base electrolyte, adding either H2PO4−/HPO42− or HCO3− markedly lowers the corrosion rates of Mg-Al-Y alloy wires, suppresses severe localized corrosion and promotes more uniform degradation. When both anions are present, their competitive interactions alter early corrosion product evolution and lead to a less continuous and less protective corrosion product film. Thermodynamic calculations indicate that phase accessibility depends on local pH and ion activities, while quasi-in situ FTIR reveals distinct early interfacial evolution of P- and C-containing species. Subsequent product retention may additionally depend on dissolution tendency and interfacial bonding. First-principles calculations further show that, in the selected idealized models, the carbonate-containing interface exhibits a higher Cl− migration barrier, whereas the phosphate-containing interface exhibits stronger interfacial adhesion. Title: Alleviating gradient conflict via bias disentanglement and noise suppression for robust autoencoder recommendation
Abstract: Autoencoders have been widely adopted in recommender systems due to their strong nonlinear representation capability. However, the global shared encoder parameters often lead to gradient conflicts in the parameter space when faced with heterogeneous rating samples, which undermines the training stability and personalized modeling capability of the model. To address this issue, we propose an improved autoencoder-based recommendation method integrating bias disentanglement and noise suppression. Title: How media narratives shape public sentiment toward electric micromobility: Stronger effects for e-scooters than e-bikes
Abstract: Public sentiment toward electric micromobility, particularly e-scooters and e-bikes, is increasingly shaping safety debates and regulatory responses; yet, these attitudes and perceptions have not been systematically evaluated within a unified framework, nor is it clear to what extent they reflect stable judgments versus sensitivity to external narratives. This study addresses these gaps by quantifying public sentiment toward e-bikes and e-scooters and evaluating their responsiveness to controlled negative media narrative exposure. A unified survey framework was developed to enable consistent evaluation, combining statement-based measures with image-based scenario assessments. Two complementary studies were conducted with Australian participants. Study 1 (N = 1027) established baseline sentiment in the absence of media exposure, and Study 2 (N = 1025) examined how responses shift following controlled exposure to negative news headlines. The results showed that public sentiment is multi-dimensional and mixed. While both modes received moderate recognition in terms of sustainability and legitimacy, practical acceptance remained lower, particularly for e-scooters. Exposure to negative media narratives produced broader and more consistent shifts toward less favorable sentiments for e-scooters, especially in perceptions of rider behavior and public-space interaction, whereas e-bike responses remained comparatively stable and more robust to media narrative exposure. In contrast, evaluations of concrete negative situations showed no systematic change following exposure, indicating that these evaluations are grounded in situational interpretation rather than external framing. The findings suggest that public sentiment should be used cautiously to inform policy development. While consistent concerns linked to observable safety issues justify targeted interventions, broader sentiment shifts may reflect narrative influence rather than actual conditions. Effective policy should therefore be informed not only by public sentiment but also by objective evidence on behavior, exposure, and risk. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Fan R.; Lu C.; Liu X.; Yao Y.; Fan A.; Yang X.
Title: Spatial optimization of land use for synergizing economic development and carbon neutrality based on an efficiency-driven PLUS model
Abstract: Optimizing land-use allocation is important for achieving regional carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality targets. Existing land-use simulation studies generally incorporate carbon objectives through ex-post assessment or macro-level land-demand optimization, leaving historical grid-level carbon–economic performance disconnected from future spatial allocation. To further address this limitation, we developed LUCE-PLUS, a framework that links grid-scale land-transition accounting and efficiency evaluation with PLUS-based spatial simulation. Using Jiujiang City, China, as a case study, we quantified conversion costs, economic-output changes, and carbon emissions induced by observed land-use transitions from 2010 to 2020 at a 30-m resolution. A single-stage mixed-integer linear programming super-efficiency range-adjusted measure (Sup-RAM) model treated carbon emissions as a weakly disposable undesirable output and enabled discrimination among efficient grid-level transition units while ensuring Pareto-efficient projections. The resulting surfaces of economic efficiency and carbon–economic synergy efficiency were incorporated into PLUS as scenario-specific predictors of land-use expansion probabilities. Land-use patterns in 2030 were simulated under natural-development, economic-dominant, and carbon–economic dual-objective scenarios while aggregate land demand and planning constraints were held constant. Mean carbon–economic synergy efficiency was 20.5% lower than mean economic efficiency, indicating that economic efficiency alone may understate the carbon-related environmental costs of land-use transitions. Compared with the dual-objective scenario, the economic-dominant scenario increased the projected GDP increment by only 0.04% but raised land-use-change-induced carbon emissions by 7.3%. Impervious-land expansion under the dual-objective scenario also showed a stronger tendency toward locations associated with lower carbon-stock losses. LUCE-PLUS therefore provides a performance-informed approach to low-carbon spatial allocation under fixed land-demand targets. From an environmental impact assessment perspective, the framework could support alternatives analysis in strategic environmental assessment of territorial spatial plans by enabling ex ante comparison of projected land-use patterns, carbon-stock changes, and economic outcomes under consistent planning constraints. © 2026

Title: Towards a Meta-model for Complex Performance Indicators: A Systematic Literature Review and an Illustration in the Cardiology Domain

Abstract: Complex Performance Indicators (CPIs) aggregate heterogeneous data streams into multidimensional constructs supporting strategic decision-making, yet their engineering remains fundamentally challenging. Title: Design and Implementation of a Service Scheduling Mechanism for Ship Task Scheduling
Abstract: In modern naval operations, ship formations need to realize cross-platform coordination (e.g., anti-aircraft, anti-submarine, and maritime strike), and the traditional single-orchestration paradigm service orchestration technology has gradually shown its limitations in the face of complex business challenges such as long transaction coordination, real-time event response, and dynamic business rule changes. Define unified model elements and combination mechanism, which include service nodes, event triggers, business rules, compensation processors and contexts, and realize flexible declarative description of complex business logic. We design a YAML-based rule description language (DSL) to support business people to define hybrid orchestration logic in a near-natural language, and propose dynamic coordination strategies such as main process-driven branch event processing and event-triggered process fragments. Compared with the traditional single-orchestration paradigm, the development and maintenance workload is reduced by more than 50%, the additional performance overhead is controlled within 150 ms, the peak processing capacity is increased by 20%, and the operational efficiency is increased by 90%. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Microstructure and bulk rheology of heat-induced emulsion-filled pea protein gels: Effect of high-pressure homogenization
Abstract: High-pressure homogenization (HPH) is often applied to process protein-stabilized emulsions. However, it remains unclear how HPH affects the interactions between protein-gel matrix and interfacial protein-coated oil or fat droplets, as well as the consequent network breakdown of the system. Small amplitude oscillatory shear (SAOS) temperature sweeps showed that gels containing 10% lipid were not significantly stiffer than gels without lipid, and their large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS) strain-amplitude sweeps showed similar yield points, yielding regimes and flow points. At 20% lipid, gel stiffness decreased notably, and yielding began at lower strain amplitude (γ0[jls-end-space/]). In contrast, HPH markedly increased gel stiffness, with further stiffening at higher lipid contents. Meanwhile, these gels yielded at lower γ0 over a broader range at higher lipid contents, and their loss modulus overshoot coincided with the rise in shear-thickening ratio. Moreover, sequence of physical processes (SPP) analysis showed that, as γ0 increased, the deltoid area changed more dramatically for 20% oil than for 20% fat, indicating that HPH shifted interfacial protein-coated lipid droplets from inactive fillers to active fillers that integrate into gradually yielding, denser networks. Fat droplets were more resistant to stretching and rupturing than oil droplets. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A reinforcement learning-guided hyper-heuristic algorithm for cold chain distribution planning
Abstract: Cold chain distribution requires routing decisions that meet service requirements while accounting for operating costs and environmental performance. Because routing choices directly affect travel cost, refrigeration energy use, and carbon emissions, effective planning is essential for sustainable cold chain operations. To address this routing problem, this study proposes a hybrid reinforcement learning-guided hyper-heuristic algorithm (HRL-HHA) that adaptively selects and combines search operators to improve search performance and reduce premature convergence. The proposed dual-layer framework enhances solution quality by coordinating intra- and inter-route search, while the parallel batch Tabu search procedure improves computational efficiency. In addition, we compare six RL-guided HHA variants, including five single-RL variants and a hybrid RL variant. This comparison allows us to examine how different RL-based heuristic selection strategies influence HHA performance. Across the benchmark instances, the proposed method achieves better results than the best solutions reported in the literature. In a real-world case study, it reduces travel distance by approximately 30% and total cost by more than 35%. Title: Natural Hazards, Critical Infrastructure Systems, and Resilience Enhancement: A Structured State-of-the-Art Review and a Synthesis-Based Rapid Assessment Framework
Abstract: Critical infrastructure systems (CISs) are increasingly exposed to natural hazards whose impacts are amplified by infrastructure interdependence, urban complexity, and the growing prevalence of compound and cascading events. Existing research provides valuable insights into individual hazards, infrastructure components, modeling methods, and resilience metrics, but these insights remain difficult to translate into preliminary decision support because they are organized across different hazard types, sectors, analytical scales, and decision contexts. This article presents a structured state-of-the-art review of natural hazards, CIS impacts, and resilience enhancement. A two-pathway review strategy was adopted. A Web of Science (WoS) core search was used to characterize the bibliometric landscape and identify WoS-sourced core synthesis studies, while a targeted anchor-search pathway was used to verify foundational concepts, hazard mechanisms, methodological approaches, resilience frameworks, and authoritative institutional sources. The review clarifies the conceptual distinction among dependencies, interdependencies, compound hazards, cascading failures, service disruption, and resilience; synthesizes cross-hazard infrastructure impact mechanisms; compares major method families for hazard-impact and resilience assessment; and develops a synthesis-derived rapid resilience assessment framework for preliminary screening and prioritization under constrained data and time conditions. The synthesis indicates that future CIS resilience assessment would benefit from moving beyond isolated asset-damage analysis toward integrated workflows that link hazard loading, component vulnerability, network functionality, service consequences, recovery capacity, uncertainty, and feasible intervention choices. The article contributes a more transparent evidence-source structure, an evidence-to-decision bridge, and a bounded decision-oriented framework for organizing future research and practical resilience screening.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: When imperfect food meets joint consumption: a social influence perspective
Abstract: Drawing on social influence theory, this research examines the interaction effect of food appearance (imperfect vs. perfect) and consumption context (solo vs. joint) on consumers' preferences. Across five experiments, we show that a joint (vs. solo) consumption context exacerbates the reduction in consumers' purchase intention toward imperfect food. In addition, perceived risk and purchase embarrassment mediate this interaction effect on both purchase intention and willingness to pay (WTP). We further identify self-construal and discount information as boundary conditions. Regarding self-construal, for consumers with an interdependent self-construal, joint consumption amplifies the effect of imperfect appearance on perceived risk, purchase embarrassment, and purchase intention. In contrast, for those with an independent self-construal, these amplifying effects are not significant. In terms of discount information, when it is displayed, joint consumption amplifies the effect of imperfect appearance on perceived risk, purchase embarrassment, and purchase intention. When it is absent, however, only the effect on purchase intention remains, albeit attenuated. Finally, the presence of discount information shifts the underlying mechanisms of the interaction toward greater reliance on indirect pathways. This research offers practical guidance for promoting suboptimal food in joint consumption contexts. © 2026

Title: A critical analysis on homomorphic searchable encryption architectures and security models over multi-medium data
Abstract: Cloud computing has become a dominant platform for large-scale data storage and processing; however, outsourcing sensitive information to untrusted cloud servers introduces major privacy and security concerns. Homomorphic-based searchable encryption enables secure search and computation over encrypted data without revealing plaintext contents or query information. This paper presents a systematic survey of homomorphic-based SE schemes for multimedia data including text, audio, and image representations. Cloud computing is now a major data storage and processing platform, but sharing sensitive data with external organizations on semi-trusted cloud servers poses significant privacy and security issues. Homomorphic SE allows for secure search via computation on encrypted data without disclosure of the plaintext data or the information of the query. This paper provides a systematic survey of SE schemes for multimedia data such as text, audio and image representations that are based on homomorphic operations. The study offers a comprehensive analysis of homomorphic encryption techniques employed in cloud-assisted retrieval systems. Special focus is given to the security of search patterns, access pattern protection, probabilistic trapdoor generation, privacy preservation, and formal security models such as IND-CPA, IND-CKA, semantic security, forward as well as backward privacy and ORAM-assisted retrieval. The research also covers emerging architectures like MPC-assisted search, FHE-ORAM hybrid architectures, as well as recent developments in FHE acceleration using GPU-based implementations and hardware-assisted optimizations. Title: Why Behavioral Representations Matter: A Framework for Comparing Their Expressiveness in Business Process Analysis
Abstract: Behavioral representations are a fundamental abstraction mechanism in process mining, where an event log is abstracted into a set of behaviors in preparation for a subsequent analysis task, such as process discovery, log-delta analysis or concept drift. However, the choice of representation directly determines which behavioral distinctions remain observable in downstream analysis, yet no formal framework exists to compare representations with respect to this criterion. Consequently, the expressive capabilities and limitations of behavioral representations are undefined, impeding assessment of the quality and completeness of downstream analysis results. In this paper, we propose a framework for formally comparing the expressiveness and information preservation of behavioral representations. We introduce losslessness as a criterion for information preservation, refinement to capture when one representation subsumes the discriminative power of another, and incomparability when neither subsumes the other. We apply the framework to five representations commonly used in process mining. Our results show that representations differ not only in granularity but also in the behavioral dimensions they capture. In addition, commonly used representations are often orthogonal in their expressivity, showing the importance of selecting the most suitable representation for a particular task, as there is currently no single best representation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Abstract: This research investigates the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in augmenting Business Intelligence (BI) capabilities within e-commerce platforms. Authors: Zheng L.
Title: Teaching by example? Teacher ICT use and middle school students’ computer and information literacy across China and the United States
Abstract: Background: In the digital era, Computer and Information Literacy (CIL) has become a crucial educational outcome. While teacher Information and Communication Technology (ICT) use is widely promoted to enhance student digital skills, its effectiveness may vary significantly across different national education systems. Aims: This study investigates the impact of teacher ICT use on middle school students' CIL in China and the United States. It aims to compare these cross-national effects and examine the mediating roles of school ICT resources and institutional support in shaping these relationships. Methods: Using nationally representative data from the International Computer and Information Literacy Study (ICILS) 2023, this research employs regression models and instrumental variable (2SLS) methods to address potential endogeneity. Mediation analyses further explore how school-level factors transmit teacher ICT effects. Results: The analysis reveals striking cross-country differences: in China, all dimensions of teacher ICT use significantly improved students' CIL, whereas these effects were statistically insignificant in the United States. School ICT resources and support fully mediated teacher ICT effects in China but only partially mediated ability effects in the U.S. Additionally, student background factors consistently influenced CIL across both countries. Conclusion: While teacher ICT experience demonstrates universal importance, the broader impact of instructional ICT practices depends critically on national context and institutional support systems. The findings highlight the complex interplay between teacher practices, school resources, and national educational environments in shaping digital literacy outcomes. © 2026

Title: Plasmon-assisted and electrostatic-driven photocatalysis at the sharp tips of au nano-bipyramids in aqueous phase
Source title: Spectrochimica Acta - Part A: Molecular and Biomolecular Spectroscopy
Abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) combined with plasmonic photocatalysis is an effective method for the in-situ analysis of molecular reaction mechanism, which has been widely employed to study the transformation process and reaction mechanism of azobenzene molecules. However, achieving highly sensitive monitoring of reactant molecules and precisely controlling the catalytic products remain significant challenges. In this study, citrate-capped gold nanobipyramids (cit-Au NBPs) were used as the plasmonic substrate, which not only utilize the “lightning rod effect” at the tips of the bipyramids to construct an extremely strong localized electric field, but also precisely drive positively charged reactants (such as p- nitroaniline) to the catalytic region at the tips through electrostatic adsorption by the negatively charged citrate on the surface. Based on this synergistic effect, the highly sensitive in-situ SERS monitoring of complex reaction process was achieved. Specifically, the plasmon-driven oxidative coupling and reduction process of p- nitroaniline under light irradiation and after the addition of NaBH4 were clearly defined. Furthermore, comparative studies on nanoparticles with different morphologies and surface ligands demonstrated the critical roles of tip-induced plasmonic enhancement and electrostatic driving in this highly efficient catalytic system. In addition, the feasibility and promising selectivity of this strategy were verified by the catalysis of p- aminophenol and o- phenylenediamine. This strategy significantly improves the efficiency of plasmonic catalysis and the SERS detection sensitivity of trace intermediates, providing an excellent platform for in-situ monitoring of complex and rapid catalytic reactions. Authors: Qian Q.; Zhang L.; Chen S.
Title: Institutional clearing priorities, behavioral feedback, and systemic fragility in dynamic multilayer real–financial networks
Abstract: Modern real–financial systems are increasingly exposed to cross-sector contagion, where shocks originating in the real economy may be transformed into banking-sector fragility. A key yet underexplored driver of this transformation is institutional clearing priority, namely the creditor hierarchy governing loss allocation upon default. This study develops a dynamic tri-layer contagion engine that integrates firm trade-credit networks, bank–firm lending, and interbank exposures into a configurable simulation-based stress-testing framework. Alternative clearing priority regimes—bank-first, firm-first, and pari passu—are implemented as institutional modules, enabling controlled counterfactual analysis under identical network structures and shock environments. The system executes a round-based contagion cycle that combines default identification, priority-based clearing, multilayer loss propagation, behavioral feedback, endogenous network updating, and joint stabilization checking. Using Monte Carlo simulations, the framework produces decision-oriented outputs capturing cross-layer loss routing, the Cross-layer Loss Transformation Index (CLTI), default allocation, systemic amplification, tail risk, and stabilization dynamics. The results show that the systemic relevance of corporate distress depends strongly on shock scope and network position. More importantly, clearing priority operates primarily as an institutional loss-routing and systemic-burden allocation mechanism: it determines whether firm-originated losses remain concentrated in trade-credit networks or are transformed into banking-sector stress. Behavioral feedback and network adaptation affect the adjustment path and persistence of contagion, but do not overturn the loss-routing role of creditor hierarchy. The analysis further shows that clearing priority generates more visible differences in systemic-burden allocation than in aggregate amplification, implying that aggregate risk measures may conceal important redistribution effects across real and financial layers. Overall, the proposed framework positions creditor hierarchy as a configurable institutional input in comparative stress-testing analysis, providing decision-relevant insights for systemic risk assessment and institutional stress testing in interconnected real–financial networks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Toward carbon-neutral desalination: Scope 1–3 carbon accounting, technological pathways, circular resource recovery, and future perspectives
Abstract: Desalination is increasingly essential for addressing global water scarcity, particularly in arid and semiarid regions with limited conventional freshwater resources. However, the process remains energy-intensive, making its environmental sustainability heavily dependent on the carbon intensity of its operational energy supply. As global climate mitigation accelerates, carbon-neutral desalination has emerged as a critical objective to align future water supply systems with net-zero emission targets. This review evaluates recent progress, key challenges, and technological pathways for reducing the carbon footprint of desalination systems. It first examines the main carbon drivers of desalination, identifying operational electricity consumption as the dominant source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, especially in reverse osmosis systems. Furthermore, this review evaluates desalination-related emissions using a Scope 1–3 GHG accounting framework, highlighting the growing importance of indirect life cycle emissions from membranes, chemicals, infrastructure, and brine management. Life cycle assessment (LCA) studies indicate that desalinated water generates approximately 1–3 kg CO2-eq m−3, depending on the electricity mix, plant efficiency, and system configuration. The review also discusses major carbon-reduction pathways, including renewable energy integration, energy recovery devices (ERDs), advanced membranes, process optimization, digital control, and emerging low-carbon desalination technologies. Solar- and wind-powered desalination systems represent key near-term strategies for reducing operational emissions, while advances in ERDs and membrane materials continue to lower specific energy consumption. Emerging technologies, including membrane distillation, forward osmosis, electrodialysis, and capacitive deionization, can further support low-carbon desalination in applications involving low-grade heat, brackish water, wastewater reuse, or decentralized treatment. Furthermore, sustainable brine management, zero-liquid-discharge systems, and resource recovery are highlighted as key components of circular desalination. Despite recent progress, carbon-neutral desalination remains constrained by renewable energy intermittency, high capital costs, limited full-scale demonstrations, energy-intensive brine treatment, and the lack of standardized Scope 1–3 carbon-accounting frameworks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Prices and prevention: decomposing the Norwegian salmon cost explosion, 2016–2024
Abstract: Production cost in Norwegian salmon farming roughly doubled between 2016 and 2024, reversing two decades of decline, and the standard explanation is a “biological treadmill” of sea lice and disease. Using firm-level data from the Norwegian Directorate of Fisheries' profitability survey, I decompose the increase and ask whether biology raises cost through damage or through prevention. Two engines dominate. Global feed-price inflation accounts for about a third of the rise, with the feed-conversion ratio almost unchanged. At least a fifth is associated with the cost of managing biological risk, which surfaces as prevention rather than damage: a shift to post-smolt—juveniles reared nearly twice as large on land, at roughly triple the cost per fish, to shorten the lice-exposed sea phase—while feed conversion and harvest weight change little. A stochastic cost frontier provides a complementary check: returns to scale are mild, technical regress is modest, and firm-level inefficiency is small and stable. The cost of biological risk in the accounts is preventive investment, visible in the smolt line rather than in fish-health costs or a collapse in productivity. © 2026

Title: Corruption and capital investment: Worldwide evidence
Abstract: Can international anti-corruption monitoring stimulate private investment? We examine staggered reviews across jurisdictions under the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), using firm-year observations from 84 economies over 2003–2023. We document that reviews are followed by improvements in economy-level corruption-control indicators. Local-projections difference-in-differences estimates indicate that reviews raise firms' capital expenditure relative to assets by 1.2126 percentage points, equivalent to 20% of the sample mean. Dynamic estimates show no systematic pre-review adjustment, and the result is robust to influential-economy exclusions, economy-level reweighting, alternative sample restrictions, lagged-outcome controls, and alternative staggered-adoption estimators. Investment responses are stronger in high-corruption economies and developing economies and among firms that are more financially constrained, government dependent, domestically concentrated, or reliant on irreversible capital. These patterns are consistent with international oversight reducing corruption-related institutional risk, financing frictions, and the value of delaying investment. UNCAC reviews are also followed by increases in employment, R&D investment, and leverage. Additional analyses provide no evidence that the increase in investment is accompanied by a systematic decline in investment efficiency. Overall, the findings show that a non-punitive international peer-review mechanism can affect firms’ real activity, particularly where initial institutional frictions are greater. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Exploring Italian consumer perceptions and acceptance of innovative foods and food technologies: insights from a national survey
Abstract: Innovative foods and food technologies face barriers to adoption in Italy, where food plays a central role in identity and social life. This study investigates Italian consumer responses to seven innovative food products and technologies using a consumer survey (N = 2000), stratified by age, gender, and geographical region. The survey included psychometric scales assessing food neophobia, food technology neophobia, disgust sensitivity, trust, sensation seeking, and health interest. It measured perceptions of risk, benefit, familiarity, and emotions associated with each product. Findings indicate that Italian consumers show high levels of food and technological neophobia, coupled with low trust and strong health concerns. Acceptability varied significantly across sociodemographic groups: higher education and income were associated with higher trust and sensation seeking and lower neophobia, whereas female and older respondents exhibited higher disgust sensitivity and greater resistance to innovation. Exploratory clustering identified two broad clusters of aggregated consumer profiles. One cluster was associated with younger age, higher educational attainment and household income, together with greater trust and sensation seeking, whereas the other was associated with older age, lower educational attainment and household income, together with greater food and food technology neophobia and disgust sensitivity. Emotional responses emerged as correlates of acceptability, with curiosity most positively and disgust most negatively. Products most aligned with product ideals were plant-based proteins, algae, and unusual fruits, while insect-based proteins and cultured meat faced the greatest barriers. These findings highlight the importance of reinforcing trust and curiosity while addressing disgust to promote sustainable Italian food innovation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Life Cycle Assessment of open single-shield Tunnel Boring Machine Tunnelling: An Integrated Parametric Exploration Framework
Abstract: A large-scale parametric Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approach for TBM tunnelling was developed based on a database of 525 tunnels excavated with Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs). This framework is intended as an early-stage environmental decision-support tool. System boundaries encompass the TBM life cycle, from manufacturing to End-of-Life, including the operational phase. Two existing parametric models, both dependent on TBM control parameters and geotechnical conditions, were integrated: one estimating excavation electricity consumption and the other assessing disc cutter wear. Parameters were sampled using Sobol’ sequences across 525 TBM-specific experimental designs of 41,984 runs each, yielding approximately 22 million tunnelling configurations and ensuring quasi-uniform coverage of the parameter space. A Sobol’ sensitivity analysis quantified each parameter's contribution to the variance of environmental indicators. Regarding climate change, results show that environmental impacts range from 2.8 to 29.7 tCO2eq per linear metre of tunnel. A Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA) using Sobol’ indices identified 12 to 16 parameters explaining from 84% to 96% of the variance across the four most impactful normalised indicators: the abiotic depletion potential of fossil resources (ADP fossils), the freshwater eutrophication potential (FEP), the global warming potential (GWP), and the abiotic depletion potential of metals and minerals (ADP metals/minerals). The most influential parameters fell into four categories: construction material-related parameters (cement content of segments and two-component grout, reinforcement ratio of segments); TBM manufacturing recycling-related parameters (reuse rates of valuable components and metallic structures); TBM control parameters (penetration rate and utilisation rate) and abrasivity-related geological parameters (Cutter Life Index and quartz content). Results also demonstrate that TBM manufacturing – often overlooked in TBM tunnelling LCAs – represents a significant contributor to environmental impacts. © 2026

Authors: Wang Y.; Liu X.; Deng Y.; Xiao H.; Zhang Y.
Title: Gendering conversational AI in human–AI interaction: The role of interaction context and sexist ideology in shaping user evaluations
Abstract: As human–AI interaction becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, users often infer social identities from AI systems, including gender. Moving beyond the conventional view of AI gender as a static, designer-assigned attribute, this study conceptualizes AI gender as a user-constructed perception shaped by contextual cues. Integrating social role theory, the stereotype content model, and ambivalent sexism theory, we conducted a 2 (AI gender cues: male vs. female) × 3 (interaction context: service-oriented, warm-authoritative, vs. serious-authoritative) between-subjects experiment with Chinese participants (N = 833) to examine how interaction context, perceived AI gender, and sexist ideology jointly shape evaluations of AI competence, warmth, and trustworthiness. The results showed that interaction context significantly influenced gender attribution, with the serious-authoritative condition eliciting stronger gender categorization and a masculinization bias regardless of assigned gender cues. The evaluative consequences of perceived AI gender were also context-dependent: perceived femininity consistently linked with warmth, but was associated with competence and trustworthiness primarily in the serious-authoritative condition. Hostile and benevolent sexism further moderated these relationships in distinct ways. By shifting attention from designed gender to perceived gender, this study offers a more process-oriented account of AI anthropomorphism and demonstrates the value of integrating the stereotype content model with ambivalent sexism theory to explain bias in human–AI evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: An enhanced polar lights optimizer with the near-distance to multi-target strategy and rebound boundary handling for feature selection
Abstract: Feature selection can improve predictive accuracy and reduce computational cost in high-dimensional data analysis. However, wrapper-based methods may converge prematurely when the associated discrete search space is large. This study integrates a near-distance to multi-target (NDM) strategy and a rebound boundary handling (RBH) mechanism into the polar lights optimizer (PLO), yielding NPLO. NDM introduces a proximity-aware auxiliary objective for environmental selection, whereas RBH preserves directional information through mirror reflection at a violated bound. On the 12 IEEE CEC 2022 functions, NPLO obtained the best Friedman average ranks of 2.5833 against 11 baseline algorithms and 1.7500 against 11 enhanced competitors, although alternative algorithms remained superior on individual functions. Search-trajectory and population-diversity analyses further characterize its exploration–exploitation behavior. A binary implementation, bNPLO, was evaluated for feature selection on 24 datasets with eight established binary metaheuristics. It achieved the lowest or tied-lowest classification error on most datasets while generally retaining compact feature subsets. These results support the competitiveness of NPLO on the evaluated continuous and discrete problems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Sensing the path forward: AI as amplifier in sensory and consumer science
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how sensory and consumer data are collected, analyzed, and used. A common fear is that algorithms will displace trained panels and that predictive models will replace expert judgment. We argue the opposite: as AI automates what is easy to formalize, the value of what only humans can do (embodied sensing, cultural interpretation, ethical judgment, and meaning-making) rises. This paper is not a systematic review. It advocates a particular perspective (AI as amplifier of sensory expertise), informed by on-the-ground experience through the recent rise of large language models, including what has worked and what has not in practice. Three industry case studies from PepsiCo, Danone, and Kenvue support that perspective. The principles (knowledge management, automation, predictive modeling, people-centered adoption; humans in the loop; culture before algorithms) are meant to apply beyond large companies, including academia and smaller groups. That perspective also guided a selective literature reading focused on Food Quality and Preference and related journals, mainly from 2022 to early 2026. We clarify what AI is and is not, trace the path from chemometrics to neuromorphic sensing, and describe a four-pillar framework from a Pangborn 2025 industry workshop. Self-reported case outcomes include up to 50% faster analysis and a 75% reduction in reporting time; calculation details were not disclosed to us and the figures are not independently validated. The three organizations built the same capabilities in different orders and met the same barriers (culture, talent, IT collaboration). We also propose narrative-driven analysis with large language models and a near-term research agenda. Central message: when machines predict, humans must decide. © 2026

Title: A multi-physics configuration space framework for tool abrasive wear evolution and predictive modeling in longitudinal–torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling of carbon fiber–reinforced polymers
Abstract: Addressing the challenges of complex wear evolution and long-term prediction accuracy in longitudinal-torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling of carbon fiber-reinforced polymers (LTUAM-CFRP), this study proposes a novel cutting edge configuration theory and establishes a configuration-space framework for wear morphology evolution. The framework provides a unified parametric physical abstraction of cutting edge geometry, enabling consistent characterization of the coupled evolution of rake-face wear, flank-face wear, and edge radius transformation. A contact state-space model is developed to describe high-frequency fiber–tool interface separation behavior under ultrasonic modulation. A stepwise wear modeling strategy integrating impact wear and abrasive wear is further established, revealing the outward evolution of impact wear from the contact region and the continuous accumulation of abrasive wear along the cutting edge. Furthermore, an error-feedback adaptive hybrid wear accumulation framework is constructed by combining cutting edge configuration and a process-aware deep learning network for multi-scale feature fusion. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed method achieves multi-cycle wear prediction accuracy of 95.32%, which is improved to 98.36% after process-aware correction, confirming the robustness and predictive capability of the framework for intelligent wear perception in LTUAM-CFRP machining. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Sensitive Data Protection for Text-to-SQL Tasks in Large Language Models
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) dominate Text-to-SQL tasks thanks to strong language comprehension. Yet domain adaptation demands knowledge distillation and supervised fine-tuning, which usually rely on real business queries full of sensitive information. Direct training on such data brings severe privacy leakage risks. We design a privacy-preserving framework combining data desensitization and knowledge distillation, working in two stages. First, a desensitization pipeline builds rule sets from security standards, uses an LLM to detect sensitive content, and runs context-aware desensitization that retains business logic while wiping private details. Second, a teacher model generates SQL from desensitized text to build high-quality training samples, which fine-tunes a lightweight student model to inherit domain skills without privacy hazards. Title: SCREEN-LCA: Ex-ante prioritization of bio-based pathways for chemicals and plastics under a climate-mitigation objective
Abstract: Life cycle assessment (LCA) is a key tool for guiding circular bioeconomy strategies, including the substitution of fossil carbon with bioresources. However, its data- and time-intensive nature can hinder its use when there are numerous candidate pathways, particularly in the chemical sector. Here, we developed SCREEN-LCA, a stepwise ex-ante framework designed to prioritize case studies before conducting full LCA. The framework combines: (i) sector-level impact estimation; (ii) identification of hotspot products within targeted sectors; (iii) mapping of corresponding alternative bio-based pathways; and (iv) pathway prioritization based on multiple criteria. We applied SCREEN-LCA in a France-oriented demonstration to prioritize residual-biomass-based pathways for subsequent LCA. The greenhouse gas footprint of incumbent petrochemicals and plastics, feedstock compatibility, and technological maturity were used as screening criteria. An extensive graph database covering 50 hotspot products and their alternative bio-based routes was assembled. Ethylene, propylene, methanol, and PET emerged as priorities with promising bio-based alternatives. Authors: Pan H.; Wang R.; Zou N.; Liu D.; Ma J.
Title: Cascading failure and robustness in supply chain networks: A case study of new energy vehicles
Abstract: The increasing complexity and vulnerability of new energy vehicle supply chain networks (NEVSNs) pose significant challenges to sustaining industrial robustness and mitigating cascading risks. This study evaluates the robustness of NEVSNs under multi-source disturbances, emphasizing the interactive roles of innovation capability, resource dependence, and network heterogeneity in collectively enhancing supply chain robustness. A dynamic four-layer directed weighted network model is developed to integrate these factors, incorporating a load-capacity interaction mechanism and probabilistic node failure to simulate cascading disruptions. Empirical data from Chinese NEV manufacturers and core suppliers are used for calibration and validation. Simulation results reveal that (1) enhancing innovation improves network efficiency and redundancy, while high resource dependence and centralization increase fragility; (2) battery and critical component suppliers are most sensitive to shocks, while network resilience is strengthened by diversified resources and collaboration; and (3) the proposed robustness metrics better capture vulnerability and recovery than conventional measures. These findings offer insights and recommendations for risk mitigation, network optimization, and robustness enhancement in NEV supply chains. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Author full names: Bruzzone, Federico (60122330800); Cazzola, Walter (6602449966); Favini, Luca (60413751400)
Title: Prioritizing configuration relevance via compiler-based refined feature ranking
Abstract: Modern programming languages, most notably Rust, offer advanced linguistic constructs for building highly configurable software systems as aggregations of features—identified by a configuration. However, they pose substantial challenges for program analysis, optimization, and testing, as the combinatorial explosion of configurations often makes exhaustive exploration infeasible. In this manuscript, we present the first compiler-based method for prioritizing configurations. Our approach consists of four main steps: (1) extracting a tailored intermediate representation from the Rust compiler, (2) constructing two complementary graph-based data structures—a feature dependency graph capturing inter-feature code-level dependencies weighted by predicate structure, and an atom dependency tree encoding the extent of code governed by each feature—, (3) using centrality measures to rank features, and (4) refining the ranking by considering the extent of code they impact. A fixed number of most relevant configurations are generated based on the achieved feature ranking. The validity of the generated configurations is guaranteed by using a SAT solver that takes a representation of feature dependencies in conjunctive normal form. We formalized this approach and implemented it in a prototype, RUSTYEX, by instrumenting the Rust compiler. An empirical evaluation on higher-ranked open-source Rust projects shows that RUSTYEX efficiently generates user-specified sets of configurations within bounded resources, while ensuring soundness by construction. The results demonstrate that centrality-guided configuration prioritization enables practical exploration of large configuration spaces, and we discuss the implications and open challenges for future configuration-aware analysis and optimization. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The neglected dimension: Arousal, emotions and product choices
Abstract: This article presents an overview of the ways in which arousal may be an important influence on consumer product choices. Authors: Dai J.; Ni P.; Su K.; Zhu J.; Wu W.; Du D.-Z.
Title: Influence maximization in online social networks: Models, algorithms, and trustworthy decision-making
Abstract: Influence Maximization (IM) in online social networks has traditionally been formulated as selecting a budgeted set of seed users to maximize expected spread under a diffusion model. This classical view enabled foundational hardness, submodularity, and approximation results, but it is increasingly insufficient for realistic online social systems, where users differ in behaviors and opinions, networks evolve, diffusion is context-dependent, objectives go beyond coverage, and influence may generate negative, unfair, privacy-sensitive, or harmful consequences. This survey provides a unified review of IM from the perspective of trustworthy influence decision-making. We first develop a six-layer Online Social Influence-Maximization Stack that links network representation, behavior and context, diffusion mechanisms, objective design, algorithmic optimization, and governance. We then synthesize diffusion and objective models through a model–objective–algorithm perspective, covering classical, context-aware, behavioral, economic, opinion-aware, competitive, harm-aware, and learned diffusion settings. Next, we compare algorithmic paradigms ranging from greedy and lazy-greedy methods to sampling, sketching, mathematical programming, evolutionary search, non-submodular search, learning-based seed selection, and adaptive policies, with respect to their theoretical guarantees, time and space complexity, and information requirements. We further discuss realistic online social network settings, including dynamics, heterogeneity, multiplexity, cyber–physical contexts, partial observability, and group-level influence. Finally, we identify robustness, fairness, privacy, harm control, causal validity, explainability, accountability, benchmarking, datasets, and reproducibility as central requirements for next-generation IM, with particular attention to their interaction with scalability. Across these developments, four tensions recur: realism versus tractability, prediction versus optimization, observability and privacy versus scalable estimation, and trustworthiness versus scalability. This survey argues that IM should be understood as trustworthy, adaptive, and utility-aware influence decision-making in complex social systems, rather than as spread-only seed selection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Li T.; Liu X.; Lei J.; Zhang X.
Title: WGLE: Backdoor-free and multi-bit black-box watermarking for graph neural networks
Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are increasingly deployed, making ownership verification critical for protecting their intellectual property against model theft. Fingerprinting and black-box watermarking are two main methods. However, the former relies on determining model similarity, which is computationally expensive and prone to ownership collisions after model post-processing. The latter embeds backdoors, exposing watermarked models to the risk of backdoor attacks. Moreover, both previous methods enable ownership verification but do not convey additional information, limiting verification efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes WGLE, a novel black-box watermarking paradigm for GNNs that enables embedding the multi-bit string in GNN models without using backdoors. WGLE builds on a key insight we term Layer-wise Distance Difference on an Edge (LDDE), which quantifies the difference between the feature distance and the prediction distance of two connected nodes in a graph. By assigning unique LDDE values to the edges and employing the LDDE sequence as the watermark, WGLE supports multi-bit capacity without relying on backdoor mechanisms. We evaluated WGLE on six public datasets across six mainstream GNN architectures. Compared to state-of-the-art GNN watermarking and fingerprinting methods, WGLE achieves perfect ownership verification accuracy with marginal fidelity degradation and exhibits robust resilience against potential ownership attacks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhang M.; Chang I.-S.; Guo Y.; Zhang H.; Wu J.
Title: Study on the effects of policy intervention on lithium-ion batteries recycling industry via an innovative AI-enabled dynamic business model
Abstract: With the rapid expansion of the electric vehicle (EV) market, a large number of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have gradually become a serious threat to resource conservation and environmental management. Proper and effective recycling of spent LIBs requires not only coordinated value chain operations but also policy instruments capable of steering industrial behavior and optimizing resource allocation. Thus, this study develops an artificial intelligence-enhanced dynamic business model (AI-DBM) that integrates system dynamics, the business model canvas, and AI-based analytical methods, addressing the limitations of existing policy analysis in characterizing business model logic and explaining the mechanisms underlying policy effect. Taking China's LIBs recycling industry as an empirical case, this study systematically and quantitatively evaluates the dynamic impacts of six policy intervention strategies, including collection subsidy, tax incentives, promoting repurposing, integrating into carbon trade market, recycling technology-driven, and mixed policies, on value chain performance, profit distribution, and industrial sustainability. Results reveal pronounced heterogeneity and nonlinear responses across value-chain stakeholders under different policies. While single policy instruments improve performance in specific segments to varying degrees and exhibit clear nonlinear marginal effects, coordinated implementation of multiple policies proves more conducive to the development of the LIBs recycling industry, boosting industry's net profit to 123.20 billion RMB by 2040 and driving collection recycling rate beyond 50%, substantially outperforming any single policy and signaling a structural upgrade of the recycling system. Overall, dynamically coordinated and diversified policy portfolios are essential for steering China's LIBs recycling industry toward a sustainable circular economy. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Zhan G.; He Y.; Li X.; Gu Y.
Title: Decoding market dynamics with financial knowledge graphs and cross-modal transformers
Abstract: Stock trend prediction is intrinsically challenging due to stochastic volatility, information heterogeneity, and the complex coupling between explicit market signals and implicit business logic. Although recent multimodal approaches have attempted to fuse quantitative data with textual sentiment, they suffer from two fundamental limitations: (1) Shallow Integration: Simple concatenation mechanisms fail to capture the dynamic, non-linear modulation between unstructured sentiment and structured technical indicators; (2) Lack of Structural Priors: Data-driven models often struggle to understand the intrinsic transmission logic of financial risks (e.g., supply chain dependencies) underlying numerical fluctuations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel Knowledge-Aware Global Cross-Modal Interaction Network (KG-GCM). First, to bridge the semantic gap between general language models and specific market micro-sentiments, we introduce a domain-adaptive extractor leveraging FinBERT with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and a task-specific semantic projection backbone. Second, we construct a Heterogeneous Financial Knowledge Graph (FKG) and propose a Side-Info-Aware Graph Attention Network (SI-GAT) to explicitly model the topology of capital flows and supply chains. Crucially, we design a Knowledge-Guided Contextual Gating mechanism that utilizes static graph embeddings to dynamically weigh the importance of time-varying financial reports and policy texts. Finally, these heterogeneous features are projected into a unified manifold and fused via a Global Transformer to form a holistic market state representation. To ensure robust optimization, we implement a Two-Stage Curriculum Learning strategy with differential fine-tuning. Extensive experiments on real-world A-share datasets demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms competitive baselines under the strict point-in-time protocol. Notably, it improves directional accuracy by 5.60% while substantially elevating ranking signal stability, achieving a Rank IC of 0.057 and ICIR of 0.55, thereby providing a stable cross-sectional predictive ranking signal in complex market environments. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
