Title: Masculine honor, social visibility, and safety non-compliance: intentions and approval judgments in high-risk sectors in Turkey
Abstract: Unsafe work in high-risk sectors cannot be explained only by knowledge deficits or weak safety management; workers may also attach reputational meaning to visible compliance. Drawing on honor theory and occupational-safety research on risk perception and social context, this study examined whether masculine honor values (hereafter honor values)—the belief that a man’s worth depends partly on a publicly defensible reputation—were associated with unsafe work intentions, lower perceived risk, and greater approval of safety-rule non-compliance among male workers in Turkish construction and shipbuilding. A worker survey (N = 244) was combined with a within-person vignette experiment in which the focal hazard was held constant while visibility was manipulated and audience identity and prior social comment varied orthogonally. Honor values were positively associated with unsafe work intentions (H1a) and approval of others’ violations (H1b), and negatively associated with perceived risk (H2). Perceived risk partially accounted for the honor–intention association (H3). The association between honor values and approval of non-compliance was stronger when the violation was public rather than private (H4), consistent with a reputational, visibility-contingent account. These findings identify a micro-level sociocultural pathway that complements knowledge- and risk-based accounts of safety decisions. They also suggest that safety communication and supervisory practice should address the social meaning of compliance, while the cross-sectional mediation and judgment-based vignette outcome limit causal and behavioral inference. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: UK bioenergy policies and implications for global land use change
Abstract: Bioenergy is central to UK decarbonisation policy, yet its reliance on imported biomass and crop-based biofuels raises concerns about land use change (LUC) and indirect land use change (ILUC) in supplier countries. This study provides a data-driven, ex-post assessment of land use implications associated with two UK bioenergy policy pathways: forestry-derived biomass supported by the Contract for Difference (CfD), and 1st generation biofuels supplied under the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation (RTFO). Import data for 2015–2022 were linked to forestry biomass productivity and country-specific crop yields to estimate direct land use footprints in major supplier countries. Wider ILUC-consistent signals were then assessed using observed land use, production and trade trends from 2000 to 2022, with particular focus on the US and Brazil. Results show that UK-bound forestry-derived biomass was mainly associated with land footprints in the US, Canada, Latvia and Estonia, while UK-bound 1st generation biofuel land demand became increasingly concentrated in the US and Brazil by 2022. Sensitivity analysis showed that lower productivity assumptions increased estimated land requirements, but did not alter the main supplier-country patterns. Overall, UK bioenergy imports represented a small share of total land use in major supplier countries. The study found no persistent national-scale ILUC signal detected in the US or Brazil. The findings suggest that ex-post land use monitoring can complement model-based ILUC assessment and improve the evidence base for bioenergy sustainability policy. © 2026 The Authors. Title: DCET: Multi-scale decomposition and channel clustering enhanced multivariate time series forecasting
Abstract: Existing multivariate time series forecasting methods address multi-scale structures and channel heterogeneity by either enhancing model expressiveness with deeper and wider network architectures or by preprocessing sequences to attenuate certain frequency components. However, these approaches often lead to increased training costs, instability from over-reliance on model capacity, difficulty in handling multiple scales, and failure to consider differing structural relationships between channels. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel framework called DCET (Decomposition and channel Clustering Enhanced multivariate Time series Forecasting), which integrates a cascading two-stage decomposition process, channel clustering, and a ChebyKAN residual head within a single unified model. The main contribution of DCET lies in its ability to directly address multi-scale and channel heterogeneity in a more efficient manner by simplifying the model structure while preserving its expressiveness. Specifically, DCET introduces an unsupervised learning-based module for parameter sharing among similar variates, and applies the two-stage decomposition to capture multi-scale features. Nonlinear models are used to represent complex fluctuations, while linear models capture long-term trends. Moreover, a multi-objective training approach minimizes both the overall prediction error and the errors of decomposed components. We validate DCET through experiments on eight public datasets, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy, robustness, and flexibility in handling high-dimensional, heterogeneous time series with manageable model complexity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Cloud continuum node evaluation and selection via mathematical programming
Abstract: Selecting appropriate compute resources in dynamic cloud–fog–edge environments is challenging due to diverse node capabilities, costs and fluctuating workloads. We introduce the Cloud Fog Service Broker (CFSB), implemented within the NebulOuS cloud-continuum platform, as a decision-support tool for resource selection. CFSB formulates node evaluation and selection as a multi-objective optimization problem that maximizes the performance score for each node across multiple criteria to derive a common weighting scheme and obtain their ranking. The model integrates quantitative criteria (e.g., CPU performance and proximity to data sources) and qualitative criteria (e.g., provider's reputation), while user-defined preferences are incorporated into the optimization through explicit constraints. CFSB retrieves dynamic measurements from the NebulOuS platform, e.g., data proximity, to support real-time evaluation under varying conditions. The proposed methodology is illustrated using a dataset comprising cloud, cluster and edge nodes. The obtained rankings are compared with those derived from Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Also, robustness is examined through sensitivity analysis of the ordinal-category discrimination parameter and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis under perturbed data values. The results demonstrate ranking agreement among the compared approaches. Title: Why this AI app? The impact of generative artificial intelligence on educators’ choices in educational apps
Abstract: In elementary education, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being incorporated into educational applications, despite still-emerging evidence of its effects on children's learning and development. Educators, who are already overwhelmed with choice in the commercial app space, may increasincly have to decide whether to incorporate GenAI-enabled apps for their classrooms. Thus, the present study investigates how mentioning GenAI in app store descriptions impacts K-6 educators' selection of educational apps. Over two studies, K-6 educators (each n = 101) from Canada, the US, and the UK viewed and evaluated eight researcher-created educational math apps with and without GenAI. Study 1 tested whether mentioning GenAI in app descriptions affected educators' app evaluations but found no effect. In Study 2, results from a repeated measures MANOVA revealed that educators rated apps without AI higher than those mentioning GenAI, but there were no significant effects of GenAI on likelihood to download or willingness to pay for apps. A hierarchical cluster analysis identified three distinct groups of educators: 1) selectors (n = 28), who exhibited a preference for downloading, rating, and paying for apps including GenAI; 2) agnostics (n = 59), who exhibit minimal preferences; and 3) avoiders (n = 14), who prefer apps without AI. Most educators were agnostic to the use of GenAI in educational apps, highlighting the need to support educators' informed decisions about when to adopt GenAI tools and encourage critical evaluation of GenAI's role in education. More research is needed to understand how educators' GenAI preferences relate to their attitudes, knowledge, and use of GenAI. © 2026

Title: XAI in the human-agent-environment loop: how do task, explanation strategy, and AI literacy shape user engagement?
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: This study explored how tasks, explanation strategies, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) literacy levels collectively influenced human interaction with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in a single-target prediction task. Using a within-subjects experiment with 70 participants, the study examined combinations of four AI-assisted prediction tasks—varying in prediction target (human-related vs. human-unrelated) and stakes (high vs. low)—and six explanation strategies (model-based, comparison-based, input influence-based, sensitivity-based, demographic-based, and case-based), across participants with varying AI literacy (AIL). Results showed that explanation strategies had the most significant impact on human-XAI interaction in most aspects, especially on prediction change with XAI assistance. Additionally, explanation strategies significantly affected all perception and experience indicators, except for curiosity. Compared to the scope of explanations, the content provided by strategies had a greater influence on user predictions. Strategies with trends and ratios, such as case-based (CA) and demographic-based (DE), were more effective. Conversely, strategies lacking trends and ratios, such as model-based (MO) and comparison-based (CO), were generally the least effective. For users, AI literacy influenced all performance metrics, especially re-prediction time. Higher AI literacy was significantly associated with longer re-prediction time. Tasks had moderate impacts on the XAI interaction process, especially experience measures. In the human-related tasks (recidivism and shipwreck survival prediction), participants reported lower subjective experience ratings among the tasks examined, particularly regarding perceived justice. In the high-stakes, human-unrelated task (wine quality prediction), participants gave the most favorable experiential ratings among the tasks in the study. Furthermore, second-order effects related to explanation strategies had significant impacts on various metrics. On the one hand, the interaction between explanation strategies and task characteristics influenced prediction changes. Global explanations, such as the input-influence-based (IN) and MO strategies, performed better on human-related tasks than on human-unrelated tasks. In contrast, local explanations, such as the sensitivity-based (SE) and CO strategies, showed the opposite pattern. On the other hand, the impact of explanation strategies on user perception and experience was moderated by AI literacy. Users with lower literacy tended to prefer local explanations, while users with higher literacy preferred global explanations. The content of the XAI explanation significantly affected the quality, while the scope had subtle interactive effects with different tasks and users. These effects with XAI, majorly interpreted through the Elaboration Likelihood model (ELM), provide evidence supporting adaptive XAI within the human-agent-environment loop. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Controlled assembly of MoSe2/N-doped carbon nanoflower spheres via coordination-induced precursor for superior sodium-ion storage
Abstract: Molybdenum diselenide (MoSe2) suffers from poor conductivity and structural degradation for sodium storage, which hinders its electrochemical performance. The enhanced electrochemical performance can be attributed to the conductive carbon framework, strengthened interfacial interactions, and efficient accommodation of volume variation. Title: Counterfactuals to Manage Ongoing Business Process Deviances
Abstract: Business Process Deviance (BPD) refers to the phenomenon of business process executions (traces) that deviate with respect to the desirable outcome. BPD detection is a Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM), which covers predictive methods designed to distinguish deviant traces from non-deviant traces. In this paper, we focus on the task of predicting BPD cases without waiting for the completion of process executions. To this purpose, we describe a PPM methodology, named FIREFOX, to monitor ongoing traces of a business process, to early identify process executions that are expected to deviate from the desirable outcome. FIREFOX equips BPD predictions with counterfactual recommendations of actions to perform in the near future, to avoid the detected deviance risk. Title: To Twin or Not to Twin? A Digital Twin Readiness Framework for SMEs
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Digital twin (DT) technology has rapidly matured into a cornerstone of Industry 4.0 and cyber-physical systems. Yet many small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and research laboratories struggle with when, not how, to adopt digital twins. The challenge extends beyond technology to encompass business necessity, data readiness, predictive requirements, organisational decision structures, and cost-value considerations. This study introduces the Effective Digital Twin Readiness (EDTR) framework, a structured decision instrument that integrates measurable variables across four dimensions (Business necessity, Data readiness, Model & prediction requirements, and Organisational readiness) to determine whether a digital twin should be pursued, deferred, or approached through a pilot implementation. To operationalise EDTR, a decision-support chatbot will be developed to guide stakeholders through structured input, scoring, and tailored recommendations. The study further provides historical context, a literature review, case archetypes, prototype conversation flow, and a critical evaluation of limitations and future research directions, offering a comprehensive reference for both researchers and practitioners. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Data-Driven Innovation in Cybersecurity for E-Business Information Systems: A Case Study on CVE Report Generation via LLM

Abstract: The backbone of modern digital economies, e-business information systems (EBIS), is security, which is an essential factor in ensuring business continuity and digital trust. Title: Representing BPMN Choreographies in OCEL 2.0

Abstract: Inter-organizational business processes describe the interaction between distributed parties. Title: Cross cultural patterns of linguistic aggression and aggressive combat content enjoyment: A computational study of PUBG reviews across six continents
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: This study explores global patterns of linguistic aggression and appreciation for aggressive combat content as expressed in reviews of PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds (PUBG), analyzing over 18.7 million Google Play Store English language reviews from over 80 countries. Grounded in the General Aggression Model (GAM), it integrates media psychology, cross cultural communication, and computational social science to assess emotional expression in user generated content. Results reveal a significant increase in the average intensity of both scores over time, with reviews grouped under South America exhibiting higher average aggression and AAC scores within the dataset, while reviews grouped under Australia show comparatively lower levels of these measures. The study uses GAM as a conceptual lens to interpret large-scale, naturalistic expressions of aggression and enjoyment. Title: Synergistic effects of operating parameters on conjugate flow field PEMFC performance
Abstract: This study examines effects of operating parameters on PEMFC performance with a conjugate flow field, revealing degradation mechanisms via overpotential, oxygen concentration, pressure drop, and temperature distributions. Increasing current density from 0.8 to 1.6 A·cm−2 expands high-loss regions to 10.93%, with pressure drop increasing by approximately 700 Pa per 0.4 A·cm−2 increment. Elevated pressure (1 to 3 atm) reduces high-loss regions, from 10.93% to approximately 0.35%, while increasing oxygen concentration fivefold. High humidity (80% RH) expanding high-loss regions to 25.45% and increasing pressure drop by 28.5%. Increasing stoichiometry (1.5 to 3.5) reduces high-loss regions from 68.69% to 10.93% and oxygen-deficient zones from 43.1% to 3.11%, though pressure drop rises from 1439 to 3781 Pa. The optimal operating window features a moderate current density of 1.2 A·cm⁻2, elevated pressure of 2–3 atm, controlled humidity of 50% RH, and a sufficient stoichiometry of 2.5, thereby balancing electrochemical performance with parasitic losses in conjugate flow field configurations. Title: From snow to rain: Spatiotemporal transitions and sensitivity patterns in the Amu Darya Basin, Central Asia
Abstract: Climate warming is altering precipitation phase with major implications for snow-dependent water resources. However, the nonlinear thresholds and elevation-modulated sensitivity governing snowfall-to-rainfall transitions remain poorly quantified. This study focuses on the Amu Darya Basin, a key water source in Central Asia, and addresses this scientific gap by quantifying transition sensitivity, identifying critical snowfall-fraction thresholds, and projecting future snow–rain dynamics. The analysis spans 1979–2100, using ERA5-Land reanalysis for 1979–2014 as the historical reference and bias-corrected CMIP6 projections for 2015–2100. A threshold-sensitivity-velocity framework is applied to characterize snow-rain phase transition behavior. The framework integrates piecewise regression, clustering analysis, and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to identify dominant drivers. Two robust snowfall-fraction thresholds (0.15 and 0.88) are identified, delineating four precipitation regimes. Projections indicate that snowfall-dominated areas will shrink by 20–25% by 2100, with the maximum snowfall elevation rising by 500–2500 m under SSP585. The transition accelerates after the 2040s, especially in the middle and lower reaches. Sensitivity analysis reveals rapid responses at low (<1000 m) and high (>4000 m) elevations, while mid-elevation zones (1000–4000 m) delay regime shifts by 20–30 years under moderate scenarios. Under the SSP585 scenario, high-elevation regions exhibit a sensitivity rebound. PLS-SEM results show temperature as the dominant suppressive driver of snowfall, with circulation effects acting indirectly. These findings advance understanding of nonlinear precipitation-phase transitions and provide a transferable framework for assessing hydro-climatic vulnerability in other snow-influenced arid and semi-arid regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: An efficient and green carbon recovery from fine slag: Machine learning-assisted evaluation of enhanced gravity separation
Abstract: Coal gasification fine slag (CGFS) contains considerable residual carbon, but its separation is challenging due to fine particle size and complex phase associations. This study compares conventional flotation and enhanced gravity separation for CGFS, integrating response surface methodology and machine learning to predict combustible recovery and analyze parameter effects. Results show that flotation achieved only ∼54% combustible recovery even at high reagent dosages, while enhanced gravity separation reached up to 96.8% under optimized conditions (20 Hz frequency, 0.020 MPa pressure, 30 g/L solid concentration). Fuerstenau curves confirm higher separation efficiency (1.587 vs. 1.288) for gravity separation. The machine learning model achieved superior prediction accuracy (R2 = 0.95) compared to RSM (R2 = 0.85), revealing parameter influence order: frequency > pressure > concentration. This study demonstrates that enhanced gravity separation offers a reagent-free, highly effective alternative for CGFS upgrading, while data-driven modeling provides significant advantages over conventional regression methods for complex separation processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Design of a Query Expression for Multi-Dimensional Graph Warehousing

Title: Semantic Execution of a High-Level Petri Net for Opportunity-Driven Decision-Making in Collaborative Business Ecosystems
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: This study introduces a hybrid simulation framework that integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with the rule-based semantic execution of a multi-token high-level Petri net, enabling systematic analysis of opportunity-driven decision-making in collaborative business ecosystems. The ABM layer captures ecosystem-level interactions among organizations, while each organization internally executes a shared Petri-net process for opportunity handling (Receive → Evaluate → Accept/Decline → Action/Collaboration), enabling concurrent processing via multiple data-carrying tokens. The Petri-net engine operationalizes domain semantics at transition firing time, including early opportunity claiming with ownership contention management, resource pre-reservation, coalition partner discovery, virtual-organization formation, and execution scheduling. Crucially, transition guards, thresholds, and delay functions are computed dynamically from organization-specific capability metrics, allowing a single Petri-net topology to generate structurally differentiated behaviors without type-specific branching logic. The framework is instantiated across five Mintzberg-inspired organizational archetypes (Adhocracy, Machine Bureaucracy, Professional Bureaucracy, Divisionalized Form, Simple Structure), allowing controlled comparative evaluation under identical opportunity streams. Detailed event run logs and KPI traces provide end-to-end traceability of stage-level and event-level outcomes together with key contextual variables such as slack, resource ratio, and skill coverage, supporting rigorous engineering analysis. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Robust fractional-order automatic differentiation and its applications in neural networks
Abstract: Fractional-order automatic differentiation (FAutograd) naturally extends fractional-order gradient descent (FGD) for neural network optimization. It builds on the standard automatic differentiation framework and uses fractional-order matrix differentiation theory. This allows symbolic differentiation based on the Riemann-Liouville derivative to be embedded into computational graphs. It thus fully realizes the potential of FAutograd in neural networks. FGD applies fractional-order differentiation only at the root node. In contrast, FAutograd extends it to intermediate and leaf nodes. This extension amplifies the instability caused by the fractional-order term. This often degrades performance in practice. To address this issue, we introduce an element-wise gradient clipping strategy for the fractional-order term. This strategy directly suppresses the source of instability in fractional-order gradient matrices. As a result, we propose a robust FAutograd method for neural network training. In this paper, we first provide a qualitative analysis of the method at the scalar level. Based on this strategy, we then develop the fractional-order Linear (FLinear) layer, a fundamental building block of FAutograd. We conduct empirical evaluations with this layer on various time series datasets. Experimental results show that FLinear improves both training robustness and evaluation performance. The results also confirm its effectiveness on SOTA baselines. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Clarifying environmental responsibility for consistent absolute environmental sustainability assessment: A global sector-level analysis
Abstract: Absolute Environmental Sustainability Assessment (AESA) aims to determine whether a system operates within its allocated share of Carrying Capacities (CCs). Initial guidelines have been proposed to establish a methodological framework. This paper proposes methodological recommendations to address three key requirements for a consistent implementation of AESA, i.e., i) additivity in the CCs downscaling, ii) no double-counting issues in environmental assessment, and iii) consistency of system boundaries between environmental assessment and downscaling steps. Proposals are based on the concept of environmental responsibility. Three environmental accounting approaches, which consider different types of actors responsible for a system's environmental impacts, are employed. These are the production-based approach (PBA), the consumption-based approach (CBA) and the income-based approach (IBA). Furthermore, identifying the responsible actor makes the CCs allocation step more transparent. The adapted AESA method is implemented across country-level economic sectors using Exiobase, an input-output database. Results obtained using the three accounting approaches and two theories of distributive justice are then compared. Similar to the choice of theory of distributive justice, AESA results are sensitive to the chosen accounting approach. Both are normative choices. Based on these preliminary findings, recommendations and further research perspectives are proposed for the AESA community. Finally, a focus on a single sector makes it possible to explore in further detail the relevance of the proposed recommendations for decision-making. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Regionalized life cycle assessment of NMC and LFP batteries across China-EU supply chain configurations under the EU Battery Regulation
Abstract: The EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 introduces stringent life cycle carbon footprint requirements that are expected to influence the regional organization of battery production. However, the carbon footprint implications of alternative China-EU supply chain configurations remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a regionalized life cycle assessment framework to evaluate the life cycle carbon footprints of lithium nickel‑manganese‑cobalt (NMC) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries under alternative regional supply chain configurations between China and the EU. The analysis follows the latest EU methodological guidance and combines proprietary industrial data from leading Chinese electric vehicle (EV) battery manufacturers. The boundary analysis showed that the calculated carbon footprints were sensitive to the life cycle stages included. Under the EU baseline, the carbon footprints of NMC and LFP batteries were 96.2 and 51.6 gCO2e/kWh under the Directive 91/157/EEC-informed reference boundary, 95.9 and 81.3 gCO2e/kWh under the Directive 2006/66/EC-informed reference boundary, and 142.9 and 128.3 gCO2e/kWh under the Regulation (EU) 2023/1542-aligned full life cycle boundary, respectively. Scenario analysis further indicated that regional supply chain reconfiguration can substantially narrow carbon footprint differences relative to Baseline-EU. For NMC batteries, the difference decreased from 59.3 gCO2e/kWh under the export (EX) scenario to 49.3 and 47.7 gCO2e/kWh under the overseas battery production (TB) scenario and partial material pre-processing in the EU (TBM) scenario, respectively. For LFP batteries, the corresponding values decreased from 74.1 to 49.4 and 47.1 gCO2e/kWh. These findings suggest that the regulatory context may encourage supply chain configurations with lower life cycle carbon footprints by altering the regional allocation of production stages. The findings highlight the importance of aligning regional production characteristics with decarbonization potential and provide policy-relevant evidence for coordinated China-EU battery supply chain strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: From black carbon reduction to coordinated fuel adoption on a trans-Arctic shipping corridor
Abstract: Arctic sea ice loss is opening trans-Arctic routes, but black carbon (BC) from conventional marine fuels amplifies climate risks in ice covered environments. This study evaluates whether lower BC fuel pathways can move from environmental advantage to coordinated deployment on a representative 14,000 km Murmansk-Shanghai corridor. The analysis integrates life cycle assessment (LCA), BC emission inventories, life cycle cost analysis (LCC), a resource–environment–economy (REE) evaluation, and a tripartite evolutionary game involving governments, ports, and shipping enterprises. Relative to heavy fuel oil (HFO) and very-low sulfur fuel oil (VLSFO), LNG and methanol reduce modeled onboard BC mass by 93.9% and 79.0%, respectively. Standard 100-year Global Warming Potential (GWP100) values are 64.68 kg CO2-eq per functional unit (FU) for LNG and 70.53 kg for CO2-methanol, compared with 81.61 kg for HFO/VLSFO. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) ranks first under Climate Priority and Balanced Development, but its Balanced Development advantage over HFO/VLSFO is only 0.0001 in closeness, with similar first-rank probabilities across 20,000 Monte Carlo draws. None of the 60 baseline scenarios or 12,960 bounded policy combinations achieves high tripartite adoption within 25 years; even ambitious LNG cases with positive payoff gaps fall below the 0.8 adoption threshold. Thus, BC is a useful screening signal, but lower BC alone cannot ensure deployment. Coordinated adoption requires simultaneous cost feasibility, port service returns, and sustained enterprise demand. The framework identifies the conditions under which environmental advantage can or cannot translate into implementation, offering a staged evidence base for Arctic shipping decarbonization policy. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Strategic packaging mechanization with sensor technologies for non-destructive in-situ quality and safety assessment of ready-to-eat fresh-cut fruits and vegetables
Abstract: The surging demand for convenience-based, ready-to-eat (RTE) fresh-cut fruits and vegetables (FCFV) is driven by health-conscious consumers for effortless food accessibility. Escalating mass demand for convenience, aesthetic appeal and intact nutrition has prompted immense research efforts for enhanced efficiency and functionality of the value chain performance of RTE foods. Title: Sorption enhanced co-gasification of pine wood and waste PET plastic with membrane assisted hydrogen separation for gasifier effluent valorisation and CO2 mitigation
Abstract: The use of gasifier effluent streams through integrated gas separation and purification technologies is important for clean H2 production and carbon emission reduction. This study develops an integrated Aspen Plus model that combines sorption enhanced co-gasification of pine wood and waste polyethene terephthalate (PET) with membrane assisted H2 separation to maximise H2 recovery while mitigating CO2 emissions. The effects of gasification temperature, steam-to-feed ratio, feedstock blending, and CaO sorbent addition on syngas composition, gasifier performance, and membrane separation efficiency were systematically investigated. Increasing the gasification temperature initially enhanced H2 production, but a slight decline was observed at higher temperatures. At 750 °C, H2 concentrations reached approximately 62 vol% for pine wood and 58 vol% for PET. CO2 concentration decreased from 26.97 to 18.95 vol% for pine wood and from 25.18 to 13.07 vol% for PET as the temperature increased. Higher steam-to-feed ratios further promoted H2 formation through steam reforming; however, excessive steam slightly reduced carbon conversion efficiency (CCE) and heating value of syngas. The addition of CaO significantly upgraded the gasifier effluent by increasing H2 concentration from 62 to 79 vol% for pine wood and from 58 to 70 vol% for PET, while decreasing CO2 from 22 to 11 vol% and from 16 to 9 vol%, respectively. Net CO2 emissions were reduced from approximately 95 to 40 kg/h, and CCE was reduced from 61.19 to 33.67% and 67.41 to 47.81% for wood and PET plastic, respectively. During co-gasification, PET enrich blends produced syngas with higher calorific value, while CaO maintained H2 concentrations of 72–76 vol% and CO2 below 12 vol%. Integration with a H2 selective membrane separated the gasifier effluent, producing high purity H2 and a CO2 enriched retentate stream for subsequent carbon capture. The integrated process offers an efficient pathway for biomass plastic waste valorisation and low carbon H2 production. © 2026 The Authors

Title: A Block-Wise Updating Strategy for Approximate Duplicate Detection
Abstract: Approximate duplicate detection in data streams aims to determine whether an item is present within a small subsequence of the data stream. It is a fundamental query problem needed in several network applications, such as web crawling and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tag management. Most of the existing algorithms are not space-efficient as they overlook the distributional information of query frequency and membership likelihood. In this paper, we propose CEll Bloom Filter (CEBF) algorithm, a space-efficient data structure designed by adopting a block-wise updating strategy, to solve this problem, and two typical distributions are considered: two typical distributions: (1) uniform query frequency of items, and (2) uniform membership likelihood of items. For an arbitrary sliding window size n and an arbitrary average false positive rate ε ∈ (0, 1), the proposed algorithm needs approximately O(nlog2(1/ε)) bits, which is significantly less than the number of bits used in existing methods. Space lower bound is also derived for these two typical distributions, which demonstrates that the proposed algorithm is near-optimal in terms of space consumption. Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real datasets, and the experimental results clearly demonstrate that the proposed method is clearly and significantly more effective and promising compared to existing other methods. © The author(s) 2027.

Title: Machine learning-based recommendation of over-the-counter treatments and exercise modalities for knee joint pain using long-tail classification
Abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a widespread chronic condition that significantly affects quality of life, yet selecting effective over-the-counter (OTC) medications and exercise modalities remains largely a trial-and-error process due to substantial inter-patient variability. Existing machine learning studies have primarily focused on disease diagnosis and progression prediction, while personalized conservative treatment recommendation has received limited attention, particularly under highly imbalanced long-tail treatment distributions. In this study, we analyzed clinical and demographic data from 1687 patients and developed a machine learning framework for personalized recommendation of OTC medications and exercise modalities. To address the severe class imbalance across 36 OTC categories and 53 exercise modalities, we systematically investigated class reweighting, SMOTE, and missing-label utilization strategies, and compared six representative machine learning and deep learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Focal Loss Neural Network, LightGBM, TabNet, and Sentence-BERT. Experimental results show that LightGBM combined with SMOTE consistently achieved the best overall performance, reaching 47.3% accuracy for OTC recommendation and 62.7% for exercise recommendation while substantially improving balanced accuracy and Macro-F1 for minority classes. Additional experiments demonstrate that advanced deep learning models do not outperform LightGBM on this moderate-sized structured clinical dataset. These findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning to provide practical decision support for personalized conservative treatment recommendations and reduce reliance on trial-and-error approaches in knee pain management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A Hybrid LLM-Based Framework for Automated Security Annotation Generation in Business Process Models
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: The modelling and analysis of secure business processes require the incorporation of security annotations into process models. Although BPMN extensions, including SecBPMN2, exist for this purpose, the derivation of accurate and complete security annotations from natural-language specifications remains a manual, expert-intensive, and error-prone task. This paper presents a hybrid framework that takes a BPMN process model and a security requirements document as input and automatically generates security annotations adhering to the SecBPMN2 specification. The approach combines Large Language Model (LLM)–based semantic extraction with schema-constrained mapping, rule-based normalization, and deterministic validation. The framework is evaluated comprehensively on a curated dataset of 27 process models from various domains. The results indicate that it consistently produces structurally valid SecBPMN2 annotations with high schema completeness. Compared to human security analysts, the system achieves substantially higher precision (0.58 vs. 0.29) while maintaining comparable recall (0.52 vs. 0.50) and reduces erroneous or misplaced annotations by nearly 50%. In addition, annotation generation is significantly faster than manual annotation. These findings demonstrate that hybrid LLM- and rule-based automation can reduce modeling effort while improving consistency and reliability, thereby providing a scalable foundation for security-by-design BPM. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Thermodynamic and economic analyses with hybrid optimization of an oxy-biogas-based polygeneration system integrating ammonia synthesis
Abstract: In this study, an integrated oxy-biogas-fueled polygeneration system is proposed and assessed for efficient energy cascading, waste-heat recovery, ammonia production, and CO2 capture. The configuration combines an oxy-fuel combustion chamber with dual gas turbines, a supercritical CO2 (sCO2) cycle, an organic Rankine cycle (ORC), and a steam Rankine cycle (SRC) to recover thermal energy across multiple temperature levels and reduce exergy destruction. A solid oxide electrolyzer cell (SOEC) utilizes part of the generated electricity to simultaneously produce hydrogen for ammonia synthesis and oxygen for the oxy-fuel combustion process, enhancing system integration and reducing external oxygen demand. The Haber–Bosch process is selected for ammonia production due to its technological maturity and compatibility with the high-pressure and high-temperature characteristics of the proposed system. Thermodynamic and exergoeconomic analyses are performed and coupled with a hybrid artificial neural network–grey wolf optimizer (ANN–GWO). The ANN acts as a computationally efficient surrogate model to accelerate multi-objective optimization. Two optimization scenarios are investigated: (I) maximizing ammonia production rate (APR) while minimizing total unit cost of products (TUCP), and (II) maximizing exergetic efficiency while minimizing payback period (PP). Compared with the base case, Scenario I increases ammonia production by 23.3% and reduces TUCP by 11.2%, while Scenario II enhances exergetic efficiency by 13.7% and shortens PP by 4.4%. Under Scenario I, the system achieves a net power output of 7.17 MW, an ammonia production rate of 480.14 kg/h, an energy efficiency of 51.75%, an exergetic efficiency of 49.03%, a TUCP of 25.31 $/GJ, and an ammonia production cost of 0.550 $/kg. Meanwhile, Scenario II yields a net power output of 8.41 MW, a PP of 3.26 years, an exergetic efficiency of 48.93%, and a net present value of 87.5 M$. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mapping the Intersection of AI, BI, and Sustainability: A Bibliometric Approach

Abstract: This paper presents a bibliometric analysis of research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, business intelligence, and sustainability. Using data from Web of Science, the study examines publication trends, thematic patterns, and intellectual structures. The results show a rapid growth in research activity, with a stable core of themes centred on AI, machine learning, big data, and sustainability, alongside several emerging but weakly integrated topics. Citation and collaboration analyses reveal a globally distributed research community and a concentration of influential journals in sustainability and engineering domains, while business- and management-oriented outlets remain less represented. Title: Ready to blossom? African city skylines, an empirical puzzle, and a proposed solution
Abstract: This paper shows that global skyscraper construction both accelerated and globalized after the 2001 attacks on the Twin Towers in New York, into the twenty-first century. Despite being increasingly incorporated into the global economy as a ‘new frontier’ for global investors, Sub Saharan Africa (SSA) did not share in this construction boom. This paper demonstrates that the absence of skyscrapers in SSA is an empirical puzzle. The key drivers of skyscraper construction – economic growth, population increase and migration, globalization, and vanity-driven competition – should all be pushing SSA into building upwards. The key to resolving the empirical puzzle of why SSA doesn't build skyscrapers lies in land markets: better functioning land markets would directly increase the supply and indirectly increase the demand for skyscrapers. This paper suggests a mechanism to allow city governments to focus their capacity on protecting the property rights of developers building skyscrapers, allowing a skyscraper project to be granted the status of a standalone Special Economic Zone (SEZ). The resulting construction of skyscrapers may simply increase the supply of luxury residential accommodation and office space and displace any pre-existing informal construction to a less advantageous location on the city periphery. The demand for formal residential accommodation is also influenced by more than price – culture matters. Consequently, the paper concludes by noting that inclusive or affordable housing construction needs to be rooted in a more holistic development strategy. © 2026 .

Title: A survey charting trust models and systems in self-sovereign identity
Abstract: Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) is widely positioned as the decentralized future of digital identity. However, although traditional SSI literature emphasizes architecture and privacy, it largely overlooks a systematic analysis of how trust is formed, propagated, and managed. Trust is fundamental because, without it, the actions performed by key actors, including credential issuers, lose much of their practical value. In this landscape, trust is the ground on which SSI systems stand; when that ground is absent or unstable, any structure built on it crumbles. Against this backdrop, we chart the landscape of trust through a comprehensive survey of Trust Models (TMs) and Trust Management Systems (TMSs) in SSI. At the abstract level, we analyze TMs by examining the types of trust relationships among SSI actors and how trust is defined and represented. At the implementation level, we discuss TMSs in terms of how trust is represented, stored, and protected in the systems proposed in the literature. We analyzed 26 sources (24 peer-reviewed papers plus the Sovrin whitepaper and governance framework document), consolidated into 24 approaches, benchmarking 16 features across these dimensions. Based on this analysis, we identify five open challenges: enabling cross-chain trust portability; designing a hybrid TM that blends Web of Trust and hierarchies; supporting heterogeneous actors such as IoT devices and humans; implementing privacy-preserving feedback mechanisms; and TM and TMS interoperability in emerging settings, including delegated AI agents. Our analysis offers a compass to guide researchers and developers in selecting trust models and advancing SSI systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Harvesting trade partners online with AI: A joint learning method for predicting the business role of massive web pages
Abstract: In small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), users often perform tedious and complex human–computer interactions between search engine data ((Formula presented) ) and webpage data ((Formula presented) ) when seeking potential business partners online via search engines (SEs). While artificial intelligence (AI) has been shown to improve search efficiency, conventional machine learning methods still face challenges in retrieval accuracy and efficiency, particularly in complex big-data environments. To address these limitations, this study proposes an AI module termed the Multi-source Data Joint Learning (MDJL) model, designed to assist SME users in efficiently retrieving online business partners. The MDJL model employs a multimodal information fusion approach to separately represent unstructured data elements in (Formula presented) and (Formula presented) as vectors. An encoder-decoder architecture then jointly learns the associations between (Formula presented) and (Formula presented). Based on these learned joint representations, MDJL incorporates a multi-label attention mechanism to train a classifier that accurately predicts the business roles of companies associated with webpages. The model’s effectiveness is validated using real business datasets annotated by domain experts. Experimental results show that MDJL can effectively learn joint information from any two cross-correlated datasets. The resulting classifier exhibits high efficiency and robustness, especially when data from certain sources are partially missing or unknown. Title: Simulating the Domain Expert: An Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Interview Training for Business Process Modeling
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Business process discovery relies heavily on stakeholder interviews, yet practicing this skill in educational settings is constrained by limited access to domain experts. This paper empirically evaluates whether LLM-based conversational agents, configured to simulate non-technical domain experts, can effectively support the training of business process elicitation and BPMN modeling skills by providing opportunities for structured practice before engaging with human experts. We conducted a counterbalanced within-subjects pilot experiment with eight Computer Science students, who each interviewed both an LLM-based domain expert and a human expert on two different business process scenarios and subsequently produced a BPMN model. Results show that LLM-based sessions were substantially faster (mean 33.4 vs. 59.5 min), perceived as equally informative, and produced models of comparable quality. Both conditions generated distinct but condition-specific error patterns, which varied across process complexity and gateway type. These findings suggest that LLM-simulated domain experts are a useful training tool for BPM education, supporting repeated practice where expert availability is limited. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Enhancing transparency of official controls according to Regulation (EU) 2017/625: development and application of a food safety management system-based rating scheme for approved food businesses
Abstract: Regulation (EU) 2017/625, which governs the official control system established to ensure the application of food law, promotes transparency, including the publication of food business (FB) rating schemes based on compliance levels determined by the outcomes of these controls. However, their application remains limited, particularly for FBs subject to official approval under Regulation (EC) No 853/2004. This study aimed to develop and apply a rating scheme for approved FBs based on a review of those existing at the international and EU levels. A total of 52 rating schemes were identified and analyzed. Subsequently, a food safety management system (FSMS)-based rating scheme grounded on multiple official controls was developed. The scheme used a scoring system with a maximum score of 40 points, converted into a 0-100% scale and structured into six rating classes: A+ (97-100%), A (88-96%), B (76-87%), C (63-75%), D (50-62%), and Not Classified (<50%). Following a pilot test on 54 FBs, it was applied to all approved FBs (n = 201) within the Local Health Unit “Azienda USL Toscana Centro”. Most FBs (67.7%) were classified in the higher rating classes (A+, A and B), indicating generally good FSMS performance. However, a substantial number of non-compliances emerged among the analyzed FBs, particularly in prerequisite programs (PRPs), especially regarding maintenance (50.8%), other prerequisite requirements (44.3%), cleaning/disinfection (36.3%), and personnel hygiene/training (33.3%). Deficiencies in Hazards Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) based procedures, traceability, and microbiological and chemical sampling/analytical outcomes were detected in 28.8%, 13.9%, and 17.4% of FBs, respectively. PRPs non-compliances were significantly associated with HACCP and traceability deficiencies, while HACCP deficiencies were also associated with sampling/analytical non-compliances. Title: Bridging Learning and Employability: The Evolving Role of Teaching, Technology, and Faculty Development in Business Schools
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: In an era marked by rapid digital transformation and changing labour market demands, Business Schools are under increasing pressure to demonstrate their contribution to graduate employability through pedagogical innovation and institutional renewal. This study examines how Teaching Approaches (TAs), Educational Technologies (ETs), and Faculty Development Initiatives (FDIs) adopted by leading international Business Schools interact to influence perceived learning effectiveness and employability outcomes. Using a quantitative survey design, data were collected from faculty members across top-ranked institutions and analysed through linear regression models to assess the relationships among pedagogical, technological, and developmental dimensions. The findings reveal that active and experiential teaching approaches, as well as technology-enhanced learning practices, are positively associated with perceived effectiveness in promoting both student learning and employability. Faculty development initiatives emerged as the strongest predictor, suggesting that professional learning and institutional support indirectly facilitate the integration of employability-oriented outcomes into curricula. Overall, the results support a systemic model of academic innovation in which pedagogical design, digital transformation, and faculty development co-evolve to enhance educational quality and graduates’ readiness for the workplace. Title: Evaluation of cost reduction effects by sector-coupling synergies in timber processing and bioenergy for sustainable forestry in Japan
Abstract: The greenhouse gas sequestration capacity of forests is an important pillar in combating global warming; therefore establishing a forest resource circulation system is crucial. Forestry, which includes everything from cultivation to harvesting forests that store carbon dioxide as they grow, and the sawmill industry, which processes this timber, frequently face significant economic challenges. Consequently, proposals are needed to establish systems that improve these industries’ economic competitiveness while also ensuring the forest resources circulation. This study developed a model to evaluate the economic relationship between timber processing and energy consumption from a sector-coupling perspective using a prospective techno-economic analysis. It specifically defines wood utilization as a comprehensive forest resource circulation that includes production, planting, processing, energy utilization, and reforestation. It evaluates the economic interdependence between timber processing and energy utilization when all wood is harvested from forests and both uses are combined. The evaluation results show that combining energy utilization in sawmills processing over 36,000 m3 annually allows for full harvesting from forests, reducing forest residues, and lowering site preparation costs for reforestation. Additionally, using inexpensive electricity from biomass power generation for sawmilling lowers sawmill costs. It has become clear that, at sawmills of a certain size or larger, combining material utilization with energy utilization results in a slight decrease in sawmilling costs, while reducing forestry management costs; overall, this is an effective approach for wood utilization. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Vibe Coding: An experiment with test-driven development
Abstract: Context: Conversational Large Language Models (CLLMs) can automatically generate code by collaborating with users through natural language. However, poor collaboration can lead to poor quality output. Objective: This exploratory study aims to investigate how humans and CLLMs can collaborate as peers through vibe coding, an approach that integrates principles from prompt engineering, agile design, and human-AI co-creation to enhance collaboration. Method: We designed four interaction models representing different collaboration patterns in the software development process: the solo model (human-only development), the collaborative model (human–CLLM collaboration), the fully automated model (development autonomously performed by a CLLM), and the agentic model (development autonomously performed by the MetaGPT X platform). Based on these models, we implemented corresponding Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflows using structured prompts and Python scripts. We then conducted a controlled pre-experimental study with TDD professionals to compare the solo and collaborative workflows. In addition, we performed repeated exploratory executions of fully automated and agentic workflows on the same development tasks to obtain complementary evidence. Results: Our findings suggest that the choice of interaction model should depend on the development objective. Agentic workflows are best suited for rapid development and functionally correct production code but may introduce additional implementation complexity. However, they may also introduce additional implementation decisions that are not explicitly required by the functional specifications, resulting in untested decision points. In contrast, collaborative workflows produce higher-quality, better-organized test suites. Conclusions: Our work explored how humans can collaborate with CLLMs in generating code in highly intensive and demanding development process. Title: Hotel resilience to prolonged uncertain disruptions: A business model dynamics analysis
Abstract: This study examines how hotels adapted their business models to sustain operations during the prolonged uncertainty of COVID-19. Using Business Model Dynamics as a systems lens and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) on data from 53 Thai hotels, the study identifies multiple equifinal configurations of strategic, operational, and financial adjustments that generated high resilience. Results show that high resilience emerged not from isolated actions but from coherent alignments among innovation, resource redeployment, and financial preparedness, with minimal cost restructuring shared across resilient hotels. Less resilient hotels followed distinct, asymmetric configurations, confirming that the drivers of low resilience differ from those of high resilience. The findings advance hospitality resilience research by extending Business Model Dynamics through configurational causality, showing how adaptive operational resilience depends on the fit among business model elements during a prolonged disruption. The study offers context-specific insights for tourism-dependent hotels and provides a foundation for future cross-country and longitudinal validation of the Configurational Business Model Dynamics (CBMD) framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: From segmentation to simulation: Joint lumbar vertebra-disc segmentation in 3D CT enabling finite element modeling
Abstract: Segmentation of lumbar vertebrae and intervertebral discs from three-dimensional computed tomography (CT) is essential for patient-specific reconstruction and downstream finite element analysis (FEA), yet remains challenging because of low soft-tissue contrast, ambiguous vertebra-disc interfaces, and the lack of joint annotations within the same volumes. We propose GSC-DPM, a three-dimensional segmentation framework that combines gated skip connections with a DualPathMamba encoder to jointly capture long-range anatomical context and preserve local boundary details. To enable supervised joint learning, we constructed VID-80 through model-assisted annotation initialization and expert consolidation. The same architecture was first trained separately for vertebra segmentation on CTSpine1K and for disc segmentation on the in-house Shanxi Bethune Hospital Lumbar Disc CT dataset (SBH-LD100; unrelated to LIDC-IDRI), and the resulting candidate masks on independent lumbar CT volumes were subsequently reviewed, merged, corrected, and refined by clinical experts to obtain final joint labels. On VID-80, the final joint model achieved Dice scores of 0.963  ±  0.013 for vertebrae and 0.903  ±  0.011 for discs, with an average Dice of 0.933  ±  0.011 and an average IoU of 0.881  ±  0.021. It also achieved the lowest average HD95 and ASSD of 1.243  ±  0.387 mm and 1.114  ±  0.285 mm, respectively, indicating improved boundary accuracy. Controlled ablation experiments further demonstrated the relative influence of gated fusion, dual-path feature mixing, and encoder depth. In addition, we performed a representative-case segmentation-to-FEA feasibility demonstration using a selected GSC-DPMJ-derived vertebra–disc prediction as the geometric basis for FE preprocessing. The remaining anatomical and mechanical components were introduced during FE construction rather than directly predicted by the network. The representative model produced a converged solution under standard lumbar loading conditions, suggesting preliminary feasibility for downstream FE preprocessing. Title: Teaching Declarative BPM: Where, When and to Whom it Matters
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: The theory of BPM has, for a long time, discussed the interaction between flows and business rules, in what some call the declarative vs imperative business process spectrum. While imperative models constitute the standard in the curricula, with standards such as BPMN being imparted in most educations, declarative BPM has received a much more specialized scope. This paper collects and discusses insights coming from experiences teaching declarative process models in academia, in courses ranging from computer science to business informatics across universities in Austria, Belgium, Denmark, and the Netherlands, with languages such as Declare, DCR graphs, and DMN. We report considerations in curriculum development, considerations for diverse backgrounds, accessibility of tools and materials, and overall student perceptions of declarative modelling. Title: The viral deviation: a quantitative analysis of social media engagement metrics on non-compliant flight deck behaviors
Abstract: Background Normalization of Deviance (NoD) is a well-documented organizational failure mode in aviation, yet its propagation through digital ecosystems remains unexplored. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) highlights a critical mentorship vacuum due to pilot retirements, and social media platforms increasingly serve as informal training environments. This study introduces the concept of Algorithmic Normalization of Deviance- ANoD, hypothesizing that recommendation algorithms systematically reward and amplify “gray-zone” cockpit behaviors that erode sterile flight deck protocols. Method We conducted a stratified netnographic analysis of 150 high-visibility aviation videos (N = 150) across Instagram Reels, split between algorithmically recommended content (n = 100) and curated influencer content (n = 50). A novel coding framework operationalized compliance (Compliant vs. Gray Zone vs. Deviant) and incentive structures. Engagement metrics were analyzed to quantify the algorithmic advantage of non-compliant behavior. Results The analysis reveals a directionally consistent “Viral Deviation” pattern rather than a statistically decisive one. Gray-zone recordings (i.e., technically legal but procedurally borderline) comprised 57% of the sample and attracted higher engagement than compliant content, although this difference was small and did not reach conventional significance (d = 0.24, p = 0.11). The clearest signal emerged between content sources: algorithmically surfaced posts showed significantly higher interaction rates than curated influencer posts (d = 0.31, p = 0.029), a small but statistically significant per-view advantage for content promoted directly by the recommendation system. Structural incentive analysis further indicates that monetization pressures co-occur with increased gray-zone production, structurally analogous to a parallel, shadow curriculum associated with conditions that may facilitate drift. Conclusion The study identifies statistical associations, not causal relationships, and the downstream behavioural impact on pilots is hypothesised from the algorithmic-pattern evidence rather than directly measured. Within those bounds, social media algorithms constitute a structurally unmonitored distribution channel whose observed associations with gray-zone content amplification are consistent with a normalisation-of-deviance feedback mechanism operating beyond current regulatory oversight — an association that warrants urgent empirical validation and proactive governance. We propose a shift from prohibition to risk-stratified governance, recommending that regulators distinguish between handheld (high-risk) and mounted (managed-risk) devices, and integrate digital algorithmic literacy into ab-initio pilot training to counter this new systemic threat. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Which smartphone reuse interventions actually reduce new device production? A stated-preference market-level analysis
Abstract: Manufacturing dominates the environmental impact of smartphones, and reuse is widely promoted to reduce production, yet not all reuse interventions achieve this. We integrated stated-preference data from 441 German consumers with a calibrated market model to quantify how four interventions affect smartphone lifetimes and production: new batteries, extended warranties, free data transfer and erasure services, and trade-in programs. The battery intervention produced the largest modelled reduction in manufacturing (32%), followed by warranties (18%). Supply-side interventions increased recirculation but did not reduce production. Combining all four reduced production by 35%, barely exceeding battery alone owing to overlapping segments and rebound effects. Risk perception was the dominant predictor of consumer response. Production reduction in mature reuse markets thus appears gated by demand-side risk mitigation rather than supply-side facilitation. Voluntary interventions alone may be insufficient for sector-level targets and likely require regulatory complements; field-based evidence is needed to confirm these patterns. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Eutectic solvent platform for the selective isolation and one-year stabilisation of astaxanthin from crustacean shell waste
Abstract: Astaxanthin is a high-value natural carotenoid with strong antioxidant activity, attractive colour properties, and broad potential for use in food, cosmetics, nutraceuticals, and pharmaceutical formulations. However, its practical application is limited by its low stability and the need for sustainable and selective extraction strategies from renewable feedstocks. In this work, crustacean shell waste was explored as a circular source of astaxanthin, using (deep) eutectic solvents (DES) as alternative extraction media. A series of DES based on choline chloride or tetrabutylammonium bromide combined with different hydrogen bond donors was screened for the selective solid-liquid extraction of astaxanthin from shrimp shell waste. Tetrabutylammonium bromide-based DES outperformed choline chloride-based systems, particularly [N4,4,4,4]Br:hexanol and [N4,4,4,4]Br:octanoic acid. Response surface methodology was then used to optimise the solid-liquid ratio (SLR) and extraction time. [N4,4,4,4]Br:hexanol achieved an astaxanthin mass balance of ~80% with minimal co-extraction of proteins (~20%) and no extraction of minerals or chitin, with a SLR of 0.4 g mL-1 and 10 min of extraction time. The long-term stability of astaxanthin in the selected DES was also evaluated for one year under different temperature and light conditions. Astaxanthin showed remarkable stability in [N4,4,4,4]Br:hexanol, retaining approximately 44% of its initial content after 365 days at 25 °C in the dark while maintaining a visible orange-red colour. Kinetic modelling further confirmed this stability, estimating a half-life (t1/2) of 265 and 282 days based on first- and second-order kinetic models, respectively. These results demonstrate that [N4,4,4,4]Br:hexanol can act simultaneously as an efficient extraction solvent and a stabilising medium, reducing downstream processing while enabling the sustainable valorisation of crustacean shell waste into stable natural colourants. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Green architectural tactics in ML-enabled systems: an LLM-based repository mining study
Abstract: Context: The increasing adoption of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies raises growing concerns about their environmental sustainability. Developing and deploying ML-enabled systems is computationally intensive, particularly during training and inference. Green AI has emerged to address these issues by promoting efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. While prior research has proposed catalogs of sustainable practices (i.e., green tactics), there remains limited understanding of their adoption in practice and whether additional, undocumented tactics exist. Objective: This study aims to investigate the extent to which existing sustainable practices are implemented in real-world ML-enabled systems and to identify previously undocumented practices that support environmental sustainability. Method: We conduct a mining software repository study on 205 open-source ML projects on GitHub. To support our analysis, we design a novel mechanism based on large language models (LLMs) capable of identifying both known and new sustainable practices from code repositories. Results: Our findings confirm that green tactics reported in the literature are used in practice, although adoption rates vary. Furthermore, our LLM-based approach reveals nine previously undocumented sustainable practices. Each tactic is supported with code examples to aid adoption and integration. Conclusions: We finally provide insights for practitioners seeking to reduce the environmental impact of ML-enabled systems and offer a foundation for future research in automating the detection and adoption of sustainable practices. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Automatic behavior tree generation for enhanced human–robot collaborative task planning in industry 5.0: A systematic review
Abstract: In the context of Industry 5.0, scheduling heterogeneous resources, such as humans and robots, has become increasingly critical. Task allocation must balance human comfort, ergonomics, and trust with productivity and responsiveness to customer demands. This review explores recent advances and prospects in the automatic generation of schedules and action plans, particularly Behavior Trees (BTs), to improve human–robot collaboration. We examine the application of artificial intelligence techniques to classical production management problems, such as Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP) and Assembly Line Balancing Problems (ALBP), for autonomous task scheduling and robotic behavior design. This includes highlighting innovative scheduling approaches and the advantages of Behavior Trees over traditional models such as Hierarchical Task Networks (HTN) and Finite-State Machines (FSM). Behavior Trees offer a modular and reactive programming structure essential for executing complex tasks assigned to robots. The review also discusses human operators’ perception of robotic actions and identifies best practices for implementing collaborative solutions that prioritize both efficiency and safety. © 2026 The Authors. Title: How Servitization Enables—And Constrains—Sustainable Value Creation: An Empirical Analysis Among Manufacturing Firms
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: In recent years, manufacturing companies have been operating in an increasingly complex environment shaped by two concurrent drivers: the evolution of business models and the ecological transition. The diffusion of servitization and Product–Service Systems (PSS), has been accompanied by growing pressure to reduce environmental impacts throughout the entire product life cycle. The relationship between servitization and sustainability has attracted increasing attention in the literature, leading to the emergence of concepts such as sustainable servitization and sustainable PSS. While prior studies highlight the potential sustainability benefits of servitized business models, they also reveal ambiguities and inconsistent evidence, suggesting that servitization cannot be considered inherently sustainable. Building on this literature, this study explores how the barriers hindering the practical implementation of sustainable servitization manifest in practice through qualitative evidence from nine manufacturing companies characterized by different levels of servitization maturity. The findings identify key challenges faced by firms when integrating sustainability into PSS and highlight practices that can help address them. The study contributes to the literature by providing empirical insights into sustainable value creation in manufacturing and by identifying best practices that can support companies in advancing their sustainable servitization strategies. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Hub-centric heterogeneous graph reinforcement learning for integrated automated guided vehicle dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling with finite-buffer constraints
Abstract: The integration of automated guided vehicle (AGV) dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling constitutes a challenging problem in flexible manufacturing systems, particularly when finite output buffers cause blocking effects and potential deadlocks. This paper investigates an integrated event-driven AGV dispatching and unrelated parallel machine scheduling problem with finite-buffer constraints, aiming to minimize the makespan. In this study, dispatching refers to the real-time assignment of AGVs to transportation tasks, whereas scheduling refers to assigning workpieces to parallel machines and determining processing sequences. These two decision processes are strongly coupled through transportation, processing, and buffer interactions. To address the strong coupling among transportation, processing, and buffering decisions, this paper proposes a framework that integrates a hub-centric heterogeneous graph neural network (HCHGNN) with proximal policy optimization (PPO), termed HCHGNN-PPO. The manufacturing system is modeled as a hub-centric heterogeneous graph comprising four node types: orders, AGVs, waiting areas, and buffer areas. In this structure, AGVs serve as hub nodes that bridge task sources and processing resources. To leverage this, an HCHGNN encoder is developed to extract structured state representations via AGV-mediated message passing and learnable feature standardization. To improve training stability, a decoupled actor–critic architecture is introduced, in which the policy and value networks use independent graph encoders and optimizers. Moreover, a priority-based action-masking mechanism reduces the risk of buffer-induced blocking by prioritizing buffer-clearance operations, while an incremental reward based on minimum idle-time progression provides denser feedback for makespan-oriented learning. Extensive experiments on various benchmark instances demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional dispatching rules and representative deep reinforcement learning baselines. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework to generate effective scheduling decisions for complex integrated manufacturing systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Robust traffic sign detection in diverse environments: A comprehensive review of methods and trends
Abstract: Robust traffic sign detection (TSD) is essential for autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems. Despite significant advances in object detection, modern detectors still suffer performance degradation under adverse conditions such as fog, rain, snow, and low-light environments, compared with clear-weather scenarios. This review highlights a critical finding: architectural evolution alone, from YOLOv1 to YOLOv12, has not resolved the challenge of adverse-weather robustness. No reviewed study reports mean average precision for the same trained YOLO model on paired clear- and adverse-condition data, so the magnitude of the loss cannot be established for this family from the published record; the only paired detection result in the corpus, an enhanced Faster R-CNN evaluated on TT100K, loses 5.7 mAP points in rain, a retention ratio of 93.8%. The 15–20% figure widely quoted for adverse-condition degradation originates in top-1 classification accuracy on pre-cropped CURE-TSR imagery and is therefore not commensurable with detection mAP, and no study evaluates a single model across all four conditions on a common protocol. To address this gap, we present one of the first comprehensive reviews to jointly examine three previously fragmented research areas: the evolution of YOLO alongside Faster R-CNN, SSD, transformer-based detectors, and vision-language models; traffic sign detection under fog, rain, snow, and nighttime conditions; and a critical analysis of nineteen benchmark datasets, which exposes limitations in geographic diversity, weather coverage, and illumination representation. Using a PRISMA-guided methodology, 246 studies were systematically reviewed, and four key contributions were made. First, we introduce the mAP Retention Ratio (adverse-weather mAP divided by clear-weather mAP) as a practical measure of robustness and apply it to the corpus in a retention audit, which finds the ratio computable for only one reviewed study; on the available evidence, no current detector has been demonstrated to achieve strong adverse-weather performance, real-time speed, and deployment efficiency simultaneously. Second, we synthesize adverse-condition detection strategies and isolate image restoration as an experimental variable: relative to an unmodified detector on the same benchmark, decoupled restore-then-detect cascades recover approximately +5 mAP points, whereas restoration jointly optimized with the detection objective recovers up to +18 mAP@0.5 points, with both incurring additional latency, and no reviewed study compares these two strategies under a common detector, dataset, and hardware configuration. Third, we identify the primary causes of poor model generalization, including biases in traffic sign categories, environmental conditions, illumination settings, and regional distributions. Fourth, we propose a focused research agenda centered on transformer optimization for edge devices, LiDAR–camera fusion for occluded signs, generative augmentation for improved cross-domain generalization, and few-shot and zero-shot detection of rare and region-specific signs. Our findings demonstrate that robust traffic sign detection requires more than incremental architectural improvements, because progress will depend on the integration of multimodal sensing, representative datasets, efficient deployment strategies, and weather-aware learning frameworks. By consolidating fragmented literature and providing quantitative insights, this review offers a comprehensive reference for developing traffic sign detection systems that are accurate, reliable, and deployable in real-world autonomous driving environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: DAIKG: Disentangled attribute interaction based on knowledge graph for fine-grained fashion preference prediction
Abstract: Mass personalized customization requires translating user characteristics into design specifications. Existing graph-based methods often learn entangled representations, weakening the alignment between design attributes and user physical profiles. These challenges are further compounded by (1) data sparsity in fine-grained preference records, limiting the learning of comprehensive user profiles, and (2) imbalanced attribute distributions, which introduces bias and degrades performance on less common yet important attributes. To address these issues, we propose a Disentangled Attribute Interaction based on Knowledge Graph (DAIKG) framework for fine-grained fashion preference prediction. First, to alleviate data sparsity, we construct a multi-modal fine-grained fashion knowledge graph and employ Relational Graph Convolutional Networks (R-GCN) to capture attribute dependencies while enriching user profile-attribute representations. Second, we implement a dynamic routing mechanism to decouple attribute preferences, ensuring that requirements from distinct physical profiles are accurately represented. Finally, recognizing that attributes are not entirely independent, we incorporate a self-attention mechanism to explicitly model the interactions among these disentangled attributes, enhancing predictive accuracy. Our study evaluates the proposed framework under a profile-to-attribute prediction setting based on reconstructed user profiles derived from event-based data. Experimental results within this setting demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms adapted graph-based and recommendation baselines across multiple runs. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
