Title: Decoupling physical and chemical effects in underground hydrogen storage: A multiscale evaluation of carbonate and shale rocks
Abstract: Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) impacts on reservoir and seal integrity necessitate a thorough understanding. Previous studies have not decoupled hydrogen-specific effects from those caused by pressure, temperature, and fluid saturation. This study systematically evaluates calcite-rich limestones ('95% CaCO3) and Eagle Ford shale for hydrogen storage conditions, integrating high-pressure laboratory experiments with molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT) simulations. Limestones (dry and brine-saturated) were exposed to H2 and control gas (N2) at 3.4 MPa and 50°C for 30 days, and shale at 6.0 MPa and 80°C. Post-exposure characterization revealed porosity variations within ± 2%, while permeability decreased in high-permeable samples and increased in tighter ones. Young’s modulus decreased by ' 20% in shale and by ∼ 13% in saturated limestone, but increased by 50% in dry limestone; unconfined compressive strength showed sample-dependent changes, with similar trends under H2 and N2, indicating that these responses were not hydrogen-specific. Similar observations were observed for H2 and N2 exposure, indicating that physical processes, rather than chemical processes, governed the responses. MD and DFT analyses confirmed negligible hydrogen reactivity, showing weak physisorption on calcite [CaCO3-(104)] surfaces, negligible charge transfer, unchanged band gaps, and no structural alteration. X-ray diffraction confirmed mineralogical stability, with minor gypsum dissolution. These results demonstrate that the tested calcite-rich limestones remained mineralogically stable under the investigated hydrogen exposure conditions. For Eagle Ford shale, the experimental observations showed no clear hydrogen-specific mechanical degradation during the tested exposure period, although direct mineralogical characterization was not performed in the present study. Overall, the observed short-term variations primarily reflect physical effects. Title: Analyzing structural, operational, and performance impact of process-aware information system updates
Abstract: Digital transformation often entails small-scale updates to the business functions exposed by enterprise systems, which support the execution of organizational business processes. These changes may increase operational friction in process execution, decreasing the process performance, increasing the complexity of maintenance activities, and making system documentation and training obsolete. Detecting and understanding their impact on process execution is therefore crucial to maintain smooth operations. Previous research contributions concerning the tracking and impact analysis of information systems updates are limited in scope, functionality, and tool support. In this paper, we propose a data-driven approach that uses the recently developed Digital Twins of Organizations (DTOs) to assess the impact of (process-aware) information systems updates. We model the updates using the configuration of DTOs and the newly introduced concept of actions in DTOs. The impact of the application of actions in a given configuration is quantitatively assessed by different types of impacts: structural, operational, and performance-related. We show the feasibility of the proposed approach by discussing a software prototype implementing it, a case study involving artificially-generated data from a standard ERP procure-to-pay process, and a case study using real-world data from a loan application process. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: SPSS concept customization driven by full-service scenarios with validation through an improved COMA and supersystem digital twins
Abstract: With the development of next-generation information technologies, smart product-service system (SPSS) has gradually emerged as an effective alternative to traditional product-service system for realizing value co-creation among stakeholders. The flexible integration of smart connected products and embedded digital services enables differentiated customization of SPSS concepts, making it an important research topic. However, most existing studies on customization focus primarily on service content in requirement analysis, with limited consideration of service processes and service scenarios. This focus confines requirement representation to a static perspective, limiting the ability to response differentiated and scenario-dependent requirements. Accordingly, this paper proposes a scenario-driven SPSS concept customization framework, with the objective of deriving more well performance SPSS concepts in full-service scenarios. First, stakeholders’ personalized requirements are elicited and mapped to personalized full-service scenarios through requirement-scenario mapping matrix. Second, to address conflicts among optimization objectives across scenarios and stakeholders, a multi-objective optimization model for scenario-driven SPSS concept customization is constructed. Then, the counterfactual multi-agent policy gradients (COMA) method is introduced and further improved to enable the dynamic solution. The improvements significantly extend the standard COMA by introducing contribution-guided sequential decision-making, Bi-LSTM-encoded joint action representation for evaluation network during centralized training, and scalarized multi-objective reward. As a result, the coordinated optimal global SPSS customized concept is generated across multiple scenarios. Third, to verify the performance of the customized concept in a rapid, cost-effective, and efficient manner, supersystem digital twin is introduced to develop the virtual prototype and scenario model. Finally, a case study involving an electric van smart product-service system for urban last-mile logistics distribution is conducted to validate the proposed framework, with experimental comparisons and in-depth analysis demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Understanding conflict in protected areas: integrating justice considerations with economic perspectives
Abstract: Despite broad agreement on the urgency of sustainability transitions that protect biodiversity, conservation conflicts continue to rise. This paper examines environmental conflicts in protected areas (PAs), highlighting the overlooked link between conflict and justice. Existing frameworks often fail to distinguish between conflict manifestations and determinants, or to integrate justice theories with economic perspectives. This study provides a comprehensive review of the literature to support the analysis of PA conflicts and develops a robust framework that integrates justice considerations with the economic perspective. Conflicts are viewed as inherent to complex social–ecological systems, shaped by social relations and rights over ecosystem services. The framework is structured around three analytical axes: substance (what the conflict is about), process (how it unfolds), and relation (who is involved with-whom). It differentiates between how conflicts appear (i.e., manifestation) and what causes them (i.e., determinants), framed through distributive, procedural, and recognition justice. This perspective challenges linear assumptions that conflicts always stem from injustices, emphasizing their potential to drive institutional change. The framework offers a novel approach to assessing justice-conflict dynamics in PAs governance, providing comprehensive toolkit for promoting equitable conservation strategies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: The enhanced ARAS method within the interval-valued neutrosophic set framework: a novel approach for climate change performance assessment
Abstract: Climate change is a global crisis caused by both natural and man-made activities. Global urgent precautions like environmentally sustainable policies, strategies for the adaptation of renewable energy, and public incentive arrangements should be taken to prevent the harmful effects of increasing greenhouse gases, including carbon emissions. For this reason, many parties, such as policy makers, academics, and researchers, are conducting many studies to analyze the current situation of the countries and the issues that need to be focused on urgently. Different from other studies, this study presents the enhanced Additive Ratio Assessment method in the interval-valued neutrosophic set environment (IVN-ARAS) and integrates the enhanced IVN-ARAS method with the interval-valued neutrosophic cross-entropy (IVN-cross-entropy) method. The applicability and effectiveness of the presented method are demonstrated in the environmental performance of G20 countries in terms of climate change. For this purpose, the linguistic data in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) is analyzed, and the new ranking scores are recalculated within an interval-valued neutrosophic set (IVNS) environment. Due to the uncertainty in the index variables, IVNS and entropy methods are preferred. In this context, index variables are weighted with the IVN-cross-entropy method, and country rankings and new ranking values are found with the enhanced IVN-ARAS method. Then, the validity of the country rankings from the enhanced IVN-ARAS method is tested with sensitivity and comparative analyses. Additionally, the IVN-ARAS method and CCPI rankings of the G20 countries are compared. The tests performed have shown that the presented method provides reliable and effective decisions in solving the decision problem under consideration. The findings also demonstrate that the uncertainty in the data is analyzed better using interval-valued neutrosophic numbers (IVNNs). Additionally, this study contributes to understanding the position of countries in combating climate change and developing sustainable policies in an uncertain environment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Succinic acid production from pineapple-derived waste within a biorefinery framework: A review of technological approaches, process integration, and technology readiness
Abstract: The industrial scale production of succinic acid remains constrained by feedstock availability, process integration challenges, and immaturity of upstream and downstream processes. Among emerging lignocellulosic resources, pineapple waste represents a promising feedstock for succinic acid production due to its renewable nature, abundance, favorable economic potential, and high cellulose and polysaccharide content. However, studies on the utilization of pineapple waste as a feedstock for succinic acid production are still very limited. This study aims to present a comprehensive summary of recent technological approaches for succinic acid production from pineapple waste to assess their potential for future implementation. This study commences by providing an overview of succinic acid production, both through chemical and biological conversion. Additionally, an overview of pineapple waste, including national and global production data, is provided. Furthermore, this study critically examined the challenges and opportunities associated with the current technology regarding the succinic acid production, covering the entire process chain from upstream to the downstream. This analysis is conducted based on the technology readiness level (TRL) to identify significant deficiencies in the transition of laboratory-scale development to industrial implementation. Authors: Feng S.; Li R.; Keung J.; Yu X.; Shi Y.; Xu M.
Title: Decision-boundary aware undersampling via Adversarial Influence for imbalanced software defect prediction
Abstract: Class imbalance severely impairs the capacity of software defect prediction (SDP) models to distinguish between defective (minority class) and non-defective (majority class) software instances. Conventional undersampling methods alleviate this problem by reducing the number of non-defective instances. However, they frequently eliminate informative non-defective instances essential for constructing reliable decision boundary, thereby compromising prediction performance. The key challenge lies in determining which non-defective instances should be retained to preserve effective decision boundary while balancing class distributions. To address this challenge, we propose Adversarial Influence-Based Intelligent Undersampling (AIIUS), a decision-boundary-aware undersampling for imbalanced SDP. In AIIUS, we introduce the Adversarial Influence metric to quantify the importance of non-defective instances to the model's decision boundary and formulate non-defective instance selection as an Adversarial Influence-based ranking problem. Specifically, we compute Adversarial Influence scores via adversarial perturbations on a surrogate model to rank non-defective instances and select the top-ranked ones most critical to decision boundary for constructing a balanced training dataset. Experiments on 18 public defect datasets and five commonly used classifiers show that AIIUS consistently improves imbalance-robust performance, achieving average gains of 9.50% in Balance, 3.43% in Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC), and 17.02% in Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) over representative resampling baselines, with statistically significant improvements in most settings (Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Cliff's δ). These results suggest that decision-boundary-aware instance selection is an effective and practical strategy for handling class imbalance in software defect prediction. © 2026

Title: Performance optimization strategy of nanometal oxide-functionalized graphene composite electrodes for efficient CO2 reduction in microbial electrolysis systems
Abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) offers a promising carbon sequestration strategy for climate change mitigation, which also provides a sustainable pathway for biomass accumulation and bioenergy resource recovery. Title: What drives happiness in 15 European Union countries? The role of income inequality, democracy, and environmental quality
Abstract: This study examines happiness as a key dimension of sustainable development by focusing on its socio-economic, political, and environmental correlates. In recent years, it has become increasingly accepted that happiness cannot be explained solely by economic prosperity but is strongly influenced by structural factors such as income distribution, democratic institutions, and environmental conditions. Despite growing interest, empirical studies examining the simultaneous effects of these three fundamental factors on happiness are scarce. This creates a noteworthy gap in the literature. This study aims to fill this gap by empirically examining the effects of income inequality, democracy, and environmental degradation on happiness in 15 European Union countries, including the United Kingdom for comparability, between 2011 and 2022. Per capita income and health expenditure are included as control variables. Methodologically, the study employs MMQR and assesses the robustness of the findings using FGLS, PCSE, and HPJ approaches. The findings suggest that income inequality and environmental degradation are negatively associated with happiness, whereas democracy is positively associated with individuals' happiness. Furthermore, it is found that per capita income and health expenditure are found to be positively related to happiness. The results point to the need for sustainable development goals to be addressed within a holistic framework rather than independently, offering important implications for policymakers. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Semantic similarity score: A new method for mapping intellectual structures in business research

Title: Parametric analysis of ethanol-based recycling of mixed plastic waste in a circular economy
Abstract: Growing concerns over the persistence and environmental impact of plastic waste highlight the need for recycling strategies that enable a circular economy by converting waste into valuable products. Despite this, integrated process models for chemical recycling of mixed plastic waste (MPW) remain limited. The novelty of this study lies in the integration of gasification of MPW to syngas, fermentation to ethanol, dehydration to ethylene, and polymerization to high-density polyethylene (HDPE) within an Aspen Plus process simulation framework, coupled with process optimization, heat integration, and energy-related GHG assessment, aiming to reduce waste and dependence on fossil resources. The framework was validated against published experimental and other data, with deviations of 0.12–4.0% across all process stages. Operating conditions were optimized through parametric analysis to maximize product yield and minimize energy consumption. Optimal gasification conditions were identified at an equivalence ratio of 0.21, steam-to-plastic ratio of 0.45, and temperature of 1000°C, producing 901.5 tonnes/day of syngas from a 500 tonnes/day plant. This syngas yielded 382 tonnes/day of ethanol, which was dehydrated at 450°C and 1 bar to produce 229 tonnes/day of ethylene. Polymerization of ethylene resulted in 228.4 tonnes/day of HDPE. The overall carbon conversion efficiency was 50.2%, corresponding to the carbon retained in HDPE relative to the carbon entering through the MPW feedstock. Heat integration reduced total heat demand by 56.1 MW (35.23%) and power consumption by 1.5 MW (6.12%), while lowering greenhouse gas emissions associated with energy consumption by 27.8% to 3.9 kg CO2e/kg HDPE. This approach supports scalable, energy-efficient plastic recycling and provides key insights for process design and implementation. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Investigation of uncertainties associated with human judgment during the inspection and condition assessment of civil infrastructures
Abstract: Inspection of civil infrastructure components is a critical task to assess their condition states and plan for appropriate maintenance actions. The process of inspection, however, involves several sources of uncertainty that can influence how a component is rated by an inspector. Despite potential consequences, such uncertainties have remained largely unexplored. This motivated the current study to develop a holistic framework to first measure the agreement and consistency of condition state predictions provided by various inspectors through the inter-rater reliability and intra-class correlation methods. Title: Data-center expansion and the dynamic regional redistribution of the water-energy-food stress in Texas
Abstract: Data centers are Texas's fastest-growing electricity and water claimants, with interconnection requests exceeding 400 GW against an 86 GW peak. Results showed that local siting restraint never relieves nexus pressure. It displaces the buildout into water-scarce agricultural regions in a closed state, or exports the industry once demand turns footloose. Under a drought of record, irrigation absorbs nearly all shortage, accumulating 6.3 million acre-feet of foregone Panhandle supplies, while an 80% irrigation-protection reservation changes nothing. Title: Optimizing online grocery service: From customer understanding to multichannel profitability
Abstract: We study the optimal online service for grocery retailers operating both physical and online stores. The challenge lies in optimizing the size of the online assortment and the delivery fees to maximize profitability across channels, while considering customer, operational, and market dynamics. Using transaction data from a major grocery retailer, we employ an alternative-specific conditional logit model to investigate how delivery fees, assortment size, network characteristics, and customer needs influence store choice and spending across physical and online channels. We develop a profitability model that incorporates online service variables, customer behavior, and operational costs, enabling us to explore optimal strategies under various conditions. By identifying favorable conditions for the online store and analyzing optimal service variables, we provide actionable insights for retailers. Our findings challenge common practices in omnichannel retail. We show that delivery fees should not merely cover costs but can be strategically set higher, particularly for retailers with strong offline presence. Additionally, while reducing fulfillment costs improves profitability, its impact is smaller than expected. Multichannel retailers can offset these costs by passing them on to customers, with minimal overall demand loss, as some customers opt to shop in physical stores rather than abandoning the retailer entirely. Lastly, maximizing the online assortment may not always be optimal, particularly if the operational inefficiencies and costs outweigh the value customers place on variety. Title: Optimization model and MIP-based heuristics for aircraft routing with crew assignment in the on-demand air transportation
Abstract: On-demand air transportation services have experienced significant growth in the business aircraft industry over the past decades. This sector requires complex decision-making in a highly dynamic environment, with associated high operating costs and requiring strict adherence to civilian aviation rules. In this context, we focus on the aircraft routing and crew assignment tasks, motivated by the collaboration with an airline that operates in the sector. The company seeks to determine which routes each aircraft must perform, considering the fleet characteristics, operating costs and crew legislation, such as working hours limit, minimum rest time, breaks, overtime payments, among others. These characteristics have been barely explored in the literature addressing on-demand air transportation services. We propose an effective mixed-integer programming (MIP) model to appropriately represent and solve the studied problem, and MIP-based heuristics, known as relax-and-fix and fix-and-optimize, to cope with large-scale instances. Computational experiments with real-world data provided by the company show that a general-purpose MIP solver finds optimal solutions within reasonable computing times for most instances when using the proposed MIP model. The MIP-based heuristics reduce computing times and reveal greater cost reductions in instances that were not solved to optimality. These results indicate the high potential for application of these approaches to effectively support decision-making in on-demand air transportation services. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Exploring generation Z nurses' experiences of shift work in intensive care units: A qualitative analysis
Abstract: Objectives: Generation Z nurses are entering the workforce with distinct expectations regarding work–life balance, professional recognition, and organisational support. Intensive Care Units (ICUs), characterised by rotating and night shifts, are associated with significant psychophysical and organisational demands. This study explored how Generation Z nurses perceive and manage ICU shift work and its impact on well-being, coping strategies, professional integration, and career sustainability. Methods: A qualitative interpretative descriptive study was conducted in ICUs of a tertiary-care academic hospital in northeastern Italy. Thirty Generation Z nurses working rotating 24-h shifts participated (mean age 25.2 years; mean ICU experience 1.7 years). Semi-structured interviews were conducted between June and September 2025, audio-recorded, and transcribed verbatim. Data were analysed inductively using Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis. Coding was performed independently by two researchers and refined through team-based analytic discussion and consensus. Results: Three themes emerged: (1) Experiencing psychophysical imbalance; (2) Seeking stability in an unstable context; and (3) Navigating professional identity. Participants described fatigue, circadian disruption, sleep disturbances, and anticipatory anxiety related to shift work. Nurses adopted coping strategies including structured routines, emotional regulation, and digital boundary-setting. Peer support facilitated professional adaptation and resilience. However, limited organisational recognition, communication barriers, and perceived undervaluation of competencies contributed to disillusionment and uncertainty about future career development. Participants questioned the long-term sustainability of shift work and considered pursuing further education or alternative career pathways. Conclusions: Generation Z nurses experience ICU shift work as demanding and potentially unsustainable early in their careers. Organisational recognition, supportive leadership, and structured transition processes appear important to promote well-being, professional integration, and workforce retention. Implications for clinical practice: These findings highlight the need for supportive leadership practices, mentorship programmes, and structured transition pathways to support the well-being, professional development, and retention of Generation Z nurses in ICUs. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Non-destructive biochemical profiling of goldenberry ripening using confocal micro Raman spectroscopy coupled with machine learning
Abstract: The accurate monitoring of the fruit ripening is crucial for maintaining quality and prevention from post-harvest economic losses. Goldenberry, being rich in vitamins, minerals, and carotenoids, yet its ripening assessment relies on variable and often subjective traditional approaches. To address this, the present study utilises rapid and non-destructive techniques using confocal micro-Raman and UV-Vis spectroscopy to track biochemical changes in both the exocarp and mesocarp of goldenberry fruit across five ripening stages: pre-mature, mature, pre-ripe, ripe, and post-ripe. The analysis of Raman spectra of exocarp shows an increase in carotenoid bands up to ripe stage, followed by a decrease at post-ripe stage, while the mesocarp exhibits a continuous increase in carotenoid intensity through stage post-ripe. The UV-Vis spectral analysis supports these observations, indicating increasing carotenoid content alongside a reduction in chlorophyll as ripening progresses. Among different machine learning (ML) approaches, unsupervised clustering demonstrates strong performance of k-means and agglomerative nesting, with high rand index values (>0.97). In supervised domain, support vector machine, logistic regression, random forest, decision tree, and principal component-linear discriminant analysis achieves the highest values of performance metrices including accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC/AUC values, and cross validation scores. Moreover, partial least squares regression analysis demonstrates excellent predictive power, with R2 = 0.93 (calibration) and 0.70 (cross-validation) for exocarp and R2 = 0.91 (calibration) and 0.89 (cross-validation) for mesocarp. The combined use of Raman with ML enables a practical and reliable framework for assessing fruit ripening, with promising applications in quality control and post-harvest management. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Sensory and consumer research with children and adolescents: A review
Abstract: Over the past decade, significant advances have been made in sensory and consumer methods tailored to children, with a growing focus on approaches that capture their perspectives more accurately. This review provides an updated overview of developments in sensory and consumer research with children and adolescents aged 4–17 years. Both classical methods (e.g., hedonic scales, paired comparison, ranking, A-Not-A tests) and innovative approaches (e.g., co-creation, projective mapping, CATA, emoji-based tools, implicit and physiological measures, temporal methods) are critically examined, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and age-appropriateness. Title: Data-Centric Architectures for Digital Business and Marketing Technologies
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The rocketing multi-channel customer data, real-time engagement spaces and AI-assisted marketing automation have presented the greatest problems ever in the quest to attain unified customer intelligence in fragmented digital environments. Conventional marketing technology (MarTech) architectures based on silos databases and batch-centric attribution pipeline analytics are challenging to provide real-time personalization, cross-channel attribution accuracy and scale-based adaptive campaign optimization. Although cloud-based solutions have enhanced scalability, they often do not provide the data-centric coherence that is essential to provide consistent customer perceptions, data lineage transparency and predictive optimization in the dynamic business environments. In this paper, we have suggested DataSphere, a data-oriented architecture model that incorporates federated data management, a real-time customer graph model, and artificial intelligence-based decision-making processes into a single Mar-Tech coordination system. The graph architecture uses cross-channel behavior prediction and next-best-action optimization based on transformers and verifiable attribution tracking based on distributed ledger technology. A simulation-based assessment is the comparison of DataSphere with conventional rule-based marketing automation systems and hybrid cloud-data-warehouse systems within the synthetic and real-world e-commerce data. Title: A Scalable Framework for Entity Resolution and Corporate Network Inference in Large Business Data
Abstract: Modern business environments produce large, complex data containing duplications, inconsistencies, and fragmented representations of ownership and control. Resolving these data into accurate and consolidated representations is critical for downstream use cases, including fraud detection, risk analysis, and regulatory compliance. Our work proposes a scalable and multi-stage entity resolution and network inference framework for business datasets from a payroll company. The framework integrates graph-based modelling and advanced analytics to eliminate redundant entities, identify ownership structures, and discover implicit relationships between them. Developed using Apache Spark and deployed in Microsoft Fabric, the pipeline achieves 85.2% resolution coverage with an estimated false positive rate of less than 3.5%, discovered over 400 tightly-knit business communities, and identified 2.3% anomalies. Authors: Zhu J.; Jiang Y.; Zhu F.; Chai Y.; Liu Y.
Title: Target item identification for injection attacks in recommender systems via graph-enhanced user representations
Abstract: Recommender systems are increasingly threatened by profile injection attacks. However, most existing defenses focus on detecting fake users, which becomes unreliable as modern attacks generate highly concealed profiles and operational platforms often lack attacker labels or attack priors. To address this limitation, we propose TIGER (Target Item Identification via Graph-Enhanced Representations), a hybrid auditing-oriented framework that reframes the final defensive output from user-level fake user labels to item-level suspicious target item candidates. Importantly, TIGER does not eliminate user-side analysis; instead, it uses unsupervised suspicious user discovery as an intermediate support step for downstream auditing. Specifically, TIGER first leverages a small trusted reference set to learn stable item embeddings and aligns unknown data into a shared semantic space. It then constructs graph-enhanced user representations by integrating rating statistics, preference patterns, and item semantics, enabling the extraction of informative suspicious user candidates for target item auditing. Finally, suspicious target item candidates are flagged through a rank-shift auditing strategy that compares recommendation outcomes before and after reintroducing suspicious users. Extensive experiments on three widely used datasets under ten representative attack scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of TIGER. Across ten attacks, TIGER achieves average DR@5/DR@10 values of 0.4430/0.6120, 0.5550/0.7500, and 0.2670/0.3400 on ML-100K, ML-1M, and Automotive, outperforming the average results of the best baseline selected for each attack by 106.20%/28.25%, 72.36%/64.84%, and 154.29%/111.18%, respectively. These results indicate that TIGER provides a reliable auditing tool for identifying high-risk target item candidates in adversarial recommender systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: ChatGPT as a Tool for Business Insight: A Case Study in Mentorship Data Analysis

Abstract: The rapid expansion of data in the business environment created the demand for tools that can transform unstructured data into actionable insights. Title: GenAI Mock Interviews for Business Chinese Learners: Benefits, Challenges, and a TAM 3 Analysis
Abstract: Grounded in Technology Acceptance Model 3 (TAM 3), this study examines intermediate-level learners’ acceptance of a generative-AI interview teaching agent (ChatGPT) for simulated Chinese job-interview practice through three constructs: perceived ease of use (PEOU), perceived usefulness (PU), and behavioral intention (BI). Ten foreign learners of Business Chinese (all master’s-level students) participated in a ChatGPT-based interview practice activity using speech recognition and spoken output to approximate real interview interaction, followed by semi-structured interviews. Findings show polarized perceptions of ease of use: some participants found the system easy and effective for practice, whereas others reported difficulties with voice input, particularly inaccurate recognition of Mandarin tones and certain words, which reduced usability. Perceived usefulness was generally positive: learners reported that generative AI helped them familiarize themselves with interview structures and procedures and provided immediate, relatively neutral feedback. However, participants also noted important limitations: the AI could not adequately correct pronunciation and intonation, showed limited tolerance for speech errors, and often provided feedback lacking depth and humanized understanding, thereby constraining learning gains. Regarding behavioral intention, most learners expressed willingness to continue using the tool—especially if speech recognition improves—and to recommend it to learners with strong self-directed learning needs. Nonetheless, they did not view AI as a replacement for teachers or face-to-face interaction. Overall, the study indicates moderate acceptance of AI-assisted interview practice and highlights the need to combine generative AI with human guidance in CFL instruction. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Bridging Transparency Gaps in Construction Claims through Blockchain Integration
Source title: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
Abstract: The construction industry plays a vital role in Pakistan's economy, yet it continues to face persistent challenges in claim administration that hinder project performance, transparency, and trust among stakeholders. This study addresses these challenges by identifying the principal shortcomings of conventional claim management systems and developing a blockchain-based claims management application to improve security, traceability, and procedural efficiency. A three-stage research design was adopted. First, a systematic literature review was conducted to identify deficiencies in traditional claim management practices. This was followed by semistructured interviews with fifteen contract specialists involved in extension of time (EOT) claims to validate and refine the identified issues. Second, a decentralized application (DApp) was developed using React.js front-end and Solidity-based smart contracts and deployed on the Polygon test network to enable faster and more cost-effective transactions. Third, the developed system was evaluated through expert review involving 32 participants drawn from contracting, consulting, client organizations, and academia, followed by statistical analysis. The findings indicate that the proposed blockchain-based claims management system (B-CMS) improves data integrity, transparency, traceability, and timeliness in claim administration compared with traditional approaches. However, the system is not intended to replace professional judgment in highly subjective claim situations and is not suitable for capturing oral instructions or unstructured design and work-pattern changes. Despite these limitations, the study demonstrates the feasibility of B-CMS for construction claim administration in Pakistan and offers insights that may be relevant to comparable project environments internationally.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Toward a Zero Trust Architecture for 6G-Enabled E-Business Ecosystem

Abstract: E-Business Information Systems (EBIS)—encompassing digital payment platforms, e-commerce order management, logistics orchestration, and B2B integration layers—face growing security challenges as they converge with 5G-Advanced and pre-6G ultra-connected environments. Heterogeneous actors and sensitive data flows render traditional perimeter-based models inadequate, requiring continuous verification and adaptive controls. Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), as defined in NIST SP 800-207, provides a promising paradigm but demands domain-specific adaptation for the unique constraints of mobile networks. This paper bridges the gap between standardization-driven research and practical E-Business security needs. We first present a critical review of prior 5G/6G security surveys, identifying the lack of holistic ZT integration and E-Business domain mapping as key research gaps. Subsequently, we evaluate the applicability of all thirteen candidate solutions outlined in 3GPP TR 33.794 (Release 19) against four criteria—transaction integrity relevance, cross-domain applicability, deployment feasibility, and latency impact—assessing their suitability for digital commerce. We derive operational guidelines for adapting these standardized mechanisms to EBIS environments, with particular attention to deployment path differentiation and regulatory compliance. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Energy transitions under anti-environmentalism via Markov chain modeling
Abstract: We analyze the effects of anti-environmentalism on the likelihood of success of the energy transition required to achieve sustainable development. We study the adoption process related to a green technology in a population formed by two sub-groups, environmentalists and anti-environmentalists, who are and are not concerned with environmental outcomes, respectively. The individual adoption decision is determined by environmental attitudes and social factors such that there exist important feedback effects within and between groups. The complexity of social dynamics and the underlying uncertainty may lead the presence of even a small group of anti-environmentalists to preclude the achievement of a green transition, especially when such agents strongly oppose the new technology or when the noise in the stochastic dynamics is sufficiently large. Authors: Qu H.; Xu J.
Title: Disruptive technological innovation strategies in manufacturing based on strategic niche management
Abstract: Disruptive technological innovation (DTI) in the manufacturing industry holds significant economic and strategic value. However, traditional innovation management frameworks based on Strategic Niche Management (SNM) theory struggle to accurately capture members’ decision-making behaviors and the “valley of death” phenomenon. This study focuses on the technology supply side to analyze the strategic decisions of manufacturing enterprises, research and development (R&D) institutions, and government in the DTI process. Based on SNM theory, we construct a delayed differential game model with niche differentiation to analyze the optimal strategies and benefits of all members. Through dynamic system stability analysis and controller-based simulations, we investigate the dynamic evolution patterns of the overall technological innovation system and derive the boundary threshold for escaping the “valley of death”. Furthermore, we conduct numerical simulations to examine the influence of different parameters on benefits and extend the model to a nonlinear technology accumulation environment. Finally, a case study is conducted to illustrate the consistency between the model conclusions and real-world observations. We find that DTI levels and total system benefits increase with niche evolution. However, when the decline in technological reserves surpasses new technological accumulation, the system enters a low-level dynamic equilibrium known as the “valley of death”. This phenomenon typically occurs at the end and transition phases of niches. Government subsidies serve as an effective incentive, significantly enhancing the engagement of manufacturing enterprises and R&D institutions. Increased time delay, self-benefit distribution coefficient, effort response coefficient, and technological sensitivity coefficient positively influence the benefits of all members. Furthermore, under a nonlinear technology accumulation environment, DTI exhibits a Matthew effect: fields with high endogenous technological growth rates accelerate their development, while those with low endogenous growth rates are highly prone to falling into the “valley of death”. Overall, we construct a DTI ecosystem for manufacturing based on SNM theory. It reveals the stages and causes of the “valley of death” and advances the application of SNM in managing DTI. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: The dynamic interplay between subjective and objective cognitive performance and their impact on the prognosis of major depressive disorder: A cross-lagged panel network analysis
Abstract: Background Subjective cognitive impairments are highly prevalent in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and, consistent with objective cognitive impairments, are associated with greater symptom severity and poorer treatment outcomes. However, their interactions and shared and distinct contributions to depressive symptoms and acute-phase clinical course remain poorly understood. Methods We analyzed 621 patients with MDD at baseline and 373 at Week 8. Treatment comprised usual care in a real-world cohort and antidepressant therapy with perospirone or placebo augmentation in a randomized, double-blind trial. Cross-sectional and cross-lagged networks integrated subjective cognition, objective cognition, and three selected depressive symptom domains. Remission-stratified and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results Subjective cognition, objective cognition, and depressive symptoms formed distinct interacting modules at both assessments, with global network strength increasing from baseline to Week 8 (ΔS = 0.65, Holm-adjusted p = 0.01). Subjective executive function was most central in non-remitters and objective processing speed in remitters. Accounting for baseline network variables, better baseline subjective executive function was associated with greater Week 8 energy ( β = 0.11), and better baseline subjective memory with greater energy and general interest (both β = 0.06). In contrast, better baseline objective immediate verbal memory was prospectively associated with worse Week 8 levels for sad mood, energy/fatigability, and general interest ( β = −0.12, −0.07, and − 0.05, respectively). Conclusions Subjective and objective cognition showed distinct associations with symptom course, supporting their combined assessment. Better baseline objective memory did not necessarily indicate fewer residual symptoms, but this association does not establish reduced treatment efficacy. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: How does blockchain address breach of contract issues in transactions?
Abstract: Blockchain, as an emerging technology, facilitates transactions in supply chain finance. This paper explores how blockchain addresses the information asymmetry between contracting parties before and after contract signing, thereby resolving corporate breach of contract issues. We conducted a two-stage game evolution analysis, demonstrating that under the blockchain model, when the marginal profit of information sharing is greater than zero and with the costs of concealing corporate breaches are high or the benefits derived from such breaches are diminished, both parties will adopt a strategy of fully sharing information and fully performing contracts. Furthermore, through empirical analysis, we emphasize the average positive effect of blockchain use in improving corporate breach of contract issues. Additionally, the heterogeneity analysis in this paper indicates that the internal factor of a company’s life cycle and external factors such as the company’s competitive intensity and media attention, respectively, influence the company’s default by affecting the completeness of information transmission, the benefits of default, and the costs of concealing a default. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A bibliometric review of farmer livelihood resilience in Indonesia: A two-decade study
Abstract: Farmer livelihood resilience is crucial given the sector's contribution to the national economic resilience, particularly in Indonesia. Despite its importance, a comprehensive synthesis of how this field has evolved over the past two decades remains limited. The objectives of this study are to provide an overview of the circumstances and challenges related to farmer resilience by examining research on farmer livelihood resilience in Indonesia. Employing a hybrid methodology that combines bibliometric analysis with a systematic literature review (SLR) guided by PRISMA protocols, this research analyzed 184 articles, 94 conference papers, and 2 review papers indexed in the Scopus database from 2005 to 2025. VOSviewer software was utilized to visualize co-occurrence networks and publication patterns. The results demonstrate a substantial increase in academic interest over the last decade, with a significant peak in publications after 2015. The analysis identified five dominant thematic clusters: (1) Smallholder Farmers’ Climate Change Adaptation in Indonesia; (2) Sustainable Agriculture and Land Conversion Policy; (3) Social Capital and Collective Action for Sustainable Agriculture; (4) Livelihood Strategies of Oil Palm and Agroforestry Farmers; (5) Sustainability of Palm Oil Smallholders. This study fills a critical research gap by bridging quantitative mapping with qualitative insights, offering a strategic roadmap for future scholarly inquiry. The findings emphasize that strengthening farmer resilience in Indonesia requires integrated policy frameworks that prioritize institutional support and optimized social capital. Ultimately, these results provide vital evidence for policymakers to design more inclusive and sustainable agricultural development strategies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Selective etching of atomically flat diamond (111) surfaces using H2+N2 plasma etching
Abstract: In this study, atomically flat (111) diamond surfaces fabricated by lateral homoepitaxial growth were employed as a platform for H2 + N2 plasma etching. Atomically flat (111) diamond surfaces have been reported to exhibit high performance in inversion-mode diamond MOSFETs, making them a promising platform for advanced diamond devices. While lateral etching is dominant in conventional hydrogen plasma etching, the introduction of nitrogen into hydrogen plasma promotes vertical etching. The etching rate was approximately 1 nm/min, and the root-mean-square (RMS) roughness ( S q) of the etched trench bottom was less than 0.25 nm. Anisotropic trenches were successfully formed, and the atomically flat surface was preserved after metal-mask removal. In contrast, previous studies using commercially available mechanically polished HPHT diamond substrates have had difficulty distinguishing the effects of surface defects and polishing-induced damage on etching behavior and surface roughness. By employing atomically flat (111) surfaces, we clearly identified N2-induced etch pits that were not observed in conventional hydrogen plasma etching, demonstrating that N2 addition promotes vertical etching on the (111) surface. Furthermore, an etching depth on the order of 100 nm was achieved while maintaining a flat surface, demonstrating the potential of the proposed process for high-precision diamond device fabrication. The influence of boron incorporated in the diamond substrate was beyond the scope of this study. The findings provide valuable insights toward the realization of diamond devices with atomically flat surfaces and are expected to contribute to further advances in device design and fabrication for diamond power electronics and quantum technologies. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: The invisible architect: Fiscal incentives and floor area ratio growth in China
Abstract: This study examines how local fiscal incentives shape the regulation of residential floor area ratio (FAR). We exploit China's intergovernmental land transfer revenue sharing reform as a quasi-natural experiment and implement a continuous-treatment DID using spatially matched land parcel data. We find that when local governments face declines in their share of land transfer revenues, they reallocate land supply toward commercial uses to broaden business tax bases, with stronger responses in cities where business tax potential is higher. This reallocation is accompanied by higher residential FAR, especially in cities with stronger business-tax potential. The floor-space results suggest that higher FAR partially offsets the contraction in residential land area. These findings provide evidence from China that fiscal institutions can shape building-intensity regulation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Beyond circularity: Topological and temporal limits of the circular economy
Abstract: The circular economy has established itself as a dominant sustainability paradigm, yet the formal properties of its foundational metaphor, the circle, remain unexamined. This paper identifies two analytically distinct constraints embedded in the dominant circular imaginary. The first is topological: when the operative metaphor functions as a single closed loop, it reproduces the cycle graph, a one-dimensional structure with zero redundancy and minimal resilience. The second is temporal: the assessment apparatus associated with circularity operates within quantitative, sequential time (chronos) and renders qualitative, heterogeneous temporalities (kairos) structurally invisible. The claim defended here is specific. Sustainability paradigms generally pose time as a problem left open; the circular economy's founding metaphor figures time as resolved (return, cycle, regeneration) while its apparatus operationalizes only chronos. This blindness is not general ignorance but performative contradiction. Empirical evidence from three continents (African solar projects, Mexican circular assessment, Peruvian extraction) substantiates the diagnosis. We propose a polyrhythmic completion structured as a wheel, with Doughnut Economics as the rim, regeneration as the hub, and ArtefactKairos (institutional devices for temporal composition) as the spokes, operationalized through the Temporal Composition Diagnostic (TCD), a four-step governance protocol. The TCD is applied to a published sugar beet pulp biorefinery assessment that models feedstock as a fixed daily input without addressing the seasonal harvest sustaining it, then calibrated ex ante against the Antamina mining region in Peru. In both settings it reveals what standard assessment cannot detect and specifies the institutional clauses it would generate. © 2026 The Author. Published by Elsevier B.V. Title: Educational legacies of christian missions: Evidence from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Abstract: This paper investigates the educational legacies of Christian missions established before independence, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, focusing on contemporary disparities in educational content, quality, access, and outcomes. Using georeferenced data from over 20,000 schools and two million students participating in the Examen National d’État (Exetat) between 2016 and 2019, as well as primary data from a phone survey of 624 school directors, we explore how proximity to Catholic and Protestant missions during the colonial period influences educational opportunities today. We find that schools near historical Christian missions offer a broader and higher-quality curriculum, with increased access to study tracks outside the basic Pedagogy section. Students attending these schools are more likely to pass the Exetat and achieve grades qualifying for university admission, although the magnitude of the effect is modest. Observable school-environment and quality characteristics attenuate the Catholic missionary-proximity coefficient by about half, while demand-side patterns point to additional differences in student composition. Our findings reveal that the strong partnership between missions and the colonial state entrenched spatial inequalities in educational access and quality, inequalities that persist to this day. © 2026

Title: Homogeneous and heterogeneous three-way granular approximations of fuzzy sets
Abstract: This paper introduces the notions of homogeneous and heterogeneous three-way granular approximations of fuzzy sets by combining and extending existing studies on rough sets and fuzzy sets. For homogeneous approximations, we take advantage of the idea of the scores of hesitant fuzzy elements, from both a direct perspective and a similarity-inspired construction. For heterogeneous approximations, we use a complete preorder on the elements of a granule determined by their membership degrees. We investigate the concept of the retrieval rate of heterogeneous three-way granular approximations of a fuzzy set in a Pawlak approximation space. We give examples to illustrate the use of these general notions. Title: Source code vulnerability detection with LLMs: A systematic evaluation of fine-tuning and multimodal fusion of code text and software metrics
Abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) present new opportunities for automated software vulnerability detection, yet their comparative behavior across models, fine-tuning conditions, imbalance strategies, and input modalities remains insufficiently characterized. We systematically evaluate 23 publicly available general-purpose, code-oriented, and security-related LLMs for binary vulnerability detection on SySeVR and Devign, comparing frozen-backbone head training with full fine-tuning. We examine data imbalance through dataset-level and training-time strategies and evaluate three input settings: software metrics only, source code only, and multimodal fusion of code and metrics. Performance is assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC AUC, execution time, and peak GPU memory usage. Fine-tuning generally improves performance, although the effects vary across datasets and metrics. Metrics-only experiments show a meaningful standalone signal on SySeVR but near-random discrimination on Devign; natural-text metric representations generally outperform structured metric embeddings. The code-only setting achieves the strongest overall performance on SySeVR, whereas multimodal gains are dataset-dependent and most evident on Devign, particularly with mid-level attention-based fusion. Artifact analysis reveals substantial overlap and template repetition in SySeVR, whereas Devign shows considerably lower overlap and repetition under the same criteria; cross-dataset experiments show weak transfer between the benchmarks. Overall, the results demonstrate that both fine-tuning gains and the usefulness of software metrics are strongly benchmark-dependent. Software metrics can complement code-text representations, but their effectiveness as standalone LLM inputs should not be generalized beyond the evaluated datasets. These findings provide a broad empirical benchmark and motivate more robust cross-dataset evaluation and multimodal vulnerability detection. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Agent Behavior Mining: Generative AI Agent Governance in Business Processes
Abstract: As organizations increasingly deploy generative AI agents to automate business processes, they face a governance dilemma: although these agents can increase operational flexibility, their non-deterministic nature challenges the control and standardization that Business Process Management seeks to enforce. This paper addresses this invisible autonomy risk by introducing Agent Behavior Mining, a governance capability that enables the application of process mining techniques to render generative AI agent decision-making observable and traceable. We (1) improve the understanding of generative AI agent behavior through an event data model that translates granular agent activities–including reasoning traces, tool usage, and token costs–into standardized process logs; (2) instantiate the data model in a multi-agent order-to-cash implementation, demonstrating how process managers can leverage agent logs to detect policy deviations and quantify operational variability; and (3) evaluate the perceived practical utility of the approach in an exploratory study with 18 industry practitioners. The results indicate that practitioners view behavioral transparency as a prerequisite for trust and consider the ability to examine agent reasoning as an important governance requirement for the next generation of AI-driven business processes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Mechanism study on the inhibition of iron precipitation behavior by microstructure transformation of slag during co-gasification of biomass and coal
Abstract: The wider application of high-iron coal in entrained-flow gasifiers is limited by the precipitation of iron-bearing minerals. The challenge can be addressed by co-gasification with silicon-rich biomass to adjust the slag silicate network structure. In this study, silicon-rich biomass (rice husk, RH) was co-gasified with high-iron coal to investigate the influence on the silicate network structure of the slag and the inhibition of iron-bearing minerals precipitation. The results showed that increasing RH content suppressed the precipitation of iron-bearing minerals by increasing the silicon content in the slag. As RH increased, the R (R = (Q4 + Q3)/(Q2 + Q1 + Q0), where R represents the degree of polymerization of the silicate network structure) increased, indicating that SiO2 promoted the formation of bridging oxygen (BO) bonds and enhanced the polymerization degree of the slag network structure. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the bond lengths of atomic pairs such as Si-O and Al-O gradually shortened, increasing interatomic forces and suppressing iron precipitation. In addition, RH addition increased the ash fusion temperatures and viscosity, reduced the slag crystallization tendency, and shifted the slag type to a glassy state, which facilitated smooth slag tapping. This study provides a theoretical basis for the co-gasification of silicon-rich biomass and high-iron coal in entrained-flow gasifiers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Procurement performance-based project success estimation and management strategy using symbiotic-attention sequential learning
Abstract: In the construction industry, procurement processes influence approximately 80% of a project’s value and directly affect key outcomes such as cost, schedule, and quality. However, existing research typically focuses on isolated procurement tasks (e.g., cost estimation or supplier evaluation), with limited attention to linking real-time procurement performance to overall project success. Inefficiencies in procurement frequently lead to delays, cost overruns, and quality issues, highlighting the need for advanced predictive tools. This study develops a Procurement Performance-Based Project Success Prediction (PP-BPSP) model to preemptively estimate project success based on ongoing procurement performance. The proposed model employs a Symbiotic-Attention Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (SABiGRU), which integrates bidirectional sequence learning with a self-attention mechanism and is optimized using the Symbiotic Organisms Search (SOS) algorithm. The model analyzes procurement metrics such as contract price variance, delivery performance, quantity sufficiency, and material quality to predict key project outcomes. The main contributions include: (1) developing a SABiGRU architecture that enhances sequential learning through attention mechanisms; (2) establishing quantitative relationships between procurement performance indicators and project success; and (3) validating the model using real-world construction project data. Results show that the PP-BPSP model significantly outperforms conventional approaches in predictive accuracy. From a practical perspective, the model enables continuous monitoring of procurement performance, provides early warnings of potential project failure, and identifies critical procurement factors requiring intervention. These capabilities support improved decision-making, cost control, schedule adherence, and quality assurance in construction project management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Portfolio optimization with decreasing absolute risk aversion stochastic dominance constraints
Abstract: An optimization method is developed for constructing investment portfolios which stochastically dominate a given benchmark for all decreasing absolute risk-averse investors, using Quadratic Programming. Title: Circular biomass waste valorisation into biolubricant for sustainable energy systems
Abstract: Scalability of biolubricant production is frequently hindered by feedstock, and valorisation of biomass waste offers a potential solution. This review examines biolubricant production pathways alongside their emerging application as transformer insulating oil. Natural ester (NE) oil offer superior biodegradability, moisture tolerance, and fire safety compared to mineral oils. Moreover, studies have already proven that biomass-derived insulating oil are technically viable and environmentally superior, but the remaining question is how to scale them up for actual use in the existing electrical grids. Therefore, it is proposed that grid-scale adoption is achievable provided that interdependent barriers of validation under real operational stresses and targeted policy that supports sustainable research are systematically addressed. To address these gaps, integration of technical, economic, and policy perspectives were conducted to provide actionable insights for biomass-derived insulating oil technology advancement. Malaysia's National Energy Transition Roadmap and complementary regulatory frameworks provide a foundation for sustainable energy infrastructure, yet with data center electricity demand expected to reach 20.9 GW by 2040, a circularity-oriented policy roadmap is essential to mitigate environmental hazards from conventional mineral oil disposal and enhance long-term grid stability. Our analysis identifies triple-helix collaboration between academia, industry, and government as essential for accelerating technology maturation, supported by targeted incentives that complement existing frameworks to ensure circular economy implementation. By addressing these aspects, transformer lifespan can potentially be extended while creating new revenue streams from biomass products. This work also mitigates environmental risks associated with mineral oil disposal and reduces reliance on fossil-based resources, while supporting UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and ensure resource circularity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Collaborative post-disaster restoration framework for transportation-distribution networks utilizing traffic management and mobile resources
Abstract: Urban distribution networks (DNs), which comprise substations, distribution buses and lines, electrical loads, and distributed energy resources, are increasingly interdependent with transportation networks (TNs). This growing interdependency increases their joint vulnerability to extreme events because failures in either network can propagate to the other and cause cascading disruptions. However, research on effective strategies to mitigate the negative impacts of these interdependencies and enhance the resilience of distribution and transportation networks remains insufficient. To address this gap, we analyze these interdependencies and propose a joint restoration framework, which co-optimizes TN traffic management strategies (including reversible lane allocation and traffic signal control) with DN restoration measures (including network reconfiguration and the dispatch of mobile energy storage systems, repair crews, and maintenance transportation crews). In this framework, the TN is illustrated using an extended Cell Transmission Model (CTM) with real-time evacuation routing to capture spatiotemporal traffic-flow dynamics, while the DN is represented with a reconfigurable DistFlow formulation. Then, a hierarchical solution approach is developed to efficiently coordinate traffic flow optimization, dynamic travel-time updating, and power restoration scheduling. Case studies on integrated distribution and transportation network test systems demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves system resilience compared to conventional separated restoration strategies, achieving higher load restoration rates and evacuation efficiency. © 2017 Elsevier Inc. Title: Optimizing multimodal deliveries with synergistic drone network design
Abstract: Problem definition: Drone-based deliveries offer significant potential to improve delivery times due to rapid deployment and independence from road conditions. However, pure drone-based cargo deliveries are expensive and restricted by drone's limited cruising range. On the other hand, pure truck freight services are efficient in well-developed road networks. To address the issue of inefficient delivery times in remote areas, we study a synergistic truck–drone network design problem that improves service performance at minimal cost. Methodology/results: We propose an optimization model that minimizes drone investment cost while meeting delivery-time targets for the longest routes. Our model uses an M/G/k queueing system to account for the waiting time during drone transportation, with the general service time distribution stemming from the heterogeneous travel time between the drone station and the discharging locations. To handle the nonlinearity of waiting time, we apply discretization and power-function approximations. The resulting nonlinear model remains tractable for solvers such as Gurobi. Managerial implications: Through a case study conducted with order information data from a major e-commerce platform in Shaanxi, China, we find that our drone network design has the potential to improve the delivery time performance by 17.17% at an economical price. Furthermore, extending the cruising range from 80 km to 120 km improves delivery time by 36.33%. We also discuss managerial insights on infrastructure design, truck–drone synergy, drone technology, and how prioritizing different portions of the longest deliveries alters the resulting design. © 2026 The Author

Title: Tree-based versus neural surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective optimization of DR-PSA biogas upgrading using MOEA/D, NSGA-III, and AGE-MOEA2
Abstract: This study presents a systematic, surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization (MOO) framework for dual-reflux pressure swing adsorption (DR-PSA) biogas upgrading, designed to overcome the computational burden of high-fidelity cyclic simulations. Machine learning surrogates were trained on 125 first-principles simulations to predict key performance indicators, including CH4 purity, recovery, bed productivity, and cycle work. To ensure statistical robustness, three established MOO algorithms were evaluated across multiple runs under bi-objective (purity versus productivity) and tri-objective (incorporating energy minimization) scenarios. The study establishes two transferable design principles: (1) surrogate selection must prioritize functional smoothness alongside accuracy, as piecewise-constant surfaces inherently mislead evolutionary search; and (2) algorithm selection should align with Pareto front geometry, with reference-point methods excelling for mildly curved fronts and geometry-adaptive methods required for curved, tri-objective manifolds. Applying this framework, the optimal DR-PSA design achieves >90% CH4 purity and ~ 90% recovery, representing improvements of approximately 18% and 16%, respectively over the unoptimized base case while reducing cycle work by up to ~50%. First-principles validation confirms that these optimal conditions are physically robust, suggesting a potentially promising, energy-efficient pathway toward high-grade biogas upgrading. Title: Combining Large Language Models with Named Entity Recognition to Automate Market Research Interview Transcription and Customer Journey Mapping – Empirical Feedback by Business Professionals

Abstract: This paper presents an automated pipeline combining large language model inference with named entity recognition to extract structured customer journey insights from interview transcripts. The system, built on Langextract library, identifies pain points, journey stages, emotions, competitors, and stage transitions with structured attributes. Title: Audiovisual aesthetic matching enhances food evaluation by amplifying pleasure and perceived tastiness
Abstract: Aesthetic experiences can shape the evaluations of consumers, including in the case of food. While matching multisensory cues can enhance perception, such interventions have not always been shown to promote consumption as effectively as predicted. The present study examined whether and how the multisensory aesthetic match of food plating and background music can enhance consumers' hedonic evaluations and purchase intentions. In two studies, participants viewed or tasted foods with varying plating aesthetics, either with music matched or mismatched in aesthetic value (e.g., ugly vs. beautiful). The participants provided food evaluations before or after tasting. The results revealed that matched audiovisual aesthetics produced enhancement effects on expected evaluations across different aesthetic levels among female participants, whereas men's ratings were enhanced only for the less-aesthetic plating. In contrast, actual evaluations were amplified only for healthy food with less-aesthetic and unhealthy food with relatively high-aesthetic plating. The multisensory enhancement of aesthetic value occurred through distinct pathways, influencing pre- and post-tasting evaluations through pleasure and perceived tastiness. These findings reveal that the mechanisms of audiovisual aesthetic matching in enhancing food consumption depend on the type of food and the gender of the participant. Aesthetic cues can be applied to nudge emotional engagement and enrich sensory experiences in daily routines, and to promote health-oriented consumption across different goal orientations (e.g., encouraging or curbing consumption). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: The Corporate Social Responsibility in Agrifood System: An Integrated Methodological Approach to Assessing Corporate Integration and Communication
Abstract: In recent decades, companies have developed innovative sustainable business management models capable of integrating green, resilient and inclusive approaches. Recently, partly as a result of EU and international regulatory guidelines, Corporate Social Sustainability (CSR) is becoming more diffuse in business models through which companies have attempted to integrate the three dimensions of sustainability (economic, social and environmental). The CSR approach has directed companies to revise their “mission” and business functions, shifting the focus from operating income to environmental and social impact. Several studies have analyzed the relationship between CSR and firm performance, between CSR and value chain, but few studies in the literature investigate the mode to communicate CSR to stakeholders, particularly through websites and in livestock enterprises. The objective of the paper is to present the methodological approach of the research, which is currently in progress, focusing on the analysis of the processes of CSR integration into business management and the related online communication of implemented sustainable actions. The integrated methodological approach is based on the analysis of the websites of Italian agribusinesses, in particular in livestock companies, using the “7S” model of analysis, supplemented by specific Focus Groups, to acquire qualitative information about the motivations toward sustainable actions, directly from a sample of companies. The paper will propose the methodological approach and initial results obtained by the analysis of the websites of a sample of livestock enterprises. The research, still in progress, will identify key drivers for the development of strategies for CSR in line with the SDGs related to the business ecosystem and could have operative developments for the application of recent European Union legislation (CSRD 2022). © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Proposal of a hybrid method for mapping local patterns in wind speed time series
Abstract: Wind speed time series modeling is particularly challenging due to its inherent nonlinear and stochastic nature. Consequently, there is a growing demand for advanced hybrid predictive methods in the wind energy sector. This study introduces a hybrid method called LocLN, which maps both linear and nonlinear local patterns. The approach is inspired by the LocPart method, employing a divide-and-conquer strategy. It is assumed that the learning process of each local subseries can be more effective than the global learning of the entire series. The results from 10 wind speed series indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method. LocLN combines fast-training models such as autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and extreme learning machines (ELM), achieving approximately 17% and 20% reductions in forecasting errors for one-hour- and three-hour-ahead horizons, respectively, compared to standalone recurrent neural network models. Additionally, the Diebold-Mariano (DM) hypothesis test on squared errors highlighted the significance of LocLN when compared to 12 other competing methods across the 10 datasets. Title: Coastal residents’ support for marine spatial planning: The role of values, place attachment, and community impacts
Abstract: Coastal environments worldwide are subject to rapid transformations, including to mitigate against climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. The potentially significant impacts of these transformations on coastal communities makes it imperative to understand their response to Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) decisions. Our research applied a value-based approach to understand how place attachment and the perceived community impacts of policy interventions influence coastal residents’ support for different MSP options that vary in emphasis between economic exploitation and nature protection. We engaged with residents around Dundalk Bay, Ireland, using a survey which presented two evidence-based MSP options (describing the status quo implying a moderate Marine Protected Area [MPA] co-existing with economic activities, versus a highly protected MPA) in randomised order. We captured participants’ personal values, economic and natural place attachment (EPA; NPA), and the perceived community impacts of each MSP option. We conducted regression analyses and a parallel-serial mediation analysis to determine each factor’s direct and indirect effects on MSP support. Most respondents preferred a shift towards stronger nature protection in the bay. Our analysis supports a multidimensional approach to place attachment and indicates that the alignment of biospheric values, NPA, and perceived community impacts is important for MSP option choice. This is less the case for EPA and its associated perceived community impacts. Overall, perceived community impacts most strongly predicted which MSP option people will support. Considering the drivers behind residents’ support for different policy options can help policymakers improve the design and communication of future MSP proposals. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Identifying Order Processing Types for Circular Production
Abstract: The successful establishment of circular production offers significant potential for companies, including reduced material costs, increased supply chain resilience, access to new business opportunities, and compliance with increasingly stringent sustainability regulations. In circular production, material loops are closed through the take-back of used products and their value-preserving recovery, refurbishment, or remanufacturing. However, the required order processing differs substantially from the order processing logic of conventional linear value creation. These differences arise from new sub-processes such as reverse logistics and reprocessing, necessary adaptations of established order processing activities, and possible changes to the underlying business model. To support companies in addressing these challenges, this paper identifies and characterizes order processing types for circular production. Similar to established types in linear production, such as make-to-stock or engineer-to-order, a typology of order processing for circular production can provide a structured understanding of different order processing logics. A combined research design integrating a systematic literature review of 17 typological approaches with an empirical analysis of 65 industrial case studies and twelve expert interviews is applied. The result is a set of eleven order processing types, characterized along four dimensions: return initiation, Re-X concept, Re-X order type, and replacement condition. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
