Title: Effects of China's Community Gridding on Coproduced Reporting of Rainstorm-Induced Emergencies: A Community-Wide Analysis
Abstract: Presently, the involvement of citizens in emergency management is inevitable and indispensable, but how to facilitate the participation of citizens remains unclear. Utilizing panel data from 174 communities in China between 2013 and 2023, this study investigated the effects of the community gridding policy (an important policy for facilitating citizen participation in public services in China) on citizens' coproduced reporting of rainstorm-induced emergencies (e.g., small-scale debris flow, water inundation, and trapped citizens) by integrating propensity score matching (PSM) and difference-in-differences (DID) methods. Statistical results showed that the community gridding significantly enhanced both citizens' reporting engagement (represented by the number of citizen reports) and reporting quality (represented by the ratio of the reports that have been accepted by communities to the total received reports). Mediating effect analysis showed that community gridding policy enhanced citizen reporting by increasing the capability of citizen training, reporting rule completeness, and technological maturity. In addition, the effects of community gridding on enhancing citizen reporting strengthened with the increase of the community scale. Furthermore, high risk perception increased the impact of community gridding on citizen reporting. The findings contribute to both the literature on and practice of emergency service coproduction and rainstorm disaster risk reduction. Moreover, those findings provide guidance of improving citizen participation for the jurisdictions that have similar rainstorm risk situations as China. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Authors: Wei S.; Hu Z.; Zhang D.; Liu X.
Title: Too personal to be accepted? How personalization visibility drives perceived surveillance and advertising intrusiveness
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: A central challenge in digital advertising is that firms seek to increase relevance through personalization, yet visibly signaling the use of personal data may provoke consumer discomfort and resistance. Guided by privacy calculus theory and communication privacy management theory, this research develops and tests a model in which personalization visibility shapes perceived intrusiveness through perceived surveillance, with data sensitivity and prior brand trust as boundary conditions. Across five studies, including four controlled online experiments and one real-world field experiment using personalized watch advertisements, we examine how explicit versus implicit personalization cues affect consumers’ privacy-related responses. Study 1 shows that explicit personalized visuals, relative to implicit personalized visuals, increase perceived intrusiveness. Study 2 validates this main effect in a live platform-based advertising environment, showing that explicit personalized visuals increase self-reported intrusiveness and produce directionally consistent behavioral ad-dismissal responses under naturally occurring exposure conditions. Study 3 replicates the effect and demonstrates that perceived surveillance partially mediates it, whereas perceived ad relevance does not account for the effect. Study 4 shows that the positive effect of explicit personalization visibility on perceived intrusiveness is stronger when the advertisement is based on sensitive rather than general consumer data. Study 5 further demonstrates that prior brand trust weakens both the direct effect of explicit personalized visuals on perceived intrusiveness and the indirect effect through perceived surveillance. These findings contribute to consumer behavior theory by identifying personalization visibility as a distinct antecedent of advertising intrusiveness and by clarifying the surveillance-based process through which visible targeting cues trigger privacy-related reactions. By combining controlled experimental evidence with field-based validation, the research also strengthens the ecological validity of the personalization visibility account. Managerially, the results suggest that firms should avoid overly conspicuous personalization cues, especially when sensitive data are involved or brand trust is weak. © 2026

Title: Agentic Business Process Modeling: Co-creating Business Processes with Human-Centric AI Agents
Abstract: Business process modeling is a highly complex, cognitively demanding task requiring deep domain understanding. While large language models make transforming natural language descriptions into formal models increasingly achievable, conventional single-prompt approaches often yield structural inconsistencies and computational inefficiency. To overcome these limitations, integrating agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems offers promising capabilities. Deploying these autonomous systems can significantly enhance execution. Such architectures iteratively construct, control, and improve models by validating logic, resolving ambiguities, and inferring implicit requirements from unstructured tasks. Yet, integrating such proactive agents into organizational workflows introduces novel socio-technical risks. When deployed with a task-centric design, these applications often impose excessive cognitive load on human modelers, negatively affecting the psychological work experience and task performance, as autonomous execution inherently limits human agency. To address these challenges, we introduce an interactive AI system for agentic process modeling, developed and evaluated through an iterative design science approach. Shifting from monolithic generation to structured collaboration, we propose a self-reflective agent architecture. The system continuously validates internal logic and actively integrates human feedback to resolve structural discrepancies. By prioritizing human-centric design, this approach mitigates risks discovered in exploratory research, including agent-induced cognitive load and the complacent acceptance of AI-generated models. Our findings offer theoretical insights and practical guidelines for configuring human-AI collaborations that ensure efficiency without compromising human agency or cognitive well-being. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Yang W.; Li J.; Wang S.; Hao Y.
Title: A context-aware dynamic ensemble interval-valued crude oil price forecasting system
Abstract: Crude oil price forecasting is crucial for economic stability and strategic planning; however, traditional point-value and static models fail to capture the market’s volatility and complexity. Existing approaches often rely on simple data processing, limited frequency models, and static ensembles; moreover, these methods typically lack interpretability. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an interval-valued ensemble forecasting system that effectively leverages multi-source mixed-frequency interval-valued information. The proposed system introduces three key innovations: a multi-stage feature engineering process that enriches information from diverse sources and overcomes the limitations of individual feature-processing algorithms; a multi-source mixed-frequency model that enables the joint processing of multiple high-frequency data streams; and a context-aware dynamic ensemble module powered by a dual-attention mechanism, which adaptively adjusts base model contributions according to prevailing market conditions while enhancing the interpretability of the developed system. Experimental evaluations show that the proposed system outperforms several advanced ensemble and state-of-the-art models, achieving Interval Root Mean Squared Errors (IRMSE) of 4.1763 and 4.5703 on West Texas Intermediate (WTI) and Brent crude oil datasets, respectively. Compared with the state of the art models, it delivers improvements ranging from 23.6% to 81.2% on the WTI dataset and from 14.2% to 76.8% on the Brent dataset. Interpretability analysis reveals the dynamic ensemble adapts its strategy intelligently, favoring different models during high volatility and strong market trends. This study thus offers a robust, transparent forecasting system for more informed and reliable decision-making. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: LLM-based multi-agent systems for code generation: A multi-vocal literature review
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled multi-agent systems to perform autonomous code generation for complex tasks. Despite the recent growth in research and industrial applications in this area, there is little work on synthesizing evidence from both academic and industrial sources to capture the current state of research on LLM-based multi-agent systems for code generation. To this end, we conducted a Multi-Vocal Literature Review (MLR), combining insights from both academia and industry, including peer-reviewed studies and grey literature. The aim of this study is to systematically synthesize and analyze existing knowledge on LLM-based multi-agent systems for code generation. Specifically, the review examines the motivations for their use, employed benchmarks and models, key challenges, proposed solutions, and potential directions for future research. We selected and reviewed 114 studies, and the key findings are: (1) the identified reasons for adopting multi-agent systems for code generation were classified into nine categories; (2) the models and evaluation benchmarks utilized across the studies were systematically analyzed to provide a structured overview of commonly adopted LLM configurations and assessment practices; (3) the reported challenges and corresponding solutions were synthesized into seven main categories and 26 subcategories; and (4) future research directions were identified and organized into six main categories and 18 subcategories. The results of this MLR will assist researchers and practitioners in pursuing further studies and supporting the real-world adoption of multi-agent systems in industrial settings. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Detection and differentiation of Salmonella Typhimurium and Salmonella Enteritidis in poultry meat using a machine learning-enabled paper chromogenic array sensor approach
Abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of Salmonella serotypes associated with foodborne illness is critical for maintaining food safety. Title: A pairwise-frontier-based classification framework for two-group classification
Abstract: Mathematical programming-based methods are widely used to generate separating boundaries in two-group classification problems. While nonlinear boundaries may often yield better performance, they typically require pre-specifying a nonlinear functional form. This contribution proposes a novel pairwise-frontier-based classification (PFC) framework that approximates nonlinear separating boundaries without the need for such a specification. The proposed PFC framework clarifies the role of axioms in classification, providing a clear basis for axiom selection based on problem characteristics. Building on this, PFC methods with nonconvex (NC) frontiers are developed, ensuring that the overlap is not artificially enlarged. To further minimize overlap, certain training observations are deliberately controlled to misclassify, provided that the total misclassification cost does not increase. This enables the extension from hard frontiers to more stable soft frontiers. The applicability of the proposed PFC methods is validated through simulation studies and real-life datasets. The results show that the proposed PFC methods are competitive with some well-established classifiers. Specifically, the PFC-NCSoft method demonstrates superior average performance and greater stability, making it particularly suitable for imbalanced classification tasks. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: AI-Decision Checkpoints for AI-Augmented Business Process Management: Framework and Educational Instantiation
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and AI agents are increasingly embedded in operational business processes. Yet Business Process Management (BPM) curricula and frameworks still largely treat artificial intelligence (AI) as an add-on technology, leaving graduates (as potential future process developers) unprepared to reason about AI as a first-class design element of end-to-end processes. This paper addresses that gap by proposing AI-decision checkpoints: explicit moments in a process development trajectory where process developers identify AI-candidate sub-processes, assess expected effects on time, cost, quality, and flexibility, consider legal and organisational constraints, and document a reasoned decision to adopt, constrain, or reject specific AI components. A preliminary formative reflection draws on instructor observations, submitted artifacts, and discovered process maps from learning-management-system logs. Title: Flexible ambition: How to make bold first offers without backlash
Abstract: One of the most vexing dilemmas negotiators experience is whether to make the first offer—and how ambitiously to do so. Although research finds that ambitious first offers lead to better outcomes on average, they can also incite extreme boomerang counteroffers, impasses, and resentment. We call these countervailing effects the first-offer double bind: Modest first offers produce poor economic outcomes, but ambitious first offers risk economic and relational backlash. To overcome the first-offer double bind, negotiators need to present their ambitious first offer in ways that invite conciliatory rather than competitive reactions. In this article, we introduce a generalizable solution to the first-offer double-bind: present ambitious first offers that signal flexibility. We highlight several strategies for producing flexible ambition: (a) frame ambitious proposals as offers vs. requests, (b) highlight how one's ambitious offer benefits the other side vs. oneself, (c) propose an ambitious range vs. point value, and (d) present ambitious multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (MESOs) vs. a single package offer. Each strategy preserves or strengthens the first-offer anchor, tethering counteroffers to the first offer, while guiding receivers to see ambitious offerers as less aggressive and more cooperative. We close by considering two research frontiers. First, we propose that the flexible ambition approach can mitigate other double binds more broadly, including the gender, social class, and low-power double binds; preliminary evidence suggests that MESOs work equally well for high and low power negotiators and for men and women. Title: BaCu₃ScSe₄ and BaCu₃YSe₄ quaternary selenides: a first-principles exploration of mechanical, optical, and energy-conversion properties
Abstract: An emerging platform for energy-conversion and optoelectronic devices is quaternary chalcogenides. Around Ba and the trivalent cations, DOS and charge-density maps reveal a mixed ionic nature with dominating Cu-Se covalency. Optical spectra derived from complex dielectric function yield prominent optical response. Photocatalytic water splitting potential of compounds shows efficient water splitting. BaCu₃ScSe₄ exhibits higher electrical and thermal conductivities temperature-dependent transport, while BaCu₃YSe₄ yields a higher Seebeck coefficient and figure of merit. Title: Ethnomedicinal use and cytotoxicity of medicinal plants used in soft porridge for infant health issues in Vhembe District, South Africa
Abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance: In South Africa, the Vhavenda tribe traditionally feed infants Tshiunza/Khongoḓoli, a very light, warm, and soft porridge prepared with medicinal plant concoctions. This practice is believed to prevent, manage, or treat various diseases and provide nutritional support. Aim of the study: The aim of the study was to document the medicinal plants administered through soft porridge, including preparation methods and dosages for infant illnesses, among the Vhavenda tribe of Vhembe District, South Africa, and to determine the cytotoxicity of selected medicinal plants. Materials and methods: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with caregivers, elderly women, and traditional healers. Cytotoxicity assay of five selected medicinal plants was conducted using the MTT assay on African monkey kidney cells (Vero cells). Results: Seventy-two medicinal plants were documented, of which 38 were used in the preparation of Tshiunza/Khongoḓoli. Roots were the most frequently used plant part, and the dominant preparation method involved soaking plant material in water and using the extract to make the soft porridge. These plants were commonly used to treat fontanelle-related illnesses and stomach problems. Combretum molle R.Br. ex G.Don. and Gymnosporia buxifolia (L.) exhibited low cytotoxicity with IC50 of 476.7559 and 276.4863 μg/mL, respectively. Title: Gender Imbalance and the Leadership Legitimacy Gap: Post-conflict Transformation of Classroom Discourse in Ukrainian Business Education
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Periods of war and large-scale social disruption frequently reshape educational environments, altering patterns of participation, authority, and identity formation within the classroom. Ukraine’s ongoing war has accelerated demographic and institutional changes across higher education. Wartime conscription, migration, and displacement have produced classrooms in which women significantly outnumber men, particularly in business education programs. This demographic shift has not only changed the composition of the classroom but has also transformed the nature of discourse, leadership expression, and perceptions of legitimacy among students. Drawing on qualitative field observations from teaching and residence in Kyiv and Dnipro, this study examines how gender imbalance influences leadership dynamics and classroom interaction in a wartime academic context. Data were collected through semi-structured and informal interviews with approximately 35 undergraduate and graduate business students, complemented by direct classroom observation. The study adopts an interpretive, practice-based approach, focusing on how students construct and negotiate leadership roles in real time within an evolving institutional environment. The findings identify the emergence of what this study conceptualizes as a “Leadership Legitimacy Gap”— a divergence between rapidly evolving leadership practice and slower institutional recognition among female students and the slower adaptation of institutional norms, expectations, and recognition structures. Unlike traditional gender-based leadership barriers, the Leadership Legitimacy Gap reflects a temporal mismatch between evolving leadership practice and slower institutional recognition under conditions of disruption. While women increasingly assume active roles in discussion, decision-making, and professional aspiration, institutional frameworks and inherited cultural expectations do not always fully acknowledge or reinforce these shifts. At the same time, the absence or reduced presence of male students alters the diversity of perspectives and reshapes the dynamics of classroom discourse, leading to new forms of consensus, contestation, and identity formation. This study contributes to cultural and educational studies by highlighting how post-conflict conditions reconfigure not only access and participation but also the symbolic and discursive foundations of leadership. It extends existing literature on gender and leadership by situating these dynamics within a wartime, post-Soviet context, where institutional transformation lags behind social and demographic change. The concept of the Leadership Legitimacy Gap offers a framework for understanding similar dynamics in other post-conflict and rapidly transforming educational environments. The study contributes to leadership and knowledge management literature by demonstrating how legitimacy shapes knowledge recognition, participation, and influence, particularly in disrupted educational environments where authority and contribution are no longer aligned. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Towards Agent-Based Automation beyond RPA: An Exploratory Design Science Study in the Public Sector
Abstract: Large organizations increasingly explore large language models (LLMs) to support knowledge-intensive process work. While Robotic Process Automation (RPA) has proven effective for rule-based and structured activities, many process improvement opportunities remain inaccessible due to unstructured natural-language artifacts that require human interpretation. This paper investigates how agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems can support process improvement by transforming interpretative work rather than merely automating execution tasks. The artifact integrates LLM-based agents into a software development business process by transforming unstructured user interface (UI) specification documents into structured JSON-based UI representations, executable code components, and automatically generated test cases. The study explores how agentic capabilities affect process structures, handover artifacts, and human roles within an existing workflow. The artifact is evaluated in a real-world setting using a mixed-method approach combining quantitative efficiency measurements and qualitative expert assessments. Results indicate significant reductions in manual transformation effort as well as improved standardization and reduced interpretative ambiguity. At the same time, the findings highlight the need for structured specification practices and human validation mechanisms. Title: Platform abandonment through push–pull–mooring: Trust, commitment, and generational patterns in U.S. social media
Abstract: Generational frameworks frequently explain platform adoption, but rarely platform abandonment. Through a stratified survey of 990 U.S. adults, this study examines how age cohorts (digital natives vs. digital immigrants) respond to platform change and what predicts abandonment across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, and TikTok. Using the push-pull-mooring (PPM) framework, we found that cohort labels did not predict exit in pooled models. Distrust was the strongest pooled push predictor. Title: Heterogeneous edge AI orchestration: A systematic review, taxonomy and future directions
Abstract: The confluence of Machine Learning (ML), Edge, and containerization has resulted in the emergence of Edge AI, which enhances reliability, fault tolerance, data security and privacy, inference time and accuracy. On one hand, accelerated hardware and advanced interconnects have reduced training times and improved accuracy. Leveraging this, the orchestration engines automate workload management but often struggle with limited features and sub-optimal policies. Edge offers a myriad of interconnected devices employing hardware and orchestration engines, but these devices are inherently distributed and resource-constrained, which adversely impacts Edge AI adoption. Moreover, leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Edge orchestration to optimize resource provisioning, scheduling, and management without compromising the quality of service has been the driving motivation. However, integrating these components to enable Edge AI poses substantial challenges encompassing the hardware, interconnects, orchestration engines, computational, application, and workload heterogeneities. Additionally, training data scarcity, constrained and heterogeneous resources, control plane management overhead, delayed data traversal, and other factors exacerbate Edge AI orchestration challenges. Considering these challenges and opportunities, this paper establishes a top-to-bottom architectural view to investigate cross-layer Edge AI orchestration progress across three layers. At the bottom layer, NVLink, Compute Express Link, and other heterogeneous interconnects that manage the underlying hardware are discussed and compared in terms of offered bandwidth, latency, topology, and other features. In the middle layer, heterogeneous container orchestration engines and their high/low-level runtimes are contrasted for Edge AI. For the top layer, a systematic review of research works empowering heterogeneous Edge AI orchestration which proposed heuristic, meta-heuristic, optimization, and AI/ML solutions for container migration, autoscaling, ML/DL model-switching, resource forecasting, and scheduling is conducted. Furthermore, this article investigates the employment and position of Generative AI in Edge computing. Subsequently, taxonomies of optimization models, ML/DL models, orchestration engines, runtimes, and orchestration objectives are provided. Finally, the identified research gaps and possible future directions conclude this article. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Talking to the screen: Influencer nonverbal cues and observed platform engagement in Douyin travel short-form videos

Abstract: Short-form travel videos have become important digital service touchpoints, yet little is known about how influencers' auditory and visual nonverbal cues jointly relate to cumulative observed likes. Highlighter gestures were more favorably associated with likes at higher vocal intensity, although this evidence was comparatively limited. Title: The value of information in stochastic-dynamic RoRo ship cargo handling
Abstract: This paper addresses the planning of loading and unloading processes, also termed stevedoring, for Roll-on/Roll-off (RoRo) ships. We consider a setting where we sequence operations, assign tugs to handle trailers, and determine the cargo positions on the ship and in the yard. In real-world settings, the outcomes of these decisions are strongly affected by stochastic uncertainty, such as considering the type of cargo to unload or traffic congestion on the ship. To account for this, we formulate the problem as a sequential decision process and describe two feature-based policy function approximations for the decision-making. We propose an effective heuristic for designing policies in an offline learning process. We evaluate this approach in a case study at the Port of Kiel, Germany, simulating the service operations of a three-deck RoRo ship. Compared to industry benchmark policies, the proposed policies reduce the ship's turnaround time by up to 26 min (8.8%). Additionally, we apply our methodology to illustrate the value of various levels of information availability. The results show that information on process completion times, especially for vehicle entry and exit at both the ship and the yard, has the potential to shave off turnaround time by an additional 8%. Title: Enhancing IT Incident Management Through BPM and ITIL V4 Integration: A Case Study in the Automotive Sector

Abstract: In the context of Industry 4.0, the automotive sector faces significant challenges in maintaining service continuity due to the increasing volume of IT incidents and the lack of formalized management processes. This study aims to optimize incident management in a Peruvian automotive dealership by proposing and validating an integrated model that combines Business Process Management (BPM) with ITIL V4 practices. Title: Artificial intelligence in negotiation research: From computational negotiators to psychological evidence
Abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence are reshaping how negotiation is conducted and studied. AI systems increasingly enter negotiation research in two broad roles: as part of the negotiation process, either as negotiators or as support for human negotiators, and as research instruments that annotate, standardize, and simulate negotiation at scale. As negotiators, these systems range from theory-driven agents to data-driven and hybrid agents, each embedding different assumptions about negotiation. As instruments, they promise scale, consistency, and control, but also raise risks of circular inference, in which AI appears to reveal patterns in human negotiation while actually reproducing patterns learned from its own training data. This review organizes emerging work on AI and negotiation around these two roles and argues that their scientific value depends on psychological grounding. Title: A gas sensing domain adaptation method for electronic nose systems based on subdomain adaptation with active learning
Abstract: In practical deployment, electronic nose (E-nose) systems often encounter distribution shifts arising from long-term sensor drift, storage-temperature-induced changes in volatile profiles, or their coexistence, which can substantially degrade target-domain recognition. Although domain adaptation (DA) can reduce source-target distribution discrepancies, unsupervised class-conditional alignment remains vulnerable to unreliable target-domain pseudo-labels. Meanwhile, active learning (AL) can acquire limited target-domain labels, but existing E-nose studies mainly use them to update classifiers rather than further guide class-conditional cross-domain alignment. We therefore propose Subdomain Adaptation with Active Learning (SAAL), a semi-supervised active DA framework for reliable E-nose recognition with limited target-domain annotation. SAAL integrates prototype contrastive learning, which promotes intra-class compactness and inter-class separation within each domain, with Local Maximum Mean Discrepancy (LMMD), which aligns corresponding source and target subdomains at the class-conditional level. Its active learning module combines entropy–margin uncertainty estimation with K-means clustering to select informative and representative target-domain samples for annotation. The queried samples and their ground-truth labels act as local class anchors to improve pseudo-label reliability and support subsequent semi-supervised subdomain adaptation. On the Vergara gas sensor drift dataset, SAAL achieved an average accuracy of 94.08% using 162 labeled target samples. On the self-collected oyster freshness dataset, it achieved an average accuracy of 95.25% using 90 labeled target samples under compound-shift conditions related to storage-temperature variation. These results demonstrate that SAAL improves E-nose recognition under long-term sensor drift and storage-temperature-related distribution shifts with limited target-domain annotation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Comparison of staff-deployed and patient-directed electronic meal ordering systems: Patient experiences and food intake in an Australian acute care hospital
Abstract: Hospital foodservice plays a critical role in patient satisfaction, nutritional intake, and recovery; however, evidence comparing electronic meal ordering systems (eMOSs) remains limited. This study assessed differences in patient satisfaction, self-reported food intake, and reasons for incomplete meal consumption between staff-deployed and patient-directed eMOSs in an Australian acute care hospital. A survey comprising quantitative items and optional free-text comments was distributed via lunch trays across the same participating wards during the staff-deployed eMOS period and repeated following implementation of the patient-directed eMOS. Fifty-one and sixty-one patients completed the survey during the respective study periods. No significant differences in patient satisfaction across foodservice domains or self-reported food intake were observed between systems. Across both groups, food quality was rated lowest, while the dining environment received the highest ratings. Incomplete meal consumption was primarily attributed to dissatisfaction with food quality, including unappealing presentation, disliked taste, and unsuitable food types, as well as reduced appetite and illness-related factors. Thematic analysis identified food quality (flavour, temperature, presentation, and menu variety), and the meal ordering process as central to patient experience. While overall satisfaction did not differ between systems, the nature of negative experiences varied: the staff-deployed eMOS was limited by staffing capacity, whereas the patient-directed eMOS was constrained by usability challenges with television-based interfaces. These findings indicate that eMOS implementation alone is unlikely to improve patient outcomes. Optimising hospital foodservice requires integrating high-quality food provision with accessible, user-centred meal ordering systems to enhance patient satisfaction, support dietary intake, and potentially reduce food waste. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The role of masculinity in understanding gender gaps in negotiation
Abstract: We review empirical research on masculinity processes in negotiations. Studies to date are typically based on the precarious manhood thesis, which suggests that men seek to demonstrate their manhood to others, or on evolutionary psychology, which suggests that men are susceptible to evolutionary pressures to compete for mates. The current empirical literature on masculinity and negotiation suggests that men negotiate assertively, or even unethically, when they perceive their manhood to be threatened. Moreover, research repeatedly has shown that men's negotiation behavior is influenced by counterpart attributes, particularly the gender of the counterpart. Future research on the role of culture, the propensity to initiate negotiations as a criterion, power, and countermeasures for unethical negotiation behavior is needed. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Is sustainable design effective? An empirical life cycle assessment of environmental impacts in basketball footwear production
Abstract: The footwear industry is characterized by labor-intensive and resource-consuming production. Sustainable design provides a pathway for reducing the environmental burdens of footwear manufacturing, yet its benefits may vary across production processes and impact categories. This study conducts a high-resolution cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment of basketball footwear by linking upstream material acquisition with seven manufacturing processes and compares eight prospective sustainable design scenarios. Environmental hotspots are evaluated using ReCiPe 2016 at midpoint and endpoint levels. Results indicate that raw material acquisition dominates impacts related to toxicity, land use, and resource consumption, while manufacturing dominates global warming potential (GWP) and water consumption potential. At the process level, blanking of upper materials and sole manufacturing are major contributors to endpoint damage, mainly due to textile inputs, petroleum-based polymers, and manufacturing energy demand. Scenario analysis reveals that the reduction scenario (S7), which combines a 3D-printed TPU upper, adhesive-free sole joining, and packaging reduction, provides a relatively balanced environmental response, reducing GWP from 6.44 to 5.90 kg CO₂-eq without the pronounced cross category burden increases observed in the combined scenario (S8). Although S8 achieves the greatest GWP reduction (5.41 kg CO₂-eq), it increases freshwater eutrophication and ecotoxicity burdens. Monte Carlo simulation confirms the robustness of these carbon reductions and the persistence of several trade-offs. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating sustainable design across multiple environmental impact categories rather than carbon reduction alone. High-resolution modeling can support process optimization and sustainable design decisions through precise identification of environmental hotspots. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: From Opportunity to Growth: A Case Study of THIRD POLE AI as an AI-Native Operating System
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is moving from experimental chat interfaces to embedded business infrastructure. Yet many organizations still adopt AI through fragmented tools that produce isolated outputs instead of integrated operational value. Agencies, consulting firms, development organizations, event companies, startups, enterprises and government contractors often manage opportunities, strategy, proposal writing, creative production, client management, events, project delivery, talent sourcing and reporting through disconnected systems. This paper presents THIRD POLE AI as a case study and implementation model for an AI-native operating system that connects these functions into one intelligent workspace. The paper frames generative AI not merely as a content generation layer, but as an operating model for turning opportunities into strategies, strategies into creative and proposals, proposals into projects, and projects into measurable growth. Drawing on retrieval augmented generation, large language model orchestration, AI agents, prompt engineering, human-in-the-loop review and responsible AI governance, the paper proposes pragmatic architecture, workflow methodology, governance model and evaluation framework. A small retrospective internal pilot using anonymized opportunity and proposal workflows is added to test the model against baseline manual workflows. The pilot indicates material reductions in preparation time and revision cycles, while improving compliance completeness and source traceability. The contribution is to identify the operational gap between AI experimentation and business transformation, and to show how an AI-native business operating system can improve speed, quality, delivery discipline and institutional learning while keeping humans accountable for commitments and public claims. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: UDA2L: Unsupervised deformation-aware adaptive learning for medical image registration
Abstract: Medical image registration plays a key role in diagnosis, therapeutic strategy design, and longitudinal studies. However, the existing methods are prone to misregistration when encountering complex anatomical changes, making it difficult to effectively maintain the topological consistency of anatomical structures. To address these problems, we propose an unsupervised deformation-aware adaptive learning method (UDA2L) for medical image registration, in which deformation information is explicitly used to guide high-risk region perception, hierarchical feature interaction, and consistency regularization. Specifically, an adaptive High-risk Deformation Area-Aware Mechanism (HDA2M) introduces deformation-field gradient information into the attention modeling process, enabling the network to emphasize regions with unstable or large local deformations. A Triple-view Hierarchical Feature Integration (THFI) module jointly integrates fixed-image features, moving-image features, and deformation-field representations through a coarse-to-fine pyramid structure, thereby strengthening deformation-appearance coupling and capturing both fine-grained anatomical details and global contextual information. Moreover, Cross-Cycle Consistency (C3) learning imposes bidirectional deformation consistency and residual-level reconstruction constraints to improve local alignment accuracy and enhance the topological stability of the learned deformation field. Experimental results on multiple 3D brain MRI image datasets (including three single-modality and one cross-modality) show that UDA2L achieves relatively ideal performance and efficiency in the image registration task, demonstrating its application prospects in this field. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Development, CT characterization, and IAEA TECDOC-1583-based dosimetric evaluation of a low-cost heterogeneous thoracic phantom for radiotherapy TPS quality assurance
Abstract: Background and Purpose : Accurate verification of treatment planning systems (TPS) dose calculations in heterogeneous media is essential for radiotherapy quality assurance (QA). However, commercial heterogeneous phantoms are often inaccessible in resource-limited settings. This study aimed to design, fabricate, and dosimetrically validate a low-cost heterogeneous phantom using locally sourced surrogate materials and to compare selected measurements with a commercial CIRS IMRT Thorax Phantom. Materials and methods A semi-elliptical phantom measuring approximately 30 × 20 × 23 cm3 was fabricated using paraffin wax as the bulk soft-tissue-equivalent material with embedded particleboard, bovine tibia, and Styrofoam inserts representing adipose, bone, and lung-equivalent regions, respectively. The fabricated and CIRS phantoms were scanned using a 120 kVp CT simulator, and material HU values, mass densities, and electron densities were characterized. Treatment plans were generated in Eclipse using the Anisotropic Analytical Algorithm with a 2.5 mm calculation grid. The fabricated phantom was evaluated using the complete IAEA TECDOC-1583 test matrix, comprising 8 test cases and 14 measurement points. In addition, selected comparative measurements were performed using a commercial CIRS phantom for representative open-field and RapidArc cases at two measurement positions. Absolute point-dose measurements were performed using calibrated ionization chambers with temperature-pressure, polarity, and ion-recombination corrections. Results Paraffin wax and bovine tibia showed reasonable agreement with soft-tissue and bone reference values, respectively. Styrofoam approximated the low-density behavior of the CIRS lung insert but was substantially less dense than average human lung. Electrometer readings across the TECDOC-1583 points ranged from 18.92 to 21.26 nC. Ten of 14 measurement points met the predefined agreement criterion, with the largest deviations of approximately 8%. Selected CIRS phantom measurements for open-field and RapidArc deliveries remained within ±5%. However, because the commercial CIRS phantom was tested only for selected cases, the comparison with CIRS should be interpreted as supportive rather than comprehensive benchmarking. Conclusion The fabricated phantom provides a practical low-cost platform for preliminary heterogeneous TPS QA and demonstrated acceptable agreement for most tested conditions. Larger deviations in low-density or heterogeneous regions indicate the need for improved lung-equivalent material selection, detailed uncertainty analysis, and further validation using advanced dose algorithms and two-dimensional dosimetry. With further refinement and validation, the phantom could provide an accessible option for heterogeneity-focused TPS verification in radiotherapy centers with limited access to commercial phantoms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Bridging game-theoretic modeling and Artificial Intelligence for fast policy recommendations in multi-channel retail
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Emerging-market milk retail is increasingly split across General Trade, Modern Trade, and E-commerce, where pricing and advertising are strategically interdependent through cross-channel substitution, advertising spillovers, and trust-sensitive demand. Yet decision support is challenging: game-theoretic models capture these interactions but are costly to solve repeatedly, while standard machine learning approaches typically require rich quantitative data, often unavailable in fragmented markets where key drivers (e.g., “low trust”) are qualitative. This paper bridges this gap by proposing a hybrid simulation–surrogate decision-support framework that operationalizes omnichannel theory into rapid decision support. First, a tri-channel game-theoretic simulator incorporating trust, advertising spillovers, and cost heterogeneity generates constrained solver benchmark pricing and advertising decisions. Second, to reduce repeated equilibrium-solving costs during scenario evaluation, a lightweight policy network is trained to approximate this structural mapping, providing feasible scenario-based recommendations at low computational cost. A rule-based natural-language descriptor layer operationalizes qualitative managerial inputs by mapping predefined cues into parameterized intervals. Across 10,000 simulated market states, the trained surrogate policy closely approximates the solver-generated benchmark decisions, with evaluation on the held-out test set yielding a mean profit ratio of 1.001, a trimmed profit ratio of 0.999, and mean economic regret of 0.40%. Stress tests under alternative parameter distributions and comparative evaluations against linear, tree-based, and heuristic baselines indicate the network's stable economic performance across regular simulated market states; while batched evaluations accelerate interactive scenario analysis by up to 14.8 times. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Decarbonization pathways for the dust-proof nets industry
Abstract: Plastic dust-proof nets (DPNs) are widely used for mitigating construction fugitive dust to safeguard urban air quality. However, the DPN life cycle entails energy consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from production and plastic pollution from end-of-life disposal. This study develops an integrated framework combining Material Flow Analysis (MFA) and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) to evaluate the resource and environmental impacts of the DPN industry across its entire life cycle under four scenarios. A roadmap for decarbonization by 2060 is also developed. The results indicate that by 2060, under a business-as-usual scenario, GHG emissions from China’s DPN industry could reach 6.14 Mt CO2e, representing increases of 5.9% in GHG emissions and 7.5% in economic costs compared to 2021 levels. Scenario analysis highlights the importance of enhancing recycling rates to reduce energy use, GHG emissions, and plastic pollution. These measures are critical for establishing a closed-loop supply system in this industry, which is key to synergizing GHG emission reduction, pollution control, and economic development. Compared to the baseline scenario, the optimal scenario achieves a 14.0% increase in economic cost while concurrently reducing GHG emissions by 47.3% and plastic pollution by 28.2%. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Development of a phenomenological spray model for next generation dual-fuel marine engines: validation in free-field conditions
Abstract: This study develops and validates a reduced-order phenomenological spray model for dual-fuel marine engines operating under reactivity controlled compression ignition (RCCI) conditions. Rather than introducing a new spray-theory class, the work adapts a Musculus-based formulation into an RCCI-oriented framework capable of predicting both spray penetration and cylinder-fixed fuel–air stratification at low computational cost. The main methodological advance is the introduction of a CV-to-zone mapping strategy for transferring spray control-volume information into the zonal structure required by multi-zone combustion models; among the three tested approaches, an angled non-uniform mapping gave the most accurate stratification representation. Validation is via high-speed optical measurements by the Optical Spray Combustion Chamber and high-fidelity CFD simulations with CONVERGE. Sensitivity analysis identified the discharge coefficient (Ca) and velocity profile factor (β) as dominant calibration parameters, with profile evolution factor (α) serving as a secondary shaper of radial distribution. A two-stage optimization strategy for local tuning per case and global tuning across conditions demonstrated that the globally calibrated model reproduces spray penetration within ∼14% of CFD, and peak high-reactivity fuel location within ±2 zones across calibration and validation datasets. Amplitude prediction of peak fuel fraction exhibited larger scatter (∼40%), but location fidelity was robust. The framework provides a reliable and computationally efficient surrogate for spray-mixing dynamics and is well suited for future integration with fast 0D/1D multi-zone combustion models to support predictive, cycle-resolved simulation of advanced RCCI engines. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Hydrological restoration in arid wetlands promotes vegetation recovery by alleviating antagonistic interactions between salinity and soil properties
Abstract: The antagonistic interaction between salt stress and soil properties in arid-zone wetlands is a core issue affecting vegetation growth; whether degraded wetlands in these regions can be restored under limited water availability is a current challenge, and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To reveal the mechanisms and effects of hydrological restoration, we investigated a representative wetland restoration project in an arid region of China and integrated soil properties, microbial activity, and plant functional traits to reveal how the restoration approach alleviated the antagonistic interaction between salt stress and soil properties. The results indicate that salt stress is a primary constraint on vegetation recovery in arid wetlands. Hydrological restoration effectively reduced salinity, leading to significant increases in vegetation height and biomass. In addition, soil properties improved, thereby promoting vegetation recovery, with soil organic carbon (SOC) showing the most pronounced increase (53.2%) under long-term flooding. Vegetation responds to environmental stress by adjusting its resource acquisition strategies: under drought conditions, plants exhibit an acquisition-oriented strategy, preferentially allocating nutrients to stems, whereas under stable flooding conditions, vegetation functional traits shift toward a more conservative strategy. Structural equation modeling (SEM) further confirmed that hydrological restoration positively affected vegetation AGB and PH. Ecological water supplementation not only significantly alleviated the direct stress of salinity on plant growth but also promoted SOC accumulation, while improvements in hydrological and soil conditions indirectly enhanced vegetation recovery by altering plant resource-acquisition strategies. Overall, these findings demonstrate the coupled interactions between salinity, soil properties, and vegetation during hydrological restoration, providing a scientific reference for formulating wetland restoration strategies based on water availability in arid regions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Organizational Memory for Agentic Business Process Execution

Abstract: LLM-based agents offer new opportunities for automating business process execution beyond the limits of rule-based systems. However, general-purpose LLMs lack the organization-specific knowledge required for reliable execution, which is typically fragmented across human-oriented artifacts such as policies, process models, and standard operating procedures. While such knowledge can technically be encoded in individual prompts or agent-specific retrieval setups, this approach does not scale in enterprises, as it gives rise to knowledge silos and rule duplicates, and makes consistent updates and learning across agents difficult. We argue that this calls for an organizational memory for agentic business process execution: a shared, governed, and agent-consumable reference layer of evolving organization-specific procedural knowledge about how work should be executed. Title: Resource-constrained parallel machine scheduling with setups, job release/due time, and resource transition limit
Abstract: The unrelated parallel machines scheduling problem with setup times and additional resources (UPMSR) is common in the manufacturing and service sectors, requiring the optimal assignment of jobs to machines supervised by limited additional resources. This paper investigates how to efficiently solve the UPMSR considering manufacturing constraints such as job release times, due dates, machine eligibility, and resource transition limits per machine. Previous research has not addressed this combination of real-world industrial constraints, leaving limitations on practical and scalable scheduling algorithms for the UPMSR. To address this gap, we develop a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model and introduce a novel biased random key genetic algorithm (BRKGA) approach. We demonstrate the scalability of BRKGA compared to the MILP model on synthetic datasets based on a real-world case study of a food processing plant. Furthermore, we demonstrate that BRKGA either outperforms or matches state-of-the-art metaheuristic and exact methods on benchmark datasets from the literature. Title: Digital Transformation for Sustainable Business

Abstract: Digital transformation has become a key enabler of sustainable business by integrating advanced technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data Analytics (BDA), and Cloud Computing (CC) into organizational processes. These technologies improve operational efficiency while supporting environmental sustainability through enhanced Resource Optimization (RO), Energy Efficiency (EE), and data-driven decision-making. Despite significant progress in this area, existing studies primarily focus on individual technological or sustainability aspects and often lack a unified framework for jointly evaluating digital maturity and sustainability performance. To address this gap, this paper proposes an integrated quantitative framework that combines the Digital Transformation Index (DTI), Sustainability Performance (SP), and an optimization-based performance function within a single analytical model. The proposed framework enables the simultaneous assessment of digital capability and sustainability outcomes while incorporating environmental constraints into the evaluation process. Simulation-based analysis demonstrates that organizations with higher DTI values consistently achieve improved SP and Overall Performance (OP). Moreover, the optimization mechanism effectively satisfies carbon emission constraints while maintaining high organizational performance, confirming the robustness and applicability of the proposed framework. The results highlight the positive relationship between digital transformation and sustainable business performance, demonstrating that strategic adoption of digital technologies enhances operational efficiency, strengthens competitiveness, improves stakeholder engagement, and supports responsible production and consumption practices. Overall, the proposed framework provides a scalable and systematic approach for evaluating sustainable digital transformation and offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to align technological innovation with long-term sustainability objectives. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Does retirement reduce household carbon emissions in China? Evidence from fuzzy regression discontinuity design
Abstract: This study examines the causal effect of household-head retirement on household carbon emissions (HCEs) in China. Combining multi-wave data from the China Family Panel Studies with household carbon accounting, we construct household-level total carbon emissions (TCEs), distinguishing between direct carbon emissions (DCEs) from household energy use and indirect carbon emissions (ICEs) embodied in the goods and services purchased by households. We estimate the local causal effect of retirement using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design based on China's statutory retirement age of 60 for urban male household heads. The results show that retirement significantly reduces TCEs by approximately 7.4–9.0 tCO₂ per household. This reduction is driven primarily by lower ICEs, while the estimated effect on DCEs is statistically insignificant. Point estimates are larger for households headed by individuals without tertiary education and for low-asset households, but formal bootstrap tests do not reject equality across education or asset groups. The mechanism results suggest that the decline in ICEs is mainly associated with a contraction in overall household consumption, particularly reductions in non-subsistence and work-related expenditure, with limited evidence of a broad shift in consumption composition. Disaggregated results further show that the emission reductions are concentrated in clothing, household facilities and services, and transportation and communication. These findings provide local causal evidence that retirement reshapes HCEs mainly through reductions in consumption-based indirect emissions rather than through changes in direct household energy use, highlighting the importance of life-course transitions for understanding demand-side emission dynamics in aging societies. © 2026

Title: Integration of CO2 capture using rotating packed beds in heavy-duty trucks: Process modeling and techno-economic optimization
Abstract: This study investigates for the first time the integration and optimization in a heavy-duty vehicle of a carbon capture system that is based on a Rotating Packed Bed (RPB), targeting reductions in transportation-related emissions. The system operates through chemical absorption of the exhaust gases in a 30 wt.% aqueous monoethanolamine (MEA) solution, followed by thermal regeneration of the solvent. A custom mathematical model is developed to represent the underlying physicochemical processes, while an optimization algorithm is applied to identify the optimal size and operating settings. The employed objectives include cost and weight minimization, while maximizing the capture performance. Sensitivity and scenario analyses are performed to assess the reliability of the optimized solutions. The results for the optimal solution indicate a carbon capture efficiency of 52%, corresponding to 34.7 tn/y of CO2 captured per truck. The optimal configuration leads to an annualized capital expenditure of 7,123 €/y and an operational expenditure of 15,063 €/y. The capture system increases by 36.73% the total fuel-related expenditure, while the additional onboard system weight amounts to only 126 kg. While the system entails an additional mass and cost, these remain acceptable within the operational constraints of heavy-duty vehicles and can be offset by potential carbon credits or regulatory incentives. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Techno-economic optimization of onboard carbon capture systems under escalating emission penalties using surrogate models
Abstract: Onboard carbon capture systems (OCCSs) are emerging as a medium-term response to progressively tightening greenhouse-gas fuel-intensity (GFI) requirements, motivating assessment of appropriate capacity and operation. This study develops a hierarchical multi-period framework that jointly determines one-time OCCS design and annual operation. Gaussian-process-regression surrogates efficiently replace rate-based process simulations, and the framework is applied to a liquefied-natural-gas-fueled very large crude carrier with a 30 wt% monoethanolamine process. On independent test sets, the surrogates achieved coefficients of determination of at least 0.9992 and mean absolute percentage errors of at most 2.01 %. Without surplus-unit trading, the optimum treats 30.0 % of the highest-load main-engine exhaust and matches capture heat demand primarily to recovered waste heat, reducing life cycle cost by 7.9 % relative to compliance without capture. Tightening the GFI trajectory alone does not necessarily increase capture because capture energy also affects attained GFI. When surplus units are traded, their price determines adoption and scale: installation is economical at 304 USD/tonCO2eq and above but not at 266 USD/tonCO2eq and below, while 342 USD/tonCO2eq drives the designs in all three regulatory scenarios to the maximum available main-engine exhaust flow. At 380 USD/tonCO2eq, gross lifetime capture increases from 199 to 634 kton relative to no trading, but net greenhouse gas avoidance increases only from 147 to 325 kton as parasitic emissions rise. Under the assumed immediate-sale surplus-unit market, the prescribed surplus-unit price and net emissions strongly influence OCCS value alongside the target trajectory. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Grassland soil quality in a changing world
Abstract: A quantitative assessment of grassland soil quality (GSQ), including its spatiotemporal variability and underlying driving factors, is pivotal for the adaptive management of grassland ecosystems. Despite extensive studies on GSQ, a systematic synthesis of research achievements, gaps and future perspectives remains underdeveloped. This study systematically reviewed literature published between 1990 and 2024 to achieve three primary objectives: (i) evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of different methods for assessing GSQ, (ii) analyze the frequency and application of physical, chemical, and biological indicators in GSQ assessments, and (iii) examine the effects of natural factors and anthropogenic activities on GSQ. The analysis highlights three critical research priorities: (i) developing a standard index system of GSQ and a method of assessment suitable for various environmental conditions and objectives of evaluation, (ii) identifying the primary socio-ecological drivers that govern the spatial heterogeneity and temporal trends of GSQ, and (iii) elucidating the global distribution, dominant controls, and effective restoration strategies for degraded grassland soil. Addressing these priorities requires innovative techniques and global networks for long-term grassland soil monitoring, standardized procedures for assessing GSQ, more effective collaboration between individuals, organizations, and governments, and an enhanced transfer of knowledge and data for combating the ongoing degradation of grassland soil. Incorporating these actions into a policy of sustainability will aid in conserving multiple services, functions and benefits that grassland soil provides in an era of rapid environmental change. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Liu Y.; Song N.; Zuo M.; Wang L.
Title: Integrated optimization for open-field layout and scheduling in flexible job shop systems
Abstract: In modern flexible job shops, integrating open-field layout with scheduling is crucial for improving operational efficiency and reducing energy consumption. However, it is difficult to obtain satisfactory solutions owing to the high-dimensional continuous solution space and the spatiotemporal coupling between layout and scheduling. To address this challenge, this paper develops a three-population collaborative framework to coordinate global exploration and specialized local exploitation. Building on this framework, a collaborative learning memetic algorithm (CLMA) is proposed to solve the integrated optimization problem with the objectives of minimizing makespan and total energy consumption. In the global exploration phase, boundary annealing and phased mutation are employed to navigate the expansive layout space and expedite convergence. By constructing problem-specific search operators and adopting a dueling double deep Q-network for adaptive selection, the rationality of the search direction during the local optimization phase is maintained. Furthermore, geometric optimization rules are embedded to correct suboptimal spatial structures and ensure physical feasibility. Through 40 benchmark instances and a real-world case, our approach outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms, demonstrating its effectiveness in solving the coupled layout and scheduling problem. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Ding M.; Zhu T.; Qu Y.; Deng Y.; Mo L.; Sun H.
Title: Disruption-induced spatial inequality in resilience loss of urban rail transit: A multi-agent simulation analysis
Abstract: With the rapid expansion of urban rail transit networks in large cities, operational disruptions occur more frequently, causing varying degrees of accessibility loss and shaping station-level resilience. From the network and spatial perspective, these differences manifest as inequalities in the distribution of transport capacity. To investigate these relationships, this study proposes a scenario-based dynamic simulation analysis framework and applies it to the Beijing urban rail transit system as a case study. High-resolution passenger travel processes are first generated using multi-agent simulation. Then, within a dynamic accessibility and resilience evaluation framework, a multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) model is applied to examine accessibility, resilience, and equity under zero-load, normal operation, and disruption scenarios. The results show that variations in accessibility and resilience are highly sensitive to the location and characteristics of disruptions. Under severe disruptions, suburban corridors and key transfer segments form concentrated clusters of low resilience. MGWR analysis further reveals distinct spatial heterogeneity in the effects of structural attributes, passenger demand pressure, and spatial environmental factors, with different drivers operating at different spatial scales. Overall, this study provides quantitative evidence to inform planning, operational optimization, and equity-oriented governance of urban rail transit systems under complex disruption conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Wu J.; Fu S.; Liang J.
Title: Balancing novelty and familiarity: Nonlinear effects of semantic progression on audience engagement
Abstract: Research on information diffusion suggests that audience engagement often depends on a balance between novelty and familiarity, but it remains unclear whether narratives follow a similar principle when organizing information for audiences. To examine this possibility, this study analyses 2578 TED talks and models narrative semantic progression along three dimensions: speed, breadth, and circuitousness. The results reveal that semantic breadth and circuitousness are associated with viewership in a nonlinear manner, with moderate levels linked to higher engagement, while both low and high extremes are less effective. In contrast, semantic speed is predominantly negatively associated with viewership. The interaction between semantic speed and semantic breadth further indicates that breadth influences the level of speed at which predicted viewership reaches its maximum. These findings indicate that narratives associated with higher engagement tend to be characterized not by maximum novelty or familiarity, but by a balance between the two. Analyses of podcast data reveal broadly consistent patterns, extending the findings beyond the highly curated context of TED Talks. This study advances a nonlinear perspective on narrative effectiveness and demonstrates the value of Transformer-based embeddings, including large language model embeddings and widely used sentence embedding models, for capturing how meaning unfolds across narrative sequences. Authors: Sun B.; Gao Y.; Li Y.; Chen Z.; Su J.; Zhufu G.
Title: A decomposition-aware dual-stream framework with component-adaptive masked self-supervision for industrial time series forecasting
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of key performance indicators is essential for the safe and efficient operation of complex industrial processes. However, industrial time series are commonly affected by non-stationary dynamics, weak periodicity, complex inter-variable coupling, and label scarcity caused by low-frequency offline assays. These characteristics limit the effectiveness of conventional supervised forecasting models and frequency-decomposition methods that rely on strong periodic assumptions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DeMAP, a decomposition-aware dual-stream framework with component-adaptive masked self-supervision for industrial time series forecasting. Specifically, a Decomposition-Aware Dual-stream Network (DeDNet) decouples process signals into long-term trend and transient residual components. Adaptively learned graphs are used to model trend-related topological dependencies, while multi-scale residual convolutions capture high-frequency local fluctuations. A trend-guided cross-attention mechanism further fuses heterogeneous component representations, and task-specific prediction heads support deterministic point forecasting and probabilistic interval forecasting. To improve representation learning under limited labels, a Component-Adaptive Masked Pre-training (CAMP) strategy is designed with different masking tasks for trend and residual components, enabling the model to exploit latent spatiotemporal structures from unlabeled data. Experiments on the Tennessee Eastman process and a real metal smelting process demonstrate that DeMAP consistently improves deterministic prediction accuracy, interval prediction reliability, and robustness under reduced training data. The results indicate that decomposition-aware modeling and component-specific self-supervision provide an effective solution for industrial forecasting under non-stationarity and label scarcity. © 2026

Title: Green Business Process Management: Approaches, Challenges, and Ways Forward
Abstract: In light of increasing environmental concerns faced by organizations and society, the Business Process Management (BPM) community has developed the Green BPM sub-field. With a wide array of approaches and capabilities, environmental impacts of business processes can be assessed and reduced, allowing organizations to establish environmentally sustainable practices. While receiving significant research interest over the last fifteen years, Green BPM is still a marginal topic at the BPM conference, as well as in BPM practice. In this tutorial, we provide a general introduction into Green BPM, and present two alternative approaches for integrating notions of environmental sustainability into Green BPM. We discuss challenges associated with the “process lens” of Green BPM, both from a theoretical and practical angle. With our tutorial, we aim to create awareness for the rich stream of existing Green BPM research and ultimately for the potential for further relevant and valuable contributions to be made by BPM researchers. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Wu S.; Liu L.; Li D.; He Z.; Zhu S.; Dong J.; Qin Y.; Liu L.; Wang G.; Zhang Z.
Title: Nature- versus non-nature-based recreation: A comparative assessment of self-reported anxiety alleviation
Abstract: Nature-based recreation delivers vital ecosystem services that shape human physical and psychological well-being, representing a core category of nature's contributions to people within urban and peri-urban social-ecological landscapes. While non-nature-based recreational activities can also improve people's quality of life by mitigating anxiety, the relative contributions of nature- and non-nature-based recreation to people's mental health, and the factors that influence them, remain largely unknown. Here, we conducted a survey of 15,522 respondents across China and applied structural equation modeling to show that nature-based recreation is associated with significantly stronger self-reported anxiety alleviation than non-nature-based recreation. A longer time allocation to nature-based recreational activities during holidays and weekends was also associated with greater self-reported alleviation of anxiety from nature-based recreation. Furthermore, predictors including environmental pressure, anxiety-related attributes, and socioeconomic status were associated with the relative contributions of nature- and non-nature-based anxiety alleviation, with these associations partly mediated via recreation engagement. This empirical evidence improves integrated landscape and urban planning frameworks by providing context-specific guidance for sustainable urban recreational space design and cross-regional governance focused on public health. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Robustness in deepfake speech detection: A survey of failure mechanisms including an experimental case study
Abstract: In recent years, the emergence of disruptive deepfake technology (referring here to computer-generated speech/audio, images, video and text) has raised significant concerns surrounding the privacy, security, and credibility of digital content. Although detection systems report high benchmark performance, most are evaluated on in-domain datasets, codecs, and generative models seen during training. In real deployment, however, detectors must contend with out-of-domain instances, that is, a mismatch between the data seen during training and the conditions encountered in deployment (e.g., unseen generative methods, unfamiliar codecs, or signals degraded by transmission channels). Under these conditions, performance often degrades sharply. While robustness has been acknowledged in the literature, it remains underexplored. This work presents a robustness-focused survey and experimental study of deepfake speech detection. Rather than broadly cataloguing existing methods, we organise the literature around three factors that influence robustness to distribution shift: dataset design, feature representations, and model architecture. To complement this synthesis, we conduct a cross-dataset evaluation with Wav2Vec2, HuBERT, WavLM, and Whisper self-supervised speech models, trained on the ASVspoof 2019 LA and evaluated on the ASVspoof 2021 Deepfake dataset. The experimental results show that robustness varies considerably across models and conditions. HuBERT demonstrates comparatively stable performance across codec and dataset shifts, while Wav2Vec2 and WavLM experience substantial degradation, particularly under MP3-based compression and neural vocoder synthesis. A diagnostic analysis further reveals that robustness failures are strongly associated with codec-induced masking of synthesis artefacts and with dataset-dependent synthesis pipelines. By combining a robustness-oriented survey with cross-dataset experimental evidence, this work puts theory to practice, highlighting key factors that limit the generalisation of current detectors and outlining practical directions for improving robustness, including diversified dataset design, feature fusion, and evaluation under realistic cross-domain conditions. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Is Europe a laggard? Comparing the EU and the US using an interdisciplinary well-being framework
Abstract: Well-being is increasingly recognized as a more meaningful measure of societal progress than economic output, yet most international comparisons continue to emphasize economic indicators. This focus has reinforced the perception that Europe is lagging behind the United States, with the productivity gap shaping the European Commission’s recent competitiveness agenda. Here, we compare European and American development from 1990–2023 using an interdisciplinary well-being framework that integrates five scientific schools of thought. We find that while the US increasingly outperformed the EU on productivity and income, the EU caught up in terms of various well-being indicators, including life satisfaction and education, while increasingly outperforming the US in life expectancy and safety. Europe also exhibits more equitable well-being outcomes and achieves them at lower environmental cost. However, in both regions, the conditions underpinning future well-being are under increasing pressure. These results challenge the dominance of economic metrics in evaluating progress and emphasize the need for inclusive development strategies that place sustainable well-being at their core. © 2026 The Authors. Title: A pragmatic, demand-driven framework to prioritise critical raw material recycling
Abstract: Every three years, the European Commission publishes a list of critical raw materials (CRMs) based on economic importance and supply risk. Boosting recovery rates is a strategy for criticality mitigation, but not equally relevant for all CRMs. This study develops a pragmatic, demand-driven framework to prioritise CRMs for recycling. The approach integrates four dimensions: criticality, relative availability, industrial demand, and recovery systems effectiveness. Industrial demand introduces a market-pull perspective, linking recycling to existing value chains and economic viability. The framework relies on publicly available data and avoids product-level modelling. Applied at the EU level and for Belgium and Germany, it demonstrates varying priorities across geographic contexts. Results position materials within a two-dimensional matrix that enables a structured diagnosis of where policy intervention is most likely to generate systemic impact. This approach translates criticality assessments into actionable recycling priorities for policymakers, aligned with industrial demand and regional specificities. © 2026 The Authors. Title: A predictive–prescriptive framework for operating room scheduling: Transformer-based duration estimation and system-coupled robust multi-resource optimization
Abstract: Operating room scheduling (ORS) is complicated by uncertain surgical durations, downstream recovery limitations, and workforce constraints. This study develops a two-phase predictive–prescriptive decision-support framework (DSF) for tactical perioperative planning. In Phase I, heterogeneous clinical, procedural, and provider information is integrated within a Transformer-based regression model using fixed BioBERT-derived diagnostic representations. The resulting out-of-fold predictions and empirical residual distribution are used to construct residual-calibrated duration bounds, thereby creating a data-driven connection between prediction uncertainty and scheduling decisions. In Phase II, these inputs are transferred to a mixed-integer convex quadratic System-Coupled Robust Operating Room Scheduling (SC-ORS) model that coordinates OR utilization, daily aggregate PACU capacity, surgeon availability, and workload balance. The complete predictive pipeline outperforms the selected machine-learning (ML) benchmarks under leakage-controlled cross-validation, while the residual-based intervals provide internally calibrated uncertainty information for the optimization phase. Computational experiments show that SC-ORS can reduce realized overtime exposure under several moderately constrained conditions, identify emerging PACU bottlenecks, and support schedule adjustments under limited surgeon availability disruptions. The results also reveal that the value of robustness depends on the demand-to-capacity ratio and on managerial preferences regarding OR utilization, downstream capacity, and workload balance. The proposed framework contributes primarily through the explicit integration of heterogeneous surgical-duration prediction, residual-calibrated uncertainty, and multi-resource tactical optimization. It provides a structured basis for moving from OR-centric planning toward coordinated perioperative decision support, while hospital-specific calibration, intra-day sequencing, and prospective validation remain necessary before operational deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
