Title: LNG/H2-rich syngas centric quad-generation plant with hydrogen-ready self-sustaining feeder; economic evaluation, Cuckoo search, and MLP neural networks
Abstract: The rising global demand for sustainable energy, coupled with the urgent need for low-carbon hydrogen production, presents a significant challenge for modern energy systems. Existing multi-generation frameworks often suffer from inefficient thermal resource utilization and high computational costs during optimization. To address these gaps, this study proposes a novel, thermodynamically integrated liquefied natural gas (LNG)-based quad-generation system that synergistically combines LNG cold energy recovery with steam methane reforming, gas turbine power, steam Rankine and Kalina cycles, and a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer. To ensure high-efficiency performance, a surrogate-aided optimization plan, utilizing a Multi-Layer Perceptron model tuned with Cuckoo Search algorithm, is developed to navigate the complex decision space. Simulation results demonstrate that the optimized system achieves a remarkable exergy efficiency of 56.50% and a primary energy saving ratio of 34.43%, while maintaining competitive specific CO2 emissions of 0.297 kgCO2/kWh. Economically, the optimal configuration yields a total unit cost of product of 10.84 $/GJ and an annual profit of 31.01 M$, with a dynamic payback period (DPP) of 3.34 years. Comprehensive sensitivity and uncertainty analyses revealed that LNG flow rate and gas turbine outlet pressure are the primary drivers of overall system performance. These findings indicate that the proposed framework offers a robust, technically feasible, and economically viable solution for industrial-scale quad-generation, providing a scalable pathway for enhancing resource efficiency and promoting sustainable hydrogen production in future energy infrastructures. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Women Empowerment and Environmental Sustainability in Africa: The Critical Roles of Electronic Government Services
Abstract: Recent literature acknowledges the significance of women’s empowerment in the global agenda for environmental sustainability. While the role of information and communication technology has been acknowledged, only a few studies have examined the relevance and peculiarities of electronic government (e-government) in combating environmental degradation in developing economies. In addition, the role of e-government in the women empowerment-environmental sustainability nexus has not been explored. This study examines the role of electronic government (e-government) in the relationship between women’s empowerment and a sustainable environment across a panel of 31 African countries from 2003 to 2022. Environmental sustainability is proxied by ecological footprint, while women’s empowerment is proxied by women’s political empowerment and the female labour participation rate. The results, based on the system generalised method of moments, pooled ordinary least squares based on Driscoll and Kraay, and panel quantile regression via moments, show that women’s empowerment reduces ecological footprints, while e-government strengthens and complements women’s empowerment to sustain environmental quality in Africa. This result underscores the significance of women’s empowerment in protecting the environment. Hence, policies to enhance the empowerment and participation of women in all spheres of life should be vigorously pursued in the region, while e-government applications serve as an important policy instrument to transition to a safer and more conducive environment. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Identifying knowledge gaps in the assessment of biochar's carbon dioxide removal potential: A Canadian case study
Abstract: Achieving carbon neutrality by 2050, as targeted under the Paris Agreement, requires the deployment of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategies such as biochar production (BC), especially in biomass-rich regions. However, its effectiveness as a negative-emission technology depends strongly on process conditions and the sustainability of biomass feedstocks, requiring robust scientific evidence to confirm its CDR potential. Canada, which is well positioned to develop an industrial BC sector and is projected to rely on it for its net-zero strategy on it, was used as a case study to assess the alignment between BC-related scientific literature and its technical CDR potential derived from exploitable organic resources.Results show that Canada has a sustainably exploitable resource of 165,771 kt C under a conservative baseline scenario, dominated by fire-killed trees (73%), followed by crop residues (14%) and harvest residues (5%). According to Puro.earth's protocol, this resource represents a CDR potential of up to 348,146 kt CO2-equivalent by BC production, excluding upstream and downstream life cycle emissions. The systematic literature review, based on 150 Scopus-indexed publications, shows that Canadian BC research focuses mainly on secondary forestry residues feedstock and agricultural soil amendment applications. Authors: Farkas M.; Kocsis I.
Author full names: Farkas, Martin (59515829300); Kocsis, Imre (55682654930)
Title: Trust No Pool: Formal Security Analysis of BPMN Collaborations
Abstract: Cross-organizational collaborations face inherent trust challenges: any participant may want to deviate from the agreed-upon process model, trying to deceive others about the shared state. Traditional verification approaches over collaborations – e.g., over BPMN collaboration models – verify correctness properties under the assumption that all participants faithfully execute their roles. They do not consider what a strategically dishonest participant can achieve, and to our knowledge, no formal framework exists for doing so. We introduce potentially adversarial participants for BPMN collaborations as a first-class concept, analyze them as security protocols, and demonstrate that this framing is both formally precise and directly actionable. We utilize a structural correspondence between BPMN’s token-based collaboration semantics and the multiset rewriting formalism of the Tamarin security protocol verifier. This correspondence allows us to define a formal, epistemically grounded threat model and to encode a core subset of collaboration semantics as Tamarin theories, enabling the formal verification of collaboration security: the automated discovery of successful attack strategies or proving of their absence. We introduce a composable attacker model whose elements reflect the underlying platform’s security guarantees – from loosely coupled integrations through smart contract orchestration to Verifiable Credential-based protocols. We demonstrate the approach on an example, examining how the attack surface shifts across the three execution platforms and revealing platform-specific attacks that arise from the interplay of business logic and platform semantics. These attacks are undetectable by standard correctness verification and sophisticated enough to warrant systematic analysis in business-critical settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Mind the Long Tail: Understanding the Difficulty of Delay Detection in Business Processes
Abstract: The early detection of delayed cases in business processes is a critical capability for organizations. Predictive process monitoring (PPM) supports this task by using historical event logs to predict the remaining time of ongoing cases, enabling timely interventions to avoid missed deadlines and service level violations. Although remaining time prediction has advanced considerably through sophisticated deep learning architectures, little is known about the intrinsic difficulty of delay detection itself. Since performance is typically assessed using aggregate metrics, prior work provides limited insight into how models perform across the target distribution, especially on the operationally most critical cases with large delays. In this paper, we address this gap by analyzing the difficulty of delay detection. Across 14 event logs, we show that remaining times are typically strongly right-skewed, with only a small fraction of cases exhibiting large delays. Existing models capture the mode of this distribution well but perform poorly on high-delay cases. We further uncover pronounced heteroscedasticity, showing that predictive uncertainty increases with delay magnitude. Based on these findings, we evaluate approaches to mitigate the imbalance problem, but find only limited benefits, suggesting that the key underlying problem may not be imbalance but higher uncertainty associated with delayed cases. We show that this correlation can be exploited to substantially improve the identification of delayed cases. Overall, our work provides new insights into the sources of difficulty in delay detection and identifies uncertainty-aware modeling as a promising direction for future PPM research. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Forecasting Approaches to Pharmaceutical Supply Management Across Healthcare Settings: A Scoping Review
Abstract: Background: Drug shortages remain a persistent global issue affecting essential medicines across healthcare settings. In healthcare settings, inadequate pharmaceutical forecasting and inventory management may lead to suboptimal medicine availability, treatment disruption, and patient harm. Despite advances in automated inventory systems, forecasting practices remain fragmented across healthcare contexts with varying demand conditions and implementation requirements. Objectives: This scoping review aimed to map forecasting methods used in pharmaceutical supply management and examine their application across operational contexts. Methods: Studies reporting forecasting or prediction models in pharmaceutical healthcare settings were included. Studies unrelated to pharmaceutical forecasting, non-healthcare logistics, qualitative designs, editorials, and inaccessible full texts were excluded. Searches were conducted in Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. Extracted data on forecasting methods, implementation contexts, and operational outcomes were synthesised narratively. A proposed conceptual framework integrating forecasting approaches and contextual triggers was developed through interpretive synthesis. Results: Twenty-four studies (2007–2026) were included, representing 13 identified countries. Four forecasting approaches were identified: rule-based, traditional/statistical, machine learning/artificial intelligence (ML/AI), and hybrid approaches. Traditional/statistical methods were most frequently reported (n = 8), followed by ML/AI approaches (n = 7), hybrid approaches (n = 5), and rule-based approaches (n = 4). Forecasting approaches were reported across operational contexts with differing demand patterns, data availability, and implementation requirements. Conclusions: ML/AI and hybrid approaches were also reported in studies involving uncertainty and demand variability. However, comparative superiority cannot be established, and the proposed conceptual framework remains an interpretive evidence synthesis structure requiring empirical validation. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

Title: Continuum modeling of granular segregation accounting for wall friction
Abstract: Sidewall friction significantly influences particle mobility within the flowing layer and plays a key role in the formation and transition of granular segregation patterns. This paper introduces a wall friction term into the traditional convection-diffusion model to consider the influence of wall friction on granular segregation, and analyzes the granular segregation characteristics within the rotating drum under different rotational speeds and filling degrees using the discrete element method. The results show that the improved convective diffusion model can effectively measure the granular concentration distribution and segregation rate distribution in the drum; at the center position of the flowing layer, the shear rate and granular velocity gradually decrease along the depth of the flowing layer, and the segregation rate shows a trend of increasing first and then decreasing; as the rotational speed increases, the shear rate and granular velocity in the flowing layer gradually increase, the segregation rate also increases, and the concentration of small granules gradually decreases, promoting the segregation pattern to change from a striped shape to a nuclear shape; when the filling degree decreases, although the segregation rate increases, the change in the concentration of small granules in the flowing layer is not obvious, so the segregation pattern always remains nuclear. The research results help to reveal the mechanism of granular segregation pattern formation and provide reference data for improving the granular segregation model. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Hospitality recovery disconnect: Why diligent responses to online reviews fail to boost ratings
Abstract: This study investigates a critical challenge in online hospitality management: the perplexing failure of high-quality managerial responses to improve business ratings on platforms like Yelp. Title: Staff interactions and individual influences on complaint behaviour in restaurants
Abstract: This study examines the influence of early staff interactions and individual characteristics on customer complaint behaviour during restaurant dining. A two-stage mixed-methods design was employed: Study 1 surveyed 790 diners, measuring sociodemographic and personality variables alongside self-reported propensity to complain. Study 2 applied these findings in a longitudinal design tracking 98 customers across 994 restaurant visits over one year, capturing individual and situational factors, including staff interactions. Drawing on voice/exit theory and cognitive appraisal frameworks, findings identify redress orientation as a consistent predictor of complaint propensity, whilst empathy reduces both the likelihood of perceived dissatisfaction and willingness to raise issues verbally. Early staff interactions, particularly making customers feel special upon arrival, significantly reduced complaint propensity, as did service quality and friendliness. Authors: Chen Q.; Qian X.; Shao E.; Tan Y.; Xia L.; Zhang H.; Xiao H.; Deng S.
Title: ASCA-SHAP dual screening of PMI-related corneal ATR-FTIR spectral bands under temperature-dependent variation
Abstract: The estimation of postmortem interval (PMI) is a long-standing scientific challenge in forensic pathology, and its accuracy is susceptible to environmental conditions. Environmental temperature can affect processes such as corneal tissue dehydration, water migration, and degradation of biological macromolecules, altering the spectral evolution characteristics of the cornea after death. Therefore, the relationship between PMI and spectral features may change with temperature conditions. This study collected attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) spectra of 144 rat corneal homogenate samples under three controlled temperature conditions (4°C, 20°C, and 30°C) and six PMI time points (0, 6, 12, 24, 36, and 48 h). Firstly, partial least squares regression (PLSR) models were established for different temperature groups and combined data to compare the modellability of the PMI-spectral relationship under different temperature conditions; subsequently, variance-synchronized component analysis (ANOVA-simultaneous component analysis, ASCA) was used to decompose spectral variations into PMI, temperature, and PMI × temperature interaction effects, and dual screening was conducted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and other equivalent contribution analyses based on PLSR linear coefficients. The results showed that the single-temperature model was superior model performance to the combined, suggesting that temperature affects the relationship between PMI and spectra. The ASCA results indicated that PMI, temperature, and PMI × temperature interaction effects explained 27.38%, 5.94%, and 21.57% of the total spectral variation, respectively. The higher interaction effect suggests that temperature does not merely introduce constant background differences but also alters the spectral evolution trajectory related to PMI. Based on this, this study constructed a dual-screening strategy integrating ASCA effect decomposition and SHAP contribution analysis to identify interpretable PMI-related spectral bands under temperature-dependent variations. Through this screening framework, 56 wave numbers were identified and merged into 9 consecutive candidate spectral bands. These spectral bands are mainly related to protein, amide region, carbonyl group and fingerprint region molecular changes, suggesting that they may reflect the molecular degradation process of the cornea after death. The above spectral bands exhibit strong PMI-related effects, relatively low temperature main effects, and relatively consistent cross-temperature change trends under the current controlled conditions. However, they should not be interpreted as completely independent biomarkers that are completely unaffected by temperature. The proposed ASCA–SHAP dual screening framework in this study can provide candidate spectral features for cross-temperature and interpretable corneal PMI models. Copyright © 2026. Title: Strategic capability prioritisation for logistics service providers: a consistency-calibrated reliability-weighted fuzzy FUCOM–MARCOS framework
Abstract: Logistics service providers (LSPs) have yet to receive guidance, supported by empirical data, on which organisational capabilities should be prioritised for development to enhance competitiveness and survival in the dramatically changing environment they face. Structured elicitation from 17 senior managers of leading LSPs based in Türkiye forms the empirical data set. This methodology contributes by transforming each expert’s deviation from full consistency into an endogenous reliability weight during the aggregation of individual weights. CCR-FUCOM weights are then used to calculate scenario scores via fuzzy MARCOS.Results show that operational capabilities and dynamic capabilities form a priority cluster. The scenario analysis converges on the same priorities: the operational leader configuration attains the highest system-level utility, with the digital pioneer second and the resilience champion third. Title: Towards ethical, co-produced and justice-oriented research with small-scale fishing communities: a multi-scalar call to action
Abstract: Small-scale fisheries underpin food security, livelihoods and cultural identity for hundreds of millions of people worldwide, yet remain marginalised within dominant ocean governance and research agendas. Recent shifts toward justice-, equity- and rights-based approaches in ocean governance and policy signal important progress, but their rapid uptake risks remaining largely rhetorical if not grounded in meaningful changes to research practice. This paper draws on the experiential knowledge of researchers working across diverse geographical and institutional contexts to critically examine the structural conditions that shape research with small-scale fishing communities. We identify seven tensions that are recurring and cross-cutting within funding architectures, institutional incentive systems, and global policy agendas that constrain the ability of researchers to conduct ethical, co-produced and justice-oriented work. These include misalignments between global priorities and local realities, knowledge hierarchies, rigid funding models, and academic metrics that undervalue relational and collaborative processes. We emphasise the need for the recognition of diverse knowledge systems and creative outputs, institutional reforms that value long-term partnerships and local impact, and strengthened training in reflexive and ethical research approaches. Framed as a multi-scalar call to action, this paper highlights the shared responsibilities of research funders, academic institutions, policy agencies, NGOs, and researchers in reshaping the systems that govern knowledge production that inform ocean governance. Title: Managing perishable production systems with extended shelf life: The role of sustainability
Abstract: A common way to reduce the waste from expired raw materials in perishable supply chains is to transform perishable raw materials into relatively non-perishable end products with extended shelf life. We consider how to coordinate production and ordering for a periodic-review serial inventory/production system in which the perishable raw material is transformed into a non-perishable end product over a finite planning horizon. When the lifetime of the raw material has a fixed lifetime, we first derive a condition that ensures the optimality of the first-in first-out policy. More interestingly, we find that if the unit expiration cost exceeds a threshold in a period, a raw material no-disposal policy is optimal and the value function in each subsequent period is decomposable under a state transformation. As a result, in each of these periods, the optimal production policy is an age-differentiated base-stock policy and the optimal ordering policy is a base-stock policy. Thus, a high unit expiration cost not only makes the supply chain more sustainable but also can simplify the operational strategy significantly. Our results provide operational guidelines and insights on managing this type of perishable production systems and improving sustainability. © 2026

Title: Re-envisioning home healthcare planning through sustainability: An operations research review
Abstract: Ageing populations, shrinking family structures, and economic considerations are accelerating the global need for effective home healthcare (HHC) systems. Realising the full benefits of HHC requires careful attention to sustainability considerations. Consequently, sustainable HHC planning has gained increasing prominence within the operations research literature. This review provides a structured, sustainability-oriented synthesis of HHC planning models. By introducing a unifying terminology and modelling structure, the review facilitates systematic comparison across diverse approaches and uncovers gaps in the explicit integration of sustainability into HHC planning. Title: Microbial functional differentiation and flavor formation across layer exchange in cereal vinegar fermentation: Multi-omics insights and targeted bioaugmentation
Abstract: Spatial heterogeneity is common in cereal vinegar fermentation, but microbial and metabolic changes across the layer-exchange process remain unclear. Before exchange, the frequently turned upper layer consumed ethanol at 1.14 times the lower-layer rate, rapidly accumulated acetic acid, and was enriched in Acetobacter and Komagataeibacter . The lower layer retained more ethanol and lactic acid, was enriched in lactic acid bacteria and yeasts, and contained more ethyl esters. After upward transfer, the original lower-layer Cupei rapidly accumulated acetic acid as several ethyl esters decreased; after downward transfer, the original upper-layer Cupei acidified more slowly while phenethyl alcohol, phenethyl acetate, ethyl lactate, and 2,3-butanediol increased. Genus-level transcript profiles showed that Acetobacter -affiliated transcripts related to acetaldehyde oxidation and the acetolactate/acetoin branch were more pronounced in upper-positioned Cupei , whereas LAB-affiliated lactate-forming transcripts were prominent in the lower layer. At the 100-kg scale, a targeted two-strain treatment using Lactobacillus helveticus and Acetobacter pasteurianus increased substrate conversion efficiency from 47.35 ± 1.36% to 51.19 ± 0.32% and final total acid by approximately 9.7% in both portions. In a → A, day-17 acetic acid was 43.8% higher than in the control, but the difference was not significant at the endpoint. The bioaugmentation samples showed changes in aroma-related volatile composition. Title: Urban forest cooling efficiency and heat exposure inequity under extreme heat: Evidence from 550 global cities
Abstract: Extreme heat has become a key factor affecting urban residents’ quality of life, existing studies on urban forest have focused on their average cooling effects, overlooking whether and how variations in cooling efficiency affect heat exposure inequity. To address these gaps, this study selected 550 cities worldwide with a main urban area exceeding 100 km2 to analyze the relationship between urban forest cooling efficiency and heat exposure inequity over the past 24 years. We found that although tree coverage increased in most cities, the enhanced vegetation index (EVI) deteriorated in nearly half of them, revealing a polarizing pattern: “High coverage turning green, low coverage turning brown.” Notably, tree coverage and EVI were particularly fragile in tropical climates and low Human Development Index (HDI) cities. We found that each 1 % increase in tree coverage reduces the average land surface temperature during extreme heat by 0.31 °C. However, this cooling efficiency is distributed extremely unevenly. The study utilized the population-weighted temperature Gini coefficient to represent the inequity of urban heat exposure. About 25.2 % of cities experienced increased heat exposure inequity, particularly in developed cities, as increasing tree coverage unintentionally exacerbated spatial inequity. At the same time, about 5.6 % of cities even exhibit a forest warming effect, especially in the desert climate zones and low HDI areas. About 66 % of the cities showed that as the cooling efficiency of urban forest increased, there was a corresponding increase in heat exposure equity. The study proposed the concept of the equity potential index and compared the possibility of achieving equity potential for the cooling efficiency of urban forest under the three scenarios: SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP3-7.0. The study showed that SSP1-2.6 is more favorable for temperate climate zones and low-HDI cities, whereas SSP2-4.5 is more beneficial for tropical, continental climates, and very high HDI cities. This study provides a scientific, equity-oriented framework for designing place-specific urban forest strategies that enhance thermal resilience and social sustainability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Effective training and support of ICU teams: The cornerstone for improved patient and staff outcomes
Abstract: Background ICU care is inherently multiprofessional, and communication failures and team dysfunction are implicated in a substantial proportion of preventable adverse events in critical care. However,et training frameworks remain fragmented, built around individual brilliance and siloed disciplines. Aim To present an integrated, evidence-based framework for building, training, assessing, and sustaining high-performance ICU teams. Methods Narrative review using a targeted, non-systematic search of the databases PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for manuscripts published between 2000 and June 2026. Grey literature from ESICM, SCCM, ANZICS was also searched. Data were synthesized by the authors from complex clinical scenarios and team behaviors, rather than by pooling empirical data. Themes, communication patterns, and organizational challenges emerged organically from the selected texts and case descriptions. Key findings ICU team effectiveness rests on four pillars: deliberate multiprofessional composition with explicit role delineation; multimodal training combining simulation, just-in-time training, and structured debriefing; rigorous measurement through structure, process, and outcome indicators; and organizational conditions, including unit design and psychological safety, that sustain safety culture and provider wellbeing. Current evidence remains heterogeneous, particularly across cultural, organizational, and resource contexts, limiting direct comparison across settings. Building on these pillars, practical recommendations for ICU leaders to translate this framework into daily practice are proposed. Conclusion A whole-team approach to ICU team selection, training and support, extending beyond physician-centric models, is clinically necessary and is operationally feasible when adapted to local resources and organizational conditions. The framework presented is adaptable to diverse and various intensive care settings, with each pillar mapped to actionable strategies for team composition, training, assessment, and sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

Authors: Shi Y.; Jiang F.; Ma Y.
Title: Quantifying the prestige of scientific awards: A network-bibliometric framework
Abstract: Scientific awards play a central role in recognizing excellence and shaping research trajectories, funding priorities, and disciplinary visibility. Yet despite their importance, scalable and reproducible quantitative frameworks for assessing award prestige remain limited, with prior efforts relying largely on small-scale or perception-based evaluations. This study introduces a data-driven framework for quantifying the prestige of scientific awards by integrating network centrality measures derived from inter-award linkages with bibliometric indicators of prize-winners’ research profiles. Using a dataset of 1352 research-related award records across seven disciplines, we treat award prestige as a latent construct approximated by two external reference dimensions: public attention (crowd-sourced engagement) and professional reputation (expert survey responses). Across three complementary modeling approaches and repeated cross-validation, the framework recovers rankings that are broadly consistent with conventional perceptions of scientific prestige, with awards such as the Nobel Prize, Abel Prize, and Turing Award consistently appearing near the top across external reference dimensions. Among the examined features, network prominence, as measured by eigenvector centrality, emerges as the most consistently important signal, followed by recent bibliometric activity and authorship leadership. The proposed framework offers a scalable and transparent approach to quantifying scientific recognition, providing empirical insights into the structure of academic prestige and informing future evaluations of emerging or underrecognized awards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Li B.; Pan C.
Title: A weighted multiple conditional value-at-risk approach to energy portfolio under market and environmental uncertainty
Abstract: Climate change and global energy restructuring have increased the demand for optimizing energy asset portfolios under uncertainty. However, existing models based on probability theory or fuzzy set theory fail to capture extreme market and environmental uncertainties effectively. To address this gap, an uncertain mean-weighted multiple conditional value-at-risk energy portfolio model is proposed based on uncertainty theory. Specifically, we define the weighted multiple conditional value-at-risk as the core risk measure within the uncertainty theory framework. The model integrates practical constraints including carbon tax, investment risk control, carbon risk, socially responsible investment demand and budget constraints. Meanwhile, we derive its analytical expressions under the assumptions of normal and linear uncertainty distributions, providing theoretical support for model solution. Numerical simulation and sensitivity analysis are carried out. The results indicate that the proposed model is capable of yielding portfolio schemes that balance economic and ecological benefits, thereby providing a feasible reference for portfolio optimization under uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Designing the future of consciousness: A components framework and speculative implications
Source title: International Journal of Human Computer Studies
Abstract: As technologies increasingly converge with users’ psychophysiology and mental states, perception and mind-altering are emerging as plausibly designable components of user experience. This gives rise to emergent phenomena of digitally induced altered states of consciousness (DIAL) that find application not only in therapeutic and mental health contexts but also in communication and leisure. Modern consciousness-altering technologies primarily exist as early prototypes, and their empirical research tends to constrain the context of use to instrumental functionality. Fictional narrative analysis proposes to push these limitations by considering concepts of technology in imaginary contexts, thereby examining the experiences, social rituals, and ethical issues associated with their use far beyond traditional technical scenarios. This article employs a reflexive thematic analysis of popular science fiction narratives to expand our understanding of how ASCs are integrated into HCI, considering broader sociocultural and sociotechnical contexts. As a result, we identify key aspects of interaction (purpose and context) and combine their subcategories into a framework that facilitates rethinking traditional HCI, revealing potentials that remain inaccessible within clear consciousness. This framework was used to construct five themes, highlighting that the benefits of mitigating cognitive load and deepening technology-mediated communication with DIAL might entail sacrificing identity and autonomy and increasing the pressures of the modern, overcompetitive, hyper-individualistic lifestyle. Thus, the article contributes to the HCI agenda by expanding existing paradigms of interaction with mind-altering technologies and by demonstrating the use of science fiction as a powerful avenue for exploring the design space and critical inquiries about these types of interactions. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Evolution and Trends: An Exploratory Review of Business Intelligence Migration to Cloud Computing

Authors: Bin Yao; Lan R.; Tan X.; Yuan J.; Duan Q.; Fu M.; Li N.; Xiong X.; Liu X.
Title: Built-in electric field-driven charge separation in an MXene@TiO2/PdTCPP-HOF S-scheme heterojunction for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution
Source title: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
Abstract: Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) have recently emerged as promising photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution; however, their practical efficiency is severely constrained by rapid charge-carrier recombination and inefficient charge transport. Herein, we hypothesize that constructing an intimate S-scheme heterojunction between MXene-derived TiO2 and PdTCPP-based HOFs can induce interfacial charge redistribution and generate a built-in electric field (IEF), thereby enabling directional carrier migration and enhanced photocatalytic activity. Based on this concept, an MXene@TiO2/PdTCPP-HOFs heterojunction was fabricated via an in-situ self-assembly strategy. As a result, the optimized MXene@TiO2/PdTCPP-HOF photocatalyst achieves a high hydrogen evolution rate of 3412 μmol g−1 h−1, which is approximately 20.3 and 2.7 times higher than those of MXene@TiO2 and PdTCPP-HOFs, respectively. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM), in-situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy ( in-situ XPS), and density functional theory calculations (DFT) collectively reveal the interfacial charge-transfer behavior and S-scheme photocatalytic mechanism. This work offers a promising strategy for modulating interfacial electric fields and charge-carrier dynamics in HOF-based heterojunctions toward efficient photocatalytic hydrogen production. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of 2-aminopyrimidine-5-carboxamide derivatives as potent selective Wee1 inhibitors
Abstract: Wee1 is a serine/threonine kinase that plays an important role in regulating DNA damage response and cell cycle checkpoints. Inhibition of Wee1 could abrogate cell cycle arrest, exacerbate DNA damage, and induce mitotic catastrophe and apoptosis. Herein, a novel series of 2-aminopyrimidine-5-carboxamide derivatives were designed, synthesized, and evaluated as Wee1 inhibitors. Among them, compound WC-27 exhibited excellent inhibitory activity against Wee1 (IC50 = 2.11 nM) and high selectivity over PLK1 (IC50 > 1000 nM), suggesting that it may reduce off-target effects on PLK1 and thereby potentially mitigate the myelosuppression associated with Wee1 inhibitors. Meanwhile, it displayed acceptable antiproliferative activity against NCI-H1299 cell line with an IC50 value of 1.05 μM. Further investigation showed that compound WC-27 could arrest NCI-H1299 cells in S phase and induce apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner. Moreover, compound WC-27 displayed moderate liver microsomal stability and an excellent pharmacokinetic profile (AUC0-t = 2370 ng h mL−1, oral bioavailability of 49.5%) in Sprague-Dawley rats, acceptable PPB, low risk of drug-drug interactions and no apparent toxicity was observed in the acute toxicity assay. Overall, compound WC-27 exhibited high selectivity over PLK1. This favorable profile may mitigate the risk of PLK1-related off-target toxicities such as myelosuppression, a well-recognized safety liability for reported Wee1 inhibitors. Collectively, these results indicate that compound WC-27 is a promising Wee1 inhibitor. © 2026

Title: Tackling data imbalance in high-end business markets: A multi-expert capsule network approach
Abstract: In the digital era, luxury businesses face a unique marketing challenge: identifying potential customers from vast user pools rather than helping users find products. This reversed recommendation scenario presents two key technical challenges: (1) the imbalance between large user pools and limited premium items and (2) the difficulty of capturing diverse user preferences with a limited set of items. We introduce MEICN-GAT (Multi-Level and Expert Interest Capsule Network with Graph Attention), a novel recommendation system designed for business-centric marketing. MEICN-GAT addresses these challenges with three key innovations: (1) a dual-layer structure that captures complex user-product relationships at multiple levels, effectively managing the user-item ratio imbalance; (2) a multi-expert system that evaluates user interests from diverse professional perspectives, alleviating data sparsity; and (3) an edge enhancement strategy that adds reliable, high-utility connections to sparse graphs. Using the luxury hotel industry as a case study, empirical evaluations on real-world datasets show that MEICN-GAT significantly outperforms existing methods in customer identification accuracy, ranking quality, and matching success rates. Although our evaluation focuses on luxury hotels in major cities, the model provides a strong foundation for business-centric marketing systems across various high-end sectors. Title: From Digitization to Transformation: Business Process Reengineering and AI-Orchestrated Governance in Public Administration

Abstract: This paper examines the strategic, organizational, and technological determinants shaping the digital transformation of public services in Slovakia, with an in-depth case study of a large public institution engaged in Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP)—funded modernization projects. These include fragmented process governance, the absence of architectural and data management frameworks, and weak impact measurement mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that the institution’s approach to digitalization remains predominantly evolutionary, focused on isolated technological upgrades rather than systemic reengineering. To address these structural limitations, the paper proposes a process-driven, orchestrated, data-connected, and partially autonomous digital ecosystem leveraging AI agents. Conceptually anchored in Business Process Reengineering (BPR), this model provides a framework for achieving end-to-end service integration, evidence-based performance monitoring, and adaptive institutional learning. Title: The long-term effects of teachers’ gender stereotypes on labor outcomes
Abstract: This paper links a teacher-level measure of gender-stereotyped grading — validated against their Implicit Association Test (IAT) scores — to the later schooling and labor-market outcomes of 1.6 million Peruvian students. Exposure to a more stereotyped teacher widens the gender gaps in high-school completion, formal-sector employment, and earnings, driven by boys’ lasting gains rather than by girls’ smaller, short-lived losses. A single year with a math teacher one standard deviation more stereotyped than average raises boys’ on-time graduation by 0.9 percentage points and lowers girls’ by 0.6. Over the five years after high school (ages 17–22), it raises boys’ formal employment by 4%–12% of the mean employment rate and widens the gender pay gap by about 11% in the first two years, while girls’ losses fade thereafter. These effects run through high-school completion, not test scores or college enrollment. The widening gap in male-dominated industries mainly reflects men's entry rather than women's exit, and students show little sign of adopting the stereotypes themselves. Where structural barriers already constrain access to higher education, teachers’ stereotypes shape who finishes school and their early labor-market outcomes, rather than who reaches college. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zou G.; Ye S.; Yang S.; Pang S.; Hu S.; Gan Y.; Zhang B.
Title: Intelligent Collaborative Edge Caching via Contextual Bandits and Convex Relaxation
Abstract: Edge Data Caching (EDC) enables low-latency delivery and alleviates backhaul congestion by caching data in close proximity to end users. However, current learning-driven methods struggle to capture the multi-dimensional business value of data. Consequently, inefficient resource allocation degrades critical services and compromises the Quality of Service (QoS). Moreover, physical node failures are insufficiently addressed, risking severe backhaul delays. To address these issues, we formulate the Value and Failure-aware Collaborative Edge Data Caching (VF-CEDC) problem as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model jointly optimizing business value and expected latency under physical uncertainties. To solve this, we propose an Online Learning and Convex Relaxation Algorithm (OLCRA). First, OLCRA leverages a Contextual Multi-Armed Bandit (CMAB) to adaptively infer data values. Second, it resolves the discrete caching topology via convex relaxation and probabilistic rounding, yielding near-optimal polynomial-time decisions. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset show that OLCRA reduces average system cost by 32.3% and expected latency by 38.3% against eight competing methods. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Bibliometric study of environmental education: Scientific architecture and the transition toward micro-educational and behavioral approaches
Abstract: Although scientific production in environmental education has grown steadily, fragmented approaches and limited interdisciplinary integration persist. Moreover, the transition from macronormative frameworks to microeducational approaches oriented toward behavioral change remains insufficiently characterized. The objective of this study was to comprehensively analyze the scientific architecture of environmental education, identifying its structural evolution, key actors, predominant sources, funding dynamics, thematic trends, and scientific production cycle, with particular attention to the shift toward microeducational and behavioral approaches. The study followed a rigorous and consolidated four-stage bibliometric method. A total of 4,952 documents indexed in Scopus were analyzed using the Bibliometrix software, examining six main indicators: (1) authors, (2) sponsors, (3) thematic evolution and conceptual structure, (4) sources, (5) documents, and (6) scientific production. The findings reveal sustained expansion in environmental education, with a productivity peak in 2025 and a projected stabilization toward 2032, confirming its advanced consolidation phase. An editorial structure concentrated in historical core journals—Environmental Education Research and Journal of Environmental Education—was identified, alongside growing interdisciplinary expansion toward sustainability, higher education, and technological innovation. Scientific leadership is concentrated in the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom, although emerging economies such as Brazil and China are gaining prominence. Thematically, macrostructural cores linked to sustainability and sustainable development persist; however, microeducational approaches such as pro-environmental behavior, outdoor environmental education, and environmental knowledge are emerging more strongly, indicating a shift toward the analysis of situated learning processes and behavioral change. Bibliometric findings were contrasted with evidence from other bibliometric studies and systematic reviews. It is concluded that environmental education has evolved from a paradigm centered on global normative frameworks toward a multidimensional model integrating experience, behavior, technological innovation, and community action. Authors: Yang F.; Chen H.; Yu X.; Zhang M.; Xiao X.; Deng M.
Title: A survey on fake review detection: From pre-trained language models to large language models
Abstract: Online reviews shape consumer decisions, platform governance, and corporate reputation. Fake reviews compromise this information channel by injecting deceptive evidence into rating systems, recommendation pipelines, and public trust mechanisms. The rise of large language models, or LLMs, has changed the problem in two directions. LLMs can generate fluent and context-aware deceptive reviews, while pre-trained language models, or PLMs, and LLMs also provide stronger semantic representations for detection. This survey reviews fake review detection from an information fusion perspective, covering 211 studies published from 2018 to early 2026. We organize existing work by evidence source and fusion level, covering review text, sentiment, rating behavior, temporal metadata, user-product graphs, multimodal content, external knowledge, and LLM-generated signals. We trace the development from traditional machine learning and deep learning to PLM-based and LLM-based methods, and examine how different approaches combine textual, behavioral, structural, and multimodal evidence. We also analyze reported performance trends on widely used Amazon, Yelp, and OpSpam benchmark families, while noting the limitations caused by different label construction procedures, data splits, and evaluation protocols. Finally, we identify open problems in adversarial generation, cross-domain transfer, uncertainty-aware fusion, missing-source robustness, interpretability, and trustworthy evaluation for AI-generated deceptive content. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: A survey of information retrieval and recommender systems in the era of large language models: Two sides of the same task
Abstract: The fields of information retrieval and recommender systems have long evolved as distinct disciplines, each with its own methodologies and theoretical foundations. This survey provides a perspective on the convergence of these fields, a transformation catalyzed by the advent of large language models. We maintain that this convergence is far from a trivial overlap of tools, but it embodies a substantial conceptual and architectural unification. Our central contribution is a novel three-part taxonomy that explains the mechanisms of this merger leveraging large language models as (1) an embedded engine, (2) a semantic re-ranker, and (3) a response generator. We show how this trajectory culminates in a paradigm inversion, from weak to strong inversion, where the information-seeking task itself is reshaped. The unification is structurally consolidated through joint search and recommendation architectures and contextually curated by retrieval-augmented generation frameworks. This hypothesis is substantiated by a rigorous, quantitative analysis of scholarly publication trends, which provides empirical evidence of this rapid evolution. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a convergence operating at different velocities dictated by domain-specific latency constraints, while acknowledging critical operational vulnerabilities regarding hallucination and bias. A companion GitHub repository is publicly available and offers the complete data collection methodology, dynamic trend analyses, and a comprehensive, categorized list of the surveyed papers, which will be actively maintained as a living resource for the research community. Title: Net Zero, Full Strategy: Integrating Environmental Goals with Business Strategy as Growth Engines
Source title: Contributions to Environmental Sciences and Innovative Business Technology
Abstract: Sustainability is not optional for businesses anymore, considering the growing constraints and challenges posed by climate change, environmental degradation, and stakeholder demands. In order to make environmental stewardship a driver of innovation, resilience, and competitive advantage, this chapter discusses how environmental goals can be effectively incorporated into business strategy. The chapter charts the evolution of business cases for sustainability, beginning with cost cutting and legal obligations and ending with increased investor appeal and brand value. It also provides helpful advice on incorporating sustainability into operations, product design, marketing, supply chain, and corporate governance through strategic models, namely the Triple Bottom Line, Shared Value Model, and the circular economy principles. Successful integration and the lessons learned are of actual business practices of powerhouses such as Patagonia, Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), and Tech Mahindra. This chapter also discusses practical issues such as balancing short-term profitability with long-term sustainability and the dangers of greenwashing. Ecological goals are now an element of company growth and have grown synonymous with it as the environment changes. Title: Licochalcone D accelerates cutaneous wound healing with improved perfusion and antioxidant responses
Abstract: Impaired local perfusion, excessive oxidative stress, persistent inflammation, and apoptosis can compromise cutaneous wound healing. Licochalcone D (LCD), a licorice-derived flavonoid, has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but its effects on cutaneous repair remain incompletely characterized. This study evaluated LCD in a rat full-thickness excisional wound model. Thirty-two male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to vehicle control or LCD treatment at 5, 25, or 50 mg/kg/day by oral gavage. Wound closure, local perfusion, histological repair, oxidative stress, inflammatory mediators, apoptosis-related proteins, antioxidant signaling-related proteins, and selected mitochondrial protein markers were evaluated. LCD accelerated wound closure, enhanced perfusion, increased VEGF expression, reduced inflammatory-cell infiltration, and improved collagen organization. LCD also increased SOD activity, reduced MDA and 4-HNE levels, and decreased TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. Nrf2, HO-1, and NQO1 expression increased after LCD treatment, supporting an association with enhanced antioxidant responses. Apoptosis-related proteins shifted toward an anti-apoptotic pattern. LCD treatment was additionally accompanied by changes in PINK1, Parkin, LC3B, SQSTM1/p62, and COX IV expression; however, these single-time-point measurements do not establish altered mitophagic flux or a causal mitochondrial mechanism. Overall, orally administered LCD improved multiple wound-healing-related outcomes, with more pronounced effects in the medium- and high-dose groups. © 2026

Title: Suppressed inquiry: The hidden toll of working with satisfaction-optimized AI
Abstract: LLMs have become thinking companions for hundreds of millions worldwide, and they often do remarkable work. But their satisfaction-optimized design produces suppressed inquiry: the tendency for LLMs to inhibit rather than facilitate users' questioning process. LLMs appear fluent, confident, and seemingly all-knowing, their near-instant and polished output making non-LLM work feel unacceptably tedious and less eloquent. They affirm rather than interrogate users' assumptions, producing output that is deceptively adequate—shallower, less original, and less carefully reasoned than it appears. Seemingly competent systems also reduce vigilance and the monitoring impulse that independent judgment requires. Their responses also confine users within the frame they establish, narrowing what users think to ask. These costs are self-concealing: detecting them requires the very engagement that they suppress. And repeated delegation gradually atrophies users' capacity to reason independently. Three converging pressures make correction difficult: commercial incentives that reward satisfaction over substance, LLMs’ tendency to revert to satisfaction-optimized defaults even when users push back, and a societal drift toward less-effortful engagement. We propose a research agenda to deepen the understanding of suppressed inquiry and how to counter it, to move closer to the remarkable thinking partners LLMs promised to be. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Exploring the platformization dilemma: How manufacturers leverage digital platforms for service business model innovation
Abstract: Recent research has highlighted the growing significance of digital platforms in manufacturing, particularly in driving service business model innovation (BMI). However, research gaps persist in understanding how a manufacturer's platform business configuration as well as its platform experience influence its service BMI capability. This paper addresses these gaps by using the digital platform capability approach as a theoretical framework and introducing the concept of digital platform experience. To conduct our study, we first derive hypotheses from literature and test them in a cross-sectional, three-stage empirical analysis using descriptive, bivariate and multivariate regression analysis. For this purpose, we use the German Manufacturing Survey, a representative, large-scale firm-level database, which encompasses 1334 firms from the German manufacturing sector. Our findings reveal that digital platforms play a central yet ambivalent role – depending on experience and configuration – in manufacturers' service BMI. Overall, moving into the platform business generally triggers service BMI. However, these effects are mostly confined to product-related BMI, while customer-oriented models are only enabled through more complex platform configurations. Notably, these positive innovation effects tend to be short-lived: in the long run, innovation dynamics slow down considerably, and manufacturers may face what we refer to as the “platformization dilemma.” © 2026 The Authors

Title: Natural Language Querying for Large Declarative Rule Repositories
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: In organizations, business processes are constrained by a large number of business rules that can, for example, be represented as process models, declarative constraints, or textual descriptions. When executing, auditing, or managing these processes, users may face specific questions that can only be answered by the declarative business rules that apply in this exact scenario. Non-technical users may only be able to specify their requirements in natural language queries, which need to be answered by specific business rules. However, the efficient matching between the natural language user query and the appropriate declarative business rules is not trivial because rules should be identified based on semantic similarity to the query, which may include synonyms and domain-specific technical terms. In this paper, we propose a system design that combines state-of-the-art technologies, namely Large Language Models, Vector Databases, and Retrieval Augmented Generation, to support cost-efficient natural language querying on large declarative rule repositories to identify appropriate rules. We provide a prototypical implementation of the system design and evaluate it on a large real-world declarative rule repository, showing the technical feasibility of the approach. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: An adaptive-problem structure framework for survival relevance in temporal processing
Abstract: Research on survival-relevant cues and subjective time often groups stimuli into immediate-survival, reproductive, and social categories. These labels do not explain why cues within one category recruit different temporal processes across contexts and perceivers. The Adaptive-Problem Structure (APS) Framework characterizes the adaptive problem indicated by a cue through two separable appraisals: ecological urgency, the time sensitivity and cost of delaying a response, and interpretive indeterminacy, the extent to which adaptive meaning and the appropriate response remain unresolved. APS predicts when these appraisals recruit established arousal, attention, information-sampling, and memory processes, how diagnostic context changes those links, and which personality differences strengthen them. Temporal consequences depend on the timing paradigm, interval, and response format. We outline independent ratings, selective within-domain manipulations, process measures, and staged construct validation. Five predictions specify task conditions, personality mappings, comparison baselines, and non-supporting outcomes. APS offers testable constraints on mechanism recruitment and prediction for new stimuli; the framework itself remains to be empirically validated. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A Business Blueprint for Data Monetization

Title: Large language model-based carbon emission forecasting: A sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework with transformer-long short-term memory networks
Abstract: Accurate forecasting of carbon emissions from coal, oil, natural gas, cement, and total CO2 is critical for formulating effective emission reduction strategies and carbon trading policies. However, existing models are plagued by overemphasis on total CO2 prediction, overreliance on single-task learning that overlooks cross-source correlations, neglect of sentiment information in carbon-related texts, and the absence of domain-adapted large language models (LLMs) for carbon sentiment extraction, which severely impairs their prediction accuracy and generalization ability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a novel sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework for carbon emission forecasting, which integrates an LLM with a Transformer-long short-term memory (LSTM) network. First, a domain-adapted LLM is developed based on DeepSeek-R1 and a multi-level fusion attention mechanism, enabling efficient sentiment feature extraction from carbon emission reports (e.g., policy, transaction, social awareness) with few-shot data. Second, a Transformer-LSTM-based multi-task learning model is designed to synergistically predict emissions from the five aforementioned sources by exploiting shared features and the complementary strengths of parallel computing and long-term dependency capture. Finally, a strengthened blood-sucking leech algorithm with Cauchy chaotic mutation and chaotic mapping is proposed to optimize the hyperparameters of the multi-task model, thus avoiding local optima and enhancing convergence stability. Validated on real-world data from the International Energy Agency, the proposed framework reduces the root mean square error by 11.14 tons compared with benchmark models. Meanwhile, the developed LLM achieves a sentiment classification accuracy 0.145 higher than baseline methods, which fully verifies the effectiveness of integrating sentiment information in carbon emission forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Biomass and MOF-derived FeCo/C aerogels with tailorable electromagnetic wave absorption performance
Abstract: The synergistic regulation of impedance matching and attenuation capability provides an effective strategy for achieving efficient electromagnetic wave absorption (EWA). However, challenges in cost and process remain for large-scale industrial applications. Herein, a facile one-step method is designed to synthesize a sugarcane-derived carbon aerogel loaded with FeCo bimetallic nanoparticle heterostructures (FeCo/C@SCA). It is revealed that the sugarcane-derived carbon aerogel retains its original pore structure without collapse after high-temperature carbonization with FeCo bimetallic nanoparticles uniformly distributed across the material surface. Its unique three-dimensional (3D) porous structure optimizes the impedance matching of the material, promoting multiple reflections and scattering of electromagnetic wave (EMW) within the material. The synergistic effect of dielectric loss and magnetic loss enhances the performance of the material in terms of EWA. Among these, FeCo/C@SCA achieves an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB, RL < −10 dB) of 7.2 GHz at a thickness of 1.7 mm when the Fe/Co ratio is 1:2; FeCo/C@SCA with an Fe/Co ratio of 1:1 achieves a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −52.60 dB at a thickness of 3.6 mm. Title: A balanced WINGS method for power-influence analysis: Simulation-based comparison with DEMATEL
Abstract: The WINGS method is derived from DEMATEL and incorporates both the influence among system elements and the power (importance) of each element into causal analysis to provide a more accurate assessment of a system. Title: Advancing decarbonization strategies: a techno-economic study of hydrogen-based SOFC cogeneration systems
Abstract: China’s industrial sector accounts for approximately 36% of the nation’s total greenhouse gas emissions and confronts mounting decarbonization pressure under the Dual Carbon targets, which mandate carbon peaking before 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. The pulp and paper manufacturing sector, a cornerstone of China’s light industry, requires sustained high-temperature process heat that cannot be readily electrified using current grid-based technologies, making it a priority candidate for hydrogen-based energy solutions. This study proposes and rigorously evaluates a hydrogen-fuelled Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) cogeneration system purpose-built for the pulp and paper industry in China, with scalable relevance to other energy-intensive manufacturing domains. Three cogeneration configurations are comparatively analysed: a conventional gas turbine operating on natural gas (C1), an SOFC system utilizing grey hydrogen derived from steam methane reforming (C2), and a fully integrated SOFC system powered by green hydrogen produced on-site via a renewable energy-driven multi-energy system comprising photovoltaic panels, electrolyzers, compressors, and hydrogen storage units (C3). The system is calibrated to the solar resource conditions of Shandong Province, the energy price structure under China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) tiered tariff framework, and domestic equipment costs expressed in Chinese Yuan. Employing a comprehensive techno-economic modelling framework, the study assesses each configuration in terms of net present cost (NPC), Levelized Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH), thermal and electrical outputs, and associated CO2 emissions across a 20-year project horizon. The findings reveal that the green hydrogen-powered SOFC system achieves near-complete grid independence and delivers an LCOH of 38.6 CNY/kg, decreasing to 34.8 CNY/kg when accounting for electricity sales revenue under Shandong Province’s distributed generation feed-in tariff. Furthermore, the hybrid SOFC system reduces CO2 emissions by 31% relative to the gas turbine baseline while reducing the mass flow of high-pressure steam by approximately 75%, a critical process integration consideration. Sensitivity analysis confirms that electricity export tariff policy is the dominant economic lever, whilst natural gas price volatility exerts the greatest influence on overall NPC. Policy scenarios under China’s National Hydrogen Strategy, including NDRC green hydrogen incentives and the national carbon emissions trading scheme, are evaluated to determine their combined impact on system viability. The results support a forward-looking policy framework that prioritises capital investment incentives and regulatory support for decentralised green hydrogen infrastructure and advanced SOFC technologies to accelerate industrial decarbonization in China. Title: Women in Business in the 21st Century: Challenges of the Socio-Economic Transition in Specific Contexts

Abstract: This paper explores the perspectives of women in business in specific contexts of the Western Balkans, with a focus on Bosnia and Herzegovina with additional data. Women in business are increasingly recognized as a vital driver not only of economic growth and poverty reduction, but of overall improvements in living standards within transition contexts. Despite the significant progress made by women in business in the Western Balkans region, they continue to face numerous socio-economic challenges that hinder their full potential. The paper provides an analysis of the key obstacles and stereotypes that persist for women in business in the 21st century in these specific contexts. Particular attention is paid to the challenges of reconciling professional and family responsibilities, which often limit women’s participation in business activities, especially in rural and smaller communities. On the other hand, the paper also highlights new opportunities and positive developments in recent years, as digital technologies, social media and online platforms offer women wider market access and flexibility in organizing their business operations. Title: MOOC Dropout Prediction with Machine Learning Techniques: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) have gained popularity as an accessible form of education, attracting a diverse and widespread student base. Despite their potential, MOOCs face a significant challenge: high dropout rates, which undermine their effectiveness and impact. The increasing interest in addressing this problem led to numerous studies developing new models to predict dropouts early and automatically, many of which use Machine Learning (ML) approaches. This research performs a quantitative synthesis of the performance of ML techniques for early dropout prediction in MOOCs. Following PRISMA guidelines, we perform a systematic review and meta-analysis. To analyze the overall performance, we use a random-effects model for a meta-analysis of proportions, analyzing two metrics: sensitivity and specificity. We have also studied the relationship between some of the studies’ characteristics and the performance obtained by means of subgroup analysis. The results indicate that ML systems are capable of accurately detecting a significant percentage of potential dropouts. However, the performance of these systems varies depending on the dataset and the definition of dropout used in each study. Despite the promising findings, the high heterogeneity observed across studies suggests that these results should be interpreted with caution. © The author(s) 2027.

Title: Climate-Informed Nonstationary Multihazard Design Load Characterization for Performance-Based Evaluation of Coastal Structures
Abstract: Current structural design guidelines face increasing challenges from interacting natural hazards in coastal regions. Climate-driven shifts in hazard intensity, frequency, and interaction add further complexity. Traditional multihazard design approaches often neglect hazard nonstationarity or treat hazards independently, resulting in inaccurate structural demands. This paper presents a probabilistic framework for simulating future multihazard scenarios under changing climate conditions. The nonstationary trends in hazard intensities and frequencies are characterized by probability distributions and regression models with time- and climate-informed parameters, respectively. Interhazard dependence is captured using multivariate copulas on the detrended hazard intensities. The framework supports two approaches: historical data-driven (suitable for regions with sufficient observations) and hybrid simulation-based (leveraging physics-based models to supplement limited observations). The framework's application is demonstrated on coastal wind and flood hazards for San Francisco (historical data-driven) and Miami (hybrid simulation-based), producing joint hazard curves (wind speed versus water level at a target return period) under multiple shared socioeconomic pathway scenarios through 2100. The resulting joint hazard curves provide a risk-consistent basis to select wind-flood intensity pairs for adaptive performance-based evaluation of coastal structures under future climate conditions. At the 100-year return period, ASCE 7 wind speeds are lower by about 21% and 17% in 2050 and 2100 for San Francisco, respectively, and by 6% and 9% for Miami, reinforcing the need to assess structural performance over the full joint hazard curve to capture compound loading scenarios and preserve reliability under nonstationary conditions.  © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Opening the black box of democracy in international business: polity, politics, and policy distances
Abstract: In the current context of democratic backsliding, different political systems, such as democracies and autocracies, as well as political differences between democracies, play an important role in shaping economic relationships. Yet, studies of political factors in international business mostly focus on destination country politics or political distance, conceptualized as cross-country differences in political institutions. Title: Visions, narratives and numbers: How roadmapping enables industrial transformation toward decarbonisation
Abstract: The transformation to a low-carbon industry requires different actors to work together and align their strategies. To support this process, policy and industry in many European countries have been driving the development of industry technology roadmaps at sectoral and national levels. However, limited attention has been paid to how visions, narratives and quantitative modelling work together within roadmapping to enable alignment and transformation across organisational, industry and policy levels. We examine industry technology roadmaps in six selected European countries, using secondary material, survey responses and two focus groups. The analysis is based on a conceptual framework that integrates the design and process elements considered important for roadmap development and implementation, complemented by the requirements for promoting industrial transformation rooted in the literature on socio-technical change. While most roadmaps included sophisticated modelling techniques and quantified scenarios, the study shows that a well-articulated narrative is equally important in mobilising stakeholders toward long-term industrial decarbonisation goals. Title: Thermo-mechanical mechanism of asperity-induced micropitting in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts
Abstract: This study develops an asperity-resolving, mechanism-oriented thermo-mechanical framework for investigating micropitting initiation in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts, using differential planetary gears as a representative high-power-density application. The framework sequentially maps transient gear-scale loading and sliding conditions onto a local representative volume element and iteratively couples thermal mixed elastohydrodynamic lubrication with mechanism-based strain-gradient plasticity. Micromorphic regularization is introduced to regularize highly localized plastic deformation under severe asperity contact. For the baseline operating condition, the coupled solution predicts a peak asperity pressure of 1.58 GPa and a localized flash temperature approaching 300 °C. Constitutive decomposition of the converged state indicates a crossover between near-surface thermal softening and subsurface geometrically necessary dislocation-mediated strengthening at approximately 1.62 μm. The associated fatigue-driving field is concentrated within a 0.63–2.30 μm subsurface band and reaches a maximum 34.6% above its surface value. Comparison with published experimental observations provides mechanism-level corroboration of the predicted damage-depth scale and preferential subsurface localization. The framework does not directly predict component-level fatigue life; rather, it provides topography-resolved, temperature- and size-dependent initiation fields that can serve as physically enriched local inputs to future macroscopic fatigue assessments. Explicit crack propagation, progressive material removal, and damage feedback remain outside the present scope. These findings clarify how frictional heat accumulation, high-frequency micro-slip, and strain-gradient strengthening jointly govern the early localization of micropitting damage in rough mixed-lubricated gear contacts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Škaljić E.; Krilašević S.; Karajko A.; Krivić S.
Author full names: Škaljić, Elma (60754841500); Krilašević, Suad (57204424292); Karajko, Ajla (60754535200); Krivić, Senka (49561566500)
Title: Artificial Intelligence in B&H: Scenarios and Strategic Pathways from the Perspective of Science and the Business Sector
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Although artificial intelligence is widely framed as a driver of productivity, innovation, and strategic decision-making, Bosnia and Herzegovina has not yet translated this potential into systemic implementation. In a post-transition setting marked by fragmented governance, dependence on imported solutions, persistent talent outflows, and weak technology transfer, the main constraint is less technological availability than institutional capacity, organisational readiness, and coordinated change. This paper addresses that gap by examining how two plausible drivers—(i) the routine standardisation of AI in firm processes and products, and (ii) the global concentration of AI expertise in wealthier economies—may shape labour markets, industrial structures, and institutional capabilities in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Drawing on two structured focus groups with representatives of academia and the business sector, the study applies a modified Futures Wheel to map primary and secondary effects across economic, social, legal, political, technological, and environmental dimensions, and then uses backcasting to construct scenario-based development pathways for 2025–2033. The results highlight path dependence and an implementation gap between declarative support and delivery capacity, pointing to risks of economic bifurcation, skill polarisation, and knowledge externalisation if early coordination fails. The paper proposes strategic interventions centred on institutional alignment, targeted sectoral prioritisation, human-capital development, governance operationalisation, and structured science–industry collaboration. By conceptualising AI adoption as an institutionally mediated and path-dependent process, the study offers empirically grounded guidance for moving from strategic ambition to feasible deployment in Bosnia and Herzegovina. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
