Authors: Zhang Y.; Cao W.; Hou R.
Author full names: Zhang, Yinsheng (55265270900); Cao, Weizhou (60856792300); Hou, Ruiqi (57673756300)
Title: RIOT: a Riemannian–optimal transport ensemble for robust supply chain delay prediction
Abstract: Accurate supply chain delay prediction is critical for enhancing operational efficiency and mitigating supply chain risks, yet existing machine learning models often struggle with class imbalance, noisy labels, distribution shifts, and feature perturbations in real-world logistics scenarios. We present RIOT (Riemannian–Optimal Transport), a geometry-aware fusion framework that integrates Riemannian geometry with optimal transport for stable and probability-aware multi-class delay prediction. Unlike conventional ensemble methods that rely on arithmetic averaging or fixed voting rules, RIOT treats base-learner probability outputs as structured distributions and performs probability aggregation on non-Euclidean geometric spaces. Specifically, Fisher–Rao intrinsic averaging preserves the local statistical geometry of class-probability vectors, whereas entropy-regularized Wasserstein barycentric alignment captures class-mass discrepancies under an ordinal delay-cost structure. RIOT combines these two summaries through a dual-geometric fusion mechanism with validation-based adaptive weighting and a selected mixing coefficient, thereby balancing local probabilistic consistency and transport-based class-mass alignment.Experiments on the INCOM2024 open dataset demonstrate that RIOT achieves the strongest aggregate performance under a leakage-controlled prediction protocol. Across five random seeds, RIOT attains an AUC-ROC of 0.887 ± 0.0064, exceeding XGBoost-v2 and LightGBM by 0.013 and 0.019 AUC-ROC points, respectively. It also achieves the highest Macro-F1 of 0.718 ± 0.0075 and the lowest ECE, Brier score, and NLL values of 0.032, 0.160, and 0.481, respectively, indicating that the benefit of geometric fusion extends beyond discrimination to class-balanced prediction and probability-quality assessment. Under stress conditions, RIOT remains top-ranked across increasing label corruption, covariate shift, concept drift, and surrogate-generated continuous-feature FGSM perturbation stress tests. At 30% label corruption, its AUC-ROC remains 0.853; under FGSM perturbation at ε = 0.20, it retains an AUC-ROC of 0.864.Ablation and ensemble-comparison analyses further show that the full RIOT model achieves higher mean AUC-ROC than its Fisher–Rao-only, OT-only, adaptive-weight-only, arithmetic-averaging, and standard ensemble-fusion variants. Pairwise DeLong tests provide statistical support for the gains over the two single-geometry variants and stacking, whereas the smaller improvement over adaptive-weight-only remains modest and does not reach the conventional significance threshold. The best mean AUC-ROC is observed at α = 0.6, while performance remains stable for α values between 0.5 and 0.8. Leakage-controlled attribution analysis identifies pre-event calendar variables, customer-region attributes, product information, payment-related variables, and order-quantity features as the main predictive factors. Complementary validation on the public Airlines delay benchmark further shows that RIOT remains top-ranked on a related binary delay-prediction task, although this independently retrained setting should not be interpreted as direct cross-dataset transfer. These gains are accompanied by higher training time, inference latency, and memory usage than strong single-model baselines, but post-hoc sparsification reduces the active model count and latency while preserving most of the predictive performance. Overall, RIOT provides an empirically supported geometric fusion strategy for stable and probability-aware supply-chain delay prediction in risk-sensitive operational settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Author full names: Semenova, Tatiana Y. (57438812500); Sokolov, Iaroslav O. (59750839300); Medvedeva, Liubov V. (59302846300); Katysheva, Elena G. (57191841154)
Title: Balanced Risk Assessment and Management in Development of Hard-To-Recover Reserves Using Example of Heavy Oil
Source title: International Journal of Engineering, Transactions A: Basics
Abstract: Depletion of conventional oil fields and increasing requirements for the economic justification of investment projects enhance the significance of developing hard-to-recover reserves, including heavy oil, which is characterized by technological complexity, high energy intensity, and multifactor uncertainty. This study proposes a balanced risk assessment framework that integrates Monte Carlo simulation with a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system. Quantitative project parameters are modeled as random variables, while poorly formalized geological, technical, operational, environmental, social, and political-regulatory risks are aggregated into an integral fuzzy risk index. The proposed framework is tested using open data for a heavy oil project and four integration variants: a baseline Monte Carlo model without fuzzy risk adjustment, a model with risk-adjusted mean values, a model with risk-adjusted standard deviations, and a combined model. The fuzzy inference system produced a high integral risk index, Rhtr = 0.782. In the baseline model, expected NPV was -1.79 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV was 66.52%. When the integral risk index was incorporated through shifts in expected values, expected NPV decreased to approximately -6.76 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV increased to 89.90%. The combined model produced a similar central shift, with expected NPV of -6.75 billion USD and P(NPV < 0) of 89.44%, while also reflecting increased distributional uncertainty. The results show that the main economic effect of integral risk is associated with systematic changes in expected CAPEX, OPEX, production rate, and decline rate, whereas variance-only adjustment has limited influence on central project metrics. The proposed approach provides a transparent tool for linking qualitative risk assessment with probabilistic economic evaluation and supports more conservative investment decision-making in heavy oil development projects. © 2026 The author(s). Authors: Rani N.; Singh S.
Title: Business Intelligence as a Strategic Tool for Enhancing Employee Engagement and Organizational Efficiency
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This study quantitatively examined the strategic impact of Business Intelligence (BI) adoption on employee engagement and organizational efficiency with Gender as a potential moderating factor. To test the hypotheses, regression analysis showed that BI adoption had a significant effect on employee engagement (R =.585) and organizational efficiency (R =.558). The findings indicate that making informed decisions based on data, and having the relevant information available, such as real-time data from BI dashboards, facilitates employee empowerment and simplifies processes, resulting in enhanced engagement and productivity. While the original hypotheses were intended to include Gender as a moderator, moderation analyses were provided for H3 and H4. There’s a contradiction: the gender has a positive interaction with the main BI impact on engagement effect, but when it comes to organizational efficiency as a whole, it shows a negative effect, so gender does not moderate the relationship between BI adoption and organizational efficiency. Clarify the coding (e.g., Female = 0, Male = 1 if you claim a stronger effect for females) and report the simple slopes with their standard errors and p-values (Female β = 1.3288; Male β = 0.7222) so the interpretation is verifiable. However, gender was determined not to be an important moderator for the BI adoption-organizational efficiency relationship. The study suggests that larger firms, with their increased resources and formalized processes, are likely to derive more value from BI, which contributes to the justification for a size-specific BI strategy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: He L.; Lv X.; Yu Y.; Huang Y.; Liang L.; Wang M.; Jin G.; Zhao J.
Title: Hydrogen-bonded assisted network of alkali lignin nanoparticles in starch/gelatin films: Concentration-dependent enhancement of UV-shielding, antioxidant activity, and oxygen barrier
Source title: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
Abstract: To address the limitations of conventional petroleum-based packaging, this study developed biodegradable composite films by incorporating alkali lignin nanoparticles (LNPs) into a corn starch (CS) and gelatin (GEL) matrix. The findings demonstrated that the LNPs were highly compatible with the CS/GEL matrix. The FTIR and XRD analyses offer indirect evidence suggesting the creation of hydrogen-bonded networks between LNPs and CS/GEL matrix. This structural integration was accompanied by simultaneous enhancement of multiple functional properties that are usually incompatible in biopolymer films. In particular, the LNPs contributed to high hydrophobicity and outstanding UV-blocking ability (over 99.9% in the UVC region) due to phenolic chromophores, while also greatly enhancing thermal stability (Tg > 120 °C) and oxygen barrier properties. Notably, antioxidant activity increased proportionally with concentration, achieving about 40–60% improvement in radical scavenging and more than 200% increase in reducing power, due to the exposed phenolic hydroxyl groups of LNPs. However, loading LNPs beyond 3% caused particle aggregation, which weakened the mechanical strength. These findings indicate that LNPs act not just as fillers but as multifunctional crosslinkers that enhance CS/GEL films into high-performance, sustainable packaging materials. This study offers an environmentally friendly approach to valorize industrial alkali lignin and address the limitation of single functionality in biodegradable food packaging. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Wu Y.; Lin B.; Liu T.; Shi Y.; Zhang Z.; Liu T.; Huang T.
Title: Macro–micro seepage interaction mechanism in coal treated by a high-temperature CO2–H2O system
Abstract: To quantitatively elucidate the coupling mechanisms between macroscopic permeability and microscopic flow behavior of coal under high-temperature CO2–H2O coupled conditions, a multiscale experimental–numerical research framework integrating permeability tests, CT-based pore network modeling (PNM), and pore-scale numerical simulations was established. Wulan and Sujiagou coal samples were selected as the research objects and subjected to high-temperature CO2–H2O treatment. The evolution of coal permeability was systematically investigated under constant gas pressure, constant confining pressure, and constant effective stress conditions. The results indicate that, under constant gas pressure, coal permeability decreases exponentially with increasing effective stress; under constant effective stress, permeability also decreases exponentially with increasing gas pressure; whereas under constant confining pressure, permeability increases exponentially with increasing gas pressure. PNM-based analyses reveal that high-temperature CO2–H2O coupling significantly alters the pore–throat structural characteristics of coal. For the Wulan coal sample, the maximum pore coordination number increases from 5 to 7, and the average equivalent throat radius increases from 19.88 μm to 22.70 μm. While for the Sujiagou coal sample, the maximum pore coordination number rises from 6 to 9, and the average equivalent throat radius increases from 28.90 μm to 33.21 μm. The increase in the equivalent throat size directly reduces the resistance to fluid flow. In addition, the fractal dimensions of the Wulan and Sujiagou coal samples increase from 2.072 to 2.223 and from 2.236 to 2.259, the increase in fractal dimension reflects a more fully developed pore structure, respectively, whereas the tortuosity of both coal samples exhibits a pronounced decrease, indicating enhanced pore structure complexity and reduced flow resistance after treatment. The pore-scale seepage simulation results obtained using COMSOL Multiphysics show a high degree of consistency with the macroscopic permeability experiments, further demonstrating that, after treatment, fluids preferentially migrate through larger pores and well-connected throats, forming localized dominant seepage channels. These findings quantitatively confirm that thermo–pressure coupling effects significantly enhance coal seepage capacity by improving pore–throat connectivity and flow efficiency, and establish a direct quantitative link between microscopic structural evolution and macroscopic permeability enhancement of coal under high-temperature CO2–H2O coupled conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Practices and Social Relations in Foreign Entrepreneurship in Catania and Messina
Abstract: This chapter investigates migrant entrepreneurship in the metropolitan contexts of Catania and Messina. Building on the growing economic and social relevance of migrant-owned businesses, the study explores their characteristics, relational dynamics, and key challenges, with particular attention to territorial embeddedness and interactions with the local ecosystem. The research adopts an integrated methodological approach combining quantitative and qualitative tools, with a primary focus on semi-structured interviews conducted with migrant entrepreneurs and key actors such as accountants, Chambers of Commerce, and trade associations. Findings show that migrant entrepreneurship is often a pathway to autonomy, evolving from necessity into a life project, with social networks playing a key role in business creation and consolidation. At the same time, significant challenges persist, including limited access to credit, language barriers, bureaucratic complexity, and weak institutional engagement. The study highlights implications for training interventions aimed at strengthening access to financial, informational, and relational resources. © The Author(s) 2027.

Authors: Bagies T.
Author full names: Bagies, Taghreed (57224616972)
Title: Automatic binary security classification of arabic mobile app reviews using transformer models and active learning
Abstract: Mobile application user reviews provide valuable insights into user-reported issues, including security concerns that are critical for software engineering activities such as requirements analysis and system design. However, existing research has largely focused on English reviews and lacks systematic approaches for identifying security-related feedback in Arabic, a low-resource language in this domain. In this paper, we address this gap by developing an integrated approach for automated binary classification of security-related versus non-security-related Arabic mobile app reviews, grounded in a structured set of security requirement categories derived from software engineering literature. We collected 14,667,283 reviews from 56 mobile applications across multiple domains, including government, finance, and social platforms. Using natural language processing techniques and sentiment-based filtering, positive reviews were removed as a dataset-reduction step, while neutral and negative reviews were retained for subsequent analysis. To construct a high-quality labeled dataset, we developed an annotation approach combining keyword-guided sample selection, expert annotation, and iterative dataset refinement using active learning. During the active learning phase, semantic feature representations were generated using Low-Rank Adaptation-enhanced sentence transformers and combined with machine learning classifiers within an agreement-based active learning strategy to identify candidate samples for expert validation. The process was conducted over ten iterations, starting with 300 expert-annotated reviews and terminating when classifier performance stabilized. Following the stopping criterion, the final classifier-agreement samples were expert-validated and used to construct a held-out test set rather than being added to the training data. The active learning process resulted in a final training dataset of 10,632 expert-validated reviews. In addition, 1000 expert-validated reviews were reserved as a held-out test set and excluded from model training. The training dataset was used to fine-tune three transformer models, namely CAMeLBERT, MARBERT, and Paraphrase, for binary classification of security-related and non-security-related reviews. CAMeLBERT achieved the highest performance among the fine-tuned models, with 95.76% accuracy and 95.77% F1-score under 10-fold cross-validation and 91.20% accuracy and 91.16% F1-score on the held-out test set. To support practical adoption, we developed a web-based interface integrated with a large language model to enable real-time classification and provide interpretable explanations. The resulting dataset and developed approach contribute to advancing security-aware analysis of Arabic user-generated content and support software engineers in identifying security-related concerns in mobile application reviews. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Ye T.; Guo P.; Deng F.; Guo Y.; Su C.; Zeng Z.; Li L.; Ma X.
Title: Mechanical compaction-assisted activation for the controlled construction of ultramicroporous biochar for efficient CO2 capture
Source title: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
Abstract: Conventional activation of porous carbon CO2 adsorbents commonly relies on higher activation temperatures or larger activator dosages, often causing carbon loss and pore widening. Herein, O/S-doped ultramicroporous biochars were prepared from sodium lignosulfonate by mechanical compaction-assisted potassium oxalate activation. Precursor packing was regulated to tune the local activation environment and transport behavior during pyrolysis. Compared with the uncompacted sample at 600 °C, compaction increased SBET from 491 to 823 m2 g−1, CO2-accessible ultramicropore volume increased from 0.264 to 0.355 mL g−1, and carbon yield increased from 26.6% to 29.3%. LSC600-5T achieved a CO2 uptake of 5.64 mmol g−1 at 25 °C and 1 bar, while LSC700-5T delivered 9.02 mmol g−1 at 0 °C and 1 bar. However, at 25 °C and 0.15 bar, LSC600-5T showed a CO2 uptake of 2.01 mmol g−1, close to that of LSC600-0T. Structural, correlation, and simulation analyses show that CO2 adsorption at 1 bar is primarily controlled by accessible ultramicropore volume and pore connectivity, while low-pressure uptake is dominated by ~0.35 nm ultramicropores, with O/S polar groups providing additional affinity. Unlike conventional activation that enhances porosity by increasing temperature or activator dosage, mechanical compaction regulates precursor packing and the local activation environment, simultaneously improving accessible ultramicroporosity and carbon retention. This work shifts porous-carbon design from surface-area maximization toward packing-controlled regulation of pore accessibility, carbon utilization, and pressure-dependent CO2 adsorption. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Extracellular vesicles in neurodegenerative diseases: A new frontier in diagnosis and therapy
Abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and Huntington's disease are among the progressive disorders of the nervous system that are characterized by the gradual destruction of neurons, the accumulation of misfolded proteins, and the limited effective therapeutic options. In recent years, numerous lines of evidence have emphasized the important role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in the formation and progression of these diseases. These vesicles are membrane-bound nanoscale structures that are secreted by almost all cell types and play a role in cell-cell communication through the transfer of molecules such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. In neurodegenerative disorders, EVs can facilitate the transport and dissemination of disease-related proteins, including amyloid-β, tau, α-synuclein, mutant huntingtin, SOD1, and TDP-43, thus contributing to the spread of pathological processes in different parts of the nervous system. On the other hand, the ability of these vesicles to cross the blood–brain barrier and reflect molecular changes occurring in the central nervous system makes them valuable candidates for the development of minimally invasive biomarkers. This review reviews the biogenesis, classification, isolation methods, and molecular content of EVs, and analyzes their role in the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment of the most important neurodegenerative diseases. Also, the importance of EV-associated proteins, RNAs, and lipids as emerging diagnostic biomarkers, as well as the therapeutic potential of natural and engineered vesicles as drug delivery systems and regulators of neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative processes, is discussed. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Author full names: Espinosa-Andrade, Noemi (57192868200); Aranceta-Garza, Fernando (36772780100); Cisneros-Montemayor, Andrés (36094057100); Zetina-Rejón, Manuel J. (6506696172); Charles, Anthony (7101891109); Espinosa-Romero, María José (37004325900)
Title: Use of Social Network Analysis for community-led area-based fisheries management: The case of tropical lobster fisheries
Abstract: Co-management is essential for successful community-based fishery reserves such as Mexico’s Fishing Refuge Zones (FRZs), but they can be hindered by gaps in institutional capacity that undermine collaborative governance. This study analyzes the governance networks underpinning FRZs in Punta Allen and Maria Elena, two small-scale fishing communities within the Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve, Mexican Caribbean. Using a social-ecological system lens and social network analysis, we analyzed the structure, cohesion, and resilience of the governance networks of both communities, using semi-structured interviews and a weighted interaction index that integrates communication frequency and quality, trust, and collaboration. Results show structural differences between governance networks. Punta Allen exhibits a more decentralized, cohesive, and diversified network that links community actors, civil society organizations (CSOs), and government agencies, fostering multiple pathways for collaboration. María Elena presents a more centralized and segmented configuration, with strong dependence on CSOs and limited integration of governmental actors. Resilience simulations further demonstrate that decentralized structures maintain coordination under disturbance more effectively than centralized ones. Although FRZs are formally established by federal authorities, their local-level operational governance is sustained by informal social relationships that enable trust, reciprocity, and local coordination. Our findings show that FRZs can function as effective co-management instruments within MPAs, but their long-term viability requires strengthening institutional coordination, diversifying actor participation, and ensuring consistent governmental presence to reduce fragmentation. By diagnosing governance gaps and highlighting structural strengths, this study provides a transferable framework for improving the design, implementation, and policy uptake of community-based conservation and small-scale fisheries management initiatives. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Local and global uncertainty quantification for a family of fuzzy multi-criteria sorting models
Abstract: This paper introduces a family of FMAVT-Sort models based on a fuzzy extension of the Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) method MAVT, alongside a framework for Uncertainty and Distinction Quantification (UQ and DQ) of the model outputs. The models differ in approaches to evaluating functions of fuzzy numbers (FNs), employing both precise and approximate techniques, and utilize four fuzzy ranking methods: defuzzification-based approaches (Centroid Index and Integral of Means), and two methods designed for ranking dependent FNs. The models are applied to a case study on university teacher evaluation. Assessment of local (within the case study) UQ and DQ and global (across a space of independent multicriteria problems) DQ is performed using algorithms that process output values from a large number of fuzzy multicriteria sorting problems simulated via Monte Carlo techniques in a fuzzy environment. A set of UQ indices, combined with a pre-uncertainty analysis stage, is implemented in a General Algorithm for Multicriteria Sorting, designed to support the decision-making process. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of UQ indices for decision support in multicriteria sorting and reveal significant distinctions among FMAVT-Sort models, underscoring the impact of model selection on final sorting outcomes. Title: Robust firm-level revenue forecasting using stacked hybrid ensemble frameworks: Evidence from the semiconductor industry
Abstract: Accurate revenue forecasting is essential for financial planning, resource allocation, and strategic decision-making in the volatile semiconductor industry. This study proposes the Stacked Hybrid Ensemble (SHE) framework, a novel forecasting architecture that integrates long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, Transformer models, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) to predict monthly revenue for Taiwan-listed semiconductor firms. Our approach incorporates time series decomposition to analyze trend, seasonality, and residual components, and examines how firm size impacts forecast accuracy. The proposed SHE framework combines stacking ensemble with a dynamic weighting mechanism to adaptively fuse model predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that SHE outperforms all individual models across four error metrics, achieving up to a 35.4% improvement in mean squared error (MSE). Through rigorous statistical validation using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, we confirm that SHE’s performance superiority is systematic and statistically significant ((Formula presented) ) across all 26 companies, providing high reliability for practical applications. For business practitioners and investors, these findings offer substantial value: (1) financial managers can enhance budgeting accuracy and cash-flow planning; (2) operations directors can improve production scheduling and inventory management; and (3) investors gain more reliable tools for company valuation and risk assessment. The framework’s consistent performance across different firm sizes makes it particularly valuable for portfolio analysis and supply-chain decision-making in the cyclical semiconductor sector. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Anchored FLoE: A Business-Guardrailed Ensemble Framework of Foundation and Local-Trained Models for Demand Forecasting
Abstract: Accurate demand forecasting is vital for retail supply chain efficiency, yet a persistent trust-capacity gap limits industrial production to low-capacity interpretable models that fail to capture complex market dynamics. We propose Anchored FLoE, a dual-model framework that bridges this gap by fusing high-capacity deep learning with rigorous business guardrails. The framework integrates: (1) FLoE, an ensemble merging a frozen Time Series Foundation Model (Chronos-2) for global generalization with a Local Specialist (TFT) for domain-specific patterns; and (2) a model-agnostic Anchor Layer that enforces economic monotonicity and business-logic consistency through discount-segmented confidence bands. Validated across 524 product-market segments, Anchored FLoE achieves an 11-percentage-point improvement in sales-weighted MAPE over production baselines, translating to a multi-million dollar impact on free cash flow. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Semantically-Guided LLM Pipeline for Business Architecture Modelling with Incremental Knowledge Acquisition
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Business Architecture (BA) modelling is a resource-intensive exercise, particularly for abstract concepts such as business capabilities that typically requires iterative workshops that are time-consuming and cognitively demanding for experts. Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising solution for automating BA modelling. However, current methods often fail to capture task context, producing semantically invalid models. Although LLMs can be pre-trained or fine-tuned to encode such context, it is costly and difficult to sustain. This paper proposes an LLM pipeline for business capability modeling that integrates rich contextual knowledge by combining a BA semantic model with organisational insights extracted from unstructured business documents and incrementally acquired expert knowledge. We evaluate the approach on three state-of-the-art LLMs by processing 495 statements extracted from business documents, and compare its performance against the baselines combine standard definitions and in-context learning. Our method reports an average performance gain of 65.2% on a commercial LLM and 58.9%–63.8% on two open-source LLMs over the baselines. This work advances the automation of LLM based BA modelling by providing an effective and efficient mechanism for incorporating existing documents and expert feedback into the automation process with minimal expert involvement. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Human-Centered E-Business Systems Based on Situation Awareness: A Contextual Framework Driven by Artificial Intelligence
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: In recent years, e-business ecosystems have evolved into complex and data-driven information systems, where adaptability to the context has become a critical success factor. Traditional decision-making models, however, often prove inadequate to manage the dynamism and uncertainty of today’s digital environments, creating a gap between the richness of available data and the ability of systems to exploit it proactively. This article proposes an innovative framework integrating Artificial Intelligence and Situation Awareness to develop human-centered and adaptive E-Business Information Systems (EBIS). Our approach combines the Situation Awareness (SA) paradigm, which is the ability to perceive, understand, and project future states of the context, with a multilevel software architecture. By leveraging the integration of data from the Internet of Things (IoT), the formalization of knowledge through semantic ontologies, and the predictive power of Bayesian probabilistic models, the framework enables systems to react and anticipate user needs. The validation of the framework, conducted through a use case in the domain of smart cultural tourism at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii, demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach by defining a solid methodological basis for the creation of next-generation e-business systems, capable of learning and reacting dynamically, improving the resilience of processes and placing the user at the center of an intelligent and personalized digital experience. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Can FinTech mitigate systemic risk? Evidence from macroprudential policies and bank business diversification
Abstract: Using Chinese commercial banks as the sample and drawing on panel data from both listed and unlisted banks, this paper systematically examines the mechanism through which financial technology (FinTech) influences bank systemic risk from 2007 to 2023. The results indicate that the development of FinTech significantly reduces systemic risk in the banking sector. Moreover, business diversification serves as an important mediating channel. Further analysis reveals that macroprudential policies strengthen the risk-mitigating impact of FinTech on bank systemic risk, with stronger statistical evidence for price-based policies. Heterogeneity tests show that the risk-mitigating effect of FinTech is stronger among banks with greater homogeneity in their asset and liability structures. Title: Debonding-on-demand adhesives for circular automotive manufacturing: Triggering mechanisms, joint performance, and process integration - A systematic review
Source title: International Journal of Adhesion and Adhesives
Abstract: Adhesive bonding is a critical enabling technology for lightweight multi-material automotive structures combining steel, aluminium, carbon fibre reinforced polymers (CFRP), and thermoplastics. However, conventional structural adhesives are permanent by design, creating a fundamental conflict with end-of-life recyclability targets that require vehicles to achieve 85% recyclability and 95% recoverability by mass and EV battery packs to use joining methods compatible with disassembly. Debonding-on-demand (DoD) adhesives—systems that maintain structural performance in service but release controllably upon application of an external stimulus— represent a promising reso-lution to this conflict. This paper presents a systematic review of the DoD adhesive literature. Although the literature search spanned 2000–2025 to capture foundational work, the field is recent and the majority of quantitative studies benchmarked here were published between 2019 and 2025; the review therefore emphasises this period while retaining seminal earlier references. Four stimulus categories are covered: thermal (Diels–Alder reversible networks, thermally expandable particles, and vitrimer/covalent adaptable networks), electrical, photothermal/UV, and magnetic/hybrid. Quantitative performance data from over 40 primary studies are benchmarked against automotive lap-shear, fatigue, and crash-stability requirements. Process integration challenges—including paint-shop cure compatibility, trigger de-livery in assembled structures, surface preparation, scalability, and supply-chain incentive alignment—are critically assessed. Key findings are: (i) TEP-modified structural adhesives achieve debonding at 120–175 °C via electromagnetic induction while maintaining 20–25 MPa pre-debond lap-shear strength on CFRP/Al/steel substrates; (ii) Diels–Alder epoxy systems now reach competitive lap-shear strengths of 12–16 MPa with debonding at 140 °C, whilst vitrimer adhesives provide an emerging route to recyclable structural bonding; (iii) the split-incentive problem is the dominant systemic barrier to adoption; and (iv) no standardised DoD test protocol, long-term durability data, or comprehensive life-cycle assessment currently exists. Five research gaps define the agenda for future work. © 2026 The Author

Authors: Le N.; Lam T.; Duong H.-P.
Title: Behavioural leakage and the illusion of actionability: A deployment-honest evaluation framework for educational early warning systems
Abstract: Educational Early Warning Systems (EWS) rely on feature-selection components that systematically conflate retrospective accuracy with operational utility. We formalise two deployment failure modes: Behavioural Leakage, an EWS-specific subclass of temporal leakage in which selectors draw signal from pedagogically actionable student behaviours that are unobservable at the prediction horizon, and the Illusion of Actionability, the limiting case in which the entire nominal actionability of a selection is illusory. To detect and prevent these failures, we contribute a machine-checkable no-leakage certificate, kept deliberately separate from an intervention-utility score and connected to it by a continuous actionability-dilution coefficient; a two-protocol evaluation design whose primary deployment estimate retrains on horizon-available features only, while a Deployment-Realistic Evaluation (DRE) audit quantifies the degradation of an already-deployed model under missing late features; and a reference selector, Intervention-Constrained Feature Selection (IC-FS), that satisfies the certificate by construction. Experiments on three public benchmarks and a real secondary-school cohort in Vietnam show that standard selectors can exhibit the strict Illusion of Actionability at course start, and that under a corrected, group-aware evaluation protocol IC-FS trades a small, explicitly quantified amount of at-risk predictive performance for substantially higher available actionability, with the certificate satisfied in every fold. A fairness audit across sensitive attributes and an exploratory single-school operational case study complete the deployment-honest evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Circular bioeconomy pathways for converting seafood processing wastes into low-emission marine fuels: Waste management, technologies, life-cycle impacts and policy enablers
Abstract: Seafood processing industries generate substantial quantities of organic residues, including fish heads, frames, skins, scales, viscera, crustacean and molluscan shells, sludge and wastewater solids, many of which remain underutilized. Converting marine processing wastes into renewable marine fuels presents a promising circular bioeconomy strategy that addresses both waste management challenges and maritime decarbonization goals. This review examines the potential of marine processing residues as feedstocks for low emission marine fuels by synthesizing knowledge across feedstock characteristics and waste management practices, conversion technologies, life cycle environmental performance and policy and market frameworks. Marine by-products can support multiple fuel pathways. The suitability of each pathway depends strongly on feedstock composition, moisture content, nitrogen levels, and system integration. Life cycle assessment studies indicate that marine waste derived fuels can reduce environmental impacts compared with conventional disposal and fossil marine fuels, although performance depends on factors such as feedstock logistics, upgrading requirements, methane leakage control and energy inputs. The review highlights the role of emerging regulatory frameworks such as the IMO greenhouse gas strategy and FuelEU Maritime regulation in shaping future fuel adoption. Marine waste to fuel systems can contribute to maritime decarbonization when implemented within cascading circular bioeconomy models that prioritize high value compound recovery before energy conversion. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Hsu Y.-C.; Chen Y.-C.; Lin K.-P.
Title: Novel intuitionistic fuzzy-enhanced deep learning network with squeeze-and-excite block model for assessment of bronchopulmonary dysplasia
Abstract: Early prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) in very low birth weight (VLBW) preterm infants is essential for timely clinical intervention. However, neonatal chest radiographs are often characterized by high diagnostic uncertainty and limited annotated data, which restrict the performance of conventional deep learning models. Therefore, this study proposes a hybrid intuitionistic fuzzy-enhanced deep learning framework that combines uncertainty-aware image enhancement with SE-block-enhanced U-Net and GoogLeNet classifiers. Specifically, an intuitionistic fuzzy (IF) transformation is first applied as an uncertainty-aware preprocessing step to enhance ambiguous radiographic patterns before image classification. Subsequently, squeeze-and-excitation (SE) blocks adaptively recalibrate channel-wise feature responses to emphasize clinically relevant lung structures. To further improve the effectiveness of the proposed framework, a genetic algorithm (GA) was employed to jointly optimize the intuitionistic fuzzy parameter (α) together with the learning rate, dropout rate, and training epochs. The GA serves as an integral component of the proposed framework to identify an effective parameter configuration, thereby improving the stability and predictive performance of the CNN classifiers under limited-data conditions.Experiments conducted under a standard 8:1:1 training–validation–testing split demonstrated that the proposed model achieved a mean accuracy of 0.857, together with favorable Recall (Sensitivity) and F1-score for the BPD-positive class, indicating competitive predictive performance among the evaluated deep learning models. Furthermore, under a more challenging 6:2:2 data-constrained partition, the proposed IF-U-Net with the SE block maintained a mean accuracy of 0.818, demonstrating stable predictive performance across different evaluation settings. Representative Grad-CAM visualizations qualitatively showed that the proposed framework focused on clinically relevant lung regions during prediction, providing interpretable insight into the model’s attention in representative cases. The experimental results suggest that integrating IF modeling with evolutionary optimization improves predictive performance and robustness under limited-data conditions. The proposed framework therefore provides a promising decision-support tool for early BPD prediction in clinical environments where labeled data are limited. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Tan L.; Song X.; Zhou H.
Title: State estimation with unknown input rejection under non-Gaussian disturbances
Abstract: In practice, system models are often subject to unmeasurable unknown input disturbances. Furthermore, communication networks are typically corrupted by non-Gaussian noise. To solve the composite disturbance in state estimation, this paper presents a maximum correntropy Kalman filter with unknown input disturbance rejection (MCKF-UIR), without making any prior assumptions about the unknown inputs. Specifically, the equivalent measurement injection is adopted as a disturbance compensation method to suppress the effects of unknown inputs on the state. Based on the modified state equation, this paper constructs an augmented state model using prior state estimates and measurement vectors. A lower-triangular decorrelation transformation is then introduced to eliminate the cross-correlation terms in the error covariance matrix, yielding a block-diagonal covariance structure. Moreover, the maximum correntropy criterion-based (MCC) optimization function along with fixed-point iteration (FPI) approach are employed to derive the optimal gain matrix and state estimate. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that compared with the traditional Kalman filter with unknown input rejection (KF-UIR), the proposed MCKF-UIR exhibits stronger adaptability to compound disturbances comprising both unknown inputs and non-Gaussian noise. Furthermore, it eliminates the need for explicit unknown input estimation and avoids the iterative computations required for solving the MCC-based optimal unknown input estimate, reducing computational complexity. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Adaptive threshold estimation for uncertain differential equations with jumps

Abstract: This study presents a parameter estimation methodology for uncertain differential equations with jumps, which are widely used to characterize complex phenomena in finance, physics, engineering, and other interdisciplinary fields. Title: Development and Validation of a Roadmapping Methodology for Servitization
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Servitization, the transition from product—towards service-centric offerings, offers manufacturers an opportunity to achieve relevant strategic advantage, sustainable impact and increased efficiency, while tackling encompassing challenges and global trends. This transition, enhanced by the combined adoption of digital technologies, requires a significant company transformation, which implies challenges related to the creation and deployment of new activities, resources mindset and partnerships. To manage the transformation and the related challenges, roadmapping can support companies in planning strategic and operational activities and effectively steer efforts. Nonetheless, current literature offers limited approaches for roadmapping in servitization. This paper proposes and validates, through the application in two manufacturing companies, a multi-step roadmapping methodology, leveraging the Business Model Canvas framework. This tool, intended for the application during the initial new business model definition phase, supports companies in building roadmaps to guide and structure strategic and operational activities for servitization, harmonizing efforts across extended timeframes. The paper complements the current research on Product Service System (PSS) design considering the extended transformational process required to sustain the new offerings, while proposing a structured tool to guide manufacturers’ efforts in deploying servitization strategies. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Future Trends in Sustainable Supply Chain Development
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Sustainable supply chain development has evolved from a peripheral corporate initiative into a central pillar of global business strategy. As industries confront climate change, geopolitical uncertainty, and digital transformation, the sustainability of supply chains has become a determinant of long-term competitiveness and resilience. This study reviews the current literature and proposes a conceptual synthesis of future trends that will shape sustainable supply chain development. Through an integrative review of studies published between 2020 and 2025, the discussion identifies six main paths: (1) circular economy integration, (2) digitalization and artificial intelligence, (3) decarbonization and renewable energy adoption, (4) stakeholder collaboration and social equity, (5) data transparency and governance, and (6) resilience through regionalization and risk diversification. The paper argues that future sustainable supply chains will be characterized by intelligent, data-driven systems embedded in circular and low-carbon business models. It concludes by outlining managerial and policy implications, emphasizing the need for collaborative frameworks, digital literacy, and global governance mechanisms to enable the transition toward sustainable, resilient, and inclusive supply networks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Least-cost optimal scenarios to a net-zero energy system: integration of battery energy storage, hydrogen storage, and carbon capture and storage
Abstract: The rapid economic development and industrialisation in worldwide, result in rising electricity consumption, which primary supplied based on fossil fuels. Emissions reduction technologies and economic drivers are important in the transition towards carbon neutral system. Ireland has set a net-zero emissions target to achieve climate goals established under Paris Agreement. This study compares four energy policy transition pathways to achieve net-zero emissions by 2040, integrating multiple fuel technologies into a long-term optimisation framework, and assessing their economic viability, policy alignment, and technological feasibility. A linear power system optimisation model was developed in Python to investigate four scenarios. Scenario 1 integrates lithium-ion battery storage; Scenario 2 incorporates fossil-fuelled combined-cycle gas turbines with carbon capture; Scenario 3 introduces power-to-hydrogen technology for long-duration storage; and Scenario 4 introduces floating photovoltaic generation. The results indicate that an electricity system dominated by offshore wind can meet hourly demand requirements and ensure supply continuity. Scenario 4 reduces the offshore wind capacity requirement by up to 26.29 GW, while Scenario 3 lowers the required battery capacity by up to 479.27 GWh. Scenario 2 achieves the lowest levelised cost of electricity, ranging from 82.99 €/MWh to 118 €/MWh. The study highlights the critical role of integrated power to hydrogen to power, natural gas flexible generation with carbon capture and storage, battery storage, and floating photovoltaic in achieving net-zero energy system and offers a policy-informed assessment of multiple scenarios. The study compare economics, technics and emissions metrics to achieve net-zero while ensuring resilience and energy security under realistic constraints of the power system. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Bridging criticality assessment and supply chain resilience: a structured framework for operationalizing mitigation actions
Abstract: Critical raw materials underpin the energy transition, defense, and digitalization, yet criticality assessments remain diagnostic: they quantify supply risk and vulnerability without prescribing how to act. This gap is addressed through a structured review, from which 139 mitigation actions across mechanisms, capability types, and disruption pathway categories were compiled, harmonized, and classified. Title: Community participation intensity on asynchronous biodiversity and human well-being responses to ecological restoration in global drylands
Abstract: Ecological restoration serves as a key strategy for addressing desertification and ecosystem degradation in global drylands. However, achieving synergistic benefits for both biodiversity and human well-being remains a significant challenge for sustainability. Although community participation is increasingly promoted, quantitative evidence remains limited on how participation intensity is associated with measured ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. A dataset encompassing 744 effect sizes from 41 independent studies across global drylands was constructed to conduct a meta-analysis. The synthesis indicated positive benefits relative to degraded baselines, while composite biodiversity and composite human well-being showed asynchronous responses across community participation intensity. For composite biodiversity, the pooled mean estimate corresponded to an average increase of 122.11% relative to degraded baselines. Limited community participation was associated with long-term positive patterns in the composite biodiversity (159.35%) and composite human well-being (130.71%), whereas extensive community participation showed an evidence-limited and marginally supported positive tendency in composite human well-being in the short term. Title: Mapping the evolution of communication research in aquatic conservation: A systematic literature review of emerging patterns and research opportunities (2015–2025)
Abstract: This review examines the development of communication research in aquatic conservation through a systematic literature review. Although communication is increasingly recognized as crucial for environmental governance, promoting aquatic conservation remains underexplored and often treated instrumentally. Using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, this review analyzed eleven articles (n = 11) published between 2015 and 2025, drawn from Scopus and Web of Science databases. Findings indicate that existing studies are predominantly presented in the Global North and tend to emphasize media representation, message framing, and individual behavioral change. These patterns suggest that communication is often conceptualized as a tool for disseminating information rather than as a broader social process. Most of the research described is qualitative, further strengthening the exploratory nature of the evidence. This review identifies limited engagement with systemic perspectives in understanding how communication shapes environmental responses. To address this, this study introduces Niklas Luhmann's social systems theory as an analytical lens for reinterpreting communication in aquatic conservation. From this perspective, communication is understood as a process of systemic resonance in which environmental issues are selectively interpreted across different social systems. This study contributes to the field by providing an exploratory synthesis of existing research and highlighting the need for more methodologically robust, geographically diverse, and theoretically grounded studies. The findings also underscore the importance of shifting from instrumental approaches to a more systemic understanding of environmental communication. © 2027, Malque Publishing. All rights reserved.

Title: Business interruption risk modeling framework for polymetallic nodule deep-sea mining
Abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodule (PMN) mining is emerging as a potential source of critical minerals for global energy and technology supply chains. Yet it operates under extreme environmental uncertainty and limited operational experience, exposing projects to substantial business interruption (BI) risk. This paper develops a probabilistic framework for modeling aggregate BI loss distributions in PMN mining under data-scarce conditions. To our knowledge, no existing study provides a system-level actuarial loss model that integrates causal dependency, restoration dynamics, and economic valuation. The proposed approach combines a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) with expert-elicited conditional probabilities. Results show that interruption probability ranges from 19.3% under favorable conditions to 77% under adverse regimes. Sensitivity analysis identifies several operational subsystems and managerial factors as dominant contributors to interruption probability. However, cost-based analysis indicates that the highest BI losses are driven by a smaller subset of technical components. For single interruptions, expected restoration times range from 17.6 ± 3.8 days to 52.7 ± 20.4 days. Modeling annual exposure as at most one major interruption per policy year, insurance premiums supporting system recovery range from approximately $0.9 M to $10.9 M. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and ecological determinants of cutaneous Leishmaniasis in Errachidia Province, southeastern Morocco: A 16-year municipality-level analysis with SARIMA forecasting
Abstract: Leishmaniasis is a vector-borne parasitic disease transmitted by female sandflies of the genus Phlebotomus and affects approximately 1.2 million people annually in more than 90 countries worldwide. Morocco remains one of the most affected countries in North Africa, where the disease continues to represent a major public health concern. This study aimed to analyze the spatial and temporal trends of leishmaniasis incidence across all municipalities of Errachidia Province between 2010 and 2025 and to assess the influence of ecological, demographic, and socio-economic factors on its distribution. Also, the study aimed to predict the monthly CL cases using the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) model. Epidemiological data on parasitologically confirmed cases obtained from the Errachidia Provincial Health Delegation were processed using geographic information system (GIS) tools and statistical methods to explore spatial patterns and correlations with environmental and socio-demographic variables. The models are trained and evaluated using monthly CL cases collected from 2010 to 2025, with the optimal model selected based on Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). During 16-years study period, 7034 cases were recorded in Errachidia Province, with the highest incidence reported in 2010 (860 cases per 100,000 inhabitants). Overall, the incidence showed marked temporal fluctuations but demonstrated a general decreasing trend over the study period. A pronounced spatial heterogeneity was observed between rural municipalities (Sid Ali, Melaab, and Ferkla) and urban municipalities (Errachidia, Arfoud, and Goulmima) ( p < 0.01). The disease was slightly more frequent in females (54.41%) than in males (45.59%), and a significant difference was observed among age groups ( p = 0.019), with the 0–9 and 10–19-year groups being the most affected. Seasonal analysis revealed a peak incidence during winter. In addition, higher incidence was associated with low- to medium-altitude municipalities, while no significant association was observed with poverty or vulnerability indices. The SARIMA (0,0,1)12 model demonstrated the best predictive performance. These findings highlight the heterogeneity and ecological determinants of leishmaniasis in southeastern Morocco and may support targeted surveillance and control strategies in high-risk areas. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: From Descriptive to Predictive Analytics in Healthcare Service Operations: A Strategic Analysis of AI-Driven Digital Twins for Emergency Department Capacity Management
Abstract: Many modern business processes operate under congestion: stochastic demand, shared and limited resources, complex routing, and tight service-level constraints. From healthcare and public services to logistics, financial operations, and large-scale customer support, these systems exhibit nonlinear behavior where small disruptions propagate quickly and performance deteriorates sharply. This paper examines how Business Process Management (BPM) can evolve to address congestion-driven environments by integrating process mining, queueing theory, simulation, and machine learning and artificial intelligence (ML&AI) into digital twins. We discuss how descriptive analytics must move beyond static dashboards toward data-driven process models that reveal how processes actually unfold in practice—capturing routing variability, rework loops, synchronization delays, and resource contention. Process mining provides structural visibility; queueing-aware modeling explains performance; ML&AI supports prediction under uncertainty. Building on these foundations, predictive and comparative analytics enable counterfactual “what-if” evaluation of staffing, routing, prioritization, and scheduling policies before implementation. Finally, prescriptive analytics embedded within real-time digital twins allow organizations to intervene proactively—anticipating congestion, reallocating capacity, and mitigating cascading delays. Drawing on industrial deployments through SiMLQ, we demonstrate how combining process intelligence with congestion-aware operational modeling transforms BPM from retrospective analysis into continuous, real-time decision support. The implications extend across service industries where variability and resource contention define performance, resilience, and competitiveness. Emergency departments are not failing because clinicians lack commitment; they are failing because the operating system that coordinates demand, staffing, beds, diagnostics, specialist consultation, and inpatient transfers remains largely reactive. Digital twins that are based on extensive descriptive analytics can transform fragmented event data into a safe, continuously updated environment for prediction, counterfactual evaluation, and prescriptive action. The managerial implication is blunt: modern businesses, such as hospitals that rely only on after-the-fact statistics will remain trapped in decision blind spots. Businesses that build validated digital twins would move capacity management upstream, detect failure before it occurs, and redirect scarce resources to the highest-leverage bottlenecks in real time. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Business strategy and director compensation in liberal versus coordinated markets
Abstract: In this study, we examined the association between business strategy and director compensation and whether this relationship differed between liberal market economies (LMEs) and coordinated market economies (CMEs). Using 27,309 firm-year observations from 16 countries for the 2002–2021 period, we found that differentiation was associated with higher director compensation, whereas cost leadership was associated with lower compensation. These relationships varied across institutional environments. Differentiation was positively associated with director compensation in LMEs but not in CMEs. Cost leadership was negatively associated with compensation in LMEs, but it was weakly and positively associated with compensation in CMEs. Additional analysis indicated that firms in LMEs are more likely to pursue differentiation and less likely to pursue cost leadership than firms in CMEs. The findings demonstrated that compensation arrangements are institutionally contingent and have implications for remuneration committees designing compensation policies to align with firms’ strategic orientations and national institutional environments. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: Media representations of corporate sustainability communication: German news coverage of lithium mining in Chile
Abstract: Introduction: The global shift toward e-mobility has intensified scrutiny of raw material procurement, particularly lithium mining in Chile–essential for the automotive industry. However, less is known about how German news media portray and evaluate the sustainability of lithium mining and how corporate messages by the automotive sector are represented in this debate. Methodology: This study analyzes how German news media frame the sustainability of lithium extraction in Chile, focusing on ideological differences across outlets, representations of automotive companies in news coverage, and their implications for industrial and environmental priorities surrounding the debate. A qualitative content analysis of 192 articles from five major outlets (2009-2024) reveals distinct narratives. Results: The left-leaning news outlet Zeit Online and the tabloid Bild emphasize socio-ecological consequences, while the financial newspaper Handelsblatt and liberal outlet FAZ foreground economic risks; the conservative newspaper Welt combines environmental and geopolitical concerns. Findings highlight temporal shifts whereby articles after 2020 reflect global awareness of geopolitical issues. Discussion: The findings suggest that German news coverage increasingly frames lithium mining through interconnected environmental, industrial, and geopolitical concerns, while automotive companies occupy uneven positions of visibility within these mediated sustainability debates. Conclusions: By identifying how automotive companies are represented in news coverage, the study highlights patterns that are consistent with agenda-building dynamics in the interaction between automotive companies and news media. © 2027, HISIN (History of Information Systems). Title: Component connectivity and component diagnosability of the (n,k)-star graph
Abstract: As a flexible extension derived from the classical star graph, the (n,k)-star graph Sn,k has been widely adopted to model scalable multiprocessor interconnection networks. This paper studies two reliability parameters that measure the behavior of Sn,k when the surviving graph may split into several connected blocks. We then prove the 2,3-component diagnosabilities that tc2(Sn,k)=n+k−3 when n≥5 and 3≤k≤n−2, and tc3(Sn,k)=2n+k−5 when n≥10 and 5≤k≤n−3 for both the PMC and MM∗ diagnosis models. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Synthetic Scenario Methodology (SSM): An AI-Driven Approach for Strategic Business Insights
Abstract: Data functions as a strategic business resource while simultaneously creating operational limitations in the current business world. The traditional collection process faces delays because of regulatory restrictions, high costs, privacy issues and insufficient insurance coverage for unusual yet essential occurrences. The paper presents the Synthetic Scenario Methodology (SSM) as an AI-based approach which studies synthetic datasets by applying structured artefact analysis instead of using them as brief replacements. The Business Context Blueprints (BCB) and Strategic Rules Matrices (SRM) enable SSM to produce synthetic scenarios which maintain transparency and auditability and allow for calibration adjustments. The process consists of four stages which include blueprinting followed by rules specification and then iterative generation and testing. The Human–AI Hypothetical Data Comparison Instrument (H-AI HDCI) achieves calibration through a dual approach that merges expert assessments with divergence mapping to validate findings. The worked example shows how SSM enables business risk planning through its structured outcome ranges which replace traditional single-point forecasts for leaders. The SSM method enables organizations to detect potential disruptions through assumption documentation and future scenario development which leads to shock anticipation strategy development and decision-making improvement. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Trends and directions in military professionalism research: A scopus-based bibliometric analysis
Abstract: The current bibliometric analysis examines the evolution of research related to professionalism in the military based on the Scopus database. Author contributions, country-based production, institutional engagement, and co-occurrence analysis were reported. The biblioshiny in the R language was used to examine the data, and the Garza-Reyes was utilised to ensure the validity and reliability of the data. In this case, a total of 35 relevant publications were selected to be reported in the bibliometric analysis. Based on the finding, the USA is the most contributing country and has a steady increase in the number of publications, which peaked in 2023. However, even though the USA was indicated as the country with the most publications in this research theme, the United Kingdom was found to have the most impactful and influential publication, with a total cited score of 49. In terms of the most contributive affiliation, Uniformed Services University from the USA was dominant and followed by two universities from the Netherlands namely, VU University Medical Centre and the Netherlands Defence Academy. For the most contributive authors, Cole Rebekah and Rudinsky Sherri L were identified as the most productive authors. In this case, the author production over time analysis indicates Cole Rebekah, and Rudinsky Sherri L, are the most productive and influential authors in this research theme. In the thematic map analysis, the concepts of 'human', 'military personnel', and 'humans' emerge as well-developed and central, indicating that discussions around military professionalism are strongly anchored in the human dimension of service members. It was emphasised in the co-occurrence analysis that highlights the centrality of military personnel, humans, and humans, which appear as the most frequent and interconnected terms, indicating that research on military professionalism is predominantly framed around the human dimension and the role of personnel. Finally, the current research reveals three major military professional research directions through Multiple Correspondence Analysis namely, (1) education and social identity, (2) healthcare personnel and military health, and (3) professionalism and ethics, with demographic factors serving as a transversal element across clusters. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Online multi-view streaming feature selection: A dynamic framework for real-time feature data processing
Abstract: In the era of big data, multi-source streaming data often exhibit multi-view heterogeneity and continuous feature arrival, posing a novel challenge to existing feature selection methodologies. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Online Multi-View Streaming Feature Selection (OMVSFS) method based on mutual information theory. Upon receiving new features from diverse views in each iteration, OMVSFS sequentially executes four core steps: 1) Online correlation analysis, where relevant features are identified by computing the mutual information between features and labels; 2) Intra-view online redundancy analysis, where redundant features within a single view are eliminated via a pairwise comparison strategy; 3) Cross-view online complementarity analysis, which retains discriminative features through the comprehensive consideration of feature interactions and inter-feature redundancy; 4) Online view weight update, where the view weights are dynamically adjusted based on the average discriminant scores of the selected features in each view. Extensive experiments on 16 real-world multi-view datasets, together with supplementary analyses of scalability, stability, ablation, and robustness, show that OMVSFS provides competitive results and maintains a favorable balance among classification accuracy, feature compactness, and computational efficiency. The source code of OMVSFS is publicly accessible at https://github.com/zhaocx-lc/OMVSFS. © 2026

Authors: Du C.; Liu Z.; Liu P.
Title: Blockchain adoption decisions and pricing strategies under consumer privacy concerns in competing mHealth platforms
Abstract: Blockchain technology has been increasingly promoted as a means of enhancing privacy traceability and trust in mobile health (mHealth) services. As consumer concerns about privacy grow and price competition intensifies, mHealth platforms face strategic decisions regarding whether and when to adopt blockchain-based privacy infrastructures. This study develops four duopoly game-theoretic models to analyze competing platforms’ pricing strategies and the market conditions under which blockchain is adopted to implement privacy traceability, thereby providing decision support for platforms’ strategic management. The results indicate that the decision of mobile healthcare platforms to adopt blockchain is influenced by consumer privacy concerns, platform market share, price competition intensity, and blockchain implementation costs. When the two platforms are technologically homogeneous, the platform with a larger market share is usually in a stronger position to improve traceability and charge higher service prices, whereas the smaller platform tends to focus on cost containment to preserve its low-price advantage. The timing of blockchain adoption and implementation costs critically shape market outcomes. When privacy concerns are strong and price competition is relatively weak, early adoption of blockchain technology to protect consumer privacy can enhance a platform’s competitive advantage. However, when privacy concerns are low, price competition is intense, and fixed adoption costs are high, blockchain adoption is more likely to undermine platform profitability and destabilize its market position. Moreover, market competition also creates higher technological entry barriers for late entrants. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A Novel Multi-frequency Inerter-based Resonant Seismic Metamaterials for Attenuating Vertical Shear Waves in Nonlinear Multi-layered Soils

Abstract: Seismic metamaterials effectively divert surface waves, but their use in attenuating vertically propagating shear waves is less explored. This study proposes a novel multi-frequency inerter-based resonant seismic metamaterial configuration to attenuate the waves in multi-layered soil. The seismic metamaterial designs incorporate inerters to create a broad attenuation zone at low frequencies. Both linear and nonlinear soil behaviors are investigated to compare the effectiveness of the proposed seismic metamaterial. Finite element analyses are conducted in the frequency and time domains, using the Christchurch Central Business District, New Zealand soil profile as an example. Results reveal that tuning inerter-based resonators to align with the characteristic frequencies of soils reduces the transmission of vertically propagating shear waves, protecting overlying buildings from seismic excitation. The proposed inerter-based resonant seismic metamaterial configuration demonstrates effective attenuation of acceleration amplitudes across a broad frequency range (1–5(Formula presented)Hz), with the peak ground acceleration reduced by about 40%. The proposed design, based on the natural frequencies of soils, advances the seismic metamaterials field and offers a practical approach for enhancing the seismic resilience of structures in earthquake-prone regions. Overall, this study introduces a novel multi-frequency inerter-based resonant seismic metamaterial, in which adjacent unit cells are tuned to distinct resonance frequencies to broaden attenuation band, and provides the numerical investigation under vertically propagating shear waves in a multi-layered profile, quantifying how soil nonlinearity and site frequency shifts influence resonator effectiveness. 2026 © World Scientific Publishing Company

Title: QSRR-Based RP-HPLC Method Development for Antiviral Drug Analysis: Machine Learning, Design of Experiments, and Sustainable Analytical Strategies—A Review
Abstract: Pharmaceutical quality control and research depend on the creation of effective, reliable, and sustainable analytical techniques for antiviral medication analysis. The development of conventional RP-HPLC methods frequently depends on lengthy experimental trials, which might raise the need for resources, analytical time, and solvent usage. A useful computational technique for connecting molecular structural characteristics to chromatographic retention behaviour and assisting in the advancement of predictive methods is Quantitative Structure–Retention Relationship (QSRR) modelling. The promise of QSRR-based approaches to comprehending retention processes, forecasting chromatographic behaviour, and improving chromatographic circumstances has been further increased by recent developments in machine learning (ML), chemometrics, and design of experiments (DoE). The latest developments in QSRR-based RP-HPLC method development for antiviral medication evaluation are covered in this review, with a focus on molecular descriptors, statistical and machine learning-based predictive techniques, DoE-assisted optimisation, and sustainability analytical strategies. Additionally, covered are pertinent databases, computing systems, and software tools for chromatographic optimisation, model creation, validation, and descriptor synthesis. The opportunity of combining QSRR with ML and DoE to lessen experimental workload, enhance prediction and optimisation, and support more effective chromatographic technique development is demonstrated by published works. The difficulties with data quality, descriptor selection, model interpretability, overfitting, validation, repeatability, and portability are further examined in the review. The application of QSRR in sustainable pharmaceutical evaluation could be further enhanced by explainable artificial intelligence, automated and high-throughput processes, sophisticated chemometric techniques, and green analytical principles, according to future viewpoints. All things considered, the integration of QSRR, ML, and DoE offers a viable foundation for developing RP-HPLC methods for antiviral drug analysis that are predictive, effective, and environmentally friendly. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Synergy-driven enhancement of sodium borohydride hydrolysis over a one-pot synthesized Co-Ni bimetallic MOF
Abstract: Sodium borohydride has significant potential for chemical hydrogen storage, and developing efficient catalysts to improve its hydrolytic hydrogen production is crucial for advancing practical applications. In this work, a cobalt–nickel bimetallic metal–organic framework (MOF) catalyst was synthesized using a simple, one-step solvothermal method. A high-performance bimetallic MOF catalyst (Co3Ni2-MOF) for sodium borohydride hydrolysis was created by adjusting the Co-to-Ni metal ratio. Multiple characterization techniques confirmed that the combined charge-transfer synergy and geometric effects between Co and Ni ions enhance both catalytic activity and structural stability. Performance tests showed that the hydrogen generation rate of Co3Ni2-MOF was significantly higher than that of monometallic MOFs, being 1.6 and 5.2 times higher than those of Co-MOF and Ni-MOF, respectively. Under optimized conditions, the rate increased further to 3147.7 mL·min−1·g−1, surpassing similar catalysts reported in the literature. Title: Temporal organization of negative affect shapes reciprocal feedback with psychotic-like experiences in daily life
Abstract: Background Negative affect and psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) reinforce each other in daily life, but which temporal properties of negative affect differ between individuals with PLEs and controls and shape this coupling is unknown. Methods 201 adults (99 with PLEs, 102 controls) completed 7-day experience sampling. Person-level mean negative affect, variability (SD), lability (RMSSD, MASD), and inertia were compared between groups, adjusting for mean negative affect. In participants with PLEs, lagged multilevel models tested whether these indices moderated reciprocal negative affect–PLEs associations, joint models separated amplitude from temporal dependency, and a continuous-time simulation quantified the moderation expected from persistence alone. Results Participants with PLEs showed larger fluctuations of negative affect beyond its higher mean level (adjusted d = 0.63–0.80), whereas their higher inertia depended on mean negative affect. Within participants with PLEs, only inertia moderated the lagged associations: coupling was absent at low and substantial at high inertia. Lability effects reflected its inverse relation to inertia and vanished once inertia was accounted for. Persistence alone accounted for the moderation of the PLEs-to-negative-affect effect and about half of the reverse effect, which operated through carry-over. Limitations Observational design; young, predominantly female, non-clinical sample; inertia estimated from one week with low split-half reliability. Conclusion Between persons, PLEs are associated mainly with the amplitude of negative affect fluctuations; within persons, the persistence of negative affect, not its intensity or amplitude, tracks the strength of its coupling with PLEs. Studies of affective dynamics along the psychosis continuum should therefore distinguish amplitude from persistence. © 2026 The Authors.
