Title: Adaptive reinforcement learning for medical image classification
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are widely used in medical image classification, yet their performance is often hindered by data imbalance, limited adaptability, and overfitting. This study aims to improve CNN robustness by introducing a reinforcement learning (RL) framework based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (DDPG) to automatically optimize data augmentation parameters. We propose an RL-driven optimization framework in which a DDPG agent autonomously adjusts data augmentation parameters to improve classification performance. The framework is evaluated across several benchmark datasets, including breast cancer, brain tumor, and COVID-19 X-ray images. Seven publicly available CNN architectures and a transformer model are used for comparison. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) using Grad-CAM is employed to validate model attention and prediction reliability. The proposed RL-based approach enables CNNs to rapidly identify optimal augmentation parameters, yielding superior performance compared to seven state-of-the-art CNN baselines and existing RL-integrated models. The DDPG agent demonstrates significant capability in automatically adapting augmentation strategies, consistently improving classification accuracy across medical. Grad-CAM visualizations further confirm improved feature focus and enhanced prediction consistency. The RL-driven DDPG framework effectively enhances image classification performance by autonomously optimizing augmentation parameters and improving CNN adaptability. Validation on multiple datasets and architectures—including transformers—shows that RL contributes to varying degrees of performance gains, establishing the proposed method as a promising direction for robust medical image analysis. Title: Tailoring the multiphase colloidal network of batters through controlled pre-gelatinization and oil droplets filling: Enhancement effects on quality of deep-fried battered clams
Abstract: Deep-fried battered foods are widely consumed but face significant quality challenges, primarily excessive oil uptake and the rapid loss of textural crispness during post-frying storage. In this study, effects of targeted pre-gelatinization and oil droplets filling on the rheological properties and colloidal network of batters were investigated, along with their subsequent impact on the color, texture, fat content, volatile flavor components of deep-fried battered clams. Results showed that the starch-flour-hydrocolloid (flaxseed, guar, or xanthan gum) based batters with lipid-anchored micro-domains exhibited higher apparent viscosity and viscoelastic moduli after pre-gelatinization, further enhancing the multiphase stability. The pick-up ratios of the batter in the untreated (CK) and oil-added (CKO) controls were 17.4% and 19.3%, respectively, whereas the corresponding value in the pre-gelatinized group with oil droplets filling and flaxseed gum (G-FGO) reached 72.1%. The improvement in the batters was related with the formation of dense and ordered networks filled with oil droplets, which might function as robust multifunctional barriers regulating the rapid evaporation of moisture during frying. The marked reduction in oil uptake and increasement of fracture force were observed in the sample treated with gelatinization, lipid incorporation and flaxseed gum (G-FGO group), guar gum (G-GGO group), or xanthan gum (G-XGO group), when compared to the CKO group. Furthermore, the specific flavor compounds including hexanal, nonanal, (E,E)-2,4-decadienal, E−2-undecenal, etc., in battered clams increased significantly after treatment. These findings provided us that regulating the multiphase colloidal network of batters via gelatinization and oil droplets filling offers a potential industrial application for the production of high-quality fried seafood. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Translating Strategic AI Use into Business Value in Organizations: A Qualitative Study
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly regarded as a transformative technology with the potential to unlock significant business value for organizations. However, many organizations are struggling to generate real business value from AI adoption. This study therefore investigates how organizations translate AI’s potential into meaningful business value from a strategic use perspective. We conducted a qualitative study based on 11 interviews from European companies engaged in AI initiatives. We find that AI initiation should be problem-driven rather than technology-driven, and organizations can develop AI-enabled exploitative and exploratory capabilities to gain business value. We propose a conceptual framework to structure how organizations initiate, apply, and scale AI for business value realization. This study contributes to our understanding of the mechanisms of AI value translation and offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to produce meaningful business value from AI use. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: How market volatility shapes algorithmic collusion: A comparative analysis of learning-based pricing algorithms
Abstract: The proliferation of autonomous pricing algorithms in digital markets has sparked intense debate regarding their potential to facilitate collusive outcomes, yet their behavior under realistic demand uncertainty remains underexplored. This study comprehensively analyzes four pricing algorithms-Q-Learning, Particle Swarm Optimization, Double Deep Q-Network, and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient-across three canonical duopoly market structures (Logit, Hotelling, Linear) under autoregressive demand shocks. Through profit- and price-based collusion indices, we systematically disentangle the interactive effects of algorithmic architecture, market structure, and demand uncertainty. Our findings reveal that supra-competitive pricing emerges as a joint property of algorithm-market pairings rather than algorithm class alone, with DDPG exhibiting the most pronounced collusive tendencies. Critically, none of the algorithms meaningfully adapt to unobservable persistent shocks; observed changes in collusion indices under volatility primarily reflect benchmark displacement rather than altered pricing conduct. Demand shocks produce divergent market-level responses: Logit markets experience significant performance deterioration, Hotelling markets remain resilient, and Linear markets exhibit shock-induced profit inflation without corresponding price changes. Heterogeneous competition reveals persistent asymmetries that widen under volatility. These results underscore the primacy of market structure in governing algorithmic competition under uncertainty within the calibrated settings examined in this study, and carry important implications for the regulation of autonomous pricing systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: WARP: Worktime-Aware Representation for Predictive Process Monitoring
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring leverages historical event logs to generate data-driven forecasts about the future development of ongoing process instances, such as the time until the completion of the next event. Recent research has focused on enhancing predictive performance through advanced deep-learning architectures and feature engineering. In this context, existing approaches typically model time as a continuous calendar-based feature. This design choice overlooks an important characteristic of real-world business processes: process execution is often constrained by organizational working patterns, including business hours, shift schedules, and weekends. In this paper, we investigate the integration of organizational working constraints into the predictive pipeline through a worktime-based transformation of the temporal axis. We propose a methodology that maps event timestamps from a conventional clocktime axis to a worktime-based axis, effectively excluding periods of scheduled resource unavailability. This transformation allows predictive models to learn temporal patterns based on active process execution rather than elapsed calendar time. We evaluate the approach using both synthetic and real-world event log data. The results show that the worktime-based transformation improves prediction accuracy, particularly in scenarios characterized by temporal gaps between discrete working intervals. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Perceptions of biodiversity benefits of regional food: A Q-method study from a German biosphere reserve
Abstract: Increasing consumer demand for food produced using biodiversity-friendly practices may create market incentives that support biodiversity conservation. However, there is limited understanding of consumer perspectives regarding the perceived biodiversity aspects of such products. This study represents an empirical approach to investigate how consumers perceive biodiversity-related attributes of regional products and how these perceptions influence purchase motivation in the context of the Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve. Regional product criteria related to biodiversity protection and prevalence within the Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve were assessed through a literature review. The Q-method was applied to determine their influence on consumer purchase motivation. Key findings include the determination of three prevalent consumer perspectives consisting of Traditional Regionalists valuing local community support and cultural identity, Environmental Pragmatists appreciating criteria with direct environmental protection benefits and Quality Seekers being motivated by concerns of food safety and transparency in the food industry. The regional product criteria were revisited regarding their importance for the individual consumer perspectives, providing insights into how each group relates to criteria associated with perceived biodiversity benefits. Title: Enhancing Business Performance Through Balanced Scorecard and Lean Management

Abstract: The increasing competitive pressure in global markets requires organizations to strengthen their planning and control mechanisms. The research resulted in the proposal of an integrated framework that combines the four perspectives of the BSC with Lean principles, oriented toward value creation, waste elimination, and continuous improvement. Title: Wind farm resilience to tornado strikes: A coupled probabilistic damage and system dynamics framework
Abstract: This study develops a coupled probabilistic damage and system dynamics framework for quantifying wind farm resilience to tornado strikes. The loss of resilience, defined as the time-integrated performance deficit, serves as the primary metric, complemented by four shape descriptors (robustness, redundancy, resourcefulness, rapidity) characterizing system performance under disturbance, with and without adaptation measures. Monte Carlo simulations on template wind farms yield mean losses of 62 ± 15 and 116 ± 18 days for EF1 and EF2 tornadoes. The framework is extended to model suboptimal turbine performance from undetected damage, coupling a stochastic capacity factor with a detection-time model, and to evaluate repowering of collapsed turbines with higher-capacity units. Comprehensive inspections reduce mean recovery time by one week and halve its variability relative to expedited inspections; repowering at a 1.3 capacity ratio reduces L by 7%. A regional-scale application to the Roscoe Wind Farm uses real turbine coordinates and Texas tornado climatology, yielding return periods near 45 and 57 years for EF1 and EF2 strikes and a 100-year resilience loss of 524 turbine ⋅ days. The resulting quantitative resilience value provides an additional decision-making criterion for inspection prioritization, spare parts logistics, and long-term risk management. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Perceived business value of digital freight platforms: Evidence from small and medium-sized enterprises in Poland

Abstract: Purpose: This study examines how SMEs operating in the Polish transport, shipping and logistics (TSL) sector perceive the business value of digital freight exchanges, and how they associate platform use with operational efficiency, empty vehicle movements, transport resource utilization and competitive positioning. The study investigates whether the functionalities offered by digital freight platforms constitute distinct value dimensions or a single integrated platform value dimension. Methodology: Empirical data were collected in 2025 through a questionnaire survey of 65 purposively selected Polish SMEs actively using digital freight exchanges. The sample is therefore not representative of the broader Polish SME road-freight population. The analysis included descriptive and reliability statistics, Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) (Principal Axis Factoring), Spearman's correlation, multiple linear regression, and Kruskal–Wallis tests with Dunn–Bonferroni post hoc comparisons. Factor stability was assessed using bootstrap analysis. Findings: Respondents primarily used digital freight exchanges to obtain transport orders, improve fleet utilization, monitor shipments and maintain operational continuity during periods of lower demand. The most valued functionalities were contractor credibility assessment, freight search, fleet utilization, transaction security and responsiveness to demand fluctuations. Exploratory Factor Analysis identified a provisional one-factor solution explaining 50.67% of the total variance, interpreted as a Perceived Integrated Platform Value dimension, and suggesting that these SMEs evaluate platform functionalities as complementary elements of an integrated business-support system, because the items measure perceived importance. This dimension is interpreted as a proxy for perceived platform value rather than as a measure of realized benefits rather than as separate capabilities. Perceived platform value was positively associated with competitive advantage (ρ = 0.411, p < 0.001). While overall platform value did not differ significantly by enterprise size, micro-enterprises reported greater competitive benefits and more frequent platform use than medium-sized enterprises. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Xu W.; Li Y.
Title: CGMR-DSR: Cross-graph multi-relational dynamic social recommendation
Abstract: Classical recommendation approaches, including matrix factorization and conventional graph-based social recommendation models, mainly rely on historical user-item interactions or a single social-link view. As a result, they often fail to jointly exploit interaction and social graphs, combine direct social links with behavior-derived similarity links, and capture the temporal evolution of user preferences. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CGMR-DSR, a cross-graph multi-relational dynamic social recommendation model. The main contributions are threefold. First, CGMR-DSR models two complementary social relation types and employs basis decomposition-enhanced R-GCN to learn relation-aware social representations with controlled parameter complexity. Second, it performs direct bidirectional feature exchange between shared user nodes in the interaction and social graphs, followed by user-item graph propagation that transfers the social-enhanced user signals to items. Third, it integrates LSTM-based temporal modeling and adaptive alignment loss to capture dynamic preference evolution and suppress noisy social influence. Experiments on seven benchmark datasets evaluate the competitiveness of CGMR-DSR against representative and recent baselines on HR@10 and NDCG@10, together with ablation analyses of its major components. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Towards embodied AI in manufacturing: Review, Evaluation, and Future directions
Abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence (AI), which integrates perception, decision-making, and execution through interaction with the physical world, has recently emerged as a promising paradigm for enabling autonomous and adaptive manufacturing systems. While AI has been extensively explored in various manufacturing tasks, the major body of work remains fragmented across different processes, model paradigms, and task stages, lacking a unified basis for assessing how far current technologies have actually progressed towards system-level manufacturing intelligence. To address this gap, this paper introduces a task-oriented analytical framework grounded in the Perception, Decision–making, Execution (P-D-E) loop, which provides a common structure for systematically organizing, comparing, and evaluating AI contributions across heterogeneous manufacturing domains. Four representative processes including additive manufacturing (AM), machining, welding, and assembly are examined to map how AI technologies participate in each stage of the manufacturing task cycle. A six-dimensional evaluation criterion covering autonomy, adaptability, objective alignment, domain expertise, physical interaction, and industrial readiness is further proposed to assess the embodied AI readiness of each domain. The cross-process analysis yields several findings that go beyond individual process descriptions: the primary bottleneck towards embodied manufacturing intelligence is not the absence of capable models but the fragmentation of existing AI functions into isolated task-specific subloops; perception and reasoning capabilities have matured considerably faster than safe, reliable physical intervention; and different processes require fundamentally different embodiment pathways shaped by their physical coupling characteristics and deployment conditions. Based on these findings, the paper argues that near-term progress should follow a hierarchical and modular embodiment strategy, consider the problem from a task requirement-driven perspective, and establish standardized workflows and shared platforms to enable scalable, interoperable, and reproducible manufacturing AI systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Plant-wide modeling and techno-economic analysis for producing bio-coal briquettes, biochar, and building materials by using biomass and coal refuse

Title: Poverty mapping: Data, models and applications
Abstract: Poverty mapping is increasingly important for monitoring Sustainable Development Goal 1 (SDG 1) of the United Nations 2030 Agenda, which aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere. Yet timely and fine-resolution poverty estimation remains difficult because conventional census- and survey-based approaches are costly, infrequent, and often sparse precisely where deprivation is most severe. As poverty emerges from complex socioeconomic systems shaped by human mobility, social interactions, infrastructure, and economic activities, emerging computational methods and nontraditional data sources have created new opportunities for poverty estimation and mapping. At the intersection of statistical physics, complex systems science, and data science, these approaches enable poverty estimation at finer spatial and temporal resolutions. This review summarizes the main concepts of poverty and the principal frameworks used to measure it, and examines recent advances in poverty estimation and mapping using satellite imagery, mobile phone data, social media data, and multisource data fusion. Title: Large language models in model-driven engineering: a systematic mapping study
Abstract: The application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) has emerged as a rapidly evolving research area. While existing systematic literature reviews have examined specific technical approaches, a comprehensive mapping of the broader research landscape (e.g., development trends) remains lacking. This study presents a systematic mapping study of LLM applications in MDE, analyzing 86 primary studies collected from five databases, covering publications from 2022 to early 2026. Guided by five research questions, we characterize the field across five dimensions: MDE task distribution and research contribution types, LLM technologies and interaction strategies, artifact representation and processing, validation practices, and publication landscape. Our findings reveal that current LLM4MDE research is heavily concentrated on Model Generation, while tasks such as Model Migration, DSL Engineering, and Metamodeling remain marginal. Most approaches rely on black-box OpenAI models accessed via remote APIs and adapted through prompt engineering, with fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation rarely employed. Inputs are predominantly natural-language artifacts, while outputs are model-oriented but usually expressed in lightweight textual formats rather than native MDE exchange formats. Validation is centered on quantitative experimentation, with 42% of studies reporting no baseline and cost efficiency reported in fewer than one quarter of studies. The field has grown rapidly, from one paper in 2022 to 42 in 2025, with research concentrated in Europe and Canada and limited industry involvement. Based on these findings, we identify gaps and opportunities across task coverage, technical configuration, and evaluation practice, offering a knowledge map to guide future work in this cross-disciplinary field. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: The Economic Value of Animals Traded for Traditional Medicine in Ghana and Its Effect on Biodiversity Conservation
Abstract: The trade and use of wildlife for traditional medicine are widespread in many developing countries and continue to expand. The increasing demand for high-value, endangered animals used in traditional medicine has raised important conservation concerns. In this first nationwide cross-sectional study of its kind in Ghana, we assessed the economic value of wildlife traded for traditional medicine through interviews with 133 vendors in 48 markets and examined its implications for biodiversity conservation. The mean annual sales per vendor were estimated at USD 15,123.6. Based on an estimated 1,074 vendors engaged in the trade of Animal-Based Medicine (ABM) nationwide, the annual economic value of the sector was approximately USD 16.2 million. We found that the vendors' sex, age and religious affiliation were not statistically associated with their annual trade values. However, vendors whose clientele consisted predominantly of females recorded significantly higher annual sales than those serving predominantly male clients (USD 247,852.8 vs. 59,765.6; p-value = 0.004). The most expensive animal parts included endangered species such as lion (Panthera leo), tiger (P. tigris), African savanna elephant (Loxodonta africana), and Home’s hinge-back tortoise (Kinixys homeana). Our findings showed that the ABM trade in Ghana provides employment and income for many actors along the supply chain, and contributes millions of dollars annually to the national economy. These findings highlight the need for stakeholders and policymakers to strengthen collaboration in regulating the harvest and trade of wildlife used in traditional medicine to promote both sustainable livelihoods and biodiversity conservation in Ghana and across sub-Saharan Africa. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Circular economy transition pathways for AI adoption in Indian municipal waste management: Scenario-based forecasts to 2050
Abstract: Indian urban local bodies generate approximately 62 million tonnes of municipal solid waste annually, with collection coverage near 75 percent and scientific processing below 30 percent (CPCB, 2023). The Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 and the Extended Producer Responsibility regime for plastic packaging impose binding obligations on ULBs and registered producers, while capability and infrastructure gaps constrain implementation. AI applications in route optimization, vision-based sorting at material recovery facilities, IoT-enabled containerization, and dealer-network digital platforms offer compliance pathways whose value is conditional on organizational capability, stakeholder legitimacy, and secondary-market depth. This study develops scenario-based forecasts to 2050 by operationalizing four theoretical frames, the circular economy framework, diffusion of innovation, the resource-based view, and stakeholder theory, into a hybrid simulation model with parameters calibrated through systematic review of 147 studies, of which 28 represent Indian or South-Asian contexts. Analysis of 100 simulated municipalities across four scenarios generates conditional projections of recycling rates, material recovery, and circularity outcomes against SWM Rules 2016 benchmarks and SDG 11.6 indicators. Under Capability-First assumptions, model outputs indicate 68 percent conditional probability of meeting the 2035 processing benchmark against 34 percent under Baseline assumptions. Technology-Led scenarios achieve 60 percent adoption by 2035 with 52 percent recycling rate, reflecting the model's capability-moderation specification. Sensitivity analysis identifies 2026 to 2029 as a decision window where capability investment timing alters simulated trajectories. Findings offer conditional roadmaps for ULB administrators, state governments, producer-responsibility organizations, and technology vendors operating in the Indian MSWM ecosystem, subject to empirical validation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Estimating the direct impact of mega sport events on domestic tourism demand: A micro-level approach using Paris 2024
Abstract: Research on mega sport events and tourism demand has largely overlooked domestic tourism and relied on aggregated data that mask individual behavioural adjustments. Using Paris 2024 as a case study, we propose a methodology to estimate the direct impact of mega sport events on domestic tourism at the individual level. A retrospective paired-sample survey is used to construct a two-period panel dataset (2023–2024). Individuals are classified as positively affected, negatively affected, or unaffected using self-reported motivations validated by counterfactual behaviour absent the event to mitigate ex-post rationalisation bias. Tourism demand remains unchanged based on the full sample due to offsetting behavioural responses: travel versus stay-at-home attraction among positively affected, and substitution versus crowding-out among negatively affected. However, focusing on actual travellers, affected individuals exhibit a larger increase in overnight stays than unaffected residents, without increasing visit frequency. Micro-level approaches are critical to capture how mega events reshape tourism demand. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Decision-Making Within a Leasing Business Model: Enabling Refurbishment of Products at the End-of-Lease Under Stochastics Condition
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Leasing is one approach towards a circular business strategy to enable the transition to CE. At the end of a lease, products are either purchased by the customer or returned to an OEM to be refurbished and resold to a new customer. Leasing contracts outline the rights, conditions, and responsibilities of both the customers and the OEM, including return or purchase conditions and penalties. However, defining these terms poses a challenge to OEMs especially under stochastic conditions. These challenges arise because the customers’ decisions influence the decision of an OEM and vice versa. Furthermore, different decision paths lead the OEM to adopt different refurbishment strategies. To enhance circularity, the life cycle of returned products can be extended through R-strategies such as refurbishment. This study develops a stochastic Stackelberg game-theoretic model in which an OEM acts as the leader and customers as followers. The game evaluates the interplay between initial pricing, leasing revenue, customer segmentation, and residual value. The findings demonstrate that customers’ decisions to return products are driven by the OEM’s upfront pricing decisions. Additionally, the study identifies a parabolic relationship between leasing revenue and NPV. Finally, results reveal that the optimal refurbishment strategy is dynamic: in-house operations are economically justified for high-value products that can amortize fixed costs. These insights provide actionable guidelines to balance secondary market supply, ensuring the long-term profitability of leasing and refurbishment in support of circularity. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Comparing AI chatbot users and non-users in Germany: Reasons for use, addictive AI chatbot use, mental health, and loneliness
Abstract: The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots is becoming increasingly popular worldwide. To prevent potential negative consequences associated with the use at an early stage, it is crucial to understand its associations with mental health. Therefore, the present study compared people who use AI chatbots with those who do not engage in AI chatbot-interactions in terms of mental health and loneliness. Moreover, we investigated potential mechanisms associated with addictive AI chatbot use. Data of 7,312 persons (3,729 users: 42.1% men, 57.9% women; Mage = 42.23, SDage = 13.33; 3,583 non-users: 42.6% men, 57.4% women; Mage, = 54.28, SDage = 14.49) from the German adult population were collected via an online survey. AI chatbot users had significantly higher levels of loneliness, depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms, and significantly lower levels of life satisfaction than non-users. Users primarily engaged in AI chatbot-interactions for informational and practical reasons, such as obtaining information and inspiration, and receiving text-related assistance. The frequency of AI chatbot use to escape negative emotions was significantly positively associated with addictive tendencies. Loneliness statistically mediated the association between addictive AI chatbot use and the mental health variables. Most observed effect sizes were small. The present findings show that using AI chatbots for emotion regulation is positively associated with higher addictive tendencies and lower levels of mental health. Further experimental longitudinal research is urgently needed to clarify causal mechanisms of these associations. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Mechanistic insights into KOH activation temperature for enhanced electrochemical performance of ammonolysis-pretreated lignite-derived carbon
Abstract: Lignite is an abundant and low-cost carbon precursor for sustainable energy storage, yet its direct carbonization yields materials with limited porosity and electrochemical activity. In this work, a two-step strategy combining ammonolysis pretreatment with temperature-controlled KOH activation was proposed to convert lignite into high-performance electrode materials, focusing on the mechanistic role of activation temperature. The results demonstrated that the activation temperature critically modulates the hierarchical pore architecture, nitrogen configuration, defect density, and graphitic ordering. At lower temperatures (400–500 °C), KOH predominantly reacts with oxygen-containing functional groups, generating micropores while preserving abundant heteroatoms and defects, which contribute to pronounced pseudocapacitance. In contrast, higher temperatures (600–900 °C) promote metallic potassium intercalation and carbon skeleton etching, facilitating the formation of a hierarchical porous network alongside enhanced graphitization, thereby favoring electric double-layer capacitance. Optimal performance is achieved at 500 °C, which features a well-balanced hierarchical pore structure, obvious carbon detects, and high nitrogen and oxygen content (1.6 and 30.6 at. %) enriched in electrochemically active pyridinic-N and pyrrolic-N. Consequently, KCSPN‑5 delivers a high specific capacitance of 320.4F/g at 0.5 A/g in a three‑electrode system, with excellent rate capability (61.4 % at 100 A/g) and outstanding cycling stability (93.1 % after 10,000 cycles). Kinetic analysis reveals a mixed charge storage mechanism with a b‑value of 0.742, confirming the synergistic contributions of surface‑controlled pseudocapacitance and diffusion‑controlled processes. This work establishes a rational temperature-guided activation protocol for upgrading lignite into high-value carbons and provides fundamental insights into the temperature-dependent interplay among porosity, defects, and heteroatom doping. Title: FlightLLM: few-shot interval forecasting for airline passenger and baggage demand
Source title: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
Abstract: Airline demand forecasting for passengers and baggage is critical for resource and service planning. As airline networks move toward higher density and complexity, travel patterns vary widely across routes, and historical demand is hard to share or transfer. At the same time, frequent route launches, seasonal shifts, and schedule changes create many cold-start routes with scarce data, posing significant challenges for forecasting. Under few-shot conditions, previous forecasting methods lack sufficient accuracy and stability, and deep learning models are uninterpretable and fail to incorporate aviation business rules or quantify uncertainty. To address these challenges, this study proposes FlightLLM, an LLM-driven two-phase framework for few-shot airline demand interval forecasting that integrates business-feasibility constraints and business-related priors into the learning and adaptation process. The offline phase generates high-quality pseudo-labels using a five-stage search guided by process reward modeling, followed by curriculum-based self-training and meta-learning to build a generalized initializer. In the online phase, the model rapidly adapts to cold-start routes using minimal real-world samples. It produces joint passenger and baggage forecasts in an interpretable “point estimate ± interval half-width” format. The proposed method introduces a new way for few-shot demand forecasting by leveraging large language models to unify data-driven generalization and rule-constrained generation, where business-feasibility constraints and business-related priors are embedded into interval prediction via meta-initialization and reliability-aware adaptation. Empirical evaluations on real cold-start route data show that FlightLLM achieves a substantially more favorable coverage–width trade-off than conventional interval baselines while maintaining competitive point-forecasting accuracy, underscoring the insight that effective few-shot demand forecasting requires the complementary strengths of empirical adaptability and operational consistency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Temporal trends across diagnostic subgroups of Dutch ICU patients over a decade; a nationwide cohort study
Abstract: Background The demand for intensive care in the Netherlands is influenced by evolving treatments, external factors such as pandemics, and policy decisions. Concerns have grown about Intensive Care Units (ICU) capacity, nurse shortages, and changing patient populations. Understanding temporal trends in ICU admissions and case-mix is essential for resource allocation and preparedness. Methods This descriptive study analyzed data from 2014 to 2023 from the National Intensive Care Evaluation registry. Patients were categorized using predefined diagnostic categories and age subgroups, alongside data-driven patient clusters identified through latent class analysis. Trends were analyzed in annual ICU admissions and average daily number of concurrent ICU patients. Results A total of 640,465 ICU admissions from 59 Dutch hospitals were included. Between 2014 and 2023, ICU admissions decreased by 15%. This decline was not linear: a modest downward trend before the pandemic followed by a more pronounced reduction during the pandemic period. The largest decrease was observed among patients aged ≥80 years (40%). In contrast, admissions for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest increased by 13%. Differing trends across diagnostic subgroups drove shifts in ICU case-mix, with an increasing relative contribution of younger and less severely ill patients, reflecting a changing ICU population. Conclusion Changes in ICU case-mix occurred alongside declining admissions and occupancy between 2014 and 2023. These temporal patterns likely reflect both an underlying secular decline and additional pandemic-related effects. Ongoing monitoring of ICU population dynamics is essential for guiding capacity planning, optimizing workforce allocation, and strengthening preparedness for future public health challenges. Title: LLM-Based Orchestration of Business Process Management Toolchains
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: There is a tradition in business process management research not only to develop theoretical concepts and powerful algorithms, but also to engineer research prototypes to showcase the contributions. These tools are typically developed in isolation and are rarely designed to interoperate. As a result, researchers and practitioners need to manually combine multiple tools to construct toolchains that address their specific needs, limiting the practical usability and reuse of existing prototypes. In this paper, we propose the PRAXIS (Process Research Artifact eXecution and Integration System) framework that leverages large language models as a natural language interface for practitioners to compose and execute process management toolchains. For a specific user question, the system automatically orchestrates and executes the respective BPM research tools. The framework is prototypically implemented based on state-of-the-art techniques to integrate several existing BPM research tools. We provide an evaluation methodology that generates test cases for a given set of tools to test the framework. Title: Divergent relationships between moral disengagement and cyberbullying bystander response behaviors: Examining the amplifying roles of humor and anonymity
Abstract: While bystander response behaviors are pivotal for cyberbullying (CB) intervention, prior research has yielded inconsistent findings regarding their correlates, partly because it has often treated diverse bystander responses as a monolithic construct and failed to distinguish constructive defense from aggressive defense. Furthermore, few empirical studies have examined how digital affordances interact with individual factors in relation to diverse bystander responses within a Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) framework. To address these gaps, this study examined the main and interactive associations of individual moral disengagement (MD), perceived anonymity, and humor of CB with four distinct online bystander responses (constructive defense, aggressive defense, inaction, and reinforcement). A final analytic sample of 1201 Chinese secondary school students, selected via multi-stage random sampling, completed a survey assessing MD, CB contexts, and real online bystander responses. Multilevel analysis indicated that MD, perceived anonymity and humor were consistently and negatively associated with constructive defense but positively associated with inaction. Conversely, MD and anonymity were positively associated with aggressive defense, whereas humor showed no significant link. Regarding reinforcement behaviors, perceived anonymity and humor were positive predictors, whereas MD exerted a non-significant association. Moderation analyses revealed that anonymity strengthened MD's positive associations with inaction and reinforcement, whereas humor amplified MD's association solely with reinforcement. These findings underscore the necessity of distinguishing constructive from aggressive defense and integrating individual moral cognition with contextual cues for both exploring correlates of online bystander response and designing CB interventions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Enhancing situational awareness in health systems: A scoping review of technologies and cross-industry insights
Abstract: Background: Situational awareness technologies are increasingly utilised in healthcare systems to facilitate timely and coordinated decision-making. Reported implementation considerations include data quality, governance, and integration into everyday workflows. Objective: This scoping review aimed to map technologies, systems, and methods used to enhance situational awareness in health service delivery and to identify approaches used in other industries that could be adapted for healthcare, particularly in regional and remote settings. Methods: We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance for scoping reviews. Electronic databases (PubMed and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between January 2000 and October 2025. Reference lists and citation searches in Google Scholar were also examined. Records meeting the inclusion criteria were screened and reviewed, with key data extracted using a structured charting form and synthesised into seven application domains. Results: Searches identified 744 records, of which 23 studies were included. These covered diverse technologies such as dashboards, forecasting models, alert systems, and geospatial decision environments. Most studies were from high-income countries (n = 19). Studies reported potential benefits for visibility, coordination, and decision-making. However, most evidence was descriptive, with limited evidence of whether these systems improve service delivery. Recurrent implementation challenges included data fragmentation, limited interoperability, and misalignment between governance and workflow. Conclusions: This review highlights the need for more rigorous and context-sensitive evaluations of technologies used to enhance situational awareness in healthcare, especially in regional and resource-limited settings. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

Title: Wearable, Display-less AI as Extended Reality in Business Education
Abstract: Wearable artificial intelligence technologies are emerging as a new class of extended reality (XR) interfaces that operate without traditional visual displays. Devices such as Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses, first-generation consumer release, combine first-person audiovisual capture, voice-based AI interaction, and real-time access to information. This short paper reports an exploratory, faculty-led technology-probe study examining how AI-enabled wearable glasses might be integrated into business administration curricula. Structured experimentation and reflective analysis were used to identify pedagogical affordances (e.g., first-person feedback for presentations, documentation of experiential activities, and instructor ‘hands-free’ access to contextual information) and to surface ethical risks (privacy, consent, and academic integrity). Title: Coordination-state regulation of aqueous negolytes: electronic structure, degradation, and high-voltage flow-battery performance
Abstract: Aqueous redox flow batteries are promising for long-duration energy storage, but their cell voltage is limited by the instability of highly reducing species in water. This review establishes a coordination-chemistry framework for low-potential aqueous negolytes, focusing on strong-field hexacyanometallates, multidentate metal chelates, and polyoxometalate-based clusters. The key premise is that negolyte performance depends not on formal potential alone, but on a reversible coordination trajectory that preserves solubility, kinetic accessibility, and chemical integrity throughout cycling and ageing. Ligand-field strength, spin state, Jahn–Teller distortion, denticity, coordinated water, free-ligand activity, protonation, counterion association, and membrane transport are therefore considered as coupled design variables. Chromium and manganese hexacyanides demonstrate how strong-field ligation stabilizes low-valent states and enables multielectron storage, whereas Fe–DTPA/Ce–DTPA and Fe(TPEN) systems highlight the roles of chelation, shared-ligand design, and ligand-exchange resistance. Polyoxometalates further show how proton-coupled electron transfer, reversible structural adaptation, and solvent-network regulation can expand the practical aqueous voltage window while maintaining low-temperature conductivity. Operando spectroscopy, electrochemical mass spectrometry, and molecular simulation are critically assessed as tools for resolving coordination-state evolution and degradation. Finally, evidence-based design principles and standardized reporting criteria are proposed to guide the development of durable, high-voltage aqueous negolytes. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Molecular background of elicitor-induced crop protection: A translational agronomic review
Abstract: Crop production is increasingly challenged by interacting biotic and abiotic stresses, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives to conventional crop protection. Plant defense elicitors have emerged as promising tools for enhancing crop resilience by activating inducible resistance and immune priming. This review provides a critical translational overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying systemic acquired resistance (SAR), induced systemic resistance (ISR), and priming, while evaluating their practical relevance for agriculture. Beyond summarizing current knowledge, we assess the variability, reproducibility, and field performance of major elicitor classes, emphasizing the influence of crop genotype, environmental conditions, microbiome composition, formulation, and management practices on their effectiveness. Commercial and near-commercial elicitors are critically compared according to their biological mechanisms, agronomic validation, and practical limitations. To facilitate objective evaluation of elicitor technologies, we propose an evidence-based translational framework incorporating standardized evidence descriptors, the Overall Evidence Index, the Normalized Translation Index (NTI), the Translation Gap Index (TGI), and a practical decision framework for elicitor deployment. Rather than focusing solely on molecular mechanisms, this review emphasizes the translation of plant immunity research into reliable crop protection strategies. Future progress will depend on standardized field validation, improved formulations, microbiome-informed approaches, and integration with precision agriculture and integrated pest management to maximize the agronomic potential of elicitor-based technologies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Pyrolysis of biomass feedstocks for hydrogen-enriched syngas production: Cold gas efficiency modelling, latin hypercube uncertainty analysis, and parametric stress analysis
Abstract: Biomass-derived syngas offers a viable pathway for producing renewable, hydrogen-rich fuel gas. However, its conversion performance is influenced by feedstock type, temperature, feed rate, and moisture content. This study develops a Cold Gas Efficiency (CGE) model for four agricultural feedstocks: wheat, barley, oilseed rape, and beans. Temperature-dependent regression correlations are developed for the main syngas components and gas flow rate using experimental data. Results show that CGE is highly sensitive to temperature, with low-temperature stress (0–5th percentile) reducing mean CGE by up to 22%. High-moisture stress (95–100th percentile) produced an even larger decline, lowering mean CGE from ∼44% to ∼35% for wheat and compressing the distribution into a low-performance regime. Regression-based tornado charts indicate that temperature is the strongest linear driver (coefficient = +0.44), while Spearman rank correlations highlight feed rate as the most monotonic negative driver (−0.41). Feedstock probability density functions (PDFs) show that wheat as the most efficient and least variable performer, while Oilseed Rape (OSR) and beans exhibited broader distributions due to higher ash-related inhibition of char reactivity. The thermochemical and statistical results demonstrate that operational uncertainty, such as temperature and moisture, dominates CGE variability. Title: Grain refinement mechanism of ultrasonic application stage in wire arc additive manufacturing of alloy steel
Abstract: Ultrasound-assisted wire arc additive manufacturing (UA-WAAM) offers a promising route to refine the coarse columnar grains found in as-deposited components. However, the effects of ultrasound applied at different stages during the rapid solidification of the molten pool remain insufficiently understood, and the grain refinement mechanism requires clarification. A novel stage–specific ultrasonic application strategy was designed based on the phase transformation temperatures and thermal history of molten pool. Five discrete ultrasound intervention stages were investigated, before arc extinction, at arc extinction, during solidification, after solidification and continuous application. Microstructural evolution was characterized using optical microscopy and EBSD, while the cavitation dynamics and mechanical response of columnar grains were theoretically modeled to establish a quantitative fragmentation criterion. Results reveal that effective grain refinement occurs exclusively when ultrasound is applied during cooling and solidification stage, transforming coarse columnar grains into fine equiaxed and refined columnar grains. Ultrasound applied before arc extinction or after complete solidification produces negligible microstructural modification due to the absence of surviving nuclei or a liquid medium. Theoretical analysis reveals cavitation-induced grain fragmentation as a key mechanism, with predicted critical fragmentation lengths (15.3–25.8 μm) aligning quantitatively with the measured mean grain size (20.9 ± 3.7 μm). Acoustic streaming plays a supporting role by dispersing fragments as heterogeneous nucleation sites. The critical window for effective ultrasonic application is limited to the sub‑second interval from arc extinction to complete solidification. These findings establish a quantitative relationship between cavitation shock wave pressure and grain fragmentation behavior, providing a scientific foundation for optimizing energy-efficient ultrasonic strategies in WAAM. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Advances in material design and applications of electronic skins: From human body to embodied intelligent robots
Abstract: Embodied intelligence is driving a transition from mechanically reactive robots to systems capable of adaptive and autonomous interaction. Electronic skin (e-skin) plays a central role in this shift by enabling high-resolution tactile perception, multimodal environmental sensing, and safe human-robot collaboration. Here, the material foundations and structural design strategies that underpin next-generation e-skin technologies have been systematically reviewed. Specifically, it discusses the advances in toughness, fatigue resistance, self-healing property, biocompatibility, biodegradability, and soft stretchable conductors, together with multiscale architectures such as micro-structured interfaces, porous and layered networks, microneedle-based designs, reconfigurable topologies, and integrated circuits used in e-skins. It also highlights representative applications in tactile sensing, exercise rehabilitation, and physiological monitoring, and outlines emerging directions toward closed-loop systems that couple sensing, computation, and decision-making for embodied intelligent robots. Title: HReMatch: HVI enhancement and robust refinement for semi-dense feature matching
Abstract: Reliable feature matching is crucial for SLAM and 3D reconstruction, yet it often fails under extreme illumination changes and geometric ambiguity, leading to unstable correspondences. Title: Enterprise Information Exchange via IE-BSE Framework: A Case Study on E-invoicing

Abstract: Digitalization has enabled enterprises to adopt API-centric business services to manage complex business operations. Title: Mobile internet connectivity and household wealth in the Philippines
Abstract: Mobile internet has become a fundamental modern infrastructure. We consider how access influences household wealth in the Philippines using a granular measure of local connectivity based on geocoded cell towers and identify causal impact through an instrument based on proximity to submarine cable landing points. Our results show that mobile internet connectivity increases household wealth, with effects across education levels and most pronounced in urban areas. We investigate potential mechanisms and find that improved connectivity stimulates activity in key economic sectors, improves educational outcomes, and increases female labor force participation, primarily in occasional work. Given the context of the Philippines as a major migrant-sending country, we conduct a complementary event study which suggests that tower rollout may facilitate international labor migration and increase remittance flows to origin households. © 2026 The Authors

Title: To show or not to show? how human vs. digital entrepreneur streamers shape brand attitudes through trust mechanisms
Abstract: Live streaming is reshaping business development, with entrepreneur live streaming emerging as a prominent trend. Despite the growing impact of digital human entrepreneurs, the effects of varying live streamer types on consumer outcomes remain underexplored. This study investigates how entrepreneur live streamer typologies (Real human vs. Digital human) and influence levels (High vs. Low) interact to affect brand attitudes. Grounded in non-evaluative meaning transfer theory and the ELM, we identify distinct mechanisms through which different streamer characteristics enhance brand attitudes. Analyzing 7,631 social media comments and conducting two situational experimental studies (N = 1004), we provide empirical support for our hypotheses. The results indicate that high-influence real-human entrepreneurs boost brand appeal by fostering affective trust, while low-influence digital entrepreneurs enhance communication effectiveness by strengthening cognitive trust. Title: Discount replenishment opportunities with limited capacity: Optimal policy and pricing dynamics
Abstract: We study an inventory model with occasional discounts on the fixed order cost, where a random capacity constraint limits the quantity ordered at the discount. We prove that the optimal policy resembles a can-order policy, characterized by a unique reorder, can-order, and order-up-to level. However, the random capacity constraints on the discount offers add complexity: the optimal policy features additional thresholds for inventory levels between the reorder and can-order point that determine when to use the discount. As these inventory-specific thresholds may render the optimal policy less straightforward to implement, we develop three heuristic replenishment policies inspired by the optimal policy structure. We compare their performance in a numerical study and derive an analytical bound on their worst-case optimality gaps in settings with an infinitely high backlog cost rate. With the buyer's optimal response to capacitated discounts in mind, we investigate the supplier's decision to set the discount price. A high discount relative to the regular order cost increases the probability that the buyer will accept the offer, but erodes the supplier's margin on discount sales and may reduce regular sales. We show that a mutually beneficial outcome requires buyer-to-supplier compensation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Bound tightening guided ABB with transformer assisted search reordering for exact P-graph optimization of complex process systems
Abstract: P-graph provides a graph-theoretic representation and structure-generation algorithms for process network synthesis and material scheduling, and the Accelerated Branch-and-Bound (ABB) algorithm guarantees solution exactness through the maximal structure, decision mapping, and feasibility-based pruning. However, with increasing operating-unit scale, multiple alternative material pathways, and additional constraints, conventional branching orders may incur substantial inefficient node visits. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a Bound tightening guided ABB with transformer assisted search reordering(BTG-ABB) framework, which encodes material nodes, operating-unit nodes, search states, and bound information in the P-graph as a unified structured sequence. Rather than eliminating candidate branches, BTG-ABB advances high-scoring branches in the visiting order, enabling earlier upper-bound tightening and facilitating the subsequent pruning of low-value branches by the original ABB rules. Experimental results show that BTG-ABB reduces the number of nodes visited in the Top-10 exact search in Case 1 by approximately 18.51%. In the ethylene feedstock scheduling case, the Top-1 hit rate is improved to 77.5%, and Top-3 to Top-10 all reach 100%. BTG-ABB provides an interpretable basis for intelligent branching strategies in the synthesis of complex process systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: An interpretable uncertainty-aware intelligent framework based on generalized multi-scale formal contexts and Bayesian deep neural networks
Abstract: Modeling uncertainty and interpretability remains challenging in intelligent systems, particularly where complex decision boundaries and ambiguous feature-label relationships coexist. Although Bayesian deep neural networks (BDNNs) offer principled uncertainty quantification, they are constrained by limited prior knowledge, feature redundancy, and opacity. We propose the generalized multi-scale formal context BDNN (Λ-BDNN), an interpretable and uncertainty-aware framework. Λ-BDNN integrates formal concept analysis with Bayesian deep learning. It constructs multi-scale contexts containing conditional and decision attributes to explicitly represent information granularity while preserving semantic structures. Mutual information quantifies attribute interdependencies to enable effective feature selection and reduce redundancy. Furthermore, non-redundant decision rules are derived to filter samples and improve data quality. To enhance robustness, Bayesian optimization is employed to establish a surrogate probabilistic model for automatic hyperparameter configuration. The optimized BDNN subsequently performs intelligent classification under uncertainty-aware constraints. Experimental results on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms ten representative methods. Additionally, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used for feature analysis; the strong consistency between SHAP and mutual information-based selection further validates the framework's interpretability, effectiveness, and applicability. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Advancing AI Integration: Exploring Business Process Management Capabilities for AI-Driven Processes

Abstract: The increased integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into business processes challenges established business process management (BPM) assumptions. Title: AI failures in the eyes of the downstream developer: a first look at concerns, practices, and challenges
Abstract: With the advancement of AI models, more software systems are adopting AI as a component to facilitate automation. Pre-trained models (PTMs) have become a cornerstone of AI-based software, allowing for rapid integration and development with lower training cost. However, their adoption also introduces failure modes such as data leakage and biased outputs, that may require careful handling by downstream developers. While previous research has proposed taxonomies of these technical concerns and various mitigation strategies, how downstream developers address these issues during the development of general AI-based software when reusing PTMs remains unexplored. Understanding downstream developers’ perspectives is essential because they directly influence how these potential failure concerns translate into practice, such as determining whether immediate risks like data leakage or model bias are recognised, mitigated, or inadvertently overlooked in real-world deployments. This study investigates downstream developers’ concerns, practices and perceived challenges regarding practical AI failures during the development of AI-based software. To achieve this, we conducted a mixed-method study, including interviews with 16 participants, a survey of 86 practitioners, and an analysis of 874 AI incidents from the AI Incident Database. Our results reveal that while developers generally demonstrate strong awareness of potential AI failures, their practices, especially during the preparation and model selection phases, are often inadequate. The lack of concrete guidelines and policies leads to significant variability in the comprehensiveness of their approaches throughout the development lifecycle, with additional challenges such as poor documentation and knowledge gaps, further impeding effective implementation. Based on our findings, we offer suggestions for AI model contributors, developers of AI-based software, researchers, and policy makers to enhance the integration of failure mitigation measures aimed at mitigating direct harms from AI failures. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: A diagnostic framework for auditing decision logic in transformer-based portfolio allocation
Abstract: Robust portfolio management requires risk-adjusted performance and auditable decision logic under changing market conditions. This paper examines Decision Transformer policies for sequential portfolio allocation and proposes a diagnostic protocol organized around contribution, necessity, and representation structure. It combines feature attribution, temporal occlusion, controlled perturbations, latent-representation analysis, and regime-conditioned portfolio behaviour.The study covers eighteen trained model families differing in lookback horizon, training rebalancing frequency, information set, trajectory objective, and inference-time conditioning. Each family has 96 correlated ex post evaluation variants applied without retraining. Diagnostic definitions, aggregation rules, thresholds, performance bands, and original recommendations were frozen before temporal-holdout inspection; a benchmark-relative economic-admissibility gate is reported separately as a post-hoc amendment. A secondary comparison with DDPG, DQN, and PPO assesses technical portability within the same setting.Complete-family screening indicates that performance and diagnostic evidence capture distinct properties. Across seventeen families with complete records, the frozen aggregate score has a moderately positive but uncertain association with holdout Sharpe. Retrospective higher- versus lower-Sharpe comparisons reveal differences in volatility-sensitive feature use, temporal dependence, regime-conditioned allocation, and latent organization, without establishing deterministic performance rules.Explanation-validity evidence is heterogeneous and method dependent. Feature-family rankings are more stable in magnitude than sign; parameter randomization, deletion, insertion, and input permutation support action dependence only for subsets of policies. Notably, benchmark outperformance during validation does not imply uniformly supported explanations. The protocol therefore supports staged model comparison and controlled validation, not future-return prediction, causal certification of explanations, or deployment authorization. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Water rights allocation in water-receiving districts of the central line project of the south-to-north water diversion, China: a hybrid multi-criteria decision framework
Abstract: Water competition in the Water-Receiving Districts (WRDs) of the Central Line Project of the South-to-North Water Diversion (CLP-SNWD) has intensified, highlighting the urgent need for a new water rights (WR) allocation scheme. This study proposes a hybrid multi-criteria decision framework that integrates triangular fuzzy numbers (TrFNs) to improve linguistic-to-numerical conversion, with expert weights to distinguish heterogeneous expertise. In addition, time weights are introduced to capture the dynamic impacts of regional development on WR allocation. Finally, the MARCOS method is employed using data from 2010 to 2022 to generate allocation results. The findings show that: (1) the new scheme prioritizes strategic cities such as Beijing, Tianjin, Zhengzhou, and Shijiazhuang, while assigning fewer WR to cities such as Pingdingshan, Hebi, Nanyang, Zhoukou, Luohe, and Hengshui; (2) compared to the current plan, the new allocation decreases WR for Beijing and Tianjin, while increasing those for Henan Province, thereby better reflecting the practical needs and improving acceptance across regions; (3) by incorporating the principle of government macro-control, the new framework balances the needs of both strategic and economically disadvantaged areas, enhancing fairness and feasibility. Overall, the proposed framework contributes to methodological innovation by combining fuzzy logic, expert systems, and time-sensitive weighting, and provides practical insights for conflict mitigation and sustainable water resources management in large-scale inter-basin diversion projects. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Authors: Pang B.; Huang L.; Feng X.; Wei W.
Title: COLF: Disentangled forecasting for non-stationary time series via contrastive learning
Abstract: Non-stationary time series are widely prevalent in real world, characterized by changing temporal patterns, which greatly challenges the out-of-distribution generalization ability of forecasting approaches. Most existing approaches seek to achieve sequence stationarization through normalization methods, whose effectiveness is still limited since non-stationarity is not simply reflected in shift in mean and variance. Given this, we consider addressing non-stationarity from another perspective by pattern disentanglement, i.e., to distinguish between stable and unstable patterns according to temporal persistence and utilize them separately for forecasting. Considering the lack of supervised signals for disentanglement as temporal persistence is challenging to measure explicitly, we achieve this in a self-supervised manner and propose a model COLF. Specifically, COLF is designed with two contrastive learning mechanisms at different levels: the across-sample contrastive learning to disentangle stable and unstable patterns at sequence level, and the within-sample contrastive learning to further extract persistent components from unstable patterns under the local smoothness assumption at subsequence level. The final forecasted result is obtained by integrating the predictions derived from both stable patterns and the persistent components within unstable patterns. COLF is evaluated on six real-world datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that COLF achieves overall superior performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches across different forecasting horizons and evaluation metrics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: SemanticSync-BI: A Framework for Multi-cloud Business Intelligence Metadata Harmonization
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Organizations increasingly adopt multi-cloud solutions for Business Intelligence (BI), benefiting from enhanced scalability, flexibility, and cost efficiency. Yet this trend introduces complex metadata management challenges, especially when maintaining semantic consistency across heterogeneous platforms. Current approaches, including technical catalogs, ontological standards, and cloud-native governance tools, face important limitations. These solutions often emphasize structural aspects, lack flexibility, or require extensive manual configuration, which restricts their capacity to adapt to changing business contexts. We present SemanticSync-BI to address these constraints, a conceptual framework for semantic harmonization of BI metadata in multi-cloud environments. Our framework operates through three integrated layers. First, the Context Extractor derives business meaning from diverse metadata sources. Second, Dynamic Mapping builds adaptive semantic similarity graphs. Third, the Multi-Cloud Synchronizer maintains semantic alignment in real time. Through conceptual evaluation using representative scenarios such as migration, enterprise merger, and SaaS integration, SemanticSync-BI shows promise for reducing inconsistencies, accelerating harmonization, and enhancing inter-cloud BI coherence. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: BenchPDM: Benchmarking pattern detection methods in microservice-based systems using automatically generated pattern-assisted testbeds
Abstract: Microservices architecture (MSA) is an increasingly popular trend in software architecture design. While the use of microservices offers numerous benefits, such as enhanced flexibility and scalability, it also introduces specific challenges and complexities. To address these challenges, various design patterns have been applied in system implementations, each aimed at resolving specific issues within microservices-based systems (MBS). Understanding the design patterns employed in a large software system can significantly enhance comprehension of the system’s functionality. However, organizations often lack strong documentation regarding the types of patterns used, the number of patterns, and their locations within the system. To date, various pattern detection methods (PDMs) have been developed with the goal of identifying design patterns within software systems. The effectiveness of these PDMs may vary depending on factors such as the scale of the software system, the types of patterns used, and etc. Therefore, the selection of an appropriate PDM is highly dependent on the specific software system being targeted. Consequently, there is a critical need for a tool that can evaluate and compare PDMs from various perspectives. Although several benchmarks have been proposed for MBSs, none have focused on assessing PDM. In this article, we present a benchmark named BenchPDM aimed at benchmarking PDMs in MBS using automatically generated pattern-assisted test beds. To achieve this, BenchPDM includes two fundamental modules. In the PBMC module, pattern-assisted microservices-based systems (PAMBS) are generated with varying degrees of complexity to simulate real-world MBSs of small, medium, and large scales. The PDM-ES module then evaluates and compares the performance of PDMs using the generated PAMBS from different factors. To assess the performance of BenchPDM, we conducted experiments on five PDM methods, two of which are among the most popular and commonly adopted approaches, SVM-based and graph-based methods. The experimental results demonstrated that BenchPDM can effectively evaluate and compare PDMs across various factors. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: An agent based model to support secondary critical materials markets development
Abstract: The development of Secondary Materials Markets (SMMs) is a promising approach to diversify and strengthen critical materials supply chains. SMMs involve the recovery of valuable materials from discarded products and reintroduce valuable materials into the economy through cooperative business partnerships. This research addresses the need for analytical tools, which can enable SMM stakeholders to evaluate potential outcomes under various operating conditions and make informed decisions regarding SMM participation and development. A novel agent based model, integrated with existing techno-economic analysis and lifecycle assessment metrics, is developed to quantitatively evaluate the feasibility and impacts of SMMs for enabling secondary critical material feedstocks. Multiple interdependent factors are considered simultaneously, including techno-economic developments, demand uncertainty, inconsistent used product management scenarios, and changing stakeholder business strategies and interactions. The model’s analytical capabilities are demonstrated using a hypothetical-realistic photovoltaic (PV) waste management case study. Under the baseline tested conditions, the model estimated recovery of approximately 72 % of regional PV waste providing secondary materials to meet the demands of co-located manufacturing firms. For example, approximately 45 % of the aluminum demand was met via recovered materials leading to 23 million USD (approximate) in savings for the partner firm buying recovered aluminum under baseline tested conditions. In this manner, this research lays the foundation for analytical tool development to support decisions related to critical material recovery through SMMs. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Shen T.; Yang Y.; Zou Y.; Zhang X.; Zhang Z.; Dong W.; Wang W.; Zhai X.; Li X.; Huang X.; Shi J.; Zou X.
Title: Advances in enrichment pretreatment for enhanced laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy detection of trace heavy metals
Source title: Spectrochimica Acta - Part B Atomic Spectroscopy
Abstract: Heavy metal contamination is a global challenge driven by industrialization and human activities. Conventional detection methods, while accurate, are hindered by high costs, labor demands, and limited speed, restricting large-scale use. Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS), with its rapid, multi-element capability and minimal sample preparation, offers a promising alternative. When coupled with enrichment pretreatment strategies, LIBS achieves improved sensitivity and reduced matrix interference. This review summarizes recent applications of LIBS for heavy metal detection in soils, water, food, and agricultural products, highlighting the limitations of direct analysis. Enrichment approaches such as electrochemical methods, ion exchange, membrane separation, and adsorption are discussed in terms of their underlying mechanisms and effectiveness. Recent advances integrating these strategies with LIBS for trace heavy metal analysis are critically evaluated, alongside challenges of sensitivity, reproducibility, and field applicability. Future directions include developing advanced enrichment materials (e.g., covalent and metal-organic frameworks), integrating with enhanced LIBS platforms, and applying artificial intelligence (AI)-driven data analysis. This review provides perspectives to guide LIBS toward reliable and efficient monitoring of trace heavy metals in environmental systems. This review aims to present a broad overview to support the continued development of LIBS as an efficient and versatile tool for trace heavy metal monitoring in evironmental and food matrices. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Author full names: Vinci, Francesco (58835802000); de Leoni, Massimiliano (22937181700)
Title: Bridging Accuracy and Interpretability in Business Process Simulation via Knowledge Distillation
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Business Process Simulation (BPS) is widely used to analyze and optimize processes in a controlled environment. Recent advances integrate AI models to improve the simulation accuracy of process perspectives such as control-flow and time. However, BPS-based improvement requires testing alternative what-if analyses. This can only be achieved through white-box models, where analysts can inspect and modify the underlying decision logic. Purely black-box models, although often highly accurate, lack transparency and limit configurability. However, traditional white-box models (e.g. decision trees) provide explicit and interpretable rules but may struggle to capture complex dependencies, leading to lower predictive accuracy, hampering the BPS realism. This paper proposes a distillation-based approach to bridge the gap between predictive accuracy and interpretability in BPS. We first train black-box predictive models (referred to as teacher models) to learn complex temporal and behavioral patterns from event logs. We then extract the knowledge captured by the teacher models and transfer it into probabilistic decision trees, obtaining interpretable surrogate white-box models (referred to as student models). The distilled models approximate the learned behavior of the teacher while offering a white-box representation and maintaining competitive predictive performance. Experimental results in four case studies, using four alternative teacher models, demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. The findings show that distillation is able to improve the accuracy of simulation models, compared to standard decision trees without distillation, while maintaining interpretability and supporting reliable what-if analyses. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: What do cross-lingual clone detectors really learn? A protocol and semantic counterfactual study
Abstract: Cross-lingual code clone detection aims to identify functionally equivalent code fragments written in different programming languages. Existing detectors often achieve high F1 scores on standard benchmarks, but these scores may be inflated by code or problem overlap and shallow lexical or structural cues. It is therefore unclear whether the detectors compare the semantics of two code fragments or exploit regularities in benchmark construction. To investigate this issue, we conduct a behavioral audit of six representative clone detectors on Java-to-X pairs from Project CodeNet. The audit combines protocols with increasingly strong isolation controls, shortcut controls, partner shuffling, and meaning-preserving and behavior-changing edits. Our results show that measured performance depends strongly on the evaluation protocol. GraphCodeBERT and UniXcoder fall from F1 scores of 0.9848 and 0.9916 under pair-random evaluation to 0.6588 and 0.6970 under problem-disjoint evaluation. Shallow Control achieves an F1 of 0.6889, showing that even problem-disjoint splits retain exploitable non-semantic cues. Partner shuffling further reveals that detectors differ in their reliance on the original cross-lingual pairing. Semantic counterfactuals show that GraphCodeBERT is stable under meaning-preserving edits but insensitive to behavioral changes, while DeepSeek-v4-flash exhibits the reverse pattern. No evaluated detector achieved both high preservation stability and high breaking rejection on this counterfactual set. Thus, neither high F1 nor clean splitting alone demonstrates cross-lingual semantic understanding. Evaluations should also test shortcut reliance, use of both code snippets, and responses to semantics-preserving and semantics-breaking edits. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
