Authors: Li L.; Wang X.; Liu S.; Liang X.; Wang H.; Cheng L.
Title: Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Profiles of NAT Gene Family in Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) and Their Potential Roles during Stolon-to-Tuber Development
Abstract: N-terminal acetyltransferases (NATs) catalyze protein N-terminal acetylation, which is crucial for plant growth, development, stress responses, and metabolic regulation. This study identified 40 StNAT members (StNAT1-StNAT40) in potato. Most were predicted to be hydrophilic cytoplasmic proteins, whereas only StNAT10 and StNAT36 were hydrophobic proteins localized to chloroplast and cytoplasm, respectively, suggesting possible functional divergence. Tandem repeats appeared to play a dominant role in StNAT family expansion. StNAT promoters contained cis-elements associated with hormone response, growth and development, circadian regulation, stress response, and transcriptional regulation. Based on conserved motif and gene structure, the 40 StNATs were divided into three subgroups. Within each subgroup, motif composition and distribution were relatively consistent, whereas significant differences were observed among subgroups. Ten representatives of StNATs were selected from the three subgroups for qRT-PCR analysis. The results showed that the representatives of subgroup I were ubiquitously expressed in various tissues, whereas all the representatives of subgroup II and III exhibited high expression in tubers and stolons, suggesting possible involvement in stolon-to-tuber development. Among these members, the majority exhibited a “V”-shaped expression pattern during stolon-to-tuber transition, peaking at stolon initiation and swelling stages but declining at stolon elongation stage. Some members showed stage-specific high expression at stolon initiation stage (StNAT22 and StNAT32) or swelling stage (StNAT4). Additionally, most members were induced by low GA₃ in stolons, whereas StNAT38 was down-regulated and StNAT2/29 were up-regulated with increasing GA₃, suggesting possible roles in GA-mediated stolon-to-tuber development. These findings suggested that StNATs might play important roles in stolon-to-tuber development, warranting further functional verification. This study provides new insights into the genetic improvement of potato tuber yield and quality. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to European Association for Potato Research 2026.

Title: Energy service companies as transition intermediaries: Functions, business models, and prospects for demand-side decarbonization
Abstract: Energy service companies (ESCOs) are established delivery vehicles for energy efficiency, but the literature remains fragmented across contract studies, country surveys, financing analyses and emerging digital-service research. This fragmentation leaves a specific knowledge gap: how ESCOs combine technical, financial, contractual, data and institutional functions to act as transition intermediaries, and under what conditions those functions generate additional, persistent and scalable demand-side decarbonization. This structured narrative review synthesizes 129 peer-reviewed and institutional sources published mainly between 2010 and 2026. It develops a transition-intermediary framework, compares contractual and organizational models, proposes a common quantitative performance scorecard, and links ESCO market development to policy, finance, technology, risk allocation and client capability. The evidence indicates that ESCO projects reported average energy savings of about 25% in 2024, while U.S. federal projects delivered reported cost savings equal to 101.0% of estimates and 108.5% of guarantees. These benchmarks demonstrate performance potential but do not support a universal ranking of shared savings, guaranteed savings, Super ESCO and energy-as-a-service models because contract choice is endogenous to client credit, technology mix, project depth and market maturity. The review further shows that ESCO opportunities extend to electrification, distributed energy resources, storage, demand response, flexibility, digital twins, artificial intelligence and carbon MRV. However, transaction costs, baseline disputes, shallow-retrofit incentives, long-term lock-in, data dependence and exclusion of less creditworthy clients can weaken outcomes. We conclude that ESCOs should be evaluated as institutional infrastructure for demand-side implementation rather than as a narrow retrofit industry. A future agenda is organized into five macro-areas and nine linked priorities spanning evidence, market design, contracts, digitalization, system integration and justice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Proactive vs reactive destination revitalisation

Title: AI-Enhanced Data-Driven Approach to Model the Mechanical Behavior of Sustainable Geopolymer Concrete
Source title: Journal of Structural Design and Construction Practice
Abstract: The growing environmental burden of ordinary portland cement has accelerated the search for sustainable alternatives. Geopolymer concrete (GPC), synthesized from industrial byproducts such as fly ash and slag, is a promising candidate. However, its compressive strength is difficult to predict because numerous mix and curing variables interact in complex, nonlinear ways. This study develops and validates an interpretable machine learning framework for forecasting GPC compressive strength. A curated data set of 350 samples was used, containing eight independent variables, i.e., fly ash, ground granulated blast-furnace slag, NaOH molarity, coarse aggregate, recycled aggregate, curing temperature, curing time, and age of testing, and one dependent variable, i.e., compressive strength. Six models (linear regression, decision tree, gradient boosting, support vector regression, artificial neural networks, and random forest) were trained and optimized. Their outputs were integrated into a stacking ensemble, i.e., the super learner (SL) model, with random forest as the metalearner. Performance was evaluated using R2, root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) under 10-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set. The SL achieved R2 = 0.994, RMSE = 0.90 MPa, and MAPE = 1.4 %, consistently outperforming all base learners and surpassing results reported in recent studies when benchmarked under comparable variable ranges. Model interpretability was ensured through Shapley Additive exPlanations and permutation sensitivity analyses, which identified curing time, NaOH concentration, test age, and curing temperature as dominant predictors. The novelty of this work lies in demonstrating that a stacking ensemble with transparent feature attribution can markedly improve accuracy and trustworthiness in predicting GPC strength, offering a rapid and nondestructive tool for sustainable mix design optimization. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

Title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Human-Centered Pedagogies in the Business Management Curriculum of State Universities and Colleges (SUCs)
Abstract: This study analyzed the role of AI in the curriculum of Philippine State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) business management through a qualitative Delphi approach. Academics specializing in curriculum, education, and AI responded to three rounds of Delphi surveys to achieve a commonality in integrating AI. Title: Auditable multimodal decision support for ordinal real estate price-band classification: Source-aware and leakage-controlled fusion
Abstract: Residential decision-support systems increasingly combine structured property attributes, listing descriptions, and photographs. With small labeled samples, however, an additional representation may duplicate its source rather than add reproducible signal. This study presents a source-aware, leakage-controlled framework for five-class ordinal classification of posted asking-price bands. Structured attributes (N), native listing text (L), photo-derived caption text (C), and frozen verified-photo features (P) are evaluated separately, while C and P are recognized as representations of the same visual source. The final analysis set contains 422 unique address–photo entities. Ten-fold entity/image-safe outer validation prevents related cases from crossing the train–test boundary, and stream-model and fusion-weight selection are confined to three-fold inner splits. Structured attributes achieved 0.666 accuracy and 0.894 quadratic weighted kappa (QWK). Photo-derived caption text was the weakest individual stream, with 0.329 accuracy and 0.439 QWK. The caption-excluded N+L+P configuration produced the best multimodal point estimates, with 0.680 accuracy and 0.892 QWK, whereas the complete N+L+C+P diagnostic configuration attained 0.664 and 0.889, respectively. The complete diagnostic configuration showed no statistically detectable advantage over the predefined controls after Holm adjustment, and fixed XGBoost produced the highest overall point estimates, with 0.697 accuracy and 0.906 QWK. Global-band performance degraded sharply in held-out markets, identifying a clear need for local recalibration and revalidation. Integrated CPU inference beginning with a model-ready listing record and an archived background-removed photograph averaged 12.96 s per listing; the preceding third-party background-removal operation was outside the measured interval. The framework therefore provides an auditable basis for evidence-based representation selection: it separates representation format from source lineage, identifies redundant streams, preserves traceable uncertainty and case-level decision paths, and exposes conditions that require deferral or external revalidation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Hydrogen-to-Ammonia Green Fuel Production via Haber–Bosch Process in a Solar–Wind Poly-Generation System: Design, Intelligent Optimization, and 4E Analysis
Abstract: Hydrogen offers a pathway to deep decarbonization; however, its storage and transport remain significant barriers for large-scale renewable energy systems. This study proposes a novel hybrid solar-wind poly-generation architecture that couples a two-level thermal cascading structure (supercritical CO2 Brayton and transcritical CO2 Rankine cycles) with a continuously operated water electrolyzer–Haber–Bosch ammonia loop, enabling stable renewable-to-hydrogen-to-ammonia conversion without auxiliary heating. This framework provides a high-density and safe long-term energy storage solution. A comprehensive 3E analysis, operational CO2 emission avoidance assessment, and multi-objective optimization were performed using an ANN-based surrogate method coupled with the NSGA-II algorithm. Exergy and economic analyses identified the solar field as the main source of irreversibility and cost, contributing to 48% and 60.1%, respectively. The surrogate-based optimization reduced computational time by 97.63% relative to direct simulation (≈38 hours to 54 minutes) while maintaining accuracy. Under optimized operating conditions (solar field area of 5624.32 m2, compressor pressure ratio of 1.93, solar irradiance of 411.29 W/m2, wind speed of 7.98 m/s, and regenerator effectiveness of 0.86), the system achieved an exergy efficiency of 35.86%, ammonia production of 1.09 kg/h, and a payback period of 5.07 years under the adopted economic assumptions. The environmental assessment indicates 167.5 kg/h of CO2 emissions avoided, corresponding to an emission reduction cost of 4.02 $/h. A Dubai-based case study demonstrated conceptual feasibility under steady-state conditions. The results highlight the system’s theoretical potential as an advanced renewable-to-ammonia platform for high-density energy storage and multi-product output, subject to further dynamic validation and detailed engineering. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Mesoporous nanoreactor with accelerated ion transport for high-performance SnO2-based anodes in sodium-ion batteries
Source title: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
Abstract: Tin dioxide (SnO2) is a promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries owing to its high theoretical capacity, yet its practical application is severely hindered by drastic volume expansion and intrinsically sluggish Na+ diffusion kinetics. Herein, we report a mesoporous yolk–shell SnO2-based nanoreactor (SnO2 mCNR) constructed via a facile interfacial polymerization assembly and selective etching strategy. The architecture features a SnO2 nanocube core, an internal void space, and a mesoporous carbon shell permeated with interconnected channels (∼7 nm). This unique design simultaneously accommodates the large volume changes during sodiation/desodiation and provides low-resistance pathways for rapid Na+ transport. Compared with its non-porous counterpart (SnO2 CNR), SnO2 mCNR exhibits a ∼ 3.5-fold higher Na+ diffusion coefficient and a transition toward pseudocapacitive-dominated charge storage (b-value of 0.90). Consequently, SnO2 mCNR delivers a high reversible capacity of 650.3 mAh g−1 at 0.05 A g−1, excellent rate capability (218.7 mAh g−1 at 5 A g−1), and outstanding cycling stability with 95.1% capacity retention over 1800 cycles at 1 A g−1. A full pouch cell assembled with a Na3V2(PO4)3-based cathode achieves a high energy density of 292.2 Wh kg−1, indicating promising application potential at the electrode-material level. This work establishes shell porosity engineering as a generalizable design principle for high-performance conversion/alloying-type anodes in sodium-ion batteries. © 2026

Title: Turán extremal graphs vs. signless Laplacian spectral Turán extremal graphs
Abstract: Let F be a graph with chromatic number χ(F)=r+1. Denote by ex(n,F) and Ex(n,F) the Turán number and the set of all extremal graphs for F, respectively. Title: Personality engineering with AI agents: A new methodology for negotiation research
Abstract: According to canonical negotiation theory, people's success in a negotiation depends on how well they balance competing demands—empathizing and asserting, demonstrating concern for other and concern for self, being soft on the people and hard on the problem. Yet people struggle to manage these tensions, so researchers have lacked the ability to rigorously test the field's prescriptions under controlled conditions. AI agents do not face the same limitations, and their precision, repertoire, consistency, and scalability enable a new class of experiments to contribute to negotiation theory. In this article, we introduce personality engineering—a methodology that precisely parameterizes the personas of AI agents based on established personality frameworks—and propose how this method can be used to study the traits and behaviors of negotiators. Given its relevance to negotiation theory, we propose the interpersonal circumplex—and its two core dimensions of warmth and dominance—as a foundational coordinate system for the field. This approach offers both a rigorous methodology for testing classic negotiation theories and a practical guide for designing the personas of AI negotiation agents. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Deng K.; Wu S.; Diao H.; Dong K.; Zhao X.; Zhang B.; Liu X.; Su Y.
Title: Contrasting responses of above- and belowground multifunctionality to increasing soil salinealkaline conditions in a semi-arid grassland in Northern China
Abstract: Salinealkaline conditions in soils represent a critical environmental stressor that threatens the sustainability of semi-arid grassland ecosystems. However, a systematic understanding how salinization affects ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF), particularly the coupled above- and belowground responses, is currently lacking. This study investigated a semi-arid salinealkaline grassland using 37 quadrats along a natural salinealkaline gradient spanning low, moderate, and high salinealkaline levels. By measuring key indicators of plant community biomass, dominant species, and soil nutrient content, we quantified the aboveground multifunctionality (AGMF) and belowground (soil chemical) multifunctionality (BGMF) as component indices of EMF. Along the gradient, EMF showed no significant overall difference, resulting from offsetting asymmetric responses of AGMF and BGMF. AGMF exhibited a unimodal pattern, driven by dominant species functional traits such as Ca²⁺ accumulation, whereas BGMF declined linearly with increasing pH and salinity, mainly due to reductions in soil organic carbon and suppression of the available nitrogen (NH₄⁺-N) pool. Soil pH acted as a bidirectional regulator, indirectly promoting AGMF by increasing dominant species Ca²⁺ content while directly inhibiting BGMF by decreasing soil NH₄⁺-N. Salinity exerted direct or indirect negative associations with both AGMF and BGMF. Although EMF did not differ significantly along the gradient, it showed a declining trend with increasing pH, suggesting that the sustained negative effects on belowground functions may dominate the long-term trajectory of ecosystem multifunctionality. This study emphasizes that coordinated above- and belowground strategies should be adopted in the management and restoration of semi-arid salinealkaline grasslands. The physiological characteristics of salt-tolerant dominant species can support aboveground productivity in the short term, but maintaining soil organic carbon pools and belowground ecological processes must be regarded as the core goal in curbing habitat degradation and achieving sustainable restoration. By systematically revealing the asymmetric response mechanisms of AGMF and BGMF, this study provides a scientific basis for shifting restoration practices from single vegetation targets to integrated plantsoil system strategies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Life cycle–informed process optimization of microwave-activated biochar from agri-residual biomass for sustainable wastewater treatment
Abstract: The growing generation of food and agro-industrial waste, coupled with rising pressures from climate change, resource depletion, and carbon emissions, has intensified the demand for sustainable engineering solutions aligned with circular bioeconomy principles. However, the environmental implications of waste-derived functional materials and their underlying production processes remain insufficiently assessed, creating a critical gap in understanding their overall sustainability. In this study, brewers’ spent grain (BSG), a major by-product of the brewing industry, was converted into activated biochar through microwave-assisted phosphoric acid (H3PO4) activation and evaluated as an adsorbent for wastewater treatment, integrating experimental process optimization with a cradle-to-gate life-cycle-based sustainability assessment. The highest adsorption capacities of 46.9 mg/g for CV and 49.5 mg/g for Or-II occurred under the most intensive activation conditions tested, but life cycle assessment (LCA) showed that such conditions were not environmentally optimal: the production phase overwhelmingly dominates environmental impacts, and the associated low biochar yield increased energy and chemical demands, whereas the application phase contributes minimally. In contrast, milder activation conditions substantially reduced life-cycle impacts while maintaining effective adsorption performance (34.3 mg/g for CV and 45.1 mg/g for Or-II). These findings demonstrate that technical and environmental optimality do not necessarily coincide, and highlight the need for life-cycle-informed optimization to balance adsorption performance with resource efficiency and environmental sustainability in waste-derived biochar systems. © 2026 The Authors. Title: M2VGF: A memory-augmented multi-view gated fusion framework for multimodal sarcasm detection
Abstract: With the rapid growth of social media content, multimodal sarcasm detection has become an important task for understanding complex cross-modal semantics. Multimodal sarcasm often involves subtle local contradictions, contextual semantics, and heterogeneous cues whose importance varies across samples. To this end, this paper proposes M2VGF, a Memory-Augmented Multi-View Gated Fusion framework. The proposed model highlights informative local contradictions through saliency-aware fine-grained alignment, enriches current representations with OCR-enhanced context and historical memory, and adaptively combines complementary semantic views through gated fusion. Experiments on the MMSD and MMSD2.0 benchmarks demonstrate that M2VGF achieves competitive and stable performance, with accuracies of 93.37% and 89.45%, and F1-scores of 93.11% and 89.36%, respectively, across five random seeds. Multi-run evaluations further demonstrate the robustness of the proposed model, while routing diagnostics show high retained-memory purity in the evaluated setting. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Machine Learning for B2B Sales Prediction: A Comparative Study

Abstract: This paper presents a framework based on Machine Learning (ML) to predict the success of Business-to-Business (B2B) commercial proposals from a multinational company. Title: Clickstream user behavior clustering using graph time series
Abstract: Introduction: Internet banking has become the primary channel for many customer interactions with financial institutions. The availability of banking services via internet banking platforms has presented new organizational challenges for financial institutions, necessitating adaptation and the creation of new strategies to enhance customer engagement on these platforms. Objective: This paper proposes a model to characterize user behavior when using an internet banking solution through time series analysis. Two specific objectives were achieved: (1) grouping customers with similar behavioral patterns associated with clickstreams (sequences of user interactions with the application) across different time series, and (2) identifying customer profiles related to the use of a specific service offered by the banking institution (checking account). Methods: A dataset with 500 million clickstream records from 2.4 million users was used. Unsupervised techniques and complex networks were employed to perform time series clustering based on the similarity of subsequences of clickstreams. Results: Users were segmented into 89 clusters that exhibited distinct behavioral profiles when using the banking services available on the institution's internet banking platform. Title: Multimodal cross-domain recommender systems using image–text fusion: A gated contrastive approach for scalable service computing
Abstract: Cross-domain recommender systems (CDRS) mitigate data sparsity and cold-start problems by transferring preference knowledge between information-rich source domains and data-scarce target domains. However, most existing CDRS methods depend exclusively on interaction signals or on a single content modality, neglecting the complementary information carried by item imagery and textual descriptions. In this paper, we propose MIT-CDRec, a multimodal cross-domain recommendation framework that (i) integrates frozen CLIP-ViT visual embeddings and BERT textual embeddings through a novel Cross-Modal Gated Fusion (CMGF) module that learns per-item modality weights; (ii) projects fused representations into a shared domain-invariant latent space via a weight-tied multilayer perceptron; and (iii) aligns cross-domain representations of overlapping users with an InfoNCE contrastive objective. We evaluate MIT-CDRec on three Amazon cross-domain benchmarks (Books↔Movies, Clothing→Sports) against eight strong baselines spanning single-domain, classical CDR, graph-based, sequential, and LLM-augmented families. Under a leave-one-out evaluation protocol with 99 sampled negatives, MIT-CDRec achieves the best results among the compared methods on every benchmark, achieving an average improvement of 8.26% in Recall@10 and 10.87% in NDCG@10 over the strongest prior baseline, with all gains statistically significant at p<0.01 across five seeds. We further provide a theoretical account of why the method transfers stably, bounding the target-domain error through an HΔH-divergence argument and showing empirically that the contrastive objective halves the cross-domain discrepancy. Beyond accuracy, we evaluate robustness to feature noise, interaction noise, and missing modalities, extend the study to multi-domain transfer, and report beyond-accuracy metrics, including diversity, novelty, coverage, and exposure fairness, on all of which MIT-CDRec improves over the strongest baseline. We further strengthen the analysis with a transfer-specific account of why per-item gating reduces cross-domain divergence, a geometric treatment of the contrastive objective, and new studies of partial/zero user overlap, encoder provenance (pretrained vs. random vs. domain-adapted), and industrial-scale caching and synchronization cost. These results show that principled multimodal fusion combined with domain-invariant contrastive alignment is a robust approach for scalable cross-domain recommender systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: The functional Choquet integral
Abstract: We introduce the notion of functional Choquet integral (FCI), a new family of fusion operators that are aggregation functions in many cases, obtained by replacing the capacity values in the discrete Choquet integral with data-dependent fusion functions applied to the ordered tail of the input vector. Unlike previous extensions, different functions are allowed at each summation term, providing additional modeling flexibility while preserving the ordered-difference structure of the Choquet integral. We provide a detailed mathematical analysis of the main structural properties of the FCI. Necessary and sufficient conditions are established for idempotency, homogeneity, monotonicity, and shift-invariance. In particular, we prove that monotonicity of the FCI is guaranteed under a double-increasing condition on the generating vector of functions, and a sufficient condition is given for comonotone additivity. These results clarify both the expressive power and the structural limitations of the proposed framework. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Creating markets for under-utilised fish species: Consumer valuation of a co-created fish finger
Abstract: It is common practice to discarded under-utilised fish species that are caught as bycatch because of their low market value. In this paper, we examine whether locally co-created and produced fish fingers, made from locally sourced under-utilised fish species are valued by consumers by employing a discrete choice experiment (DCE). A novel feature of this study is that we consider three versions of the fish finger, sourced from three UK ports: Plymouth, Lowestoft and Grimsby. Our DCE employs a novel set of attributes to capture the unique characteristics of product design and development of the fish finger. Results reveal that all attributes are positively valued, with the largest for fish that are sustainably caught. We also find that distance to the product locality does not materially affected consumer valuation. Location comparisons indicate limited differences overall for the three versions of the fish finger. These results indicate that sustainability information is a primary driver of demand for processed seafood using species with historically low market uptake, while local cues add value without substituting for sustainability. Our findings can help inform efforts to reduce discarding of under-utilised fish species that remains a significant issue in many fisheries. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Humans Shaping a Landscape - Ethnobiology, Hunting Traditions, and Wildlife Conservation of Diverse Language Communities in the Indus Kohistan, Pakistan
Abstract: Wild fauna has been hunted by humans for many purposes, including meat consumption, sport, ornamentation, and traditional medicine. Hunting, especially for meat, remains widespread across the Himalayan region, yet ethnozoological hunting practices in the Kohistan region of the Hindu Kush–Himalaya remain poorly documented. We gathered data from five linguistic communities, i.e. Shina Kohistani, Indus Kohistani, Gujjari, Pashto, and Batteri Kohistani, using semi-structured questionnaires, complemented by direct observations. Hierarchical cluster analysis and ordination techniques were used to analyze the data. The local fauna was utilized for multiple purposes, including zootherapy, food, culture, decoration, and recreation. Meat was the most frequently utilized animal part, while the most treated health conditions were sexual dysfunction, respiratory diseases, and skin diseases. Our cross-cultural analysis showed that the Gujjari, Shina Kohistani, and Indus Kohistani groups exhibited the highest similarity in fauna use (14% overlap), potentially reflecting their seasonal migration and geographic interactions. The least overlap (3%) was observed between Gujjari and Batteri groups, consistent with their limited seasonal interaction and narrower shared geographic range. The study identified six culturally associated indicator species across the five linguistic groups, highlighting taxa that may warrant attention in community-based conservation initiatives. In Shina Kohistani and Indus Kohistani, Capra falconeri and Lophophorus impejanus had significant indicator values (p ≤ 0.05) across both communities. In the Gujjari linguistic group, Capra sibirica and Moschus leucogaster were indicator species. Columba livia and Nemorhaedus goral were indicator species for the Pashto and Batteri linguistic groups, respectively. Common hunting methods included 12-bore repeater shotguns (chari), snares (kurki), pit traps (Dhoko), and netting (Jal). Most species (43%) were hunted occasionally, 30% commonly, and 27% rarely. Our study indicates that linguistic and cultural differences are associated with distinct patterns of wildlife use across the Kohistan region. With the development of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), associated socioeconomic changes may affect traditional knowledge and biocultural relationships in the region. To our knowledge, this is the first cross-cultural ethnozoological assessment of these communities and provides baseline information for conservation and sustainable-development planning, with potential relevance for protecting wild fauna, traditional knowledge, and cultural heritage. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Toward Agentic Privacy-by-Design: A Conceptual Framework for AI-Supported Process Compliance
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Privacy compliance in business processes is a regulatory obligation and a core requirement for trustworthy digital systems. Yet legal principles such as those of the EU GDPR are abstract, hard to translate into concrete process logic, and existing tools either rely on expert-curated formal rules or treat compliance as a post-hoc verification step disconnected from process design. This research introduces PRAISE, a conceptual, pattern-aware framework for AI-supported Privacy by Design in business process models, and asks how an agentic, retrieval-augmented system can identify privacy gaps and generate explainable, legally traceable improvement recommendations. The framework combines a layered privacy knowledge base built on the Data and Process Privacy Pattern Model with a hybrid retrieval-augmented reasoning pipeline; process models are translated into text, symbolically classified as fully, partially, or not covered against GDPR obligations, and refined through pattern-based recommendations under external orchestration and session-level tracing. Applied to a mobile-app registration scenario, PRAISE detects four interrelated GDPR violations and produces a redesigned BPMN model that addresses all of them in a single pass. The framework lays the architectural foundation for AI-supported, governance-aware privacy-compliant process design and outlines a three-phase evaluation roadmap toward prototype, expert validation, and comparative use. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: An innovative modified biochar derived from antibiotic mycelial dreg: Enhanced tetracycline adsorption performance and underlying mechanism
Abstract: Use of antibiotic mycelial dreg (AMD) for biochar production is an eco-friendly and cost-effective strategy to achieve the goals of hazardous waste management. However, the low adsorption capacity of pristine AMD-derived biochar limits its practical application. Thus, KMnO4-modified biochar was developed to enhance tetracycline (TC) removal from aqueous solution in this study. Various characterization experiments showed that the modification process introduced MnOx on the surface of pleuromutilin mycelial dreg (PMD) derived biochar and resulted in a higher BET surface area, well-developed pore structure, more oxygen-containing surface functional groups, and altered elemental components. Batch adsorption studies indicated that the pH of the solution had a significant impact on the adsorption of TC by pristine biochar, but had little impact on the modified biochar. TC adsorption by pristine and modified biochar was a combination of physical and chemical adsorption, but the chemical adsorption was dominant. The maximum adsorption capacity of MBC500 and MBC700 was 802.4 mg/g and 894.6 mg/g, which were 16 and 22 times larger than that of pristine biochar, respectively. TC adsorption by both pristine and modified biochar was spontaneous (ΔG < 0), endothermic (ΔH > 0), and a randomness-enhanced process (ΔS > 0). The adsorption mechanisms of pristine biochar included pore filling, π–π interaction, and charge-assisted hydrogen bond (CAHB). KMnO4 modification efficiently improved these interactions as well as increasing the complexation and redox interaction, resulting in an excellent adsorption capacity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Deepening the Conceptual Debate on Sportswashing: Institutional narratives of reputational projection of Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo on Social Media; [Profundizando en el debate conceptual sobre sportswashing: narrativas institucionales de proyección reputacional de Ruanda y la República Democrática del Congo en redes sociales]
Abstract: Introduction: In recent decades, sport has become a strategic instrument within international politics, used by states to project national image, strengthen global reputation and enhance territorial positioning. At the same time, the concept of sportswashing has gained prominence in both academic and media debates to describe the use of sport as a reputational legitimization strategy in the face of political or social criticism. However, its widespread use has generated conceptual ambiguity and confusion with other sport-related strategies such as sport diplomacy and sport place branding. Methodology: This study adopts a quantitative approach based on digital content analysis of social media, examining 684 posts published in 2025 by institutional accounts related to the territorial promotion strategies of Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Data were collected using the social media analytics tool Fanpage Karma and analyzed through three complementary dimensions: communication activity, digital engagement performance and lexical-discursive narrative analysis. Results: The findings reveal a clear asymmetry in the communication strategies of both countries. Rwanda displays a highly centralized strategy around the Visit Rwanda brand, where sport functions as a key instrument for international visibility and high levels of digital engagement. In contrast, the Democratic Republic of Congo presents a more fragmented communication strategy focused primarily on cultural and tourism promotion. Discussion: The results confirm the usefulness of the proposed political triangle of sport framework for interpreting these strategies, highlighting the predominance of sport place branding over sport diplomacy and sport for development narratives. Furthermore, the study argues that sportswashing can be understood as a critical interpretative outcome that may emerge across these strategies. Conclusions: The research contributes to clarifying the conceptual debate by proposing an integrative analytical framework that distinguishes legitimate territorial branding strategies from their potential reinterpretation as sportswashing in contexts of reputational controversy. © 2027, HISIN (History of Information Systems). Title: An adaptive real-time decision-support framework for dynamic school transportation reoptimization
Abstract: This paper addresses real-time school transportation reoptimization under evolving operational conditions. It formulates the Dynamic School Transportation Reoptimization Problem (DSTRP), which extends classical school bus routing by incorporating time-dependent travel times, rolling-horizon decisions, hard-committed route segments, configurable transportation policies, and operational modification costs.An adaptive decision-support framework, denoted ARTHGS, combines Hybrid Genetic Search and ALNS-based improvement. Two complementary strategies are evaluated: localized rolling-horizon repair (ARTHGS), which restricts reoptimization to impacted route neighborhoods, and global reconstruction (ARTHGS-GR), which reoptimizes the remaining active non-committed plan.Computational experiments cover three transportation-policy families, three instance-size categories, and five operational scenarios. Relative to No-Reopt-HGS, RH-ACS, ARTHGS, and ARTHGS-GR reduce cumulative lateness by 55.9%, 59.0%, and 68.7%, respectively. The corresponding on-time stop ratios increase from 28.06% with No-Reopt-HGS to 55.40%, 62.31%, and 64.31%. ARTHGS introduces fewer operational changes than ARTHGS-GR.Nonparametric tests, an ablation study, and RH-CPLEX validation support these findings. On tractable subproblems for which RH-CPLEX proves epoch-level optimality, ARTHGS-GR, ARTHGS, and RH-ACS obtain average local objective gaps of 0.20%, 0.85%, and 1.65%, respectively. The results show that localized repair provides greater plan stability, whereas global reconstruction achieves stronger punctuality recovery under severe or cascading disruptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: m-QIEA: A modified quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithm for feature selection in code smell detection
Abstract: Code smells, indicative of structural defects in software, signify sub-optimal design practices that impede software maintainability. Detecting and mitigating code smells is essential for improving software quality, particularly in both classical and quantum systems. However, conventional machine learning (ML) approaches for code smell detection often suffer from feature redundancy, increased computational cost, and suboptimal model performance. Feature selection (FS) plays a pivotal role in enhancing code smell detection by improving classification accuracy while reducing model complexity. This research aims to improve code smell detection by introducing an FS-driven approach that optimizes feature selection to enhance classification accuracy. The proposed approach leverages deep learning (DL) models for feature extraction, followed by a modified Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (m-QIEA) to refine the feature subset for classification. Compared with standard QIEA, m-QIEA incorporates a time-decaying rotation schedule and Gaussian mutation, which are intended to mitigate premature stagnation during the feature-selection search. Experimental evaluations are conducted on a comprehensive suite of six datasets. For classical systems, the primary MLCQ benchmark is used and further the work is extended to SmellyCode++, and a multi-language corpus (Python, Java, and C++). For quantum systems, the primary QNet benchmark is used, extended to a derived large-scale LintQ corpus, and tested on the independent Smelly Eight benchmark. Across all settings, the results demonstrate that m-QIEA achieves superior accuracy and generalization. The study establishes the critical role of FS in optimizing code smell detection accuracy. By integrating DL for feature extraction and m-QIEA for FS, the proposed approach enhances the classification of code smells across multiple programming paradigms and dataset scales. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Adapting the business model to ensure resilience: The case of michelin-starred french restaurants during the Covid-19 crisis
Abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic exposed the vulnerabilities of the fine-dining hospitality sector and reignited debates on organizational resilience. While the literature distinguishes operational, functional, and strategic resilience, it often conflates temporary business model adjustments enacted under crisis conditions with genuine strategic reconfigurations, leaving the boundary between short-term adaptation and strategic resilience theoretically ambiguous. This article elaborates on these distinctions by drawing on a longitudinal, processual case study of Michelin-starred restaurants in France, based on 33 semi-structured interviews, 316 press articles, and archival data, which were analyzed. Our findings identify three empirically distinct response trajectories: (1) a bounce-back trajectory based on preservation mechanisms, characterized by a suspension of restaurant activity made possible by public subsidies; (2) a bounce-back trajectory grounded in continuity mechanisms, involving temporary and reversible business model adaptations; and (3) a bounce-forward trajectory driven by irreversible transformation mechanisms, marked by durable business model reconfigurations. Despite the apparent continuity of bounce-back trajectories, they mask a post-crisis erosion of key BM components, questioning the idea of a complete return to pre-crisis configurations. This study contributes to the literature by (i) clarifying the relationship between strategic resilience and business models through a component-level, processual analysis using the RCOV framework, (ii) challenging the implicit equation between BM change and strategic resilience, and (iii) showing that bounce-forward trajectories—rather than bounce-back responses—constitute the core mechanism of strategic resilience in hospitality contexts. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Battery Swapping Business Models for Heavy-Duty Machines in Road Construction and Quarry Operations
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Battery swapping has been discussed as a potential approach to support the electrification of heavy-duty machines in road construction and quarry operations. These applications require high energy use, continuous operation, and reliable uptime, which can make conventional charging challenging to implement. At the same time, battery swapping is not widely adopted in these sectors, and there is limited understanding of suitable business models across different operational scenarios. The purpose of this paper is to examine battery swapping business models for heavy-duty machines in road construction and quarry operations under different operational conditions. The study considers five operational scenarios, ranging from single-machine use to multi-machine and high-intensity operations, including synchronized fleets, off-grid construction sites, and large quarry environments. The analysis focuses on four main criteria: machine utilization, project duration, energy infrastructure, and number of subcontractors. These criteria influence the design of battery swapping systems and the corresponding business models. Based on this analysis, the paper proposes a continuum framework of business models, ranging from simple battery rental solutions to more integrated energy-as-a-service approaches. The results show how different operational conditions may require different configurations, from flexible and low-investment solutions to more advanced and service-based models. The findings provide a structured way to explore how battery swapping could be implemented in different construction and quarry settings. The paper contributes to the literature on battery-based business model innovation and servitization, with a specific focus on heavy-duty machine industry. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Hidden Markov Model variants for prognostics: A comprehensive review and model selection framework
Abstract: This paper reviews and systematizes the use of Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and their semi-Markov extensions for prognostics within Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). It argues that prognostic models should be evaluated not only by prediction error but also by four key characteristics: uncertainty quantification, robustness, interpretability, and feasibility. The review organizes HMM-based methods into three groups: standard HMMs, Hidden Semi-Markov Models (HSMMs), and non-homogeneous HSMMs. Each group is assessed based on how it contributes to the four characteristics. Building on this analysis, the paper formalizes four representative models under a common notation for prognostics: HMM, HSMM, Adaptive HSMM (AHSMM), and Similarity Learning HSMM (SLHSMM). These models are benchmarked on the C-MAPSS turbofan dataset and on impacted open-hole composite specimens to evaluate both controlled and out-of-distribution scenarios. Results show that SLHSMM achieves the highest accuracy and provides sharper, well-calibrated uncertainty when test trajectories resemble training patterns. In contrast, AHSMM shows greater robustness to unexpected shifts and impact-induced behaviors. HMM and HSMM remain attractive choices when simplicity and computational efficiency are most important. The study concludes with practical guidance for selecting among HMM-based approaches based on the four key characteristics required for real-world PHM applications. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: The evolving nature of collaboration in business academia: Network structures and the role of editorial proximity in publishing
Abstract: Scholars have long suggested that network structures within academia may play a significant role in how knowledge is produced and disseminated, thus abetting the very research success of academics and their institutions. The nature of these structures, how they have evolved over time, and how individuals come to occupy certain positions requires further empirical exploration. This study examines the evolving structure of academic collaborations within business research from 2016 to 2024. Using publication metadata for 1,323,092 records from 530 business journals, we use network analysis to map co-authorship collaboration patterns while also assessing the structural benefits that may accrue from having journal editors as co-authors. Findings indicate that research networks have become increasingly collaborative over time, increasing to an average of 2.84 unique collaborations per author in 2024 from 1.72 in 2016. Despite this increase, we observed a 12.3 % increase in clustering during our study window, suggesting fewer bridges between authors publishing in different parts of the academic business literature. We replicated these analyses, focusing on journals in the Financial Times 50 (FT50). We found these trends were generally more pronounced in this subset. Research connections to journal editors likely fueled some of these growth patterns. Collaborating with an editor was positively related to both volume (degree) and type (betweenness) of collaborations in every year examined. This latter finding is particularly noteworthy because an increase in clustering suggests the occurrence of fewer bridging opportunities but publishing with an editor relates to increased bridging opportunities. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Explainable AI in dyslexia diagnosis and intervention: A systematic review and a novel conceptual multimodal framework
Abstract: Dyslexia is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by difficulties in reading, writing, and language processing. Early diagnosis is essential, as prompt intervention can significantly improve educational outcomes and quality of life. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and deep learning, have enabled automated dyslexia detection. However, most of these models function as “black boxes,” lacking the transparency required for personalized intervention and clinical trust. This systematic review, conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, critically analyzes research from the past decade on the use of Explainable AI (XAI) in dyslexia diagnosis, classification, and intervention. It highlights how XAI techniques enhance the interpretability of AI models, making them more applicable in clinical and educational settings. The review covers a range of XAI approaches, including LIME, SHAP, Grad-CAM, attention mechanisms, and inherently interpretable models. Findings show that while traditional AI often achieves high predictive accuracy, the lack of explainability hinders practical use. In contrast, XAI methods reveal interpretable patterns, such as irregular handwriting, atypical eye movements, or neuroimaging features, enabling clinicians and educators to better understand and trust model decisions. To bridge the gap between high-performing algorithms and actionable clinical insights, future research should focus on developing multimodal, interpretable systems suited for real-world application. Based on our synthesis, we propose a novel conceptual framework outlining a longitudinal, XAI-driven pipeline for dyslexia diagnosis and personalized intervention. This framework integrates multimodal data fusion, explainability techniques, and adaptive support strategies, paving the way for more transparent and personalized dyslexia management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Authentication and traceability of tea as a high-risk product: A comprehensive review of spectroscopic and chemometric solutions
Abstract: Food fraud poses a serious threat to the tea market, impacting sellers, consumers, and the entire supply chain. Chemometrics combined with spectroscopic techniques has gained increasing attention as a rapid, non-destructive, and cost-effective alternative to conventional methods for tea authentication. This review provides a comprehensive overview of these combined approaches, summarizing recent progress in detecting common fraudulent practices, including misrepresentation of variety, origin, and grade, as well as adulteration through substitution and addition. Beyond summarizing existing studies, this review also examines the practical limitations that constrain the translation of these methods from laboratory research to real-world application. Future directions, including the development of online monitoring systems and the integration of emerging technologies and metabolomics, are also discussed. Overall, this review highlights both the promise and the current challenges of spectroscopy and chemometrics in safeguarding the authenticity and traceability of tea products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Unveiling the dynamics of data driven innovation in human resource analytics: A grounded theory of strategic approach to HRM
Abstract: Data-driven innovation (DDI) in Human Resource Analytics (HR Analytics) presents a significant potential for strategic organizational change. A persistent gap exists between the theoretical promises of HR Analytics and its practical, value-generating implementation within organizations. This study aims to develop a conceptual model for the effective implementation of HR Analytics within private-sector organizations in a developing economy (Iran), framed through the lens of DDI. Employing a Grounded Theory (GT) approach, specifically the systematic coding methodology of Strauss and Corbin, this research gathered rich qualitative data through in-depth, semi-structured interviews with HR Analytics and Business Analytics experts operating within the Iranian organizational context. Data analysis, facilitated by MAXQDA, involved rigorous open, axial, and selective coding until theoretical saturation was achieved, with study rigor confirmed via Lincoln and Guba's criteria. The resulting conceptual model elucidates the complex interplay of causal conditions (e.g., transformation in human resource management, data-driven approach), context (e.g., technology adoption, cultural contexts), strategies (pre-adoption, decision-making, adoption phases), intervening obstacles, and possible outcomes. By highlighting the contextual features of the Iranian economic environment, this model offers a coherent framework to assist private enterprises in comparable settings to more effectively navigate their transition toward data-driven HR management, offering insights for organizations aiming to leverage HR Analytics as a driver for strategic innovation and business value enhancement. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Organizational Climate for Service Robot Integration
Abstract: The use of robots in service industries has sparked interest and attention among academia and industry. As its implementation often entails challenges for adaptation, the realization of the anticipated benefits of service robots (SRs) might be hindered. Based on organizational climate (OC) literature, well-managed OC for SR integration fosters integration within the organization and the realization of its benefits. However, empirical evidence on the effect of service-robot-oriented OC on organizational and employees’ performance in service organizations remains limited. To fill the void, this study aims to assess the relationship of service-robot-oriented OC prevalent in service organizations on both organizational (i.e., processes, customers) and employees’ performance (i.e., need satisfaction, work engagement). A cross-sectional survey is conducted with international data collection. Data analysis using PLS-SEM shows that internal process performance (IPP) statistically mediates the relationship between OC and customer performance (CP). Furthermore, employees’ need satisfaction (NS) statistically mediates OC and employees’ work engagement (WE). Theoretically, this study contributes by extending the mechanisms underlying the association between OC and organizational and employees’ performance. In practice, study results suggest that shaping a proper service-robot-oriented climate is of strategic importance for service organizations’ performance. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Farmers’ perceptions of conflict-prone neighborhoods – Insights from a choice experiment
Abstract: Recent research documents the growing frequency of land-use conflicts in rural areas. As conflicts between farmers and other stakeholders intensify while farmland resources continue to decline, spatial planning and the legal protection of agricultural land have become key policy priorities. This makes understanding farmers’ preferences regarding neighboring land uses particularly important. However, quantitative evidence remains limited. To address this gap, we used a discrete choice experiment to examine farmers’ perceptions of potentially conflict-generating neighboring land uses in a sample of 960 farmers from the Warmińsko-Mazurskie voivodeship, Poland. The results show that residential and business activities, especially when conducted at a large scale, are perceived as the most conflict-generating types of neighboring land uses. However, farmers’ perceptions vary across farm characteristics and locations. Residential neighborhoods are perceived as particularly conflict-generating by livestock farmers and farmers in highly urbanized municipalities, while patterns by farm size and nature-protection status are less consistent. © 2026 The Authors

Title: The relations between executive function, spatial skills, and building complexity during block play in young children
Abstract: This study investigated the associations between executive function (EF), spatial skills, and both the average levels and developmental trajectories of building complexity in preschoolers during block play, across two instructional contexts. Data were drawn from a large block play intervention study that included three conditions: free play, semi-structured, and business-as-usual (BAU). Intervention included 15-minute small group sessions that occurred twice per week for eight weeks. The present sample focused on 142 preschoolers (Mage = 54 months) who were randomly assigned to the free play and semi-structured conditions. Only participants in these two conditions engaged in block-play sessions, thereby yielding data on block-building complexity. Results indicated that children in both conditions generally showed a decline in building complexity scores over the 8-week intervention. However, after the introduction of picture prompts, children in the semi-structured condition exhibited an initial decline followed by subsequent improvement in block building complexity, whereas no clear patterns were observed in the free play condition. There was a significant positive association between children’s baseline spatial skills and their average building complexity across the intervention, which aligned with the hypothesis. Marginally significant positive associations were observed between baseline aggregate EF and the developmental change of building complexity over the course of the intervention. Implications for future research are discussed. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: From institutional pressures to employee involvement in organizational sustainability: The role of common good HRM
Abstract: Employee involvement in organizational sustainability is critical to achieving long-term environmental, social, and economic goals, yet the drivers of such involvement remain underexplored. Drawing on institutional theory and social exchange theory, this study develops a cross-level serial mediation model to explain how institutional sustainability pressures may become associated with employee involvement in organizational sustainability. We propose that institutional pressures, as perceived by senior executives, are associated with employee-experienced common good human resource management (CG-HRM), which in turn relates to perceived organizational support and, subsequently, employee involvement in organizational sustainability. Using time-lagged, multisource survey data from 96 firms in China, we find support for the proposed model. The findings contribute a more micro-foundational account of how institutional sustainability pressures, as perceived by senior executives, may become meaningful at the employee level through organizational and psychological processes, and clarify the role of employee-experienced CG-HRM in explaining employee sustainability-related behavior. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: Review and Experimental Evaluation of ML Models for DDoS Detection
Abstract: —DoS and DDoS attacks overload targets (servers) with unnatural and large amounts of traffic, resulting in the disruption of online services. Such attacks can have direct impact on regular business operations and can result in a loss of reputation as well as money for organizations. The aim of this study is to explore multiple ML algos. and compare the different possibilities when it comes to classification models to reduce these risks. ML facilitates the detection of anomalous activity and helps identify patterns in network traffic. We aim to evaluate multiple machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, Decision Tree, and XGB (eXtreme Gradient Boosting), using the UNSW-NB15 dataset. Accuracy, Precision, recall and F1 score are the four metrics used for evaluation. The results show that XGB performs very well, attaining 89% accuracy with baseline hyperparameter tuning. Title: A Comparative Study of Ensemble Machine Learning and Spatiotemporal Deep Learning for Vehicle Theft Location Prediction
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Vehicle theft remains a significant socioeconomic challenge, and accurate forecasting of theft locations is important for proactive policing and risk-based insurance interventions. This study formulates vehicle theft location forecasting as a spatiotemporal multi-class classification problem that integrates spatial, temporal, and contextual features. Using South African data, ensemble machine learning models (Random Forest and XGBoost) are compared with spatiotemporal deep learning approaches (TCN and CNN-LSTM) within a unified spatial-temporal binning framework. LSTM is included as a temporal benchmark to assess whether explicitly modelling spatial structure improves predictive performance. Evaluation across classification, calibration, statistical comparison, and insurance-oriented criteria showed that TCN provided the strongest overall predictive performance among the tested models. Random Forest was the closest performing classical model, with paired bootstrap testing giving directional evidence of improvement by TCN, although the confidence interval crossed zero and therefore indicated a modest rather than strongly conclusive advantage. In contrast, the business-oriented evaluation showed that Random Forest captured a higher share of potentially saved claim value under the selected alert threshold. These findings indicate that spatiotemporal deep learning improves predictive accuracy, while operational insurance value also depends on alert coverage and threshold selection. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Liu M.; Di G.; Liu F.; Feng K.; Huang B.; Li H.; Lv Y.
Title: A Chaos Engineering Based Simulation Method for Blockchain Consensus Protocol Reliability
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: The security and reliability of blockchain systems are critically dependent on their consensus mechanisms; however, a significant gap exists between theoretical design and engineering implementation in terms of security transformation and environmental adaptability. This research proposes a simulation testing methodology and implementation platform, ChaosConsensus, based on chaos engineering principles, for systematically verifying the robustness and fault tolerance of blockchain consensus protocols in complex production environments. Through proactive fault injection and abnormal behavior simulation, ChaosConsensus constructs a multilayered, cross-protocol verification environment that overcomes the limitations of traditional testing approaches, which are typically confined to unit-level testing and simplistic fault simulation. The platform is capable of providing simulation support for diverse failure scenarios that may occur across various blockchain system environments. The primary innovations of this research encompass four key aspects. First, we propose a universal hierarchical and domain-partitioned consensus fault test case framework that integrates multiple fault-tolerance model use cases. This framework exhibits two distinctive features: (1) it integrates both BFT-type and CFT-type fault tolerance models within a unified test case structure, and (2) drawing upon the upper-lower tester methodology from the international standard ISO 9646 for protocol conformance testing, it introduces a three-layer tester architecture consisting of “upper tester - inner tester - lower tester” to enhance the mapping and correspondence of test cases. This framework achievement has been further refined and incorporated into the ITU-T international standard for blockchain stability testing entitled “Stability assessment methods for distributed ledger technology platforms” (Document No. ITU-T T22-SG16–240415-TD-WP1–0258). Second, we propose a high-precision fault injection mechanism based on the message constructor and HOOK methods, which enables precise intervention in the fine-grained behaviors of consensus protocols. Third, we propose a universal multichain multiconsensus adaptation scheme decoupled from the business layer, thereby enhancing the platform’s portability and practical deployment capabilities. Fourth, we design a multidimensional simulation evaluation system incorporating both primary and secondary metrics, providing a unified benchmark for comprehensive quantitative assessment of consensus protocol fault simulation. In terms of practical applications, this solution has been tested and validated across multiple national-level financial blockchain payment systems and electricity trading blockchain systems that deploy various consensus protocols, including Dasheng, Dino, Raft, Tendermint, and HotStuff. The testing and verification were conducted in testing environments, preproduction environments (with configurations identical to production systems), and production environments. The results demonstrate that the platform is capable of discovering deep-seated issues that are difficult to detect using traditional testing methods, significantly enhancing the security and reliability of critical infrastructure and providing a valuable complement to existing blockchain system testing methodologies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Machine Learning Models for Customers Contact Channel Recommendation
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: The intense competition in all business sectors has raised the need to effectively attract customers, highlighting the importance of interaction through social media, which has been shown to provide significant benefits. This study proposes three models to recommend the most effective communication media for product acquisition or sales, aiming to optimize the customer attraction process by identifying the channels through which companies should promote their products to reach the most interested users. Clustering techniques were applied to analyze customer contact channels and support decision-making in marketing strategies. The methodological approach includes data collection, data preparation, the development of hybrid clustering methods, model testing, and results analysis, using a 70/30 split for training and testing data. Results show that the most frequently used media are Instagram, Pinterest, and Telegram. The hybrid approach used in this paper demonstrated that social media holds more influence over female users. Furthermore, social media appears to influence students more than professionals. Moreover, we found that the most used social media varies among clusters. Overall, our findings reveal that higher education institutions should incorporate different communication strategies rather than a “universal solution” for all their customers. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Ontology-Grounded Fact-Checking for E-Commerce: A Neuro-Symbolic, Claim-Centric Approach
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Misinformation in e-business—discounts based on volatile prices, fictitious stock levels, erroneous certifications, and implausible delivery commitments—erodes trust, competition, and regulatory adherence. This study introduces EBFN-Detect, a neuro-symbolic framework for claim-centric verification that incorporates a domain ontology (EBFN-O), a commercial knowledge graph, and natural language processing models. The pipeline extracts claims from diverse sources, conducts entity linking for products, brands, and sellers, retrieves ontology-guided evidence (RAG on KG), and assesses truthfulness by integrating a claim-evidence aware classifier with symbolic verifications of temporal consistency, price plausibility, and regulatory compliance. The output generates calibrated probabilities and verifiable explanations derived from supported or refuted chains with provenance. The work delineates the method, introduces EBFN-O in accordance with schema.org/GoodRelations/PROV-O, presents a multi-source corpus annotated at three tiers (claim, linking, truth) with reproducible guidelines, describes a RAG + KG pipeline featuring transparent fusion and calibration, and proposes an evaluation protocol that integrates metrics of accuracy, retrieval quality, and explanatory utility. Consequently, EBFN-Detect demonstrates enhancements in macro F1 and Brier/ECE relative to pure neural baselines, exhibiting significant benefits in time-sensitive scenarios and in categories characterized by substantial variant ambiguity, thereby delineating a feasible approach to dependable, traceable, and contestable verification in digital commerce. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: “Are BPM Graduates Future-Ready?” Reframing BPM Competencies for the Future-of-Work
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Business Process Management (BPM) is at the forefront of digital transformation, yet it remains an open question whether BPM graduates are equipped for this role. This study conducts a thematic discourse analysis to examine how BPM competencies are discursively constructed in academic literature and how they align with emerging skill demands in the World Economic Forum (WEF)’s Future of Jobs reports published between 2016 and 2025. The analysis shows that BPM competency is progressively framed as a hybrid profile spanning process, digital, analytical, social, and adaptive domains, with process and analytical capabilities dominating. This profile is broadly congruent with future-of-work skill projections. In contrast, social, adaptive, and sustainability-related competencies are less strongly foregrounded, despite their growing importance in future-of-work narratives. The study contributes a competency-skill alignment matrix and argues that BPM’s challenge is not a lack of relevant competencies, but uneven emphasis on how they are taught, assessed, or resourced. For educators, the key task is to identify ways to orchestrate BPM curricula that integrate process foundations with digital fluency, learning agility, social capability, and transformational leadership competencies, which are increasingly central to the digital transformation of work environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Development of an adaptive governance model for managing overtourism in sustainable tourism destinations
Abstract: The phenomenon of overtourism has emerged as a critical challenge in global destination management, precipitating severe environmental degradation, sociocultural disruptions, and declining quality of life for host communities. Conventional top-down strategies have proven inadequate in addressing the complex dynamics of excessive tourist influx. This study aims to develop a contextual adaptive governance model designed to effectively control overtourism while promoting sustainable tourism development. Employing a qualitative descriptive-analytical approach, the research focuses on Penglipuran Village, a prominent culture-based destination in Bali, Indonesia. Primary data were gathered through in-depth interviews with twenty-four key informants, comprising traditional leaders, village officials, tourism business operators, local residents, and domestic and international tourists, alongside participatory observation and comprehensive document analysis. The data were processed using rigorous thematic analysis techniques. The findings reveal that overtourism management necessitates a flexible, multi-dimensional framework rather than rigid regulatory measures. The developed model highlights three pivotal components: institutional flexibility that integrates customary laws with formal policies, structured multi-stakeholder collaboration fostering synergistic decision-making, and a continuous learning mechanism enabling iterative policy adaptation. Results further indicate that while tourism generates substantial economic benefits, it simultaneously triggers cultural commercialization, shifts in local social values, and intensified environmental strain. Critical governance gaps were identified, particularly the fragmentation between traditional and formal institutional systems, reliance on manual monitoring, and the absence of systematic coordination structures. By embedding social negotiation and cultural legitimacy into governance processes, the proposed model successfully balances economic imperatives with ecological and sociocultural preservation. Theoretically, this research enriches the tourism governance literature by systematically integrating adaptive governance principles within the overtourism discourse. Practically, it provides destination managers and policymakers with a scalable, context-sensitive framework that leverages local wisdom, digital monitoring, and collaborative institutional design to ensure long-term destination resilience and sustainability in the face of escalating tourism pressures. Title: Readiness of the taxonomy used by ECCAIRS 2 for Causal Analysis based on Systems Theory
Abstract: This paper examines whether the taxonomy used by the European Co-ordination Centre for Accident and Incident Reporting Systems (ECCAIRS 2) can provide suitable inputs for Causal Analysis based on Systems Theory (CAST), a method grounded in the System-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes (STAMP). The methodology combines analysis of CAST inputs and outputs with Semantic Web technologies, Unified Modeling Language (UML) and Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) diagrams to map ECCAIRS 2 entities, attributes, and values to individual CAST steps. A representation of the ECCAIRS 2 taxonomy and an ontology implemented in Protégé were developed to support querying and traceability, and the approach was validated using four real aviation occurrences recorded in ECCAIRS 2 for which CAST analyses were available. The results show that key ECCAIRS 2 attributes can systematically support CAST activities such as defining system boundaries, identifying losses and system-level hazards, identifying controllers of the safety control structure, and formulating Unsafe Control Actions and systemic causal factors. The findings confirm that the ECCAIRS 2 taxonomy can be used as a structured input source for CAST, while highlighting limitations related to incomplete coverage of CAST activities, constrained representation of system context and interactions, and dependence on the quality of occurrence reports. The proposed methodology offers a decision-support framework that enhances consistency, transparency, and efficiency of STAMP-based accident and incident investigations and provides a basis for further tool development and partial automation. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: State-Owned Enterprises in Bosnia And Herzegovina: Footprint, Performance and Fiscal Impact
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This paper assesses the footprint, performance, and fiscal impact of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s SOEs within a fragmented, multi-level governance system. Using a consolidated dataset of 542 SOEs (2021–2024), we benchmark outcomes against private firms and regional norms via ratio analysis focusing on ROA, ROE/ROC, revenue per employee, leverage, and liquidity metrics. Findings show persistent structural underperformance. SOEs control assets near 82% of GDP and employ 9% of the workforce yet record negative returns and roughly 50% lower productivity. Using a conservative repayment-capacity screen, we estimate high-risk short-term liabilities of about 5.4% of GDP that are likely to require government intervention. While leverage ratios are comparable to those observed in peer countries in Central and Eastern Europe, rising liabilities, weak short-term repayment capacity, tax arrears, and reliance on budget transfers indicate increasing fiscal risks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Risk-aware and network-compatible bidding of aggregated DER under energy-as-a-service model
Abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) and the adoption of distributed energy resources (DERs) introduce new layers of uncertainty for the operation of distribution networks. This variability, however, represents a valuable source of flexibility that can be unlocked when these resources are managed intelligently and with a coordinated approach. This work presents a unified bidding framework that manages DER-related uncertainties by coordinating residential DERs under an energy-as-a-service (EaaS) model. A Wasserstein distributionally robust bidding scheme is proposed to generate frequency control ancillary services and energy offers that remain feasible under uncertain DER behavior, while dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) are incorporated to ensure that all bids respect local network constraints. The simulation results indicate that coordinated DER flexibility substantially improves the aggregator's wholesale market performance, with frequency control ancillary services (FCAS) Raise and Lower revenues approximately 62% and 41% higher than in the business-as-usual (BAU) case, respectively, while reducing customers’ electricity costs. In addition, DOE-based bidding improves voltage compliance to 100% and reduces the maximum transformer loading from 142.7% to 81.5%, supporting operation within the prescribed network limits. These findings show that risk-aware bidding, network-aware coordination, and a customer-focused EaaS framework can unlock reliable, scalable, and economically beneficial DER flexibility. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Wei H.; Gao H.
Title: SwanMixer: Fine-Grained Channel Modeling with Sliding-Window Adaptive Normalization for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
Abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting (MTSF) is important for decision-making in many real-world applications, including business decision-making, financial investment, and resource planning. Although recent Transformer-based models have improved long-horizon forecasting, two limitations remain. Existing channel dependence methods mainly rely on global interactions and therefore model cross-channel relations too coarsely, while existing normalization strategies are often too coarse to handle strong local distribution shifts in non-stationary data. To address these limitations, we propose SwanMixer, a forecasting architecture that combines Sliding Window Adaptive Normalization (SWAN), Patch Embedding, and GroupMixer. SWAN performs dynamic normalization within sliding windows to align local distributions while preserving informative non-stationary variations. On top of patch-level representations, GroupMixer introduces a hierarchical channel interaction scheme with intra-group and inter-group attention, which captures fine-grained local dependencies and aggregates global channel information efficiently. Experiments on Weather, Electricity, Traffic, and Solar-Energy show that SwanMixer consistently achieves superior or competitive results and obtains the largest number of best results among the compared methods. These results show that combining local adaptive normalization with fine-grained channel interaction is effective for MTSF. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.
