Title: Was I scammed? Understanding consumer scam reporting behavior through cognitive appraisal
Abstract: Underreporting has been hampering regulatory efforts due to consumers’ hesitance to report ambiguous unsatisfactory transactions, particularly in online marketplaces or consumer services where deceptive business practices are uncertain or difficult to prove. This study examines how consumers appraise harm, effort, and resolution uncertainty when deciding whether to respond to potential scams. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory and Consumer Complaint Behavior, we develop and test a dual-pathway model that explains when victims pursue private action (e.g., contacting the seller) or public action (e.g., filing a complaint). Using nationally representative data from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission's 2017 fraud survey, we show that financial loss, perceived effort, outcome uncertainty, and their interactions jointly shape complaint behavior. We find that private action is driven by restitution motives and is amplified in high-loss or online scenarios, where it is perceived as a low-cost first step. Public action, by contrast, is less influenced by financial stakes and more by confidence in evidence, reflecting a justice-seeking mindset. This research contributes to the theoretical understanding of consumer behavior after perceived scam experiences by adopting long-standing marketing and consumer behavior theories and offers practical managerial insights by shifting the focus from victim profiling to behavioral process modeling. Our findings highlight the need for system-level interventions such as standardized dispute mechanisms, centralized complaint portals, and structured evidence logs to reduce harm and improve reporting confidence in scam-prone “gray areas.” © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Liu C.; Liu J.; Hou X.; Guo M.
Title: TierServe: Revenue-Maximizing LLM Inference Scheduling Across Multiple Subscription Tiers
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference systems serve clients across multiple subscription tiers with heterogeneous latency requirements and revenue contributions. Existing schedulers optimize throughput or service-level objectives (SLO) attainment, treating all requests as equally valuable. In multi-tier settings, this leads to a fundamental mismatch: a scheduler that maximizes goodput may allocate substantial resources to low-tier requests while high-tier requests miss their stricter SLOs, resulting in suboptimal operator revenue. We present TierServe, a revenue-driven LLM inference scheduler that jointly leverages both subscription-tier priority and per-request SLO slack. TierServe prioritizes high-value requests while dynamically utilizing available slack to improve overall efficiency, aligning scheduling decisions with both business value and latency urgency. We evaluate TierServe across a range of workloads and load conditions. Results show that TierServe consistently improves system revenue over state-of-the-art baselines while maintaining competitive per-tier latency. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Author full names: Faling, Marijn (56910220500); Vellema, Sietze (20735738600)
Title: Crowding-in pathways in inclusive agribusiness partnerships: Towards a heuristic for responsible scaling
Abstract: CONTEXT: Inclusive agribusiness partnerships (IABs) are widely promoted as vehicles for agricultural transformation yet achieving scale while maintaining inclusion remains a persistent challenge. These challenges highlight the need to understand how inclusive outcomes become embedded and sustained at scale in wider institutional environments. OBJECTIVE: This article develops and empirically grounds a theory-informed typology of ‘crowding-in’ pathways through which external actors adapt their practices in response to partnership-induced innovations. The typology aims to help partnerships recognize and proactively engage with different pathways through which surrounding actors may contribute to their inclusive objectives. We examine how these pathways can contribute to responsible scaling and the conditions under which they are more likely to do so. METHODS: The study follows an abductive action research approach combining a narrative literature review with empirical action research and practitioner engagement. The research was embedded within the 2SCALE program, an agribusiness incubator initiative operating in Sub-Saharan Africa and funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The literature review led to a draft conceptual typology of crowding in pathways, which was empirically validated and refined through analysis of five purposively selected 2SCALE partnerships in Ghana, Kenya, and Nigeria. Data was collected through literature study, interviews, participatory workshops, program document analysis, and longitudinal engagement with partnership actors. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: We distinguish, for each actor type, between an organizational advantage–driven pathway—where actors crowd in to gain capabilities or capital—and an issue-informed pathway—where actors engage to advance inclusive outcomes. This results in the identification of six crowding-in pathways across business, state, and civil society spheres: competitive, normative, facilitative, dependence, credibility, and re-institutionalization crowding-in. The cases illustrate how external actors from government, business, and civil society adapt business models, infrastructure and extension services, and coordination support, extending inclusive outcomes beyond partnership boundaries. However, crowding-in also introduces risks, including corporate market capture, unequal allocation of public resources, and increased farmer dependence on tightly coupled market actors. We conclude that responsible scaling requires continuous attention to power asymmetries, inclusion criteria, and institutional pluralism. The typology offers both an analytical lens and a practical heuristic to anticipate and steer systemic responses in agricultural systems. SIGNIFICANCE: This study advances understanding of responsible outcome-oriented scaling by shifting attention from the performance of individual partnerships to the wider actor networks and institutional environments through which inclusive outcomes become embedded and sustained at scale. Introducing crowding-in as an analytical heuristic, it provides a heuristic for examining how private, public, and civil society actors contribute to scaling processes beyond project boundaries. The typology supports more anticipatory and strategic engagement with external actors while acknowledging the uncertainty and trade-offs inherent in scaling inclusive agribusiness outcomes. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Wei L.; Yin N.; Li T.; Li D.
Title: A dominant-subordinate generative approach to imbalanced deceptive review detection
Abstract: Online reviews play an important role in both consumer purchase decisions and business performance analysis. However, deceptive reviews reduce the reliability of decisions based on online reviews. Although several studies developed algorithms to detect deceptive reviews, most of them ignored the negative impact of class imbalance, where legitimate reviews far outweigh deceptive reviews in practice. In this paper, we propose a deep generative approach called dominant-subordinate conditional variational auto-encoder and generative adversarial network (DC-VAEGAN) to address the class imbalance problem in deceptive review detection. Specifically, a dominant-subordinate condition structure is designed to generate and fine-tune deceptive review data at the review veracity and polarity levels. Empirical results show that the DC-VAEGAN provides statistically characterized, but not uniformly large, improvements in imbalanced deceptive review detection. The method is most useful for improving threshold-level balance indicators such as G-mean, while several Macro-F1 and AUC differences remain modest or non-significant. Further, interpretable analysis indicates that the augmented data helps the models learn reviewer-behavior and review-content anomalies more effectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Object-Centric Process Querying in SQL: Translation Rules and In-Database Execution
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Object-Centric Process Querying (OCPQ) is a visual query language and accompanying tool for expressing queries and constraints over Object-Centric Event Data (OCED). Such queries span multiple object and event types that case-centric query languages cannot natively address. Its existing execution engine processes data in memory: Dataset size is capped by host memory, and the relational database systems that organizations already operate cannot serve as backends, forcing data export or migration. In this paper, we present a translation from OCPQ to SQL, defined as a recursive mapping over the OCPQ query tree with a rule per construct, emitting SQL for SQLite, DuckDB, and PostgreSQL. An OCEL 2.0 Virtualization Layer accommodates source schemas that diverge from the OCEL 2.0 layout via direct rewrite or VIEW generation, so the translation can target them without data migration. We evaluate using three types of workloads: Seven queries from prior work, an automatically generated corpus of 6919 OCPQ trees, and a non-OCEL Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) database schema queried through the virtualization layer. The resulting query outputs match the in-memory engine across all queries, demonstrating that the translation preserves its semantics. Our evaluation also shows the memory decoupling enabled by the translation: SQL backends scale to support large datasets on which the native OCPQ engine runs out of memory. When data fits in memory, the in-memory OCPQ engine remains fastest, with DuckDB roughly 3–12× slower and PostgreSQL 14–71× slower as drop-in replacements. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Aviation Workforce 4.0: Competences for a Sustainable and Digitalized Sector

Abstract: The transition toward a sustainable and digital economy requires new workforce models that combine technical, digital, and transversal competences. Authors: Merkert R.; Hess S.; Khan F.; Bliemer M.C.J.
Title: The relevance of traditional postal services in a diversifying last-mile delivery landscape: The role of human to human (H2H) interactions
Source title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review
Abstract: Last-mile delivery research increasingly focuses on business-to-consumer (B2C) automation to satisfy consumers with an ‘I want it now’ mentality, reduce firms’ carbon footprints, and improve cost efficiency. Much less attention has been given to the possibility that there might be differences across consumer segments in their preferences for technology‑enabled or more traditional, human-mediated delivery modes. Building on random utility theory, we developed a hybrid choice model with a latent class kernel and applied it to stated choice data on delivery service preferences collected from 1,007 customers across metropolitan and regional areas of Australia. Our results reveal two latent classes of consumers with distinctly different preferences. The largest group, which we label techies , value speed and low cost last-mile delivery and prefer traditional postal services, followed by aerial drones and parcel lockers, with the effect moderated by parcel value and the availability of a safe place for unattended delivery. The second group, relational, trusting people , place a stronger emphasis on trust and interpersonal aspects of service and substantially prefer traditional postal services (assuming a safe place for delivery is available) and lockers while showing a strong dislike of aerial drones. To interpret these patterns, we draw on social exchange theory and the human-to-human (H2H) relationship model to explain how relational considerations may influence delivery mode preferences. H2H interactions matter for a subset of consumers. Importantly, our broader findings highlight the continued relevance of traditional postal services in a diversifying delivery landscape. Although no direct spatial effect emerges in the class allocation model, our results suggest that residential location (metropolitan versus regional) has a structural effect by influencing consumers’ underlying latent attitudes. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Xu Y.; Zhang F.; Cai Y.
Title: Synergistic management of nitrogen budgets and non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions in China's livestock sector: A scenario-based assessment
Abstract: Livestock production supplies dietary protein and supports agricultural development, but it also contributes substantially to nitrogen pollution and non-CO2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Amid growing pressures related to climate change, resource scarcity, and environmental protection, enhancing nitrogen use efficiency and curbing pollution have emerged as important objectives for the green transformation of the livestock sector. This study combined a livestock-centred coupled human and natural systems (CHANS) accounting framework, the IPCC emission-factor approach, and a spatial-equilibrium trade model to quantify provincial nitrogen budgets, non-CO2 GHG emissions, and trade-induced virtual transfers of environmental pressures in China's livestock sector from 2000 to 2024. A business-as-usual (BAU) baseline and four mitigation scenarios were developed to assess dietary adjustment, improved feed conversion efficiency, enhanced manure recycling, and their combined implementation through 2050. The results showed that total livestock-sector non-CO2 GHG emissions peaked at 546.98 Mt. CO2-eq in 2005 and subsequently declined with fluctuations to 415.59 Mt. CO2-eq in 2024. CH4 from enteric fermentation was the main non-CO2 GHG source. The livestock sector maintained a persistent nitrogen surplus, and NH3 volatilization remained the dominant nitrogen-loss pathway. Relative to BAU in 2050, dietary adjustment was projected to reduce non-CO2 GHG emissions by approximately 42%, whereas improved feed conversion efficiency and enhanced manure recycling were projected to reduce nitrogen losses by approximately 28% and 31%, respectively. The combined mitigation scenario was projected to achieve the strongest co-mitigation effect, reducing non-CO2 GHG emissions and nitrogen losses by approximately 45% and 50%, respectively. These findings suggest that coordinated dietary adjustment, feed-efficiency improvement, and manure-management optimization may offer considerable potential for synergistically reducing nitrogen losses and non-CO2 GHG emissions, providing a scientific basis for regionally differentiated, whole-chain mitigation strategies and the green transformation of China's livestock sector. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: The Impact of Big Data Analysis on Claims Management in Jordanian Insurance Companies
Abstract: The aim of the research is to demonstrate the impact of big data analytics (quantitative analysis, qualitative analysis) on claims management in Jordanian insurance companies. Title: Green debt for nature-based solutions: aligning municipal budgeting and banking practices
Abstract: Local governments face growing risks from climate change, which require substantial investments in climate adaptation to safeguard future generations. Nature-based solutions (NBS) have been recognized as a cost-efficient strategy to redevelop public space, to create greener and more climate adaptive urban environments. However, development of NBS is hindered by a lack of financial resources to fully scale up the transformation. To overcome this barrier, literature calls for clear sustainable finance frameworks and business model approaches to include private financing in the development of public NBS. In our research we consider the perceptions of municipalities and banks, as institutional lenders, towards using green debt-financing to finance NBS. We draw on sustainability transitions literature to theorize NBS as a niche innovation within established banking-municipal relations. Using qualitative interviews with Belgian banking experts and urban and financial planners from Flemish cities, we reveal competing financial logics between municipal financing practices and banking requirements, limiting the uptake of green debt for NBS. While NBS are mostly absorbed in traditional municipal deficit financing, this conceals their value and prevents market development. Alternatively, project finance remains difficult due to capacity constraints and differing valuation logics. Emerging sustainable finance frameworks create opportunities but shift administrative burdens onto municipalities. Overall, current practices mainly support NBS to fit and conform, rather than transform established debt-practices. Substantial upscaling of NBS will require changes in both banking practices and municipal financing approaches, including explicit integration of physical climate risk and collective financing mechanisms. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Modelling the Stages of an Organisational Whistleblower’s Journey
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Whistleblowers perform an essential service in revealing wrongdoing. Most feel compelled to highlight nefarious organisational activities. If their efforts within the organisation are ignored and they feel driven to “go public”, disclosures can harm the organisation’s cybersecurity and whistleblowers themselves usually pay a high price for their actions. We argue that, rather than vilifying whistleblowers, organisations ‘harness’ their propensity to keep the organisation on the straight and narrow. To achieve this, it is crucial to understand the whistleblower’s journey from being triggered by some unethical organisational activity to the final external whistleblowing act. We reviewed the archival literature to produce a synthesis of whistleblower stages. We carried out a case study and interviewed two whistleblowers to inform derivation of a staged whistleblowing model. This makes it possible to identify pressure points for targeted interventions which can encourage internal whistleblowing and thereby prevent the tangential dismantling of organisational information security. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Optimization of Home-to-Home Energy Trading Using Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning in a Smart Community
Source title: Lecture Notes of the Institute for Computer Sciences, Social-Informatics and Telecommunications Engineering, LNICST
Abstract: In recent years, home energy management systems (HEMS) have become increasingly popular as part of efforts to achieve a decarbonized society. HEMS can efficiently use electricity generated from renewable energy sources by managing a household's electricity consumption on a schedule. However, in the previous model, HEMS managed only the electricity consumption of individual households and did not consider interactions between households. Also, battery life depletion due to battery charging and discharging was not taken into account. Therefore, we created an environmental model that enables electricity trading among households and takes battery health into account. Simulations were conducted using this environmental model and a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm. The simulation results showed that the total energy consumption and electricity prices of all cooperating households could be reduced based on the status and electricity prices of each household. Title: Digital transformation and supply chain Resilience: Inverted U-shaped effect and mechanisms with dual Moderation—Evidence from China’s A-share listed firms
Abstract: Against the background of rising global supply chain risks and deepening digital transformation, this study draws on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities perspective and uses data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2013 to 2023 to examine the effect of digital transformation on supply chain resilience. Findings reveal a significant inverted U-shaped effect: moderate levels of digital transformation strengthen supply chain resilience, whereas excessive levels of digital transformation weaken it. Absorptive, innovative, and adaptive capabilities partially mediate this nonlinear effect. Further analysis shows R&D intensity steepens the inverted U-shaped curve, whereas firm size flattens it. Moreover, the inverted U-shaped effect is more pronounced among firms in regions with higher factor market development and among firms with higher supply chain concentration and lower financing constraints. Title: Corporate social responsibility and environmental performance in the lebanese travel and tourism sector: Through the lens of green practices
Abstract: This study examines the impact of green human resource management (GHRM) and green innovation (GI) on environmental performance (EP) in the Lebanese travel and tourism sector, with corporate social responsibility (CSR) as a mediator. In addition, the study investigates the moderating role of green transformational leadership (GTL). Grounded in NRBV theory, the study conceptualizes green practices and CSR as internal resources and capabilities that contribute to improved EP. Data were collected from 397 employees and managers through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement items were adopted from well-established scales and assessed using a five-point Likert scale. The results indicate that both GHRM and GI have significant positive effects on environmental performance. Furthermore, CSR plays a significant mediating role, suggesting that organizations adopting green practices are more likely to engage in broader CSR initiatives, which ultimately improve environmental performance. The findings also demonstrate that GTL moderates the relationship between GI and EP, highlighting the importance of visionary leadership in maximizing the environmental benefits of innovation. Interestingly, the results indicate that GTL does not moderate the relationship between GHRM and environmental performance, suggesting that the effectiveness of GHRM may depend more on organizational systems than on leadership influence alone. The coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.68, indicating that 68% of the variance in EP is explained by the variables included in the model. The study provides important theoretical and practical implications. From a theoretical perspective, the findings extend NRBV theory by demonstrating how green practices and CSR jointly contribute to environmental performance. Practically, the results suggest that tourism organizations can improve their EP by integrating GHRM, green innovation, and CSR initiatives into their operational strategies, thereby enhancing sustainability while maintaining competitiveness. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: The Hack4CBL Framework: A Challenge-Based Learning Approach for Multidisciplinary Hackathons in Higher Education

Abstract: This paper introduces the Hack4CBL framework, integrating Challenge-Based Learning (CBL) principles into hackathon design for multidisciplinary higher education. We illustrate Hack4CBL’s effectiveness through the “Second International Hackathon of Intelligent Solutions for the Promotion of Agribusiness 4.0,” involving 142 undergraduate students from Colombia and Costa Rica across Systems Engineering, Business Administration, and Agronomic Engineering. Its application in a formal undergraduate course is also discussed. Over 16 weeks, interdisciplinary teams tackled real-world agribusiness challenges, developing minimum viable products. Results show that CBL integration enhances collaboration, deepens domain knowledge, and accelerates professional skill development. Title: Cost-Predictable Web3 for Public Asset Auctions: An Industry Case Study of Deterministic-Fee B2G Infrastructure
Abstract: Blockchain can improve transparency and auditability in public services, but its adoption in Business-to-Government (B2G) settings is constrained by a practical cost problem. Auction Organizers (AOs) are typically paid through fixed-price, fiat-denominated contracts, while blockchain execution costs are paid in native tokens and may vary sharply under congestion. This paper presents an industry case study of a Cost-Predictable Web3 Infrastructure (CPWI) for public asset auctions. The design combines three elements: deterministic-fee execution, compliance-preserving hybridization, and a treasury policy for planned token procurement. We instantiate the design on Algorand, where bidder onboarding, KYC, fiat deposits, and regulatory coordination remain off-chain, while critical auction state transitions are anchored on-chain. Under an asynchronous bid-sniping workload of 50 requests per second over 2,500 transactions, the deployed MainNet system maintained a constant per-bid protocol fee of 0.003 ALGO and a median time-to-finality of 7.49 s (p95 16.70 s). To assess financial operability under a fixed-price contract, we evaluate a treasury policy based on Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) and a 50% reserve through a 10,000-path Monte Carlo simulation. In the evaluated setting, this policy reduces the simulated probability of cost overruns above 20% from 25.23% to 13.75%, while reducing Cost Overrun VaR from $36.18 to $9.05 at 95% confidence and from $84.84 to $21.21 at 99% confidence. The case suggests that cost predictability is a practical design requirement for blockchain-based B2G services, not a secondary implementation detail. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Deployment-Sovereign AI Infrastructure for BPM Education: An Open-Source Stack from Document Analysis to Process Execution

Abstract: This paper investigates whether deployment-sovereign AI infrastructure can support BPM education without dependence on commercial LLM APIs. Commercial endpoints exhibited provider-specific availability failures and content-policy refusals, most visibly Claude 3.5 Haiku on selected healthcare, chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN), substance-destruction, and self-harm documentation prompts. In the tested PCSS deployment, all five open-weight models completed the high-sensitivity corpus without API errors or policy refusals. A preliminary, non-blinded expert assessment found no obvious quality deficit for routine BPM documentation tasks, but does not establish statistical equivalence to commercial models. Title: Transforming Emerging Markets: Digital Economy as a Driver of Sustainability
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The digital economy is significantly altering global economic environments, particularly in emerging markets through technological adoption, mobile connectivity, and novel business models. This paper reviews literature on the digital economy in these markets, emphasizing key drivers, challenges, and opportunities. A PRISMA-guided literature selection process identified 85 peer-reviewed studies published from 2010 to 2025. Findings indicate that mobile banking, e-commerce, digital entrepreneurship, and government-led digital initiatives serve as the primary catalysts for growth in the digital economy. However, this growth faces significant challenges, including infrastructure gaps, cybersecurity risks, a lack of digital literacy, and various regulatory barriers that need to be addressed to ensure sustained progress. This review emphasizes the capacity of the digital economy to facilitate progress towards Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), notably SDG 8, which focuses on Decent Work and Economic Growth; SDG 9, which pertains to Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure; and SDG 10, which aims to reduce inequalities. Title: Inside out: cutting-edge methods to decode external opportunities for startup growth

Title: Co-creation in sustainable family entrepreneurship
Abstract: This study examines how co-creation unfolds in sustainable family entrepreneurship across nine co-creation cases in two family firms in Mexico and Colombia. These dimensions operate through six mechanisms: generating a shared view, conveying different interpretations, family coupling, family decoupling, family inclusion, and family separation. Title: Simulating Dynamic Relationships in Object-Centric Processes

Abstract: Several Business Process Simulation techniques have been proposed to generate case-based event logs. Title: Progress and Constraints in the E-commerce Sector: A 2023–2025 Study of Webshops in Bosnia and Herzegovina

Abstract: This paper examines the evolution of the e-commerce landscape in Bosnia and Herzegovina (B&H) between 2023 and 2025 based on three consecutive annual surveys of 423 webshops (162 in 2023, 154 in 2024 and 107 in 2025) conducted in cooperation with the eCommerce Association in B&H. Merchants consistently identified similar barriers, including customer habits, informal competition, market size limitations, regulatory ambiguity, and skills shortages, while emphasizing product quality, competitive pricing, delivery reliability, payment security and branding as key success factors. Title: Transboundary cascading economic impacts and efficiency dynamics of power shortages induced by extreme heatwaves: An integrated weather-shock input-output data envelopment analysis framework for China
Abstract: Efficiency analysis is critical for evaluating economic impacts of extreme heat-induced power shortages. It detects inefficient sectors and resource misallocation to boost economic resilience. However, existing studies only examine associated economic losses, ignoring post-shock efficiency analysis. This limitation impedes the full assessment of cascading socio-environmental risks and the design of targeted resilience policies. This study constructs an integrated Weather-Shock Input-Output Data Envelopment Analysis framework. Empirical results reveal: First, macroeconomic risks triggered by heatwaves stem from two sources: the direct physical impacts of heatwave shocks and the institutional rules that shape power rationing schemes. Under our baseline scenario where energy-intensive industries bear priority cutbacks, indirect economic losses are roughly twice as high as direct losses; however, both the scale and composition of total losses vary significantly when adopting alternative power rationing policies. Second, this study differentiates the functional roles of various sectors in risk transmission. While agricultural and financial sectors act as passive absorbers, sectors like food & tobacco processing and leasing & business services are identified as key amplifiers that propagate supply-chain shocks. Third, power shortages widen disparities in efficiency, with more than 90% of this inequality attributable to within-group heterogeneity, a pattern prominent in western China and secondary industries. The findings support a transition from “one-size-fits-all” energy rationing toward supply-chain-based strategies that protect loss transmission pathways and optimize cross-regional resource reallocation. © 2026

Title: Crowdshipping for reverse logistics: unlocking sustainability, trust, and fairness
Source title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review
Abstract: This study investigates the integration of crowdshipping (CS) into e-commerce reverse logistics, specifically applied to the parcel transport stage between return points and transhipment facilities. Several barriers have limited CS adoption in forward logistics, such as trust, privacy, and security concerns due to direct customer–crowdshipper interaction, and the inability to offer bundled CS tasks that would enable attractive compensation schemes, but these constraints are mitigated in this transport-stage-focused reverse logistics setting. The proposed CS-integrated system operates in a business-to-business (B2B) context, eliminating customer contact and allowing bundled CS task assignment, thereby providing a more secure and operationally efficient setting for CS deployment. In this study, operational and external costs (i.e., per-kilometre social costs) for both conventional and CS-integrated reverse logistics systems are modelled and simulated across diverse spatial and demographic contexts, system scales, configurations, and levels of CS supply and behavioural dynamics. These simulations generate a large database that identifies the conditions under which the CS-integrated system can achieve operational and/or environmental advantages compared with the conventional system. Using a comprehensive simulation experiment based on systematically generated parameter combinations (45,000 simulation runs) and applying decision tree analysis, we find that the CS-integrated system reduces operational costs in nearly all cases, with savings reaching up to 70 % , particularly under conditions with sufficient CS supply and high participation willingness (i.e., low sensitivity to detour and compensation). Title: Evaluating Students’ AI Literacy and Reflective Capacity in an Entrepreneurship Course Using Professor E
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has the potential as a powerful tool to enhance and strengthen student learning experiences. The focus group interview results highlighted students’ concerns on technical, practical, critical, and ethical factors when utilising Professor E for reflective purposes. Title: The Couscous Game: An Academic Case Study on Advancing Gamification in Operations and Supply Chain Management Education

Title: State ownership, media sentiment, and the completion of cross-border acquisitions
Abstract: Media sentiment plays an important but underexamined role in shaping the completion of cross-border acquisitions (CBAs) by state-owned enterprise (SOE) acquirers. While SOE-led CBAs face a baseline completion disadvantage relative to non-SOE deals due to host-country concerns over political motives, government influence, and national security, we argue that this disadvantage is not static but is actively shaped by how the deal is portrayed in the media. Drawing on agenda-setting and legitimacy theories, we show that positive media sentiment attenuates the legitimacy concerns attached to state ownership, while negative sentiment reinforces them. The effect is amplified when the sentiment is conveyed by prestigious outlets with greater agenda-setting influence. This study contributes to SOE internationalization and CBAs research by showing that legitimacy is not static but socially constructed through deal-level media evaluations. © 2026 The Authors. Title: Bridging the pitch and the canvas: Synergistic insights for advancing empirical research a pre-registered report
Abstract: High-quality empirical research depends on guidance tools that are structured, coherent, and lifecycle-spanning. Yet researchers across business disciplines continue to draw on fragmented, piecemeal advice that was never designed to integrate into a single system. Two independent responses to this challenge have emerged from within the business academic community over the past decade: the Pitching Research Framework (PRF; Faff, 2015, 2024) and the AMJ Management Research Canvas (MRC; Dorobantu et al., 2024). Developed independently and in different disciplinary communities, they have never been systematically compared, and the prospect of their integration has not previously been explored. This paper presents the protocol for a conceptual study that addresses this gap. We advance the conceptual proposition that integrating the PRF and the MRC produces a unified, end-to-end research guidance pathway that is meaningfully greater than either framework alone in advancing research clarity, rigour, and transparency across the full research lifecycle (from embryonic ideation through to manuscript completion). The research design involves systematic comparative analysis of the components of each framework, leading to the development of an integrated synergistic model grounded in Responsible Science principles (cRRBM, 2017; Faff, 2021; Tsui, 2021, 2022). Title: Risk-Aware MIS Frameworks and Advanced Cybersecurity Solutions

Abstract: The problem of phishing attack is among the most widespread cybercrimes that impact the information system of the organisation offering the lack of trust and endangering sensitive data. Such threats should be monitored and controlled via developed analytics to be embedded in the risk conscious Management Information System (MIS). Within the scope of this paper, it is proposed to implement a data analytics structure to combine machine learning with MIS reporting to deliver actionable intelligence with phishing attacks. Using Kaggle Phishing Detection Dataset that had 662 591 records and 11 attributes, a Random Forest classifier was used to classify the URLs as a phishing or a legitimate site. The model was found to have a 94% accuracy, 92% precision, 91% recall, and ROC-AUC of 0.96, which can be seen as evidence of an improved performance as opposed to the baseline classifiers whose typical accuracy is and usually falls below 85% in the framework of the model created. The framework provides risk scores, confusion matrices, precision and recall curves, which are displayed in MIS dashboards and are used by managers to assist them in deciding. It is shown in the use case that it is critical how organisations can target the high-risk entries, deal with the false positives and false negatives, and make organisations more resilient towards phishing attacks. It may be applied to prevent cybersecurity of enterprises monitoring, risk-aware decision-supporting, and embedded to sophisticated MIS infrastructures. Numerical comparisons can prove the soundness of the given solution, as it positions it as a scalable and explainable operational tool of cybersecurity in a business setting of the modern era. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Human resource management strategy for internalizing and internationalizing traditional culinary in SMEs: A case study of Mie Lethek in Indonesia
Abstract: This study investigates strategic workforce practices in heritage-based food enterprises, focusing on Mie Lethek producers in Indonesia, to examine how people-centered approaches support cultural continuity and global market engagement. Using a qualitative case study design, four enterprises (two small-scale and two medium-scale) were purposively selected based on generational experience and market orientation. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participant observation, and document analysis, and were analyzed using thematic coding to identify patterns in principles, implementation, and impacts. The findings reveal that workforce practices operate through dual strategic orientations. First, they reinforce cultural continuity by embedding heritage values into daily work routines, facilitating intergenerational knowledge transfer, and maintaining standardized craftsmanship rooted in local traditions. Second, they enable outward expansion by integrating digital competencies, structured training systems, and adaptive planning to meet broader market demands and evolving consumer expectations. These dual orientations illustrate how enterprises balance authenticity preservation with innovation, allowing them to remain competitive without diluting cultural identity. Furthermore, the study highlights that workforce practices function not merely as operational mechanisms but as integrative systems linking cultural sustainability with economic resilience and organizational adaptability. The results suggest that heritage-based enterprises can achieve global readiness by aligning cultural values with capability development, institutional support, and technological adaptation. In addition, collaboration with external stakeholders, including government agencies and digital platforms, further strengthens market access and workforce capacity. This research contributes to the literature by conceptualizing workforce strategy as a culturally embedded and adaptive system that bridges local identity and international opportunity, offering practical insights for similar enterprises seeking sustainable growth, policy alignment, and cross-cultural competitiveness in an increasingly globalized economy. Title: The Landscape of Eco-Tourism in Rajasthan: Challenges and Prospects

Abstract: Eco-tourism is a type of tourism which has emerged out of a desire to move toward more sustainable forms. While combining economic and cultural development, at the same time caring for the environment. In Rajasthan, a state renowned for its culture and multi-locational landscapes, eco-tourism could very well lead to sustainable growth. The aim is to relieve over-tourism and environmental degradation. This paper provides an overview on contemporary trends in eco-tourism in Rajasthan, listing majors destinations such as Sariska Tiger Reserve, Keoladeo National Park and desert eco-camps. It discusses activities by local communities, government agencies and private companies in green tourism. Eco-tourism in Rajasthan has developed greatly, as the report shows. This was done despite a poor transport infrastructure, an unfuzzy attitude on the part of both townies and tourists, achieving a balance of environmental sustainability with the growth and use of eco-tourism and so forth other challenges. But there are also some fairly positive gaps that need to be filled. These gaps revolve around technological improvement for marketing purposes, local community participation in eco-tourism programs, a mechanism which gets revenue back into the hands of poor people and assistance provided to individual households in the marketing of handmade items. Potential trends like community-based tourism and digital marketing could further underpin eco-tourism in Rajasthan. Finally, the study ends and offers some attitudes with respect to how to promote eco-tourism in Rajasthan. Ways sit astride capacity building, awareness raising through education and social media and getting involved in businesses never before ventured into. It makes the point very clearly that in order to make eco-tourism happen for Rajasthan, one needs to bring in business people, planners and local people together. Title: Multi-model Data Warehouse for Multidimensional Analysis of Flavescence Dorée: Application to the Bordeaux Region

Title: All Eyes on the Workflow: Automated and Efficient Event Discovery from Video Streams
Abstract: Disciplines such as business process management and process mining aid organizations by discovering insights about processes on the basis of recorded event data. Title: SLM-Driven Schema Evolution for IoT Data Streams

Abstract: Data schemas in Internet of Things (IoT) environments change constantly as devices are updated, vendors migrate APIs, and business requirements shift, yet downstream pipelines are expected to keep running without interruption. Title: Proprietary Software Licensing Models: History, Evolution and Trends

Abstract: Proprietary software licensing models have undergone significant transformations over the years, driven by technological advances and changing market demands. This article reviews this evolution using narrative review methodology, highlighting the key developments and comparing different models. Title: OpenCert for AI Act: A Capability-Based Framework for Trustworthy AI in Critical Infrastructures

Title: A RAG-Based Pipeline for Automated COSMIC Functional Size Measurement
Abstract: Functional size measurement is essential for reliable software project management. While automation of the COSMIC method (ISO 19761) has long enabled large-scale application in industry, the rise of Large Language Models combined with Retrieval-Augmented Generation offers new opportunities for further advancement. This paper presents CosmoScope, a RAG-based pipeline for automating COSMIC functional size measurement that builds a structured knowledge base from five richly annotated official COSMIC case studies, applies domain-aware contextual prefixing based on Anthropic’s Contextual Retrieval technique, and dynamically retrieves relevant examples during inference. Title: Classification of Postal Distribution Centres
Abstract: This work was conducted in the context of industrial mathematics, in partnership with CTT-Correios de Portugal, S.A., highlighting the strong link between academia and the business world. It addresses the classification of Postal Distribution Centres using multivariate statistical methods combined in a less common way. First, a correlation analysis was conducted on the variables selected for the study, revealing several statistically significant associations. To mitigate collinearity, Principal Component Analysis was applied to derive uncorrelated components, which were then used as inputs to Cluster Analysis. Both hierarchical and partitional clustering methods were applied, and solution quality was assessed using graphical inspection, silhouette coefficients, and within- and between-cluster sums of squares. Ward’s method, k-means, and k-medoids produced consistent and similar groupings; in this paper, the k-means results are considered. Linear Discriminant Analysis and Multinomial Logistic Regression were used to assign new Postal Distribution Centres to the previously identified groups. The second classifier was used to corroborate the classification results obtained by LDA, since some LDA assumptions are violated and one of the clusters is small. The classification results from both methods showed a high degree of agreement. To avoid inflated accuracy caused by using the same data throughout all stages of the pipeline (standardisation, PCA, CA, LDA/MLR), the leave-one-out cross-validation method was applied across the entire pipeline, rather than only at the classification stage. Title: Integrated Payroll Management System Based on Cloud Computing and Microservice Architecture

Abstract: Issues associated with the current enterprise payroll management are fragmentation of data, lengthy processing time, and the ability to handle multi-departmental cooperation and dynamic human resource scheduling, and these issues make it challenging to meet the requirements of multi-departmental cooperation and dynamic human resource scheduling. The system uses a containerized deployment, where functional modules like the calculation of salaries, verification of salaries, files of employees and performance evaluation are split into various microservices; This article uses the dynamic scheduling of components between components by using the service registration and load balancing between components. It employs cloud database clusters to ensure that there is consistency of data and real time backup with high concurrency accesses and provides a Role Based Access Control (RBAC) model to provide security of data. Title: Critical Success Factors for AI Adoption: A Multivocal Literature Review and a Top Management Perspective

Abstract: The strategic adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a critical determinant of competitive advantage, yet organizations face high failure rates. This paper aims to identify and categorize the Critical Success Factors (CSFs) that influence successful AI adoption by synthesizing academic and practitioner knowledge from a top-management perspective. We conducted a multivocal literature review of 57 academic and 20 practitioner sources, screened per PRISMA. From vote-count synthesis we identified 16 CSFs grouped via the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, with organizational factors dominating such as leadership support, AI literacy, and cultural readiness. Title: Does concentrated ownership structure affect ESG disclosure? Role of corporate life cycle and market competition
Abstract: Using a sample of Indian listed firms, this study examines the role of concentrated ownership structure in shaping firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure. We find concentrated ownership has a significant negative impact on ESG disclosure, and the result is more prominent in the case of domestic, family, and state ownership. ESG disclosure is considered to enhance information symmetry and transparency, and the results reveal the role of concentrated ownership, including domestic, family, and state ownership, in limiting transparency. In contrast, foreign and institutional ownership positively impact ESG disclosure, indicating their monitoring role and preference for transparency. Next, we highlight the mediating role of audit quality between concentrated ownership types and ESG disclosure. We also find concentrated ownership negatively impacts ESG disclosure in low market competition and mature product life cycle stages but positively impacts when it interacts with business group affiliation. We also show that ESG disclosure reduces the cost of debt and financing constraints to firms, but concentrated ownership reduces ESG disclosure, highlighting the trade-off preference for concentrated owners between short-term control benefits and long-term value losses. Finally, we show that the results are robust at various robustness checks, including alternative variables, instrumental variables, entropy balancing and propensity score matching. Showing the varying opacity and transparency preferences among different concentrated owner types, the study offers valuable insights to investors, regulators and broader stakeholders. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Instructional Design in Process Modelling: Surveying Educators’ Perspectives
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing

Title: Collective identity, organizational commitment, and environmental conservation: An integrated model for U.S. hotels
Abstract: The study tests a new approach to linking collective environmental identity (CEI) and high organizational identity (HOI) to environmental conservation through affective, normative, and continuance commitment. Title: Talent, Compensation and Productivity: Workforce Dynamics in Shared Service Centres in Slovakia
Source title: Lecture Notes on Data Engineering and Communications Technologies
Abstract: We examine how compensation relates to productivity in Shared Services Centres (SSCs) amid digital transformation and COVID-19. Using FinStat database for 32 Slovak SSCs (2013–2022), we calculate compensation per employee, value-added productivity per employee, and revenue-based productivity per employee. SSCs are classified as per their current hiring strategy as Hiring, Stable, or Downsizing via three-year average headcount change (±8%). We compare pre-COVID (2013–2019) and post-COVID (2020–2022) periods. Three results emerge: (1) Hiring SSCs start with lower employee compensation, accelerate wages after 2016, and show a sustained rise in revenue-based productivity up to 2022; post-COVID dispersion roughly doubles, implying uneven returns to digital investment. (2) Stable SSCs pay the most and sustain high value-added productivity but show muted growth in revenue-based productivity, consistent with centralisation and capability-driven efficiency rather than revenue intensity. (3) Downsizing SSCs pay lowest compensation yet record high revenue per head at the median and upper quartile, consistent with portfolio pruning and a retained high-performing core; a post-2020 rise in value-added productivity suggests restructuring/selection effects. Divergences between value-added and revenue-based measures underscore pricing and client-mix influences versus internal process efficiency. We provide time-varying evidence from Slovak setting on when higher pay aligns with higher productivity. Limitations include a single-country perspective, descriptive design and no parent-company benchmarks. Future work could therefore add parent company comparisons, broader coverage, stronger identification, and additional performance metrics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Building a Service Ecosystem Through the Metaverse

Abstract: This paper develops a conceptual and empirically illustrated framework for constructing a service ecosystem through the metaverse by integrating servitization and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). Title: Artificial Intelligence for the Sustainable Development Goals: Corporate Opportunities and Ethical Dilemmas a Qualitative Meta-Analysis
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: In the current landscape, artificial intelligence (AI) is no longer an option but a necessity for businesses. These organizations emerge as key players in the deployment of AI to support the achievement of the sustainable development goals (SDGs). Thus, their capacity to design, finance, and disseminate digital solutions positions them as pivotal agents in accelerating both digital and ecological transitions. This paper aims to provide a structured and practice-oriented synthesis of the literature on the role of AI in supporting corporate contributions to the SDGs by identifying the key opportunities and ethical dilemmas discussed in peer-reviewed research. To this end, a qualitative meta-analysis was conducted on articles indexed in the Scopus database between 2015 and 2025 by mobilizing IRAMUTEQ 0.7 Alpha2, NVivo 12 and Rayyan, we performed text mining and qualitative content analysis to extract and classify relevant contributions. Our findings suggest that corporate AI-related opportunities are mainly associated with operational efficiency, innovation, sustainability performance measurement, and data-driven decision-making, yet they remain marginal compared to broader sustainability discussions. However, AI adoption raises notable challenges, such as data governance issues, organizational resistance, risks of greenwashing and skills constraints. In this regard, our analysis reveals a real empirical gap and lack of field-based studies focusing on how companies operationalize AI to support the SDGs. This gap invites future research to explore these opportunities and challenges through empirical, corporate-level studies that demonstrate how AI can effectively help companies in achieving the SDGs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Xu G.; Kang N.; Zhou X.
Title: More than regulation: How policy mixes shape innovation ecosystems in digital transformation
Abstract: The era of digital transformation drives the continuous restructuring of innovation ecosystems, challenging regulators to move beyond conventional regulations to address market and system failures. Although policy mixes are essential to address these challenges and promote innovation ecosystems, the efficacy of specific policy mix characteristics remains underexplored. This study develops a conceptual model to explore the mechanisms through which policy mix characteristics affect firm innovation in the digital transformation era. Specifically, we conceptualize policy mix coordination across three dimensions: temporal (policy stability over time), horizontal (policy similarity across regions), and vertical (policy coherence and complementarity between central and local governments). Firm innovation is examined through firms' technological and business positions within the innovation ecosystem. We conduct an empirical study of Chinese listed companies (2001-2021), employing machine learning techniques to identify policy themes, multi-source heterogeneous network analysis to measure firm innovation, and panel regression to test hypotheses. Results show that temporal and horizontal coordination stimulate firms' technological positions but inhibit business positions, whereas vertical coordination significantly enhances firms' technological positions within innovation ecosystems. Title: Paradoxical Psychology in disability entrepreneurship
Abstract: Social exclusion and constraint shape how individuals with disabilities mobilize psychological dispositions and resources, calling for a perspective on disability entrepreneurship that departs from mainstream entrepreneurship research. This study compares entrepreneurs and non-entrepreneurs with disabilities to examine these distinct motivational dynamics. The findings reveal a paradoxical structure: entrepreneurial self-efficacy is negatively associated with entrepreneurial motivation, whereas self-stigma and resilience are negatively associated with self-efficacy yet positively associated with motivation. These dynamics also differ by entrepreneurial status. These patterns may be interpreted in terms of constraint-induced and adaptive motivational pathways. The findings suggest that disability entrepreneurship may constitute a contextual boundary condition for prevailing theories of entrepreneurial motivation and position resilience as a context-dependent rather than uniformly beneficial resource. Title: Participatory Process Mining: A Framework and Call for Research
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Process mining is used to create transparency about organizational work by analyzing event data from business processes. Although such transparency is often assumed to be inherently beneficial, the dominant strand is that transparency is imposed “top-down”. Decision-makers and developers initiate and direct process mining initiatives, while those performing the work have hardly any say. This can be problematic, not least because transparency can lead to perceived surveillance, misrepresentation, and resistance on the side of workers. We propose a conceptual framework that distinguishes the levels (data, tool, organizational) at which participation can be enabled across the process mining lifecycle, and the degrees of participation that can be realized at each level. Title: Harnessing Big Data for Sustainable Global Supply Chains: Challenges and Opportunities in Indonesia’s Export-Oriented Sectors

Title: Artificial intelligence and corporate environmental performance: The mediating role of green AI practices and green intellectual capital
Abstract: Despite widespread artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in corporate settings, mechanisms through which this technology translates into environmental performance remain unclear. This study examines how AI impacts corporate environmental performance through green AI practices and green intellectual capital dimensions. Integrating Resource-Based View, Knowledge-Based View, and Natural Resource-Based View, we develop and test a serial mediation model using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Data were collected from 265 key informants, including Chief Digital Officers, Chief Sustainability Officers and Corporate Social Responsibility Directors, in SBF 120 companies. Results reveal that AI operates primarily through serial mediation rather than direct effects, with 67.8% of the total effect transmitted through the serial mediators. AI adoption positively impacts green AI practices, which develop three green intellectual capital dimensions: human, relational, and structural capital. These dimensions contribute positively to environmental performance, with comparable magnitudes across the three dimensions. The model explains 60.1% of environmental performance variance. This research challenges the assumption that technology adoption alone drives environmental performance. By demonstrating serial mediation and revealing the theoretically consistent ordering of green intellectual capital dimensions, we show that organisations cannot purchase environmental performance through AI investments but must deliberately transform technology adoption into green practices and organisational capabilities. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Evaluation of Generative AI Tools for Process Modeling with Educational Purposes
Abstract: Process modeling is an important topic that has faced multiple advancements, as a result of its integration with artificial intelligence. This study includes an empirical experiment with engineering students, who worked on generating and refining BPMN diagrams using iterative prompts, to match ground-truth diagrams. Title: KGIA-Model: A Knowledge Graph-Driven Text-To-SQL Model for Intelligent Auditing

Abstract: Automated interpretation of regulatory documents is essential for realizing intelligent auditing. Leveraging the fine-tuned language model, it dynamically generates SQL queries that transform audit rules into executable operations. Title: COD-ssi: Enforcing Mutual Privacy for Credential Oblivious Disclosure in Self Sovereign Identity
Abstract: The Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) paradigm is instrumental for decentralised identity management, allowing an entity to create, manage, and present their digital credentials without relying on centralised authorities. Credential Selective Disclosure (SD) is one of the most attractive privacy-preserving features of SSI, allowing users to partially reveal information from their credentials. However, current SD mechanisms primarily focus on protecting Holders’ privacy, while credential Verifiers. Indeed, the specific information requested by a Verifier can inadvertently reveal sensitive information, including internal decision-making criteria, business rules, or strategic plans. In this work, we address this threat by proposing, to the best of our knowledge, the first approach enforcing mutual privacy in credential exchanges. To this end, we introduce COD-ssi (Credential Oblivious Disclosure for SSI), a novel framework that leverages Oblivious Pseudorandom Functions to allow credential selective access without revealing to the credential Holder which specific claims were requested. The security of our solution is formally verified and its feasibility is assessed through the experimental evaluation of our open-source prototype implementation, showing that provable mutual privacy in the context of SSI can be achieved with just moderate computational and communication overhead. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: What Do Process Embeddings Learn? A Probing Investigation
Abstract: Process representation learning transforms event data into numeric vectors, called embeddings, that machine learning models can use for downstream tasks like prediction, clustering, or anomaly detection. To support these tasks, the goal is to create general-purpose embeddings that encode all relevant data properties. However, embeddings are typically evaluated by downstream task performance, assessing only task-specific quality. Thus, it remains unclear which properties of the event data are encoded in the embeddings and how accessible they are, making it difficult to design, improve or compare task-agnostic general-purpose embeddings. To address this issue, we present a probing evaluation framework that investigates embeddings of process instances by training small classifiers, called probes, to recover predefined process properties. We define seven probing tasks, each dedicated to one property, ranging from simple ones, like duration, to more complex ones, like order relations. We apply the framework to embeddings from three existing representation learning approaches on synthetic and real-life event data. The results show that the embeddings reliably encode simple properties, but have difficulties with more complex ones. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models for End-to-End Diagram Recognition
Abstract: Graph-structured diagrams (GSD) are frequently used in documents to visualize processes or relationships in an easily understandable way for humans. Extracting the underlying information from the diagram images in a structured format is important for various downstream applications. We curate a publicly available dataset of 843 hand-drawn and machine-generated diagrams from related work covering flowcharts, business process modeling diagrams, and others. We evaluate the extractions with string matching against ground truth. Title: Online operating of photovoltaic–energy storage-charging and swapping stations in coordinated energy and regulation markets
Abstract: With the rapid and sustained growth of electric vehicles (EVs), integrated photovoltaic-energy storage-charging and swapping stations (PV-ES-CSSs) are emerging as a new business model that enhances station profitability while providing flexible resources for mitigating EV-induced grid impacts and promoting renewable energy accommodation. However, uncertainties in PV generation and EV charging/swapping demand, along with volatile real-time electricity prices, challenge the reliable and economic operation of PV-ES-CSSs. This paper proposes an online operation strategy for PV-ES-CSSs in a multi-market environment to maximize station revenue while ensuring operational feasibility under uncertainty. First, a state of charge (SOC)-consistency-based flexibility aggregation model is developed to quantify heterogeneous regulation capability and reduce station-level flexibility overestimation, providing a unified scheduling basis for coordinated participation in energy and regulation markets. Then, an opportunity value function model integrating supervised learning and dynamic programming is proposed to map the residual energy states of ES, charging EVs, and swapping batteries into future revenue, enabling coordinated optimization of immediate profits and future regulation potential. Furthermore, a geometric-water-filling-based power allocation strategy with urgency indicators is designed to decompose station-level dispatch commands online under different market conditions while ensuring service demand fulfillment and regulation response accuracy. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy satisfies real-time response requirements, and reduces flexibility overestimation by 4.81%. Compared with coordinated multi-market operation without considering future opportunity values, the proposed strategy increases the total revenue by 2.98%. Moreover, compared with the cases involving participation only in the energy market and only in the regulation market, the total revenue is increased by 176.84% and 2.37%, respectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Entrepreneurial bankruptcy as a career-sorting event: income trajectories, re-entry, and risk-taking
Abstract: Entrepreneurial bankruptcy is a salient failure event, yet little is known about its association with subsequent income trajectories and career paths. Using matched employer–employee data, we examine the income consequences of entrepreneurial bankruptcy and heterogeneity in post-bankruptcy careers among entrepreneurs operating incorporated firms. Bankruptcy is associated with persistent income losses on average, though this conceals pronounced heterogeneity. Entrepreneurs who do not re-enter experience significant income declines, whereas those who re-enter earn higher post-bankruptcy incomes. Re-entry is associated with higher revealed risk preferences, along with descriptively higher human capital and financial resources. Entrepreneurs who re-enter tend to operate ventures that grow faster but are more leveraged, less profitable, and more likely to fail again, consistent with higher-variance strategies. Overall, the findings show that entrepreneurial bankruptcy functions as a career-sorting mechanism in which post-failure outcomes reflect both selection into distinct career paths and systematic differences in subsequent strategic behavior. Title: From breakdown to breakthrough: How entrepreneurs craft vulnerability narratives on social media
Abstract: Entrepreneurial narratives are widely understood as strategic tools for building legitimacy and mobilizing resources. Yet we observed that some entrepreneurs openly share stories of fear, doubt, and struggle on social media - foregrounding emotional exposure rather than demonstrating strategic purpose. We conceptualize these as entrepreneurial vulnerability narratives: a distinct narrative form through which the lived consequences of entrepreneurial uncertainty are publicly shared and opened to social negotiation. These disclosures expose entrepreneurs to interpersonal risks, heightened for women entrepreneurs who contend with gendered biases and less supportive social contexts. To examine this phenomenon, we conducted interviews with 33 women entrepreneurs and a 21-month observation of their Instagram activity. Our analysis reveals that women entrepreneurs hold multiple and coexisting motivations for disclosure - self-oriented, relational, and normative - oscillating between them as needed, while developing narrative-crafting tactics that sustain the benefits of sharing while managing interpersonal risks. Our study contributes by theorizing entrepreneurial vulnerability narratives as a distinct narrative form; by challenging the view that entrepreneurial narratives serve primarily persuasive functions; and by showing how entrepreneurs actively construct precarious holding environments in fragmented digital contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Evaluating the Parallelization Capabilities of State-of-the-Art Agentic Large Language Models
Abstract: Advancements in large language models (LLMs), including base model improvements, various chain-of-thought approaches, and agentic tool use, have substantially increased their capacity for autonomous programming and software engineering. Their performance on such tasks is widely studied, tracked, and publicized; however, the majority of evaluations are based on Python, Java, or other high-level languages, with application domains in the web, business logic, or data analysis. From the perspective of parallel language, programming interface (API), and systems research in the field of high-performance computing (HPC), the question arises whether these results translate to the capability of effectively parallelizing applications. In order to answer this question, we design and carry out a comprehensive study, tasking 8 state-of-the-art LLM agents with the parallelization of 11 small-to-medium-sized HPC benchmark applications. For each, we evaluate shared-memory, distributed memory, accelerator, and hybrid parallelization goals with appropriate APIs, and multiple agent invocations are performed for every data point to quantify random variance in outcome quality. Our experimental setup includes validation in several steps, comprising semantic inspection, compilation, monitored execution, internal result checking, and external verification via known-good comparisons. For all valid programs, we also perform comparative performance benchmarking on a production supercomputer. We synthesize overall conclusions and quantify to what extent parallelization performance of LLMs correlates with time and tokens spent. Champions close the gap between big data and the rest of the organization by propagating the use of data and integrating latest analytics tools in how workers do their jobs. Title: Navigating Complexity in the Circular Economy: A Systems Perspective on Scotch Whisky

Abstract: Despite ambitious circular economy (CE) policies in Scotland, translating national commitments into effective industrial implementation remains a critical challenge. This study examines how Scotland’s emerging CE policies enable or constrain CE adoption within Scotch whisky - an industry characterized by export orientation, premium packaging, and untapped potential to valorize by-products. Our analysis reveals twelve interconnected feedback loops across three thematic domains: bio-based distilling resource circularity, product packaging circularity, and industry-wide knowledge-sharing dynamics. The findings demonstrate how operational priorities, brand heritage, and export-oriented business models create distinct barriers for the CE transition of Scotch whisky. Title: Reconceptualizing strategic partnerships islamic philanthropy networks in Indonesia
Abstract: This study aims to reconceptualize the framework of strategic partnerships within the Islamic philanthropy sector through an interdisciplinary integration of Strategic Partnership Theory, Network Theory, and General Systems Theory (GST). Employing a descriptive qualitative method with a conceptual approach based on systematic literature synthesis, this research analyzes contemporary literature on management and organizational theory to develop an original model that positions Islamic philanthropy as a holistic, interconnected, and dynamic ecosystem. The findings indicate that the effectiveness of strategic partnerships no longer relies on simple bilateral relationships, instead, it requires sophisticated multidimensional synchronization among the input (resource mobilization), process (digital transformation), and output (social impact) subsystems. A systemic analysis reveals that the integration of Maqasid al-Sharia serves as a critical regulatory parameter ensuring that collaboration among managing institutions, the fintech sector, the government, and the public leads to sustainable value co-creation. Socially, this model has the potential to accelerate equitable resource distribution and broader financial inclusion. Title: Knowledge Management Strategies in the Era of Algorithms and Data

Abstract: The study explores the integration of Knowledge Management (KM) and Human Resource Management (HRM) in the academic preparation of future managers in the digital era. The research was conducted among 126 students of the Staropolska Academy of Applied Sciences (StANS), representing three programs: Finance and Accounting, Marketing and E-Business, and Business Economics. A mixed-methods approach, based on methodological triangulation, was applied—combining quantitative analysis (survey, SPSS) and qualitative exploration (FGI, NVivo 14). The results demonstrate that awareness of KM–HRM integration varies by field of study. Marketing students display the highest knowledge orientation and digital awareness, Finance students show strong analytical skills but lower social understanding, while Economics students present a balanced, T-shaped profile. The chi-square test (χ2 = 7.82; p < 0.05) confirmed significant differences between groups, and a strong correlation (r = 0.64; p < 0.01) was found between digital competence and readiness to assume the role of a knowledge manager. Qualitative findings emphasized the importance of creativity, collaboration, and technology—particularly artificial intelligence—in effective knowledge management. The study confirms that KM is a strategic component of modern HRM systems and that future managers must integrate analytical, technological, and interpersonal skills to manage knowledge effectively. It recommends introducing interdisciplinary, project-based modules that combine HRM, KM, and digital transformation in higher education. Developing T-shaped competencies—analytical, communicative, and systemic—is identified as the key direction for managerial education in the knowledge-based economy. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: RAG Automation of COSMIC Functional Size Measurement Using Large Language Models

Abstract: Functional Size Measurement (FSM) methods, such as COSMIC (Common Software Measurement International Consortium), provide standardized techniques for software effort estimation and efficient project management. However, manual measurement of Natural Language (NL) requirements remains time-consuming, prone to human error, and subject to human interpretation biases. By injecting domain-specific COSMIC knowledge at inference time, the RAG-enhanced framework reduces this gap to 0.01, yielding more balanced performance across domains. Title: Is competition good or bad for employee innovation? Examining the double-edged sword effect of team and individual responses
Abstract: Amid an increasingly competitive environment, fostering innovation among employees has emerged as a central concern for both academia and the business community. Title: What Matters to Them? Generation Z and Their Expectations as Future Employees: A Research Path Towards Comparing Two Contexts
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The focus of this paper is on Generation Z (Gen Z), currently consisting of young people, as it is the latest generation that is entering the labor market. As other generations, Gen Z is distinguished by its characteristics, influencing their working behaviors. Yet, despite being called a global generation - as they share common elucidation that influences them worldwide - Gen Z do not share the same personal values and life experiences. This presents a challenge for researchers to reveal an insight into their differences regarding life values and work attitudes, for business endowment. The aim of this paper is to portray a research path for analyzing the differences related to life values and work attitudes of Generation Z in two different contexts of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Slovenia. Research opportunity is interesting nowadays, as two countries share deep interrelationship as part of intense changes in global work boundaries due to migration, as implies possible direction to human resource (HR) attraction and retention strategies, as well as multicultural and multigenerational management HR strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Patent-Market Correlations via Fuzzy Technology Transfer Analysis
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This paper presents an interpretable methodology to analyze Technology Transfer (TT) by combining Fuzzy Logic with t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE). The approach builds a “Technological Print”, i.e., a fuzzy vector that summarizes a firm’s technological orientation by matching patent abstracts and business filings. We analyze approximately 300 companies and over one million patents. t-SNE is used as an exploratory visualization tool to verify whether the resulting prints align with known market sectors. In the Technology sector, we observe a strong temporal correlation (R2=0.9594) between patent activity in the G16H (Healthcare Informatics) subclass and sectoral growth over 2000–2021. The contribution is an explainable correlation framework that supports strategic interpretation of patent-market relationships without relying on opaque embeddings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.
