Authors: Lakshmi K.; Revathy G.; Subha S.; Dhavamani L.
Title: FOCUS: hybrid secretary bird super fairy optimized customer segmentation in omni-channel environment
Abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid secretary bird super Fairy Optimized CUstomer Segmentation (FOCUS) approach has been proposed for accurate clustering and meaningful customer groups. Textual data is analyzed to extract lexical and keyword-based features, whereas transactional behaviors are captured through RFM scoring. The features are clustered using the hybrid Secretary Bird Super Fairy (SBSFO) optimization, in which Secretary Bird Optimization (SBO) uses global exploration and Super Fairy Wren Optimization (SFWO) uses local exploitation. This model segments customers into meaningful groups, including top customers, loyal buyers, and occasional or lost customers. This approach provides businesses with deeper behavioral insights and enhances targeted marketing strategies. The proposed approach achieves an SI of 0.77, whereas existing RFM-FCA, RFM-K-Medoids, and SONN achieve 0.61, 0.65, and 0.58, respectively. The proposed FOCUS method achieves a minimum DBI of 0.34, outperforming RFM-FCA at 0.57, RFM-K-Medoids at 0.51, and SONN at 0.60. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Model for the Assessment of Financial Reporting Quality in Contemporary Management
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The quality of financial information is a key assumption for making efficient business decisions. Assessing the quality of financial statements, as a complex non-financial aspect of information, requires consideration of several factors that influence their reliability and relevance. This paper analyzes the quality of financial statements based on the structure and oscillations of their elements, as well as through key financial and analytical indicators. The goal of the paper is the development of a model that enables a quick and simple assessment of the level of quality of financial statements and the level of confidence in the presented information, including the assessment of the probability of the existence of a significant substantive error. Empirical research was conducted on a sample of companies from Bosnia and Herzegovina whose securities were traded on the Sarajevo and Banja Luka Stock Exchanges for a period of 6 years, and the sample includes a total of 100 companies. The condition for the selection of the sample was the continuous six-year public publication of financial and audit reports. Binomial logistic regression was used for modeling, where the dependent variable is the quality of financial statements, and the independent variables are selected, characteristic elements of financial statements. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: AI-Driven Automation in Knowledge-Intensive License Management: An Empirical Analysis of Enterprise Constraints and Automation Potential
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Software License Management (SLM) is a complex, Knowledge-Intensive Process (KiP) in which fragmented data, heterogeneous IT landscapes, and frequent vendor audits contribute to significant process governance gaps, reducing organizational agility and increasing contractual and financial risk exposure. This study investigates the relationship between operational burden and contractual risk by examining SLM in the context of the Agentic Business Process Management (Agentic BPM) framework and the design–emergence gap. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was used, starting with a quantitative survey (N = 60) to establish three novel metrics: the Cost and Risk Exposure Index (CREI), the Operational Burden and Visibility Index (OBVI), and the Automation Readiness and Demand Index (ARDI). These quantitative findings were refined through twelve semi-structured interviews with senior IT and license managers. The findings reveal that traditional rule-based systems fail to address the dynamic nature of license governance, leaving the SLM undermanaged despite growing financial exposure. To bridge the design–emergence gap, this study presents three process governance-oriented design principles for Agentic BPM: lifecycle visibility, cross-functional coordination, and human-in-the-loop oversight. The study concludes with a proposal for a cross-functional process governance framework that shifts the focus from rigid task automation to a lifecycle-oriented agentic oversight model, thus enhancing audit readiness and supporting the development of process-oriented governance capabilities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Simulation-Based Data Generation for On-Demand Bus-as-a-Service Analytics
Abstract: On-demand mobility systems, such as bus services, are gaining importance due to their role in sustainable urban transport. Their flexible and context-specific nature poses challenges for planning, optimization, and performance evaluation, particularly due to the scarcity of related operational data needed to support data-driven decision-making. This work is motivated by a real-world Bus-as-a-Service (BaaS) project, where the lack of available data limited the development of analytical tools. To address this gap, this paper proposes an artifact for the generation of event data (i.e., operational data) related to an on-demand bus service. Thus, the main contributions of this paper include the artifact tailored for on-demand bus services, but also the methodology that was followed for this instantiation. The purpose is that such methodology can be replicated in other cases to generate synthetic data. Without access to real data and without the possibility of gathering data from an existing on-demand bus service, the first step consisted of gathering customers’ requirements and analyzing similar business models, resulting in the definition of an Entity-Relationship Diagram that allowed us to identify the data that needed to be generated by the artifact. This artifact simulates the required operational processes, capturing critical elements such as passenger requests, vehicle routing, and other service constraints. The results show that this artifact produces valid simulations for multiple scenarios and enables the generation of structured datasets that meet predefined analytical requirements. Thus, the obtained datasets can be consumed by data-driven analytics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Impact of Agile and Hybrid Methodologies on Fintech Software Project Outcomes
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Burnt by the lightning-fast pace of the digital transformation of the global fintech industry, the need to establish software development practices that can deliver all three, i.e., speed, quality, and regulatory compliance, has become more urgent. Although the method of Agile and hybrid project management is quite popular in fintech software development, the literature is dispersed and focused mainly on the qualitative study, and there is little empirical validation at the industry-specific level. Specifically, both large-scale quantitative comparisons between pure Agile and hybrid approaches to development in the context of a regulated fintech space and longitudinal information on its long-term effectiveness in terms of project outcomes are wanting. The study will be a systematic effort to study how agile and hybrid approaches affect the performance of software projects in the world fintech sector. By concentrating on such key performance indicators as delivery efficiency, software quality, stakeholder satisfaction, risk management, and alignment, the study considers the critical enablers with the usage of a structured empirical approach. The research design will be a combination of cross-organizational information of the fintech projects implemented over the past years and will allow drawing comparisons based on the methodological paradigm and organizational dimensions. This study aims to achieve this by providing evidence-based observation to the academic and business communities by setting quantifiable links between the development methodologies and project performance measurements. It is anticipated that the findings will assist in making informed decisions because fintech organizations under regulatory pressure will be faced with methodological choices, and also, the findings will enhance the theoretical conception towards hybrid agility in the complex and compliance-driven software ecosystems. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Singh G.P.

Title: Institutionalization in Consumption Meets Improvisation: A Case Exemplar Approach
Source title: Contributions to Environmental Sciences and Innovative Business Technology
Abstract: Consumption does not arise from a single cause (e.g., a campaign), but rather from an interplay of multiple internal and external drivers, including psychological, social, cultural, affective, and cognitive factors. These factors are embedded in consumers’ personalities, immediate surroundings, and situational contexts. Their relationship makes consumers’ lives and decision-making a complex matter that even the most comprehensive marketing guidance can only partially anticipate. Although firms provide product guidance and brand narratives to help consumers navigate this complexity, it is during the usage episode that consumers improvise their practices. While improvisation is typical in consumption episodes, it is usually inadequately acknowledged. Using an interpretive paradigm, the paper employs case studies to elucidate how consumption practices lead to improvisations. We examine how consumer-led improvisation thrives outside the institutionalized consumption norms. We note that consumers oscillate between following and bending institutional guidance, and the previously untapped “value pockets” become available. A conceptual framework is proposed to illustrate the interconnectedness of institutionalized and improvised consumption. Thus, the framework sheds light on their mechanisms and outcomes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Authors: Chen L.; Zhou D.; Shohrab M.; Tao X.; Hao L.; Ma T.; Yu D.
Title: Tensor-TimesFM: High-Dimensional Sparse Time Series Forecasting with Tensor Decoders and Latent Dynamics Prediction
Abstract: Time-series forecasting in business domains—such as markets, finance, and the broader economy—is challenging due to sparsity, high cross-sectional dimensionality, and temporal skewness with short or irregular histories. These issues cause standard forecasting algorithms to perform poorly. We address these challenges with two key innovations: tensor reconstruction and forecasting in a latent factor space. Tensor-TimesFM couples low-rank tensor completion with a pretrained foundation model applied to latent factors. The tensor component leverages low-rank techniques to denoise and impute at scale, while the foundation model utilizes its strong generalization and zero-shot capabilities to model temporal dynamics. Together, they transform the cross-sectional prediction task into a standard tensor reconstruction problem. We further introduce a regularizer that promotes decorrelation among the generated latent factors and aligns with current foundation models designed for univariate time series. On sparse EPS data, Tensor-TimesFM improves over Tensor-GRU, reducing up to 35.2% forecast error and improving out-of-sample R2 by 39.8%. Code is available at https://github.com/LarryC01/Tensor-TimesFM-ECML-2026. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Deep Learning and IoT Framework Using Dark Net-Based CNN for Automated Papaya Growth Monitoring and Yield Prediction
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The tropical fruit papaya is excellent for business. From early development until ripening, monitor its development for the optimum production and quality. Traditional and present Internet of things (IoT)-deep learning (DL) systems for papaya growth monitoring have several issues. Because they lack preprocessing and employ broad model designs, they are hard to use, do not operate well in varied situations, and are inaccurate. Many models do not react quickly and rely on human observation, which costs resources and delays decisions. A novel IoT-based Dark Net Convolutional Neural Network (IoT-DNetCNN) approach for Papaya Growth Tracking and Productivity Enhancement was established to overcome these limits. The IOT-DNetCNN model constantly takes papaya photos using ESP32-CAM modules. Video frames and cloud-based semantic analysis are used. Gabor filtering normalizes and finds, and a hybrid DarkNet-19 convolutional neural network extracts features. The Python-based IOT-DNetCNN model can identify papaya ripeness and predict yield using regression. The proposed model has a high accuracy (0.98), low MAE (0.02), and low RMSE (0.14). Overall, in classification and regression it performed better than benchmark models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Fonger F.; Koschmider A.
Author full names: Fonger, Frederik (58298028400); Koschmider, Agnes (13605575800)
Title: Respecting Object Relationships: An Object-Centric Sampling Algorithm
Abstract: Recently, object-centric process mining has emerged as a new process mining direction that places the relationships among multiple data objects at the center, with the Object-Centric Event Log (OCEL) serving as the standard exchange format. OCEL can contain a high volume of events and complex object relationships. Particularly, the size of real-life OCELs presents a challenge for conformance checking, hindering the scalability. This makes it necessary to extract representative subsets of the log for analysis purposes, thereby calling for appropriate sampling algorithms. Currently, only random sampling exists to allow for scalability. However, it disregards dependencies between multiple objects and therefore does not produce reliable conformance checking results. Thus, it cannot be considered as an appropriate sampling strategy. To overcome this, we propose the sampling algorithm RP-OCEL that incorporates object relationships, while reducing the size of the OCEL. RP-OCEL applies weighting according to the connectivity of object types and selects only object types that exhibit below a connectivity score, while the final sample still contains all object types. We applied our approach on a well-known OCEL dataset and compared it to random sampling. The results show that, in contrast to random sampling, RP-OCEL is suited for conformance checking, can perform sampling without altering the objects associated with an event and can significantly reduce processing time. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Yin C.; Zhao L.
Title: Leadership succession and corporate social responsibility in family firms
Abstract: This study investigates the impact of CEO succession on corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance in family firms. Drawing on socioemotional wealth perspective, we argue that CEO succession creates tension between financial accountability and non-financial objectives as successors seek to establish legitimacy and maintain organizational stability. During this period, successors are likely to prioritize financial accountability, organizational continuity, and family control, reducing attention to reputational objectives maintained through CSR. We further propose that external pressures, including peer firms’ CSR practices and media attention, moderate this relationship by increasing the legitimacy costs of reducing CSR engagement. Using data from Chinese family firms, we find that CSR performance declines significantly one to two years after succession. This negative relationship is stronger when external pressure is weak but is mitigated, and may even reverse, under stronger peer and media pressures. Our findings demonstrate how family firms balance financial and non-financial objectives during leadership transitions. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Silent Responsibility Voids: Evidence for Process Twins in Clinical Trials
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Responsible Business Process Management (RBPM) and process mining have matured as independent research streams, yet their integration on real operational data remains rare, particularly in clinical research, where responsibility obligations are most consequential. This study investigates the protocol deviation management process of Clinical Research Centers (CRCs) using an event log of 13,331 deviation cases from an operational clinical trial management system, complemented by a formative expert evaluation with specialists from contrasting roles and regulatory contexts. Applying process discovery, conformance, and performance analysis, it finds that the most critical responsibility tensions surface less in what the process records than in what it fails to record. We introduce the concept of Silent Responsibility Voids (SRVs): points where the operationalization of an RBPM principle leaves no auditable trace, manifesting as absence, systematic incompleteness, or ceremonial recording. In the studied data, corrective action is documented in 0.1% of cases, regulatory notifications are largely absent, and the typical deviation is registered a median of 153 days after it occurred. We argue that such voids are detectable only by a technology that carries the normative expectation of the process, and use them to specify the monitoring functions a Responsible Digital Process Twin would require. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Carney R.W.; Lu J.; Zhang H.
Title: Authoritarian capitalism and foreign investment
Abstract: A core determinant of firms’ international investment decisions is the ability of host-country political institutions to reduce policy uncertainty. While prior research has focused largely on formal constraints within democracies, this paper introduces a novel theoretical framework that reclassifies all political regimes −- democratic and authoritarian −-based on the protections they provide to private capital. This approach allows us to differentiate countries that appear similar under existing measures of executive constraint but vary widely in their institutional treatment of investors. Using firm-level foreign direct investment data, we show that this regime classification significantly improves predictions of investment patterns. Our results reveal that semi-competitive authoritarian regimes attract more investment than their non-competitive authoritarian counterparts, underscoring the importance of moving beyond democracy-centric frameworks when assessing political risk. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: Application of Artificial Intelligence Tools in Modern Auditing
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Modern auditing is being transformed and taking on new dimensions with the development of artificial intelligence (AI). Globally, practices that apply AI tools in control testing, detection of irregularities, and processing of unstructured data have already been developed and proven highly successful, indicating both the need and significant potential for introducing such practices in audit firms in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The advantages of using AI tools in auditing are reflected in increased accuracy in data verification necessary for forming an audit opinion, faster generation of reports, more efficient analysis of large datasets, automation of routine tasks, and quicker identification of irregularities that indicate business areas requiring more detailed examination. This paper presents primary research conducted on a sample of audit professionals with the aim of examining their perceptions regarding the use of AI. The defined sample consists of 126 respondents who answered 40 survey questions. In addition to professionals from Bosnia and Herzegovina, the research also includes, to a lesser extent, professionals from Serbia and Slovenia, enabling a clearer overview of both the current situation and the potential for the application of AI in auditing. The research conclusions were drawn using appropriate statistical methodologies applied to primary descriptive scales, which enable the measurement of the impact and interrelationships of respondents’ attitudes, thereby ensuring an adequate assessment of perceptions regarding the methods and effects of AI usage in auditing. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Assessing Technological Barriers of Blockchain Adoption in the Energy Sector Using AHP for Group Decision-Making
Source title: Advances in Science, Technology and Innovation
Abstract: After its implementation in cryptocurrencies, blockchain, a Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT), has attracted the attention of researchers in various sectors, while its potential use cases have been explored in a number of fields. As far as the energy sector is concerned, blockchain could enable decentralised electricity and carbon trading, effective energy management of complex systems with high penetration of renewables, coordination of energy storage units and electric vehicle charging, and secure data storage of energy-related data generated by metering infrastructure, among other applications. However, several technical issues hinder the wide-spread adoption of DLT in the energy field, such as scalability and speed constraints, poor performance, as well as security threats. In this paper, the most prominent technological barriers of blockchain adoption in energy services are recognised and assessed. The barriers are ranked, using a Multicriteria Decision Analysis method, the Analytical Hierarchy Process for Group Decision-Making. The findings of the research provide useful insight in the EU funded project InEExS (Innovative Energy (Efficiency) Service Models for Sector Integration via Blockchain), which is going to apply blockchain technology in specific energy-related business cases. The final ranked list of technical constraints could be a useful guide for any market actors interested in overcoming barriers to integrate blockchain technology in energy applications. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: PIM.3: A Hidden Accelerator Behind ASPICE Level 3 Success

Abstract: The indispensable role of the Process Improvement Process (PIM.3) in developing and maintaining organizational standard processes—and thereby enabling smoother deployment of these processes into projects—has become a key focus area across the automotive industry. Increasingly, car manufacturers expect projects to achieve ASPICE Level 3, which requires teams to begin with mature, ready-to-use process artifacts that accelerate product development and reduce time-to-market pressure. In this paper, members of the SoQrates initiative, representing major automotive organizations, present the relationship between ASPICE Level 3 and PIM.3, citing practical examples and best practices for aligning process improvements with business goals. Title: Bargaining never stops: Post-entry bargaining in decentralized emerging markets
Abstract: This study examines how multinational enterprises (MNEs) bargain with host-country stakeholders after market entry as they expand their operations across decentralized emerging markets characterized by multiple layers of government and influential non-state actors. Drawing on a longitudinal case study of a global MNE with 24 extractive sites across Indonesia, we show that post-entry bargaining requires continuous engagement with multiple layers of government over permits and regulations, as well as with local communities over employment, land and environmental impacts to avoid social unrest. In one region, community opposition forced the MNE to exit, despite substantial sunk costs, demonstrating that formal permits and government support cannot substitute for a social license to operate. We find that post-entry bargaining under institutional complexity requires cross-level strategies that address tensions across government and community levels. These strategies generate spillovers, allowing MNEs to alleviate tensions beyond their intended target. We thus demonstrate that foreign investment is shaped not only by national governments, but also by subnational authorities and communities who play a direct and often decisive role in shaping the terms and success of investments. © 2026 The Authors.

Abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into Business Intelligence is often hampered by context limits and hallucinations when processing raw data. This paper proposes a hybrid framework that integrates unsupervised clustering with Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) to analyze the 2025 Portuguese Legislative Elections. Title: Turning Inward and/or Outward: Which socioemotional skills pay for agribusiness entrepreneurs in Nigeria?
Abstract: Socioemotional skills programs are widely used to promote economic empowerment, yet their returns may depend on the type of skills targeted and social context. We study this question using a randomized controlled trial (RCT) among 4,500 aspiring agribusiness entrepreneurs in Nigeria within a large-scale government program. Participants were randomly assigned to an interpersonal-skills curriculum, a combined interpersonal and intrapersonal-skills curriculum of the same length, or a control group. Both trainings substantially increase women's business performance, raising average profits by 50%. The two trainings generated broadly similar economic impacts overall. Effects are largest in communities with more liberal gender norms, where women report improvements in interpersonal skills such as empathy and negotiation, and better relational outcomes. Despite large economic gains, we find no corresponding increases in women's empowerment or intrahousehold decision-making. For men, interpersonal-skills training increases household income, while the combined curriculum raises profits but only in the most gender-liberal environments. The results show that the returns to socioemotional skills programs depend not only on which skills are taught, but also on whether prevailing social norms permit individuals to express and deploy those skills. Title: BACHunter: An Automated Fuzzing Framework for Discovering Broken Access Control Vulnerabilities in Java Web Applications
Abstract: Broken Access Control (BAC) remains one of the most critical security threats in Java Web applications. Existing automated analysis techniques often struggle with the complex business logic and execution overhead inherent in these sys-tems. To the best of our knowledge, we present BACHunter, the first fuzzing-based framework designed for discovering BAC vulnerabilities in Java Web applications. BACHunter combines an in-memory service dispatcher to elimi-nate network-induced performance bottlenecks, a hierarchical mutation engine to systematically explore diverse authorization scenarios, and an entity-centric dif-ferential oracle for precise vulnerability verification. We evaluated BACHunter on a benchmark of 15 representative CVEs drawn from real-world open-source projects. Title: GNN4PPM: Multi-Target Predictive Process Monitoring with Relational Graph Convolutional Networks
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) aims at predicting at runtime and as early as possible the future states of a process execution. Common tasks include predicting the next event, the time to completion of a trace, and outcomes. Existing approaches typically consider an event from the perspective of the executed activities along with their timestamps and case identifiers. This leads to the disadvantage that in real-life settings, there is much more information recorded in the event log that is not captured or completely ignored when performing prediction tasks. We introduce GNN4PPM, an approach that predicts all next events along with their complete data payload at once. We represent event information in a heterogeneous knowledge graph that captures the event log as an RDF semantics, and train the embeddings with a Relational Graph Convolutional Network (R-GCN). Our approach is promising in comparison to existing solutions, and experiments with state-of-the-art solutions prove the accuracy and applicability of GNN4PPM in complex settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Continuity Matters: Improving Predictive Process Monitoring Based on Path Coherence
Abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring aims to forecast the future behavior of ongoing cases based on historical event log data. It is well established that predictive performance suffers when models treat cases and events as strictly isolated entities. While various approaches have attempted to integrate operational context to mitigate this limitation, the social dynamics in and around organizational processes have not been addressed in depth. We address this gap by drawing on research from the organizational science, specifically on research around organizational routines and operational friction. Specifically, we focus on the coordination friction and delays introduced when the execution context–such as the assigned resource or physical location–changes between consecutive events. This paper incorporates the concept of path coherence to explicitly quantify this situational continuity, as well as the friction that occurs when continuity breaks. We adapt this concept to event logs by engineering path coherence as an event-level feature and integrating it into a prediction pipeline based on Long Short-Term Memory models. Two variants are proposed: a resource-based coherence feature capturing responsibility handoffs and an all-attribute variant reflecting broader situational change. Using eight real-world event logs, we compare coherence-based feature sets with benchmark feature sets. The results show that coherence-based feature sets consistently reduce Mean Absolute Error, yielding statistically significant, mostly medium effect sizes, and that resource-based coherence explains the majority of the predictive performance gains. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: From Implementation to Impact: Technology Acceptance, Absorptive Capacity, and the Productivity Paradox of Cashless Payment Systems
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: This study investigates how the implementation of cashless payment systems translates into organizational outcomes through the mediating roles of technology acceptance and absorptive capacity. Drawing on the productivity paradox literature, we argue that digital payment systems do not generate performance gains automatically; instead, their effects depend on post-implementation organizational processes. Using survey data collected from 266 firms in the retail and trading sectors, we tested a research model that links cashless payment implementation to supply-side and demand-side outcomes via technology acceptance and absorptive capacity. The results of covariance-based structural equation modeling reveal that while advanced implementation enhances technology acceptance, it does not directly increase absorptive capacity. Technology acceptance positively influences absorptive capacity and supply-side outcomes, whereas demand-side outcomes are shaped primarily by absorptive capacity and prior operational improvements. These findings indicate that the benefits of cashless payment systems emerge in a sequential and non-synchronous manner, highlighting the limitations of evaluating digital transformation initiatives based solely on short-term or single performance indicators. By integrating technology acceptance and absorptive capacity into a unified model, this study extends cashless payment research beyond adoption and provides a process-based explanation of the productivity paradox in contemporary digital transformation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: The Role of Explainable AI in Enhancing Investment Decisions and Risk Management in Financial Markets
Abstract: Financial markets are becoming increasingly complex, creating an urgent demand for transparent and reliable decision-support systems. This study investigates the role of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in enhancing investment decision-making and risk management between 2020 and 2025. The analysis focuses on four dimensions: reducing decision-making time, mitigating financial risks, improving the quality of investment choices, and strengthening investor confidence. Secondary data from official reports and industry case studies were analyzed using paired T-tests, Value at Risk (VaR) comparisons, Sharpe and Sortino ratios, and regression models. The results demonstrate that decision-making time was significantly reduced after the adoption of XAI, showing its capacity to accelerate execution without compromising accuracy. Portfolio stability improved as indicated by lower VaR levels, while risk-adjusted returns, measured by Sharpe and Sortino ratios, showed significant gains, confirming better investment outcomes. Investor confidence was also positively linked to interpretability, underscoring the importance of transparency in fostering trust. Collectively, these findings position XAI as a catalyst for efficiency, stability, and trust in financial markets, while future research should extend the analysis to emerging markets and explore alternative interpretability methods. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Abstract: High-quality reviews reveal consumer satisfaction with product attributes and greatly affect the decisions of others. Title: How does China's unilateral visa-free policy affect its international aviation market? empirical evidence on passenger volume, flight frequency, and airfare
Source title: Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice
Abstract: China introduced a unilateral visa-free policy in late 2023 as part of its broader effort to restore international mobility and support post-pandemic economic reopening. The policy grants ordinary passport holders from selected countries visa-free entry to China for short stays, thereby reducing travel frictions and potentially stimulating inbound tourism and business travel. Against this background, this study examines how China's unilateral visa-free policy has shaped the recovery and structural evolution of its international aviation market. Using route-level data from January 2023 to March 2025, we apply a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) framework to identify policy-induced changes in passenger volume, flight frequency, and airfare. The empirical results show that the policy substantially increases international passenger volume and flight frequencies. Airfares rise in the short term following the policy change, but this increase fades over time. Heterogeneity analyses further uncover substantial variation across regional markets and routes departing from Chinese airports with different levels of slot constraints. Specifically, on European routes, capacity expansion is driven primarily by the deployment of larger aircraft, whereas on Asian routes it is achieved mainly through increased flight frequency. Moreover, estimated airfare effects are positive on routes serving more slot-constrained airports and negative on routes serving less constrained airports, consistent with differences in the flexibility of capacity adjustment. These findings offer nuanced insights into the joint responses of passenger traffic, airline capacity, and airfares to visa facilitation, providing actionable guidance for airline capacity optimization and strategic aviation policy design. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: An Enhanced System Usability Scale for Evaluating Organizational Systems with Database and Knowledge Management Components

Abstract: When designing organizational systems, usability evaluation is crucial to show that the system is efficient to complete tasks and that the user is satisfied and can process information effectively. The results show that the proposed Enhanced SUS framework could provide more comprehensive usability information than traditional SUS, as organizational usability attributes related to the management of information and database-supported environments have been added. Title: Mapping and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions from urban sewer networks in China
Abstract: Urban underground sewer network is the backbone of modern cities, yet its role in global urban carbon metabolism remains a critical blind spot. Here, we establish a bottom-up, province-level accounting framework integrating multi-source socio-environmental datasets to quantify sewer-related greenhouse gas emissions across China's 30 provinces from 2010 to 2023, with projections to 2060 under five mitigation scenarios. The framework disaggregates emissions into five categories, namely leakage, in-sewer CH4 from gravity sewers and rising mains, N2O generation, and electricity consumption for pumping, each estimated using source-specific emission factors derived from the SeweX model and IPCC guidelines. A profound structural transition is revealed: driven by improved sewage collection, leakage-related emissions dropped from 90.3% to 58.3%; however, the expanding and maturing pipe networks inadvertently functioned as vast bioreactors, driving in-sewer process emissions from 9.3% to 38.8%. Spatially, this evolution follows an urban-development gradient, with eastern coastal agglomerations peaking earlier than rapidly developing inland regions. Sensitivity analysis identifies sewage collection rate as the most influential parameter. Emissions intensity strongly correlates with economic development, sewage volume, and pipeline length. Scenario analysis demonstrates that integrating end-of-pipe methane recovery with targeted leakage control offers the highest mitigation potential, reducing emissions by up to 79.2% by 2060 relative to business-as-usual. We further propose a regionally adaptive mitigation portfolio that prioritizes methane recovery in eastern coastal provinces with extensive rising mains and improves sewage collection in northwestern regions with low collection coverage, offering a transferable blueprint for decarbonizing underground infrastructure in rapidly urbanizing regions worldwide. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: AD-SQL: An Optimization Model for Text-To-SQL Based on Audit Prompt Fusion and Step-By-Step Strategies
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Text-to-SQL technologies play a critical role in intelligent auditing by converting natural language or policy texts into executable SQL, thereby enhancing audit efficiency. However, due to the insufficient integration of domain knowledge, existing methods often demonstrate limited accuracy and adaptability to business needs when handling complex queries. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a new model named AD-SQL (Audit Prompt Adaptation and Decomposition SQL), a query optimization model integrates audit prompts technology and query decomposition process. The model employs a three-stage architecture. First, an enhanced RAG framework integrates audit rules and a knowledge base to encode structured knowledge into prompt vectors. Second, the query generation model recursively decomposes natural language queries into single-table queries, multi-table joins, and nested queries, applying customized strategies for each type. Finally, a structural integration mechanism synthesizes the subqueries into a complete SQL statement. A multi-loss supervision mechanism is introduced to jointly optimize SQL generation, execution consistency, and rule alignment losses. Experiments on both public and self-built audit datasets demonstrate that the overall accuracy of AD-SQL reaches 67.7%, with the accuracy of complex queries improving to 53%. Title: Sustainable Leadership and Digital Transformation in SMEs: A Literature Review
Source title: Lecture Notes on Data Engineering and Communications Technologies
Abstract: This paper explores the relationship between sustainable leadership and digital transformation in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Although leadership has been widely studied, its role in navigating digitalization and sustainability transitions within SMEs remains underexplored. Using a systematic literature review inspired by the PRISMA-P guidelines, the study synthesizes recent empirical findings on leadership styles in SMEs, emphasizing the emerging relevance of sustainable leadership and digitalization. The analysis highlights that sustainable leadership fosters innovation, collaboration, and ethical decision-making, which are critical enablers of successful digital transformation. SMEs, constrained by limited resources and informal structures, rely heavily on leaders’ vision and adaptability to align digital initiatives with long-term organizational and societal goals. Title: Analysis of Environmental Profiles of Logistics Companies in Estonia to Enhance Technology Choice
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Growing environmental and regulatory requirements are driving logistics companies to implement solutions that enhance sustainability and improve resource efficiency. In practice, however, companies often lack clarity on which technological choices align with their strategic objectives and the priorities arising from environmental targets. This descriptive study applies thematic content analysis to environmental technological maturity among Estonian logistics companies to map key sustainability practices through the lens of Supply Chain Operational Reference performance metrics. In parallel, the technologies in use are identified and mapped. The resulting dataset is combined with company logistics domain information to conduct an exploratory cluster analysis and develop a typology of firms. The typologies reflect distinct environmental profiles and help to clarify associations between sustainability practices and technology adoption. In the final stage, sustainability best practices are classified within the identified typologies to support companies in selecting technologies that best enable sustainable transformation. The study contributes to the academic literature by using systematic thematic analysis to highlight the relationships between sustainable technology practices and the profiles of their use. The study proposes a maturity-technology alignment model that enables firms to select technologies consistent with their logistics domain and sustainable strategy. Title: Behavioral involvement and structural influence in negative word-of-mouth diffusion: Exploring online firestorms during service crises
Abstract: Online firestorms arise when service failures aggregate individual grievances into collective criticism on social media. This study investigates how user behavioral involvement and structural influence shape negative word-of-mouth (NWOM) dissemination in corporate crises, and the contingent roles of firm-initiated and peer-driven interactions. Based on regulatory focus theory and social motive perspectives, we analyze 33 official crisis announcements and 26,449 user records from Sina Weibo amid the 2023 Typhoon Doksuri refund crisis. Results indicate a behavioral asymmetry: highly involved users spread more NWOM, whereas influential users disseminate less. Proactive corporate responses mitigate NWOM for both user groups. Peer social support amplifies NWOM only among highly involved users, with no significant effect on influential users. These findings enrich research on online firestorms and social media crisis communication and provide actionable strategies for service crisis management. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Filling the legitimacy void: The value of sustainability orientation across investor segments in venture financing
Abstract: When and why does sustainability attract entrepreneurial funding? Drawing on legitimacy theory, we argue that prior institutional backing segments ventures into distinct contexts in which public investors value sustainability orientation differently. Without such backing, sustainability can compensate for missing commercial validation by providing an alternative source of moral legitimacy. When institutional backing already certifies pragmatic legitimacy, sustainability may conflict with return-oriented expectations. Examining 2222 token-based crowdfunding campaigns, we find that sustainability orientation is positively associated with funding among non-backed ventures but negatively associated with funding among institutionally backed ventures. Consistent with this segmented valuation logic, non-backed ventures display stronger sustainability orientation. An LLM-based decomposition shows no statistically significant difference between the extent to which substantive and symbolic sustainability attenuate the funding disadvantage of non-backed ventures; their greater sustainability orientation is most clearly concentrated in symbolic social content. Our findings position sustainability not as a universally beneficial cue, but as a compensatory source of legitimacy whose value depends on what other types of legitimacy ventures already possess. Title: AI-Assisted Event Log Generation for Process Mining in Healthcare
Abstract: Process mining in healthcare requires structured event logs, yet extracting such logs from complex clinical databases remains a manual, error-prone task requiring substantial SQL skills and domain expertise. This paper investigates the use of large language models to generate SQL queries for event log generation from healthcare data structured according to OMOP, a common data model in healthcare. We develop an artifact to evaluate four prompting strategies across three state-of-the-art LLMs using real-world healthcare data and six clinical treatment processes of varying schema complexity. Generated queries are compared against expert-written ground truth using five metrics: executability, schema conformance, event log completeness, process fidelity, and prompt sensitivity. Results show that prompting strategy has a stronger impact on performance than model choice, while schema complexity is the primary driver of task difficulty. This paper provides a framework as well as practical guidance for LLM-assisted event log generation for process mining from clinical relational data using SQL, further enabling process mining on healthcare data. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Quantifying transfer coefficients in battery recycling routes for material flow analysis: current state and future scenarios
Abstract: The growing volume of end-of-life batteries in the European Union necessitates robust quantification of secondary raw material recovery potential to support material flow analysis and policy evaluation. However, empirical data on recycling process performance remain limited. Transfer coefficients (TCs) quantify the fraction of a material transferred from input into a specific output stream at each process step. The product of step-wise TCs along a route determines recovery for each element and links process-level performance to system-level recovery outcomes. This study compiles route-specific TCs for five lithium-ion battery recycling routes encompassing pyrometallurgical, hydrometallurgical, mechanical, and direct recycling, alongside established processes for zinc-based, nickel-based, and lead-acid batteries. TCs compiled from patents, peer-reviewed literature, and industry data were integrated into a Python-based recovery model, generating 36,358 scenario-ready values from 2010 to 2050. Two scenarios are analysed: business-as-usual, with technological stagnation and continued black mass export, and recovery scenario aligned with EU Battery Regulation targets. A gap analysis reveals highly element-specific challenges. While TCs for cobalt, nickel, and copper already approach regulatory thresholds, lithium recovery from pyrometallurgy-based routes are far below the regulatory target. Non-regulated materials such as graphite, manganese, and phosphorus show zero or marginal recovery, a structural blind spot in the regulatory framework. A structural decomposition shows that process-level efficiency is the dominant driver of system-wide recovery for most elements, whereas route composition acts as a secondary and often counteractive effect. The publicly available TC dataset provides a transparent basis for secondary supply estimation while highlighting uncertainties requiring industrial-scale validation and chemistry-differentiated parameterisation. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Smart Cities Evolutionary Progress in the B5G/6G Era: The 6G-PATH European Paradigm

Abstract: Technological solutions play a vital role in addressing urban challenges and transforming the city environment into a resilient, efficient and sustainable setup. The deployment of fifth-generation (5G) wireless networks has already laid the ground-work for futuristic smart cities but along with this, it has also triggered the rapid growth of a wide range of applications. However, continuous demands for higher throughput, lower latency and more energy efficiency have set the path towards B5G/6G, especially in the corresponding smart cities’ vertical sector. Smart cities represent one of the most dynamic and strategically prioritised verticals for 6G adoption in Europe and their further evolutionary progress can be affected by a variety of factors ranging from technology and infrastructure readiness to specific regulatory and policy enablers. Our work focuses upon the specific ecosystem created by the innovative 6G-PATH EU-funded research framework, via assessing three selected use cases relevant to: (i) connected and sensing city; (ii) automated logistics, and; (iii) security coordination. For these, we provide a closer look at sector-specific market dynamics by highlighting concrete demand drivers, strategic challenges and adoption barriers. Then we identify potential pathways for businesses by assessing strategic visions and value propositions, market commercialisation channels and related key challenges for growth. Title: Non-market strategies and environmental management: Framework for effective sustainable transformation
Abstract: As environmental concerns intensify, businesses are increasingly adopting non-market strategies (NMS) to navigate regulatory pressures and improve environmental performance (EP). However, there has been no systematic effort to synthesise existing studies on the environmental benefits of NMS and to provide an integrated conceptual understanding of the field. Title: Decoding Netflix: An Explainable AI Approach to Analyze Customer Churn and Content Preferences

Title: TabRLLM: Tabular Data Generation via Local-to-Global Rule Extraction in Low-Data Regimes
Abstract: Machine learning on tabular data is often constrained by data scarcity, especially in domains where data collection is expensive or highly sensitive. Although data generation is widely adopted to alleviate this problem, existing approaches frequently fail to capture complex cross-feature dependencies and implicit business rules. To address these challenges in low-data regimes, we propose TabRLLM, which leverages large language models for semantic feature grouping. It extracts partial-table integrity rules and integrates them into full-table constraints. TabRLLM further combines these rules with statistical constraints, including marginal distributions and feature correlations, and converts them into prompts to guide data generation. Abstract: API flexibility is a key enabler of Service-based Architectures, yet achieving it comes with pitfalls. Title: Process Externalities: A Missing Construct for Responsible BPM
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Responsible Business Process Management (RBPM) asks the discipline to account for the effects of processes on stakeholders, society, and the environment. Yet BPM’s models are scoped within the process boundary and assessed against internal objectives, so they often fail to capture broader societal or environmental effects. Existing approaches – stakeholder analysis, risk management, sustainable BPM, value-sensitive design – each addresses a particular category of such effects; what they lack is a first-class lifecycle construct that treats them as a single class through a shared generative mechanism, complementing rather than replacing them. We propose the construct of Process Externalities (PEs) to capture consequences borne by parties other than a process’s intended beneficiary, or that affect values absent from its objective function, which are generated systematically by optimisation under an incomplete objective. Understood in this way, PEs will be defined by this mechanism rather than merely by the stakeholders they affect, and ultimately, after standardisation, they may be subject to externalities accounting following the direction already set by impact-weighted accounting initiatives in management. This paper shows that PEs are elicitable through a design-fiction method aimed at effects not yet visible in process data, and actionable through an externality register attached to the lifecycle, for which we give a graduated, three-level operationalisation and a sketch of externality accounting. Title: David vs. Goliath in Next Activity Prediction: Argmax vs. LSTM, Transformer, and LLM

Abstract: Next activity prediction (NAP) is a cornerstone of predictive process monitoring (PPM), enabling organizations to move from retrospective analysis to proactive process steering. The PPM field has progressed from classical machine learning through deep learning architectures such as LSTMs and Transformers to large language models (LLMs). Despite growing model complexity, no benchmark jointly compares LLMs, Transformers, LSTMs, and simple baselines in a direct sequence modeling setting for NAP. Title: Joint fulfillment and consolidation of multi-item orders in e-commerce: A two-phase heuristic
Abstract: In today's business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce, high order volumes, multi-item orders and shipments, split deliveries, and escalating transportation costs, pose significant operational challenges. In this environment, jointly optimizing order fulfillment and consolidation is crucial to achieving economies of scale and ensuring cost-effective delivery. This study addresses the Multi-Item Orders Fulfillment and Consolidation Problem (MOFCP) faced by e-commerce retailers that manage both online channels and physical warehouse networks. We develop a model that identifies the optimal set of warehouses to fulfill orders and their corresponding consolidation points to minimize transportation costs. We formulate the problem as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model with a piecewise linear cost function and propose a two-phase heuristic to solve MOFCP efficiently: in the first phase, we find an initial solution by LP-rounding; in the second phase, we employ a General Variable Neighborhood Search (GVNS) algorithm to improve the initial solution. In addition, we design two benchmark instances based on item coverage in the network and the inventory-to-demand ratio. Extensive computational experiments show that the two-phase heuristic yields solutions close to the ones found by Gurobi, within significantly lower computation time (up to 30 times faster). Title: Lead and succeed: R&D executives and bank digital transformation
Abstract: Digital transformation (DT) is reshaping the business of banks in the age of big data, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence. We further identify that stronger public digital attention attenuates such a transformation effect. The impacts exhibit heterogeneity, varying across different dimensions of transformation and bank characteristics. These findings remain robust after controlling for endogeneity in various robustness tests. Title: Industrial robot and cross-border M&As
Abstract: Using panel data of Chinese listed firms over 2007–2023, we examine the impact of industrial robot penetration on cross-border merger and acquisition (M&A) decisions, constructing a firm-level penetration measure from industry-level statistics. Baseline results show that a 1% increase in robot penetration raises firms' likelihood of conducting cross-border M&A by 4.89%, and this finding remains robust after addressing endogeneity concerns and performing a battery of robustness checks. Mechanism analysis reveals that robot adoption facilitates cross-border M&A by improving profitability, alleviating financing frictions, and most critically, enhancing corporate risk-taking. Cross-sectional tests further indicate the positive effect is more pronounced for private firms and firms with top management teams lacking overseas education experience, where technology-driven risk-taking substitutes for traditional advantages in international expansion. Title: Implications of drone delivery: Strategic interaction and competitive equilibrium
Abstract: Logistics capability has emerged as a critical strategic asset that shapes business models and competitive landscapes. Within this context, drone delivery represents a disruptive technology that is redefining the nature of interfirm competition and cooperation. This study explores the strategic interactions between a smart retailer that uses drones for delivery and a traditional retailer that relies on conventional methods only, utilizing both Stackelberg and Nash games to analyze drone adoption and pricing decisions. The effective delivery capability of drones and consumer preferences for delivery efficiency are critical factors in this study. The findings suggest that drones enable retailers to increase prices while expanding their market share, thereby creating a competitive advantage for smart retailers when drones are used exclusively. Traditional retailers are more inclined to adopt drones when effective delivery capabilities are high, whereas smart retailers may focus on using drones to optimize efficiency under varying delivery conditions, depending on consumer preferences. Finally, drone-enabled delivery can generate multi-win outcomes under certain conditions, where retailer profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare are simultaneously improved compared with the truck-only benchmark. Title: Unpacking complementarities in emerging circular economy innovation ecosystems: The case of industrial plastic waste from the Norwegian aquaculture industry
Abstract: Despite growing awareness of plastic waste, industrial plastic use continues to rise, while recycling rates remain low. Addressing this challenge requires a transition toward a circular economy (CE), in which value depends on interactions among independent yet interdependent actors across sectors. CE innovation ecosystems and complementarities offer lenses for understanding such interdependencies. This paper explores how orchestrators facilitate complementarities in emerging CE innovation ecosystems by drawing on an embedded qualitative case study of plastic waste from Norwegian aquaculture. Four types of complementarities are identified—materials data, from waste to resource, recycling capacity, and regulations—conceptualized along two dimensions: resource flow and infrastructure complementarities. This illustrates where orchestrators facilitate value at present and where their role is constrained by limited infrastructure and regulatory requirements. Title: Understanding Digital Accounting Adoption in SMEs: A Systematic Literature Review of Influencing Factors, Implementation Challenges, and Research Gaps

Abstract: The main objective of this study is to provide a comprehensive overview of the key variables influencing adoption decisions, difficulties encountered during implementation, and important information gaps that need to be filled to guide future research. To guarantee rigor and transparency, the study used a systematic literature review (SLR) methodology in accordance with PRISMA criteria. Between 2012 and 2025, there are 315 peer-reviewed journal publications were found, examined, and condensed into 43 thorough and pertinent articles. The results of this literature study unequivocally show that the human factor and implementation gap must be addressed if SMEs are to fully benefit from accounting digitization. Title: Artificial intelligence in sales (2017-early 2026): field consolidation and the rise of human-AI collaboration

Title: Customizable Declarative Process Specification Scenarios via Automated Planning
Abstract: Declarative specifications define the behaviour of processes by means of temporal rules exerting dependencies between the occurrence of activities. Those rules can constitute the system requirements and normative boundaries within which the workflow is framed. The multitude of rules and their interrelations, though, make it reportedly difficult for users to linearly figure out unfoldings that depict the admitted behaviour in the form of explicative scenarios. While simulation engines can produce example traces of customizable length and in varying numerosity, these state-of-the-art tools adopt random approaches that do not permit the selection of a subset of runs exhibiting characteristic traits. In other words, simulations could produce traces that show common behavior, leaving out significant parts of the possible execution paths, and thus substantially hindering a proper validation of specifications. To mitigate this issue, we propose a principled solution that leverages automated planning to produce execution scenarios depicting the specified behavior according to desirable execution costs, diversifying the enacted behavior, or matching a given subsequence of steps. We demonstrate its efficiency and efficacy through experiments demonstrating its scalability and superiority in terms of behavioral coverage with respect to the state-of-the-art simulation tool for declarative process specifications. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Environmental Literacy for Managerial and Economic Professions in Slovakia

Embedding this competence into subjects such as financial analysis and financial planning, strategic management, tax systems, intra-corporate controlling, behavioural economics and internet communication can enhance graduate readiness for labour markets shaped by sustainability transitions. Title: CV-Driven Window Selection for Multi-perspective Concept Drift Detection in Event Logs

Abstract: Process mining leverages event logs recorded in information systems to discover and analyze business processes. Title: Gamified Marketing as a Tool for Sustainable and Positive Educational Change

Title: What determines the adoption of space cooling technology in households? Evidence from regions in Belgium and Poland
Abstract: Frequent heatwaves are common, especially during the climate crisis. Hence, the topic of mitigating the impact of hot summer days is attracting increasing attention, and the demand for cooling solutions is rising. This research aims to identify and assess the factors that individuals in the Antwerp Province of Belgium and the Kuyavian-Pomeranian Voivodeship of Poland might consider when adopting a cooling solution. These regions are experiencing heatwaves during the summer, which are becoming more frequent, intense, and prolonged due to climate change. These two regions are characterized by similar population sizes (∼2 million) but differ in climate, urbanization, and economic roles, making them suitable for comparative analysis. This study employs a discrete choice experiment to examine households' preferences for cooling options, considering the following characteristics: thermal comfort, air quality, sound level, environmental impact, lifespan, and cost. The results indicate that in the Polish region, which is in a more extreme climate zone, households are much more willing to invest in cooling technology than those living in Antwerp Province, which has a milder climate. The Willingness-to-Pay analysis revealed that reduced noise is the most valuable feature of household cooling solutions in the Belgium region, which is much more densely populated. The air quality improvement feature is most valued in areas where people perceive poor air quality. The study suggests that the business sector should design cooling devices to be silent and more environmentally friendly, and that policymakers should make cooling systems more affordable and accessible. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: DoRA-Based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Corporate Compliance Determination
Abstract: Corporate compliance determination plays an important role in enterprise risk management, as it requires not only judging whether business conduct conforms to relevant rules but also producing explanations that can support lawful operation and regulatory risk prevention. Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently been explored for compliance review and legal risk identification, yet their direct use in this setting is still limited by strict rule constraints, low tolerance for errors, and the need for interpretable and consistently structured outputs. These requirements expose the limitations of general-purpose foundation models, which may produce inaccurate judgments, unstable reasoning processes, or inconsistent report structures. To improve adaptation under such constraints, we propose DoRA-Variant, a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) framework built on Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA). DoRA-Variant introduces two modifications. First, the Frozen-A and Adaptive Learning Rates (FA) mechanism keeps the A matrix fixed and assigns asymmetric learning rates to the magnitude parameter m and matrix B, thereby restricting the update space and promoting more stable adaptation under small-sample conditions. Second, Directional Strength Calibration (DSC) rescales the directional update increment during inference, allowing the effective strength of directional adaptation to be controlled without additional training. Experiments on three public commonsense reasoning benchmarks and a controlled low-resource corporate compliance evaluation setting indicate that DoRA-Variant achieves a favorable trade-off between task performance and parameter efficiency compared with representative PEFT baselines. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Beyond Linear Impact: A Nonlinear Theory of Change and a Six-Level Indicator System for Evaluating Culture-Led Regeneration in Left-behind Territories
Abstract: Left-behind territories have characteristics that are not easily identified using traditional impact assessment methods, in particular with regard to cultural-led initiatives. Evaluating cultural-led regeneration processes of such territories requires new assessment models capable of capturing processes of transformation that unfold across cognitive, relational, behavioural and socio-economic dimensions simultaneously. The model conceptualises cultural investment as an activator of cognitive and relational processes, reconfiguring predictive models, expanding perceived agency and consolidating social cohesion, rather than as a direct generator of economic outcomes. The paper describes the resulting six-level indicator system comprising 36 indicators. It integrates composite indices derived from Likert-scale questionnaire items with direct indicators from secondary sources, including administrative records, business register data and mobile network-derived visitor flow estimates. The architecture is designed for longitudinal, independent-samples comparison and for disaggregated sub-group analysis, with explicit methodological provisions for addressing compositional confounds in low-density demographic contexts. Title: Towards an OR-Join Semantics that Meets Expectations
Abstract: The OR-join is an essential but semantically complex construct in process modeling that has challenged process modelers and analysts for decades. Because it possesses non-local semantics – an OR-join may need to wait for tokens to arrive from “further away” – making it difficult to determine when it is enabled or not. The BPMN specification provides “official” semantics, but despite its complexity, these semantics lead to “surprising” behavior in certain scenarios. This paper investigates the complexities of the BPMN OR-join specification and explores whether alternative semantics better align with the expectations of modeling experts. To assess different OR-join policies, a questionnaire featuring 14 example models was distributed among a large group of process experts. Analysis of the responses shows a significant lack of consensus among experts regarding the expected behavior of OR-joins. None of the experts gave answers fully consistent with the official BPMN standard. Title: Semi-automated vs. Manual Process Model Generation: A Comparative Study of the Process of Process Modeling
Abstract: Due to recent advances in large language models (LLMs), semi-automated approaches to business process modeling have emerged. These fundamentally shift the modeling task from manual model creation to prompt-based model generation and refinement. Prior research has focused on the capability of LLMs to generate (BPMN 2.0) process models, but little evidence exists on the way the involvement of an LLM affects the process of process modeling itself. A controlled eye-tracking study was conducted with 24 participants, with each participant creating process models manually as well as semi-automatically with an LLM-based chatbot. Efficiency was measured through task completion time, cognitive load was assessed through eye-tracking metrics and NASA-TLX scores, and process model quality was evaluated with respect to syntactic and semantic correctness. Our results show that semi-automated model creation significantly increases efficiency and reduces both objective and subjective cognitive load. Notably, these advantages do not come at the expense of process model quality. The LLM-generated process models exhibited only moderate syntactic errors and achieved very high semantic accuracy. Title: Enhancing the social innovation ecosystem: university-led incubation pathways for rural sustainability
Abstract: Universities are increasingly called upon to contribute to sustainability transitions, yet their roles as active intermediaries within social innovation ecosystems remain under-theorised. This study examines how universities can incubate social innovations that advance rural sustainability. Using an exploratory, theory-building case study, we draw on interviews, documents and observational materials from multiple rural revitalisation initiatives led by The University of Hong Kong to identify how incubation processes configure relationships, mobilise resources and reshape institutional environments. Stewardship initiatives cultivate bonding capital by transforming individuals into rural change agents through experiential learning and place-based engagement. Platform initiatives build bridging capital by providing shared infrastructures that connect rural and urban actors, lowering market and regulatory barriers. Community-focused initiatives mobilise linking capital, enabling collective governance arrangements and facilitating negotiation across local and institutional boundaries. Synthesising these findings, we develop a configurational framework of university supported social innovation incubation that elucidates how these pathways operate through different forms of institutional work across community and institutional boundaries. The framework demonstrates how universities, when locally embedded and institutionally trusted, can orchestrate multiple, complementary pathways that cumulatively reshape social innovation ecosystems. Title: ESG Investing: A Bibliometric Study

Title: From nature-inspired innovation to nature conservation and restoration financing
Abstract: Biomimicry—the practice of emulating nature's time-tested patterns and strategies—has generated transformative innovations across multiple sectors, while the biodiversity crisis is accelerating. This paradox reveals an innovation debt to nature: humanity increasingly benefits from ecosystems’ intellectual capital, while ongoing ecological degradation erodes the very knowledge base upon which future innovations depend. Grounded in the semiconducting principle—which permits environmental value to generate monetary gains while rejecting the use of monetary gains to offset or compensate for environmental degradation—this perspective proposes a profit-sharing mechanism designed to redirect socio-economic systems toward activities aligned with ecological thresholds and long-term sustainability. Specifically, the proposed mechanism channels a portion of revenues or profits derived from biomimicry-based innovations toward conservation and restoration activities, thereby helping address the biodiversity finance gap and fostering an eco-surplus culture in which business success and ecological regeneration mutually reinforce one another. In doing so, it creates a positive feedback loop: the more humanity innovates through nature, the more it contributes to sustaining and regenerating it. © 2026 Elsevier GmbH

Title: Perspectives on scaling up clean energy technologies in the energy transition
Abstract: Carbon neutrality requires massive, rapid scaling up of clean energy technologies, with economic factors playing a central role in market uptake. We investigate how economic drivers and investment behaviors affect technology growth using a novel, multi-model analytical framework. By combining macro-level cost-driven technology diffusion with micro-level business profitability modeling, this framework captures realistic, investment-centric decision-making. Cost-competitiveness-dependent, varying technology adoption rates realistically reflect market growth and saturation, indicating a declining adoption rate as market share increases. Growth is initially influenced by technical and technoeconomic factors, but shifts toward complex systemic, social, and socioeconomic factors around the inflection point (halfway to saturation). This transition triggers, for instance, when solar PV share reaches around 20% of global electricity. At higher market shares, cost-competitiveness encompasses both basic technology costs and system-level limitations, better captured by the value-adjusted levelized cost of electricity than pure cost. Furthermore, micro-level profitability analysis underlines that sustained scaling up requires adequate business margins and profits. Growth can be accelerated through higher sales margins, reinvesting more profits into investments, reducing the time cash is tied up in sales, etc. Public support speeds up market entry but risks creating unhealthy competition and oversupply if sustained too long. Future technologies benefit from policies supporting a shorter development phase followed by rapid adoption. Finally, insights for future scaling up emphasize low costs, profitability, granularity, modularity, system flexibility, learning and scale effects, and technology-push versus market-pull trade-off. This multitude of factors stresses an integrated, multidisciplinary systems view to accelerate scaling up of clean energy. © 2026 The Author

Title: The dynamics of customer participation in service recovery: The roles of failure severity, quality signals, and responsiveness
Abstract: In high-contact hospitality settings, service failures can disrupt encounters in ways that prompt customers to intervene. Drawing on control theory and signaling theory, we conceptualize customer participation (CP) as a solution-oriented behavioral response through which customers attempt to influence recovery when service delivery is disrupted. We examine how quality signals and frontline employee responsiveness shape the extent to which participation translates into recovery outcomes. Across five studies, we show that severe service failures can prompt solution-oriented participation, but this response is contingent on contextual conditions. Quality signals attenuate the likelihood that failure severity translates into participation by shifting perceived responsibility toward the firm, creating a conditional quality signaling paradox. Employee responsiveness strengthens the positive effects of participation once enacted, but cannot compensate when participation is not initiated. Title: Deep Learning Driven Multimodal Digital Twin Framework for Risk Prediction and Decision Intelligence in Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Systems
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The need to facilitate enterprise risk prediction and decision intelligence is essential, operational resilience, financial losses mitigation and proactive mitigation of the potential threats in Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems. In this paper, a Multimodal Foundation Model Driven Digital Twin approach of enterprise risk prediction and decision intelligence is presented, which incorporates the ERP data for enterprise operations. The proposed system integrates heterogeneous data on a Transformer-based foundation model, and is supported by a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, and enables the processing of heterogeneous features in a modal fashion and cross-modal representation learning. The joint embeddings are then fed into a simulated digital twin that runs the enterprise until it executes the operations in a virtual world to perform predictive analytics and risk assessment. Finally, a decision intelligence system converts the forecasted risks into the recommendations to be followed on and graphical knowledge via a business dashboard. The proposed framework is experimentally proven to reach performance that is significantly higher than six benchmark CNN, LSTM, BERT, Transformer-XL, BioBERT, and SciBert- on a range of different metrics.
