Title: Toning it down: How competition shapes CSR communication positivity amid external stakeholder pressures
Abstract: Amid intensifying scrutiny of corporate environmental and social impacts, firms increasingly use positive CSR communication to shape stakeholder perceptions. However, its effectiveness varies across contexts. We develop an impression management risk perspective, arguing that heightened product market competition (PMC) increases the anticipated backlash risks associated with overly positive CSR communication. As PMC intensifies, firms anticipate that economically oriented stakeholders will interpret highly positive CSR tone as evidence of inefficient resource allocation and managerial distraction, leading firms to use less positive CSR tone. We further argue that unfavorable analyst recommendations strengthen this negative relationship by heightening concerns about firms’ financial prospects, whereas CSR-related shareholder proposals weaken it by increasing pressure for CSR performance improvement. Title: Financial and Performance Indicators of Supply Chains: An Econometric Analysis
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This study aims to contribute to the understanding of how intellectual capital efficiency and innovation influence financial performance in European ports operating within maritime supply chains, particularly under systemic shocks and crisis conditions. Using the Value Added Intellectual Coefficient as a measure of intangible asset management, the study assesses whether ports’ innovation capacity and intellectual capital efficiency enhance financial performance and resilience during adverse macroeconomic environments. Empirically, the analysis employs System GMM estimators to account for unobserved heterogeneity across ports and the dynamic nature of financial outcomes. The sample comprises 23 European ports observed from 2018 to 2023, encompassing disruptive events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, geopolitical conflicts, and economic uncertainty. Financial performance is modelled as a function of VAIC, innovation variables, port size, and macroeconomic controls. Results indicate that intellectual capital efficiency has a positive and significant impact on port financial performance, even during crisis periods. Innovation further strengthens value creation, competitiveness, and adaptive capacity within maritime logistics chains. This study advances port economics by integrating an adapted VAIC and innovation as organizational resilience drivers. Diverging from cross-sectoral analyses, the research demonstrates the strategic primacy of intangible assets in sustaining performance and viability during exogenous shocks. The results provide a robust framework for academics and policymakers to enhance the maritime sector’s adaptive capacity through intellectual capital. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Navigating the in-between: Contradictions in transitioning service ecosystems
Abstract: While research on change in service ecosystems has expanded considerably, one specific type of process—transitions—has received comparatively limited attention. This gap is consequential, as transitions are critical for addressing systemic problems, including sustainability challenges. More specifically, little is known about the nature of contradictions—coexisting yet opposing elements—within these processes. Addressing this gap, we conduct an abductive qualitative study of a transitioning energy service ecosystem, which surrounds a European utility firm. Our findings reveal the individual-level struggles that actors experience amid service ecosystem transitions, especially when the contradictions within transitions go unrecognized or unmanaged. Abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping organizational practices across industries, particularly in how firms pursue performance improvements while addressing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) objectives. This paper presents a structured literature review examining the role of AI in enhancing organizational performance through ESG-oriented management practices. By synthesizing recent academic contributions, the study explores how AI-driven tools and data analytics support decision-making, operational efficiency, risk management, and sustainability-oriented strategies. The review highlights key mechanisms through which AI contributes to economic performance while simultaneously enabling greater transparency, accountability, and social and environmental responsibility. In addition, the paper discusses emerging challenges and limitations identified in the literature, including ethical concerns, data governance, algorithmic bias, and energy consumption. Title: Security Engineering in Product-Line Development: Concept and Practitioner Evaluation

Abstract: As modern software systems grow in complexity and configurability, organizations increasingly rely on Product-Line Engineering (PLE) to manage variability and reuse. Yet, security remains insufficiently integrated into these processes and is often treated as an afterthought rather than a core design concern. To address this gap, we propose a dedicated security-engineering extension that systematically embeds security in the PLE framework. The extension was developed through a structured framework development process and synthesizes insights from 52 existing publications. An initial survey with 36 security practitioners confirmed the framework’s necessity, clarity, and usefulness, with over 90% positive responses. Title: Does Fraud Risk Affect Legality Ratings? Evidence from Italian Listed Firms
Abstract: Within the framework of the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, Goal 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions) aims to combat all forms of organized crime and significantly reduce corruption and illegality. In this context, Law No. 190 of November 6, 2012, introduced the Legality rating, which serves as an institutional mechanism designed to promote ethical behavior and integrity among Italian firms. This study examines whether the elements considered in the attribution of the legality rating can indirectly capture factors associated with financial statement manipulation. Results reveal no significant relationship between the legality rating and the likelihood of fraudulent reporting, suggesting that the rating captures formal compliance rather than substantive financial integrity. Title: The impact of platform verification badges on social media influencer engagement
Abstract: Verification badges play an important role in signaling authenticity and influence for social media contributors. However, recent platform shifts have turned badges from merit-based indicators into purchasable commodities, raising questions about their effectiveness. Drawing on signaling theory, this research examines how verification impacts engagement under three conditions: merit-based, hybrid, and non-merit-based. Using a multimethod design that combines influencer interviews, consumer discussions on Reddit, an experiment, and an empirical analysis of over 8 million daily observations from X, we found verification increases perceived authenticity, which in turn enhances perceived influence, thereby driving higher engagement. Title: Port coordination dilemmas in green shipping corridors under unilateral carbon policies
Source title: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment
Abstract: Under unilateral carbon regulation, including the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), green shipping corridors (GSCs) face asymmetric coordination challenges among ports and shipping companies (SCs). We develop a tripartite evolutionary game incorporating reduced-form SC heterogeneity, carbon-price feedback, an attractiveness-based green-capacity allocation rule, and stochastic disturbances. A real-world-informed synthetic Europe–Southern Africa container-shipping scenario supports the analysis. Results show that the EU ETS strengthens SC cooperation incentives, but full cooperation requires sustainable port payoffs. The developing-country port lies near its cooperation threshold and is sensitive to incremental green-business revenue, subsidies, and green operational capability. Under the specified rule, improvements in this port’s attractiveness increase its modeled share of configurable green-service demand and can support cooperation without undermining the developed-country port’s cooperation incentive. Stochastic disturbances amplify differences across evolutionary paths for the weaker port. Green-capacity allocation thus links port heterogeneity, competition, and cooperation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: B2B influencer marketing collaborations: A relational governance perspective
Abstract: Influencer marketing has grown rapidly in business markets, yet existing research remains largely rooted in consumer contexts and organization-centric perspectives. Little is known about how B2B influencers perceive collaborations with companies. Addressing this gap, this study conceptualizes B2B influencer collaboration as an interactionally constituted governance process and examines how governance mechanisms are interpreted by internal and external influencers. Title: Research on the Application Scenarios and Implementation Strategies of all-Round Digital
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: The growing digitalization trend in the industries compels business organizations to put in place holistic strategies that may be in the form of integrating technology, optimization of operations, and long-term value generation. The paper presents the uses cases and implementation strategy of all-round digital transformation with particular emphasis on its application to various business and service scenarios. A new approach, Intelligent Multi-Layer Orchestration Model (IMLOM), is introduced to the successful planning and implementation. MLOM comprises three layers architecture: Perception Layer collects and reconciles data across sources in the environment and market systems context; Cognition Layer makes use of advanced analytics and machine learning to identify trends, predict problems and generate scenario-specific intelligence; and Execution Layer implements ideal strategies automatically by using rule-based and AI-driven decision engines. This architecture has the benefit of organizations responding easily to increased requisitions because resources are synchronized effectively and there is also consistency in service delivery. The following paper will cover some of the spheres of implementation, such as intelligent manufacturing, smart grid operations, digital financial services, and modernization of public services, and will present plans to implement it in stages, taking both the cost of technology and the prospect of successful performance into consideration. This would provide a cross-sector framework that is scalable and can enjoy the benefits of holistic digital capability to ensure flexibility in reacting to the hidden innovations of the future. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Discovering Relationships in Data Lakes Using Large Language Models: An Industrial Case
Abstract: Data lakes rely on metadata to remain usable, yet this metadata is often limited or weakly informative for column relationship discovery, especially in ERP-derived datasets with coded or abbreviated schema labels. We propose ColRel, a two-stage method that builds column embeddings from metadata and data available at ingestion time. In difficult cases, such as coded schemata, business dictionaries help interpret column names and support the generation of short natural-language descriptions used in the second stage. Experiments on public benchmarks and an industrial ERP dataset show that ColRel is particularly effective in semantically related, weak-signal settings. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Samorin M.C.M.
Author full names: Samorin, Maria Corazon M. (60905386600)
Title: Sustainability and Emerging Issues in the Cooperative Sector: Evidence from Iloilo, Philippines
Abstract: This study investigates the sustainability challenges and emerging trends influencing the cooperative sector in Iloilo Province and City, Philippines, over the past 5 years, situating local experiences within global cooperative discourse. Using a qualitative case study design, data were gathered from 25 purposively selected key informants, including cooperative development specialists, managers, officers, and members, through in-depth interviews and focus group discussions. Thematic analysis revealed four persistent issues that constrain cooperative sustainability: taxation, governance, membership engagement, and technological adaptation. Taxation concerns revolve around inconsistent regulatory requirements and threats to long-standing privileges under the TRAIN Law, while governance issues highlight leadership monopolies and weak succession planning. Membership apathy and limited participation undermine accountability, and technological gaps limit efficiency and transparency. At the same time, four notable trends were identified: a growing recognition of cooperatives as economic contributors, diversification into innovative and nontraditional businesses, increased adoption of insurance and risk management mechanisms, and strengthened gender and development initiatives that enhance inclusivity. The findings underscore the dual reality of cooperatives as both challenged and resilient institutions that continue to advance equity, social justice, and inclusive economic development. The Iloilo experience offers valuable lessons for policy reform, governance innovation, and sustainability strategies applicable to cooperatives globally. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Author full names: van Rooijen, Bram R. (60986462800); Tekeli, Songul (60223978500); Ursavas, Evrim (56100437000); Zhu, Stuart X. (36149074000)
Title: Institutional risk, finance, and the limits of techno-economic optimality in green hydrogen deployment
Abstract: Green hydrogen is widely positioned as a key option for deep decarbonization, yet large-scale deployment remains limited despite growing techno-economic potential. This review examines how non-technical conditions influence the feasibility of green hydrogen business models, using the Netherlands as an illustrative case. A review-driven mixed-methods framework integrates evidence from a systematic literature review, semi-structured expert interviews, and an established hourly-resolved techno-economic optimization model to examine how policy design, investment risk, infrastructure constraints, and demand formation influence both the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) and deployment feasibility. A multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is employed to synthesize qualitative and quantitative evidence and prioritize the principal drivers and barriers identified across the different sources. The synthesized evidence, supported by the illustrative techno-economic analysis, indicates that LCOH values below €6 kg−1 are attainable under favorable assumptions, including low renewable electricity prices, reduced weighted average cost of capital (WACC), and access to underground hydrogen storage. However, regulatory fragmentation, grid congestion, weak demand coordination, and limited institutional legitimacy substantially constrain the realization of such conditions in practice. The findings demonstrate that techno-economic assessments alone may overestimate the deployability of green hydrogen when institutional risk and market coordination challenges are not explicitly considered. The proposed integrative framework provides a structured approach for assessing hydrogen market readiness in early-stage European contexts and supports the alignment of techno-economic competitiveness with governance capacity, investment conditions, and social acceptance. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Feature Attribution-Based Explainability Analysis of Deep Learning Models in Predictive Process Monitoring
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Predictive process monitoring supports the optimization and control of operational business processes by forecasting the future state or outcome of ongoing cases. While deep neural networks have achieved strong performance for these tasks by modeling sequential dependencies in event logs, their black-box nature limits trust and practical adoption. Feature attribution methods are often used to address this, but applying them directly poses a dilemma: event-level attributions impose high computational complexity for long traces, while explanations based on aggregated trace representations often fail to capture the underlying control-flow dynamics. To address this issue, we propose a local post-hoc explainability method for deep neural networks in outcome prediction. The method relies on a control-flow-aware segmentation algorithm that partitions a trace into meaningful segments and supports the computation of segment-level SHAP explanations. This makes it possible to identify which parts of a trace influence a prediction and which change points steer the case toward the predicted outcome. We assess the proposed segmentation method on a synthetic dataset with known process logic, where meaningful change points can be explicitly verified, and we demonstrate its usefulness on real-world event logs from a loan application process and an administrative process of a Dutch municipality. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Luo N.; Zhang C.; Dong K.
Title: Does circular transformation matter for firm value?
Abstract: Corporate adoption of circular solutions has become a prominent pathway for generating new sources of value. This study examines the value-shaping effects of corporate circular transformation using panel data for 351 Chinese listed companies spanning 2015–2024. Five circular transformation indicators based on more than 7000 annual reports and corporate social responsibility reports were constructed. Results show that circular transformation significantly enhances firm value. Among specific circular practices, circular material substitution exerts the strongest positive effect, followed by product life extension and macro-strategic response, whereas circular working modes do not exhibit a significant influence on firm value. The analysis further identifies investor sentiment and supply chain resilience as mediating mechanisms, alongside positive moderating effect of digital transformation and institutional pressure. These findings provide important implications for promoting circular transformation at the micro level. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Digital Evidence and Reporting on the Decision of Administrative Matters in Administrative Procedures
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The quality and timeliness of administrative decision-making represent important indicators of the state of public administration, particularly with regard to the quality of public services. Research findings confirm that the quality of public services is directly correlated with the level of public trust in public administration, the ease of doing business, and overall social development. Assessing the efficiency of administrative authorities in deciding on the rights, obligations, and legal interests of natural and legal persons requires the availability of objective and reliable data, which can be ensured through appropriate records on administrative decision-making. This paper analyzes the normative framework and practice of recording and reporting on administrative procedures in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a particular focus on the institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the period 2019–2024. It proposes the introduction of a digital model of recording and reporting based on the principles of e-government. The proposed model includes standardized recording templates, automated reporting, real-time performance indicators, and advanced analytical tools. The aim of the paper is to demonstrate that the digitalization of administrative records is a key prerequisite for improving administrative decision-making, strengthening accountability, and achieving alignment with the standards of the European Administrative Space. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: “The System Did It”: Bias, Opacity, and the Misalignment of Ethical Mitigations in (Robotic) Process Automation
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and Agentic AI are reshaping business processes, but their ethical governance lags behind deployment. Based on a scoping review of 29 papers that establishes the general, cross-sector landscape of ethical issues and mitigation strategies, and a municipal focus group that serves as an example case why these generally proposed mitigations fail in practice, we identify five recurring ethical issues (loss of autonomy, opacity, bias, responsibility diffusion, privacy) and four mitigation strategies (human-in-the-loop, audit logs, explainable interfaces, impact assessments). Loss of autonomy is the most-cited concern (62%), yet it attracts the least targeted mitigation, while algorithmic bias (14%) commands the most. The focus group confirms this asymmetry and reveals that even well-understood mitigations depend on organizational resources, governance maturity, and cross-departmental collaboration, factors that the literature fails to explore. The result is a framework of socio-technical governance mechanisms that translates abstract ethical principles into actionable guidance for responsible process automation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Low-Code Platforms Adoption: A Motivational Adoption Process Perspective
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: The growing demand for digital transformation in organizations, coupled with a shortage of skilled-IT workers, presents a challenge that can be addressed through the utilization of low-code platforms (LCPs). While existing literature examines organizational drivers of LCPs adoption, our human-centered study shifts the focus toward the individu, investigating motivations of non-technical users adopting LCPs on their own initiative for professional needs. Through qualitative interviews and by refinement of Keller’s ARCS Motivational Model, an adoption framework emerged in the form of a five-stage motivational adoption process (interest, need, ability, learning, reinforcement). By effectively articulating key motivational factors in the adoption of LCPs by citizen developers in this cohesive framework, it can help organizations better foster low-code initiatives. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Intergenerational eco-craft, women's agency, and climate adaptation in Telaga Biru Coastal Village, Madura, Indonesia
Abstract: This study examines how coastal women in Telaga Biru Village, Madura, Indonesia, use natural-dye batik as an everyday practice of livelihood adaptation, ecological knowledge transmission, and community sustainability. Rather than treating women only as vulnerable subjects of climate and coastal change, the article asks how women's craft labour enables them to negotiate socio-ecological uncertainty within unequal gender relations, unstable markets, and limited institutional support. Based on feminist ethnography, the study draws on participant observation, in-depth interviews with 15 women batik artisans, and supplementary interviews with the village head and a local batik business owner. The findings show that women's natural-dye batik work operates as intergenerational eco-craft: it sustains household livelihoods, preserves coastal motifs and natural-dye knowledge, supports small-scale waste management, enables limited digital marketing, and anchors community-based environmental care through women's informal and organisational networks. At the same time, the article cautions against romanticising women's resilience, as their adaptive labour remains under-recognised, poorly supported, and shaped by patriarchal household and community structures. By conceptualising natural-dye batik as intergenerational eco-craft, this study contributes to feminist climate scholarship by showing how women's craft labour connects ecological knowledge, livelihood adaptation, cultural continuity, and coastal sustainability in the Global South. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises as Providers of Regional Environmental Open Data: Connecting LCA Indicators with ESG Reporting and Sustainable Regional Development
Abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) generate considerable amounts of environmental data in their everyday operations, but much of this information remains unused outside the enterprise. These data could support regional policymaking, especially if they were collected and shared in a structured form. In practice, business-generated data often do not meet the standards required for integration into public databases. This paper examines how SMEs can contribute to regional environmental open data, with a focus on Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), ESG reporting, and sustainable regional development. The study combines preliminary empirical evidence from Slovak SMEs with a systematic review of relevant literature. It investigates whether SMEs monitor environmental indicators more frequently in the earlier stages of the product life cycle, particularly procurement and production, than in the later stages, such as consumption, use, and end-of-life treatment (H1). Five specific indicators are examined: product origin transparency (H2a), energy consumption in production (H2b), fuel consumption (H2c), average product lifespan (H2d), and the proportion of repaired products compared with discarded products (H2e). The findings show that SMEs tend to focus mainly on indicators linked to internal processes. Indicators from downstream life cycle phases are monitored less frequently. The paper contributes to the discussion on how SME-generated environmental data can be transformed into regional open data and used more effectively in sustainability-oriented policy and reporting. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Characterizing Process Variants with Natural Examples
Abstract: To improve business processes, it is crucial to analyze why processes differ across process variants. To support this analysis, prior research has often relied on machine learning models trained to classify process variants and used model explanations to distinguish them. User studies in explainable artificial intelligence show that these explanations can be expanded through the inclusion of examples. To this end, we introduce an approach that uses declarative behavioural constraints to support variant classification tasks. Building on these constraints, we perform a post-hoc probability analysis and derive a set of multi-feature measures to characterize cases that are representative of each process variant (prototypes) alongside cases that are close to the classification boundaries between process variants (boundary cases). We assess the explanatory power of those natural examples with two real-world event logs. The results demonstrate that our approach shows the distinctive behavioural traits of variants effectively and intuitively. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Integrated Model of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0–Case Studies

Abstract: Siemens integrates Industry 4.0 (digitalization, automation, IoT, cyber-physical systems, and data-driven efficiency) with Industry 5.0 (human-centric collaboration, resilience, sustainability, and AI augmentation) through its Siemens Xcelerator open digital business platform. Core Foundation (Industry 4.0 Legacy) are: Builds on digital twins (DT), Industrial IoT (eg, Insights Hub, formerly MindSphere), edge computing, and comprehensive portfolios like NX, Teamcenter, and SIMATIC for end-to-end integration across product lifecycle, production, and supply chains, and Enables vertical/horizontal integration, predictive maintenance, and mass customization in smart factories. Siemens’ model views Industry 5.0 as a seamless extension of Industry 4.0-not a replacement-delivering resilient, sustainable, and personalized production where humans, AI, and machines co-create value. Title: Mindfulness in organizations: how and when mindfulness shapes perceptions of distributive justice in society
Abstract: Although social inequality is widespread, managers do not necessarily perceive it as unfair. Across four field studies involving European managers, we investigate how mindfulness influences managers’ perceptions of distributive justice in society (PDJS). Three results emerge. First, mindfulness leads managers to perceive societal inequalities as more unfair. Second, social-justice awareness mediates this relationship. Third, organizational context conditions these effects: workplace ostracism weakens the positive influence of mindfulness on social-justice awareness and PDJS, whereas organizational justice buffers this detrimental effect. These results make three contributions. First, we extend mindfulness research by demonstrating its relevance to managers’ perceptions of societal outcomes. Second, we empirically support the mindfulness capability for social justice theory by identifying social-justice awareness as the key mechanism linking mindfulness to PDJS. Third, we establish organizational context as an important boundary condition, showing when the societal benefits of mindfulness are weakened or preserved. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Kocak F.; Park G.
Author full names: Kocak, Furkan (61010375900); Park, Gyunam (57210637161)
Title: Toward Automated Ticket Escalation in Customer Support Processes: From Emails to Explainable Predictions
Abstract: Business processes in customer support often remain undocumented, with critical decisions such as ticket escalation relying on tacit knowledge rather than explicit process models. Automating such process decisions is challenging because the underlying data is unstructured email text, not structured event logs assumed by existing process mining and predictive monitoring approaches. We present a novel pipeline artifact that addresses this gap: a semi-automated four-stage pipeline that extracts structured features from customer support emails using large language models (LLMs) together with lightweight domain-expert validation, and employs explainable machine learning to predict the optimal timing of ticket creation, a key decision point in the support process. Our pipeline generates an initial feature schema from sample threads, consolidates semantically similar features through embedding-based clustering under domain-expert review, extracts cumulative feature values at each email point, and constructs a structured dataset ready for machine learning. We introduce a SHAP-based active feature learning strategy that identifies which missing features, when acquired, would most improve prediction confidence, enabling principled decisions about when to request additional information versus making immediate predictions. We evaluate our approach in two stages: first, on a reproducible synthetic dataset where comparison against six baselines demonstrates that LLM-extracted features provide complementary semantic information, with combined features achieving the best overall performance (ROC-AUC 0.90) while end-to-end LLM classification performs worst (ROC-AUC 0.46), validating our design of using LLMs as feature extractors rather than decision makers; second, on 1,500 email instances from 800 real-world email threads from Nosco, a commercial CRM platform, where we demonstrate effective feature extraction, predictive performance, and active feature learning for practical deployment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Authors: Cao N.A.T.; Nguyen N.T.
Author full names: Cao, Nhan Anh Thi (59935703700); Nguyen, Ngoc Tien (57209181081)
Title: The board of directors characteristics research: A bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer and Rstudi
Abstract: The Board of Directors (BOD) is widely recognized as a central governance mechanism influencing corporate effectiveness, strategic decision-making, and organizational performance. As corporate governance challenges have intensified in the post–global financial crisis era, scholarly interest in board characteristics has expanded significantly, generating a rapidly growing and fragmented body of literature. In response, this study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to systematically map the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and emerging research trends in studies on board of directors’ characteristics over the period 2014–2025. Using 862 peer-reviewed journal articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, this study applies performance analysis and science mapping techniques with the support of Bibliometrix (R) and VOSviewer. The analysis includes descriptive statistics, citation and co-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, three-field plots, and thematic evolution analysis. The results show that publication output has grown a lot since 2018, with Spain, the United States, the United Kingdom, and China being the most important contributors. The bibliographic coupling and cocitation analyses identify three dominant thematic clusters: (1) corporate governance, corporate social responsibility (CSR), and firm performance; (2) board characteristics and firm outcomes; and (3) ownership structure, governance mechanisms, and firm performance. Furthermore, thematic evolution analysis highlights a gradual shift from traditional board structure and agency-oriented research toward emerging themes related to board diversity, ESG (environmental, social, and governance), audit committees, executive roles, and sustainability-oriented governance. By extending the temporal scope beyond earlier bibliometric reviews and incorporating advanced visualization techniques, this study provides updated and more nuanced evidence on the evolution of board characteristics research. The findings contribute to the corporate governance literature by illustrating the field’s theoretical transition toward broader stakeholder-oriented perspectives and provide helpful suggestions to scholars, practitioners, and policymakers seeking to enhance governance effectiveness in an increasingly sustainability-driven business environment. © 2026 The Beryl Institute. Title: An Integration Between Blockchain Technology and Artificial Intelligence in the Urban Population
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Nowadays, cities face diverse issues, including traffic congestion, disorganized urban planning, rising house prices, and the consequent increase in CO2 emissions. In this vein, this study aims to examine the benefits and drawbacks of integrating cutting-edge technologies, specifically Blockchain Technology (BT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), to advance sustainability and align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the urban population. This research conducted a systematic literature review analysing 25 research papers published between 2009 and June 2025, indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database. Findings show that applying AI and BT in urban populations improves road conditions for smart mobility, enhances citizen security and participation, improves waste management, reduces counterfeiting in supply chains, and diminishes energy consumption in smart buildings. Nonetheless, there is a series of concerns, among them, economic, social, legal, educational, and environmental. Implementing groundbreaking technologies could lead not only to positive implications but also to negative consequences, such as unemployment, privacy issues, a lack of knowledge, or excessive energy consumption. Moreover, this study proposes diverse ideas to make cities more environmentally friendly, such as gamified apps, crypto payments, or AI systems, to name but a few. Furthermore, this paper contributes theoretically by explaining the relationships among AI, BT, and urban sustainability, and practically by providing policymakers and businesses with insights to improve various sectors of smart cities. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Inventory management: A strategic approach to profitability in microenterprises in La Candelaria – Medellín
Abstract: The objective of this research was to analyze inventory management from a strategic perspective, with a focus on profitability, in microenterprises in the commercial sector of La Candelaria, Medellín. It was developed using a descriptive qualitative methodology that incorporated fundamental quantitative analysis in the processing of the results. Simple random sampling was used to select 137 participating microenterprises, which were then interviewed using a previously validated semi-structured interview guide. The instrument explored four central themes: daily inventory management practices, tools used to control stock, product storage and rotation strategies, and the perceived relationship between inventory management and business profitability. The findings were classified into three categories: organizational practices in inventory management and control; inventory optimization: strategies and challenges; and inventory management as a factor in business success. It was found that most microenterprises review their inventories monthly, although the frequency varies according to product turnover. Seventy-eight percent of microenterprises do not utilize specialized software, instead relying on manual controls and traditional methods. Turnover is measured by tracking sales, counting units, and comparing initial and final stock, without resorting to technical indicators or formal accounting formulas. Factors affecting turnover include the season of the year (45.99%), fashion trends (31.39%), and poor internal management (22.62%). Microenterprises employ promotions, offers, and sales to accelerate inventory turnover. All respondents recognize the strategic importance of inventory management for decision-making, stock adjustment, and competitive advantage. 59.12% indicate that effective turnover increases profits, 24.09% that it improves cash flow, and 16.79% that it facilitates the incorporation of new products. Although these productive units have a solid empirical base and show interest in optimizing inventories, operational weaknesses remain—especially in data systematization for strategic decisions—whose improvement would strengthen competitiveness, efficiency, and long-term sustainability. © 2027, Malque Publishing. Title: Multi-scale, multi-dimensional data mining for agentic AI micro-dramas recommendations
Abstract: Micro-dramas, also known as micro-short dramas, are ultra-short, serialized video series optimized for mobile viewing, with episodes typically lasting 1–20 min. Agentic AI recommendation refers to an autonomous, interactive, and goal-oriented AI system that transcends traditional recommendation paradigms. The framework addresses challenges related to data heterogeneity, dynamic user interactions, and context-aware decision-making. Using a sample of 3,016 Taiwanese consumers, we first segmented users into three distinct clusters via K-means analysis. Subsequently, association rules were mined within each cluster to uncover behavioral patterns and preferences related to micro-drama consumption and cross-screen e-commerce activities. The results provide actionable insights for micro-drama producers and e-commerce operators, enabling the design of personalized content and integrated business strategies. Title: Digital Sovereignty in Organisational End-to-End Processes: An Early-Stage Design-Oriented Research Roadmap
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: European organisations increasingly depend on cloud-based and AI-enabled services provided by non-European vendors. These dependencies create sovereignty-relevant risks emerging within operational processes, not only at policy or infrastructure levels. Existing research addresses digital sovereignty primarily from state-centric, legal, and technical perspectives. How sovereignty concerns arise within organisational process design remains insufficiently researched. This paper presents early-stage doctoral research developing a conceptual framework for analysing digital sovereignty at the organisational level. A concept-driven literature review synthesises multi-level and discursive-category perspectives into an analytical schema. The schema locates four process-level sovereignty challenges (control, accountability, decision authority, and autonomy) across governance levels and claim types. The framework conceptualises digital sovereignty as an organisational capability by mapping dynamic capability activities onto Business Process Management (BPM) practice phases. Title: Neuro-symbolic predictive process monitoring for multi-attribute suffix prediction
Abstract: Leveraging historical process execution data to predict the evolution of an ongoing process is a challenging task in Business Process Management. In recent years, transformer-based models have shown promising results in multi-attribute sequence prediction, which refers to the task of forecasting not only the next activity in a process but also its associated attributes (e.g., timestamp, resource, and data values). However, although the accuracy of these models is generally high, there are specific situations in which background knowledge about the process can be beneficial. In particular, such knowledge can improve prediction quality for outlier executions in the training data and in scenarios where process changes occur due to concept drift in the test data. In this paper, we propose a principled method for integrating prior knowledge into an autoregressive transformer-based model for multi-attribute sequence prediction at test time. This knowledge is expressed using Multi-Perspective Declare, a process modeling language capable of describing process behavior from multiple perspectives, including control flow (i.e., the expected sequence of activities executed in the process), data flow (i.e., the data attributes associated with these activities during process execution), resources, and timestamps. We evaluate our method on real-life event logs and demonstrate that incorporating background knowledge consistently improves the performance of multi-attribute sequence prediction, especially in rare and exceptional situations. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: A Hybrid Conversational Framework for Interactive Data Analysis and Time Series Forecasting Using Large Language Models
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The integration of conversational artificial intelligence with data analysis enables broader access to insights. Currently, powerful AI-enabled prebuilt tools such as Tableau GPT, Power BI Copilot, Looker, and OAC are used for data preparation, data analysis, visualisation and faster decision making operating within platform-specific ecosystems. Existing methods of forecasting and dataset exploration present accurate and reliable analysis connecting to data sources linked to them but often rely on technical skills and complex interfaces that may limit their use by non-expert users requiring them to follow predefined workflow. To address this, we present a conversational AI-powered framework that integrates natural language querying, dataset exploration, visualisation and time-series forecasting in a single chatbot interface without the need to download and install the application or purchase license. The framework relies on large language models via Azure OpenAI, LangChain and Prophet library. Users can upload CSV datasets and pose queries through natural language prompts with the system providing text-based outputs. Evaluative measures ensure forecasting reliability and accuracy of the chatbot. We also describe experiments to demonstrate the system’s ability to interpret forecasting results, identify temporal patterns, enhanced by visualisations to illustrate analysis. The framework shows promise in terms of its performance and future work will concentrate on extending the framework through contextual memory, multimodal dataset input and large-scale evaluation adaptable across diverse data sources such as education, health care and business intelligence. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Study Regarding the Digital Transformation of Quality Management in Knowledge-Based Industrial Organizations

Abstract: The paper examines how digital technologies transform quality assurance processes in knowledge-based organizations, from data collection and processing to reporting and continuous improvement. It focuses on environments where knowledge, collaboration and fast access to reliable information are critical for organizational performance and innovation. The study evaluates solutions such as integrated digital quality management platforms, automated approval workflows, audit and nonconformity management modules, as well as advanced data analytics and business intelligence tools. It proposes a conceptual model for integrating these technologies into existing processes, with emphasis on reducing human errors, increasing traceability, standardizing procedures and shortening response times. The model is aligned with organizational maturity levels and governance structures, highlighting the conditions under which automation generates measurable improvements in quality performance. The paper includes scenarios and use cases that illustrate how end-to-end digital workflows and real-time quality indicators can support faster and better-informed managerial decisions. Based on these analyses, the study formulates recommendations for prioritizing digital investments in quality assurance, guiding organizations from basic digitization of documents and records towards integrated, data-driven quality management. Title: Co-founder selection from a marriage market perspective: How the dark triad shapes judgments of interpersonal attraction, resources, and equity demand
Abstract: Co-founder selection is a pivotal decision in new venture formation, yet how lead founders evaluate potential partners remains underexplored. Drawing on insights from marriage market theory, we conceptualize co-founder selection as an act of individuated judgment guided by cooperative logic and associated joint utility projection, wherein lead founders assess co-founder candidates based on social-emotional, instrumental, and distributive considerations reflected in interpersonal attraction, resource contributions, and equity demand. We further propose that lead founders' dark triad shifts this judgmental process from joint utility logic to personal utility maximization. Using a conjoint experiment with 206 entrepreneurs making 3296 co-founder selection decisions, we find that interpersonal attraction and resource contributions positively influence willingness to select a co-founder candidate, whereas higher equity demand reduces candidate attractiveness. Critically, lead founders higher in the dark triad display distinct patterns: they discount interpersonal attraction and display heightened sensitivity to equity dilution—assessments that indicate their prioritization of personal over joint value creation. Taken together, these findings reveal how dispositional tendencies influence the judgments underlying co-founder selection, indicating a shift away from the cooperative logic assumed in marriage market theory and co-founder selection toward greater emphasis on personal utility considerations. We discuss theoretical implications of these findings and offer practical guidance for navigating the complexities of co-founder selection. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Multi-dimensional Summarization Agents with Context-Aware Reasoning over Enterprise Tables

Abstract: We propose a novel framework for summarizing structured enterprise data across multiple dimensions using large language model (LLM)-based agents. Traditional table-to-text models often lack the capacity to reason across hierarchical structures and context-aware deltas, which are essential in business reporting tasks. Our method introduces a multi-agent pipeline that extracts, analyzes, and summarizes multi-dimensional data using agents for slicing, variance detection, context construction, and LLM-based generation. The improvements are especially pronounced in categories involving subtle trade-offs, such as increased revenue due to price changes amid declining unit volumes, which competing methods either overlook or address with limited specificity. Title: Making the Metaverse Viable: Vendor Framings and the Conditional Realisation of Sustainable Value
Abstract: Extended reality (XR) and digital twin (DT) solutions are increasingly presented as technologies that can create organisational value and support sustainability. Yet these claims are often made in emerging and uncertain markets, where clients may not immediately understand what the technologies are for, how they may generate value, or under what conditions that value becomes relevant for sustainability. Vendors are therefore important because they translate XR/DT possibilities into client-facing value propositions. However, less is known about how vendors present these technologies as valuable for clients and connect such value claims to sustainability. This qualitative exploratory study draws on semi-structured interviews with 16 domain experts involved in the development, provision, implementation, or organisational use of Metaverse-related solutions. The data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings identify a vendor-side conditional value pathway in which vendors first made XR/DT commercially recognisable and justifiable and then emphasised technological possibilities. Whether these possibilities became practically valuable depended on organisational, technical, material, and ecosystem conditions. Sustainability implications were associated with substitution, reconfigured participation, and context-dependent trade-offs. The study therefore interprets XR/DT as conditional sustainability mediators. Particular uses can connect technological possibilities to sustainability implications, but these implications are neither inherent nor automatic. The study contributes an account of how vendors connect XR/DT value propositions to sustainability, while recognising that the findings reflect participants’ accounts rather than independently verified client outcomes or sustainability impacts. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Deception and detection: The impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-based resume screening on entry-level job seekers’ deceptive behaviors
Abstract: Recognizing the unintended consequences of artificial intelligence (AI) in resume screening, this research investigated whether AI-based resume screening increases deceptive behaviors among entry-level job seekers. Across four experiments involving common forms of resume deception, we demonstrated that AI is perceived as less effective at detecting deception, resulting in increased deceptive behaviors, compared with human resume screening. These interventions significantly improved AI’s perceived detectability, making AI-based resume screening more effective at discouraging deceptive intentions and experience inflation in resume reporting. Title: Innovating for a Sustainable Future: The Interplay of Green, Socially Responsible, and Sustainable HRM Practices

Abstract: Organizations, in their efforts to meet the sustainability goals set worldwide, have no option but to adopt the environment and society-friendly practices while at the same time getting pressure. Moreover, one of the key motivations behind the present research is to study the overlapping areas and integration of these three variables and to uncover their potential in terms of sustainability and innovation. Utilizing a PRISMA method, this research has analyzed 179 research articles dating from 2008 to 2025 to discover the trends, theme clusters, and their contributions to sustainability. According to the results, one of the most efficient methods to foster innovation is through GHRM, and at the same time, SRHRM and SHRM are becoming very popular due to the no-brainer of their practices being close to GHRM. The implications of this research are significant for both theorists and practitioners who need to consider the areas of innovation, green creativity, sustainability, and digital transformation as main drivers. Title: A Smart Framework for Integrating Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and IoT in Construction Project Management

Abstract: The construction sector continues to face persistent structural challenges, including execution delays, recurring cost overruns, low productivity, fragmented communication among stakeholders, and limited levels of technological maturity. These issues are particularly acute in developing economies, where small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) dominate the industry. This study aims to formulate and validate a comprehensive framework that supports the effective integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, and the Internet of Things (IoT) into construction and civil engineering project management, with a specific focus on SMEs while remaining applicable to larger organizations. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, comprising four stages: a bibliometric analysis of academic literature published between 2015 and 2024 to identify trends, methodologies, and application areas of emerging technologies; a 21-item Likert-type survey administered to 55 Colombian construction-related companies to assess their level of digital maturity; the formulation of the Comprehensive Model for incorporating Technologies into Construction and Civil Engineering Project Management (CMTCCPM); and its validation through a two-round Delphi study involving five international experts. The results indicate an average digital maturity level of 2.8 out of 5, with relatively higher development in customer and supplier management and significant weaknesses in Industry 4.0 strategy and experience. The proposed model integrates interoperable BIM 5D/6D, connected digital twins, AI-assisted predictive maintenance, advanced analytics, circular material tokenization, smart certifications, and ethical AI frameworks to enhance planning, risk management, automated execution, intelligent operation and maintenance, sustainability, and digital governance. Expert validation yielded an average score of 4.51 out of 5, highlighting high relevance, feasibility, innovation, and impact, and recommending the inclusion of implementation roadmaps, key performance indicators, and ROI-oriented business cases. Title: Unpleasant moral memory and the formation of inclusive orientation under incomplete institutional guidance
Abstract: Leaders increasingly face decisions about what inclusion requires in settings where formal guidance is incomplete or unevenly applied, a situation this study conceptualizes as institutional ambiguity. Title: Strategies for Efficient Cost Management in Hybrid Cloud It Infrastructure
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Hybrid cloud infrastructures offer organizations substantial flexibility, elasticity, and operational scalability; however, they also introduce complex financial risks associated with multi-cloud environments, including hidden costs related to re-source consumption, data transfers, licensing models, and ongoing maintenance. Effective cost management in such ecosystems requires an integrated governance framework that combines financial discipline with technical optimization and operational efficiency. This study examines key strategies for achieving financial control in hybrid cloud environments, emphasizing the role of FinOps as a collaborative model that aligns IT, finance, and business units in decision-making. Core mechanisms include policy-as-code for automated enforcement of cost-related rules, accurate capacity planning and right-sizing of resources, as well as workload placement based on performance, compliance, and cost metrics. Additionally, techniques such as data location optimization, caching, compression, and the use of spot/preemptible instances are highlighted as essential approaches for reducing operational expenditures. Advanced capabilities including real-time observability, multi-cloud cost dashboards, and artificial intelligence-driven dynamic resource allocation further enhance financial predictability and operational efficiency. Title: Mapping Migrant Entrepreneurship and Integration in Italy: A Descriptive Analysis
Abstract: This chapter analyses migrant entrepreneurship and migrant integration in Italy, examining their interaction across provinces between 2013 and 2022. Using an original dataset covering 102 provinces and 24 economic sectors, the study reconstructs the evolution, sectoral structure, and territorial distribution of foreign individual-owned firms (self-employment), alongside two composite integration indicators: the Social Integration Index and the Occupational Integration Index. Results show a steady growth of migrant entrepreneurship. Title: What, how, and where: the effects of multidimensional CSR communication strategies focusing on content, framing, and target
Abstract: As corporate social responsibility (CSR) becomes important, so does consumer skepticism, making it difficult for firms to communicate CSR as intended. Integrating the Tri-dimensional CSR Model with Activating Events-Beliefs-Consequences (ABC) cognitive theory, this study exploratorily examined the differential effects of what firms communicate (content domain), how they frame and deliver CSR messages (strategic orientation and operational perspective), and where these messages are received (U.S. and China) on consumers’ CSR motivation perceptions and behavioral intentions. To examine these multi-faceted CSR communication effects, a 3x2x2 experiment was conducted with U.S. and Chinese samples. Three-way MANCOVA revealed that consumers’ CSR motivation perceptions differ by the what, how, and where aspects of CSR communications. Title: HASTE: Enhancing Fraud Detection in Financial Time Series with the Novel Ensemble Hierarchical Transformer Framework
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Fraud detection in financial transactions is challenged by extreme class imbalance, concept drift, high-dimensional feature spaces, and the need to balance detection performance with false positives. This study introduces HASTE (Hierarchical Attention-based Stacked Ensemble), a deep learning architecture that integrates multiple base models via a hierarchical attention mechanism with temporal awareness. HASTE dynamically weights base model predictions based on input features, enabling adaptive prioritization of high-confidence fraud predictions and improved robustness to evolving fraud patterns. The model is evaluated against Random Forest, SVM, and Logistic Regression on four benchmark datasets: BankSim, FraudGuard (22% fraud with concept drift), IEEE-CIS, and PaySim. Using statistical evaluation, McNemar’s significance testing, and business impact analysis, HASTE consistently outperforms all baselines. Key results include a 91.3% relative F1 improvement on IEEE-CIS and 88.8% on PaySim, along with statistically significant gains over SVM on three of four datasets. Most importantly, HASTE demonstrates strong economic performance, achieving ROI improvements of 56% on BankSim, 93% on FraudGuard, 105% on IEEE-CIS, and 144% on PaySim. These results highlight its robustness across diverse fraud scenarios, including severe imbalance and concept drift. Title: Processes of multi-system co-evolution: Insights from carbon capture and storage in Norway
Abstract: Net-zero solutions such as carbon capture and storage (CCS) require the creation of whole new clusters of innovations rather than “merely” a transition in existing systems or the diffusion of single technologies. While prior work highlights negative cross-system interdependencies (e.g., chicken and egg problems), this paper presents a theorization and an empirical study of the processes of multi-system co-evolution that contribute to the formation and development of multi-system complexes. To do this, a framework that integrates the concepts of a meta-rule, structural couplings (institutional, technological, organizational) and complementarity formation mechanisms — synchronization, amplification, and integration — is developed. The framework is illustrated through a qualitative case study of two Norwegian carbon capture and storage projects, Mongstad (2006–2013) and Longship (2016–), drawing on a broad range of media and documentary sources, including policy documents and funding agreements, and 20 interviews. The analysis shows how, in Longship, actors have sought to realize CCS by, for example, (i) fostering coordination and simultaneous co-development between CCS systems via contracts and standards, (ii) enabling CCS systems to expand and diffuse via a scalable ship-to-terminal transport design; and (iii) creating robustness in CCS multi-system complex by involving multiple actors, user sectors and business cases. This differed from Mongstad, where actors failed to prioritize the management of CCS system couplings and related uncertainties. The paper proposes how the processes of multi-system co-evolution can be conceptualized, and explores how actors may seek to deal with the issue of system interdependencies in sustainability transitions. © 2026 The Authors. Title: A multi-product operations-emission cost optimization model with stochastic demand
Abstract: Production of multiple products sequentially is widely practiced in industries. Their unpredictable demands and lead times generate inefficient supply chain flow in meeting demands. Besides, production-based business activities emit carbon. However, researchers developed conventional inventory models with deterministic/stochastic demand, ignoring environmental impact. Here we present a model assuming stochastic demands of products processed sequentially by incorporating the costs of operations and multi-source carbon emissions. A lot of a product is assumed to be multiple of its demand plus approximated safety stock. Usually, larger production in lesser setups minimizes setup and processing costs imposing higher holding and carbon emission costs (due to warehousing and temperature control), and vice versa. Consolidated shipments with fuel-efficient slower transportation decrease transportation cost and carbon emission, requiring higher lot sizes and safety stocks, increasing inventory-related carbon emission. This operations-emission cost trade-off encompasses balancing these conflicting objectives. We minimize this total cost via calculus method of differentiation, synchronizing the production flow of satisfying demand of a product during production of other products. The model is illustrated with an example problem and applied to a local Coca-Cola production plant of bottling five types of this beverage. Minimum total carbon emission cost is found to be about 30-32% of the minimum total cost for the former, and 12-13% for the latter. When standard deviation of demands and lead times are jointly increased by 30%, the minimum total cost increases by 5.44%. Finally, results of sensitivity analyses on various parameters and managerial implication of the optimal solution policy are highlighted. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Sena I.; Mendes J.; Pereira A.I.
Title: A Comparative NLP Study of Semantic and Thematic Changes in AI Research Pre - and Post-generative AI
Abstract: With the advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly with the emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs), has significantly influenced the scope, accessibility, and dissemination of scientific research. This evolution raises important questions regarding how AI-related scientific discourse has changed over time. This study search lexical, semantic, and thematic changes in a dataset of approximately 50,000 AI-related publications retrieved from the Web of Science (WoS), comparing a pre-GenAI period (2015–2019) with a post-GenAI period (2022–2025). Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques were applied, including TF-IDF for lexical analysis, Logistic Regression for temporal classification, and BERTopic for topic modeling. The results achieved an accuracy of 89%, revealing a clear separability between the two periods based on textual features. The analyses reveal a transition from predominantly technical and methodological terminology, focused on algorithms and infrastructure, toward more application-oriented and generative themes, including GenAI and LLMs. Furthermore, topic modeling shows the growing prominence of interdisciplinary domains such as education, healthcare, and business applications in the post-GenAI period. Overall, the findings suggest a significant lexical and thematic evolution in AI-related scientific discourse, reflecting broader transformations in research priorities and application domains following the emergence of GenAI technologies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Process Management in the Adoption of Digital Solutions: Lessons from Healthcare for Industry 4.0

Abstract: Digital transformation is redefining how organisations structure and manage their processes, creating new paradigms of efficiency and adaptability under Industry 4.0. Based on quantitative research conducted among 100 healthcare providers in Slovakia, the article analyses the relationships between leadership characteristics, workplace type, experience, and the degree of digital tool adoption. Authors: Zhang C.; Li M.; Su F.; Tao R.
Title: Political patronage, rent-extraction, and social costs: Evidence from China's environmental cleanup
Source title: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
Abstract: This paper investigates how informal political patronage subverts environmental regulation and local economic performance in China. We demonstrate that patronage provides local officials with political insurance, enabling them to safely shield polluting firms from top-down enforcement. Contrary to the promotion tournament hypothesis, this forbearance does not drive GDP growth. Instead, it is sustained through localized rent extraction. Utilizing firm-level data and shocks induced by provincial party secretary turnover, we find that connected officials extract a political tax, measured via perk expenditures, from both polluting and non-polluting enterprises. This systemic extortion generates broad negative spillovers: while shielding incumbent polluters, patronage crowds out productive investment and deters clean market entrants, ultimately degrading both environmental outcomes and the regional business environment. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: The IFIP WG5.7 Service Systems Special Interest Group Renewed Research Framework and Agenda on Product-Service Systems and Digital Servitization

Abstract: Product-Service Systems (PSSs) and Digital Servitization are increasingly recognized as key enablers for sustainable and data-driven industrial transformation. However, the rapid evolution of digital technologies, circular economy principles, and service ecosystems is reshaping the PSS research landscape, calling for updated and integrated research frameworks. This paper proposes a Research Framework and Agenda developed within the IFIP WG5.7 Special Interest Group (SIG) on Service Systems Design, Engineering and Management (SSDE&M). The Research Framework and Agenda are grounded in a two-step methodology combining an online brainstorming workshop and a structured survey involving the SIG members. The results identify and structure current research priorities across five core research areas, while also revealing emerging research themes related to ecosystem integration, data-driven value creation, and lifecycle management. Building on these insights, the proposed Research Framework and Agenda organise PSS research into three interconnected levels: (i) Design and Methods, (ii) Business and Organizational Transformation, and (iii) Ecosystem and Governance Context, complemented by four cross-cutting analytical dimensions: (i) Circular Economy and Rebound Effects, (ii) Digital Technologies and Artificial Intelligence, (iii) Service Ecosystems and Governance, and (iv) Responsible and Socially Sustainable Service Systems. The proposed Research Framework and Agenda contribute to consolidating fragmented research streams and provide a structured basis for future research work within the IFIP WG5.7 SSDE&M SIG and broader PSS research community, supporting both academic research and industrial practice. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Strategic leadership in cross-border mergers and acquisitions: a unified CEO advice-seeking framework
Abstract: Cross-border mergers and acquisitions (CBMAs) require executives to coordinate decisions across resource, institutional, organizational, and stakeholder domains. Yet CBMA literature largely examines these challenges separately, offering limited explanations of how executives mobilize expertise across them. This study synthesizes the intellectual structure of CBMA research using bibliometric and thematic analysis of 1,833 articles published between 1970 and 2023. Viewed through the lens of the CEO advice-seeking framework, the themes translate into several executive challenges. Title: How consumers respond to social media influencers’ cross-domain recommendations?——A person brand perspective
Abstract: Influencer marketing has become an integrated component of marketing strategy for many companies competing in the current digital marketplace. However, research on how to enhance its effectiveness is still limited. Taking social media influencers as person brands, this study investigates key factors influencing consumer reactions towards social media influencers’ cross-domain recommendations from a brand extension perspective. Through five experiments, this study shows that (1) when social media influencers make cross-domain recommendations, purchase motivation moderates the effect of domain relevance on consumers’ purchase intentions, with hedonic consumers more tolerant of low-relevance recommendations; (2) perceived influencer authenticity mediates the effect of domain relevance on purchase intentions but only for functional (vs. hedonic) consumers; (3) when low-relevance products are recommended, hedonic (vs. functional) consumers are inclined to purchase products from warm (vs. competent) influencers. Title: From Text to Economic Exposure: Measuring Intrinsic Risk in Urban Real Estate
Abstract: Corporate disclosures usually describe the firm’s strategies, expectations, and perceived risks. Beyond purely numerical indicators, these narratives provide a broader and often more nuanced view of the firm. In this sense, working with textual information allows researchers to capture and organize these insights in a more structured and meaningful way. The starting point of this paper is that traditional classifications, such as sector categories or fixed developer typologies, are often too rigid to reflect the diversity of the firms that are operating in the built environment. In practice, mixed-use models, infrastructure-linked assets, and the changing nature of urban functions tend to blur these boundaries. For this reason, the study has adopted an approach that considers firms as interpreters of economic and urban change, drawing on their own published language to capture underlying exposure. The empirical strategy builds a textual corpus for each firm, using sources such as regulatory filings, investor presentations, earnings calls, and business descriptions. Embeddings then convert these texts into semantic representations, enabling them to position firms within a continuous economic space. Rather than assigning each firm to a single category, similarity within this space is used to infer partial exposure to different economic narratives. This makes it possible to identify shared sensitivities to structural drivers, such as financing conditions, tenant composition, logistics demand, retrofit pressures, technological change, and urban redevelopment. Afterward, it incorporates these semantic exposures into a multi-factor risk model, which distinguishes common structural risk from firm-specific residual risk. By incorporating semantic exposures into a multi-factor risk model, the analysis distinguishes common structural risk from firm-specific residual risk. Real estate benefits particularly from this framework. Interest-rate shocks, liquidity stress, and capital allocation changes can alter firm risk in real estate before conventional classifications fully capture these alterations. More broadly, the study links firm-level narratives, asset pricing, and urban transformation, showing how the analysis of corporate text can contribute to a more adaptive understanding of risk. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: An Analysis of Mobility Styles and Carsharing Adoption Intentions in Major Urban Areas of Japan: Evidence from Tokyo, Osaka, and Kanagawa
Abstract: This study links mobility styles with carsharing intentions and next-generation vehicle preferences in urban Japan. An online survey of licensed drivers in Tokyo Metropolis, Kanagawa Prefecture, and Osaka Prefecture captured mode use frequencies and stated preferences by travel purpose. Cluster analysis identified three mobility styles: private-car users, public-transport users, and a diversified, high-carsharing group. The diversified profile combined high carsharing participation with high private-car ownership, indicating that carsharing can complement rather than replace existing car access. Random Forest results indicate that age, car usage frequency, and income best distinguish carsharing users from non-users. Carsharing preferences varied substantially by stated-use context. For daily and business trips, most respondents prefer carsharing stations within 400 m and short distances; for tourism and hometown visiting, they accept longer access to carsharing stations and longer trips. Compact and Kei cars (Japanese light vehicles) in Japan dominate daily use, while minivans and SUVs gain importance for leisure. Gasoline and hybrid vehicles are most preferred, with limited willingness to pay extra for electric vehicles. The findings support segment- and purpose-specific carsharing station placement, fleet composition, and gradual electrification strategies in mature, transit-rich metropolitan areas. © 2026 Hong Kong Society for Transportation Studies

Title: Design Strategies and Solutions for Circularity Across the Building Lifecycle
Source title: SpringerBriefs in Applied Sciences and Technology
Abstract: The built environment is one of the most resource-intensive sectors globally, yet progress towards circularity remains constrained by fragmented implementation, limited lifecycle integration, and insufficient governance frameworks. This chapter examines design strategies and solutions for circularity across the entire building lifecycle, drawing on a systematic comparative analysis of 45 international case studies. Using a matrix-based analytical framework, circular strategies are mapped across six dimensions: design for circularity, materials and products, construction practices, building operations and maintenance, end-of-life and deconstruction, and business models and policy support, and aligned with the 10R circular economy hierarchy. The findings reveal a clear concentration of circular maturity at the design and material levels, with strategies such as adaptability, flexibility, design for disassembly, and low-carbon material selection widely present across the dataset. In contrast, operational circularity, advanced end-of-life planning, digital traceability, and enabling business models remain significantly underdeveloped in mainstream practice. Cross-case analysis identifies five building clusters and six transferable circular design patterns, ranging from reuse-first approaches and design for disassembly as a system, to procurement-driven circularity and use-based strategies. The evidence consistently demonstrates that high circular performance is achieved through integrated, multi-lifecycle-stage approaches rather than isolated interventions. Policy and practice recommendations are derived directly from the pattern analysis, targeting design regulation, public procurement, operational management, and end-of-life governance. The chapter concludes that scaling circularity requires moving beyond project-based experimentation toward systemic frameworks that connect design intent, supply chain mechanisms, and institutional conditions across the full building lifecycle. © The Author(s) 2027.

Title: Board gender diversity, cultural logics, and corporate tax behaviour
Abstract: Corporate tax aggressiveness tests corporate accountability, yet less is known about when board gender diversity translates into more restrained tax behaviour across institutional settings. Using 27,275 firm-year observations from 29 countries across Europe, Asia, and Australasia during 2013–2023, we examine whether board gender diversity is associated with lower tax aggressiveness and whether national culture conditions this association. Board gender diversity is negatively associated with tax aggressiveness: greater female board representation is associated with higher cash effective tax rates and more restrained tax behaviour. This association is stronger in high masculinity, uncertainty avoidance, and long-term orientation settings, but weaker in high power distance, individualism, and indulgence settings. Results are robust to an alternative sign-reversed accrual-based tax proxy, lagged board gender diversity, placebo randomisation, entropy balancing, and two-step difference GMM. The findings contribute to business ethics, governance, and tax research by showing that culture shapes how female board representation translates into accountability-relevant tax outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
