Title: Bringing arts integration to universal pre-K: Variation in impact of New York City’s Create
Abstract: Professional learning with training and coaching has been shown to improve preschool classroom quality and strengthen children’s school readiness skills. Even so, training in the arts has rarely been studied in early childhood education, even though this approach is aligned with teachers’ interests and has been shown to support children’s learning and engagement. We examine heterogeneity in the impacts of Create, an arts-integrated professional learning program developed by NYC Public Schools for Pre-K for All. We analyzed 437 pre-K students in 47 sites randomized to Create or business-as-usual as part of a research-practice partnership. We estimate variation in impacts of Create on children’s assessed skills in reading, math, executive function, and self-regulation by children’s neighborhood income, gender, and whether the child is a Dual Language Learner (DLL). This exploratory study is the first to examine impact heterogeneity of arts integration professional learning on children’s school readiness. Create appears to be broadly effective across neighborhood subgroups; there were no statistically significant differences in the strength of impacts across lower vs. higher income neighborhood groups. Impacts of Create differed by child gender on language and literacy, favoring boys. Finally, impacts of Create were far stronger for a small sample of DLLs on literacy, math, executive function, and attention regulation scores. This suggests that Create may be an effective professional learning series for teachers to engage diverse groups of children through the arts, even while further research is needed to confirm these promising findings. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Unboxing the dynamic-capability microfoundations of springboard internationalization: strategic brand transformation in emerging-market firms
Abstract: Emerging-market firms (EMFs) increasingly transform from brandless manufacturing subcontractors into international brand competitors, yet springboard internationalization theory has left the internal organizational dynamics of this leap underspecified. Integrating a dynamic-capability mechanism into the springboard framework, this study theorizes the 3A architecture—Adaptability, Ambidexterity, and Amalgamation—as the EMF-specific tailoring of dynamic capabilities, anchoring each at a distinct layer of internal transformation. Organizational learning culture (Adaptability) activates two complementary knowledge-development streams (Ambidexterity), which enable two strategic levers (Amalgamation) that build brand-based differentiation advantage and, in turn, superior international performance. We test this processual model with a mixed-method design combining qualitative evidence from ten transformed EMFs and a two-wave longitudinal survey of 1,114 Taiwanese firms analyzed through cross-lagged structural equation modeling. Results support the full hypothesized sequence, robust across endogeneity, heterogeneity, and confounding checks. The study specifies the dynamic-capability microfoundations of springboard internationalization and repositions brand as a rent-yielding strategic resource. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: Ownership structure and the international expansion of German firms
Abstract: Despite decades of falling trade barriers and advancing globalization, most multinational enterprises (MNEs) never venture beyond their home region. We argue that part of the explanation lies in ownership structure: who ultimately controls the firm determines how broadly it operates and how freely its geographic scope can be adjusted. Drawing on the attention-based view, we derive eight hypotheses about how ownership origin, international experience, and concentration shape the breadth of geographic scope and the direction of its adjustment over time. Using a large panel of German MNEs, we show that domestic ownership is associated with broader scope and greater propensity for upward adjustment, with the advantage strongest for internationally experienced owners. Ownership concentration constrains the level of geographic scope but not whether it expands or contracts. These findings provide the first evidence on ownership and geographic scope for developed-country MNEs and reorient theoretical debate from resource transfer to organizational authorization. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc.

Title: A Practical Predictive Maintenance Pipeline Integrating Machine Learning and Deep Learning on the Scania Component X Dataset
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This study focuses on evaluating predictive maintenance (PdM) classification models using the SCANIA Component X dataset released in 2025. The dataset is highly imbalanced, as Component X operates in a healthy state for about 97% of the time, while failures occur only around 3% of the time. This imbalance reflects real maintenance conditions in industry and creates both challenges and opportunities for applying machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models to PdM tasks. The main objective of this study is to develop a complete and practical pipeline for supervised learning models that achieves high prediction performance while reducing maintenance-related costs, thereby providing real business value. The proposed pipeline is structured into four main steps: (1) Business Understanding, (2) Data Understanding, (3) Modeling, and (4) Evaluation. Several models are trained and evaluated, including Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), XGBoost (XGB), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), and Transformer Encoder (TE). In particular, DL models consistently outperform traditional ML approaches under severe class imbalance, with BiLSTM and TE achieve the best performance, with balanced accuracy scores of 0.7767 and 0.7907, and cost per prediction values of 3.1519 and 2.3816 on test set, respectively. In addition, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis is applied to improve model interpretability. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Protection by Entanglement: Inseparable Design-Embedded Watermarks for Manufacturing-as-a-Service (MaaS)
Abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) is a technology that uses 3D printers to manufacture parts based on their digital design without the need for retooling. Thus, it is well suited for the scalable Manufacturing-as-a-Service (MaaS) business model. However, a more flexible but often short-term low-volume manufacturing relationship between customers and providers of this service raises security concerns on both sides. The customer is concerned with the misuse of shared design: Theft, illegal distribution, or infringement of parts are real security threats. The manufacturer, on the other hand, is concerned with a possible bait-and-switch of designs between the quote request and the agreed upon contract. We propose a watermarking solution that addresses this complex threat and mutually protects the parties involved. Watermarking is a technique of embedding information in a defended object, e.g., to assert intellectual property (IP) rights. We exploit the inherent causation between the digital design that defines a part and the physical qualities of the manufactured part to propose a novel method that ensures the robustness of the watermark. While in other domains watermark robustness is commonly achieved through hidden redundancies, our proposal ensures that its removal or manipulation will make the high-quality design unattainable (thus, noticeable in the parts produced: an issue external of the file system!). Note that robustness is a hard-to-achieve property in general because quantifying hidden redundancies is fundamentally difficult. This work achieves this by binding a digital file property to the necessary aspects of the output domain. More generally, our approach is a blueprint for entangling the integrity of the watermark with the utility of the asset. We release the source code developed for this approach under GPL. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Enhanced Document Clustering Using Residue Modulo Partitioner in Map-Reduce Framework

Abstract: Information Retrieval (IR) is a domain within computer science focused on the efficient retrieval of text documents based on user queries containing specific keywords. Recent techniques have proposed various IR frameworks utilizing different data mining algorithms, as well as novel map and reduce approaches, while leveraging default partitioners. Title: Fashion Second-Hand Market and Re-Branding of Humana Portugal: One Strategy for Sustainability and Circular Economy
Source title: Springer Series in Design and Innovation
Abstract: The transformation of the fashion ecosystem from a linear to a circular economy model is driving the development of innovative business models. One way to contribute to the circular economy is by extending the lifecycle of products, either through the purchase of higher-quality items or by enabling these items to have a second life through resale in second-hand clothing stores. This business model, already established in the market, particularly resonates with younger generations, such as Generation Z, both in online and offline retail environments. However, how can the value of second-hand fashion products and brands be effectively enhanced? One approach lies in the implementation of a branding strategy aligned with the values the brand seeks to communicate, supported by a coherent visual identity. This project aims to develop a re-branding strategy for a prominent second-hand fashion brand with national and international relevance: Humana. Based on established branding principles, the objective is to reposition the brand in a way that appeals more strongly to Generation Z consumers—thereby investing in the future while simultaneously fostering awareness of circular economy practices. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Multimodal Process Monitoring with On-demand Disambiguation

Abstract: Process monitoring is increasingly supported by Internet-of-Things (IoT) environments. However, the abstraction of sensor data into process events often leads to ambiguity. Existing approaches that leverage IoT data do not address how to resolve such ambiguity dynamically. To address this challenge, we present MMPMOD, a novel architecture for multimodal process monitoring that detects ambiguity in IoT-based events and orchestrates contextual sensing modalities on-demand to resolve it. Upon ambiguity detection, it activates cameras to capture the visual context, and applies scene understanding to disambiguate events. Title: Neuro-symbolic AI for BPM: A Tutorial on Predictive and Prescriptive Process Analytics
Abstract: Process analytics has become predominantly data-driven: deep sequence models such as LSTMs and Transformers now dominate predictive and prescriptive process monitoring and deliver strong average-case accuracy. These models are, however, opaque, require large amounts of data, and do not incorporate the process knowledge that organizations already hold in the form of regulations, declarative constraints, and reference process models. The symbolic side of Business Process Management (BPM) carries exactly this knowledge but is brittle on noisy, real-world event data. Neuro-symbolic AI (NeSy) aims to bridge these two traditions, and a growing body of BPM work has begun to use it. This tutorial gives the BPM community an accessible overview of the relationship between BPM and NeSy. It introduces Kautz’s architectural taxonomy of NeSy and the Learning from Logical Constraints paradigm together with its main implementation, Logic Tensor Networks. It then traces how NeSy attaches to concrete BPM analytics tasks through a sequence of case studies spanning compliance-aware prediction, robust rule injection, healthcare outcome prediction, and prescriptive analytics. The tutorial highlights the failure modes that practitioners must avoid when injecting domain knowledge into deep process models, examines how to evaluate whether injected knowledge actually helps, and closes with open problems and a practical decision aid for when NeSy is worth adopting. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: When public meets private: How dual digital channels reshape subscription E-commerce
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Leveraging online private-domain channels, retail-controlled platforms accessible only to designated customer segments, for subscription commerce has become a cornerstone for many retailers seeking stable revenue streams and deeper customer engagement. In pursuit of an omnichannel presence, however, an increasing number of retailers have begun to roll out subscription offerings through online public-domain channels: third-party platforms open to all users. The impact of this strategic expansion on their existing private-domain subscription business remains ambiguous. Drawing on Decision Field Theory and granular subscription-order data from a leading subscription retailer, we employ a multi-period difference-in-differences design to assess how the introduction of public-domain channels affects subscription volume and subscription cycle length in private-domain channels. Our findings reveal that public-domain entry negatively affects both subscription volume and subscription cycle in the private-domain channel. However, these adverse effects are attenuated for products whose consumer bases exhibit higher pre-treatment subscription frequency or longer prior subscription cycles. This research offers both theoretical insights and actionable guidance for retailers seeking to calibrate their multi-channel subscription strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Stakeholder attention to advanced air mobility reveals worldwide disparities
Abstract: Advanced air mobility (AAM) has garnered escalating attention from academia, government, business, and the general public. Previous studies tended to investigate these main stakeholders separately, failing to identify their various attentions, attitudes and focus areas. This research employs bibliometric and social media large language model (LLM) text mining methods to explore the perspectives of main stakeholders on AAM for a decade (2015-2024), with approximately 300,000 texts in total. Our findings show a consistent rise in text volume across all key stakeholders, with government stakeholders demonstrating the fastest growth rate. Globally, the text sentiment is predominantly either positive or neutral, with negative sentiment being the least prevalent. The topic analysis reveals stakeholders have heterogeneous priorities, with businesses and governments tending to emphasize AAM-related infrastructure, the general public focusing more on end-user experiences and air mobility infrastructure and integration, while academia concentrating on aerodynamics and safety concerns. This research seeks to inform actionable policy formulation and air-transport planning, thereby facilitating AAM integration into urban and regional transportation systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: From Principles to Practice: Embedding GEDSI in Process Design

Abstract: This paper investigates the integration of Gender, Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) principles into process design, highlighting their significance in promoting equitable processes. A GEDSI-Process Maturity Framework is introduced to assess process alignment with GEDSI dimensions, although further development is required. Title: The Role of Serious Games for Boundary-Object Negotiation in Innovation Projects
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Innovation projects that span multiple disciplines and organizations depend on cross-functional collaboration and knowledge integration to succeed. Boundary objects—shared artifacts, models, or methods that enable coordination across different social and knowledge domains—are key means for realizing such collaboration and integration. However, boundary objects are rarely self-explanatory or automatically accepted. To become effective, they must undergo negotiation cycles through the active participation of the actors involved in the collaboration. This negotiation process is difficult to achieve, yet essential for developing shared understanding, fostering collective sensemaking, and enabling the effective use of boundary objects. To facilitate this process, this paper explores Serious Games (SGs)—structured, goal-oriented games designed for purposes beyond entertainment—as potential mechanisms for boundary-object negotiation. Guided by a Research through Design perspective—where knowledge emerges through the design and application of artifacts—an SG workshop was developed and implemented within a European rail innovation project, where a Business Case methodology acted as a boundary object for integrating domain-specific knowledge. Drawing on design-thinking principles, the SG enabled participants to understand, analyze, and negotiate the selected boundary object. The study demonstrates how the SG acted as a catalyst for cross-functional dialogue, facilitating shared understanding and collective sensemaking around the boundary object. The findings highlight how playful, participatory, and human-centered interventions can enhance boundary-object negotiation and strengthen methodological alignment, especially in complex innovation environments. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Supporting strategic decisions for coastal watersheds in crisis: A system dynamics model for socio-ecological sustainability
Abstract: Sustainable development of coastal lagoons facing complex socio-ecological crises requires quantification of impacts of solutions on all sectors involved. We present a System Dynamics Model (SDM) representing interactions between agriculture, livestock, tourism, and nutrient stocks (aquifer, soils, wastewaters) of the Mar Menor socio-ecological system (SE-Spain), following a participatory process. Business-as-usual (SSP2) and agricultural intensification (SSP5) scenarios reduce water security due to climate change and groundwater contamination. End-of-pipe interventions do not provide long-term solutions, whereas source-oriented interventions lower nutrient inputs, providing socioeconomic benefits. Title: LLM-Assisted Logic Rule Learning: Scaling Human Expertise for Time Series Anomaly Detection in Supply Chain Management
Abstract: Time series anomaly detection is critical for supply chain management to take proactive operations, but faces challenges: classical unsupervised anomaly detection based on exploiting data patterns often yields results misaligned with business requirements and domain knowledge, while manual expert analysis cannot scale. We propose a framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to systematically encode human expertise into interpretable, logic-based rules for detecting anomalies in supply chain time series data. Distinct from direct LLM deployment, our approach utilizes LLMs to generate and iteratively optimize deterministic rules offline. Deployed at Amazon for monitoring millions of individual products, our approach achieves detection accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs while delivering 1) orders of magnitude faster execution with 2) zero inference API costs in production. This establishes a scalable paradigm for bridging expert-driven decision-making with automated production systems, eliminating the latency and stochasticity barriers of direct LLM deployment. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
Abstract: The clean energy transition demands unprecedented quantities of critical minerals — lithium, cobalt, copper, and rare earth elements — with demand projected to rise six-fold by 2030, far beyond what primary mining alone can supply. Circular economy (CE) practices offer a strategic pathway to close this mineral gap while simultaneously reducing the carbon intensity of energy production. Yet despite growing scholarly interest, the empirical relationship between firm-level CE adoption and energy transition performance (ETP) remains fragmented across disciplines, with no unified framework linking these constructs at scale. This study addresses that gap through a two-phase mixed-methods design. Phase 1 delivers a PRISMA-compliant systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of 405 synthesised articles, confirming the absence of firm-level empirical models in this nexus. Phase 2 develops and tests multi-level conceptual model grounded in Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Natural Resource-Based View, and Institutional Theory, using structural equation modelling–partial least squares (SEM-PLS) on survey data from 318 EU energy-intensive firms, complemented by fixed-effects panel regression merging Eurostat and IEA databases. CE practices significantly predict ETP (β = 0.312, p < 0.001). This study makes three contributions: an empirically validated firm-level framework linking CE practices to ETP, which to our knowledge is the first of its kind at this scale; the introduction of critical mineral circularity as novel strategic moderator; and cross-national evidence on how policy environments condition the CE–energy transition nexus. Findings carry direct implications for corporate supply chain strategy, EU regulatory design, and achievement of SDG 7, SDG 12, and SDG 13. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Hydraulic lobe-pump inter-operational transportation of cheese spreads
Abstract: When pumped from one production unit to another, molten cheese spread is a highly viscous liquid, which inevitably affects all hydraulic calculations for optimal pipeline characteristics. However, such calculations often miss out the effect of the viscosity on the pump efficiency. This article introduces a new method for determining the optimal pipe diameter to transport liquid media during food production. It takes into account the viscosity of the liquid and the technical characteristics of the rotary lobe pump. The research featured a lobe-pump hydraulic system for transporting highly viscous cheese spreads. The calculations involved the technical parameters of the lobe pump and pipelines, as well as electricity tariffs. To determine the annual electricity costs, we used electricity tariffs for small businesses as of June 2024 in three random regions of the Russian Federation. The parameters of different cheese spreads (55–95°C) came from scientific publications in the public domain. Among the various factors that affected the optimal pipe diameter, the greatest impact belonged to the temperature-related changes in viscosity. As the operation time of the lobe pump increased, so did the share of electrical energy costs. As a result, the optimal diameter of the pipeline increased significantly to compensate for the hydraulic pressure losses and energy costs. The optimal diameter also depended on the investment parameters. Bigger Life-Cycle values correlated with larger optimal pipe diameters, i. e., the reduced costs went down. Higher interest rates, on the other hand, correlated with smaller optimal pipe diameters, i. e., the reduced costs went up. In general, the overall efficiency of the pumping station depended quite strongly on all the factors featured in this research. The new method made it possible to determine the optimal pipe diameter for inter-operational transportation of cheese spreads in particular and highly viscous laminar fluids in general. It relied on viscosity values and lobe pump specifications. Numerically, it was based on a step-by-step calculation of economic and hydraulic parameters. The method demonstrated good prospects for food pipeline design. © 2026, Akhmedova et al. Title: AI-Based System for Automatic Backlog Generation and Preliminary Estimation from Requirement Documents
Abstract: In the context of digital transformation and Agile software development, requirement analysis and backlog preparation remain largely manual processes that rely heavily on individual experience and interpretation. These activities are time-consuming, error-prone, and often inconsistent, particularly in large-scale software projects. This paper presents an AI-based system for automatic backlog generation and preliminary effort estimation from requirement documents, designed to support Business Analysts (BAs) and Project Management Offices (PMOs) in Agile environments. The proposed system automatically analyzes software requirement documents, such as User Requirement Documents (URD) and Requirement Specification Documents (RSD), and generates structured Agile backlog artefacts, including Epics, User Stories, Acceptance Criteria, and Tasks/Sub-tasks, together with preliminary effort estimations. The system integrates large language models with rule-based estimation logic and provides seamless integration with enterprise project management platforms through REST APIs, enabling automatic synchronization with tools such as Jira and Confluence. The end-to-end workflow includes document ingestion, requirement extraction, contextual analysis, backlog generation, estimation computation, and structured export to project management systems. Experimental evaluation on real-world software requirement documents demonstrates that the proposed system significantly improves backlog preparation efficiency. The results show that the system can reduce backlog preparation time by approximately 75%, simplify the backlog creation workflow, and generate backlog items with a high level of accuracy and consistency compared to traditional manual approaches. These findings highlight the practical potential of AI-assisted systems in automating requirements engineering activities and improving productivity in Agile software development processes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Conceptual Normalisation as a Foundation for Clear and Correct Organisational Models
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Organisational models frequently suffer from semantic ambiguities and structural redundancies that hinder consistency, maintainability, and correct system interpretation. This paper proposes that these issues stem from conceptual redundancy and can be addressed through a principled application of Conceptual Normalisation (CN) - a theory based on the ontological premise that the real world contains no redundancy. Title: The impact of digital leadership style on employee work motivation in small and medium-sized enterprises: A case study in Vietnam
Abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution has been strongly driving the digital transformation process within organizations, particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Digital technologies, artificial intelligence, digital platforms, and smart management systems not only transform business models but also reshape leadership practices and human resource management within organizations. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory, this study aims to examine the impact relationships between digital leadership style and employee work motivation in small and medium-sized enterprises in the North Central region of Vietnam. The study employs a quantitative research approach using the structural equation modeling (SEM) technique. To provide data for the analysis, a survey was conducted with a sample of 317 respondents, including managers at different levels and employees working in SMEs in the North Central region. The results indicate that digital leadership style not only has a direct and positive effect but also exerts an indirect effect on employee work motivation through the mediating role of perceived digital safety. In addition, job satisfaction plays a mediating role in the relationships between job autonomy and perceived digital safety and employee work motivation in SMEs in the North Central region. From a practical perspective, the research findings provide valuable insights for policymakers and business managers by highlighting the importance of adopting digital leadership practices in organizational management. These insights can serve as a foundation for proposing effective solutions to enhance employee work motivation, thereby improving organizational performance and sustainability in small and medium-sized enterprises. These findings highlight the theoretical and practical contributions of the study and provide a valuable foundation for future research. Based on the research results, the authors propose several recommendations to enhance employee work motivation in SMEs in the North Central region of Vietnam. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. Title: Artificial Intelligence as an Information and Knowledge Management Capability: A Comparative Systematic Literature Review of Managerial Impacts in Africa and Europe
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Artificial intelligence has evolved into a strategic organizational capability that shapes information and knowledge management and managerial decision-making. This study conducts a comparative systematic literature review of AI-enabled Information and Knowledge Management across Africa and Europe from 2005 to 2025, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. From an initial corpus of 100 records, 21 peer-reviewed studies were retained and analyzed using descriptive, thematic and bibliometric techniques. Quantitative evidence reveals the presence of pronounced regional asymmetries. European organizations demonstrate higher AI readiness (avg. 1.01), adoption (avg. 0.83), and knowledge maturity (avg. 0.85), supported by sustained R&D investment (2.2% of GDP) and harmonized regulatory frameworks. African contexts exhibit lower readiness (avg. 0.59), adoption (avg. 0.51), yet show accelerated post-2018 growth driven by mobile-first and frugal-AI innovations. Across regions, AI enhances decision accuracy and firm performance primarily when it is used to reconfigure organizational and managerial processes, whereas automation-led deployments yield mixed efficiency outcomes. This study advances theory by extending the Knowledge-Based View toward a Dynamic Managerial Capabilities perspective, positioning AI as a context-dependent knowledge transformer, and providing actionable insights for aligning AI deployment with inclusive and sustainable knowledge strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: A graph-theory-based order batching method for pharmaceutical warehouse with tail-bin coupling avoidance
Abstract: As pharmaceutical fulfilment rapidly shifts toward split-case picking, warehouses require order batching methods that balance aggregation efficiency with tail-bin coupling risk. Existing studies rarely consider tail-bin coupling in pharmaceutical split-case picking, which can reduce batching effectiveness and prolong completion time. To address this gap, this study proposes a graph-theoretic order batching model incorporating a master–slave association set mechanism that limits excessive concentration of related orders and mitigates tail-bin coupling risk. A Stock Keeping Units (SKU)-association graph is constructed from SKU-sharing relationships among orders to decompose the order set into independent connected subgraphs. The model minimizes the total number of bin presentations. To solve the model efficiently, we develop a memorized branch-and-bound backtracking algorithm that combines graph decomposition, branch-and-bound pruning, and state memorization, followed by a constrained re-binning merging strategy for global batch reorganization. Numerical experiments show that, compared with GUROBI and ALNS, the proposed algorithm delivers the best overall performance, producing solutions close to the GUROBI optimum with an average deviation below 3 % while greatly improving computational efficiency to satisfy real-time engineering requirements. Tests on different order structures and real business data further confirm the algorithm's applicability and convergence stability in pharmaceutical split-case picking. Wilcoxon and Friedman tests confirm that it significantly outperforms ALNS and other methods. Sensitivity analysis indicates that increasing the order limit of the master correlation set T reduces bin presentations but increases tail-bin coupling risk; thus, setting T to 6–8 is recommended for typical pharmaceutical split-case picking scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Prioritising seafood diversification in Sweden: Integrating biological screening with stakeholder constraints
Abstract: Diversifying seafood production and consumption has been proposed as a strategy for improving the sustainability and resilience of food systems. Along the Swedish west coast, numerous low-trophic marine species remain underutilised despite growing interest in sustainable seafood diversification. However, biological suitability alone does not determine whether such species become viable food resources. This study combines biological screening of 38 underutilised marine invertebrate and macroalgal taxa with stakeholder evidence generated through interviews, workshops, and surveys conducted between 2018 and 2024. Species were assessed using a scoring framework, while stakeholder evidence was analysed to identify opportunities and constraints across the seafood value chain. The biological screening identified several promising candidates for diversification, including macroalgae, cephalopods, tunicates, sea urchins, and species of crabs. Stakeholder evidence revealed strong interest in these and other underutilised species but also highlighted recurring barriers related to supply reliability, processing capacity, market access, food-safety requirements, and regulatory uncertainty. The findings demonstrate that the principal constraints to seafood diversification are not primarily biological but organisational and institutional. Diversification opportunities appear strongest where biological feasibility aligns with enabling conditions across production, processing, markets, and governance. In particular, reducing regulatory uncertainty, strengthening value-chain coordination, and creating confidence for investment and market development emerged as important prerequisites for translating biological opportunities into viable seafood products and businesses. By integrating biological and stakeholder perspectives, the study provides a practical framework for identifying priority species and guiding policy and industry efforts to support seafood diversification. Title: The power of effortful communication in recovering from woke-washing allegations: impact on brand morality and firm outcomes
Abstract: Brands are increasingly seen as agents of social change through brand activism, with some consumers expecting brands to use their moral authority to influence others. However, allegations of inauthentic brand activism, often referred to as “woke-washing,” present significant challenges and can undermine consumers’ brand perceptions. Across a pilot thematic analysis and four experimental studies, we offer insights into woke-washing and its consequences and provide guidance for effective brand response strategies. Specifically, high-effort responses increase purchase intentions and positive word-of-mouth through a sequential process involving perceived brand communication authenticity and perceived brand morality. Abstract: Microservice-based applications offer scalability and flexibility but introduce security challenges, including security smells, i.e., possible symptoms of poor security decisions. The occurrence of these smells can be resolved via known refactorings, which, however, impact not only security but also other quality attributes, such as maintainability and performance. Deciding which refactoring to implement first is complex due to service interdependencies and varying business priorities. In this paper, to support practitioners in deciding under these complex and dynamic conditions, we introduce a decision support method designed to account for these multifaceted constraints. The proposed approach offers a holistic perspective that considers the urgency of each security smell instance alongside the effort needed to concretely implement the refactoring and cross-team dependencies, ultimately enabling context-aware decisions. We also present a prototype tool implementing the proposed method and assess the perceived usefulness of our method through a preliminary empirical study following a one-group pretest-posttest design. After being introduced to the method, participants perceived the decision process as easier and reported greater confidence in their selected refactorings. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Title: A Deep Learning-Based Model for Identifying Abnormal Access Behavior and Security Protection in Low-Carbon Park Networks
Abstract: The network system of low-carbon parks is responsible for various important tasks, including energy control, equipment status monitoring, and user service support. However, abnormal access behavior caused by network attacks not only directly affects the normal operation of business, but may also lead to a sudden increase in energy consumption during emergency response, further causing an increase in carbon emissions. The commonly used anomaly detection methods based on rules or statistical features are often difficult to handle the rapid changes and complex situations of network behavior patterns. Therefore, this article proposes a multimodal anomaly recognition and dynamic protection framework that combines deep learning mechanisms. On the basis of summarizing existing research results, this article carefully analyzes the shortcomings of existing methods and focuses on designing lightweight feature extraction modules, adaptive threshold adjustment strategies, and low resource consumption protection mechanisms. This model not only maintains high detection accuracy, but also fully considers the overall energy efficiency of the system, providing a feasible technical route for network security management in low-carbon parks. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2027.

Title: Platform governance and value co-creation in online food delivery ecosystems: capacity allocation and commission strategies
Abstract: Online food delivery (OFD) platforms represent a prominent class of service digital ecosystems in which platform governance mechanisms shape multi-sided value co-creation among platforms, restaurant partners, and consumers, the joint gain from coordinating rather than deciding independently. This study examines how OFD platforms strategically govern restaurant networks through incentive-based contracts, specifically, minimum business guarantees (MBGs), and how these governance choices interact with restaurant capacity allocation decisions and pricing strategies across online and offline channels. We develop a Stackelberg game model embedded in a Hotelling-Bertrand competition framework to capture the hierarchical decision-making structure of this ecosystem. The model yields closed-form equilibrium outcomes for the restaurant's optimal capacity allocation between dine-in and online channels, the platform's commission fee, and pricing strategies for both ecosystem participants. Our results reveal that a restaurant's capacity allocation is significantly influenced by the relative share of offline dine-in demand within a fixed total market, and that price mimicking by restaurants is profitable under low dine-in demand but erodes platform value when offline demand is high. Numerical analysis further demonstrates that increasing consumer disutility costs prompt both platforms and restaurants to raise prices across channels, highlighting critical trade-offs in ecosystem optimization. These findings provide actionable governance insights for OFD platforms designing incentive structures and for restaurant partners navigating channel trade-offs. The study contributes to the growing literature on data-driven platform governance and ecosystem optimization in service digital ecosystems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Semantic Risk Scoring of Aggregated Metrics: An AI-Driven Approach for Healthcare Data Governance
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Large healthcare institutions typically operate multiple business intelligence (BI) teams segmented by domain, including clinical performance, fundraising, operations, and compliance. Due to HIPAA, FERPA, and IRB restrictions, these teams face challenges in sharing patient-level data needed for analytics. To mitigate this, A metric aggregation table is proposed, which is a precomputed, privacy-compliant summary such as “Average Patient Wait Times by Department” or “Donor Conversion by Campaign.” These abstractions enable decision-making without direct access to sensitive data. However, even aggregated metrics can inadvertently lead to privacy risks if constructed without rigorous safeguards. A modular AI framework is proposed that evaluates SQL-based metric definitions for potential overexposure using both semantic and syntactic features. Specifically, the system parses SQL queries into abstract syntax trees (ASTs), extracts sensitive patterns (e.g., fine-grained GROUP BY on ZIP code or gender), and encodes the logic using pretrained CodeBERT embeddings. These are fused with structural features and passed to an XGBoost classifier trained to assign risk scores. Queries that surpass the risk threshold (e.g., >0.85) are flagged and returned with human-readable explanations (e.g., “Metric may overexpose sensitive groupings like gender or ZIP”). This enables proactive governance, preventing statistical disclosure before deployment. This implementation demonstrates strong potential for cross-departmental metric sharing in healthcare while maintaining compliance and auditability. The system also promotes role-based access control (RBAC), supports zero-trust data architectures, and aligns with national data modernization goals by ensuring that metric pipelines are explainable, privacypreserving, and AI-auditable by design. Title: Community Archives as Innovation Driver for a Network of Territorial Enterprises in Inner Areas
Abstract: This contribution explores the role of community archives as enabling infrastructures for territorial regeneration and entrepreneurial innovation in inland areas. The research is developed within the framework of the “Archivio Atena” project, promoted by the Department of Architecture of the University of Naples Federico II in collaboration with the Municipality of Atena Lucana, a small town in Southern Italy involved in the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) programme for the regeneration of historic villages. The study investigates how a community archive can evolve from a mere tool for preserving collective memory into a relational and operational innovation driver for local enterprises by fostering a new territorial business network. The contribution proposes and tests a methodological decision-making framework based on mutual learning and value-oriented territorial development, involving multiple actors and structured around four interconnected phases: identification of territorial values through the archive; co-design and reciprocal learning processes; experimentation between students and local enterprises; reintegration of results into the archive through a circular knowledge process. The experimentation, carried out between 2024 and 2026, highlights how community archives can support the emergence of collaborative networks, the strengthening of local skills and the transformation of cultural heritage into strategic resources for community-led development models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Heuristic Work Crafting: A BPM-Inspired Approach to Individual Process Redesign
Abstract: Knowledge workers have considerable autonomy in how they structure their daily tasks, yet systematic guidance for improving individual work practices remains scarce. This paper introduces CRAFT@work, an approach that bridges job crafting theory from Work & Organisational Psychology with process redesign heuristics from the BPM field to support self-directed work improvement. We developed a catalogue of 29 individual work redesign heuristics, adapted from established process redesign heuristics, and evaluated them through an intervention study with 12 knowledge workers across diverse occupational contexts. The intervention consisted of individualised coaching sessions in which participants reflected on their current work, created a Personal Crafting Plan, and subsequently enacted and reflected on their chosen heuristics over a four-week period. Results show that the heuristics are broadly applicable across the occupational contexts included in this study, with every heuristic considered relevant by at least five participants. Almost all participants were able to enact meaningful changes to their work, with several reporting concrete improvements. The most impactful heuristics specifically target the ambiguities and information bottlenecks that slow down or complicate work, making BPM a uniquely situated discipline for addressing the friction that knowledge workers experience. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Customer ducation in sales: A ystematic iterature eview
Abstract: Customer education in sales (CEd) is an emerging research area, yet the literature remains fragmented across multiple fields with inconsistent terminology and conceptualizations. This fragmentation has hindered the development of cumulative knowledge and left fundamental questions about CEd’s effectiveness, mechanisms, and theoretical foundations unanswered. We conduct a systematic literature review of 42 journal articles, examining CEd research across four dimensions: (1) industry contexts and business settings, (2) delivery modes and their outcomes, (3) mechanisms and boundary conditions, and (4) the application of pedagogical theories. Our analysis reveals that across seven distinct delivery modes, CEd generally produces positive, sales-supporting outcomes, such as customer loyalty. Frontline interactions are the most studied mode, while formal programs show the strongest return on investment. However, significant gaps remain: B2C research predominates, direct financial outcomes are understudied, and few studies engage with pedagogical theory. Title: Preliminary Research and Verification of an Algorithm for an Expert Recommendation System for Assessing the Readiness of Airlines to Implement Artificial Intelligence Technologies
Source title: EAI/Springer Innovations in Communication and Computing
Abstract: This paper presents preliminary research and validation of an algorithm for an expert recommendation system that assesses airline readiness to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. The approach includes an information model that fuzzifies survey data—covering implementation possibilities and managerial understanding of AI—and a hybrid fuzzy model that combines multidimensional assessments into a single readiness indicator and offers targeted recommendations. The proposed solution integrates organizational and data-driven factors, reduces the subjectivity of expert judgments, and directly supports management decisions to enhance business process efficiency and flight safety. The experimental application involving five aviation companies confirms the consistency of the proposed methodology and demonstrates the interpretability and managerial relevance of the readiness indicators obtained. The results provide a structured basis for comparative assessment of AI readiness, enabling the formulation of targeted strategic recommendations for aviation companies. In practical terms, the developed system may support strategic planning, prioritization of AI investments, and risk-informed decision-making in airline management. The proposed approach can also serve as a methodological foundation for further digital transformation initiatives in the aviation sector. © European Alliance for Innovation 2027.

Title: Who are my people and what can I do? Community remapping for entrepreneurial venturing after forced migration
Abstract: Scholarship on post-disruption adaptation largely assumes conditions of partial disruption—situations where despite losing access to one or multiple domains, other important domains remain intact. Yet wholesale disruptions pose a qualitatively different challenge for entrepreneurship. We explore how experiences of wholesale disruption shape actors' reconstruction of their contextual structure, perceived scope of their entrepreneurial possibility space, and the long-term trajectory of their ventures. We conduct an inductive study of the venturing efforts of refugees following their wholesale disruption caused by forced migration to the USA. We develop a grounded theoretical model of community remapping for venturing after wholesale disruption that explains why some refugees enact dynamic, growing ventures while others enact more stable, static ventures and eschew growth aspirations. Title: Starting with Operations Management in Software Startups. Motivations and Initial Activities

Abstract: A software startup is an emerging company focused on creating and developing an innovative software-intensive product or service as a basis for creating business value. Operations management is usually not a priority in the early stages of this type of venture, but the need to establish it arises due to specific events or circumstances. Through semi-structured interviews and focus group sessions with experienced founding partners and representatives of software startups, we identified four key reasons or circumstances that lead to the initiation of operations management in these new ventures. Title: Managers’ Educational Level and Sustainability. Its Impact on the Well-Being of C-Top Managers: A Literature Review

Abstract: This literature review explores how C-level education connects to corporate sustainability and executive well-being. Title: Towards Ethics into BPM Research Through Ethical Dilemmas Assessment
Source title: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
Abstract: Business Process Management (BPM) research increasingly influences organizational decision-making, automation, and human work practices, raising important ethical concerns about fairness, transparency, privacy, accountability, and societal impact. Despite their growing importance, ethical aspects are often addressed only implicitly or considered in isolated stages of BPM research projects. In this paper, we argue that ethics should be integrated throughout the BPM research lifecycle. To support this goal, we propose a framework that identifies potential ethical dilemmas at different research stages, and outlines possible strategies to address them. The framework is grounded in perspectives from Philosophy and Information Systems ethics, emphasizing the socio-technical implications of BPM technologies and methods. We demonstrate its applicability through an analysis of three papers published at the BPM 2025 conference, selected as representative cases of BPM research projects. The analysis illustrates recurring ethical gaps and highlights the need for more structured ethical reflection during the design, development, evaluation, and deployment of BPM solutions. Title: Major Trends in the Development of Airports from Central and Eastern Europe between 2010 and 2024
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: After the liberalisation of air transport in Europe in the nineties, the policy for the aviation market has changed, the European Union becoming a single aviation market. The airline-airport relationship has developed and the European airports compete now to attract the services of airlines, especially for having aircraft bases which can bring essential business development. These new features of the air transport market have had a great influence on governmental policies regarding the development of airports in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) over the last 15 years. In order to provide airports with strategic information for building development strategies, this paper presents a comparative analysis of the main parameters of airport development. Title: Joining schools of thought on value propositions: a review and research agenda
Abstract: The value proposition (VP) is foundational to business research, yet literature devoted to it remains fragmented, hindering the theoretical development and practical application of this key concept. Title: Navigating the paradox: Empowerment and power dynamics in international social entrepreneurship
Abstract: Social entrepreneurship (SE) often seeks to empower marginalized beneficiaries by reshaping unequal power relations and promoting more enduring forms of social change. Yet efforts to empower others inherently involve the exercise of power and may therefore reproduce the very asymmetries they seek to overcome. While this “empowerment paradox” has primarily been conceptualized through discrete empowerer-empoweree relationships, considerably less is known about how it unfolds across broader relational systems, particularly in international social entrepreneurship (ISE), where organizations operate across institutional contexts characterized by Global South-North asymmetries. Drawing on a qualitative multi-case study of six ISE ventures, informed by 45 interviews and extensive archival data, we develop an integrative model explaining how the empowerment paradox is structured, experienced, and navigated in these settings. We show that empowerment is organized through multilevel relational chains spanning ecosystem, organizational, and operational levels, that the paradox is experienced differently depending on actors’ positions within these chains, and that organizations navigate persistent tensions through the recursive interplay of relational and structural mechanisms. Building on these findings, we introduce ethical ambidexterity, the capacity to integrate pragmatic and critical orientations toward the use of power, as a means of engaging with rather than resolving the empowerment paradox. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: From Global Policies to Local Strategies: Multi-objective Optimization of Resource-Specific Handover Policies
Abstract: Efficient resource allocation is a key challenge in business process management, with direct implications for cost, throughput time, and utilization. While recent Reinforcement Learning (RL) approaches have shown promise in deriving adaptive allocation policies, they typically neglect inter-resource collaboration patterns that can strongly influence real-world task handovers. Recognizing this, this paper introduces the first approach for multi-objective optimization of resource-level decision-making, enabling the recommendation of person-specific handover policies. To achieve this, our work combines an existing Multi-Agent System-based process simulator with a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. The resulting approach produces Pareto-optimal, resource-specific policies that optimize the process across multiple objectives. Title: Motivated by differentiation or assimilation: How consumer motives shape luxury channel use
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: The rapid digitization of luxury retail has changed how consumers interact with luxury products and services, expanding the range of both online and offline channels. In this evolving landscape, understanding the factors that can influence consumers' online channel use is critical for luxury businesses. This research explores the role of two core social identity motives in luxury consumption, differentiation (the desire to stand out) and assimilation (the desire to fit in), in shaping consumers' luxury channel choices. Using a proprietary dataset of 1,879 verified luxury consumers from eight major Chinese cities, we provide empirical evidence that differentiation reduces exclusive online channel use, whereas assimilation increases it. Additionally, we demonstrate that status signaling amplifies the negative effect of differentiation on exclusive online channel use, whereas social engagement strengthens the positive effect of assimilation. These findings offer novel insights by applying social identity motive theory to the context of digital luxury consumption and examining luxury channel choice, an understudied aspect of luxury behavior. Title: A Large Language Model Agent-Assisted Method for Generating Formally Verifiable Code and Its Applications in Blockchain
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Protocols in blockchain systems, including consensus protocols, cryptographic algorithms, smart contract interaction protocols, and business transaction flow protocols, exist in the form of natural language documents such as research papers, standard specifications, and technical proposals during the design and specification phases. Natural language descriptions of blockchain protocols inherently suffer from ambiguity and imprecision in interpretation, which can lead to significant risks during the engineering phase due to misunderstandings or unclear descriptions. Generating formally verifiable descriptions represents a viable approach to addressing these issues. However, existing formal verification methods (taking model checking as an example) face multiple challenges. First, manually writing formally verifiable code makes it difficult to guarantee completeness and reliability. Second, the manual development of formally verifiable code is labor intensive and highly inefficient. Title: Balancing risk and opportunity: Digital transformation, cybersecurity investments, and export performance in low-tech firms
Abstract: This study examines whether investments in digital technologies raise export sales among low-tech firms, and whether cybersecurity spending conditions these returns. Reading the Resource-Based View through resource orchestration, we frame digital technologies as enabling resources and cybersecurity as a protective commitment securing their value but competing for the investment budget under scarcity. This competition is sharper in low-tech firms, with thinner slack. Using Bank of Italy data (2016–2023), we find digital investment positively associated with export sales where cybersecurity spending is absent. This association is negative in the highest protective-spending brackets, and a specification imposing no functional form locates the reversal at the top of the distribution. The pattern is clearer among SMEs and manufacturing firms; among larger firms, digital investment shows no association with exports, while protective spending is associated with higher export volume. This is a cyber-risk paradox: under scarcity, protection substitutes for, rather than complements, digital expansion. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. Title: A Multi-Layered and Conceptual Framework for the Digital Product Service System Passport
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: The transition toward Product-Service Systems (PSS) requires continuous and seamless data exchange across the value chain. However, fragmented data silos and stakeholder reluctance often hinder this process. While the emerging Digital Product Passport (DPP) offers a structured approach to data sharing, current literature predominantly views it as a static regulatory compliance tool, lacking a cohesive framework to support dynamic PSS provision. To address this gap, this study proposes a comprehensive and multi-layered framework for the Digital Product Service System Passport (DPSSP). Grounded in Design Research Methodology (DRM), the framework was developed by synthesizing current academic literature and EU-funded projects and subsequently validated through cross-sectoral expert focus groups spanning the machinery, manufacturing, and textile industries. The proposed framework shifts the passport’s paradigm from compliance to a dynamic PSS enabler. Specifically, this paper details the Conceptual Layer of the DPSSP, mapping the interactions among lifecycle phases, a criticality-driven hierarchical data structure (product vs. component levels), multi-level decision-making processes, acquisition and analysis technologies and multi-actor ecosystem. The findings demonstrate that the DPSSP can act as a strategic facilitator for servitization, providing practitioners with a modular blueprint to improve PSS business models. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Implementation of Corporate Strategy in Era of Industry 4.0: A Comparative Study of Slovak and Georgian Manufacturing Firms
Source title: Lecture Notes on Data Engineering and Communications Technologies
Abstract: Corporate strategy follows the vision and sets actions that guide the organization’s direction, resource allocation, and long-term competitiveness. In the era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0), this role has become more critical as technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, and big data transform not only production systems, but also organizational structures, business processes and business models. Existing research has focused mainly on technological and operational dimensions, while the strategic perspective remains less examined. The purpose of this study was to analyze how manufacturing firms in Slovakia and Georgia formulate and implement corporate strategies in Industry 4.0. A structured questionnaire survey was conducted with 300 firms, and the analysis focused on three areas: (1) the existence and centrality of corporate strategy, (2) implementation practices and mechanisms, and (3) managerial perceptions of opportunities and barriers. The results indicate two main patterns. First, although many firms report having a corporate strategy, it is often treated as one of several priorities rather than the central framework for decision-making. Second, implementation practices differ: Slovak firms employ more formalized mechanisms, while Georgian firms rely on informal approaches and show less systematic integration of Industry 4.0 into their corporate strategy. Across both contexts, barriers are perceived mainly in technical and resource terms, and the lack of a clearly defined strategy is seldom acknowledged. The study extends existing research by linking Industry 4.0 adoption with corporate strategy in a comparative context. It concludes that a structured strategic framework is required to ensure that technological adoption supports long-term competitiveness. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Constrained occupational pathways: Historical ethnic penalties in career mobility among Japanese immigrants in the United States, 1920–1940
Abstract: Racial and ethnic stratification was a persistent feature of the early 20th-century U.S. labor market. While acknowledging structural barriers such as organized exclusion, studies of Japanese immigrants have typically emphasized their upward mobility from laborers to independent farmers or small-business owners before World War II. Yet, few studies have examined how such barriers shaped Japanese mobility relative to that of contemporaneous immigrants from Europe, as well as Canada and Mexico. Using linked 1920–1940 U.S. census panel data, this study compares occupational mobility between first-generation Japanese immigrant men (born 1881–1900) and other immigrants by educational attainment. Findings indicate substantial ethnic occupational penalties for Japanese immigrants, particularly pronounced at higher levels of education, where they ranked below even their similarly educated Mexican counterparts. Whereas European and Canadian immigrants frequently ascended into managerial, professional, and skilled or semi-skilled blue-collar occupations, upward mobility among Japanese immigrants remained largely confined to small-business ownership and farming. Such an absence from mid-tier occupations is consistent with historically documented patterns of organized exclusion from labor unions and labor market discrimination. Additional analyses align with constrained occupational pathways as a major channel of the Japanese immigrants' economic disadvantage: within the same detailed occupations, salaried Japanese immigrants faced only modest observed wage penalties relative to U.S.-born Whites. Overall, my findings qualify optimistic narratives about first-generation Japanese immigrants by foregrounding the institutional constraints that structured their career mobility. © 2026 The Author

Title: “We apologise for any inconvenience”: A local grammar of apology in corporate apology letters
Abstract: Corporate apologies serve as strategic responses to organisational crises, balancing expressions of regret with reputational, legal, and stakeholder management concerns. This study analyses 389 apology letters issued by Fortune 500 companies between 2014 and 2023, with a focus on the recurrent lexico-grammatical patterning of apology expressions. Through a local grammar approach to mapping recurring form–meaning regularities in the corpus, 25 patterns were identified and grouped into six sets, revealing a preference for specification-rich, structurally explicit, and emotionally moderated apology constructions. The findings show that corporate apologies are typically elaborated through contextual specification, while intensification and direct reference to the offended remain comparatively limited. Implicit realisations, such as acknowledgements of harm or responsibility, were identified, although less frequent, through a model-assisted prompting procedure using ChatGPT. To situate the linguistic findings, the study also considers the crisis contexts in which the letters were produced, including service failures, product issues, reputational controversies, and regulatory or community-facing incidents. The study contributes to ESP and business discourse research by offering a systematic account of how apology is conventionally realised in corporate letters and by providing a descriptive framework that can support genre awareness in professional communication pedagogy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Entrepreneurship Education in Action: Preventing the NEET Phenomenon. Lessons from La Paranza Case Study
Abstract: The rise of young people not in employment, education, or training (NEET) is a major concern in Europe, particularly in disadvantaged areas. Entrepreneurship education is seen as a strategy to enhance inclusion and employability, though it remains underexplored outside formal schooling. This study examines La Paranza cooperative in Naples and identifies key drivers, including experiential learning, place-based approaches, mentorship, active participation, and stakeholder networks. These factors foster skills, self-esteem, and local identity, supporting pathways into employment. The findings show that entrepreneurship education can develop beyond schools, contributing to inclusive policies that address youth marginalization and reduce NEET conditions. © The Author(s) 2027.

Title: Private Quantised Neural Network Inference
Abstract: Neural networks based machine learning models are used in many classification problems yet privacy issues in model usage are mostly unresolved. When a model owner provides their model to other parties for inference, either the model owner has to share the parameters of the model or the model user must share their query and result with the model owner. Depending on the usage scenario, the user’s query or query result could contain sensitive information that the model provider should not see. And on the other hand, the model parameters themselves could be a valuable business secret or leak private training data. In such cases, neural network inference must be performed in a privacy preserving manner, for example, using secure multi-party computation (MPC). We propose protocols for the private inference of neural networks and evaluate them within the Sharemind MPC secure computation framework. Our protocols are based on the per-tensor quantisation scheme in PyTorch which maps floating point model parameters to 8-bit integer values. Quantisation improves the efficiency of our protocols and our protocols are interoperable with models trained using PyTorch. We extend constant round integer convolution and matrix multiplication protocols for quantised model weights, propose constant round protocols for re-quantising values and analyse the optimal secret share bit width for efficient re-quantisation. The resulting protocols are used to evaluate the VGG16 image classification network with an amortised throughput of 24.3 s per image classification in a LAN setting. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Increasing the Efficiency of Using the Energy Potential of Wood: Solutions for Ukraine
Source title: Studies in Systems, Decision and Control
Abstract: The aim of the research is to develop directions for increasing the efficiency of using wood as an energy source in Ukraine. The state of global forestry and the use of the energy potential of fuel wood from 2013 to 2023 is assessed on the basis of data from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). The analysis of global trends in logging, wood processing, and the use of wood as fuel revealed discrepancies in global trends regarding the rates of change in the share of fuel wood production, wood pellets, and briquettes. Significant growth rates in the production of wood agglomerates worldwide indicate an intensification of the use of energy potential of wood driven by ecological and economic factors. With one of the highest shares of fuel wood in total wood volume, Ukraine produces nearly 7 times less wood pellets than Germany. Based on the developed regression models, a scenario has been elaborated to enhance the efficiency of utilizing the fuel potential of wood in Ukraine. It has been demonstrated that there are reserves in Ukraine for processing fuel wood and waste from both wood processing and saw-milling industries into more efficient products in terms of energy production and compliance with environmental conditions, namely pellets, briquettes, and so on. It is concluded about advisability to process wood waste directly at the sites of logging or wood processing, using technologies and equipment for collecting and sorting the waste from saw-milling and woodworking production and by-products. Title: Barriers to Blockchain Implementation: A Multidimensional Analysis of Technological, Organizational, and Regulatory Challenges
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The reason for the great interest in blockchain technology is its potential to make many industries, such as banking, logistics, healthcare, and governance, transparent, secure, and optimized. Whereas blockchain technology may be very instrumental in effecting wide changes in the world, its usage has been limited so far. The purpose of this research paper is to identify and discuss some of the main technological, business-related, and regulatory barriers that impede the full-scale implementation of blockchain technology. The report uses a qualitative approach that is guided by Technology Adoption Theory, Institutional Theory, and Innovation Diffusion in Literature. This study adopts a qualitative systematic literature review approach, synthesizing evidence from 44 peer-reviewed articles selected through a PRISMA-guided screening process shows that the issues surrounding the implementation of blockchain technology can be broadly classified into three different sections: issues revolving around technology, factors related to the readymade nature of the organization, and regulatory/legally related issues. The paper shows that scalability, power consumption, compatibility, and cybersecurity act as factors that may hinder the adoption due to their complexities in implementing novel technologies themselves. Other factors that may hamper adoption include lack of knowledge, lack of recognition, increased cost of implementation, and lack of values themselves. In addition, the lack of standardized legal practices surrounding the absence of the technology affects organizations that plan to implement blockchain technology in their firms. This research refines the existing literature on blockchain and innovation by providing an elaborated framework that can be used to address the issue of the implications of the mentioned barriers to the results of the adoption of blockchain technology. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Towards a Mental Model-Driven Approach for User Interface Development: Evolving DataForm
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: User interface development often faces usability challenges due to discrepancies between developers’ conceptual models and users’ mental models. This paper introduces an enhanced model-driven approach centered on DataForm, a formal language designed to capture, structure, and operationalize users’ mental models in UI design. We extend DataForm to support visual customization, rendering flexibility, and real-time propagation through a modular architecture that separates business logic from interface representation. Integrated into the Task and Data Model-Based User Interface Development (TD-MBUID) framework, DataForm enables model-driven prototyping and dynamic updates. Its abstract syntax is formalized to allow hierarchical structuring of data and interface elements, while propagation mechanisms ensure synchronization between the back-end and the front-end. A case study in a virtual learning environment demonstrates the approach’s potential to enhance interface adaptability, streamline UI evolution, and improve alignment between system behavior and user cognition. While preliminary results are promising, they are based on a structured implementation scenario. Further experimental validation with end users is necessary to empirically assess the extent to which DataForm supports cognitive alignment and usability improvements across diverse interaction contexts. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Local Brands, Digital Shelves: Brand Authenticity and E-commerce Consumer Behavior in Vietnam’s Fashion Industry
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Abstract: Brands significantly influence customers’ identity goals, as they rely on brands for self-expression, self-promotion, or affirmation of their values. Consequently, consumers are predisposed to alter their purchasing behaviors, and their demand for authenticity is pushing Vietnamese local fashion producers to reconsider their branding. Nonetheless, there is a scarcity of research on the influence of the authenticity of Vietnamese domestic fashion brands on consumer behavior in the contemporary era of e-commerce growth. This article introduces a theoretical framework that integrates the S-O-R theory with the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to analyze the impact of local fashion brand authenticity on consumer behavior in e-commerce. This research specifically focuses on product quality, brand reputation and online shopping experience as cues of authenticity that are used by consumers to evaluate the authenticity of local brands when shopping online. The results offer a more comprehensive understanding of the effect that brand authenticity has on consumers’ behavior in online buying environments. This is done by studying the relationship among brand authenticity, perceived usefulness, and personal attitude in the context of E-commerce consumer behavior. The conceptual framework of the research was checked using the data gathered from an online questionnaire specifically targeting 221 consumers in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC). The data were then analyzed by employing the PLS-SEM method. The findings can guide local fashion businesses in Vietnam to develop in the future, particularly in terms of publicity and marketing. Title: Industry 5.0: Between Theory and Practice

Abstract: Digital transformation has become a new research trend in the last few years, unveiling complicated and creative technologies to change various features of an organization, such as its business models, value chain, products, and services. In the literature, this concept has been linked to Industry4.0 (I4.0) and Industry 5.0 (I5.0) contexts in particular. Although the two paradigms bear some similarities from a technological perspective, the emerging I5.0 paradigm is transitioning from merely representing a technological advancement to establishing a more human-centric, resilient and sustainable manufacturing system. Consequently, it has become a strategic objective for companies to remain competitive and manage uncertainties, particularly in today's era, where demand volatility, changing consumer behavior, geopolitical turmoil and environmental concerns are the norms. This study systematically maps the literature with three primary objectives: (1) to identify application fields and usage environments, (2) to compare theoretical and empirical models employed, and (3) to establish critical success factors (CSFs) for implementation. Title: Makeup and Skincare Endorsement by Virtual Influencers: Product-Influencer Congruence and Persuasion Outcomes

Abstract: Social media influencers effectively promote beauty products, and virtual influencers offer novel opportunities for promotion in this domain. However, their artificial nature raises questions about their ability to endorse products that rely on sensory experience. Drawing on the sensory marketing literature, we examine whether product type (makeup vs. skincare) affects the perceived congruence, product attractiveness, influencer credibility, and purchase intentions associated with a virtual influencer endorsement. However, a multi-group analysis shows that the persuasion mechanism differs: for makeup, product attractiveness drives purchase intentions, whereas for skincare, influencer credibility is the dominant driver.
