Title: From trash to treasure: How exclusivity influences quality perception across different recycled materials in luxury fashion
Source title: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
Abstract: Luxury fashion brands increasingly respond to corporate social responsibility expectations by integrating recycled materials into their products to reduce environmental impact. However, little is known about how these brands should communicate their use of recycled materials on social media without compromising product evaluation. To address this issue, through two between-subjects experimental studies, this paper examines whether and how luxury fashion products crafted from different types of recycled materials (natural vs. synthetic) affect product evaluation on social media, and whether exclusivity moderate this effect. These findings contribute to sustainable luxury fashion literature by identifying material type as the key dimension differentiating consumer evaluations of recycled materials in luxury fashion. The findings also show that exclusivity is the critical contextual trigger that activates this material-driven effect through perceived product quality. Title: A Systematic Review of Research on Digital Platforms - DeepTech Innovation: Broadening Our Horizons

Abstract: In digital platforms, constructs are a critical issue that can affect the development and diffusion of innovations in organizations. Our goal is to identify the constructs to strengthen DeepTech innovations in innovation ecosystems. Through a comprehensive review, we offer a new perspective on this challenge. As digital platforms enhance value generation, DeepTech innovations become stronger. Title: Hurt at home, loafing at work: Spillover effect of family ostracism on hospitality employees’ cyberloafing and its mitigation through self- and others’ care
Abstract: In the hospitality industry, employees’ cyberloafing is more visible to customers, potentially harming key business outcomes such as customer experience and satisfaction. Given these detrimental effects, it is critical to examine the underlying drivers that trigger cyberloafing behavior among hospitality employees. From this perspective, this study examines the influence of interpersonal stressor in the home domain—specifically, family ostracism—on cyberloafing among hospitality employees. Guided by the work-home resources framework, the present study explores a spillover process whereby family ostracism exacerbates hospitality employees’ cyberloafing via family emotional exhaustion. Additionally, it explores how these adverse effects can be mitigated through self-care efforts (self-compassion) and others’ care (family-supportive coworker behavior). Data were obtained from a three-wave survey involving 291 employees and their coworkers at two five-star hotels located in Southeastern China. The results confirm an indirect spillover effect wherein family ostracism leads to cyberloafing via family emotional exhaustion. However, this effect becomes insignificant when employees demonstrate high self-compassion or benefit from family-supportive coworker behavior. Title: Leveraging large language models for agentic process analytics assistants: Assessing accuracy in process mining tasks

Title: Deconstructing Digital Transformation in Global Construction Firms
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Digital transformation has become a strategic concern for large contractors, yet it remains difficult to assess systematically because transformation unfolds unevenly across different organisational domains and dimensions. This paper presents a new analytical framework for assessing digital transformation, developed from literature, and applies it to examine how digital transformation unfolds in large contractor firms. The study employs a structured literature review and a qualitative multiple-case study. The framework structures transformation through five domains and three dimensions, enabling a more fine-grained analysis of how digital initiatives are expressed in practice. The analysis demonstrates the value of the framework by revealing systematic variation in digital transformation across firms, as well as across domains and dimensions within the same firm. Empirically, the findings show that digital transformation is not a uniform or linear process, but varies in how firms create value, manage change, scale pilot outcomes, renew business models, and engage at the corporate level. The findings further reveal three distinct strategic profiles: advanced transformation, internally orchestrated, and operational oriented digitalisation. Based on these findings, the paper contributes an analytical approach for identifying and comparing transformation patterns across large contractors. It also offers practical value by helping managers assess digital transformation more systematically and identify areas where development remains fragmented or weak. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Promotion and prevention regulatory focus in equity crowdfunding reinvestment decisions
Abstract: Using qualitative comparative analysis, our study draws on regulatory focus theory to examine how chronic promotion and prevention foci and situational factors are associated with reinvestment decisions in equity crowdfunding. Evidence suggests that both chronic promotion and prevention foci are sufficient conditions for reinvestment and that situational factors, particularly the absence of inhibitors related to information asymmetry, valuation difficulties, and exit constraints, play an important role. Title: When Indexes Work: Optimizing SQL Queries for Low-Code Applications
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Low-code tools are soaring in popularity because they let users quickly create applications without coding. Oracle Application Express (APEX) is a leading low-code platform that runs within the Oracle Cloud, making it convenient and easy to use. Business users can create database-driven interactive dashboards with forms, reports, and graphs, in less than an hour without writing a single line of code. However, the SQL queries that APEX generates are not optimized for performance, many APEX users lack the skills to optimize them using the Oracle tuning tool, and there is little guidance on when indexes are efficient in APEX applications. This study investigates which query types benefit from indexing within APEX dashboards, and which query types do not benefit from indexes. The dashboard that was evaluated employed common types of auto-generated APEX queries. Query baseline performance was captured using debug mode, and the execution plans analyzed. B-tree indexes drastically improved filtered query performance by over 87% in execution cost and almost 36% in query time. However, B-tree indexes provided no benefit for aggregation queries that process all rows in the table. Surprisingly, composite indexes actually degraded performance by 228%, increasing execution costs substantially. These findings show indexes are not a silver bullet. This research offers practical guidance for APEX developers on how to optimize their queries effectively. The results demonstrate that developers should use indexes strategically, based on the type of query, rather than blindly assuming that all indexes boost performance. © 2026, Springer Science and Business Media Deutschland GmbH. Title: Digital Financial Literacy as a Mediator of Fintech Use and Financial Inclusion in SMEs: Evidence from West Sumatera Indonesia
Abstract: Financial inclusion enhances SME sustainability and growth by expanding access to formal financial services, expanding opportunities for capital acquisition, and supporting business stability. This study empirically investigates the effect of FinTech adoption on financial inclusion, with digital financial literacy serving as a mediating variable among SMEs in West Sumatra, Indonesia. Using purposive sampling, data were collected from 253 SMEs through both direct on-site surveys and online questionnaires via Google Forms for geographically inaccessible areas. Path analysis with Smart PLS 3 was employed to test the hypothesized relationships. The findings reveal that FinTech use and digital financial literacy significantly enhance financial inclusion, FinTech use significantly affects SME financial inclusion mediated by digital financial literacy. Results indicate that both FinTech use and digital financial literacy are central to promoting SME financial inclusion. The research provides actionable implications for policymakers and stakeholders when designing effective strategies to foster inclusive finance through the reinforcement of digital financial literacy and FinTech use. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Female Entrepreneurs 4.0 in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Is 4IR an Opportunity or a Threat?
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is bringing fundamental changes to the global social context, ushering technologies such as automation and artificial intelligence. For female entrepreneurship in Bosnia and Herzegovina, this era represents a specific duality: on one hand, digitalization offers opportunities to overcome traditional gender barriers and facilitates easier access to the global market; on the other hand, it poses a threat by further deepening the digital divide and marginalizing sectors where women-led businesses are traditionally most prominent. The paper explores the position of female entrepreneurs in Bosnia and Herzegovina by analyzing current trends in both, the accessibility and utilization of 4IR resources. The objective is to answer a key question: does technological disruption serve as a catalyst for gender equality or as a new barrier within the transitional economic landscape of Bosnia and Herzegovina for women-led micro and small enterprises? While answering specific research questions, this paper is yet offering actionable strategic recommendations for policymakers, emphasizing the need for specific digital inclusion programs for female entrepreneurs in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the 4.0 era. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Mapping the Maturity of Servitization and PSS Research: Evidence from an International Scientific Panel
Source title: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Abstract: Over the past three decades, research on servitization and Product-Service Systems (PSS) has evolved into a consolidated and multidisciplinary field. While numerous literature reviews have mapped dominant themes and theoretical foundations, limited attention has been devoted to assessing the maturity stage of different research streams and identifying their evolutionary trajectories. This study proposes a maturity assessment of servitization and PSS research based on a literature-informed expert panel involving the international Scientific Advisory Board of the ASAP Interuniversity Research Centre on Servitization. The study adopts a lifecycle positioning lens to assess five thematic areas. Through pre-meeting structured inputs, collective discussion, and post-meeting synthesis, the panel evaluated the research streams by positioning them across emergent, maturity, and relaunch stages. Findings reveal heterogeneous maturity levels within the field. Domains such as IoT-enabled service and subscription-based business models achieved conceptual maturity. In contrast, ecosystem governance, customer adoption dynamics, digital regulation remain in the emergent stage. Structural tensions, including organizational capability gaps, scalability challenges, and methodological limitations, suggest that theoretical consolidation has not yet translated into systemic implementation, acting instead as relaunch triggers for the field. By introducing a lifecycle-based perspective and integrating expert-based field evaluation, this study contributes a reflexive assessment of where servitization research currently stands and identifies the emergent challenges and relaunch dynamics. © IFIP International Federation for Information Processing 2027.

Title: Commons without borders: How entrepreneurs can engage local actors into collective action for the governance of supra-local common-pool resources
Abstract: Based on 41 interviews across three UK-based commons enterprises, this study addresses one of the most pressing challenges of our time: encouraging local actors to contribute to the sustainable governance of supra-local common-pool resources (CPRs)—shared resources whose use and impacts extend beyond community boundaries. While existing research has focused on locally bound natural CPRs, we lack understanding of how entrepreneurial ventures can mobilize the members of local communities to govern resources that span multiple jurisdictions. Our findings reveal a two-step process through which entrepreneurs first embed their commons enterprises in the local community, using asset locks and diversified engagement strategies to involve citizens, local businesses, and public authorities. Building on this embedding, three commoning practices emerge: collective learning about the CPR, collective action and capacity building for CPR stewardship, and collective institutionalization of CPR governance. Around these practices, a community of commoners emerges that is nested within the local community and increasingly sustains collective action independently of the entrepreneur. These practices anchor the supra-local CPR within the local community through three mechanisms: resource proximization, local conditionality, and bonding as a selective incentive, thereby overcoming the collective action barriers arising from lacking resource proximity and perceived responsibility. Our study contributes to research at the intersection of entrepreneurship and the commons by demonstrating the strategic role of common property regimes, shifting attention from the resource to the commoning practices and communities that form around it, and specifying the mechanisms that enable local collective action for supra-local CPR governance. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Between mission pull and governance burden: Geographic distance and deal realisation in impact investing
Abstract: Impact investing is widely expected to direct capital to locations where social and environmental challenges are most severe. Yet such opportunities are often found in places geographically distant from major pools of investment capital. We examine how geographic distance affects the realisation of impact investment deals and how host-country conditions alter that relationship. Integrating transaction cost economics with the location logic of the eclectic paradigm, we argue that impact investment decisions reflect the joint consideration of anticipated transaction value and governance costs. Distance raises the costs of screening, contracting, monitoring, and supporting ventures, while severe sustainability challenges can increase a location's mission-specific attractiveness by signaling greater unmet need and potential scope for additionality. By contrast, trade and investment risk increases transaction hazards that make distant deals harder to execute. We test these arguments using PitchBook data on 3126 impact deals closed in 2022–2023. We analyse 3606 realised investor–venture ties against matched unrealised alternatives in a choice-based sampling design. Distance reduces the likelihood of deal realisation. Challenge severity modestly weakens the distance penalty for a subset of sampled dyads, whereas trade and investment risk strengthens it across most observations. These findings contribute to impact investing by explaining why severe unmet need does not automatically translate into realised investment relationships. They extend transaction cost reasoning in entrepreneurial finance by incorporating mission-adjusted transactional value. They refine international business location logic by distinguishing mission-specific locational attractiveness from host-country transaction hazard. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Customer Churn Prediction: From Data to Decision
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: Restaurant customer churn is an increasing concern due to the growing use of online food delivery systems, loyalty programs, and other forms of e-commerce. When restaurants lose repeat customers it has a negative impact on the restaurant’s long-term revenue, as well as on their brand reputation and overall viability as a business. By being able to identify which customers are at risk of stopping or reducing their ordering activity, restaurants can develop the necessary retention strategies (e.g., personalized offers, loyalty incentives, targeted marketing campaigns) to keep those customers engaged. The traditional methods of performing churn analysis are often manual and based upon simple statistical reports and therefore, have limitations in terms of their predictive accuracy and scalability. In this paper, we propose a machine learning-based predictive framework to identify restaurant customer churn based upon historical order data, transaction records, customer behavior patterns, frequency of visits, feedback ratings, and spending trends. The methodology proposed combines the use of various ensemble learning algorithms (i.e., XGBoost, LightGBM) with preprocessing techniques (e.g., feature scaling, SMOTE) to address the issue of class imbalance within the dataset. The use of feature engineering will also provide the opportunity to derive additional behavioral characteristics (e.g., frequency of visits, average order size, time since last order, etc.) that will enhance the overall ability to predict customer-churn. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: “To be a personal trainer, you have to look like 4% body fat”: How online personal trainers negotiate social media and body image
Abstract: The online personal training industry is continuing to increase in popularity. Sociocultural pressures for personal trainers to maintain a certain physique to be deemed credible and marketable to consumers are well-documented, however no studies have qualitatively explored this in online personal trainers. Whilst previous research has highlighted that consuming certain types of fitness content may negatively impact body image, there is a paucity of research exploring the relationship between content creators and body image.This study aimed to examine how online trainers navigate social media as a digital workplace and their perceptions of its influence on their body image. 17 online coaches (Mage = 33.5; S.D. = 7.4 years), 58.8% female, participated in semi-structured interviews in which they discussed social media, body image and self-selected online content. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Overall, trainers viewed maintaining a social media presence as non-negotiable for business. However, participants also experienced pressure to uphold unrealistic standards online, including showcasing a lean physique and presenting an image of authenticity online whilst concealing body image struggles from consumers. Whilst some trainers rejected these industry standards, other trainers leveraged these norms by utilising their physique to gain traction on social media and enhance perceived desirability and competence to consumers. Title: Implementation of a Scrum-Based Digital Coupon Web Application in the Retail Sector
Source title: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
Abstract: This study presents the implementation of a Scrum-based web application for managing digital coupons in a retail company, addressing the need for agile, scalable, and cloud-oriented promotional systems. The application was developed through five iterative sprints following the Scrum framework and deployed on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) platform using services such as Elastic Beanstalk, S3, CloudFront, Route 53, and Cognito to ensure scalability, security, and operational efficiency. The instrument used to evaluate the system’s commercial effects demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.945), and the Shapiro–Wilk test confirmed the normality of the data. Pearson’s correlation analysis revealed positive and statistically significant associations between the use of the web application and key business indicators, including sales performance (r = 0.557, p = 0.001), new product promotion (r = 0.511, p = 0.004), and private-label product promotion (r = 0.565, p = 0.001). These findings indicate that the implemented solution not only meets technical and operational requirements but also contributes to measurable improvements in promotional effectiveness and commercial visibility. Title: Meta-analysis of antecedents and consequences of customers’ perceived advertisement value
Abstract: The literature has frequently studied the effect of privacy concerns, irritation, trust, incentives, enjoyment, innovativeness, usefulness, ease of use and subjective norms on mobile advertising value. However, the findings are inconsistent regarding the real effect of these antecedents, leaving practitioners uncertain about which antecedents to rely upon to design effective mobile advertisements triggering a problem for them. Using a meta-analytic approach, the current research synthesises 211 empirical studies to test the relationship between these antecedents and advertisement value, which subsequently influences attitudes, intentions, and actual behaviour of receiving mobile advertisements. In terms of findings, our study suggests that usefulness is the strongest driver of advertisement value, whereas irritation is the strongest mitigator, and subjective norms have minimal influence. Similar patterns were observed for the effect of the antecedents on attitudes and intentions. Findings also suggest that strength of these relationships varies depending on contexts and methodological approaches adopted in prior studies. Specifically, the effects of antecedents on the outcome variables are comparatively stronger in recent studies, published in high-quality journals, in developed countries, younger samples, experimental designs, smartphone contexts, customized ads, permission-based and location-aware ads, and in-app formats. Accordingly, this study resolves the inconsistent findings of previous research which makes a novel contribution to the mobile advertising literature. Regarding implications, we recommend mobile advertisers use precision targeting using customers’ geographical area and age group, prioritise customised content over generic campaigns, and adopt permission-based communication as a standard practice. © 2026 The Author(s). Authors: Xu F.; Wang J.; Wu D.
Title: Reliability analysis of cloud-based machine learning services under poisoning attacks
Abstract: Cloud-based Machine Learning as a Service (CMLaaS) platforms provide businesses with on-demand machine learning capabilities, accelerating the commercial adoption of ML technologies. However, these platforms are vulnerable to poisoning attacks that compromise service integrity. In this paper, we introduce a service-attack framework based on a retrial queueing model to evaluate CMLaaS performance in the presence of such attacks. In our model, external adversaries launch targeted poisoning attempts that remain undetected unless specifically checked; if an attack is not neutralized (i.e., repaired) before service completion, the resulting output is deemed invalid. To address the need for rapid and precise reliability assessment in engineering practice, this paper introduces an algorithm based on Monte Carlo simulation to estimate instantaneous reliability. Then, the strategic behavior of customers in self-interested and altruistic cases is analyzed, revealing the important role of curbing selfish behavior in improving system reliability. In addition, the optimization problem of the cost-effectiveness ratio (CER) under different cost structures is studied to provide a more comprehensive analysis of operational strategies for CMLaaS platforms with different purposes. Finally, the benchmark model is extended to the cases of imperfect detection, imperfect repair and finite capacity. The model is validated through numerical experiments, demonstrating the necessity of enhancing repair capability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Tell me about yourself and I might recommend you: a motivation-based explanation of crowdlending investors’ customer citizenship behavior☆
Abstract: Competition among entrepreneurial funding platforms has made it more important than ever to attract and retain investors to ensure the sustainability of entrepreneurial ecosystems. The analysis also confirmed the synergistic effects of intrinsic/self-oriented and extrinsic/other-oriented motivations as sufficient conditions for explaining investor behavior. Nonetheless, such behavior can still be explained exclusively by intrinsic/self-oriented conditions.
